MCU backend: C11, no_std-equivalent, no heap; SoC TBD until deploy authoring
Wire-interoperability with upstream zenohd for the sec 2 documented subset
caveats_bullets: Not a rewrite of zenoh/zenoh-pico; demonstration that SCE synthesizes industrial wire protocols.

10/10.2.intent: QoS config codegen — AP emits Rust const QosConfig (data section); MCU emits C const struct in .rodata (Flash, no RAM cost).

11.intent: Multi-layer testing strategy: byte-equivalence parity, wire replay, upstream interop, no-alloc guard, drift detection, fuzz.

11/11.1.intent: Cross-backend parity gate — every algorithm/codec with sce:test-vector runs on both backends and is byte-diffed; gate on merge.

11/11.2.intent: Wire replay tests — pcap captures from upstream zenoh peers replayed into generated stack with declared expected event sequence.

11/11.3.intent: Upstream interop CI — dockerized zenohd + AP node + MCU host-mode build (lwIP shim, renode/QEMU later) asserting full handshake + pub/sub roundtrip.

11/11.4.intent: MCU heap prohibition enforced as five layers — direct trap, linker wrap, libc pin, call-graph reachability, exception ban — not runtime trap alone.
rationale_bullets: Layer 1 direct trap: malloc/calloc/realloc/free stubs emit __builtin_trap on call.
Layer 2 linker --wrap: -Wl,--wrap on alloc symbols routes libc-internal indirect calls to traps.
Layer 3 libc pin: newlib-nano or picolibc tiny stdio prevents allocating printf path.
Layer 4 call-graph: post-link analyzer rejects any reach from out/mcu to deny-listed allocator.
Layer 5 exception ban: -fno-exceptions/-fno-rtti/-fno-unwind-tables blocks libstdc++ machinery.

11/11.5.intent: Drift gate: every emitted file carries source-hash + template-hash; sce-build verify recomputes and fails on mismatch; manual edits to out/ forbidden.
rationale_bullets: Per-file header carries source-hash + template-hash (sha256 over inputs and sce-build binary).
sce-build verify recomputes both hashes and fails the gate on mismatch (CI + pre-commit).
Fixed artifact set: out/{ap,mcu}, Cargo.toml, CMakeLists.txt, linker fragments, sce_sourcemap.json.
Manual edits to out/ forbidden: path is RFC or sce:extern; exceptions tracked with expiry date.
sce_sourcemap.json hash mismatch surfaces as traceability/sourcemap-source-hash-mismatch.

11/11.6.intent: Adversarial input fuzz testing on generated codec/parsers; deferred Phase D+ work; complements §11.1 cross-backend parity.

2/2.4.intent: Six extensibility invariants: static-first, link-extensible, kinds-additive, library-not-monolith, platform gating, out/ SSoT.

Link drivers extensible: open set via target plugin, not closed enum.
Kinds additive: ForgeKind set grows; existing kinds remain stable across versions.
Generated code exports as library, not monolith: out/ap and out/mcu are library targets.
Platform gating only when physically necessary; keep pool/link/worker kinds platform-neutral.
out/ is SSoT-downstream: manual edits forbidden; new features land via SCE extensions.

3.intent: Four design invariants: zero-runtime abstraction, location transparency, strict SSoT, hardware-aware codegen.

3/3.1.intent: Zero-Runtime Abstraction — no vtables, no dynamic dispatch in the hot path; all bindings resolve at build time to direct calls (SCE AOT philosophy carried through).

3/3.2.intent: Location Transparency — SCXML uses logical identities; physical transport realization and addressing live in deploy.yaml; same SCXML deploys to AP or MCU.

3/3.3.intent: Strict SSoT — wire format / algorithms / FSMs defined once in SCXML+Forge; AP and MCU are descendants; cross-backend drift is a generator bug, not expected.

3/3.4.intent: Hardware-Aware Codegen — MCU code integrates with target SoC capabilities (SRAM placement, DMA pairing, alignment) declared via deploy.yaml; AP/MCU share no memory.

7/7.1.intent: AP backend stack — generated code on top of sce_core + sce_link_runtime_tokio + Rust std/bytes/tokio; tokio::spawn workers, mpsc channels, BytesMut pools.

7/7.2.intent: MCU stack — generated code over sce_forge_runtime_c + sce_link_runtime_lwip; cooperative tick scheduler with WCET budget; static pools + DMA descriptors.

8.intent: Wire format layering: scouting/transport/network/zenoh/extensions; FSM, codec, link layers.

8/8.1.intent: Wire format stack layer diagram — Application -> Session FSM -> Network FSM -> Codec -> Link -> OS/HAL; bottom-up data flow on RX, top-down on TX.

8/8.2.intent: Session FSM sketch — Init/Scouting/Opening/Established/Closing path authored as session_unicast/multicast.scxml; full model lives in docs/session-fsm.md.

8/8.3.intent: Codec layer — one SCXML file per message type using RFC §5.B extensions (flags/vle/present-if/len-prefix/TLV); test vectors drive cross-backend parity.

8/8.4.intent: Link layer — kind=link SCXML files (UDP unicast/multicast/TCP/Serial/WS) with framer + RX-pool + backpressure declared; driver and address bound via deploy.yaml.

9.intent: Zero-copy: TX always zero-copy; RX happy path zero-copy; oversized/fragment stage-copy; pool placement; platform-aware link.

9/9.1.intent: TX path zero-copy — Codec encodes directly into pool slot, link send-from-slot, DMA reads via prebuilt descriptor; pool slot in DMA-coherent SRAM.

9/9.2.intent: RX happy path zero-copy — DMA writes pre-programmed RX slot; codec parses in place; event emitted with slot borrow; slot returned to freelist.

9/9.3.intent: Stage-copy RX path for oversized/multi-DMA — one copy DMA-slot to stage; build-time fragmentation analysis; stage_copy_policy warn/error/forbid per machine.

9/9.4.intent: Pool placement across .dtcm/.sram1/.flash regions; per-pool placement declared in kind source; memory regions in deploy.yaml; linker fragment ties them.

9/9.5.intent: Platform-aware link substrate: 5-row matrix (MCU bare_metal, linux+epoll, linux+io_uring, QNX, etc) sharing pool FSM.

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-1-unic.intent: Unicast session FSM has eight states plus Closed terminal; splits Opening (initiator) and Accepting (acceptor) explicitly.
inputs_bullets: Init: created, link not yet open; entry from outbound or inbound
LinkOpening: outbound link driver attempting open (TCP connect / WS upgrade)
Scouting: active scout loop pre-target (mode=active deploys only)
Opening: initiator driving 4-way Init/Open handshake
Accepting: acceptor responding to remote-driven handshake
Established: handshake done, RX/TX regions enabled (sub-region container)
Closing: graceful close in progress; sends Close with reason
Closed: terminal, link released, pool slots freed

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-2-unic.intent: Unicast transitions — outbound (LinkOpening → Opening.SentInitSyn → GotInitAck → Established) + inbound (Accepting.AwaitingInitSyn → SentInitAck → SentOpenAck → Established).

Inbound: Init → Accepting.AwaitingInitSyn → SentInitAck → SentOpenAck → Established
Inbound entry guarded by half_open_cap_available + accept_rate_token (silent drop if denied)
Cookie validation guard: Accepting.SentInitAck → SentOpenAck rejects invalid/expired cookie
stateless_accept mode: AwaitingInitSyn→SentInitAck does not allocate FSM instance (cookie-only)
Framing errors → Closing(reason=INVALID); peer Close → Closed(peer-rejected)

TxSchedule: Idle / Batching / Flushing per (reliability, priority) band
Keepalive: Armed / Sending; timer = lease × keepalive_ratio (default 1/3)
LeaseMonitor: Healthy / Warning / Expired; warning at lease×2/3

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-4-clos.intent: Close paths from Established by trigger; six trigger types; Closing state has 100ms default timeout for Close-frame flush before link teardown.

TX congestion budget exhaust on RELIABLE batch → Closing(UNRESPONSIVE) → Closed

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/6-link-l.intent: 6 inbound link events + 3 outbound invocations. R52.1-R63 prototype: encode_init/encode_open/encode_close emit base body; transport-message header prepended by wz session_glue.

OpenSyn flags=T_OPEN_T per lease unit; OpenAck adds T_OPEN_A (0x20); T_MID_OPEN (0x02)

link.rx(bytes): pass to codec, codec emits recv(MsgType) events
link.tx_drained: TX pool slot freed → wake TxSchedule
link.backpressure(on|off): TX queue watermark crossed → TxSchedule pause/resume
link.framing_error: codec decode failed → Closing(INVALID)

Round 100.decision_summary: R100 promotes SubscriberRegistry from literal-only to zenoh chunk-wildcard matching (`*` single-chunk, `**` zero-or-more chunks) — production-realistic keyexpr semantics that closes R98 carry #3 and matches what real zenoh-pico subscribers use (`home/**`, `sensors/*/temp`).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs: `Subscriber.keyexpr_literal: String` replaced with `pattern_chunks: Vec<String>` pre-split on `/`. Registration eagerly splits the pattern so the hot dispatch path only re-borrows the slice as `&[&str]` per Push rather than reparsing per match.

New free function `keyexpr_pattern_matches(pattern_chunks: &[&str], target: &str) -> bool` implements the matcher as a two-cursor walk with a single `**` backtrack frame (mirrors standard glob-match algorithms; worst-case `O(|pattern| * |target|)` for single `**`, linear for the productive `home/**` / `sensors/*/temp` patterns).

`SubscriberRegistry::register` accepts `impl Into<String>` (unchanged signature) but reinterprets the argument as a zenoh chunk-wildcard pattern. Backward compatibility: a literal keyexpr like `"topic/a"` still matches itself because all chunks are literals — the existing R98/R99 tests continue to pass without modification.

`SubscriberRegistry::dispatch` walks subscribers and runs `keyexpr_pattern_matches(&chunks, suffix)` per registered pattern; non-zero `keyexpr.id` filtering preserved (DECLARE mapping still deferred).

Module-level doc updated to declare R100 scope: chunks split on `/`, `*` matches exactly one chunk, `**` matches zero or more chunks (incl. empty), literal chunks compare byte-for-byte, `$*` intra-chunk substring deferred until a consumer surfaces.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib pubsub: 12 passed — 6 pre-R100 tests stay green (literal patterns still match themselves) + 6 new wildcard tests cover literal-equality, single-chunk `*` (including the negative case where `*` does NOT collapse to zero), and `**` at prefix / middle / trailing positions plus the zero-chunks case.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --test session_fsm_drive_session r99_subscriber: still 1 passed — R99 integration test uses a literal pattern `"demo/topic"` so it stays unchanged.

scripts/run-ci.sh all 5 lanes pass: Layer A (validate-workspace), Layer B (verify-codegen), Layer C1 (cargo test), Layer C2 (cargo clippy -D warnings), Layer D (deploy yaml schema). Clippy clean first try.
Workspace tests: 134 → 140 (+6 = new wildcard matcher unit tests).
atomic ledger entries: 112 → 113 (this Round 100 entry).
T1=0 / RT 12/12 / GENERATED.md=sync preserved.
carry_forward_bullets: AP MVP demo binary — R98+R99+R100 cover the publisher → subscriber registry path with zenoh-realistic keyexpr matching. The next user-visible deliverable is a runnable Linux + tokio binary that opens a real TCP session against a zenoh-pico peer (or two wz peers), subscribes via the registry, and exercises the demo. Estimate 2-3 rounds for scaffolding + real-peer fixture + golden-path assertion.

`$*` intra-chunk substring wildcard — zenoh full keyexpr language includes patterns like `home/temp$*` matching `home/temperature`. Per-chunk pattern compilation needed (chunk-internal `$*` parsing + per-chunk match). Defer until a consumer surfaces; AP MVP typical patterns (`home/**` / `sensors/*/temp`) don't need it.

DECLARE codec (0x1E) — 9 declaration sub-types per zenoh-pico declarations.c, multi-round chain (~3 rounds like RESPONSE). Closure unblocks the mapping-id resolver on the registry so non-zero `wireexpr.id` Pushes route through resolved-base + suffix concatenation.

Symmetric dispatch for Reply / Err / Response — dispatch is Push-only. A future round adds the symmetric `NetworkMessage::Response` arm (`Response.body` peek-byte dispatches to reply / err; reply itself wraps a push_body so keyexpr matching passes through). Kind-filtered subscriptions (publish-only vs reply-also-accepted) are the textbook surface.

Layer 3 wire-interop tests — R90 / R91 carry. The wildcard matcher in R100 stays internally testable, but a wire-interop fixture against zenoh-pico's actual `_z_keyexpr_intersect_*` would prove cross-stack semantic compatibility. Estimate 1 round once the zenoh-pico-sys FFI surface exposes the keyexpr matcher symbols.

The zenoh-pico fixture patches three fields off zero-init to reach the wz default state: (1) `_qos._val = 5` matches `_Z_N_QOS_DEFAULT._val` so `has_qos_ext` evaluates false; (2) `_body._is_put = true` routes the union to the PUT branch (zero-init would pick DEL via `_is_put=false`); (3) `_key._mapping = 1` (non-LOCAL) prevents zenoh-pico's encoder from auto-setting the M flag.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_declare.rs new — 1 byte-equivalence test asserting `wz_codecs::declare::Declare::default().encode() == _z_declare_encode(default _z_n_msg_declare_t with 2 field patches)`. Wire bytes `[0x1E, 0x1A]` (envelope MID 0x1E with no flags + decl_final inner MID 0x1A).

Two-patch fixture: (1) `_ext_qos._val = 5` matches `_Z_N_QOS_DEFAULT._val` so `_z_declare_encode`'s `has_qos_ext` evaluates false and envelope Z stays clear; (2) `_decl._tag = 8 = _Z_DECL_FINAL` overrides zero-init's tag of 0 (= `_Z_DECL_KEXPR`) so the inner dispatch reaches `_z_decl_final_encode` (1 byte emit) instead of `_z_decl_kexpr_encode` (3 byte emit). The patch matches wz's R88 declared default arm `DeclareVariant default = CodecZenohDeclFinal`.

Tag-enum literal pinned to a `const Z_DECL_FINAL_TAG: u32 = 8;` rather than relying on bindgen's anonymous-enum surface naming. This keeps the test robust against bindgen pinning shifts (the `_Z_DECL_FINAL` ordinal is fixed by the upstream enum declaration order in declarations.h:97).

sources/codecs/ext_entry.scxml: `<sce:arm value="0x00" type="codec_zenoh_ext_unit"/>` → same arm + `default="true"`. Round 114.decision_summary: R114 closes the CI Layer B mismatch leak that R112 surfaced: a) the R88/R106/R108a wire-correctness improvements in msg_del/query/request (and the msg_put family member) are audit-traced as Deliberate Divergences from SCE upstream — same R44 pattern previously applied to init_body/join; b) LAYER2_KNOWN_DIVERGENCE list expanded to cover all 6 wz-side wire-correctness improvements; c) a sce-codegen freshness gate auto-rebuilds the binary when vendor/sce HEAD outpaces it, preventing the stale-binary path that let a green local pre-push push CI-red onto main.
changes_bullets: sources/codecs/msg_del.scxml header comment expanded — R44-pattern Deliberate Divergence block records the R88 mid `value="0x02"` baking, references the parent layer3 tests that anchor the bake, names the SCE PR carry (R114 KNOWN_DIVERGENCE), and preserves the original pre-R88 alignment claim for history.
sources/codecs/query.scxml header comment expanded — same shape: R88 mid `value="0x03"` baking + layer3_request.rs proof + SCE PR carry.

sources/codecs/request.scxml header comment expanded — three-divergence record: R108a mid `value="0x1C"` + R106 M=1 baking + R88 query-as-default-arm vs SCE fixture's msg_put-as-default-arm. Layer 3 proof at layer3_request.rs (R108b).

sources/codecs/msg_put.scxml header comment expanded — element-level identical to SCE upstream today but explicitly enrolled in the R88 family so a future SCE drift on msg_put is recognized as a regression. Also folds in the R114 GitHub Actions observation: msg_put can report backend-specific MISMATCH transiently without an element-level diff (defense-in-depth listing).

scripts/run-ci.sh `LAYER2_KNOWN_DIVERGENCE` array extended from `(init_body join)` to `(init_body join msg_del msg_put query request)`; per-entry rationale recorded in the comment block above the array.

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer B opens with a sce-codegen freshness check: compares vendor/sce HEAD `git log -1 --format=%ct` to the binary's `stat -c %Y`; if the binary is older, runs `scripts/build-sce.sh` automatically before continuing. The R112 -> R114 GitHub Actions failure traced exactly to this stale-binary path — binary mtime 2026-05-18 00:00 vs vendor pin checked out at R112 13:51. The gate eliminates that whole class of false-green pre-push results.
Log label fix: `audit-traced R44` was hard-coded for every KNOWN_DIVERGENCE entry; now reads `audit-traced KNOWN_DIVERGENCE` so the R88/R106/R108a-era divergences aren't misattributed to R44.
verification_bullets: scripts/run-ci.sh full sweep: 7 layers (0/A/A2/B/C1/C2/D) pass green. Layer B reports `msg_del/query/request L2 MISMATCH (audit-traced KNOWN_DIVERGENCE)` and continues, mirroring the init_body/join precedent. msg_put OK at the current pin.

Freshness gate verified by code inspection rather than negative testing (would require destroying the binary mid-run, which the harness avoids). The comparison logic: `bin_mtime_epoch -lt sce_head_epoch` triggers rebuild; both epochs fall back to 0 on stat/git error so the gate is no-op when state is unreadable rather than spuriously rebuilding.

Root cause analysis end-to-end: R112 bumped vendor/sce 189bf7f4 → 4d1ef3f2 (15 commits including the variant-default-uniformity parse-time enforcement series). The bump's wz-side break (ext_entry default arm) was caught + fixed in R112. The wz-side audit-traced wire-correctness improvements in msg_del/query/request from R88/R106/R108a were ALREADY divergent from SCE fixtures at that pin — but local pre-push hit a sce-codegen binary built BEFORE R112 (5月 18 00:00, pre-R112), which silently matched both sides through pre-R112 semantics. CI built sce-codegen fresh against the R112 pin and detected the audit-traced divergences as Layer 2 MISMATCH. The freshness gate ensures local and CI see the same emit logic going forward; KNOWN_DIVERGENCE makes the expected MISMATCHes non-fatal as the R44 precedent prescribed.
carry_forward_bullets: SCE upstream PR for the R88/R106/R108a divergences — add `value=` attributes to mid flags + M flag in codec_zenoh_msg_del / codec_zenoh_query / codec_zenoh_request, plus the default-arm marker swap in codec_zenoh_request (query as declared default vs msg_put). When SCE merges, the corresponding entries can be removed from LAYER2_KNOWN_DIVERGENCE. Same lifecycle as the R44 init_body/join PR carry.

Negative-test for the freshness gate — a future R<X> could add a dedicated test that touches a temp binary's mtime backward and asserts auto-rebuild fires. Not gating; R114 ships the gate logic with code-review verification.

Round 116.decision_summary: R116 bumps the SCE vendor pin from 4d1ef3f2 to 122f851d, adopting upstream commit fa3a2fda ("fix: route scheduler clock through Hal trait under std builds") which the watching-zenoh R115 carry-verification surfaced as a blocker for deterministic timer-driven testing under host CI; with the routing fix in place, wz authors TestHal in wz-runtime-tokio-test-support (process-global AtomicU64 backing) and adds the hal_timer_routing.rs integration test that exercises the substrate against the 4 SCXML delay values session_fsm_unicast.scxml uses (link.open_timeout=5s / init_ack.timeout=2s / open_ack.timeout=2s / closing.timeout=100ms), proving the wz consumer can now drive the SCE scheduler clock from a synthetic Hal under std builds for the first time.
changes_bullets: vendor/sce submodule pointer 4d1ef3f2 -> 122f851d (6 commits drift: 5b069ff9 / 76b71756 / a81cc368 / 4d54811c / fa3a2fda / 122f851d — the load-bearing change is fa3a2fda which unifies SchedTimePoint to u64 ms and routes sched_now/sched_now_plus through <P::Hal as Hal>::now_ticks_ms on both std and no_std; StdHal's Instant::now-backed now_ticks_ms keeps std production behavior byte-identical).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio-test-support/src/lib.rs adds the TestHal zero-sized type plus the test_hal_set_ticks / test_hal_advance_ticks / test_hal_now_ticks helpers; the implementation mirrors SCE's own hal_clock_routing.rs MockHal but lives in the test-support sibling crate so wz consumer tests can author Hal-mocked policies without re-publishing the AtomicU64 backing inside each test binary.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/hal_timer_routing.rs (NEW, 6 tests) — declares an in-test TimerProbePolicy whose `type Hal = TestHal`, anchors a fresh epoch via the helper, schedules a delayed event matching one of the session-fsm SCXML delay values, advances TestHal across ready_at, and asserts has_ready_events flips false->true at the exact synthetic tick. Coverage: 5s link.open_timeout (advance 4999 -> still pending, advance +2 -> ready), 2s init_ack.timeout (exact-equal Hal tick satisfies <=), 2s+2s sibling schedules with distinct send_ids (both ready), 100ms closing.timeout (millisecond resolution), Hal clock reset-backward path (event re-pends), public helper-vs-trait observable consistency.

crates/wz-integration-tests/Cargo.toml dev-deps add sce-rust-runtime path dep — only the test surface reaches into Engine / Hal / StatePolicy directly; production wz crates remain on sce-forge-runtime + generated Policy code.

hal_timer_routing.rs adds a process-binary-local Mutex<()> HAL_LOCK guarding every test fn so the multi-thread default of cargo test cannot race on the process-global TestHal AtomicU64. Poison recovery via PoisonError::into_inner keeps subsequent tests runnable after a panicked test — each test re-anchors at entry so the poisoned tick value is overwritten before any assertion reads it. The lock is the textbook fix for the failure observed during R116b authoring: 5x consecutive multi-thread runs surfaced one race in test 2/5, single-threaded baseline was 5/5 green; post-lock 8x multi-thread runs are all green.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: 159 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (was 153/0/1 in R115 baseline; +6 from hal_timer_routing.rs).

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test hal_timer_routing: 6/6 green under both single-thread (--test-threads=1) and the multi-thread default; 8 consecutive multi-thread runs all 6/6 confirm the HAL_LOCK serialization removed the AtomicU64 sequence race.

Round 121f.decision_summary: R121f lands wz initiator (dial) code path + role-agnostic publisher gate; closes the role-symmetry matrix (wz acceptor/initiator × wz subscriber/publisher) for the AP MVP pubsub demo.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs — new Role enum (Acceptor{listen:String} | Initiator{connect:String}) for argv-driven role select; --connect <addr> flag added (mutually exclusive with --listen); print_usage refreshed for the (--listen | --connect) shape; argv-validation matrix rejects both-set / neither-set / --publish-without-value etc. with exit code 2; demo_session_init_params signature shifts from () to (&Role), keeping whatami=Peer(0x02) on the Acceptor branch (R121b/c/d/e baseline preserved) and shifting to whatami=Client(0x04) on the Initiator branch (zenoh-pico's well-tested handshake shape is Client → Peer/Router; peer-peer over TCP unicast without prior multicast scouting is fragile in 1.5.0).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs run_demo signature shifts: now takes Role instead of String listen. Step 1 TCP setup is role-conditional (TcpListener::bind+accept for Acceptor, TcpStream::connect for Initiator) but lands at the same TcpStream value. Step 4b FSM role-start is role-conditional: Acceptor dispatches InboundStart (R121d baseline); Initiator dispatches OutboundStart + LinkOpened in sequence (mirrors R60 session_fsm_real_tcp.rs::r60_fsm_drives_real_tcp_loopback pattern) so the FSM lands in SentInitSyn with send_init_syn already fired. tokio::net::TcpStream import added.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs publisher_task gate refactor — polls actions.trace_snapshot().record_established_at > 0 instead of send_open_ack > 0. record_established_at is the role-agnostic Established.onentry counter (fires on both acceptor send_open_ack → Established AND initiator OpenAckReceived → Established transitions). The R121e gate was acceptor-only by accident; R121f generalizes without role-aware branching. Doc comment + diagnostic log message updated.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs InboundReadDriver.poll_event — hex-dump diagnostic log at log::debug! level (`inbound frame len={N} bytes={hex array}`). Fires per inbound frame; visible only with RUST_LOG=debug. R121f authoring needed it to diagnose the wz-initiator → zenoh-pico peer-mode-listener failure mode (no inbound bytes ever reach wz — zenoh-pico closes the TCP connection silently); kept at debug so RUST_LOG=info production runs stay quiet.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor.rs new — R121f hard-gate test. Spawns two wz-ap-demo instances: first as --listen <addr> --key demo/** (acceptor + subscriber), then as --connect <addr> --publish demo/test --value hello-from-wz-initiator (initiator + publisher). Three-stage wait: (i) acceptor 'listening on' — bind succeeded; (ii) initiator 'connected to' — dial succeeded; (iii) acceptor 'SUBSCRIBER FIRED' — full handshake + publisher_task emit + pubsub resolver fired. Belt-and-suspenders assertions on keyexpr='demo/test' + wireexpr_id=0 substrings so a regression on either wire path or DECLARE-alias drift localises. Foreign-interop wz initiator → zenoh-pico peer-mode test deferred (carry) — file header documents the rationale (zenoh-pico 1.5.0 peer-listen does not reply to Client-whatami InitSyn; verified empirically during R121f authoring via debug hex dump showing zero inbound bytes in a 10s window).

Single build/link step keeps the lane timing predictable; lane count remains at 8.

Wire-trace evidence (R121f initiator → zenoh-pico peer-listen failure mode — known carry): RUST_LOG=debug run shows 'connected to 127.0.0.1:<port>' (TCP dial succeeds), 'driving session FSM' (engine starts), then ActionTrace { link_driver_open: 1, send_init_syn: 1, send_open_syn: 0, send_close_frame_with_reason: 1, close_reason: Invalid, record_established_at: 0 }. NO 'inbound frame' debug line surfaced in 10s — zenoh-pico's peer-mode listen accepts the TCP socket but never sends back any session-handshake bytes. Foreign-interop on the initiator side needs a Zenoh router binary or zenoh-pico CLI patch; carried for R121f1 / R121g.

Manual whatami sanity: demo_session_init_params(&Role::Acceptor{..}).whatami == 0x02 (Peer, R121b/c/d/e); demo_session_init_params(&Role::Initiator{..}).whatami == 0x04 (Client). Round 121h.decision_summary: R121h replaces the hand-rolled u16 LE length-prefix framing in TcpDriver::send and TcpDriver::poll_event with calls into the generated wz_codecs::stream_envelope::StreamEnvelope encoder/decoder, lands a 5-vector byte-compare regression test against the zenoh-pico _z_link_send_t_msg reference (including the 256-byte multi-byte-length critical case), and removes the last hand-rolled wire-framing site from the AP tokio runtime.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs imports: add `sce_forge_runtime::codec::SceCursor` and `wz_codecs::stream_envelope::StreamEnvelope`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs TcpDriver doc comment rewritten: removes the R121d-era `framing remains hand-rolled` deferral note and replaces it with the R121h SSOT statement plus a rationale paragraph for the 2-byte prefix sniff at the start of poll_event (until SCE exposes a codec MIN_FRAME_BYTES associated const, the wire-shape requires this read before the structural decode can run).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs TcpDriver::send (lines 160-181): replaces the `len.to_le_bytes()` + two `write_all` pair with a single StreamEnvelope construction + encode + write_all. Behaviour is byte-identical to the prior path (verified by R121h byte-compare test); the codec catalog now owns the wire-shape.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs TcpDriver::poll_event (lines 191-224): two-step read pattern. First reads the 2-byte prefix raw (sized by the codec's min_frame_bytes), then sizes a frame buffer to `2 + payload_len` from the LE-decoded prefix, reads the payload tail into `frame[2..]`, and decodes the full frame through `StreamEnvelope::decode` for SSOT byte interpretation. The codec validates the structural decode; the manual prefix sniff is a bounded duplication of `min_frame_bytes=2` documented in the call-site comment.

crates/wz-codecs/tests/smoke.rs: new `stream_envelope_wire_bytes_match_zenoh_pico_reference` test exercising 5 vectors (empty payload, 3-byte payload, 255-byte boundary, 256-byte boundary, 300-byte payload). The 256-byte case locks the multi-byte length regression that the pre-R121h-pre2 SCE simple-path decode silently truncated to `raw[0] = 0x00`; the post-let-binding decode now reconstructs the full u16 through the named local and the test catches any future regression. Three small expected-wire helpers `expected_wire_255`/`256`/`300` build the reference byte sequences inline.

Round 121h-perf-bump-1-study.decision_summary: R121h-perf-bump-1 reduced to a study round: empirical impact survey shows the prior session's 3-phase carry is infeasible because partial SCXML migration breaks the build at every intermediate state, so the carry is revised from 3-phase to 2-phase (atomic bump+migrate, then TcpDriver hot path).
changes_bullets: No wz src or vendor changes this round. Study-only entry; the audit trail captures the revised migration plan so the next session can execute against a verified scope rather than the prior session's misdiagnosed 3-[REDACTED].

Empirical scope: 12 wz SCXML files use the legacy `<sce:requires-parent-flags>` element and/or `parent.X` predicate (prior session estimate was 11). The 12: init_body, open_body, hello, join, push, request, interest_body, timestamp, decl_kexpr, decl_subscriber, decl_queryable, decl_token, wireexpr, wireexpr_local, wireexpr_nonlocal (correction: actually 15 files surface in grep but decl_kexpr / decl_token / wireexpr / wireexpr_local / wireexpr_nonlocal grouping needs per-file checks during the migration round; the 12 = files with non-zero RPF blocks OR non-comment parent.X predicates).

Partial migration is infeasible. SCE Phase D2+D3+D4 (commit 19b0fcf0) deletes the legacy RPF mechanism + `<sce:requires-parent-flags>` XSD element entirely. The new grammar (`<sce:flag-inputs>` / `<sce:flag-bind>` from Phase A 36c0750e + Phase B 63daab97 codegen wire-up) is rejected by the current vendor pin 54d513af. There is no overlap window where both grammars parse; the bump and the 12-file migration must land in one commit.

Migration pattern reference (SCE Phase C bf41498c migrated 19 conformance fixtures with this exact pattern). Old form on a leaf consumer: `<sce:requires-parent-flags carrier="header"><sce:flag name="S" bit="6"/></sce:requires-parent-flags>` + `sce:present-if="parent.S"` on gated fields. New form: `<sce:flag-inputs><sce:flag-input name="S" width="1"/></sce:flag-inputs>` + `sce:present-if="S"` (no `parent.` prefix; SCE Phase B snake_cases the identifier for the typed encode/decode parameter so uppercase leaf flag names retain their literal form). Parent importers add `<sce:flag-bind input="S" source="S"/>` as a child of the `<sce:import>` element to wire each declared input to a source flag (dotted carrier.flag form or chain-forwarder bare-name form).

init_body.scxml-shaped example (the smallest migration in the 12): drop the RPF block declaring `S`(bit=6) and `A`(bit=5) on carrier=header; add `<sce:flag-inputs>` with `<sce:flag-input name="S" width="1"/>` and `<sce:flag-input name="A" width="1"/>`; rewrite the 4 `parent.S` predicates to `S` and the 2 `parent.A` predicates to `A`. init_body is NOT imported by any wz SCXML (wz constructs the transport envelope in Rust runtime), so no parent flag-bind is needed.

Variant-dispatcher cases (wireexpr.scxml + wireexpr_local.scxml + wireexpr_nonlocal.scxml): Phase D1 b8f86b46 added variant arm flag-bind threading codegen — the dispatcher's `<sce:import>` of each arm body now needs the same `<sce:flag-bind>` wire-up as a regular consumer. wireexpr.scxml has the variant-dispatch + RPF combination; the migration needs care to preserve the B5-ν chain-forwarding (parent.N gates the suffix in each arm body, threaded through the dispatcher's flag-bind to the arm's flag-inputs).

Encoder API impact after vendor bump (separate from SCXML grammar). SCE B1-α series (cb1b40b7 / 4eafcc7b / e01aac02 / 35998fd7 / 100a2ca0 / de5d5e9a) introduced `SceSink` trait + `SliceSink<&mut [u8]>` + `VecSink<&mut Vec<u8>>` + an `encode_to_vec()` feature-gated wrapper. The `*.encode()` zero-arg method that wz callers rely on is replaced. Mechanical drop-in: rename to `*.encode_to_vec()` (alloc feature on by default for std builds). Hot-path sink-based migration (TcpDriver) is a separate concern. ~10+ wz call-sites need the rename.
verification_bullets: Impact count gathered via `grep -l 'requires-parent-flags|parent\.[A-Za-z_]' sources/codecs/*.scxml` (15 files surfaced) and a follow-up per-file count of non-zero RPF blocks + non-comment `parent.X` predicates (12 files actually need migration; the 3 comment-only ones are not at risk).

SCE Phase C migration pattern verified by reading the diff at SCE commit bf41498c (tests/forge/resources/codec_init_syn_body.scxml + codec_zenoh_decl_subscriber.scxml). Both files showed the same RPF → flag-inputs / parent.X → X / import flag-bind addition pattern.

Coexistence-window check: SCE Phase A (36c0750e) commit body states `legacy RPF + parent.X predicate paths coexist during Phase A pending later atomic`. SCE Phase D2+D3+D4 (19b0fcf0) commit body states `Removes RequiresParentFlags struct + CodecModel field + PresentIfScope::Parent variant + ... XSD drops <sce:requires-parent-flags> element`. The current SCE main HEAD is post-D2 (de5d5e9a), so the coexistence window has closed. No vendor pin between A and D2 is reachable because SCE main is now past D2; the only safe target is HEAD (de5d5e9a).

No wz src changes → no test surface to verify. The next round's verification surface is `bash scripts/run-ci.sh` 8 lanes (especially Layer B verify-codegen.sh and Layer E ap_demo_round_trip 5-test bundle).
carry_forward_bullets: Revised R121h-perf-bump scope (replaces the 3-phase carry from R121h-perf-bump-attempt). Round 121h-perf-bump-2 (atomic): vendor pin 54d513af -> de5d5e9a + all 12 SCXML migrate (init_body + open_body + hello + join + push + request + interest_body + timestamp + decl_subscriber + decl_queryable + decl_token + wireexpr trio) + `*.encode()` -> `*.encode_to_vec()` mass rename + 8-lane CI pass + 14 byte-compare invariants preserved. Round 121h-perf-bump-3 (refinement): TcpDriver / hot path sink-based migration to consume `SliceSink<&mut [u8]>` directly, retire the `.to_vec()` + extend pattern flagged at R121g.

Migration order recommendation for R121h-perf-bump-2: start with the simplest leaves (init_body, open_body, timestamp — single-flag RPFs with no variant-dispatch), validate each via `cargo check` at the new vendor pin, then handle the variant-dispatcher cluster (wireexpr.scxml + wireexpr_local + wireexpr_nonlocal) which needs flag-bind threading. Decl_* family last (they import wireexpr and inherit the wire-up from the dispatcher fix).

Inventory hazard for R121h-perf-bump-2: per-leaf input narrowing per SCE Phase C convention (`declared inputs narrowed to actually-used flags`). E.g. decl_subscriber's RPF declared N/M/Z but only N is actually consumed by the leaf body; M became codegen-derived (B5-ν variant dispatch), Z is unused. Each wz SCXML migration needs the same narrowing audit — trust grep-confirmed predicate usage as the authoritative input list, not the RPF block's flag count.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_undeclare_kexpr(mapping_id) builder added: emits [header(_Z_UNDECL_KEXPR_MID=0x01), VLE(mapping_id)] mirroring zenoh-pico _z_undecl_kexpr_encode at declarations.c:86-89. No wireexpr body, no Z ext surface (unlike the other three Undecl_* variants); the retraction is purely id-based because the peer already has the (id -> keyexpr) entry from a prior DeclKexpr.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_undeclare_subscriber / build_undeclare_queryable / build_undeclare_token builders added: each emits [header(MID 0x03/0x05/0x07), VLE(id)] mirroring _z_undecl_subscriber_encode / _z_undecl_queryable_encode / _z_undecl_token_encode at declarations.c:90-130 with has_keyexpr_ext=false. AP MVP scope: the wz codec for these does not model the optional _z_decl_ext_keyexpr_encode tail (declarations.c:38-50) — SCXML stops at id. Future router cross-validation paths that need the ext_keyexpr surface extend sources/codecs/undecl_*.scxml + add _with_keyexpr builders; the no-ext contract here stays byte-stable.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_declare_final() builder added: single-byte marker (header=_Z_DECL_FINAL_MID=0x1A) per _z_decl_final_encode at declarations.c:131-135. No body, no id, no ext — the full wire is exactly 2 bytes (N_MID_DECLARE envelope + DeclFinal.header). Reserved for the future Interest/Reply path (R121j+) that needs to close multi-DECLARE reply batches; the unsolicited DECLARE outbound path the AP MVP uses today does not emit DeclFinal.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs SessionLinkActions: 5 new send_* actions added — send_undeclare_kexpr / send_undeclare_subscriber / send_undeclare_queryable / send_undeclare_token / send_declare_final. All hard-coded to the reliable channel for the same SN-window ordering reason as the DECLARE outbound path: the peer must observe the retraction before any later Push that still aliases the retracted id, otherwise the peer dispatches to the stale entry.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs tests: 5 new unit tests covering the 5 builders. build_undeclare_{kexpr,subscriber,queryable,token}_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes each lock 2 vectors: id=42 (single-byte VLE) + id=200 (multi-byte VLE boundary, encodes as 0xC8 0x01 — the 7-bit VLE boundary). build_declare_final_emits_two_byte_marker pins the stateless [0x1E, 0x1A] shape. Each test also includes an inner-arm sanity check so a future codegen drift on the DeclareVariant arm dispatch surfaces immediately.

Same `(id, mapping_id, suffix)` signature as the Local-arm builders; inner `Wireexpr` arm flipped to `WireexprNonlocal`; codegen-derived M bit (0x00 vs Local's 0x40 — verified at `wz-codecs-*/out/decl_subscriber.rs` line 134's `_derived_header` match). `build_declare_kexpr` deliberately has no Nonlocal companion — DeclKexpr's encoder-perspective locality is by construction Local (sender installs the (id, literal) pair into its OWN mapping table).

Each `_nonlocal` builder panics on `keyexpr_mapping_id == 0` mirroring `build_declare_kexpr_rejects_zero_mapping_id`. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs imports: replace `use wz_codecs::request::Request;` with `use wz_codecs::request::{Request, RequestVariant};` (the variant enum is needed by the builder) and add `use wz_codecs::query::Query;` for the inner body type.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_request_query(rid, keyexpr_mapping_id, keyexpr_suffix) builder added next to build_declare_final. Emits the minimal AP MVP shape: Request.header = _Z_MID_N_REQUEST(0x1C) | optional N(0x20) suffix gate, with M(0x40) codegen-derived from the WireexprLocal arm via the same <sce:variant-dispatch flag=header.M> mechanism the DECLARE builders use. Inner Query.header = _Z_MID_Z_QUERY(0x03) only — no C(consolidation) / P(params) / Z(exts) flags. Doc comment enumerates the three layered follow-up helpers (build_request_query_with_consolidation / _with_parameters / _with_exts) that future rounds will add.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs encode_frame_with_request(sn, request, reliable) helper added: composes the one transport-envelope header byte that lives outside the body codec's scope (parent_flags | T_MID_FRAME) with Frame {sn, payload: request.encode()}.encode() body. Mirror of encode_frame_with_push (R121e) and encode_frame_with_declare (R121g); the reliable-channel default matches the DECLARE outbound contract (SN-window ordering ensures the peer sees the Query before any Response/ResponseFinal that depends on the rid).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs SessionLinkActions::send_request_query(rid, mapping_id, suffix) action added: build_request_query -> next_outbound_frame_sn -> encode_frame_with_request -> driver.send_blocking(Reliable). Same SN-window ordering reason as the DECLARE outbound path; unreliable Query is unsupported by this minimal builder because the local z_get future would hang on a dropped Query.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `pub enum ConsolidationMode { None, Monotonic, Latest }` mirroring zenoh-pico's `z_consolidation_mode_t` (constants.h:185-187) for the three transmitted values. `Z_CONSOLIDATION_MODE_AUTO = -1` is intentionally NOT representable since zenoh-pico's encoder treats AUTO as the `do not transmit` sentinel — callers wanting that case use plain `build_request_query`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `ConsolidationMode::wire_byte(self) -> u8` const fn returning 0/1/2 per the zenoh-pico enum integer values. Const-fn so the mapping is verifiable at compile time.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_consolidation(rid, mapping_id, suffix, consolidation)`. Built on top of `build_request_query` (calls it then mutates the inner `Query` body via the `RequestVariant::CodecZenohQuery` arm match): ORs Q_C(0x20) into `Query.header` and sets `Query.consolidation = Some(consolidation.wire_byte())`. The 1-byte consolidation field then emits at offset 4 of the Request wire shape (after the existing 4-byte minimal-shape prefix). No params, no exts — those are separate layered helpers (R121j-1b/c/d carry).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two unit tests. `build_request_query_with_consolidation_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes` byte-compare-locks the three modes (alias case, mapping_id=7, no suffix): NONE → 0x5C 0x2A 0x07 0x23 0x00; MONOTONIC → ...0x23 0x01; LATEST → ...0x23 0x02. The 0x23 = MID(0x03) | Q_C(0x20) replaces the minimal-shape 0x03. `consolidation_mode_wire_byte_matches_zenoh_pico_enum_values` independently locks the enum-to-byte mapping so a refactor of the const fn without an encoder change still catches the regression.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `ConsolidationMode::wire_byte(self) -> u8` const fn returning 0/1/2 per the zenoh-pico enum integer values. Const-fn so the mapping is verifiable at compile time.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_consolidation(rid, mapping_id, suffix, consolidation)`. Built on top of `build_request_query` (calls it then mutates the inner `Query` body via the `RequestVariant::CodecZenohQuery` arm match): ORs Q_C(0x20) into `Query.header` and sets `Query.consolidation = Some(consolidation.wire_byte())`. The 1-byte consolidation field then emits at offset 4 of the Request wire shape (after the existing 4-byte minimal-shape prefix). No params, no exts — those are separate layered helpers (R121j-1b/c/d carry).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two unit tests. `build_request_query_with_consolidation_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes` byte-compare-locks the three modes (alias case, mapping_id=7, no suffix): NONE → 0x5C 0x2A 0x07 0x23 0x00; MONOTONIC → ...0x23 0x01; LATEST → ...0x23 0x02. The 0x23 = MID(0x03) | Q_C(0x20) replaces the minimal-shape 0x03. `consolidation_mode_wire_byte_matches_zenoh_pico_enum_values` independently locks the enum-to-byte mapping so a refactor of the const fn without an encoder change still catches the regression.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `pub const REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN: usize = 256` mirroring sources/codecs/query.scxml's `sce:max-size="256"` on the parameters field.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_parameters(rid, mapping_id, suffix, params)`. Built on top of `build_request_query` (same one-shot composition pattern as R121j-1a): ORs Q_P(0x40) into `Query.header`, sets `parameters_len = Some(params.len() as u64)` and `parameters = Some(params.to_vec())`. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two assertion gates. `assert!(!params.is_empty(), ...)` rejects the empty-slice case (zenoh-pico's `has_params` predicate at message.c:398 is `_z_slice_check && len > 0`, so an empty slice would silently clear Q_P and emit no params — the caller's intent is then `build_request_query` no-params). `assert!(params.len() <= REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN, ...)` rejects oversize at the call site rather than at the peer's decoder.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added three unit tests in the `tests` mod. Byte-compare locks small-params (k=v) + multi-byte VLE boundary (params_len=128 → 0x80 0x01) + max-size (256-byte payload → VLE 0x80 0x02). Two `#[should_panic]` tests guard the empty-slice and over-max rejections.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_attachment(rid, mapping_id, suffix, attachment)`. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two assertion gates. Empty attachment rejected (zenoh-pico's `_z_msg_query_required_extensions` only sets attachment requirement on non-empty bytes — the empty case is functionally `build_request_query` with no ext). Oversize rejected at QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN=32 to surface the wz codec bound at the call site rather than as a runtime decoder error.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added three unit tests in the `tests` mod. Byte-compare locks small attachment (b"hi") + at-max (32-byte sequence 0..32). AP MVP client-side z_get does not need either; both are router/queryable surfaces.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_timeout_ms(rid, mapping_id, suffix, timeout_ms)`. One-shot pattern mirroring R121j-1a/1b/1c: calls `build_request_query` then mutates Request to set the Request-level N_Z flag (0x80, the network-message-layer extensions chain present bit at request.scxml's `<sce:flag name="Z" bit="7"/>`) and append a single ExtEntry with header=`ENC_ZINT(0x20)|id_timeout(0x06)=0x26` and ExtZint body. M=0 (timeout is informational — the peer may ignore without breaking query semantics; matches zenoh-pico network.c:152 emitting no M, unlike target ext at line 140 which DOES set M).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — doc comment clarifies the two distinct Z bits at two layers (Request.header.Z gates Request-level tlv-chain; ExtEntry.header.Z is the per-entry chain-continuation marker). For single-ext, only the former is set; the latter stays clear. Same shape pattern applies to R121j-1c's Q-level ext chain (Query.header.Z + entry-Z).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — assertion gate: `timeout_ms != 0` rejected. zenoh-pico's encoder predicate at vendor/zenoh-pico/src/protocol/definitions/network.c:29 is `ext_timeout_ms = msg->_ext_timeout_ms != 0`, so a zero value silently clears the ext from the wire — the helper surfaces this as a panic at the call site rather than letting the caller think their timeout is being honored.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two unit tests. Byte-compare locks single-byte VLE (timeout=50ms → 0x32), multi-byte VLE boundary (timeout=1000ms → 0xE8 0x07), and large VLE (timeout=2^32 ms → 5-byte VLE `0x80 0x80 0x80 0x80 0x10`). One panic-rejection test guards the timeout_ms=0 case. Inner-arm sanity verifies the Request-level Extensions vec, the ExtEntry.header byte, and the ExtZint.value independently — Query body stays minimal (no Q_C / Q_P / Q_Z).

Scope-deferred (audit-traced carry): four other Request-level exts. QoS (ext_id=0x01, ZINT u64, no M): priority + congestion-control + reliability packed into one zint per zenoh-pico session-level helper. Timestamp (ext_id=0x02, ZBUF, no M): timestamp_t struct (zid+time pair). Target (ext_id=0x04, ZINT, M=1!): query target enum (BestMatching / All / AllComplete). Budget (ext_id=0x05, ZINT u64, no M): max replies count. Each follows R121j-1d's pattern with appropriate ENC and ext_id; target's M=1 means the peer MUST handle it or fail the frame.

Open Request-level ext sub-helpers carry (lower priority, AP MVP client rarely needs them): `build_request_query_with_target(rid, mid, suf, target_enum)` (M=1!), `_with_qos(rid, mid, suf, qos_packed_u64)`, `_with_budget(rid, mid, suf, max_replies)`, `_with_timestamp(rid, mid, suf, timestamp_t)`. Each follows R121j-1d's pattern. Target is the only mandatory ext (M=1 at network.c:140) — routers may reject queries that omit it for cross-network forwarding.

Both are router/queryable-side surfaces, not AP MVP client needs.

Round 121j-2a.decision_summary: R121j-2a introduces the RequestQueryBuilder fluent composition pattern that unifies the 5 one-shot Query helpers (R121j-1a/1b/1c/1d/1e) and unlocks multi-layer composition the one-shots could not express; existing helper signatures unchanged.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `pub struct RequestQueryBuilder` with per-layer Option fields (consolidation / parameters / query_attachment / request_target / request_timeout_ms). Fluent setters validate per-call (panic on empty / oversize / zero per the corresponding zenoh-pico encoder predicates). `.build()` materialises the Request, applying Query-layer settings to the inner Query body and assembling Request-level extensions in zenoh-pico's emit order (target before timeout per network.c:122-167) with Z chain-continuation bits set on every entry except the last.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — refactored 5 one-shot helpers into thin builder wrappers: `build_request_query_with_consolidation` / `_with_parameters` / `_with_attachment` / `_with_timeout_ms` / `_with_target`. Each is now a 3-line `RequestQueryBuilder::new(…).<setter>(…).build()` chain. Public signatures unchanged — callers see the same surface; internal implementation now goes through the builder, eliminating ~150 lines of duplicated Query mutation boilerplate.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — panic message body moved from the helper to the builder setter (e.g. `RequestQueryBuilder::parameters requires a non-empty params slice` replaces `build_request_query_with_parameters requires a non-empty params slice`). The three pre-existing `#[should_panic]` rejection tests were updated to match the new substring; behaviour (panic-on-bad-input) is identical and the max-size tests' panic strings stayed verbatim (`exceeds wz Query codec's max-size (256)` etc.) so those tests required no edits.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added four new tests in the `tests` mod. `request_query_builder_composes_consolidation_and_parameters` verifies two Query-layer settings combined (the multi-layer case one-shot helpers cannot express). `request_query_builder_composes_all_five_layers` is the full-stack regression: it locks the wire shape with consolidation+parameters+attachment+target+timeout combined, verifies Request-level ext ordering (target → timeout), Z chain bit on the target ext, all three Q-flag bits set together, and the Q-attachment ext positioning. Two `#[should_panic]` tests guard the builder's per-setter validation directly.

Layer C2 equivalent: `cargo clippy -p wz-runtime-tokio --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
carry_forward_bullets: R121j-2a closes the composition gap noted in every prior Q-helper entry (R121j-1b/1c/1d/1e all carried it forward). Future Request-level ext sub-helpers (qos / budget / timestamp) add as `.request_qos(...)` / `.request_budget(...)` / `.request_timestamp(...)` setters on the builder + matching one-shot helpers as thin wrappers. The textbook function-count growth is now bounded — each new layer is one setter, not one helper duplication.

Currently Response/Reply has only literal/aliased variants (no layered exts), so the function count there is still 4 helpers — below the builder threshold. The carry triggers when Reply consolidation / responder / del-body / Err encoding sub-helpers land.

Recommended next session focus once perf-bump unblocks or independently.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `use wz_codecs::reply::{Reply, ReplyVariant};` and updated `use wz_codecs::response::Response` to `use wz_codecs::response::{Response, ResponseVariant};` (the variant enum was needed for the inner-arm construction).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_response_reply_literal(request_id, keyexpr_suffix, payload)` for literal-keyexpr replies (id=0 + suffix). Wire shape: Response.header = MID(0x1B)|N(0x20)|M(0x40 codegen-derived), VLE(rid), wireexpr Local, Reply.header(0x04), MsgPut.header(0x01), VLE(payload_len), payload. No Response-level exts, no Reply consolidation, no Reply exts, no MsgPut T/E/Z gates. Empty suffix rejected (literal shape's purpose is inline keyexpr).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_response_reply_aliased(request_id, mapping_id, suffix: Option<&str>, payload)` for peer-declared-mapping replies. Convention matches the DECLARE/Request builders ((N,None) pure alias / (N,Some) compound). Panics on mapping_id=0 (literal-sentinel inversion); use the _literal variant for that case.

Round 121j-3c.decision_summary: R121j-3c .responder(zid, eid) on both Reply+Err builders: envelope-level ExtZbuf ext (id 0x03) on Response.extensions per zenoh-pico network.c:281-291. +7 lib tests.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs ResponseReplyBuilder and ResponseErrBuilder each gain a new responder: Option<(Vec<u8>, u32)> field plus a chainable setter pub fn responder(self, zid: &[u8], eid: u32). Both setters share the same 1..=16 zid-len assertion (zenoh-pico ZenohId wire constraint, transport.h:31-37). The two builders intentionally carry their own copy (rather than a shared trait) because their inner-body invariants differ; the symmetry is on the wire, not on the Rust type.

Both build() bodies grow an envelope-level emit step after the inner-body if-let. When responder is set, response.header |= 0x80 (_Z_FLAG_Z_Z on the Response envelope) and response.extensions = Some(vec![ExtEntry { header: 0x40 | 0x03, body: ExtZbuf { value_len, value } }]) where value = encode_responder_ext_body(&zid, eid). Sole-entry shape (no Z chain-continuation bit); future qos / tstamp envelope exts will plumb chain bits via the same iter-and-set-Z idiom used in RequestQueryBuilder.build at session_glue.rs:2772-2782.

New module-scope helper encode_responder_ext_body(zid: &[u8], eid: u32) -> Vec<u8>: pushes ((zid_len - 1) << 4) leading byte + raw zid + VLE(eid). Reuses encode_vle_u64_into (R121j-4b). Distinct from encode_source_info_ext_body in that no sn trailer is emitted (responder identifies the entity; source_info identifies the entity + per-source sequence position). Capacity = 1 + zid.len() + 5 worst-case VLE u32.

ResponseReplyBuilder docstring updated: prior wording listed Reply source_info as future sub-round R121j-3b without qualifying that it would be Reply-LEVEL ext. The new docstring records R121j-3b retraction (Reply body has no extensions chain per zenoh-pico _z_reply_encode message.c:507-519) and R121j-3c realization. ResponseErrBuilder docstring extended with the same R121j-3c note and an explicit cross-reference to network.c:281-291 documenting that responder applies symmetrically to Reply and Err inner bodies.

No changes to one-shot encode_frame_with_response* helpers or to build_response_reply/err_aliased/literal baselines; the additive shape preserves all R121j-2b / R121j-3d / R121j-4a / R121j-4b wire contracts. response_reply_builder_no_setters_matches_aliased_baseline + response_err_builder_no_setters_matches_aliased_baseline still pass.

Mirror R121j-3 Reply builders with `ResponseVariant::CodecZenohErr(Err)` arm instead of `CodecZenohReply(Reply)`. Structural difference from Reply documented: Reply wraps a MsgPut which itself carries a MID byte (0x01) before its own payload_len/payload pair, so a literal Response(Reply) wire ends with `[Reply.header(0x04), MsgPut.header(0x01), payload_len, payload]`. changes_bullets: R121j-4c (ResponseErrBuilder.attachment): RETRACTED. zenoh-pico _z_err_encode at src/protocol/codec/message.c:545-573 encodes only encoding (via _Z_FLAG_Z_E_E header bit) and source_info ext (_Z_MSG_EXT_ENC_ZBUF | 0x01). changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs ResponseErrBuilder gains a new source_info: Option<(Vec<u8>, u32, u32)> field and the chainable setter pub fn source_info(self, zid: &[u8], eid: u32, sn: u32). The setter asserts (1..=16).contains(&zid.len()) per the zenoh-pico ZenohId wire constraint at transport.h:31-37; defence-in-depth assert is repeated inside encode_source_info_ext_body so future direct helper callers cannot smuggle invalid lengths past the public boundary.

build() extends the CodecZenohErr arm: when source_info is set, err.header |= 0x80 (_Z_FLAG_Z_Z) and err.extensions = Some(vec![ExtEntry { header: 0x40 | 0x01, body: ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf(ExtZbuf { value_len, value }) }]) where value = encode_source_info_ext_body(&zid, eid, sn). Sole-entry shape (no Z chain-continuation bit) matches zenoh-pico _z_err_encode at message.c:545-573 which emits source_info as the only ext-chain element; future Err exts (if any) will plumb the chain bits via the same iter-and-set-Z idiom used in RequestQueryBuilder.build at session_glue.rs:2772-2782.

New module-scope helper encode_source_info_ext_body(zid: &[u8], eid: u32, sn: u32) -> Vec<u8> at session_glue.rs builds the ExtZbuf value body: pushes ((zid_len - 1) << 4) as the leading byte, then the raw zid bytes, then VLE(eid) and VLE(sn). Capacity pre-reserved = 1 + zid.len() + 5 + 5 to fit the worst-case VLE u32 length pair. Wire layout exactly matches zenoh-pico _z_source_info_encode_ext at message.c:243-254 (whose `zsize(ext_size)` length prefix is supplied by the surrounding ExtZbuf codec's value_len field).

New module-scope helper encode_vle_u64_into(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) emits a base-128 zint into a Vec<u8>. Free-function shape (no SceSink) because the source_info ext body is constructed before any SceSink is in scope: the body lives inside ExtZbuf.value and the surrounding ext codec sees only the already-built Vec<u8>. Mirrors the inline VLE loop in encode_frame_envelope (session_glue.rs:3663-3669) and zenoh-pico _z_zsize_encode at src/protocol/codec/core.c.

Wire-shape pinned independently of the builder: encode_source_info_ext_body_matches_zenoh_pico_layout asserts that source_info(zid=[0xDE,0xAD], eid=128, sn=16384) yields [0x10, 0xDE, 0xAD, 0x80, 0x01, 0x80, 0x80, 0x01] — leading byte (2-1)<<4 = 0x10, raw zid, VLE(128) = 0x80 0x01, VLE(16384) = 0x80 0x80 0x01. Verified Request::decode already complete via SCE codegen at crates/target/debug/build/wz-codecs-*/out/request.rs:97-147 — 1:1 with zenoh-pico _z_request_decode (network.c:209-238): rid(VLE) + keyexpr(N/M flag) + extensions(Z flag, ExtEntry chain capacity 4) + 4-variant body dispatch (MsgPut/MsgDel/Query/Default).

Verified parse_frame_payload at crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs:4172 already emits NetworkMessage::Request(Box<Request>) from Frame.payload bytes — the silent gap is *not* parser absence but downstream dispatch absence.

Silent gap identified: registry.dispatch arms at crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs:278-282 cover only NetworkMessage::Push (dispatch_push) and NetworkMessage::Declare (absorb_declare). Request/Response/ResponseFinal/Interest/Oam variants fall through silently with no panic or trace.

Design decision A — location: QueryableTable lives in a new crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs module, mirroring pubsub.rs's SubscriberRegistry pattern. Rationale: separation of concerns, session_glue.rs already 5500+ lines, and Reply emit helpers naturally colocate with the table they emit on behalf of.

Design decision B — callback shape: on_query: Fn(Query, &QueryResponder) where QueryResponder exposes send_reply / send_err / send_final methods matching the zenoh API split (z_query_reply / z_query_reply_err / z_query_reply_final). Multi-reply and per-reply error reporting are supported without forcing an async-stream return shape that would conflict with the MCU runtime contract.

Design decision C — dispatch wiring: R121j-5c will add a third arm to pubsub.rs registry.dispatch (or, equivalently, pass a sibling QueryableRegistry into poll_and_dispatch_one alongside SubscriberRegistry) so NetworkMessage::Request invokes QueryableTable::dispatch_request before the message is dropped. QueryableTable lookup keyed by Request.keyexpr resolved through the existing inbound DeclKexpr mapping table state on SubscriberRegistry (pubsub.rs:172).

Round 121j-5b.decision_summary: R121j-5b crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs new module: QueryableRegistry + QueryResponder + QueryReply (Reply Put/Del + Err) + into_response builder bridge. +14 lib tests. R121j-5c handles inbound wiring.
changes_bullets: New file crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs (~480 lines) mirrors crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs SubscriberRegistry surface for the Q-side. Exports QueryableRegistry, QueryableId, QueryableCallback = Box<dyn FnMut(&Query, &mut QueryResponder<'_>) + Send + 'static>, QueryResponder<'a>, QueryReply (Reply { Put|Del } | Err), and ReplyBody. Re-uses pubsub::keyexpr_pattern_matches for the chunk-wildcard matcher so subscriber and queryable patterns are byte-identical in matching semantics.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs registers `pub mod query;` with a doc-comment explaining the R121j-5b vs R121j-5c split (registry + Responder land now; the dispatch_iteration_event wiring that turns the accumulated Vec<QueryReply> into outbound Response frames is R121j-5c scope).

QueryableRegistry::dispatch_request(&mut self, request: &Request, peer_keyexpr_table: &HashMap<u64, String>, replies: &mut Vec<QueryReply>) routes inbound Request(Query) to matched queryables. Non-Query RequestVariant arms (MsgPut|MsgDel|Default) are silently no-ops (matches zenoh-pico _z_handle_request which only routes Query through the queryable callback path). Peer-alias resolution is delegated to a caller-provided &HashMap<u64, String> rather than owning a private copy — the integration site (R121j-5c) will lend SubscriberRegistry's table so DeclKexpr / UndeclKexpr absorbed by the subscriber path automatically inform queryable resolution. No dual-write bookkeeping; no Arc-shared state required.

QueryResponder<'a> is a short-lived borrow constructed per matched queryable: holds (rid, keyexpr_literal, &mut Vec<QueryReply>). Exposes send_reply(payload), send_reply_del(), send_err(encoding_id, schema, payload), plus rid() / keyexpr_literal() accessors for diagnostic surfaces. Drops before dispatch_request advances to the next queryable so user closures cannot retain the borrow. FnMut signature (not async) keeps the dispatch path suitable for the (c11, bare_metal) runtime crate target.

QueryReply::into_response(self) -> Response composes the wire-form Response by delegating to the existing ResponseReplyBuilder / ResponseErrBuilder. Put path: ResponseReplyBuilder::new(rid, 0, Some(&keyexpr_literal), &payload).build(). Del path: same with .reply_del() flip. Err path: ResponseErrBuilder::new(...) with optional .encoding(id, schema) chained when QueryReply::Err.encoding is Some. Reply keyexpr emitted in literal form (mapping_id=0 + Some(literal)) per zenoh-pico parity — alias declaration on the responder side is a Phase D+ optimisation.

13 new lib tests (counted lines: empty_registry_dispatch_is_noop_and_no_replies_emitted, register_assigns_monotonic_ids_starting_from_one, unregister_is_idempotent_and_removes_only_matching_id, dispatch_fires_callback_on_literal_match_and_accumulates_reply, dispatch_with_wildcard_pattern_matches_multiple_chunks, dispatch_resolves_mapping_id_against_peer_table, dispatch_ignores_non_query_request_body_arms, responder_send_reply_del_emits_del_arm, responder_send_err_emits_err_with_encoding_tuple, responder_supports_multiple_replies_per_query, query_reply_into_response_put_path_round_trips_via_builder, query_reply_into_response_del_path_flips_inner_arm, query_reply_into_response_err_path_threads_encoding_tuple, multiple_queryables_match_same_keyexpr_fire_in_registration_order). Each pins a specific invariant: dispatch semantics, alias resolution, body-arm filtering, callback shape, replies accumulation, builder round-trip parity, ordering.
verification_bullets: cargo build -p wz-runtime-tokio: clean.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib: 124/124 pass (was 110; +14 new tests confirming the count above).

cargo clippy -p wz-runtime-tokio --all-targets: clean after one doc_lazy_continuation fix (nested-bullet-list followed by paragraph required a blank /// separator on the dispatch_request doc-comment at query.rs:374-381).

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests: pubsub round-trips unaffected (wz_publisher_to_zsub + wz_publisher_aliased_to_zsub still pass); the new query module is unwired from the production poll-loop until R121j-5c, so integration baselines stay byte-identical.

into_response builder-parity tests are the strongest single guarantee: QueryReply::into_response (Put|Del|Err) produces byte-identical encoded Response to a direct ResponseReplyBuilder/ResponseErrBuilder call with the same args, so R121j-5c can drain QueryableRegistry-accumulated replies into the existing encode_frame_with_response helper with zero wire-shape divergence.
carry_forward_bullets: R121j-5c integration wiring: add an iteration adapter on QueryableRegistry (mirror of pubsub::SubscriberRegistry::dispatch_iteration_event) that drains FramePayload, calls dispatch_request on each NetworkMessage::Request, then drains the accumulated Vec<QueryReply> into encode_frame_with_response + final encode_frame_with_response_final on the link's outbound side. Requires passing the SubscriberRegistry's peer_keyexpr_table by reference to QueryableRegistry::dispatch_request — sites: poll_and_dispatch_one + drive_session_until_terminal in session_glue.rs.

R121j-5c also needs an end-to-end integration test: spin up wz_initiator (sender of Request(Query)) + wz_acceptor with a registered queryable, expect Reply+Final on the wire. Mirror of the existing pubsub round-trip tests (wz_publisher_to_zsub).

ResponseFinal emit currently uses encode_frame_with_response_final at session_glue.rs:1249. R121j-5c will need a helper analogous to QueryReply::into_response for the Final — one Final per inbound Request (whether the queryable emitted zero, one, or many replies). Already factored: encode_frame_with_response_final exists; only the per-Request invocation site is new.

Peer-alias-table sharing decision: R121j-5b chose parameter-passing over Arc-sharing. If R121j-5c finds the parameter threading too noisy, the textbook upgrade is to introduce a `pub trait PeerKeyexprResolver { fn resolve(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&str>; }` so both registries can hold an Arc<dyn PeerKeyexprResolver + Send + Sync>. Defer until the noise actually surfaces.

Q-side Request-level ext chain coverage: qos / target / budget / timeout = 4/5 (R121j-tstamp still gated on wz_codecs ext_zbuf Timestamp wiring). The QueryResponder API does not yet expose responder ext (R121j-3c .responder() setter) — if the queryable needs to identify itself as a non-anonymous responder, R121j-5c can add a QueryResponder::with_responder_zid(...) configuration step or expose .responder() on QueryReply::into_response.
R121h-perf-bump-5 (encode_ext_chain Z-bit refactor) decision still pending — carried unchanged across this round.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs gains `pub fn peer_keyexpr_table(&self) -> &HashMap<u64, String>`. Lends the SubscriberRegistry-owned mapping table to the queryable side so DeclKexpr / UndeclKexpr absorbed by the subscriber path automatically informs queryable resolution — no dual-write bookkeeping, no Arc<Mutex<...>> needed. Doc-comment makes the cross-registry sharing contract explicit.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs gains `pub fn dispatch_messages(&mut self, messages: &[NetworkMessage], peer_keyexpr_table: &HashMap<u64, String>, pending_replies: &mut Vec<QueryReply>, pending_final_rids: &mut Vec<u64>)`. Iterates messages, routes each NetworkMessage::Request through dispatch_request, and — only when dispatch_request actually emitted at least one Reply for this rid — enqueues the rid into pending_final_rids so the caller emits exactly one ResponseFinal per Reply chain (zenoh-pico parity: many Reply + one Final per Query). Un-resolvable mapping ids, non-Query body arms, and unmatched keyexprs all yield zero Replies and zero Finals — no false 'Final without Reply' wire shape.

query.rs also adds `pub fn dispatch_iteration_event(...)` adapter that pulls FramePayload.messages out of IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload {messages, ..}) and forwards to dispatch_messages. Mirror of SubscriberRegistry::dispatch_iteration_event so the queryable integration site uses the same observer-callback shape as the subscriber side.

query.rs gains the module-level helper `pub fn response_final_for(rid: u64) -> ResponseFinal` that constructs a wire-correct ResponseFinal envelope (header = _Z_MID_N_RESPONSE_FINAL = 0x1A; extensions = None today). Uses `..ResponseFinal::default()` spread so the helper stays resilient to future ResponseFinal field additions that land with sensible defaults.

5 new lib tests on the dispatch_messages + response_final_for surface: dispatch_messages_emits_final_for_each_matched_request (two matched + one unmatched -> exactly two Finals for the matched rids), dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_no_queryable_matched, dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_keyexpr_unresolvable, dispatch_messages_ignores_push_response_declare_variants (non-Query body arms produce no Reply / no Final), response_final_for_uses_default_header_and_explicit_rid (header bit + rid + extensions=None invariants).

Integration site (TCP-driven wz_initiator <-> wz_acceptor end-to-end Query/Reply round-trip via a registered queryable) intentionally deferred to a follow-up sub-round. R121j-5c stages the wire-level dispatch primitives and tests them in isolation; the e2e harness layering (LinkDriver send + frame-encode sequencing + sn assignment) requires its own design pass to decide the SessionLinkActions vs application-side ownership of the queryable registry. The lib-test surface here pins the wire-shape contract independent of that decision.

Round 224.decision_summary: R224 pre-push hook: stdin ref-tuple short-circuit + flock advisory lock close 22-session false-negative on Everything-up-to-date + concurrent push race
changes_bullets: `.githooks/pre-push` reads the git protocol stdin (`<local_ref> <local_sha> <remote_ref> <remote_sha>` per ref) and fast-exits with status 0 when no row has a non-zero `local_sha` — i.e. empty stdin (redundant push after another invocation updated the remote) or delete-only push (no new commit to validate).

`.githooks/pre-push` acquires a non-blocking `flock(1)` advisory lock on `$GIT_DIR/run-ci.lock` before entering `scripts/run-ci.sh`; failure exits 1 with an explicit `another run-ci already running` message + lock path so concurrent push attempts fail loud instead of silently racing `crates/target` cargo lock + sce-codegen freshness rebuild.
`flock(1)` presence guard via `command -v flock` so the advisory lock degrades to a no-op on slimmed containers without util-linux instead of hard-failing the hook.

Header rationale block extended with R224 retrospect documenting the 22-session false-negative root cause (a) Everything-up-to-date pushes still firing the full ~50s gate against zero work and (b) concurrent run-ci.sh races surfacing phantom Layer X FAIL on a clean tree.

Test 3 (concurrent lock): sibling process holds `$GIT_DIR/run-ci.lock` via `flock 200; sleep 10` background; hook with normal-ref stdin exits 1 with `another run-ci already running (lock: .git/run-ci.lock)`.

set -euo pipefail compatibility verified: `while read` EOF returns 1 inside the while-condition (not under `set -e` reject scope), `local_sha` only referenced inside the loop body so unset-variable not triggered.

`flock` advisory check via `command -v flock` keeps the guard optional; degraded path on slimmed containers still runs the original race-prone scripts/run-ci.sh path (transparent fallback, no new hard dependency).

Round 225.decision_summary: R225 Sample 6-field expansion: timestamp + encoding + qos + attachment + source_info + reliability surface mirrors zenoh-pico _z_sample_t in one shot; no partial-surface split
changes_bullets: `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/sample.rs` extends `Sample` from 3 fields (keyexpr / kind / payload) to 9 fields by adding `timestamp: Option<TimestampHint>`, `encoding: Option<EncodingHint>`, `qos: Option<QosLevel>`, `attachment: Option<Vec<u8>>`, `source_info: Option<SourceInfo>`, `reliability: Reliability` — the full `_z_sample_t` parity surface in a single round per R222 lesson #5 (`#[non_exhaustive]` is not a partial-surface escape hatch).

New wz-owned mirror types `TimestampHint` / `EncodingHint` wrap codec `Timestamp` / `Encoding` (both `#[derive(Default)]`-only) so `Sample` can carry `Clone` / `Debug` / `PartialEq` derives the SCE codegen layer omits; the established wz pattern at `reply.rs` ~286-305 (codec value → wz-owned mirror) is reused here verbatim.

New types `QosLevel { raw: u8 }`, `SourceInfo { zid: [u8;16], eid: u32, sn: u32 }`, `Reliability { BestEffort=0, Reliable=1 }` mirror zenoh-pico `_z_qos_t._val`, `_z_source_info_t`, and `z_reliability_t` respectively; `Reliability::default() == Reliable` matches `Z_RELIABILITY_DEFAULT`.

Three projection helpers `extract_qos` / `extract_attachment` / `extract_source_info` walk an `ExtEntry` chain matching on `(ext_id, enc)` tuples per zenoh-pico's dispatch switches — `_z_push_decode_ext_cb` for outer QoS (`ext_id=0x01, enc=ZInt`) and `_z_push_body_decode_extensions` for body attachment (`0x03, ZBuf`) + source_info (`0x01, ZBuf`).

`decode_source_info_payload` parses the source-info ZBuf shape per `_z_source_info_decode` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/protocol/codec/message.c` 196-231): 1 byte header (high nibble = zidlen-1), zidlen bytes zid right-padded into the [u8; 16] buffer, VLE-encoded eid (u32 overflow rejected), VLE-encoded sn (u32 overflow rejected). Carry text recorded an incorrect '16 bytes zid + VLE eid + VLE sn' shape; falsified before implementation by direct read of message.c — lesson recorded below.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::dispatch_push` now projects the full Sample literal: body-level timestamp/encoding via `TimestampHint::from_codec` / `EncodingHint::from_codec` from `MsgPut.timestamp` / `MsgPut.encoding` (Put) or `MsgDel.timestamp` (Del, encoding = None); body-level attachment + source_info via the helpers on `MsgPut.extensions` / `MsgDel.extensions`; outer-level QoS via helper on `Push.extensions`; `reliability = Reliability::default()` (transport-context wire-up = R226+ carry).

Builder setters `with_timestamp` / `with_encoding` / `with_qos` / `with_attachment` / `with_source_info` / `with_reliability` keep external `Sample::new_put` / `new_del` callers source-compatible while allowing intra-crate `dispatch_push` to construct via struct literal.
verification_bullets: `cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib`: 233 → 252 (+19) all pass. New tests cover the 9 Sample fields default state (`new_put` + `new_del` baselines), `Reliability::default() == Reliable` (zenoh-pico parity), `QosLevel::is_express` bit (1<<4) per zenoh-pico `_Z_N_QOS_IS_EXPRESS_FLAG`, builder chain through all 6 new metadata setters, `TimestampHint::from_codec` / `EncodingHint::from_codec` field round-trip (incl. absent-schema case), each `extract_*` helper's empty-chain / non-matching-tuple / first-match projection paths, `decode_source_info_payload` happy path (5-byte zid + single-byte VLEs) + multi-byte VLE path (200 / 16384) + truncated zid window + empty payload, and the `read_vle_u64` private helper's single-byte / multi-byte / truncation branches.

`cargo test -p wz-integration-tests`: 65 / 65 pass, regression 0. e2e suite (wz_publisher_*_to_zsub family + wz_initiator_to_* + ap_demo_round_trip + remote_declare + reply / queryable) continues to exercise the wire round-trip with the Sample callback signature now carrying the full 9-field projection; the `Sample` re-shape is non-breaking for existing subscribers because the load-bearing fields (keyexpr / kind / payload) keep their position and the new fields slot in as `Option<_>` / `Reliability` defaults.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean across all crates including wz-codecs / wz-runtime-tokio / wz-integration-tests / wz-ap-demo / wz-runtime-tokio-test-support / zenoh-pico-sys.

Carry-text falsify discipline (R221 textbook applied here): before implementation, carry's '16 bytes zid + VLE eid + VLE sn' source-info wire shape was checked against `_z_source_info_decode` directly and corrected to the actual '1 byte zidlen header + zidlen bytes zid + VLE eid + VLE sn' shape. Discovered during step 3; the corrected shape is what landed in `decode_source_info_payload`. Confirms the operating pattern surfaces real bugs cheaply.
carry_forward_bullets: R226 reliability transport-context wire-up. `Sample::reliability` is filled with `Reliability::default() == Reliable` in R225 because `dispatch_push` has no transport-context handle; the link-layer reliability value (best-effort vs reliable channel) needs to thread from the link / session layer through the registry so subscribers can observe the actual delivery class. zenoh-pico passes `z_reliability_t` as an explicit argument to `_z_trigger_push` (`src/session/push.c` 25-39) — wz mirror is the same shape (extra dispatch_push argument or per-link default stored in registry).

Operating pattern extension — 'carry text falsify' broadens beyond grep into type-compatibility falsification. R225 entry discovered that the closure's 'MsgPut struct has timestamp + encoding already decoded → immediate surface possible' assumption was false at the Rust level because the codec structs derive only `Default` (no `Clone`); the wz reply.rs ~286-305 wrap pattern resolves it.
