Round 226.decision_summary: R226 unifies Reliability enum + threads link-layer reliability from FramePayload.reliable through dispatch chain into Sample.reliability, closing R225 carry
changes_bullets: `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` extends the crate-root `Reliability` enum with `Default` / `Hash` / `repr(u8)` / explicit discriminants (`BestEffort=0`, `Reliable=1`, default `Reliable`) so the outbound driver hint and inbound `Sample.reliability` share a single typed surface. New `Reliability::from_reliable_bool` adapter maps the `DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload.reliable` discriminator to the typed enum.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/sample.rs` retires the duplicate `Reliability` enum that R225 introduced under the sample module; the previous `pub enum Reliability { ... }` is replaced with `pub use crate::Reliability;` so the sample-module re-export keeps `crate::sample::Reliability` source-compatible for callers while collapsing to one definition.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::dispatch_iteration_event` now destructures `FramePayload.reliable`, converts it via `Reliability::from_reliable_bool`, and threads the value through every per-message `dispatch` call. `dispatch(message, reliability)` and `dispatch_push(push, reliability)` grow an explicit `Reliability` argument so the link-layer classification reaches the `Sample` literal instead of the R225 placeholder `Reliability::default()`.

All 30 in-crate `registry.dispatch(...)` call sites (28 in pubsub.rs tests + 2 in the ResponseFinal / undeclare paths) now pass `Reliability::Reliable` explicitly. The Declare-arm absorb stays reliability-agnostic (declarations always travel on the reliable channel per session-fsm §6); the argument is consumed only by the Push arm via `dispatch_push`.
verification_bullets: `cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib`: 252 -> 256 (+4) all pass. New tests cover `dispatch(_, Reliable)` -> `Sample.reliability == Reliable`, `dispatch(_, BestEffort)` -> `Sample.reliability == BestEffort`, `dispatch_iteration_event(FramePayload { reliable: false, .. })` -> `Sample.reliability == BestEffort` (end-to-end frame -> sample projection), and `Reliability::from_reliable_bool(true|false)` adapter pairing.

`cargo test -p wz-integration-tests`: 65 / 65 pass, regression 0. The full e2e suite (pubsub round-trips against zenoh-pico, queryable / reply, remote declare, ap_demo) continues to interop with the now-threaded reliability argument because `dispatch_iteration_event` keeps its external signature; the new argument lives only on `dispatch` / `dispatch_push` whose external callers are limited to internal unit tests (already updated).

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean across wz-codecs / wz-runtime-tokio / wz-runtime-tokio-test-support / wz-integration-tests / wz-ap-demo / zenoh-pico-sys. The duplicate-enum cleanup did not surface any new lints; `pub use crate::Reliability` re-export is unambiguous.
carry_forward_bullets: R227+ Self-publish loopback infrastructure (R222 cluster carry). `dispatch_push(push, reliability)` now has a stable shape; the self-publish path will reuse it by routing the local Sample through the same dispatcher with the registry's default reliability (or a per-publisher override). Locality::SessionLocal short-circuit in the allows_remote() branch from R223 is the matching dormant surface that activates with this work.

Round 228.decision_summary: R228 Session bundle: Arc<SessionLinkActions> + Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>; publish() fans wire + loopback per PublishOptions.allowed_destination Locality predicate
changes_bullets: New module `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs` introduces `Session` — the application-level bundle mirroring zenoh-pico's `_z_session_t`. `Session` owns `Arc<SessionLinkActions>` (outbound handle) and `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` (inbound registries bundle). A single `Session::publish(keyexpr, payload, opts)` call fans both branches: wire-side `send_push_literal` / `send_push_del_literal` under `Locality::allows_remote()`, and loopback `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish` under `Locality::allows_local()`. Mirrors `_z_write` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/primitives.c` 170-205) which is the single zenoh-pico entry point that fans both branches off a single record.

`PublishOptions` is the new options bundle for `Session::publish`. `#[non_exhaustive]` to allow R229+ additions without breaking external callers. R228 scope: 3 fields (`allowed_destination: Locality`, `reliability: Reliability`, `kind: SampleKind`). Builder API: `put()` / `del()` constructors (defaults to `Any` locality + `Reliable` + matching kind) + `with_locality(...)` / `with_reliability(...)` / `with_kind(...)` chainable setters. The remaining 5 `Sample` body fields (`qos`, `attachment`, `timestamp`, `encoding`, `source_info`) are deferred to R229+ because the wire-side `send_push_literal` does not accept them either — propagating them through `Session::publish` now would silently fork wire (loses metadata) vs loopback (preserves metadata) symmetry.

`Session::publish` reads `opts.allowed_destination` and routes: `allows_remote()` → wire send through the existing `SessionLinkActions` API (Put picks `send_push_literal`, Del picks `send_push_del_literal`; the `payload` argument is ignored on Del kind — zenoh-pico `_z_n_msg_make_push_del` does not carry payload). `allows_local()` → build a `Sample` via `Sample::new_put` / `Sample::new_del` + `with_reliability(opts.reliability)` and dispatch through `observer.lock().unwrap().subscribers.local_publish(&sample)`. Returns the loopback `fired` count (0 when wire-only or no matching subscriber).

`Session::actions(&self) -> &Arc<SessionLinkActions>` and `Session::observer(&self) -> &Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` accessors expose the handles for non-publish call sites (e.g. `send_declare_subscriber` / `send_request_query` still go through `actions()`, callback registration goes through `observer().lock().unwrap().subscribers.register(...)`). This keeps `Session` from monopolizing the API surface during the migration window.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` adds `pub mod session;` with a 9-line doc block citing R228 scope, the `_z_session_t` zenoh-pico mirror, and the R229+ carry list. The module slot lives after `observer` so the dependency order (`observer::ApplicationLayerObserver` defined first, then `session::Session` bundles it) is reflected in lib-level ordering.

Locking discipline (module-level doc): `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` uses `std::sync::Mutex` (not `tokio::sync::Mutex`) because the loopback branch fires subscriber callbacks synchronously — exactly the semantic of zenoh-pico's `_z_session_deliver_push_locally` which fires callbacks in-line under the session lock. A `tokio::sync::Mutex` would force `publish` to be `async`, propagating an unnecessary coloring change across every call site for no measurable benefit (the lock window is one subscriber-table walk).

13 new R228 unit tests on `Session::publish` + `PublishOptions`: defaults yield Put/Any/Reliable; `put()` / `del()` constructor parity; `with_*` builder chain through all 3 setters; `Locality::Any` fires both branches (wire frame count = 1, loopback fired = 1); `Locality::Remote` fires wire only (frame count = 1, fired = 0); `Locality::SessionLocal` fires loopback only (frame count = 0, fired = 1); Sample reliability + kind propagation through loopback callback; Del-kind routes to Del wire builder + Del-kind Sample loopback with empty payload; reliability translates to wire-frame reliability hint for both `Reliable` and `BestEffort`; empty-registry returns 0; Remote-only-with-matching-subscriber returns 0 (loopback branch never entered); multi-subscriber count returns total fired; mixed-locality isolation (Any + SessionLocal + Remote on same keyexpr, Session::publish(SessionLocal) fires Any + SessionLocal, suppresses Remote, wire frame count = 0).

Tests reuse the existing `RecordingDriver` mock shape from `session_glue.rs` test module so the wire branch is observable without requiring real TCP setup. `fixture_params()` helper produces a minimal `SessionInitParams` (zid + lease + cookie + 32-byte signing key) sufficient for the action-layer's outbound paths.

Round 228.publishable_decision_summary: R228 Session bundle: Arc<SessionLinkActions> + Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>; publish() fans wire + loopback per PublishOptions.allowed_destination Locality predicate
publishable_changes_bullets: New module `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs` introduces `Session` — the application-level bundle mirroring zenoh-pico's `_z_session_t`. `Session` owns `Arc<SessionLinkActions>` (outbound handle) and `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` (inbound registries bundle). A single `Session::publish(keyexpr, payload, opts)` call fans both branches: wire-side `send_push_literal` / `send_push_del_literal` under `Locality::allows_remote()`, and loopback `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish` under `Locality::allows_local()`. Mirrors `_z_write` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/primitives.c` 170-205) which is the single zenoh-pico entry point that fans both branches off a single record.

`PublishOptions` is the new options bundle for `Session::publish`. `#[non_exhaustive]` to allow R229+ additions without breaking external callers. R228 scope: 3 fields (`allowed_destination: Locality`, `reliability: Reliability`, `kind: SampleKind`). Builder API: `put()` / `del()` constructors (defaults to `Any` locality + `Reliable` + matching kind) + `with_locality(...)` / `with_reliability(...)` / `with_kind(...)` chainable setters. The remaining 5 `Sample` body fields (`qos`, `attachment`, `timestamp`, `encoding`, `source_info`) are deferred to R229+ because the wire-side `send_push_literal` does not accept them either — propagating them through `Session::publish` now would silently fork wire (loses metadata) vs loopback (preserves metadata) symmetry.

`Session::publish` reads `opts.allowed_destination` and routes: `allows_remote()` → wire send through the existing `SessionLinkActions` API (Put picks `send_push_literal`, Del picks `send_push_del_literal`; the `payload` argument is ignored on Del kind — zenoh-pico `_z_n_msg_make_push_del` does not carry payload). `allows_local()` → build a `Sample` via `Sample::new_put` / `Sample::new_del` + `with_reliability(opts.reliability)` and dispatch through `observer.lock().unwrap().subscribers.local_publish(&sample)`. Returns the loopback `fired` count (0 when wire-only or no matching subscriber).

`Session::actions(&self) -> &Arc<SessionLinkActions>` and `Session::observer(&self) -> &Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` accessors expose the handles for non-publish call sites (e.g. `send_declare_subscriber` / `send_request_query` still go through `actions()`, callback registration goes through `observer().lock().unwrap().subscribers.register(...)`). This keeps `Session` from monopolizing the API surface during the migration window.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` adds `pub mod session;` with a 9-line doc block citing R228 scope, the `_z_session_t` zenoh-pico mirror, and the R229+ carry list. The module slot lives after `observer` so the dependency order (`observer::ApplicationLayerObserver` defined first, then `session::Session` bundles it) is reflected in lib-level ordering.

Locking discipline (module-level doc): `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` uses `std::sync::Mutex` (not `tokio::sync::Mutex`) because the loopback branch fires subscriber callbacks synchronously — exactly the semantic of zenoh-pico's `_z_session_deliver_push_locally` which fires callbacks in-line under the session lock. A `tokio::sync::Mutex` would force `publish` to be `async`, propagating an unnecessary coloring change across every call site for no measurable benefit (the lock window is one subscriber-table walk).

Round 229.decision_summary: R229 Session::publish_aliased: mapping_id + suffix + caller-asserted loopback_keyexpr; mirrors send_push_aliased on wire side, fires local_publish on loopback with the asserted literal
changes_bullets: `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs::Session` adds `publish_aliased(mapping_id, inline_suffix, loopback_keyexpr, payload, opts)` — aliased-keyexpr counterpart to R228's `publish` for literal keyexpr. Wire branch routes through `SessionLinkActions::send_push_aliased` (Put) or `send_push_del_aliased` (Del) so the peer resolves the keyexpr through its inbound mapping table (populated by an earlier outbound `send_declare_keyexpr`). Loopback branch builds a `Sample` with `loopback_keyexpr` as the literal and dispatches through the same `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish` the R227 wire-path-equivalent does. Returns the loopback fired count, same shape as `publish`.

Caller precondition documented inline: `loopback_keyexpr` MUST equal the literal form the peer would resolve `(mapping_id, inline_suffix)` to. Typical usage: (1) `send_declare_keyexpr(7, "home/temp")` registers `7 -> "home/temp"` on the peer; (2) `publish_aliased(7, None, "home/temp", payload, opts)` carries `(id=7, suffix=None)` on the wire and fires loopback on `"home/temp"`. With an inline suffix: `publish_aliased(7, Some("/kitchen"), "home/temp/kitchen", payload, opts)` carries `(id=7, suffix="/kitchen")` on the wire and fires loopback on `"home/temp/kitchen"` — the caller resolves the composite form explicitly.

Caller-resolved `loopback_keyexpr` choice over wz-side outbound mapping table: zenoh-pico's `_z_session_t._local_resources` is the local-side resolution table populated by self-declarations (`vendor/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/session/resource.h`). wz does not yet have an equivalent outbound table — introducing one is the natural R230+ carry. Until then, the caller is the single source of truth for the loopback literal; documented inline.

Implementation re-uses R228 patterns verbatim: locality predicate selects branches; `opts.kind` selects Put-vs-Del routing; `Sample::with_reliability(opts.reliability)` propagates the link-layer hint into `Sample.reliability`. The two branches are independent (wire branch ignores the loopback_keyexpr argument; loopback branch ignores the mapping_id + inline_suffix pair) so callers can intentionally decouple the wire form from the loopback form, which the regression-guard test pins.

src/runtime.rs Runtime trait: type JoinHandle<T: Send + 'static>: Future<Output = Result<T, RuntimeError>> + Send + 'static GAT + spawn<F: Future + Send + 'static>(fut: F) -> Self::JoinHandle<F::Output>. Mirrors tokio JoinHandle as a Future contract so tokio impl can satisfy directly via JoinError -> RuntimeError::JoinFailed wrap.
src/time.rs TimeSource trait: now_monotonic_ms(&self) -> u64 + sleep(&self, ms: u64) -> impl Future<Output=()> + Send + '_ (RPITIT shape user-confirmed; Rust 1.75 stable).

src/allocator.rs Allocator trait: alloc(&self, Layout) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> + unsafe dealloc(&self, NonNull<u8>, Layout). Local trait (NOT core::alloc::Allocator which is nightly-only on MSRV 1.75) with explicit Option-on-OOM failure surface; buffer-pool / TLSF allocator pivot space preserved.

src/error.rs RuntimeError enum: JoinFailed + Shutdown variants, non_exhaustive. Display impl. core::error::Error impl deferred (requires MSRV 1.81); std::error::Error impl behind std feature deferred to R252+ AP integration round.
src/lib.rs cfg_attr no_std gate + alloc extern + module re-exports. deny(missing_docs) for trait-surface doc completeness.

carry_forward_bullets: R264 lesson: any architectural decision that adds select! arms to drive_session_until_terminal must FIRST audit poll_and_dispatch_one's cancel-safety against the concrete LinkDriver impls in scope (wz-ap-demo InboundReadDriver uses length-prefixed read_exact x2 — NOT cancel-safe). The original R264 attempt to add a sweep_tick_ms parameter that clamps the lease sleep arm tripped this hazard and broke wz_query_reply_round_trip. Future architectural changes touching the inner select! must include the cancel-safety audit in the design step.

R264 lesson: AskUserQuestion sequence (3 rounds of questions in one round of work) is the correct pattern when an architectural attempt surfaces a downstream regression mid-execution. Each AskUserQuestion presented previews of code shape so the user could evaluate the trade-off without reading source. The textbook beats 'silently revert and pick a different approach' because it leaves audit trace of the decision chain.

InboundReadDriver poll_event cancel-safety hazard (R264 surfaced): the function reads u16 length then variable-length payload via two read_exact calls. select! cancel between the calls drops the captured length and leaves the socket cursor 2 bytes ahead of where the next iteration expects. This was acceptable under R263 lease=10 s cadence (cancellation rare in steady-state traffic) but blocks any future sub-second sweep cadence work that would race poll_and_dispatch. Textbook fix: make poll_event truly cancel-safe by buffering partial-read state in InboundReadDriver. Scope estimate: 1-2 rounds (read state machine + matching changes in any other length-prefixed driver impl). Tag: cancel-safety carry, R265+.

R264 production-grade follow-ups (deferred to dedicated rounds): (a) FinalCallback FinalCause Normal vs TimedOut differentiation — wz-ap-demo's FINAL RECEIVED log line currently logs the same shape for both peer-final and timeout-sweep-final; if a deploy use case needs to differentiate, promote FinalCallback to FnMut(u64, FinalCause). YAGNI hold pending user inspection. (b) sweep cadence configurability via deploy.yaml — the 100 ms constant is currently a hardcoded literal in wz-ap-demo run_demo; production AP deploys may want to tune per topology. Topology-schema migration carry (R123b-pre) already tracks this surface.

R264 carry: sweep_task graceful shutdown is via abort() which is fine for current state (no async-cleanup-needed). If sweep_task ever owns external resources (open files, network sockets, etc.) abort() may bypass Drop guarantees; the textbook upgrade is a CancellationToken + select! { tick | cancel } shape. Not needed now; documented for the cancel-safety carry round.

tcp_driver_cancel_safety scenarios: (1) partial-length-prefix-survives-cancel: write 1 of 2 length-prefix bytes, race poll_event against 100 ms sleep (sleep wins), write remainder, verify Rx with full payload. Round 266.decision_summary: R266 lands the panic_payload capture path on RuntimeError::JoinFailed under feature = "alloc": tokio's JoinError::into_panic() result is now propagated through to AP-profile callers as Box<dyn Any + Send + 'static>, accessible via a new RuntimeError::panic_payload() accessor + a Display impl that extracts String / &'static str payload bytes as a "panicked: <msg>" suffix; MCU no-alloc builds keep JoinFailed as a unit variant (no heap to box onto, no panic-infrastructure parity); R258's compile-time Send/Sync/Clone/Eq pin gates Sync/Clone/Eq on cfg(not(feature = "alloc")) because Box<dyn Any + Send> is not Sync (tokio surfaces Send-only payloads), not Clone (Any erases the concrete type's Clone) and not PartialEq; tokio test sites switch from assert_eq! against PartialEq-bound Result to matches! against variant shape (preserving R257 panic-vs-cancel split semantics) and unwrap-+-value-compare for Ok(value) checks.

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: new smart constructors. `RuntimeError::join_failed()` available in both builds (None-payload under alloc; unit variant under no-alloc); `RuntimeError::join_failed_with_payload(Option<Box<dyn Any + Send + 'static>>)` available only under alloc. The constructor pair lets runtime impls produce the variant without `#[cfg]` switches at the call site (constructor itself dispatches the cfg internally).

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: new `RuntimeError::panic_payload(&self) -> Option<&(dyn Any + Send + 'static)>` accessor. Returns Some(&borrowed Box content) for JoinFailed-with-payload; None for JoinFailed-without-payload, JoinCancelled, Shutdown, or under no-alloc (where the slot does not exist). Doc-comment includes the textbook downcast snippet for the two common panic payload types (String / &'static str).

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: Display impl extended. Under alloc the JoinFailed arm tries `payload.downcast_ref::<String>()` first then `payload.downcast_ref::<&'static str>()`; on match Display emits `RuntimeError: spawned task panicked: <msg>`. Unknown payload type or no-payload falls back to the plain prefix string (preserves log-grep stability for callers that pattern-match on the prefix).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs — new `pub fn keyexpr_intersect_patterns(a_chunks: &[&str], b_chunks: &[&str]) -> bool` helper. Algorithm: recursive descent over both chunk slices with symmetric handling of `**` (zero-or-more chunks, with backtracking on either side), `*` (exactly-one chunk on either side), `$*` intra-chunk DSL (single-side reuses chunk_matches_with_dsl, two-side $* uses leading + trailing anchor prefix/suffix compatibility check as a sound over-approximation), and literal chunks (byte equality after each side's chunk_intersects accepts). Sibling private fns `intersect_chunks` (recursive driver) + `chunk_intersects` (single-chunk router) keep the public surface a single function. Module-level doc-comment names the approximation boundary explicitly.

Doc-comment rewritten: removed the `approximation boundary` paragraph; added the honest two-pattern overlap case as a first-class supported semantic; clarified the wz spec / peer-declared bifurcation (wz-own KE = compile-time fixed per RFC Appendix C; peer-declared KE = runtime string-based, matcher lives in the wz-runtime-tokio layer).

changes_bullets: crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h + build.rs — expose `_z_keyexpr_forward_intersects` (chunk-level forward-scan matcher that `_z_keyexpr_intersects` in session/keyexpr.c:581 dispatches into). Round 299.decision_summary: R299 lands Layer 3 keyexpr canonicalization fixture; cross-validates wz canonize_keyexpr against zenoh-pico _z_keyexpr_canonize and surfaces three pico canon bugs as documented divergences (incl. one SIGABRT denial-of-service path).
changes_bullets: crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h + build.rs — expose `_z_keyexpr_canonize(char *start, size_t *len)` and the `zp_keyexpr_canon_status_t` enum. The symbol is declared in `vendor/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/session/keyexpr.h:69`; the enum lives in `api/constants.h` and is already transitively included via `zenoh-pico.h`. Bindgen allowlist gains the function + the status enum; the wrapper header adds an explicit `#include <stddef.h>` + `#include "zenoh-pico/session/keyexpr.h"` to keep the keyexpr-domain FFI surface visible at one site (R297 intersect symbol lives next to it).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_keyexpr_canon.rs — new Layer 3 fixture (~330 lines). 9 tests: `canon_identity_on_already_canonical_input`, `canon_singleify_collapses_dollar_star_runs_in_dsl_chunks`, `canon_lone_dollar_star_alone`, `canon_drops_double_star_after_double_star`, `canon_rejects_invalid_grammar_single_violation` (agreed-subspace cross-validation), `canon_known_pico_anomaly_star_after_double_star`, `canon_known_pico_anomaly_dsl_rewrite_chunk_walk_overrun`, `canon_known_pico_anomaly_double_star_literal_star_aborts` (divergence pin), `keyexpr_canon_wz_pico_property` (proptest 512-case constrained generator). The status-code 1:1 map (wz `KeyexprCanonError` ↔ pico `zp_keyexpr_canon_status_t`) lives at `wz_error_to_pico_status` per the wz module doc-comment line 64-65.

Three wz/pico canon divergences discovered + documented in the fixture module doc-comment (lines 25-66): (1) `**` followed by `*`-shape chunk — pico's case-1 unconditional write + deferred `in_big_wild` produces `*/**/...` instead of `**/...`; (2) initial `$*` rewrite + any later chunk with `*` — pico's main-canonize char-walk uses `c < end` (should be `c < chunk_end`) so the per-chunk validation reads past the boundary and trips STARS_IN_CHUNK on a later chunk's `*`; (3) `**` + literal + `*` — pico's `__zp_canon_prefix` case-1 else-continue path skips `in_big_wild = false` reset, so a subsequent `*` returns SINGLE_STAR_AFTER_DOUBLE_STAR with `*len` pointing at the `/` between literal and `*`, then main canonize fails its `chunk_end - reader == 2` precondition and triggers `assert(false)` at `keyexpr.c:340` (process aborts via SIGABRT — wz peer sending such a keyexpr could DoS a pico client). Wz handles all three cleanly per spec.

Property generator constrained to AGREED subspace — R298-style canonical chunk strategy (alphabet [a,b,c], 1..=4 chunks, literal / `*` / `**` / flanked-DSL) with an in-generator post-process that drops every `*`-shape or `$*`-prefixed chunk appearing AFTER any `**` chunk in the sequence (avoids pico bugs #1 and #3 deterministically; #2 is avoided because dsl_chunk_strategy emits only flanked DSL chunks that stay in case-1/case-2 of the chunk handler, never falling through to the buggy char-walk). The constructive filter keeps shrinking on canonical inputs.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test layer3_keyexpr_canon — 9 pass / 0 fail / 0 ignored. Property fn ran 512 random canonical cases in <100ms; zero divergences found within the constrained subspace.

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings — clean across the full workspace. No new lint surface from the wrapper.h additions, the bindgen allowlist expansion, or the proptest macro expansion.
scripts/run-ci.sh --skip-codegen — Layer 0 / A / A2 / C0 / C1 / C1b / C2 / D / E all green; `run-ci: all required layers pass`.

Pico bug discoveries reproducibly trigger — bug #1 (`**/*` → `*/**`) and bug #2 (`$*/a/*` → STARS_IN_CHUNK) pinned by `canon_known_pico_anomaly_star_after_double_star` and `_dsl_rewrite_chunk_walk_overrun` respectively; bug #3 SIGABRT path verified by hand (`**/c/*` aborts the process via assert(false) at keyexpr.c:340) and is intentionally NOT runtime-asserted (would kill the test binary) — the `_double_star_literal_star_aborts` test instead locks wz's identity output on these inputs and documents the pico abort analytically.
carry_forward_bullets: R299 surfaced THREE wz/zenoh-pico canon divergences — wire-interop hazards that affect any wz ↔ pico session where keyexprs containing `**`, `$*`, or specific chunk-shape combinations are exchanged. R300+ candidate (architectural): decide between (a) wz tracks pico's buggy output (lossy but interop-safe), (b) wz adds an inbound-side normalization shim that fixes pico's output before storage, or (c) wz upstreams patches to zenoh-pico (best long-term, requires merge cycle). User confirmation needed — architectural decision with cross-repo coordination if option (c).

Bug #3 (`**` + literal + `*` SIGABRT path) is a DoS risk: a malicious or buggy wz peer sending such a keyexpr to a pico client triggers a process abort. wz-side mitigation: caller MUST canonize_keyexpr() before sending Declare(DeclKexpr) so the post-canon string can never trip pico's assert. Add a pre-send canonize-or-reject gate in wz's send-declare path as R300+ candidate.

Round 300.decision_summary: R300 closes R299 carry #1 (DoS mitigation): adds outbound DECLARE-side keyexpr gate that rejects R299 bug #3 SIGABRT pattern family pre-emit, plus argv eager-reject in wz-ap-demo.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/keyexpr_canon.rs — adds `OutboundKeyexprError` enum (NotCanonical(KeyexprCanonError) + PicoBugThreeFamily { keyexpr, offending_chunk }) and `check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe(input: &str) -> Result<(), OutboundKeyexprError>`. The gate first runs canonize_keyexpr for structural validity, then walks chunks with a 2-flag state machine (seen_double_star + seen_literal_after_double_star, reset on every fresh `**` chunk). Reject fires when both flags are set and the current chunk's canonical form is `*`-shape (single `*`, `**`, or any `$*`-only run via `chunk_canonizes_to_star_shape` private helper). Conservative scope: also rejects trailing `**` after a literal-after-`**` segment (`**/a/**` etc.) — R299 fixture empirically pins SIGABRT only for trailing `*`/`$*` (cannot cross-validate `**` trailing without process abort), but the underlying `in_big_wild` stale-state mechanism does not distinguish the closer's exact star-shape. False-positive zone documented; narrowing pending empirical fork-based pico abort probe.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — adds `SendDeclareError` enum (Keyexpr(OutboundKeyexprError) + ReservedMappingIdZero + UnknownMappingId(u64) + MissingKeyexpr) with Display/Error/From impls. Adds private `SessionLinkActions::reconstruct_outbound_keyexpr(mapping_id, suffix) -> Result<String, SendDeclareError>` covering all four wire shapes ((0,None)=MissingKeyexpr / (0,Some(s))=literal / (id,None)=pure-alias prefix lookup / (id,Some(tail))=composite prefix||tail). Changes `send_declare_keyexpr`, `send_declare_subscriber`, `send_declare_queryable`, `send_declare_token` signatures from `()` to `Result<(), SendDeclareError>`. Each method gate-checks BEFORE wire emit or mapping-table side effect; send_declare_keyexpr also rejects mapping_id=0 (mirrors build_declare_kexpr's assertion as typed error). send_undeclare_kexpr unchanged (no keyexpr input). 9 new unit tests: reserved-id-zero / bug-three / structurally-invalid / missing-keyexpr / unknown-mapping / cross-boundary-bug-three / safe-alias-form / queryable+token gate inheritance / reconstruct shape table.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — `Session::declare_token` signature now `Result<LivelinessToken, OutboundKeyexprError>` (literal-mode, only Keyexpr variant reachable; unreachable! guards future refactors). `Session::declare_token_aliased` now also returns the existing `LivelinessAliasError` extended with `InvalidKeyexpr(OutboundKeyexprError)` variant + Display + Error::source impl. 13 declare_token test callsites updated to `.expect("hardcoded canonical literal keyexpr")`. 23 direct `send_declare_keyexpr` test callsites updated to chained `.expect()`.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs — adds eager argv-level R300 validation loop for the three DECLARE-side flags (--declare-subscriber/-queryable/-token); rejected keyexprs exit code 2 with a diagnostic stderr line BEFORE the tokio runtime / driver loop is built. Receive-side keyexprs (--key/--queryable/--query/--liveliness-subscribe) deliberately not gated — they register local pattern slots that match inbound peer keyexprs and are never emitted on the outbound wire.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/tasks.rs — declare_task and publisher_task callsites for send_declare_subscriber/queryable/keyexpr + session.declare_token now `if let Err(e) = ...` → log::warn + eprintln + early return (CLI bad-input path, no panic). Mirrors the argv-eager path so library API users still get the same gate at the runtime layer.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/r300_outbound_keyexpr_gate.rs — new Layer E fixture (4 tests, all #[ignore = "binary-dep e2e ..."]). Pins exit-code 2 + stderr diagnostic for the 3 R299 bug #3 family inputs via --declare-subscriber, plus uniform gate firing across --declare-queryable / --declare-token, plus structural reject path (empty chunk). Uses --connect 127.0.0.1:1 (unreachable target) so the argv-eager gate fires before any connect attempt — fast + peer-independent.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace — 589 lib tests pass / 0 fail (was 579 pre-R300; +10 = 9 SessionLinkActions gate tests + 1 reconstruct shape table test). 23 keyexpr_canon tests pass (was 15 pre-R300; +8 R300-specific). Layer E `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test r300_outbound_keyexpr_gate -- --ignored` — 4 pass / 0 fail in <1s (no peer dependency).

cargo build --workspace --tests — clean across wz-runtime-tokio, wz-runtime-tokio-test-support, wz-ap-demo, wz-integration-tests. Cascade scope: 13 declare_token + 23 send_declare_keyexpr test callsites + 4 wz-ap-demo prod callsites, all updated to handle Result.

validate_workspace baseline preserved — docs=12/12, T1 orphan total=0 (ledger=1 R193 known-stale unchanged), round-trip mandatory=12/12, T3 warn=855 / T4 info=427 unchanged, atomic ledger entries=298/sections=215/sync. R300 commit pre-commit hook passed.

Gate semantic correctness — R299 fixture 3 bug #3 cases (`**/c/*`, `**/foo/*`, `**/a/b/*`) reject; bug #1 cases (`**/*`, `home/**/*/temp`, `**/$*/temp`) pass (no false positive; wz canon converts these to safe wire form internally per R221, separate wire-drift handling deferred to R301+). Cross-boundary case verified: prefix `**` registered via send_declare_keyexpr, suffix `/c/*` via send_declare_subscriber → gate reports reconstructed full keyexpr `**/c/*` in the error (a suffix-only check would have missed this — the gate's raison d'etre).

No regression on R299 layer3_keyexpr_canon fixture (the 8 documented divergence pins + proptest 512-case property continue to pass — R300 added a separate safety layer above canonize_keyexpr without touching canonize_keyexpr itself, preserving R221 spec-mirror contract intact).
carry_forward_bullets: R299 carry #1 (DoS mitigation gate) — CLOSED by R300.

R299 carry #2 (other wz/pico equivalence inventory) — still open; recommend R301 to grep wz-runtime-tokio for `mirror` / `equivalent` / `zenoh-pico's` doc-comments and inventory each module's empirical re-verification need. R299 retrospect lesson: every 'functionally equivalent' claim deserves an R299-style cross-validation fixture.

R299 carry #3 (wz↔pico canon divergence handling — bug #1 wire-interop drift) — still open; R300 narrowed scope to SIGABRT-only, leaving bug #1 family allowed. Decision among (a) wz traces pico bug / (b) wz inbound normalization shim / (c) zenoh-pico upstream patch still requires user input.

R300 conservative-reject false-positive zone (`**/a/**`-shape inputs are semantically valid zenoh keyexpr — 'a appears somewhere' — but the gate rejects them defensively). Empirical SIGABRT verification via a fork()/wait()-based pico subprocess probe would let R301+ narrow the gate to the literal-trailing-* subset. Currently conservative.

wz-ap-demo eager argv gate is DECLARE-side only. R301 could evaluate whether --key / --queryable / --query / --liveliness-subscribe (receive-side keyexprs) should also be argv-validated for grammar correctness (not pico-safety — they never leave wz) so CLI users get the same UX as DECLARE flags. Likely a low-effort UX tweak, not a correctness concern.

changes_bullets: crates/wz/ new top-level facade crate. Cargo.toml ~600 lines with [features] table holding 144 atomic + 19 domain-aggregate + 6 preset = 169 entries (plus default=[]). lib.rs minimal facade with #![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)] so preset-mcu-* (no_std) flows through. No [dependencies] yet — features compile to no-op labels at R302a; downstream gating lands R302b+ as modules move into the facade.
144 atomic features named <domain>-<capability> kebab-case per R301 inventory. Identical id set, zero renames. Source of truth = inventory entries; Cargo.toml is the mechanical projection.

19 domain-aggregate features `domain-<name>` = union of each domain's atomic set. Granularity layer between hand-picking atomic and pick-a-preset. Used as `cargo add wz --features domain-pubsub` for whole-domain opt-in.

6 preset features as EXPLICIT per-preset atomic lists; no preset-extends-preset. Rationale: v0.1.0 is a frozen semver contract — atomic catalog growth cannot silently shift preset membership. Counts: preset-mcu-minimal=36 / preset-mcu-extended=59 / preset-ap-client=67 / preset-ap-router=80 / preset-ap-full=131 / preset-zenoh-cpp=118.

Implication edges encoded only where inventory reason field says 'requires X' / 'builds on X': attachment-encoding-aware→attachment-bytes; declare-keyexpr→keyexpr-mapping; pubsub-attachment→attachment-bytes; pubsub-priority→session-extqos; query-attachment→attachment-bytes; liveliness-get→query-get; liveliness-historical-samples→liveliness-history; codec-fragment→transport-fragmentation; codec-join→session-multicast; link-fragment→transport-fragmentation; locator-{quic,serial,tls,unixsock,vsock,ws}→transport-link-{same}; runtime-tokio-uring→runtime-tokio; scouting-gossip→routing-router; scouting-multicast→transport-link-udp; transport-link-tls→transport-link-tcp; access-extauth-{jwt,pubkey,usrpwd}→session-extauth; session-extcompression→transport-compression; session-extshm→transport-shm; routing-{failover,routes,static-routes}→routing-router; storage-{history,replication}→storage-backend.

default=[] (no-default). Composable-framework contract: user explicitly opts into a preset or hand-rolls atomic combos. Differs from batteries-included crates like tokio. Matches kconfig / NixOS USE / Buildroot semantics where the user authors the config.

changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml [features] section added: default=["liveliness-token", "liveliness-subscriber"], liveliness-token=[], liveliness-subscriber=[]. Backward-compat: existing in-workspace consumers (wz-ap-demo, integration tests, session_fsm tests) build unchanged because defaults stay on.
src/declare.rs: gate `mod liveliness` + `mod liveliness_subscriber` declarations + their `pub use` re-exports on respective features. Queryable + subscriber sub-modules stay unconditional.

src/observer.rs: gate `ApplicationLayerObserver::liveliness` field on `liveliness-token`, `::liveliness_subscribers` field on `liveliness-subscriber`. Same gates on the `new()` initializers and the `dispatch_iteration_event()` calls. Import statements split — `use crate::declare::LivelinessRegistry` now `#[cfg(feature = "liveliness-token")]`, same shape for the subscriber registry.

src/session.rs 17 gate points: 4 methods (declare_token, declare_token_aliased, declare_liveliness_subscriber, declare_liveliness_subscriber_aliased) + 4 structs (LivelinessOptions, LivelinessToken, LivelinessSubscriberOptions, LivelinessSubscriber) + 4 impl/Drop blocks (impl LivelinessToken, Drop for LivelinessToken, impl LivelinessSubscriber, Drop for LivelinessSubscriber) + 5 enum/Display/Error pairs (LivelinessAliasError enum + Display + Error, LivelinessSubscriberAliasError enum + Display + Error). Use statements split so OutboundKeyexprError/SendDeclareError/LivelinessSample/LivelinessSampleCallback become conditional.

src/declare/cross_tests.rs: gate the `three_registries_share_a_message_stream_independently` test on liveliness-token. The two-registry test (subscriber + queryable) stays unconditional. Test count diff: feature-off mode loses the 3-registry test, keeps the 2-registry test.

src/declare/test_helpers.rs: gate `decl_token` / `undecl_token` / `declare_envelope_decl_token` / `declare_envelope_undecl_token` helpers + their underlying `use wz_codecs::decl_token::DeclToken` / `use wz_codecs::undecl_token::UndeclToken` imports on `any(feature = "liveliness-token", feature = "liveliness-subscriber")` — either feature needs the helpers (liveliness.rs uses them with -token; liveliness_subscriber.rs uses them with -subscriber). Imports + helpers stay symmetric so no half-active state.

wz/Cargo.toml: [dependencies] wz-runtime-tokio = { path = "../wz-runtime-tokio", optional = true, default-features = false }. Forwarding: runtime-tokio = ["dep:wz-runtime-tokio"]. liveliness-token = ["wz-runtime-tokio?/liveliness-token"]. liveliness-subscriber = ["wz-runtime-tokio?/liveliness-subscriber"]. Cargo `?` syntax means liveliness-* enabled WITHOUT runtime-tokio stays a label (no crate pull); WITH runtime-tokio it forwards the sub-feature into wz-runtime-tokio.
verification_bullets: cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio (default features) → pass 1.04s. Existing consumer path unchanged.

cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio --no-default-features → pass 1.89s after fixing 3 use-statement errors (OutboundKeyexprError, SendDeclareError, LivelinessSample{Callback}). All liveliness symbols correctly removed from the build.
cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio --no-default-features --features liveliness-token → pass 0.79s. Token-only path: LivelinessSubscriber surface absent.
cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio --no-default-features --features liveliness-subscriber → pass 0.67s. Subscriber-only path: LivelinessToken surface absent.
cargo check -p wz --no-default-features → pass. wz-runtime-tokio not pulled.
cargo check -p wz --features runtime-tokio (bare) → pass. wz-runtime-tokio pulled with --no-default-features (liveliness OFF).
cargo check -p wz --features liveliness-token (no runtime-tokio) → pass. Label-only — `?` syntax skips forwarding because optional dep not active.
cargo check -p wz --features runtime-tokio,liveliness-token → pass. wz-runtime-tokio pulled with liveliness-token only.
cargo check -p wz --features preset-ap-client → wz-runtime-tokio rebuilds with both liveliness features active (preset includes runtime-tokio + liveliness-token + liveliness-subscriber).
cargo check -p wz --features preset-mcu-minimal → wz-runtime-tokio NOT pulled (preset selects runtime-no-std, not runtime-tokio). 0.05s cache-hit.
cargo check --workspace → pass 1.98s. All 8 workspace members build cleanly.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib → 589 passed; 0 failed. Liveliness inline unit tests (6 in liveliness.rs + 12 in liveliness_subscriber.rs) run as part of default-features build.
cargo test --workspace --no-run → all test binaries compile. Integration tests (echo_demo, session_fsm_*, ap_demo_round_trip, layer3_*, wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip, etc.) link successfully.

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip → 1 test marked `ignored, binary-dep e2e (wz-ap-demo bin); Layer E runs via --ignored`. Compile passes; Layer E e2e behavior is pre-R302b state preserved.

carry_forward_bullets: cargo test --no-default-features cargo gotcha — wz-runtime-tokio-test-support's Cargo.toml line 47 has `wz-runtime-tokio = { path = "../wz-runtime-tokio" }` WITHOUT `default-features = false`. Cargo feature-unification then forces wz-runtime-tokio defaults (both liveliness ON) during `cargo test` even with --no-default-features. Production `cargo check --no-default-features` works correctly (verified). Fix: future round mark test-support's wz-runtime-tokio dep as default-features=false + explicit feature pulling. Establishes the `use wz::liveliness::LivelinessToken` user-facing import path.

Round 304.decision_summary: R304 retires Layer E test harness strict-UTF-8 decode: `read_captured` switches `read_to_string+expect` → `read_to_end + String::from_utf8_lossy`, removing the sporadic flake source.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: `pub fn read_captured(file: &mut File) -> String` rewritten. Old shape: `file.read_to_string(&mut s).expect("read captured output")` — panics on first non-UTF-8 byte the child wrote, surfacing the panic IN PLACE OF the captured content (caller sees the harness error, not the test's actual fail mode). New shape: `file.read_to_end(&mut bytes).expect("read captured bytes") + String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()` — non-UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD markers and the caller still sees the full captured snapshot.

Doc-comment expanded with the failure-mode background — child panic backtrace under tokio's worker-thread pool can interleave with a libc-side `abort(3)` message at byte granularity, producing mid-codepoint truncation. The strict-decode path masked this as a separate panic; lossy decode surfaces it as inline U+FFFD markers in the diagnostic output so the caller can see what the child actually wrote.
No source-level changes to wz-runtime-tokio / wz-codecs / wz-ap-demo — the flake was purely a test harness defect (R215 strict-decode legacy).
verification_bullets: Reproduction context — R302b push to origin/main triggered pre-push hook → scripts/run-ci.sh Layer E → `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor --release -- --ignored` failed once with `read captured output: Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }`. Manual retry passed. User flagged: flaky-1-occurrence-is-still-flaky — retry-pass is NOT diagnosis exemption.

Root cause analysis — grepped `wait_for_substring` in src/lib.rs, found `read_captured` at line 151 using `.read_to_string(...).expect(...)`. Rust std `read_to_string` returns `io::Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }` on first invalid byte. Exact match for the observed panic. Mechanism: child stderr captured to tempfile via Stdio::from; child panic + abort interleave can write byte-granular non-UTF-8; harness reads + decodes strict → panic.
Fix applied: read_to_string → read_to_end + from_utf8_lossy.

Empirical confirmation: 30 consecutive iterations of `cargo test ... --ignored` post-fix. Result: pass=30 fail=0. With pre-fix flake rate observable in 1 of 2 push attempts (~50% per-push, lower per-iteration), 30 consecutive passes carries >99% confidence that root cause is mechanically removed — not chance.

Side-channel verification: /tmp/wz-flaky-1.log (one of 30 captured passes) contains 0 U+FFFD replacement characters. So in this measurement window the child stderr was actually valid UTF-8 — the pre-fix flake was driven by a child output mode that fires rarely; the lossy-decode fix protects against future occurrences regardless of frequency.
cargo check -p wz-integration-tests --tests → pass 1.63s. Build clean.

Round 305.decision_summary: R305 introduces ChildGuard RAII wrapper across 9 Layer E tests + 2 unit-test mechanical proofs, eliminating the orphan-subprocess class that caused the R302b push-time .git/run-ci.lock outage.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs::common: new `ChildGuard` struct wrapping `std::process::Child`. `wrap(label, child)` constructs from an already-spawned Child; `child_mut()` returns `&mut Child` for the existing `.kill() / .wait()` call shape; `label()` exposes the spawn-time label for diagnostics. `impl Drop` runs `kill + wait` idempotently — explicit cleanup in the test body still works, and the guard's Drop is the safety net for any panic-unwind path.

9 Layer E tests refactored to wrap every `Command::spawn().expect(...)` in `ChildGuard::wrap(label, ...)` and change `child.kill() / .wait()` to `child.child_mut().kill() / .wait()`: ap_demo_round_trip.rs, wz_initiator_to_zsub.rs, wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor.rs, wz_remote_declare_round_trip.rs, wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs, wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs, wz_publisher_del_to_zsub.rs, wz_query_reply_round_trip.rs, wz_queryable_round_trip.rs. Each wrapped Child uses a short human label (e.g. `"wz-ap-demo acceptor (--listen --declare-token)"`) for forensic logs.

wz_remote_declare_round_trip.rs + wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs: `graceful_terminate(&mut child, ...)` call sites updated to `graceful_terminate(child.child_mut(), ...)`. The helper signature stays `&mut std::process::Child`, so passing through the guard's `child_mut()` keeps SIGTERM-based graceful shutdown working alongside the panic safety net.

2 unit tests in src/lib.rs added: `child_guard_drop_kills_running_child_on_normal_exit` spawns `sleep 60`, wraps in ChildGuard, exits the inner scope, then verifies the PID is gone via `kill -0 <pid>` (exits non-zero on ESRCH). `child_guard_drop_kills_running_child_on_panic_unwind` spawns sleep 60, publishes its PID through `Arc<Mutex<Option<u32>>>`, wraps in ChildGuard inside a `std::panic::catch_unwind` closure, panics, then asserts the captured PID is dead post-unwind. Mechanical proof that the Drop runs on both exit shapes.
verification_bullets: cargo check -p wz-integration-tests --tests → pass 1.41s. All 9 refactored Layer E tests + the rest of the integration suite compile clean.

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --lib → pass. Both new unit tests succeed: `kill: (PID): 그런 프로세스가 없음` (the `kill -0` ESRCH stderr from the post-Drop liveness check) appears in the test stdout, confirming the child was reaped after both the normal-exit and panic-unwind paths.

10 iterations of `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --release --tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1` → pass=10 fail=0 across all 9 Layer E tests = 90 total e2e runs. Sequential `--test-threads=1` keeps PortReservation deterministic; no ChildGuard-related regression observable.
fuser .git/run-ci.lock during measurement → no PID held. No orphan wz-ap-demo / z_sub / stdbuf processes accumulated in `ps -p`.

Round 308.decision_summary: R308 converts wz-ap-demo eprintln! → log::info! across runner.rs + tasks.rs to unify stderr writes through env_logger lock, closing the 5% Layer E e2e flake measured at R307.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: 11 eprintln! sites converted to log::info!. Observer-callback closures (REMOTE SUBSCRIBER / QUERYABLE / TOKEN DECLARED + UNDECLARED, REPLY RECEIVED, FINAL RECEIVED, SUBSCRIBER FIRED, LIVELINESS SAMPLE, QUERYABLE FIRED) all route through env_logger's BufferWriter + io::stderr().lock() path. Pre-R308 the mixed eprintln! / log::info! writes serialised in theory (both acquire the same io::stderr() Mutex) but the empirical 30-trial measurement showed ~3-5% byte-interleave at the LIVELINESS SAMPLE callback fire site. Routing every callback line through env_logger collapses the writers onto a single Mutex<BufferWriter> + write_all(buf) discipline.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/tasks.rs: 5 eprintln! sites converted. declare_task / publisher_task previously had a dup-write pattern on the error path (log::warn! + eprintln! emitting the same message) plus eprintln! on the success-emission lines (DECLARED SUBSCRIBER / QUERYABLE / TOKEN, QUERY EMITTED, PUBLISHER DECLARED, PUBLISHER EMITTED). R308 drops the duplicate eprintln! on error paths (log::warn! already covers them) and converts the success eprintln! to log::info!. Net: 5 eprintln! removed; 5 log::info! added (3 of those replace removed-eprintln on success paths; 0 net-add).

Integration test substring matching preserved by design — env_logger renders each record as `[<ts> <LEVEL> <module>] <message>` and `<message>` carries the pre-R308 line verbatim. Test fixtures (e.g. wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs's wait_for_substring(`LIVELINESS SAMPLE PUT`)) match the substring inside the env_logger-prefixed line without modification.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R308 didn't touch main.rs eprintln! sites — those run BEFORE env_logger::init() (lines ~142-310 are argv-validation paths that exit non-zero). They stay as eprintln! because no env_logger lock exists yet. Plus the ABOUT-line eprintln! at line 379 (immediately after env_logger::init()) stays because it's single-threaded (no race target). No follow-up needed.

Root-cause of the eprintln!/env_logger interleave under default Stderr mutex — both writers theoretically share `io::stderr().lock()`, but the empirical 5% interleave rate indicates the lock is NOT actually shared, OR the env_logger BufferWriter releases the lock between formatting + writing the record's bytes. R308 sidesteps the question by routing every wz-ap-demo write through env_logger, but the underlying std/env_logger interleave question is interesting enough to track. Low priority — 30/30 measurement says the practical fix works. 0.5R analysis follow-up if a future round has spare cycles.

Session::declare_subscriber + SubscribeOptions + Subscriber + SubscribeAliasError stay unconditional in R310 — they wrap the LOCAL pubsub::SubscriberRegistry (inbound Push routing to user callbacks), not the peer-observation RemoteSubscriberRegistry that declare-subscriber gates. The pubsub-side gating belongs to a future pubsub-domain round (R311+ candidate).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Querier::get_matching_status (line 1945) loses its method-level `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")]`. The signature is now always visible whenever `Querier` exists (i.e. whenever `feature = "query-get"` is enabled — the `impl Querier` block-level gate). The body branches: `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")] let matching = { ... obs.remote_queryables.has_matching(&self.keyexpr) };` and `#[cfg(not(feature = "declare-queryable"))] let matching = false;`. The rustdoc records the R310.5c rationale (zenoh-cpp API parity, conservative-false default).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:QuerierAliased::get_matching_status (line 2082) loses its method-level cfg. The `UnknownMapping(id)` validation (resolve_outbound_mapping + ok_or) still always fires — callers see the declare-before-query invariant regardless of feature subset. Only the registry consult is gated; on the success path the method returns `Ok(MatchingStatus{matching:false})` when declare-queryable is off. The composed `_effective_keyexpr` binding takes a leading underscore so the unused-warning is silenced when the registry consult branch is elided.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Publisher::get_matching_status (line 2195) loses its `#[cfg(feature = "declare-subscriber")]`. Same shape: signature always visible (Publisher itself has no cfg gate), body branches on declare-subscriber, conservative false-default when off. The rustdoc records the same R310.5c parity rationale.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:PublisherAliased::get_matching_status (line 2287) loses its method-level cfg. UnknownMapping validation always fires; registry consult body-gated on declare-subscriber; `_effective_keyexpr` underscore-prefix for the elided-branch warning suppression.

Net effect: under `--no-default-features` (no declare-queryable, no declare-subscriber), `Publisher::get_matching_status` and `PublisherAliased::get_matching_status` are now callable (always returning `matching:false`); Querier/QuerierAliased::get_matching_status are callable iff `query-get` is enabled. This matches the zenoh-cpp shape where every Publisher / Publisher_alias / Querier / Querier_alias instance has a `get_matching_status()` method that always answers — whether the runtime actually tracks matching is a build-time question, not an API-surface question.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs imports: `use tokio::task::JoinHandle;` 제거, `use wz::runtime_core::Runtime;` + `use wz::runtime_tokio::runtime_impl::{TokioJoinHandle, TokioRuntime};` 추가. import 블록에 R311at 이유 설명 (TokioJoinHandle .await가 Result<T, RuntimeError> resolve / TokioRuntime.spawn() unit struct 제로 비용 / wz-runtime-lwip+embassy 프로파일이 채움 후 reference binary가 per-profile swap shape 시범 / teardown.rs lockstep 명시).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs spawn 마이그레이션: line 147 writer_handle (wire_link_pipeline), line 431 publisher_handle, line 442 query_handle, line 456 declare_handle, line 666 sweep_task — 총 5건 `tokio::spawn(fut)` → `TokioRuntime.spawn(fut)`. 함수 반환 타입 (wire_link_pipeline tuple 3 element) `JoinHandle<()>` → `TokioJoinHandle<()>`. crates/wz-ap-demo/src/teardown.rs imports: `use tokio::task::JoinHandle;` 제거, `use wz::runtime_tokio::runtime_impl::{TokioJoinHandle, TokioTime};` 합쳤 (TokioTime 기존 import 파이프에 TokioJoinHandle 추가). R311at 이유 설명 주석 첨부 (.abort() surface 보존 + .await Result<(), RuntimeError> 전환, timeout-join 소비자 `let _` discard 이미 있어 consumer-invisible 명시).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/teardown.rs 필드 타입: TeardownInitial.{sweep_task, publisher_handle, query_handle, declare_handle, writer_handle} 총 5개 + TasksJoined.writer_handle + TokenDropped.writer_handle + CloseEmitted.writer_handle + ActionsDropped.writer_handle 총 9개 사이트 `JoinHandle<()>` → `TokioJoinHandle<()>`. typestate 체인 전체가 이제 trait wrapper 관통.

consumer 차이 분석: TokioJoinHandle.poll() → Result<T, RuntimeError> (JoinError는 RuntimeError::JoinFailed/JoinCancelled R257+R266 매핑). teardown.rs step 3 / step 7의 timeout-join 사이트는 기존에도 `let _ = self.clock.timeout(200, h).await;` 패턴으로 결과 무시 — error type 전환 invisible. .abort() API는 TokioJoinHandle에 동일 존재 (R259+ 컨트랙트). 의미론적 일치 입증 완료.

changes_bullets: D1 link-class UDP-first: 5.C enum udp/tcp/serial/ws/raw_eth additive; R311az ships udp only; TCP stateful R311az-alpha cascade
D2 lwIP raw API not BSD socket: udp_new/bind/recv/sendto/remove/disconnect; LWIP_SOCKET=1 rejected (footprint, mandatory pbuf copy break of 5.E zero-copy invariant)

D5 LwipRuntime sync site: LwipLink::recv future polls mpsc rx returning Pending; deploy main loop interleaves sys_check_timeouts and runtime.run_until_idle cooperative non-preemptive
D6 alloc and thumbv6m exclusion: Pin Box dyn Future Send requires alloc; Layer G.4-alloc 6-target subset (M0+ excluded until R311bb portable-atomic CAS polyfill closes ARMv6-M atomic-ptr gap)
D7 netif init is deploy responsibility: wz-link-lwip exposes LwipLink::bind_udp(port) only; lwIP netif_add plus DHCP/static IP plus PHY driver lives in deploy binary (5.K tier separation)
D8 trust_class placeholder for UDP: 5.C domain_attrs.trust_class plus OQ-W22 listener-link lifecycle deferred; R311az UDP single trust=public code path; multi-trust waits on OQ-W22 ratify

Two options: (a) wait for cortex-m-rt's planned ARMv8-M Secure-init feature, (b) inline a __pre_init that runs all-Secure with SAU=0. Decision is a small architectural fork; pick after surveying cortex-m-rt 0.8 plan + the embedded community's mps2-an505 demo template (if any).

changes_bullets: deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs SystickClock: TICKINT bit added (SYST_CSR_TICKINT = 1<<1) + RELOAD changed from 0xFFFFFF (~671ms wrap) to 24999 (1ms reload @ 25 MHz). `wraps` field now represents milliseconds since boot, incremented exclusively from the `SysTick` exception handler; `last_cvr` field + COUNTFLAG accumulation path removed (ISR is the single writer). `now_us` rewritten to a double-snap pattern (load wraps -> read CVR -> load wraps -> retry on mismatch) using Acquire ordering pairs with the handler's Release fetch_add — standard ISR-vs-thread lock-free read for an interrupt-incremented counter + an independently-decrementing hardware counter.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs new #[exception] handler: `#[exception] fn SysTick() { GLOBAL_CLOCK.wraps.fetch_add(1, Release); }` — sole side effect is the wraps increment so the ISR stays minimal (no allocation, no locks, no re-entrant work). cortex-m-rt 0.7's `exception` attribute is imported alongside `entry`.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs main loop: `cortex_m::asm::nop()` -> `cortex_m::asm::wfi()` + comment rewrite documenting the IRQ-driven idle pattern (textbook MCU: cycles only burn during work + tick ISR handling, not in a tight nop spin). R311be's contrary comment ('We deliberately do NOT call wfi() here — QEMU mps2-an386 has no SysTick configured') retired; R311bf's SystickClock was the prerequisite that makes wfi() safe (a SysTick wake source now exists).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs hprintln + PAYLOAD strings: 'R311bf' -> 'R311bi' (echo identity payload bytes change but the round-trip identity test is invariant of payload content; PAYLOAD const is still 29 bytes either side).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs header doc: 'Why SysTick poll mode' section replaced with 'Why SysTick IRQ-driven ClockSource + wfi() main loop' — documents the R311bi reload-value choice (1 ms tick = one ISR per LwipTime::sleep iteration), the wfi() power-down semantics, and the double-snap lock-free read pattern.

publishable_changes_bullets: deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs SystickClock: TICKINT bit added (SYST_CSR_TICKINT = 1<<1) + RELOAD changed from 0xFFFFFF (~671ms wrap) to 24999 (1ms reload @ 25 MHz). `wraps` field now represents milliseconds since boot, incremented exclusively from the `SysTick` exception handler; `last_cvr` field + COUNTFLAG accumulation path removed (ISR is the single writer). `now_us` rewritten to a double-snap pattern (load wraps -> read CVR -> load wraps -> retry on mismatch) using Acquire ordering pairs with the handler's Release fetch_add — standard ISR-vs-thread lock-free read for an interrupt-incremented counter + an independently-decrementing hardware counter.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs new #[exception] handler: `#[exception] fn SysTick() { GLOBAL_CLOCK.wraps.fetch_add(1, Release); }` — sole side effect is the wraps increment so the ISR stays minimal (no allocation, no locks, no re-entrant work). cortex-m-rt 0.7's `exception` attribute is imported alongside `entry`.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs main loop: `cortex_m::asm::nop()` -> `cortex_m::asm::wfi()` + comment rewrite documenting the IRQ-driven idle pattern (textbook MCU: cycles only burn during work + tick ISR handling, not in a tight nop spin). R311be's contrary comment ('We deliberately do NOT call wfi() here — QEMU mps2-an386 has no SysTick configured') retired; R311bf's SystickClock was the prerequisite that makes wfi() safe (a SysTick wake source now exists).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs hprintln + PAYLOAD strings: 'R311bf' -> 'R311bi' (echo identity payload bytes change but the round-trip identity test is invariant of payload content; PAYLOAD const is still 29 bytes either side).

Round 311di-pre-a.decision_summary: R311di-pre-a — wz-runtime-tokio adds hashbrown + portable-atomic deps; session_glue.rs HashMap + AtomicU64 imports route through them; first step toward wz-session-core no_std move-readiness.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: add `hashbrown = "0.15"` and `portable-atomic = "1"` to [dependencies]. Both crates resolve under default features — hashbrown ships foldhash + inline-more + allocator-api2 (match std::collections::HashMap behaviour on AP), portable-atomic forwards to core::sync::atomic when native u64 atomics exist (this crate, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and falls back via critical-section on MCU profiles (wz-runtime-lwip already pulls the same dep per R311bb). The version surface is the same one wz-session-core (R311di proper) will inherit when session_glue.rs / session.rs extract — pulling here first means the extraction is a file-move, not a dep-graph rewrite.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: lines 53-55 import surface lift. `use std::collections::HashMap;` → `use hashbrown::HashMap;` (hashbrown::HashMap is the upstream implementation of std::collections::HashMap — std re-exports it via the alloc crate's collections, so the API surface is byte-identical at the call sites: new() / insert() / remove() / get() / iter() / Entry API). `use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` → `use portable_atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` (portable_atomic::AtomicU64 mirrors core::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 method-for-method; load() / store() / fetch_add() / Ordering enum identical). `use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};` retained for this round — Mutex<T> field types on SessionState route through Session<R>::Mutex<T> GAT at R311di proper (the GAT is already declared on the Runtime trait via R311ar, but the construction-side `Mutex::new(...)` calls on SessionState fields need a `Runtime::new_mutex<T>(t: T) -> Self::Mutex<T>` helper which is a separate ratify) and Arc is a zero-cost relabel (std::sync::Arc and alloc::sync::Arc are the same type) deferred to the same round.

Source-side effect: the 4 SessionState AtomicU64 fields (outbound_frame_sn, next_outbound_request_id, next_outbound_token_id, next_outbound_interest_id at session_glue.rs:865 / 900 / 924 / 949) and 1 HashMap field (outbound_mappings: Mutex<HashMap<u64, String>> at session_glue.rs:882) now hold portable_atomic / hashbrown types respectively. AP semantic unchanged — portable_atomic on x86_64 std forwards to native atomics and hashbrown is the same implementation std re-exports.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/runtime.rs: trait Runtime gains two construction-side methods. `fn new_mutex<T>(value: T) -> Self::Mutex<T> where T: Send + 'static` (complement of with_mutex_mut — generic-R code cannot invoke inherent methods on the GAT type Self::Mutex<T> since the trait declares the type as opaque; the trait method takes ownership and returns the GAT-typed value). `fn new_rwlock<T>(value: T) -> Self::RwLock<T> where T: Send + Sync + 'static` (one tighter bound than new_mutex because shared-read access lets &T cross threads, matching the type-level Self::RwLock bound). Round 311di-pre-f7.decision_summary: R311di-pre-f7 — decision-only round: 4 AtomicU64 fields keep `portable_atomic::AtomicU64` raw across profiles (option b ratified); Runtime trait stays at Mutex + RwLock abstractions only; portable_atomic IS the portable abstraction (option a R::Atomic GAT rejected as over-engineering).
changes_bullets: No source changes — decision-only round per the R311bp pattern (decision_summary records the ratification + atomic store ledger entry; no .rs file mutation). Mirrors the R311di-pre-f6 carry_forward question evaluation: option (a) Runtime trait extension with R::Atomic<u64> GAT + new_atomic + atomic_fetch_add* + atomic_load* methods (cleaner trait surface) vs (b) keep portable_atomic::AtomicU64 raw across profiles (zero added abstraction).

Ratification rationale: portable_atomic IS already the portable abstraction this problem domain needs. AP profile resolves to std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 (hardware atomic instructions on x86/ARM64); MCU profile via the unstable-portable-atomic-critical-section feature resolves to a critical_section-emulated atomic that gives correct semantics on single-core MCUs without hardware atomic ops. Wrapping it inside Runtime adds 4+ trait methods without expressivity gain — every binding would call back to portable_atomic verbatim. The Mutex abstraction earned its trait surface because std::sync::Mutex + critical_section::Mutex have genuinely different APIs (lock + PoisonError vs borrow + RefCell); atomic ops do not have that gap.

Inventory captured for future reviewers: 4 fields (outbound_frame_sn + next_outbound_request_id/token_id/interest_id; session_glue.rs:884/919/943/968) hold AtomicU64 directly. 4 fetch_add sites in the R-generic impl block (line 1343/1364/1383/1402). 4 AtomicU64::new construction sites in the concrete TokioRuntime impl block (line 1121-1125). 11 total portable_atomic references including the module-level import (line 72). All sites stay verbatim; portable_atomic is a workspace dep per R311di-pre-a + pre-b sweep so the dependency surface does not change.

Round 311ek.decision_summary: R311ek shuts the wz-runtime-tokio internal arbitrary-subset gap (north-star mechanism 1): observer ungated to alloc, sample + source_info encoders split out; 4 facade subsets build + new C4b lane.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: the `observer` module gate widened from `all(alloc, codec-declare)` to `alloc` so a codec-push-only subset can compose the bundle (it holds the always-compiled `subscribers` + `replies` registries that pub/sub dispatch needs); the `liveliness_subscribers` field + its import + its `new()` construction now gate on `liveliness-subscriber`, and the four declare consumer features (`declare-subscriber`/`declare-queryable`/`liveliness-token`/`liveliness-subscriber`) now imply `codec-declare` so each gated field's registry type is guaranteed to exist.

New `wz-session-core::source_info_ext` (alloc, no codec gate): `encode_source_info_ext_body` + the shared `pub(crate)` VLE primitive lifted out of the `codec-response`-gated `response_build` module so the `codec-push` body-extension path (`build_body_extensions`) reaches the encoder; `response_build`'s responder encoder re-imports the VLE helper.

New `wz-session-core::declare::liveliness_sample` (alloc): the codec-agnostic `LivelinessSample` / `LivelinessSampleKind` / `LivelinessSampleCallback` split out of the `codec-declare`-gated `liveliness_subscriber` module so the unconditional `Session::declare_liveliness_subscriber{_aliased}` Result-form signatures compile in a codec-declare-off subset; the registry stays gated and re-imports them.

wz-runtime-tokio: `declare.rs` re-exports retargeted (sample types unconditional from `liveliness_sample`, `LivelinessSubscriberRegistry` gated `liveliness-subscriber`, `encode_source_info_ext_body` under `any(codec-push, codec-response)`); the `LivelinessSubscriber` handle's `history_complete`/`undeclare`/`Drop` observer access gated `liveliness-subscriber` (signature-stable fallbacks); `Queryable.session` gated `query-queryable` with a PhantomData arm keeping `R`/`T` live; the `MsgPutOwned`/`MsgDelOwned`/`ExtZbufOwned` imports regated `codec-push` (their `codec-response`/`codec-request` arms were stale after R311dv/R311eh moved the response/request builders to session-core).

New Layer C4b facade arbitrary-incomplete-subset matrix in `scripts/run-ci.sh` + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: cargo-builds the wz facade under four deliberately-incomplete coherent consumer subsets (pubsub-only / queryable-only / zget-reply-only / declare-observer) under deny-warnings — the facade-level analog of C1h that the named-preset C4 lane does not cover.

wz-session-core default build + the C1h arbitrary-subset matrix unchanged-green; the new C4b lane reports all four facade subsets OK.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new scout_trace::ScoutTrace (4 u32 dispatch counters) + scout_params::ScoutParams (version/what/zid); pure value-type siblings of action_trace/session_init_params, kept out of the session bundle (scouting is a pre-session subsystem).

wz-codecs/src/lib.rs wire_const: S_MID_SCOUT (0x01) / S_MID_HELLO (0x02) / FLAG_S_HELLO_L (0x20) scouting-message header bytes, gated codec-scout/codec-hello; disjoint MID namespace from T_MID_*/N_MID_* (scout link vs session link).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/scouting_glue.rs (new, scouting-active): ScoutingActions deps bundle + install_scouting_actions + register_scout_fns binding the four scouting.scxml actions as pure encode/decode+stash (scout_emit / record_hello_and_emit / emit_scout_timeout / diag_scout_tx_failed) + async drive_scouting_until_resolved loop (loop owns all socket IO; SCXML <send delay> serviced via Engine::tick) + new_scouting_engine.
wz-runtime-tokio/src/script_bind.rs (R311eo): bind_unit/bind_guard extracted from session_glue and generalised over the deps type so the scouting glue reuses them (no scouting->session module edge).
scouting-active feature now implies codec-scout + codec-hello (scout_emit/record_hello need both body codecs).

Round 311eq.decision_summary: R311eq adds static scouting mode: ScoutingMode{Active,Static} discriminator + synth_static_locators returning the deploy.connect[] locators verbatim (scouting FSM bypass; no codec/socket/FSM, not scouting-active gated).
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new scout_static module — ScoutingMode {Active, Static} discriminator + from_deploy_str (passive -> PassiveDeferred err, unknown -> Unknown(s); no silent fallback) + synth_static_locators(&[String]) -> Vec<String> returning the deploy.connect[] locators verbatim (trimmed, blank entries dropped).

Static mode is the scouting-FSM bypass (docs/scouting-fsm.md §2.4.3): no scout codec / link / FSM. The module is NOT gated on scouting-active (which gates the active FSM in wz-runtime-tokio) — a static-only deploy compiles the active FSM out and reaches session-open through synth_static_locators alone. Pure alloc value transform placed in wz-session-core (MCU static-deploy usable), the wz analog of zenoh-pico _z_locators_by_config.
6 unit tests cover the mode parse (active / static / passive-deferred / unknown) and synth (verbatim in deploy order / whitespace-trim + blank-drop / empty connect).
verification_bullets: wz-session-core builds clean; the 6 scout_static unit tests pass under Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace runs wz-session-core with its default alloc feature, which gates the module + tests).

Round 311er.decision_summary: R311er adds wz-session-core::locator parse_locator: the mode-agnostic seam turning active-discovered + static-synth locator strings into a typed ParsedLocator{Proto, SocketAddr} via core::net (MCU + AP).
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new locator module — Proto{Tcp,Udp} + ParsedLocator{proto, addr: core::net::SocketAddr} + parse_locator(&str) -> Result<ParsedLocator, LocatorParseError{MissingProtoSeparator|UnknownProto(s)|BadAddress(s)}>.

The mode-agnostic seam: active mode's ScoutOutcome::Discovered(String) and static mode's synth_static_locators(..)->Vec<String> both produce zenoh locator strings; parse_locator turns either into the typed endpoint a link dial consumes, enforcing "a discovered locator is a discovered locator regardless of mode" in one runtime-agnostic place.

Pure core::net + alloc (no std, no socket, no FSM) so it cross-compiles on the MCU static-deploy profile; distinct from wz-codecs::locator (the wire codec). MVP scope = numeric tcp/udp SocketAddr (IPv4/IPv6); DNS / metadata-suffix / other transports surface as parse errors (deferred, not silently mis-parsed).
8 unit tests (tcp/udp ipv4, ipv6 bracketed, missing-separator, unknown-proto, DNS-as-BadAddress, metadata-as-BadAddress, out-of-range-port).
verification_bullets: wz-session-core builds clean; 8 locator unit tests pass under Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace, wz-session-core default alloc gates the module + tests).
full scripts/run-ci.sh 0/A/A2/B/C0/C1/C1b..C1i/C2/C3/C4/C4b/D/E EXIT 0.

Layer G MCU 7-target cross-compile pass — core::net::SocketAddr is no_std (Rust 1.77+, MSRV 1.81), so wz-session-core (and the facade that re-exports it) cross-compile on every Phase W target (G.2 facade + G.5 runtime-lwip OK on all triples).
carry_forward_bullets: parse_locator is the parse half of scouting -> session-open; the dial half (ParsedLocator -> connected TcpDriver/UdpDriver) + the drive-to-Established orchestration are the next step. They are AP-bound (TcpStream::connect / split read+write halves) and reuse the existing drive_session_until_terminal; lifting the demo runner.rs open path into a reusable connect_and_open_session lib API is the bigger follow-on (user-scoped: this round was parser-only).
DNS hostname resolution + locator metadata suffix (#iface=..) parsing are deferred (AP std concern / config tail), surfaced as BadAddress for now.
non-tcp/udp transports (serial/ws/quic/unixsock) extend Proto as those link drivers land.

Round 311es.decision_summary: R311es adds TcpDriver::connect / UdpDriver::connect: the dial half of the scouting locator seam, turning a ParsedLocator endpoint into a connected Initiator-side link driver.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: TcpDriver::connect(addr) -> io::Result<Self> — TcpStream::connect then from_stream; the Initiator-side counterpart to the acceptor-side from_stream, fulfilling the standing open() doc note ('outbound dial flow lands when the Initiator path is wired').

wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: UdpDriver::connect(peer) -> io::Result<Self> — bind an ephemeral local socket (bind address family mirrors peer so an IPv6 locator binds an IPv6 socket) targeting peer for unicast send; distinct from bind_multicast_v4 which joins a scouting group.
Widened the std::net::SocketAddr import cfg from transport-link-udp to any(transport-link-tcp, transport-link-udp) so the tcp connect signature can name the type.

Both constructors consume the numeric endpoint a wz_session_core::locator::ParsedLocator carries: the parse half landed R311er, this is the dial half. The mode-agnostic dispatcher + read/write-split orchestration stay for the next round.

changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-pubsub (Cargo.toml + src/main.rs): a minimal single-purpose e2e consumer binary that pins the pubsub-only foreign-interop facade subset (wz dep default-features off + explicit subset list). Acceptor + literal-keyexpr Put burst + drive-until-terminal/SIGTERM + minimal teardown, using ONLY the public facade pub/sub surface so it compiles under the subset with zero #[cfg]. Textbook single-responsibility — the alternative (cfg-gating the wz-ap-demo monolith for subset builds) is a ~70-site cfg-soup the project rejects. Registered as a workspace member in crates/Cargo.toml.

crates/wz-integration-tests: new wz_e2e_pubsub_to_zsub.rs e2e test (mirrors wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs but drives the subset binary against zenoh-pico z_sub) + wz_e2e_pubsub_binary() locator in the common lib.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer E2 (facade-subset behavioural e2e) drives the wz-e2e-* subset-pinned binaries vs zenoh-pico — the behavioural counterpart of the C4b facade BUILD subset matrix. Layer E now runs `--ignored --skip wz_e2e_` so the subset family runs ONLY in E2 (no test runs twice); header layer-list + run_layer dispatch updated.
.github/workflows/release.yml: build wz-e2e-pubsub (Layer E2 dep) + run Layer E2 steps added after the existing Layer E flow.
verification_bullets: Layer E2 e2e PASS 10/10 consecutive (no-flaky-ever sweep): the wz-e2e-pubsub acceptor's literal-keyexpr Put burst reaches zenoh-pico z_sub's subscriber callback (witnessed by ">> [Subscriber] Received" + the keyexpr + the value substrings).

FINDING — transport-batching is load-bearing for FOREIGN interop: with it off the pubsub subset BUILDS (C4b passes) and two wz peers interoperate (both force batch_size 65535) but zenoh-pico's z_sub rejects the InitAck (FSM closes SentInitAck -> Closed; z_sub logs "Unable to open session!"). Adding transport-batching to the pinned subset fixed the handshake. Only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces this; the build guard (C4b) and the in-process behavioural guard (C1j) both pass without it.
wz-e2e-pubsub builds clean (0 warnings under deny-warnings) under its isolated, feature-unification-free pinned subset (cargo build -p wz-e2e-pubsub).

full run-ci EXIT 0: all required lanes pass, including Layer E (full preset-ap-client demo suite, now run with --skip wz_e2e_) and the new Layer E2 (facade-subset e2e). fmt + clippy clean (the new crate + test; an earlier draft's fmt drift + a doc_lazy_continuation in the test doc were fixed before this run).
carry_forward_bullets: First facade-subset behavioural e2e guard lands (pubsub). Sibling subset binaries (wz-e2e-queryable / wz-e2e-liveliness) follow the same single-purpose-crate shape when their planes need foreign-interop coverage; each pins its own foreign-interop-coherent subset and adds a wz_e2e_* test that Layer E2 picks up.

FINDING generalisation: the foreign-interop-coherent subset is strictly larger than the build-coherent one (pubsub needs transport-batching for the zenoh-pico handshake). The other C4b/C4c/C1j build-coherent subsets may carry latent foreign-interop gaps that only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces — worth auditing as the wz-e2e-* family grows.

FOLLOW-UP (uncaught latent): an isolated `cargo clippy -p wz-e2e-pubsub` (the clippy analog of C3 for subset binaries) surfaces clippy::needless_return at session.rs:1181/1331/1433 — the signature-stability query-get methods whose `cfg(not(query-get))` arm's `return Err(FeatureDisabled)` becomes the function tail under the subset. No current CI lane clips wz-runtime-tokio under query-get OFF, so this is pre-existing + latent, not an R311fg regression. Adding a subset-isolated clippy guard requires resolving these per feedback_signature_stability (prefer cfg over #[allow]) first — coupled follow-up.

Left as-is pending a ruling on whether C4b models build- or interop-coherence; the e2e binary pins the interop-coherent superset regardless.
