Round 311fk.decision_summary: R311fk closes R283: the wz liveliness DECLARER answers an inbound non-final Interest with its held tokens (new LocalTokenRegistry + ResponseSink::send_declare, interest_id-tagged DeclToken + DeclFinal); proven deterministically vs zenoh-pico z_get_liveliness via the new wz-e2e-liveliness-token binary.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new declare/local_token.rs LocalTokenRegistry — the DECLARER-side registry of wz's own held LivelinessTokens (register/unregister + respond_to_interest). On an inbound non-final TOKENS Interest it stages an interest_id-tagged Declare(DeclToken) per held token whose keyexpr intersects the Interest pattern (keyexpr_intersect_patterns) + a terminating Declare(DeclFinal). Gated liveliness-token. 7 unit tests.

wz-session-core observer: new local_tokens field + pending_declares staging buffer (gated liveliness-token); dispatch_event fans the inbound Interest into local_tokens (two-phase stage), flush_pending drains pending_declares through the sink (two-phase drain, mirror of the queryable reply path). response_sink.rs: ResponseSink gains send_declare(DeclareOwned) (gated liveliness-token) + the &S / Arc<S> blanket impls.

wz-runtime-tokio: SessionLinkActions impls ResponseSink::send_declare (the inherent send_declare encodes via encode_frame_with_declare + send_blocking on the reliable channel). Session::declare_token registers (token_id, keyexpr) into observer.local_tokens; LivelinessToken::Drop + undeclare() unregister it. The interest_id-tagged response is the exact shape zenoh-pico's _z_liveliness_pending_query_reply / _z_liveliness_process_declare_final expect (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/liveliness.c:218-256). No SCXML / SCE change — the declare codec already carries the interest_id field + DeclFinal body variant.

New crate crates/wz-e2e-liveliness-token: the DECLARER-side e2e binary (symmetric sibling of wz-e2e-liveliness). Declares its token SYNCHRONOUSLY before the drive loop so the token is registered before any inbound Interest is processed — the deterministic ordering a one-shot CURRENT querier needs (wz-ap-demo declares in a background task gated on Established, too racy for this proof). Pins the liveliness-token declarer subset (handshake core + liveliness-token; no declare-interest — the declarer RECEIVES the always-decoded Interest and REPLIES via codec-declare). Workspace member.

Round 311fl.decision_summary: R311fl review-driven textbook cleanup (no behaviour change): extract wz-e2e-harness lib (4 e2e binaries 977->379 lines, boilerplate dedup, subset-pinning preserved) + centralise inner declaration MIDs in the wz_codecs::wire_const SSOT (byte-identical wire output).
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-harness: shared acceptor scaffolding for the wz-e2e-* family — run_main (env_logger + multi-thread tokio runtime + block_on + ExitCode wrapper), run_acceptor_e2e (bind/accept/open/drive/teardown), OpenedE2e (the {session, clock} surface a setup registers into), AbortOnDrop (publish-task stop), session_init_params, shutdown_signal. Each binary now carries ONLY its CLI parse + a plane-specific setup closure (publish burst / declare_queryable / declare_liveliness_subscriber / declare_token). The 4 binaries' main.rs shrank 977 -> 379 lines (+239 harness); session_init_params + shutdown_signal had been byte-identical 4x.

Subset-pinning preserved: the harness pins ONLY the handshake-core intersection of all four binaries' subsets, so Cargo feature unification resolves each binary's wz to (core ∪ that binary's plane) — the harness adds nothing a binary did not already pin, and its source uses only core APIs so it compiles under the core alone. Each binary still builds + is clippy-clean (deny-warnings) under its isolated pinned subset.

Teardown ordering preserved in the harness: the setup's returned hold is dropped FIRST (RAII unregister / LivelinessToken Drop's UndeclToken emit / pubsub AbortOnDrop) before the action senders close the writer channel — so the R283 liveliness-token UndeclToken-before-writer-close and the pubsub burst-abort semantics are unchanged. The declarer's declare-before-drive-loop determinism is now a structural property of run_acceptor_e2e (setup runs before the loop).

wire_const SSOT: the inner declaration-body MIDs are centralised in wz_codecs::wire_const (gated codec-declare): D_MID_KEXPR/SUBSCRIBER/QUERYABLE/TOKEN (0x00/02/04/06), D_MID_UNDECL_* (01/03/05/07), D_MID_FINAL (0x1A), FLAG_D_N (inline-suffix N), FLAG_N_DECLARE_I (outer Declare interest_id-present I). The 12 session_glue build_declare_* / build_undeclare_* literals and the R283 wz-session-core::declare::local_token builders now reference them.

The context-dependent 0x20 N-flag COMPUTATIONS (wireexpr-N vs declare-N vs interest-C all share the bit) deliberately stay local — DRY applies to the disjoint MID enum, not to a coincidentally-shared bit; forcing them to one const would conflate distinct flags.

Builder unification (#3 of the review) deliberately NOT done: after the wire_const SSOT the proactive build_declare_token and the interest-response build_decl_token_reply share the constants; the two are legitimately different shapes (mapping-id + WireexprNonlocal sibling + interest_id None vs literal-only + interest_id Some), and collapsing them into one over-parameterised cross-crate function would be the wrong abstraction.
verification_bullets: Pure refactor, no wire / behaviour change. The layer3_declare (1) + layer3_inbound_declare (3) wire-byte tests — which pin exact declare bytes — pass, proving the wz_codecs::wire_const consts produce BYTE-IDENTICAL declare output vs the prior per-site literals. The 7 wz-session-core local_token unit tests pass.

All four wz-e2e-* e2e tests pass via the harness (Layer E2). Flake sweeps after the refactor: 20 x 2 on the trickiest two (liveliness-token determinism + pubsub teardown) and 10 x 4 on all four = 0 failures — the harness's hold-dropped-first teardown and setup-before-drive-loop ordering preserve the determinism and the UndeclToken-before-writer-close semantics.
Each of the four binaries builds + is clippy-clean (deny-warnings) under its own isolated pinned subset; the harness builds under the handshake-core subset alone (no plane features).

full scripts/run-ci.sh EXIT 0: all required lanes incl. the C4c/C1j/C4d 7-subset matrices, Layer E (wz-ap-demo suite, which exercises the rewired session_glue declare builders), Layer E2 (4 harness-backed binaries), and the layer3 wire-byte tests. Layer G 7-MCU cross-compile OK (the rewired wz-codecs wire_const + session_glue cross-compile clean; G.6 riscv SKIP env-only). entries 525->526.

Round 311fp.decision_summary: R311fp C4b ruling = DECLINE pinning interop supersets (C4b stays BUILD-minimal; interop supersets live with the wz-e2e-* binaries + Layer E2) + consumer-plane subset SSOT: a single _wz_consumer_plane_subsets map now feeds the facade build lane (C4b) and the crate build/behaviour/clippy lanes (C4c/C1j/C4d), killing the duplicated plane map; queryable-only build promoted to the full plane (codec-response-final), resolving the build-vs-interop name collision and collapsing the 3 historical deltas to one uniform transport-batching base delta.

Before R311fp the facade lane C4b held its OWN copy of the 4 overlapping plane strings while C4c/C1j/C4d shared a second copy = two sources of truth free to drift; now both consume this one map.

C4b (facade BUILD) rewritten to iterate the SSOT, prepending the facade base. Broadened 4->7 planes: handshake-only + liveliness-sub-only + liveliness-token-only are now facade-build-guarded too (previously only the crate lanes guarded them).

C4b base transport-link-udp -> transport-link-tcp: matches the crate base + every wz-e2e-* binary; the prior udp was unexplained drift, not a UDP requirement (facade builds identically on either link feature). Facade base now differs from crate base by exactly runtime-tokio (facade selects a runtime; the crate IS one) + the facade-only forwarding markers keyexpr-literal / transport-keepalive.

queryable-only BUILD extras now include codec-response-final (was query-reply-err only). The name now uniformly means the FULL queryable plane (consistent with declare-observer already being its full bundle); resolves the collision where C4b/C4c said queryable-only=query-reply-err while wz-e2e-queryable interop pinned the reverse. Closes the R311fh codec-response-final gap at the BUILD layer.

_wz_runtime_tokio_coherent_subsets() reduced to a thin wrapper that prepends the crate base to the shared SSOT rows (was the second hardcoded copy). C4c/C1j/C4d unchanged in behaviour, now drift-proof against the facade lane too.

C4b and Layer E2 are different guards; pinning a superset would weaken the over-broad-import guard, duplicate the wz-e2e-* builds, and erase the build-vs-interop distinction E2 exists to show. The 3 historical per-plane deltas (transport-batching R311fg, codec-response-final R311fh, query-reply R311fm) collapse to ONE uniform transport-batching base delta, carried by Layer E2.

Round 311fq.decision_summary: R311fq decouples query-get from query-queryable: the forced feature edge that welded the requester (z_get client) plane onto the queryable (responder) plane is removed, the in-process loopback fan is cfg-gated on query-queryable, and the SSOT zget-reply-only subset becomes a genuine pure getter — closing a north-star arbitrary-composition smell and a SSOT-truthfulness defect the audit-on-pattern carry surfaced.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — query-get edge changed from ["query-reply","query-queryable","codec-request"] to ["query-reply","codec-request"]. The R307 baseline welded query-get->query-queryable so the loopback fan always compiled, but that fused two ORTHOGONAL consumer planes (issue gets vs answer queries) into one forced edge and made the SSOT zget-reply-only composability subset a misnomer (it silently pulled the queryable responder in). Comment rewritten to document the emergent-capability model.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the in-process queryable loopback fan in Session::query (observer.queryables.local_query -> QueryReply -> InboundReply) and Session::query_aliased is now wrapped in cfg(feature = query-queryable); the synthetic loopback Final (deliver_local_final) stays OUTSIDE that gate under query-get, so a wire-only getter (query-queryable OFF) finalises a SessionLocal/Any get immediately with zero local replies (semantically correct: no queryable capability => no local queryable to answer). query_aliased gains a cfg(not(query-queryable)) let _ = loopback_keyexpr since the wire branch routes by (mapping_id, inline_suffix).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the bare use wz_codecs::query::Query and use crate::query::QueryReply imports moved from cfg(query-get) to cfg(all(query-get, query-queryable)) to match their sole call site (the now-gated loopback fan).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — new unit test query_session_local_with_no_queryable_finalises_inline_with_zero_replies guards the invariant the decouple relies on (synthetic Final fires for a SessionLocal get with no matching queryable; deliver_local_final outside the query-queryable cfg). The query-queryable-OFF behavioural twin is the now-genuinely-isolated wz-e2e-zget binary (Layer E2).

No preset change required: every wz facade preset that lists query-get already lists query-queryable explicitly (paired in wz/Cargo.toml), so dropping the implication only changes the arbitrary-subset zget-reply-only case — confirming the edge was redundant for presets and load-bearing only for the composability gap.
verification_bullets: Build isolation (true composability proof): cargo build -p wz-runtime-tokio under the SSOT zget-reply-only subset (codec-response,codec-response-final,query-get,query-reply, no query-queryable) with RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings — compiles clean, 0 dead-code surfaced. cargo tree --edges normal confirms 0 query-queryable nodes (was >=1 before, via the dropped edge).

Real interop (behaviour proof): wz-e2e-zget binary now resolves 0 query-queryable nodes (genuinely isolated wire-only getter); built clean -D warnings, and wz_e2e_zget_round_trip_against_zenoh_pico_z_queryable PASS 3/3 against a real zenoh-pico z_queryable — the isolated getter receives replies from a foreign REMOTE queryable with no local queryable plane compiled in.

All 7 SSOT subsets pass on every composability lane — C4b 7/7 (facade build), C4c 7/7 (crate build), C4d 7/7 (crate clippy), C1j 7/7 (crate behaviour); Layer E2 pass (6 facade-subset e2e incl. zget interop); Layer G 49 cross-compile targets pass. C2 workspace clippy -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean.

New unit test query_session_local_with_no_queryable_finalises_inline_with_zero_replies passes under the default (query-queryable-ON) lane; existing 326 wz-runtime-tokio lib tests + query loopback tests unchanged (the loopback still fires identically when query-queryable is selected, as ap-demo + AP MVP tests select both planes).

NEWLY SURFACED CARRY — C1j behaviour-lane isolation is compromised: wz-runtime-tokio-test-support (a dev-dependency) declares wz-runtime-tokio WITHOUT default-features=false, so during cargo test cargo unifies the crate's DEFAULT feature set (incl query-queryable + all planes) back ON. Every C1j subset therefore compiles+runs the full default feature set, not the named isolated subset — the behaviour matrix provides false isolation assurance for ALL subsets (only the dev-dep-free cargo build C4c/C4b and cargo clippy C4d lanes are genuinely isolated). Textbook fix is large + separate: test-support dep -> default-features=false AND cfg-gate the entire per-plane test surface (session.rs test module references .queryables / pubsub fields unconditionally, so it only compiles under query-queryable-ON today). This blocks a query-queryable-OFF UNIT test of the wire-only getter; the gap is currently covered by C4c build + wz-e2e-zget Layer E2 interop.

audit-on-pattern decode-arm dimension is CLEAN and CLOSED: the R311fm/fn cross-plane-gate bug class has exactly one structural instance (reply.rs Reply Put/Del body decode, the sole wire body shared across two consumer planes), already fixed at arm (R311fm) + unit-test (R311fn) layers; all other inbound decode arms are plane-exclusive (Push=pubsub, Query=queryable, Declare variants=per-registry). Round 311gp.decision_summary: R311gp gc-3a: switchboard static generator foundation -- wz-switchboard-schema + wz-switchboard-codegen pure lib (forge-ast.v1 ingress events -> closed no-heap match, build-validated).
changes_bullets: New crate wz-switchboard-schema: no_std+alloc serde model of wz-switchboard.yaml (SwitchboardSpec{machine, bindings:[Binding{keyexpr,event}]}) -- the single shape both the AP dynamic SwitchboardRegistry loader and the MCU static generator bind to. Leaf data crate, no format backend pinned (YAML/JSON chosen at each consumer's I/O boundary), deny_unknown_fields.

New crate wz-switchboard-codegen: PURE transformation lib (no process/IO) -- generate(SwitchboardSpec, MachineFacts) -> Rust source for a closed no-heap dispatch_switchboard match; parse_machine_facts deserializes only the forge-ast.v1 statechart subset (v / kind / name / external_ingress_events) per docs/SCE_FORGE_AST.md + apis/forge-ast.v1.schema.json. Logic in a pure lib (not a build.rs) so validation + emission are unit+golden testable.

Validation = W3C SCXML 3.12.1 event-descriptor matching of each Binding.event against the machine's external_ingress_events (SCE's documented event-injection contract, drift-proof: SCE owns the reserved-family filter). Build errors: UnknownEvent, MachineMismatch, non-canonical Keyexpr, NotStatechart, UnsupportedAstVersion -- never a silent runtime no-op.

Emission reuses wz-session-core SSOT: canonize_keyexpr at build time (strict-reject where the runtime registry merely warns) + keyexpr_match::keyexpr_pattern_matches (no-alloc, BoundedVec-backed) over &'static str chunk literals. Mirrors SwitchboardRegistry::dispatch (every matching row fires in declaration order; signal path injects empty _event.data). No canonicalization/matching reimplemented.

Both crates added to crates/Cargo.toml workspace members (grouped with wz-statechart-bridge in the statechart domain). build.rs orchestration (shell-out sce-codegen --emit-ast + OUT_DIR include) and a real example machine deferred to gc-3c; the pure-lib boundary means that wiring -- and any future SCE in-process statechart API -- only changes the thin I/O layer, not the validated logic.
verification_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: 11 unit+golden tests pass -- parse_machine_facts (v1/kind/empty-ingress), W3C 3.12.1 descriptor matching (exact / token-boundary prefix / trailing .* / non-match / reverse), generate happy-path byte-exact golden, plus UnknownEvent / MachineMismatch / non-canonical-keyexpr rejects, prefix-descriptor accept, empty-switchboard constant-zero emit.
wz-switchboard-schema: 3 tests pass (serde round-trip, deny_unknown_fields reject of a typo'd key, keyexpr/event field-name contract).
cargo clippy --all-targets on both crates clean under workspace deny(warnings); cargo build --workspace green -- no regression to the existing 22 crates (purely additive members).

Empirically confirmed sce-codegen --emit-ast on a real statechart (sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml) emits ast.document.external_ingress_events as an 18-event closed set with error.* filtered -- the generator's input contract is verified against SCE, not assumed.

carry_forward_bullets: gc-3b (next): value path -- extend wz-switchboard-schema with an optional payload-decode field + wz-switchboard-codegen to emit a typed EventSchema decode -> _event.data (forge-ast.v1 imported_event_schemas). This is the serialization SSOT deferred from gc-2; deserves its own round of design care.

A future AP dynamic loader (wz-runtime-tokio, std) deserializes wz-switchboard.yaml via wz-switchboard-schema to populate SwitchboardRegistry -- the schema crate is the shared SSOT, ready for it.

Long-term-ideal surfaced (non-blocking, SCE-owner decision): SCE exposing the statechart codegen+forge-ast pipeline in-process would remove the build.rs shell-out; the pure-lib boundary is designed so that change would touch only the I/O layer.

Round 311gq.decision_summary: R311gq gc-3b: switchboard generator value path -- typed raise_<event> via generated <Machine>Inject; typed_inject_events gate + EventSchema/codec multi-doc join + codec-superset cross-check; pin c16811a9b.
changes_bullets: wz-switchboard-schema: Binding gains an optional `codec` field -- None = signal binding (empty _event.data, gc-3a behaviour); Some(name) = value binding naming the wire forge codec. skip_serializing_if so existing signal-only sidecars stay byte-stable. Value round-trip test added.

wz-switchboard-codegen: MachineFacts + parse_machine_facts gain `typed_inject_events` (forge-ast.v1 pin c16811a9b) -- the eligibility SSOT. A value binding gates on event-in-set rather than re-deriving SCE's native-lowering rule (primitive-only schema + guard-read); the absent-event case is a build error (EventNotTypedInject).

wz-switchboard-codegen: new EventSchemaFacts + CodecFacts + parse_event_schema_facts / parse_codec_facts -- the multi-doc join the consumer feeds (each imported EventSchema doc + each codec doc forge-ast). Fields parsed as id + SceType (primitive string vs non-primitive opaque). forge-ast does NOT carry imported_event_schemas (serde-skip), so the join is wz-side.

wz-switchboard-codegen: generate() reworked to take GenInput {spec, facts, schemas, codecs, machine_module}. Branches signal-only (gc-3a `&mut dyn EventInjector` shape, byte-identical sans marker) vs value-bearing (`&mut Engine<{Machine}Policy>` + `use {Machine}Inject;`). Value row: decode payload via `SceCursor::new` + `{codec}::decode`, field-map into `{Machine}{Variant}Payload`, call `engine.raise_<event>(payload)`. wz-owned codec-fields-superset-of-schema cross-check (SchemaFieldNotInCodec) so the wire format and the _event.data view cannot drift.

wz-switchboard-codegen: SCE naming filters to_pascal_case / to_snake_case mirrored (forge-ast stays language-neutral; the two published filters are the contract, loud-fail-backstopped, unit-pinned). 4 new CodegenError variants (EventNotTypedInject / MissingEventSchema / CodecNotFound / SchemaFieldNotInCodec). Crate module doc updated (gc-3a/gc-3b, signal+value).

Round 311gr.decision_summary: R311gr gc-3c: switchboard value path wired e2e in wz-switchboard-example -- build.rs runs sce-codegen (statechart+schema+codec) then the generator; first real compile + runtime smoke of the typed value path.
changes_bullets: New example crate wz-switchboard-example -- the first consumer of the gc-3a/gc-3b generator, wiring the value path end to end. sources/: sensor_monitor.scxml (statechart with a native typed guard `_event.data.celsius_centi > 3000` + `<sce:import kind="event-schema">`), temp_update_schema.scxml (EventSchema, celsius_centi uint16), temp_payload.scxml (codec, big-endian uint16). wz-switchboard.yaml: a temp_update VALUE binding (codec=temp_payload) + a reset SIGNAL binding.

build.rs orchestrates: shell-out `sce-codegen -l rust --emit-ast` over the three docs (mirrors wz-runtime-tokio/build.rs, the documented public path) -> sensor_monitor_sm.rs + temp_payload.rs + three forge-ast JSONs; strip_inner_attrs makes the _sm.rs / codec.rs include!-able; parse_machine_facts / parse_event_schema_facts / parse_codec_facts + serde_yaml_ng read of the sidecar; wz_switchboard_codegen::generate(GenInput) -> dispatch_switchboard.rs in OUT_DIR.

lib.rs: pub mod sensor_monitor + pub mod temp_payload (include! + outer #[allow] restoring the generator's stripped inner-attr budget, per wz-runtime-tokio) + crate-root include! of the dispatch (so its sensor_monitor:: / temp_payload:: refs resolve). New `alloc` feature forwards to sce-forge-runtime/alloc (the codec gates its heap encode facade on feature=alloc). Added to crates/Cargo.toml workspace members.
feature-inventory §5.20: caveat appended recording gc-3c wired the generator into a build with the value path verified e2e.
verification_bullets: cargo build -p wz-switchboard-example green = the FIRST real compile of a value-path dispatch -- the generated `engine.raise_temp_update(SensorMonitorTempUpdatePayload { celsius_centi: decoded.celsius_centi })` type-checks against SCE's actual Engine<SensorMonitorPolicy> + SensorMonitorTempUpdatePayload + temp_payload::TempPayload (the gc-3b golden asserted only the emitted string).

4 smoke tests pass (runtime end to end): hot (wire 3500 -> codec decode -> raise_temp_update -> native `_event.data.celsius_centi > 3000` guard fires -> Hot), cold (2000 -> guard misses -> Idle), reset (signal binding -> raise_external_by_name with empty data -> Idle), unmatched keyexpr -> 0 injected.

cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean; cargo build --workspace green (the new member integrates; build.rs reuses the existing sce-codegen binary the wz-runtime-tokio build already requires).

Probe-confirmed before wiring (direct sce-codegen runs): standalone event-schema emit-ast yields kind/event_name/fields; the statechart AST carries typed_inject_events=['temp_update'] + external_ingress=['reset','temp_update']; the generated SensorMonitorInject / raise_temp_update / SensorMonitorTempUpdatePayload names match the gc-3b to_pascal_case / to_snake_case mirrors exactly.
validate_workspace: §5.20 caveat added; sections 257 unchanged, entries 551->552, T1 orphan=0 (new=+0), round-trip 13/13, T3 warn 862 unchanged, GENERATED.md=sync.
carry_forward_bullets: AP dynamic value path: the runtime SwitchboardRegistry (wz-runtime-tokio) is still signal-only; extend it to decode -> raise_external_typed so AP and MCU share one guard semantics (SSOT across profiles). The gc-3c example proves the static/MCU shape; the dynamic shape is the remaining half.

String/Bytes payload fields: the gc-3c example uses a primitive uint16; native-eligible EventSchemas also allow String/Bytes, whose codec decode produces borrowed views (lifetimes on the decoded struct) -- the field-move emission + a borrowed-codec example are a follow-up.

Live demo: the example is a unit-level smoke (hand-laid wire bytes + a directly-driven Engine). A full wz-ap-demo wiring -- a real zenoh peer publishing temp samples through the ApplicationLayerObserver fan-out into the switchboard -- is the next composability milestone.

Multi-codec switchboards: generate() handles N value bindings over N codecs; the example exercises one value + one signal row. A multi-event example would exercise the join over several EventSchema + codec docs.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core `switchboard::EventInjector` gains a defaulted `inject_value(event_name, payload) -> bool` (the value shape of the same cohesive, SCE-free ingress port -- not a second port: a value injector necessarily owns the one `&mut Engine` borrow the signal path needs, so the borrow checker forbids splitting them). Signal-only impls inherit the `false` default, so the bridge `EngineInjector` and every gc-2c consumer ripple zero.

`SwitchboardEntry` gains a value/signal routing kind; `register_value()` mirrors a yaml `Binding` carrying a `codec`; `dispatch` routes value rows to `injector.inject_value(name, sample.payload())` (counting only on a successful decode -- byte-for-byte the static arm's `if let Ok(decoded)` semantics) and signal rows to `inject(name, "")`.

wz-switchboard-codegen refactors the value-arm decode+raise into a generated per-event `inject_<event>` helper (one decode body, deduped across keyexprs targeting the same event) shared by BOTH the static `dispatch_switchboard` arms (MCU) and a NEW generated `{Machine}Injector` newtype that impls `EventInjector` (signal via `raise_external_by_name`, `inject_value` matching `event_name` -> helper). The codec/payload-union mangling stays encapsulated in the generated injector (ACL); the static arm collapses to `if match && inject_<event>(payload, engine)`.

wz-switchboard-example enables `wz-session-core/switchboard` and adds 4 AP-dynamic smoke tests that drive the SAME machine through a runtime-populated `SwitchboardRegistry` + the generated `SensorMonitorInjector`, asserting state outcomes identical to the static `dispatch_switchboard` tests.

Structure note: the registry stays type-erased + non-generic (no `StatePolicy` leak into the SCE-free session-core tier); genericity over the machine lives behind the port in the generated injector. This refines R311gr's carry premise (which framed the registry itself decoding) -- the textbook split keeps the ACL/DIP boundary intact while the value path still reaches `raise_external_typed`.

Round 311gt.decision_summary: R311gt: switchboard value path handles scalar string/bytes payload fields -- the generated dispatch deep-copies the codec's borrowed &str/&[u8] view into the owned String/Vec<u8> payload struct via .into().
changes_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: new `owned_field_move(sce_type, expr)` threads `.into()` for a scalar string/bytes schema field. SCE decodes a scalar string/bytes codec field as a borrowed view (`&'a str` / `&'a [u8]`, lifetime tied to the wire buffer) but the native-lowered `<Machine><Variant>Payload` struct holds it owned (`String` / `Vec<u8>`, no lifetime -- it derives Clone+Default and outlives the buffer once queued). `.into()` bridges the two with the target inferred from the struct field's known type, so no alloc/std path is named and the one shared helper compiles on both the AP (std) and MCU (no_std+alloc) tiers. A primitive (Copy) field moves verbatim, keeping the primitive-only golden byte-identical.

wz-switchboard-codegen: the typed_inject_events MachineFacts doc corrected -- the native-lowerable schema rule is "non-enum" (primitive plus scalar string/bytes fields), not "primitive-only" (verified against SCE schema_is_native_payload_eligible, which rejects only SceType::Enum).

wz-switchboard-example: sensor_monitor adds a native string guard (hot --temp_update[_event.data.sensor_id === 'kitchen']--> alarm) + an alarm state, so the decoded value is observed semantically -- proving the borrowed-view -> owned field-move delivered the right value, not just that it compiled.

Round 311gu.decision_summary: R311gu: bump vendor/sce pin c16811a9b -> 1474bd0a9, landing the SCE all-6-backend fix for the per-state native-guard-index collision (multi-state typed _event.data guards) + clippy 1.96 clears.
changes_bullets: vendor/sce pin c16811a9b -> 1474bd0a9 (+13 commits). Lands SCE 87ab3ccac "Co-locate native _event.data guard on its owning transition": all 6 codegen backends keyed the native typed-guard map by a per-state transition_index, so two states each carrying a native `_event.data` guard at the same local index collided in the machine-global map (the later-inserted guard won, mis-rendering the other transitions' guard). SCE now carries the rendered guard on Transition::native_payload_guard (no index lookup) + a cross-state regression fixture asserted across all 6 backends.

The fix corrects the wz-switchboard-example sensor_monitor: its `hot --temp_update[_event.data.sensor_id === 'kitchen']--> alarm` guard was mis-rendered as `ev.celsius_centi > 3000` (idle's guard won the shared index-0 key) under the prior pin; it now renders `ev.sensor_id == "kitchen"` correctly. This retroactively makes the R311gt alarm_sample_branches_on_decoded_string test valid (it now genuinely depends on the decoded string, not a coincidental celsius>3000).
Also lands clippy 1.96 lint clears (relevant to this rustc 1.96 host) + pre-push embed/MANIFEST drift hooks (SCE-internal chores).

wz-switchboard-example: new non_kitchen_hot_sample_stays_hot discriminating/regression test -- a hot non-kitchen sample (celsius 3600 > 3000) must STAY hot because the hot->alarm guard reads sensor_id, not celsius. Round 311ha.decision_summary: R311ha: gc-3 carry #2 CLOSED -- live switchboard value-path e2e: a real zenoh-pico z_put to demo/sensor/temp drives the demo's app machine idle->hot through the production session + observer + switchboard.
changes_bullets: New Layer E e2e test wz-integration-tests/tests/ap_demo_switchboard_inbound.rs: a REAL foreign peer (zenoh-pico z_put CLI) publishes a temperature sample to the demo's switchboard value keyexpr (demo/sensor/temp), and the demo's session inbound -> ApplicationLayerObserver switchboard fan-out -> generated SensorMonitorInjector decodes the wire payload into the typed _event.data and drives the application machine idle -> hot. Asserts the demo stderr line `APP SWITCHBOARD FIRED ... app_state=Hot`. Mirrors the ap_demo_round_trip harness (spawn demo --listen, wait "listening on", z_put -e tcp client, wait the marker, SIGTERM).

Test data note: zenoh-pico z_put -v takes a STRING value, so the wire payload is the literal ASCII bytes; temp_payload decodes a big-endian uint16 from the first two bytes, and every printable ASCII byte is >= 0x20, so any two-character value decodes to celsius_centi >= 8224 -- over the 3000 guard. The value "OK" (0x4F4B = 20299) therefore reaches Hot. SUB-threshold discrimination (a cold sample that must STAY idle) needs arbitrary wire bytes the CLI cannot express, so it stays covered by the in-process fan-out test (R311gz); this e2e owns the live-wire plumbing proof.

Layer-classification: named ap_demo_* (full preset-ap-client wz-ap-demo, Layer E) rather than wz_e2e_* (the facade-subset family Layer E2 drives against wz-e2e-* binaries). Round 311j.decision_summary: R311j codec-request wire-layer cascade — request envelope + Query inner body gated; query-* implies codec-request; send_request_query body-cfg.
changes_bullets: wz-codecs/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = []` feature added + appended to default. Caveat scopes the gate: SCXML codegen for request envelope + Query inner body + matching `pub mod` blocks; downstream wz-runtime-tokio session_glue.rs Request wire surface + 6 build_request_query_* + encode_frame_with_request + RequestQueryBuilder + NetworkMessage::Request variant + parse arm.

wz-codecs/build.rs — `request` and `query` stems routed to `CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_REQUEST` env-var check + matching `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed` line. Single match arm via `|` pattern covers both stems.
wz-codecs/src/lib.rs — `pub mod query` and `pub mod request` blocks gated `#[cfg(feature = \"codec-request\")]`. Query is the Request body inner type so they share the codec-request gate.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = [\"codec-frame\"]` declares the third body-codec-implies-envelope edge (after R311h codec-push and R311i codec-declare). wz-codecs Cargo dep features gain `\"codec-request\"` so the consumer module (query.rs / reply.rs / session.rs Query/Queryable/Reply APIs) always have the request/query types available. `codec-request` appended to the default feature list.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — query-get / query-queryable / query-reply features gain `[\"codec-request\"]` implication so toggling a high-level query feature on automatically pulls codec-request on (query-get retains its existing implications + adds codec-request).

wz/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = [\"wz-runtime-tokio?/codec-request\"]` facade forward replaces the previous placeholder. Same wire-layer scope as R311h/R311i; consumer module (query.rs/reply.rs/session.rs) stays compiled — R311m architectural round for the consumer side.

session_glue.rs — `use wz_codecs::query::Query;` cfg-gated. `use wz_codecs::request::{Request, RequestVariant};` cfg-gated. `wz_codecs::timestamp::Timestamp` import gated on `any(codec-request, codec-push)` (consumed by RequestQueryBuilder + push metadata setters). `N_MID_REQUEST` const gate broadened from `codec-frame` to `codec-request` (the request envelope is now its own atomic body codec).

session_glue.rs — 6 `pub fn build_request_query*` builders cfg-gated on codec-request (principled exemption: return type `Request` is itself feature-gated): build_request_query / build_request_query_with_consolidation / _with_parameters / _with_attachment / _with_timeout_ms / _with_target. 1 `pub fn encode_frame_with_request` cfg-gated. `RequestQueryBuilder` struct + impl block cfg-gated.

session_glue.rs — `NetworkMessage::Request(Box<Request>)` enum variant cfg-gated. `Self::Request(_) => f.write_str(\"Request(..)\")` Debug arm cfg-gated. `parse_frame_payload` `wire_const::N_MID_REQUEST => { ... }` match arm cfg-gated.

session_glue.rs — send_request_query + send_request_query_with_meta SessionLinkActions methods retrofit to signature-stable + body-cfg shape per R311g1 / `feedback_signature_stability` MEMORY note. Both `()` returning so body-cfg branch silently no-ops when codec-request off; matching peer's z_get future hangs until per-call timeout fires (documented minus-codec-request contract). `let _ = (args)` suppresses unused-variable warnings on the disabled branch.

Implication chain extended: codec-request = [codec-frame] is the third body-codec-implies-envelope edge after codec-push (R311h) and codec-declare (R311i). Handshake-only-deploy contract closure progresses: codec-frame OFF now requires codec-push + codec-declare + codec-request OFF; R311k will add codec-response = [codec-frame] to complete the closure.
verification_bullets: cargo check matrix — default-features clean; --no-default-features (minus-all-codecs) clean. The Cargo implication chain (query-* implies codec-request) auto-pulls codec-request when query features are on so the body-cfg branch of send_request_query is mechanically reachable.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib: 589/589 pass — unit-test baseline preserved.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean.
cargo fmt --all --check: clean.
Layer E lane — wz_publisher_to_zsub 30-trial flake-0 confirms the Request wire emit + parse path stays bit-identical under the cfg cascade (pure refactor).
validate_workspace: entries 328→329, sections 255, T1=0, RT 13/13, sync.
carry_forward_bullets: R311k codec-response cascade — wire-layer gates for Response/ResponseVariant/Reply/Err imports, N_MID_RESPONSE const, build_response + encode_frame_with_response + reply/err builders, NetworkMessage::Response variant, parse arm. send_response body cfg per R311g1 pattern. Also includes the deferred R311e signature-deletion retrofit on build_response_final / encode_frame_with_response_final / send_response_final per R311g1 signature-stability pattern. codec-response = [codec-frame] imply. After R311k codec-frame elision becomes coherent (every body codec implies codec-frame so codec-frame OFF → handshake-only deploy: Init / Open / Close + KeepAlive).

R311m consumer-module cascade — the deferred pub/sub / declare-consumer / query-consumer / reply-consumer module gates. session.rs Session::publish + declare_subscriber{_aliased} + Subscriber struct + Drop + observer.rs subscribers field + declare/ subscriber.rs/queryable.rs/liveliness.rs/liveliness_subscriber.rs equivalents + query.rs QueryableRegistry + reply.rs ReplyRegistry + observer.rs queryables/replies fields. Architectural cascade distinct from per-cascade locality deferral.

Type-ungating carry forward unchanged — session.rs API surface (declare_querier / declare_queryable / declare_token / declare_liveliness_subscriber + QueryOptions builder methods) + ResponseFinal-using helpers. Blocked on type-gate elimination; R267 Session<R,T> reparam architectural pivot is the natural carrier.

Tier 3 measurement automation carry forward — extend scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh + CI Layer F to auto-verify each codec-* feature has a non-trivial mechanical delta WHEN the dependent high-level features are ALSO turned off (the imply chain makes single-feature elision misleading at the catalog level). Multi-feature elision lanes (e.g. `minus-codec-request --features=no-query-*`) become the truthful measurement for body codecs after R311h..R311k cascade closure.

changes_bullets: No code change. Assessed watching-zenoh vs zenoh-pico from zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_* (37 flags, config.h.in) + wire MIDs (transport.h) + wz actual code/tests (2 Explore surveys + direct reads).

Parity result: client-over-TCP/UDP ~90% (pub/sub, query/queryable, declare/undeclare, liveliness token+subscriber, scouting, keyexpr all wire-byte-compatible vs zenoh-pico per layer3_* + wz-e2e-* vs zenohd); zenoh-pico DEFAULT-feature build ~70-75%; everything incl default-OFF optional ~50-55%.
NOTE: the wz catalog active=63/143 (~46%) is a DIFFERENT denominator - it includes non-pico MS3+ atoms (router/storage/SHM/QUIC), so it is NOT the zenoh-pico parity number.

Corrected a stale survey claim: the multicast cluster (Rounds A-H, pushed 340b591) is DONE - session FSM + per-peer FSM (addr-keyed, zenoh-pico _z_find_peer_entry parity) + Join beacon + RX classify + lease sweep; transport-multicast is ACTIVE. NOT 'stub/absent'.

Confirmed remaining gaps by direct grep: batching (only batch_size MTU negotiation, no real msg-grouping), auto-reconnect (comments only), fragmentation (codec+dispatcher present, AP drive-loop + e2e incomplete), multicast DATA plane (transport done, Frame-payload->subscriber delivery NOT wired), liveliness-get + query-source-info-rx (stubs).
verification_bullets: Evidence base: ~/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/config.h.in (37 Z_FEATURE_* flags) + protocol/definitions/transport.h (MIDs) + src/transport/multicast/rx.c (_z_find_peer_entry by addr); wz layer3_*.rs wire-byte-compare tests + crates/wz-e2e-* round-trips vs zenohd; claudedocs/composability-audit-2026-06-05.md.

carry_forward_bullets: NEXT-WORK PRIORITY (ratified) - finish UNICAST robustness FIRST (client-over-TCP/UDP is the common deployment, ~90%->100%): (A2) fragmentation completion = wire the reassembly dispatcher into the AP drive loop + a >1-MTU payload e2e; (A3) batching = collect N network messages into one transport frame + flush; (A4) auto-reconnect = re-dial + re-handshake on link loss.

THEN (A1) multicast DATA plane = decode multicast Frame PAYLOAD and deliver to the subscriber/queryable registries (pub/sub over multicast) - the layer above the transport peer-attribution Rounds A-H added.
SMALL wins: liveliness-get (CURRENT token snapshot); query-source-info RX (codec exists, add the receive arm); matching-listener callback.
THEN (B, optional - pico default-OFF too): TLS/serial/WS/BT links, advanced publisher/subscriber, admin space, RX cache, multicast declarations.
NOT zenoh-pico parity (pico itself lacks): router/routing, storage, full access-control, SHM, gossip scouting, QUIC/vsock/unixsock - these are wz north-star MS3+ only.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core `sn.rs` NEW: zenoh-pico `transport/utils.c` mirror (`mask_from_res` / `half` / `precedes` / `decrement` / `increment`), pure no_std unconditional; half-window SN ordering SSOT (first consumer = multicast data plane).

`multicast_dispatch.rs`: `PeerSlot` gains `sn_mask` + per-channel `rx_sn_reliable`/`rx_sn_best_effort`; `ingest_join` signature gains `JoinSnBaseline` (sn_res + next_sn pair) and seeds baselines via decrement (the §3.2 `init_rx_seq` effect point, realised; re-seeds on refresh JOIN per pico `_sn_rx_sns` copy); NEW `ingest_frame_by_src(src, reliable, sn, now)` -> `FrameIngest` (Admitted / OutOfOrder / UnknownPeer / SessionNotRunning) applying the half-window gate per channel; OutOfOrder still refreshes lease (pico sets `_received = true` BEFORE its SN gate - liveness independent of data validity).

`multicast_glue.rs` (wz-runtime-tokio): `decode_join` full-body decode (decode_join_zid now a thin projection); NEW `validate_join` (§3.2 rejection rules: version + sn_res compat, absent sn_res = own default); JOIN RX arm validates before `ingest_join`; `T_MID_FRAME` arm now decodes via `parse_inbound`, admits via `ingest_frame_by_src`, parses payload via `parse_frame_payload`, and fans `IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload)` through the NEW `on_event: FnMut(IterationEvent)` parameter of `drive_multicast_session` (the unicast `drive_session_until_terminal` observer-fan mirror - one `ApplicationLayerObserver` serves both transports); malformed/unknown-peer/stale frames dropped without touching the session FSM.
`MulticastParams` gains `seq_num_res` (own 2-bit resolution; multicast has no negotiation, mismatched JOINs are ignored).
wz-runtime-tokio Cargo: `transport-multicast` forward gains `codec-frame` (kconfig select - the data plane is the point of a transport; consumer arms stay per-feature like unicast).

Round 311jy.decision_summary: F2 reconnect-window send gate: SessionLinkActions.transport_available gates the dispatch chokepoint - data sends inside the RECONNECTING window reject SendWireError::TransportUnavailable (pico _Z_ERR_TRANSPORT_NOT_AVAILABLE parity) instead of vanishing into the dead writer channel.
changes_bullets: `SessionLinkActions` gains `transport_available: R::Mutex<bool>` (initial true): `false` at `release_link` (FSM Closing/Closed entry) + `reset_for_reopen` (supervisor re-dial window), `true` at `record_established_at` (Established (re-)entry, right before the supervisor replay).

`dispatch_network_message` (the R311jq chokepoint every network-message send routes through) returns `Result<(), SendWireError>` and gates on the flag: a data send inside the RECONNECTING window rejects `SendWireError::TransportUnavailable` (zenoh-pico `_Z_ERR_TRANSPORT_NOT_AVAILABLE` parity — pico's tx fails on the dead transport's mutex/NULL where wz's writer-channel enqueue silently swallowed bytes). Handshake INIT/OPEN/CLOSE + KeepAlive transport messages bypass the chokepoint and stay ungated.

6 typed `dispatch_*` wrappers -> Result; ~31 call sites threaded: Result-returning senders propagate (`?` / `SendDeclareError::from`), `()`-returning drain surfaces (`send_response`/`_final`, undeclares, interest-final, declare replies) drop-with-comment (no error channel; the reject lands where the dead link loss landed before, now deterministic); `replay_one` maps into `ReplayDeclarationsError`.

New variants: `SendWireError::TransportUnavailable`, `SendDeclareError::TransportUnavailable` (+ `From<SendWireError>`), session-tier `PublishError`/`PublishAliasError`/`QueryAliasError`/`LivelinessAliasError::TransportUnavailable`; `LivelinessGetError`/`LivelinessSubscriberAliasError` map to their existing `NotEstablished` (same contract). wz-ap-demo publisher logs-and-skips the new reject.

session_reconnect_e2e (real TCP sever -> re-dial -> replay) PASS with the gate live — the supervisor cycle re-opens the gate via record_established_at exactly before replay.

deferred_fire cell backlog (R311lg-pre commit): DeferredListenerCell::invoke grows a FIFO backlog — an invoke that finds the callback mid-fire on another drainer hands the call to the active drainer instead of dropping it (the prior documented skip), making multi-drainer overlap lossless; required because this round introduces auxiliary drainers (query-tail drain + wz-ap-demo sweep-task drain) beside the drive loop; invoke signature gains Send + 'static (4 existing call sites move-capture)

reply/final plane: query / query_aliased route (on_reply, on_final) into a deferred cell holding the BoxedReplySink pair; the registry-stored staging sink copies each inbound reply to the owned InboundReply (the existing AP retention form — no third reply struct) and stages per-fire jobs; the staged on_final job kills the cell after firing (Final is terminal, user closures drop outside every lock); query tail calls drain_deferred_fires so SessionLocal loopback replies still deliver synchronously before query returns (pico _z_session_deliver_query_locally caller-thread parity)

changes_bullets: R311lf delivery round (c) — the queryable plane, the last ratified data plane: declare_queryable{_aliased} install a staging sink (owned query copy: keyexpr/parameters/attachment/source_info/rid/is_local); the handler runs at the drain OUTSIDE the observer lock over a QueryResponder bound to a job-local buffer, then routes replies by origin — wire queries emit through actions directly, local queries deliver into the local reply registry (their deferred reply fires drain in the same pass); handler signature unchanged

Reply-before-Final restructure: the dispatch SSOT (dispatch_iteration_event_with) stages each matched request's ResponseFinal as a deferred-fire JOB contiguous with the handler jobs (same observer lock window) instead of flushing finals under the lock — a drainer executes a taken batch sequentially, so per-rid ordering is structural and drainer-identity-independent (an auxiliary query/publish-tail or sweep drainer stealing the batch preserves it); observer grows flush_pending_replies + take_pending_final_rids, the combined flush_pending stays the raw-registry / MCU drain

Final trigger fix (live gap, pico parity): QueryableRegistry::dispatch_messages keys the Final on the MATCH count (fire_matching_queryables/dispatch_request/local_query now return it), not the staged-reply delta — a matched-but-silent inline handler previously sent NO Final and starved the querier until timeout (zenoh-pico emits the reply Final on query-object drop regardless of reply count); non-Query bodies and un-resolvable keyexprs still owe nothing

QueryView grows is_local (default false; BorrowedQuery field) — the pico _z_query_t._is_local parity the deferred job routes replies by; QueryResponder::new public constructor for the job-local responder

query/query_aliased local sequencing: the loopback Final is delivered AFTER the tail drain ran every deferred local handler (then a second drain fires on_final) — on_final after every local on_reply, the pico deliver-query-locally emit-final-at-tail ordering preserved across the deferred shape

changes_bullets: session review of the R311lf..li data-plane deferral cascade (lf ratify + lg/lh/li the 4-plane implementation): lf/lg/lh verdict textbook — no hack / doc-around-hack / workaround; SSOT axes hold (single DeferredFireQueue, owned-staging reuses Sample::from_view / InboundReply / QueryResponder / into_response with zero third structs, dispatch SSOT strengthened); li carried one real defect (Finding A below), closed in this same round

Finding A (real, li-introduced) CLOSED: the Reply-before-Final ordering li claimed as structural held only when a stealing drainer acquired the observer lock first; an auxiliary drainer taking the queue with the queue lock ALONE (drain_deferred_fires / publish / query / sweep tails) could mem::take a half-staged dispatch window — a queryable handler job staged before its trailing ResponseFinal job — and emit the Final ahead of the handler's last Reply on the wire

fix = observer-serialized batch take (NOT the FinalGuard the review floated): DeferredFireQueue::take_batch + Session::drain_deferred_fires wraps each take in the observer lock; since every stage() runs inside the staging site's observer-lock window, an observer-serialized take observes only whole numbers of complete windows, so [handler, final] always land in one batch on one drainer in FIFO order; jobs still RUN outside the lock (the lock is held only across the cheap Vec swap), preserving the lock-free callback invariant. Chosen over FinalGuard (pico query-rc-drop parity) because it is a localized lock-discipline fix with an obvious invariant vs a cross-layer per-request refcount threaded through sink->job + a raw-path double-emit interaction; FinalGuard is now unnecessary (the Final stays a staged job emitted by the existing send_response_final)

secondary cleanup: publish / publish_aliased drain only on the allows_local path — a Remote-only publish stages nothing, so its prior unconditional drain was gratuitous (ran drive-loop-staged callbacks on the publish thread); now a method drains iff it staged

self-contained DeferredFireQueue::drain_and_fire retained (queue lock only) for single-thread fixtures (the deferred_fire_infra unit tests) where no concurrent stager exists; its doc states the non-serialized caveat

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply { declare: DeclareOwned } variant (gated liveliness-token, the sole producer; it implies declare-token -> codec-declare) + loop TX arm (mint reliable SN -> encode_frame_with_declare -> multicast_frame_or_fragments, reliable).

MulticastReplySink intentionally does NOT impl LivelinessGetPrune: the get-prune concern is the session-reconnect declaration-cache prune, and the connectionless multicast transport (JOIN + lease, no re-dial) has no cache to prune. The loop drains via the narrow flush_query_replies + flush_declare_replies, not the 3-concern flush_pending - honoring the R311lq ISP split rather than stubbing an empty LivelinessGetPrune.

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastResponseSink renamed MulticastReplySink - it now drains two concerns (query reply + declare interest-response), so the "Response" name was a misnomer.

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastReplySink impls DeclareReplySink (send_declare_token_reply / send_declare_final_reply build the owned Declare via build_token_reply / build_final_reply .try_into_owned() and enqueue MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply) - mirror of the unicast SessionLinkActions: DeclareReplySink.

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply { declare: DeclareOwned } variant (gated liveliness-token, the sole producer; it implies declare-token -> codec-declare) + loop TX arm (mint reliable SN -> encode_frame_with_declare -> multicast_frame_or_fragments, reliable).

MulticastReplySink intentionally does NOT impl LivelinessGetPrune: the get-prune concern is the session-reconnect declaration-cache prune, and the connectionless multicast transport (JOIN + lease, no re-dial) has no cache to prune. The loop drains via the narrow flush_query_replies + flush_declare_replies, not the 3-concern flush_pending - honoring the R311lq ISP split rather than stubbing an empty LivelinessGetPrune.

Round 311lv.decision_summary: R311lv review fix (Finding 1+3): §3.1 multicast RxDispatch extracted to shared wz_session_core::multicast_rx::dispatch_multicast_inbound; AP + MCU loops de-duplicated; wire_const via session-core re-export.
changes_bullets: Finding 1 (SSOT): the §3.1 multicast RxDispatch classify+dispatch (JOIN admit / Frame admit-and-fan / KeepAlive refresh) - duplicated across the AP multicast_glue and the MCU multicast_drive loops - extracted to a new wz_session_core::multicast_rx::dispatch_multicast_inbound (+ the MulticastRxNext enum). Both loops now call the one SSOT; each keeps only its reassembly-divergent tail (Fragment reassembly / out-of-order chain abort / pre-Close chain abort), handed back via MulticastRxNext, since those touch a profile-specific reassembly Router the runtime-agnostic SSOT does not own. This realises the engine-free contract both loops state ("every decision PRIMITIVE is the shared wz_session_core SSOT; the loops own only the IO + clock structure").

Round 311lw.decision_summary: R311lw Finding 2: run_session #[allow(too_many_arguments)] retired via a SessionDriveConfig param object (timeouts/role/max_iters), the unicast sibling of MulticastDriveConfig.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip session_drive.rs: introduce SessionDriveConfig { timeouts, role, max_iters } - the static parameterization of one run_session drive, separated from the loop's live collaborators (the runtime / link / driver / actions / clock handles + the on_event observer) via Introduce-Parameter-Object. run_session drops from 9 args to 7 (runtime, link, driver, actions, clock, config, on_event) and the #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] the prior signature carried is removed. The body destructures config into the local names at the top, mirroring how the two multicast loops handle MulticastDriveConfig.

All three fields are Copy (SessionTimeouts derives Copy, SessionRole is a Copy enum, max_iters is Option<usize>), so SessionDriveConfig owns them by value and carries no lifetime - unlike wz_session_core MulticastDriveConfig, which must borrow its non-Copy params (the Vec-bearing MulticastParams). The HandshakeDeadlineTracker::new(*timeouts) deref becomes a by-value pass.

SessionDriveConfig is defined LOCAL to wz-session-lwip (next to SessionRole + run_session), not hoisted into wz-session-core: run_session is the MCU-only unicast loop (the AP unicast drive_session_until_terminal has a different shape), so unlike MulticastDriveConfig it is not shared across both transport profiles. Exported via the wz_session_lwip lib pub use; it reaches the facade through the existing pub use wz_session_lwip as session_lwip.

Round 311lx.decision_summary: R311lx Round A: multicast TX emit extracted to shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (MulticastTxItem + multicast_tx_emit, the TX twin of multicast_rx); AP loop de-duplicated to call it.
changes_bullets: New wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (the TX twin of R311lv's multicast_rx): MulticastTxItem (moved from wz-runtime-tokio) + MulticastTxFrames + multicast_tx_emit(item, &mut TxSn, &MulticastParams) -> MulticastTxFrames. The §3.1 TxData decision (item variant -> mint -> encode_frame_with_* -> multicast_frame_or_fragments) now has ONE home consumed by both transport profiles' loops, realising the engine-free contract for the egress half - it was inline-duplicated in the AP loop, the same smell R311lv removed for RX. Module gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc); the per-variant body codecs (codec-push/response/response-final/liveliness-token) gate the enum variants + emit arms; the emit fn is union-gated so it exists only when a body codec inhabits the item.

multicast_put_literal moved alongside MulticastTxItem (it composes the session-core build_push_literal SSOT, so it belongs with the shared item type). Both re-exported from wz_runtime_tokio::multicast_glue via pub use, so the AP loop's public TX API + its tests are unchanged by the move.

wz-runtime-tokio multicast_glue de-duplicated: the inline 4-arm outbound match (Push/Response/ResponseFinal/DeclareReply, ~110 LOC) replaced by a multicast_tx_emit call + a send loop, so the AP loop now owns only the IO (the mpsc recv + the async LinkDriver::send). The emit import + the outbound Some(item) arm are union-gated, with a not(union) `match item {}` arm preserving the uninhabited-item build (matching the prior per-codec import gating; no robustness regression). The encode_frame_with_* / multicast_frame_or_fragments / build_response_final / push_build imports retired from the loop (the SSOT owns them); build_token_reply / build_final_reply stay (the AP MulticastReplySink composes them before enqueuing).

ResponseFinal now routes through multicast_frame_or_fragments like the other three variants (one uniform egress path): byte-identical (a single tiny VLE rid never reaches the budget, so it returns its one frame with no follow-on mint) but it removes the special-case arm and keeps params + tx_sn used by every arm, so the union-gated emit fn has no unused-parameter edge in any single-codec config.

Round 311ly.decision_summary: R311ly Round B: MCU multicast TX seam - run_multicast_session next_tx pull-callback feeds the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT (z_put over the group); 8->7 args via clock-derivation, no #[allow].
changes_bullets: wz_session_lwip::multicast_drive::run_multicast_session gains the application TX publish seam (the R311lu/lv carry): a next_tx: FnMut() -> Option<MulticastTxItem> pull-callback, symmetric with the on_event push-callback - the MCU busy-poll mirror of the AP loop's tokio mpsc outbound receiver. Each iteration, right after the JOIN beacon and before the lwIP pump, the loop drains pending outbound items and frames each through the SAME shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx::multicast_tx_emit SSOT (R311lx) the AP loop calls, multicasting the datagrams via send_to_group so they ride that iteration's run_until_idle. The MCU multicast loop now emits app data, not only the JOIN beacon.

The TX emit + the mut tx_sn binding are gated on codec-push (wz-session-lwip's only forwarded TX body codec); a codec-free transport-multicast build leaves MulticastTxItem uninhabited, so the seam stays in the signature - next_tx is consumed by a not(codec-push) `if let Some(item) = next_tx() { match item {} }` - without an unused-parameter or unused-mut lint, so the RX-only multicast build is unchanged.

New wz-session-lwip `codec-push` feature forwards wz-session-core/codec-push (orthogonal to transport-multicast; a publishing multicast node enables both). build_push_literal needs only codec-push, so multicast_put_literal builds a literal-keyexpr Put with no extra pub/sub feature.

Adding next_tx took the loop to 8 args (clippy too_many_arguments 8/7). Resolved NOT with #[allow] (the hack R311lw just removed from run_session) but by dropping the redundant clock parameter: the multicast loop derives its monotonic clock from the runtime it already pumps (LwipTime::new(runtime)). Unlike the unicast run_session (R263 external clock to share the actions clock-clone epoch) or the AP loop (ambient tokio, no runtime param), the multicast loop has no actions bundle, so an external clock was a redundant re-derivation. 7 args, no #[allow].

Deterministic real-lwIP test run_multicast_session_publishes_a_put_over_loopback (codec-push): a queued Put is framed + multicast, echoed by multicast loopback, admitted at our own source via a pre-injected distinct-zid JOIN (the §3.2 source-keyed peer entry), and observed by on_event as a Push - a true TX -> loopback -> RX round trip, frozen-clock deterministic.

Round 311ma.decision_summary: R311ma: MCU multicast observer staging - MulticastReplyQueue (no_std DeclareReplySink, mirror of AP MulticastReplySink); observer flush_declare_replies -> queue -> next_tx auto-reply to Interest.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip gains MulticastReplyQueue (wz_session_lwip::multicast_drive), the no_std MCU mirror of the AP loop's MulticastReplySink: an Rc<RefCell<VecDeque<MulticastTxItem>>> (the single-task busy-poll analogue of the AP's tokio mpsc - on_event pushes, next_tx pops, same thread, so no cross-thread Send) implementing DeclareReplySink. The observer drains its staged liveliness interest-response replies into it (flush_declare_replies); the sink owns the encode by building the owned Declare via the shared build_token_reply / build_final_reply SSOT (the same wire shape the unicast SessionLinkActions: DeclareReplySink derives) and enqueues a MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply. Clone shares the backing store between the on_event + next_tx closures; pop() drains FIFO for the next_tx seam.

Per the R311lq interface segregation the queue implements ONLY DeclareReplySink - the concern a liveliness declarer drains. It does NOT implement LivelinessGetPrune (the connectionless multicast transport has no reconnect declaration cache to prune, same rationale as the AP MulticastReplySink). The queryable ResponseSink reply chain is deliberately NOT here: it names wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned, a codec type this MCU crate does not yet dep, and needs the query-queryable registry forward - carried as the follow-on.

New integration test run_multicast_session_stages_observer_declare_replies_into_next_tx (liveliness-token): an inbound liveliness Interest (CURRENT, interest id 9) for a held local token (build_interest_liveliness_get + encode_frame_with_interest, injected at the JOIN-advertised SN 0) is dispatched to the observer, which stages a DeclToken + terminating DeclFinal; the on_event closure flushes them through the queue's DeclareReplySink into the shared queue, and next_tx drains both - asserting exactly 2 DeclareReply items reached the seam (observer -> sink -> next_tx). The MCU mirror of the AP drive_loop_emits_liveliness_token_reply_over_multicast.

The test asserts on the DRAINED items, not a loopback echo: the injected Interest at SN 0 advances the shared source peer entry past our reply mints, so an echoed DeclToken at our tx SN 0 would be SN-stale-dropped (a loopback-observation artifact, not a bug). Round 311mb.decision_summary: R311mb: MCU queryable observer staging - MulticastReplyQueue impls ResponseSink (query-queryable + wz-codecs dep); box large MulticastTxItem variants to fix large_enum_variant + shrink MCU queue.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip's MulticastReplyQueue (R311ma) now also implements ResponseSink (the queryable reply chain), completing the MCU observer-staging mirror of the AP MulticastReplySink: the observer drains its staged query replies (flush_query_replies -> Response + terminating ResponseFinal, reply-before-final) into the queue, the loop's next_tx seam drains them out. So a registered queryable on the MCU now auto-replies to an inbound Query over the group, as the liveliness declarer (R311ma) does for an Interest. The type's gate widened from liveliness-token to the reply-variant union any(codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token); each producer-trait impl stays gated by its own codec family (ResponseSink any(codec-response, codec-response-final); DeclareReplySink liveliness-token).

New wz-session-lwip query-queryable feature forwards wz-session-core/query-queryable (the QueryableRegistry + codec-request for inbound Query decode + codec-response). codec-response now ALSO forwards wz-codecs/codec-response, and a wz-codecs direct dep (default-features=false, alloc) is added SOLELY so the ResponseSink::send_response signature can name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned (the one wz_codecs type this MCU crate references; the declare / push arms use inferred owned types). Mirrors how wz-runtime-tokio deps wz-codecs for the AP reply path.

New integration test run_multicast_session_stages_observer_query_replies_into_next_tx (all(query-queryable, codec-response, codec-response-final)): an inbound Query (rid 7, at the JOIN-advertised SN 0) for a registered queryable is dispatched to the observer, whose handler stages a Response; flush_query_replies drains it + its terminating ResponseFinal through the queue's ResponseSink into the shared queue, and next_tx drains exactly one Response + one ResponseFinal. Asserts on the drained items (the injected Query at SN 0 advances the shared peer entry past our reply mints, so a loopback echo would SN-stale-drop - the same artifact the liveliness sibling avoids).

Boxed the large MulticastTxItem variants (R311mb): Push -> Box<PushOwned>, Response -> Box<ResponseOwned>, DeclareReply -> Box<DeclareOwned> (the small ResponseFinal, a bare rid, stays inline), mirroring NetworkMessage's own Box<PushOwned> / Box<ResponseOwned> / Box<DeclareOwned> in the same crate. changes_bullets: The wz facade now weak-forwards the multicast feature cluster to wz-session-lwip, so a session-lwip consumer reaches the MCU multicast drive loop + observer staging without naming wz-session-lwip directly. Six features gained a wz-session-lwip?/ forward alongside their existing wz-runtime-tokio?/ (AP) one: transport-multicast (run_multicast_session + MulticastReplyQueue), codec-push / codec-response / codec-response-final (the TX body codecs multicast_tx_emit frames), and liveliness-token / query-queryable (the DeclareReplySink / ResponseSink observer-staging registries). The ?/ weak-forward stays inert unless session-lwip is also enabled, so AP-only builds are unchanged - the transport-keepalive R311kx forwarding shape.

run-ci G.11 (the facade session-lwip cross-real lane) gains two facade builds proving the forwards cfg-in the MCU multicast loop THROUGH the facade on real MCU targets. Build 3 (Arc-free: transport-multicast + TX codecs + query-queryable) cross-compiles on EVERY Phase W target including thumbv6m - the queryable observer-staging ResponseSink is Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>>-backed, so it rides M0. Build 4 ADDS liveliness-token but SKIPS thumbv6m: this surfaced that liveliness-token pulls the deferred_fire module (Arc over R::Mutex, target_has_atomic=ptr), which the lib.rs gate documents as the host/atomic-only "thumbv6m Arc-free envelope". The build respects that boundary (the same invariant the deferred_fire gate states: no Layer G MCU cross lane enables a deferred-fire arm).

This is the FIRST MCU cross-compile of the R311ma/R311mb multicast observer staging (C1m only host-tested it). It revealed: queryable staging (query-queryable / ResponseSink) is M0-compatible (Arc-free); liveliness staging (liveliness-token / DeclareReplySink) is NOT - the observer's declare-reply path pulls deferred_fire, whose MCU inline-fire alternative is not wired for the multicast observer drain. liveliness MCU staging works on every ATOMIC Phase W target (M3 / M4F / M23 / M33 / M55 / RISC-V); only thumbv6m (M0, ARMv6-M) is excluded.

Cargo.toml + run-ci.sh only, no source change - the MCU loop + sinks already exist (R311lt..R311mb); the facade is a feature-edge re-export layer. Pre-existing unrelated facade gap, untouched (out of scope): runtime-tokio,transport-multicast WITHOUT transport-unicast fails to compile (wz-runtime-tokio's unicast session_glue is unconditionally built but its session modules are session-unicast-gated).

The + liveliness-token superset cross-compiles on every ATOMIC target (verified thumbv7em M4F) and is correctly skipped on thumbv6m by the G.11 conditional (the deferred_fire Arc envelope). The plain session-lwip facade build is unchanged.

Round 311md.decision_summary: R311md: reply-sink SSOT - generic MulticastReplySink<Q> + MulticastReplyEnqueue in wz-session-core; AP/MCU give only a backing; dedups the sink impl + drops wz-session-lwip wz-codecs dep.
changes_bullets: New wz-session-core module multicast_reply_sink (gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc) - the multicast_tx gate): a generic MulticastReplySink<Q> + a MulticastReplyEnqueue trait. The "given a ResponseSink / DeclareReplySink call, which MulticastTxItem does it become" construction (the build_*_reply + try_into_owned + Box::new + variant choice) lives here ONCE - the TX-staging twin of the multicast_rx (RX dispatch) and multicast_tx (TX emit) SSOTs. ResponseSink (codec-response / codec-response-final) + DeclareReplySink (liveliness-token) are impl'd once for MulticastReplySink<Q: MulticastReplyEnqueue>; Q decides only HOW each constructed item is queued for the loop.

Before R311md the AP MulticastReplySink (wz-runtime-tokio) and the MCU MulticastReplyQueue (wz-session-lwip) duplicated those four trait methods byte-for-byte except the enqueue line (tx.send vs queue.push_back). Both collapse to a MulticastReplyEnqueue backing: AP TokioReplyBacking (wraps UnboundedSender, enqueue = send) + pub type MulticastReplySink = MulticastReplySink<TokioReplyBacking> (the public name is preserved); MCU MulticastReplyQueue becomes the Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>> backing (enqueue = push_back, keeps pop() for next_tx). The observer drains MulticastReplySink::new(backing.clone()); the loop pops the backing.

wz-session-lwip's wz-codecs DIRECT DEP (added R311mb only to name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned in its duplicated send_response signature) is REMOVED, and its codec-response feature no longer forwards wz-codecs/codec-response: the ResponseOwned-named send_response now lives in wz-session-core (which already deps wz-codecs), and the backing's enqueue takes the already-constructed MulticastTxItem. So the dep was a pure symptom of the duplication - folding the impl removed both. The MCU backing crate names no codec type.

Behaviour-identical: no wire / FSM / SN / construction change - only the home of the 4 trait methods moved from two crates to one generic. AP multicast_glue reply tests + MCU observer-staging tests updated to drain through MulticastReplySink::new(queue.clone()) instead of the queue directly (the queue is now the enqueue backing, not the sink). The R311lz DeclareReply loopback test fully-qualifies alloc::boxed::Box::new (the top-level Box import moved out of wz-session-lwip with the impls).

changes_bullets: lib.rs: the deferred_fire module #[cfg] collapses from all(feature="alloc", any(deferred-fire, session-matching, declare-subscriber, declare-queryable, liveliness-token, liveliness-subscriber, query-reply)) to feature="deferred-fire" alone (the feature implies alloc). Root cause closed: liveliness-token in the gate forced `use alloc::sync::Arc;` (deferred_fire.rs:101) to compile on the MCU multicast profile; thumbv6m (ARMv6-M) has no target_has_atomic="ptr", so the otherwise-unused module failed to build (E0432 unresolved import alloc::sync). Round 311mf.decision_summary: R311mf: MCU multicast Fragment RX/TX - the AP R311kn/ko arms ported to run_multicast_session: reassembly RX wiring + a transport-fragmentation feature that splits TX via the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-lwip/src/multicast_drive.rs: run_multicast_session now wires the reassembly-divergent RX tail through the shared wz-session-core SSOT, the MCU twin of the AP loop's R311kn arm. Under `reassembly` a per-(slot,channel) Router (mcu_reassembly = ReassemblyDispatcher<4,4096>, the same run_session owns) is built before the loop; the FrameOutOfOrder arm aborts the channel's in-progress chain (reasm.abort_channel via peer_index_by_src), the Fragment arm parses the inbound T_MID_FRAGMENT (parse_inbound -> InboundFrame::Fragment) and reassembles via ingest_multicast_fragment (per-peer SN gate -> chain -> the completed message fans as the SAME FramePayload Poll a whole Frame does), and the Close arm aborts the departing peer's chains before close_by_src. The sweep arm becomes sweep_with(now, abort_peer_chains) + sweep_reporting under `reassembly`, the bare sweep otherwise. Without the feature the arms keep the prior drop-Fragment behaviour (pico fragmentation-off).

crates/wz-session-lwip/Cargo.toml: a new `transport-fragmentation` feature = [reassembly, wz-session-core/transport-fragmentation] forwards the core umbrella (reassembly + codec-fragment + alloc) and re-uses this crate's reassembly forward for the wz-runtime-lwip Router. No drive-loop code change for TX: run_multicast_session already frames its next_tx seam through the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT, which splits an oversize payload via multicast_frame_or_fragments once the feature is on - exactly as the AP loop. The MCU TX port was a feature forward; the fragmentation SSOT was already shared (R311ko).

Test run_multicast_session_reassembles_a_fragmented_put_over_loopback (gated transport-fragmentation,codec-push): the real-lwIP fragment leg. A 200-byte z_put at batch_size 64 is proven to fragment (>1 datagram via a direct multicast_tx_emit probe), multicast to the group, echoed back, and reassembled by the Fragment RX arm into one observed Push (no ReassemblyDropped). The pre-admitted peer JOIN advertises batch_size 64 to match self: validate_join admits only when the JOIN's batch_size equals the receiver's params, else the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop.

scripts/run-ci.sh: C1m gains a transport-multicast,reassembly arm (the reassembly RX path composing WITHOUT fragmentation) + a transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push arm (the round-trip), test + clippy each. G.11 cross-real adds a wz-session-lwip transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push build on every non-riscv target - the reassembly Router + TX splitter cross-compile on thumbv6m (Vec-backed, no Arc), the M0 fragment reach.
verification_bullets: Full host run-ci + Layer G (WZ_RUN_LAYER_G=1): RUNCI_EXIT=0 (read from the trailing exit-code line, not a pipe/tee-masked tail). "run-ci: all required layers pass", no FAIL lines.

Layer C1m pass: the new transport-multicast,reassembly + transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push arms (test + clippy each) pass alongside the existing multicast lanes; the fragment round-trip test passes (5 tests in the fragmentation build).

Root cause found during bring-up + recorded: the first round-trip failed silently (saw_push false, no drop event) because validate_join (multicast_join.rs) rejects a JOIN whose batch_size != the receiver's params; the pre-admitted peer was on the default 2_048 while self ran 64, so the peer was never admitted and the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop. A direct-drive diagnostic (admit + feed the 5 probe fragments through dispatch + ingest) confirmed the SSOT completes (completed=1, dropped=0) once batch_size matches; the fix set the peer JOIN's batch_size to 64.

G.11 session-lwip cross-real OK on all 6 ARM targets incl thumbv6m-none-eabi (the new fragment build); riscv32imac SKIPs on the missing toolchain. A standalone thumbv6m cross-build of -p wz-session-lwip --features transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push returns 0 - the fragment path is Arc-free (M0-safe). fmt --check + clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean for the new arms.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/multicast_rx.rs: two new SSOTs close the session-review Finding B (the dispatch CLASSIFY was already shared via dispatch_multicast_inbound, but the reassembly TAIL wiring was hand-mirrored byte-for-byte in the AP multicast_glue + MCU multicast_drive loops). dispatch_multicast_inbound_reassembling wraps the classify + applies the full tail (FrameOutOfOrder -> abort_channel, Fragment -> parse_inbound + ingest_multicast_fragment, Close -> abort_peer_chains + close_by_src) with the caller's Router; sweep_multicast_reassembling does the deadline-reclaim-report + evict-with-chain-abort pair. Both gated all(reassembly, alloc); the Router type stays caller-owned (profile-specific pool dims), passed by &mut.

crates/wz-session-core/src/{drive.rs,reassembly_dispatch.rs}: sweep_reporting RELOCATED from the session-unicast-gated drive module to reassembly_dispatch (next to ReassemblyDispatcher). It is a pure reassembly helper (no unicast actions / runtime generic, unlike its ingest twin report_outcome_reassembling which stays in drive); housing it in drive would have forced sweep_multicast_reassembling to gate on session-unicast - a false coupling (multicast does not need unicast). Now gated all(reassembly, alloc) at its true home.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multicast_glue.rs + crates/wz-session-lwip/src/multicast_drive.rs: both loops drop the ~30-line duplicated tail match + the duplicated sweep pair, replaced by one dispatch_multicast_inbound_reassembling call (reassembly build) / a bare dispatch_multicast_inbound + Close-only match (non-reassembly), and one sweep_multicast_reassembling call / bare sweep.
