Round 311tr.decision_summary: R311tr: revert the tp face-establishment zid-dedup -- it broke the pure acceptor/router (legitimately holds N same-zid faces; the demo's fixed fixture zid exposed it). The single-source faces map + dial-intent dedup stay; the two-faces-one-zid hazard re-tracks to the graph layer.
changes_bullets: run-ci Layer E3/E5 caught the regression (RUNCI_EXIT=1, masked by a wrapper echo -- the 'judge by unpiped exit code' lesson): wz_router_holds_two_concurrent_peers + 2 wz_router_forward FAILED. Two demo --connect initiators share the fixed fixture zid 0x01020304 (only --peer derives a distinct zid), so the establishment dedup dropped the second face.

Root cause: the establishment dedup was the WRONG LAYER -- in the shared face_drive_loop it applied to the pure acceptor/router (NoOpForwarder, no routing graph), which legitimately holds N faces. The two-faces-one-zid hazard is a ROUTING-GRAPH concern (add_link/remove_link key the self-edge on zid).

Reverted the Step::Opened zid-dedup; KEPT the held_zids->faces:BTreeMap single-source collapse (clean; the value is read by the dial-intent dedup) and the dial_decision dial-intent dedup (autoconnect-only, never touches the acceptor).

The two-faces-one-zid corruption re-tracks as a PRE-EXISTING graph-layer debt: make add_link/remove_link zid-aware (refcount links per zid, or remove the self-edge only when the last link to a zid drops) -- fixes it at the source without touching the transport-agnostic face loop.

Round 311tt.decision_summary: R311tt: §5.16 access-control first atom — port zenoh's 3-part interceptor subsystem (pure AclPolicy engine + interceptor seam/chain + ACL enforcer adapter) after a 3-agent adversarial review refuted the original inline plan; keyexpr_includes_target is the verified intersection-vs-inclusion correctness fix.
changes_bullets: Adversarial calibration (the recurring textbook?/SSOT?/north-star? trigger): 3 independent agents (architecture / SSOT / honesty) REFUTED the original inline plan; the 2 load-bearing findings were re-verified by direct read before acting.

Verified correctness fix: zenoh ACL matches by directional INCLUSION (interceptor/authorization.rs:603/615 nodes_including, rule keyexpr ⊇ message keyexpr), NOT intersection. Reusing keyexpr_intersects_target would have shipped a security defect (rule `home/*` does not include `home/**`, yet the two intersect). wz already had keyexpr_includes_patterns documented "awaiting a routing/aggregation caller" — the ACL is that caller.

wz-access-control (new pure crate = zenoh authorization.rs analog): Permission / AclMessage(Put) / AclFlow(Ingress) / SubjectSelector(Any|Zid) / AclRule / AclConfig / AclPolicy::decision (deny-first → default → allow). Kernel/driver split (autoconnect precedent); std AP-only; deps wz-routing-graph(Zid) + wz-session-core(matcher). No message types.

keyexpr_includes_target (wz-session-core keyexpr_match.rs): the directional rule⊇msg entry point mirroring keyexpr_intersects_target (same candidate-split + malformed-target guard), wiring the previously-unconsumed keyexpr_includes_patterns. A regression-guard test locks the divergence from intersection.

interceptor/{mod,access_control}.rs (zenoh interceptor/mod.rs + access_control.rs): Interceptor trait + InterceptorChain (admit = all) + AclInterceptor enforcer adapter (per-kind match, Put arm live, rest pass-through). Consulted ONCE at the top of forward()'s message loop, ahead of the kind-dispatch — a single composable seam, not an inline if-deny per message arm (the review's central fault).

LinkstateForwarder wiring: an empty-default interceptor chain (= access control disabled, zenoh AclConfig.enabled=false) + set_acl_policy config seam (set_gossip_target/enable_autoconnect family) + a per-face IngressContext (subject zid via peer_zid_routing + alias-aware keyexpr resolve via resolve_wireexpr) + an acl_denied witness counter.

demo --acl-deny <keyexpr> opt-in (mirrors --autoconnect): builds an allow-default + ingress-Put-deny AclPolicy and calls set_acl_policy, so the enforcement is LIVE in a binary, not inert (the inert-in-all-binaries debt the session review flags).
verification_bullets: wz-access-control 6/6 (decision table: default permission, deny-first, allow-on-deny-default, zid-subject scoping, cross-flow non-apply). keyexpr_match 16/16 incl includes_target_is_directional_not_intersection (the divergence regression guard). interceptor adapter 4/4 (deny / admit / Del-ungoverned / no-subject). wz-runtime-tokio routing-peer lib 381/381 incl 2 forwarder relay-enforcement tests (a denied Put is not counted as data and not relayed to the interested child + acl_denied witness; a selective allow still relays).

clippy -D clean (wz-access-control, wz-runtime-tokio routing-peer, wz-ap-demo routing-peer); fmt clean; base (non-routing-peer) build clean — the interceptor module is gated out, no regression to the MCU/base surface.

Full run-ci all required layers pass, judged by the unpiped RUNCI_EXIT=0: Layer A/A2/A3 (validate-workspace orphan 13 unchanged), the C* host test lanes, Layer Q MCU (mps2-an500 + microbit + multicast-e2e all PASS; keyexpr_includes_target adds +12B text on multicast-e2e, within the ±256 tolerance), Layer Z zenohd interop 9/9.
carry_forward_bullets: R311tt = §5.16 access-control first atom, built to the textbook structure from the start (the 3-part zenoh interceptor subsystem port). Scope = INGRESS Put enforcement at the mesh-RELAY boundary (forward()), by the auth-free zid subject — what a routing peer FORWARDS onward.

Honest deferrals (the next §5.16 atoms): (1) LOCAL-delivery gating needs the full Primitives/DeMux seam — the session layer is a SEPARATE consumer of the inbound frame, so a leaf's own subscriber is not yet gated; the demo flag is live but relay-suppression is best shown 3-node. (2) egress (the Mux twin) + the per-transport subject-resolution factory (resolve once at register, cache). (3) Del/Declare/Query/Reply actions = new match arms in the adapter. (4) interface/cert/username/link subjects = extauth (access-extauth-* features need transport auth). (5) downsampling + quota = new Interceptor impls on the same chain. (6) YAML deploy config: the typed AclConfig shape exists now, only the loader is deferred (one construction funnel). (7) KeBoxTree sublinear matching (the linear scan is the wz posture, tree is the perf follow-up). access-downsampling / access-quota / access-extauth-* inventory stay reserved.

LESSON re-confirmed (Nth time): the recurring textbook?/SSOT?/north-star?/cost-no-object trigger demands independent adversarial review, never self-assessment. It caught a real security-correctness bug (intersection vs inclusion) AND the inline-vs-seam structural shortcut the original plan had. Verify the agents' claims by direct read too — the inclusion finding was confirmed against authorization.rs:603 + keyexpr_match.rs:735.

North-star remaining: the rest of §5.16 (the breadth above), or the untouched Storage(§5.11) / SHM subsystems. Routing filter/failover/static was verified MATURE this session (filter complete). Round 311tu.decision_summary: R311tu: §5.16 access-control atom 2 — extend the ingress ACL enforcer to the Delete and DeclareSubscriber actions on the same interceptor seam (new match arms, not new check sites); a verified read corrects the atom-1 'local-delivery' deferral (the routing peer has no separate local consumer).
changes_bullets: AclMessage enum extended +Delete +DeclareSubscriber (wz-access-control). The engine AclPolicy::decision is action-generic, so the new actions flow through unchanged — only the enum + its doc grew.

acl_action adapter (interceptor/access_control.rs): a Push body now maps to Put OR Delete (CodecZenohMsgPut / CodecZenohMsgDel); a CodecZenohDeclSubscriber Declare maps to DeclareSubscriber. Each is a new arm in the existing match, not a new check site (the seam's payoff).

IngressContext.full_keyexpr (linkstate_forward.rs) gains a Declare arm: declare_subscriber_wireexpr + resolve_wireexpr, alias-aware against the inbound face's table — the same keyexpr resolution forward_subscription does for the registration path.

Verified finding (corrects the atom-1 deferral framing): the "local-delivery gate" deferral does NOT apply to the routing peer. Its only inbound consumer is forward() (accept_loop.rs:360); dispatch_iteration_event (local subscriber/queryable delivery) is the Session API path only (observer.rs:412+ SessionObserver). So atom-1's forward() gate already FULLY covers the routing peer; the true "local delivery" is a SEPARATE Session API subsystem (no forwarder/policy), not a clean atom. atom-2 broadens actions on the existing seam instead.

demo --acl-deny <keyexpr> now denies Put + Delete + DeclareSubscriber for the keyexpr, so a neighbour can neither publish to nor subscribe on it through this node — the intuitive "block this keyexpr" semantics, still LIVE.
verification_bullets: wz-access-control 7/7 (incl a_rule_only_governs_its_listed_actions: a Delete+DeclareSubscriber rule denies those actions and leaves Put to the default). routing-peer lib 382/382 incl a_del_on_a_denied_keyexpr_is_denied (adapter: Del now governed) + an_acl_deny_drops_an_inbound_declare_subscriber (forwarder: a denied DeclareSubscriber is NOT registered (fwd.interested empty) + acl_denied witness; an allowed keyexpr still registers). Round 311ty.decision_summary: R311ty: §5.16 — collapsed the three per-feature interceptor setters (set_acl_policy / set_downsampling / set_low_pass) into ONE set_interceptors(InterceptorConfig), the wz mirror of zenoh's interceptor_factories(config) funnel, closing the R311tx duplicate-on-recall + unspecified-order footgun; an independent adversarial review caught that the collapse also re-aligns the interceptor order to zenoh (downsampling -> ACL), observable for a deny-ACL + downsample-overlap deploy, so it is framed as behavior-aligned-to-zenoh with a new ordering-lock test.
changes_bullets: Collapsed the three per-feature forwarder setters (set_acl_policy / set_downsampling / set_low_pass), each of which APPENDED to both interceptor chains, into ONE set_interceptors(config: InterceptorConfig) that REPLACES both chains — the wz mirror of zenoh's single interceptor_factories(config) funnel (net/routing/interceptor/mod.rs:122). InterceptorConfig { acl: Option<AclPolicy>, downsampling: Vec<DownsamplingRule>, low_pass: Vec<LowPassRule> } is the wz analogue of the config slices zenoh reads (config.downsampling()/access_control()/low_pass_filter()). Closes the R311tx-review footgun: re-calling a setter duplicated an interceptor, and the cross-setter order was unspecified.

build_chain(flow) assembles each flow's chain in zenoh's FIXED factory order — downsampling, then access-control, then low-pass (interceptor_factories mod.rs:133-136, minus the qos-overwrite wz does not implement) — so the order is deterministic regardless of which features a deploy enables, no longer dependent on setter call order. Per-flow instances preserved (each flow gets its own downsampling timer and an ACL enforcer bound to that flow), matching zenoh's separate per-flow enforcers. The demo (wz-ap-demo runner.rs) now assembles ONE InterceptorConfig from its --acl-deny/--downsample/--max-payload flags and installs it once; the 6 forwarder tests migrated to the single seam.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (the recurring calibration discipline): a default-refute review of the diff. It UPHELD per-flow isolation, factory-order fidelity, the empty-config fast path, and footgun closure, but REFUTED the self-assessed "behavior-preserving" framing — and was correct (every claim re-verified by direct read of zenoh before acting).

CORRECTION from the review's CRITICAL finding: the collapse also re-aligned the interceptor ORDER. The old demo/test call order was ACL -> downsampling; the new fixed order is downsampling -> ACL (zenoh's). Because InterceptorChain::admit short-circuits (Iterator::all) and the downsampler records its rate timer only on the messages IT admits (downsampling.rs:92), the order is OBSERVABLE when an ACL selectively denies: in zenoh order the downsampler stamps a message the ACL then denies (consuming the rule's rate budget); in the old order an ACL-denied message short-circuited before the downsampler saw it. So this is behavior-ALIGNED-to-zenoh, not behavior-preserving — zenoh's downsampler likewise stamps a message its ACL later denies (zenoh downsampling.rs:242-244 updates the timestamp only on admit, and the factory runs downsampling before the ACL).

Added a test (downsampling_precedes_the_acl_and_accounts_a_denied_message) that LOCKS the new order: an allow-default ACL denying demo/secret + a demo/** 1s downsample rule; a denied demo/secret followed back-to-back by an allowed demo/data shows demo/data rate-limited (the denied demo/secret consumed the budget) — under the old ACL-first order demo/data would relay, so the test fails if the order regresses. Also fixed two stale doc comments still naming the removed set_acl_policy / set_downsampling.
verification_bullets: routing-peer lib 390/390 (was 389; +1 the new ordering-lock test downsampling_precedes_the_acl_and_accounts_a_denied_message), including the migrated ACL / downsampling / low_pass forwarder tests now driving the single set_interceptors seam, plus the interceptor submodule units 9/9. Each adversarial-review finding was re-verified by direct read of zenoh ground-truth before acting (interceptor_factories order mod.rs:133-136; downsampling timestamp-updated-only-on-admit + factory-runs-before-acl, zenoh downsampling.rs:242-244) — the agent was right on both.

Round 311tz.decision_summary: R311tz: §5.15/§5.16 query routing atom 1 — the QUERYABLE interest control plane (the query-plane twin of the subscriber one): generalized LinkstatepeerSubs into a reusable LinkstatepeerInterest (subs + qabls) and unified the declare-reflood + tree-change re-advertise into shared kind-parameterized seams, so DeclareQueryable now floods, registers, converges to late joiners, and purges on face-down; UndeclareQueryable + Request/Response routing + Query ACL are honestly deferred; a 3-agent adversarial review's 'codec lacks ext_keyexpr -> FALSE' CRITICAL was itself refuted by direct read (it read an SCE forge fixture, not the wz-codecs type).
changes_bullets: Generalized `LinkstatepeerSubs` -> `LinkstatepeerInterest` (renamed linkstate_subs.rs -> linkstate_interest.rs; `subscriptions()` -> `entries()`): ONE generic keyexpr->peer-set interest table, the forwarder now holds TWO instances — `subs` (DeclareSubscriber interest) and `qabls` (DeclareQueryable interest) — the wz mirror of zenoh's per-Resource linkstatepeer_subs + linkstatepeer_qabls (hat/linkstate_peer/mod.rs:515,517), both the same peer-keyed shape. Avoids a 145-line clone (the SSOT call the sb-review precedent demands).

Unified the proven subscriber declare re-flood + tree-change re-advertise into shared kind-parameterized seams: forward_interest_declaration(.., table, build) backs forward_subscription + the new forward_queryable, and re_advertise_interest(.., table, build) backs re_advertise_subscriptions + the new re_advertise_queryables. Each plane is a thin wrapper supplying its body extractor + interest table + carrier builder; source-resolve + register-gate + tree-children + fan_out live once. forward_unsubscription stays standalone (a different retraction shape).

forward() dispatch: CodecZenohDeclQueryable -> forward_queryable (register the source peer's queryable interest in qabls, re-flood a clean sourced literal DeclareQueryable along the source's tree on a NEW registration — zenoh declare_linkstatepeer_queryable / propagate_sourced_queryable, queries.rs). recompute_and_advertise now also calls re_advertise_queryables so a queryable converges to a late-joining child (queries_tree_change, queries.rs:663-697). purge_detached_interest purges BOTH tables on face-down + ingest-detach (queries_remove_node).

UndeclareQueryable DEFERRED (a codec limit, not a routing one): the wz-codecs UndeclQueryable body the dispatch matches is { header, id } — no keyexpr ext (its subscriber twin UndeclSubscriber carries `extensions`, which is exactly why forward_unsubscription can read an ext_keyexpr and this cannot; zenoh's UndeclareQueryable has ext_wire_expr, declare.rs:520-523). A faithful queryable undeclare needs a wz-codecs SCHEMA extension first (a separate codec atom). Dropped via an EXPLICIT no-op arm (not the subscriber catch-all); face-down purge is the safety net.

3-AGENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (the recurring textbook?/SSOT?/north-star? trigger): architecture + honesty UPHELD (accurate zenoh citations, sound generalization, clean atom boundary). The correctness agent's CRITICAL ("the codec HAS ext_keyexpr, the deferral is FALSE") was REFUTED by direct read — it cited vendor/sce/tests/forge/expected/..., an SCE forge fixture, not the wz-codecs generated UndeclQueryable the forwarder dispatches on (declare.rs:48,158; undecl_queryable.rs:25-28 = header+id only). Lesson re-confirmed: agents can be confidently wrong; direct read is the arbiter.

Remediation from the valid findings: sharpened the deferral comment to cite the authoritative wz-codecs type (preventing the SCE-fixture confusion); added a "declarations only" note to forward_interest_declaration; added a no-op-arm regression test (an UndeclareQueryable on a live face is inert — it neither withdraws the queryable interest nor mis-routes to the subscriber table). interested_queryables kept pub, the observer twin of interested.
verification_bullets: routing-peer lib 395/395 (was 390; +5: forward_queryable_floods_to_tree_children_and_registers, re_advertise_queryables_reaches_a_late_joining_child, deregister_purges_the_departed_peers_queryable_interest, a_queryable_and_a_subscription_on_one_key_are_tracked_independently, an_undeclare_queryable_is_inert_until_a_codec_extension_lands). The unified seams preserve subscriber behavior — every prior subscriber/forward test still passes. base lib 277/277.

SCOPE = the FORWARD half only: the rid is carried VERBATIM and no pending-query state is allocated. A routed Query's Response/ResponseFinal route BACK to the querier via a new PendingQueries table with per-hop query-id remapping: forward_request allocates a per-outbound-face qid + records (out qid -> (inbound, rid)), forward_response peeks+rewrites+unicasts back, forward_response_final takes (frees)+routes back; deregister purges. Also wired the Response/ResponseFinal arms into send_network_message (they hit the FeatureDisabled catch — the bug blocking the reply send). 2-agent adversarial review: no critical (qid lifecycle correct vs zenoh) + caught a stray debug eprintln (removed). Per-query timeout + multi-hop e2e deferred (tracked).
changes_bullets: New crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_pending.rs: PendingQueries — the per-outbound-face `out qid -> (inbound face, inbound rid)` return table, the wz analogue of zenoh's per-FaceState pending_queries + next_qid (dispatcher/face.rs, queries.rs). allocate (per-face monotonic qid + record, zenoh insert_pending_query), peek (Response — entry survives, zenoh route_send_response uses get), take (ResponseFinal — frees, route_send_response_final removes), remove_face (face-down), len. Unit-tested (monotonic per-face, peek-non-consuming, take-prunes, selective remove_face).

forward_request RETROFIT (atom-2b verbatim-rid -> atom-3 remapped-qid): build the re-stamped TEMPLATE once, then PER outbound face allocate a fresh local qid + record (out qid -> (inbound, src_rid)) and stamp it as the carrier's rid. The per-face qid is why each child gets its own carrier (zenoh route_query's insert_pending_query per target). Remapping is required for correctness: two queriers' identical rids would collide on a shared relay face without a per-face-unique local qid.

forward_response: resolve the reply keyexpr against the inbound (forward-out) face's table, peek the return mapping for (inbound, response.request_id), rewrite request_id back to the recorded upstream rid, B1-normalize the keyexpr (new set_response_keyexpr_literal, N bit 0x20 = zenoh response::flag::N), and unicast to the recorded inbound face (a back-hop via fan_out single-face, NOT a tree fan-out — the pending table IS the return route). forward_response_final: TAKE (free) + rewrite + route back (no keyexpr). Dispatch arms for Response + ResponseFinal; deregister purges a departed face's pending entries.

send_network_message (session_actions.rs) Response/ResponseFinal arms: these hit the `_ => Err(FeatureDisabled)` catch, so fan_out's send returned Err and NO reply routed — the bug the e2e test surfaced. Added arms routing to the PRE-EXISTING (previously orphaned) dispatch_response / dispatch_response_final; widened the fn-gate any(...) + the routing-peer feature with codec-response + codec-response-final (the reply twin of the codec-request forward). AP-only — no MCU footprint.

2-AGENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (correctness + architecture): NO CRITICAL. The qid lifecycle (per-face uniqueness, peek-vs-take, the remap key = the inbound face), borrow safety (pending vs faces distinct RefCells), the send-seam, the keyexpr N bit, and the face-down purge + orphaned-src-face self-heal were all verified correct vs zenoh by direct read. The architecture agent CAUGHT a stray debug eprintln left in forward_response's error path (removed) and flagged the multi-hop / multi-queryable e2e tests as deferred (integration-test layer).

Round 311uf.decision_summary: R311uf: query-routing per-query TIMEOUT — the tick-loop sweep GC for pending-query return entries (zenoh's per-query QueryCleanup). A forwarded Query's pending entry now carries a deadline (allocate-time + a configurable query_timeout, default 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout); the LinkstateForwarder tick sweeps expired entries each coalescing window and routes a synthesized ResponseFinal back to the querier (zenoh finalize_pending_query), freeing the entry — so a queryable that crashes without a final on a still-up face no longer leaks the entry nor hangs the querier. The Err('Timeout') reply body is honestly deferred (separate Err-response origination; relay correctness = the closing final alone).
changes_bullets: PendingQueries (linkstate_pending.rs): entries gain a per-entry deadline (PendingReturn { inbound, inbound_rid, deadline: Instant }); allocate(.., deadline) stamps it; new expired(now) -> Vec<ExpiredQuery> removes & returns entries past their deadline and prunes emptied faces (HashMap::retain) — the wz form of zenoh QueryCleanup. peek/take return shape unchanged.

LinkstateForwarder (linkstate_forward.rs): new query_timeout: Cell<Duration> (default DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT = 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout) + set_query_timeout config seam (twin of set_gossip_target etc.); forward_request stamps deadline = Instant::now() + query_timeout on every allocated entry.

tick() now also calls reap_timed_out_queries(): sweep expired(Instant::now()) (borrow released before send), bump a timed_out witness, and for each reaped entry synthesize build_response_final(inbound_rid) (the SSOT builder) + fan_out it back to the inbound face — exactly zenoh QueryCleanup::run -> finalize_pending_query. Cadence = the existing trees_delay coalescing window, so a query is reaped within one tick of its deadline (a coarser, allocation-free GC vs zenoh's per-query sleep task).

pending_timed_out() accessor added (GC witness, the timed_out twin of recomputes); pending_len() + remove_face docs updated (the timeout is now the 2nd GC path beside face-down purge). Err('Timeout') reply body deferred: a synthetic Err Response is a separate codec-build atom; the relay-layer correctness (no leak, no hang) is the closing final alone.

A forwarded Query's pending entry now carries a deadline (allocate-time + a configurable query_timeout, default 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout); the LinkstateForwarder tick sweeps expired entries each coalescing window and routes a synthesized ResponseFinal back to the querier (zenoh finalize_pending_query), freeing the entry — so a queryable that crashes without a final on a still-up face no longer leaks the entry nor hangs the querier. The Err('Timeout') reply body is honestly deferred (separate Err-response origination; relay correctness = the closing final alone).
publishable_changes_bullets: PendingQueries (linkstate_pending.rs): entries gain a per-entry deadline (PendingReturn { inbound, inbound_rid, deadline: Instant }); allocate(.., deadline) stamps it; new expired(now) -> Vec<ExpiredQuery> removes & returns entries past their deadline and prunes emptied faces (HashMap::retain) — the wz form of zenoh QueryCleanup. peek/take return shape unchanged.

LinkstateForwarder (linkstate_forward.rs): new query_timeout: Cell<Duration> (default DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT = 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout) + set_query_timeout config seam (twin of set_gossip_target etc.); forward_request stamps deadline = Instant::now() + query_timeout on every allocated entry.

tick() now also calls reap_timed_out_queries(): sweep expired(Instant::now()) (borrow released before send), bump a timed_out witness, and for each reaped entry synthesize build_response_final(inbound_rid) (the SSOT builder) + fan_out it back to the inbound face — exactly zenoh QueryCleanup::run -> finalize_pending_query. Cadence = the existing trees_delay coalescing window, so a query is reaped within one tick of its deadline (a coarser, allocation-free GC vs zenoh's per-query sleep task).

pending_timed_out() accessor added (GC witness, the timed_out twin of recomputes); pending_len() + remove_face docs updated (the timeout is now the 2nd GC path beside face-down purge). Round 311un.decision_summary: R311un: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 4a/N — the PRODUCER. LinkstateForwarder::declare_queryable(keyexpr, complete) originates a LOCAL queryable into the mesh: register self's queryable in qabls under its own zid + flood a sourced DeclareQueryable CARRYING the QueryableInfo (set_declare_queryable_info; complete=false = DEFAULT, OMITTED = byte-identical no-info wire) to self's tree children — the query-plane twin of declare_subscription, the self-origination twin of forward_queryable. This is the complete-queryable producer the atom-3 select was waiting on: a node can now declare complete=true, a relay stores it, and BestMatching FIRES instead of always falling back to All (proven e2e). The forward_request target-read dispatch (All/BestMatching/AllComplete from the Request ext_target) needs a wire decode (MCU footprint) and is split to atom 4b.
changes_bullets: linkstate_forward.rs declare_queryable(&self, keyexpr, complete) -> Result<usize>: the local-queryable origination, mirroring declare_subscription. Registers QueryableInfo{complete, distance:0} under self_zid (zenoh declare_simple_queryable registers under tables.zid -> the tree-change re-advertise re-floods to late joiners), builds build_declare_queryable(0,0,keyexpr) (node_id 0 = self-originated) + set_declare_queryable_info(info), floods via flood_to_tree_children. distance 0 at origination (zenoh's client QueryableInfo carries 0; the per-hop increment is the tracked downstream-carry, and BestMatching reads GRAPH distance anyway). complete=false packs to DEFAULT -> set_declare_queryable_info OMITS the ext (byte-identical no-info wire). Imports set_declare_queryable_info.

SCOPE: atom 4 split. 4a = the producer (this entry) — self-contained, forwarder-level, NO wire change (reuses the uj set_declare_queryable_info codec). 4b (TRACKED) = forward_request reads the carried QueryTarget (Request ext_target) and dispatches All/BestMatching/AllComplete; the Request codec wz-codecs/request.rs does NOT decode ext_target today (the WRITE side build_request_query_with_target exists, the READ side does not), so 4b needs a wire-decode addition (MCU footprint) = its own atom. Until 4b forward_request always BestMatching-selects-else-All, which is CORRECT for the wire default (absent ext_target == BestMatching, zenoh/pico); only an explicit All/AllComplete query would be mis-narrowed.

The Session-struct high-level queryable builder (.complete(true)) + get() target plumbing stay Session-API scope (the query-routing track lives at the LinkstateForwarder; Session is the separate single-node API). declare_queryable IS the routing-peer producer the track needed.

Round 311uq.decision_summary: R311uq: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 4d/N — the DOWNSTREAM carry that completes MULTI-HOP BestMatching. Both queryable re-flood paths now CARRY the source's QueryableInfo, not a clean declaration: forward_queryable's inbound re-flood (captures the read info) AND re_advertise_queryables' tree-change re-flood (entries() is now value-bearing). re_advertise_interest seam: build is now Fn(&str, &V) and consumes the value-bearing entries(), so the tree-change re-advertise carries the per-peer value too. re_advertise_queryables stamps the QueryableInfo (build_declare_queryable_with_info), re_advertise_subscriptions ignores V=(). linkstate_interest.rs entries() -> Vec<(String, Zid, V)> (V: Clone) — the value-agnostic deferral note is now CLOSED.

WHY no distance increment: wz qabls is keyed by the queryable's ORIGIN zid (resolve_source maps every hop's re-stamped node_id back to it), and select_best_matching reads net.distance_to(origin) — the GRAPH distance from THIS relay — so the carried distance is IRRELEVANT to wz routing. zenoh's insert_target_for_qabls likewise reads net.distances[qabl_idx], not qabl_info.distance, and propagate_sourced_queryable re-floods the registered qabl_info VERBATIM (queries.rs:278). Round 311us.decision_summary: R311us: tracked-debt paydown — forwarder clock INJECTION (the uk session-review finding). LinkstateForwarder's two Instant::now() sites (the pending-query deadline stamp in forward_request + the timeout reap in reap_timed_out_queries) now read through an injected clock field (Box<dyn Fn() -> Instant>), defaulting to Instant::now in production (new / with_trees_delay) and injectable via the new with_clock constructor. This unblocks a DETERMINISTIC non-zero-timeout test: the zero-timeout test could only prove 'reaped immediately', while a base+offset injected clock now pins the deadline arithmetic — a query is reaped AT, not before, its deadline.
changes_bullets: linkstate_forward.rs: + clock: Box<dyn Fn() -> Instant> field + a private now() that is the SINGLE read site the forward_request deadline stamp AND the reap_timed_out_queries sweep share. The two Instant::now() calls -> self.now(). Constructors funnel through a new private build(zid, whatami, trees_delay, clock) so the field initialiser lives once; new / with_trees_delay pass Box::new(Instant::now), the new pub with_clock passes a custom clock (DI for deterministic tests).

The deterministic test a_pending_query_is_reaped_only_after_its_non_zero_deadline_passes: a base+offset fake clock (Instant is opaque, so a fake returns base + a controllable offset; the base cancels in the deadline comparison, leaving offset as virtual time). forward_request stamps deadline = base + 0 + 100ms; a sweep at offset 99ms does NOT reap (survives, no premature final to the querier); a sweep at offset 100ms reaps + routes the Err(Timeout) + closing final back to A.

changes_bullets: storage_state.rs (NEW, wz-session-core): StorageState<B: StorageBackend> = the newer-wins service gate over a backend. process_put / process_delete / get / matching_entries. Pure no_std (no Subscriber/Queryable/async); the runtime-agnostic half of a storage service.

newer-wins gate (zenoh guard_cache_if_latest service.rs:510-544): accept iff incoming >= recorded (reject iff a STRICTLY newer ts recorded, service.rs:536); older Put/Delete -> Outdated, backend untouched. timestamp_strictly_newer mirrors uhlc Timestamp Ord (timestamp.rs:33-37: time then zid lexicographic).

tombstone: an accepted Delete records its ts in `latest` (cache_latest mirror) even though the value leaves the backend, so an older Put after a Delete rejects Outdated instead of resurrecting the key.

matching_entries (zenoh get_matching_keys service.rs:628-658): scan get_all_entries, keep keys that keyexpr_intersects_target the query, pair with value via get. Reuses the shared pub/sub matcher (storage reply set == subscriber set). Wildcard via keyexpr-wildcard-* features; literal-degrades without them.

Round 311v.decision_summary: R311v QueryEvent.attachment extraction. Inbound Query extension chain (ext_id 0x05, ExtZbuf) decoded to Option<&[u8]> view threaded through fire_matching_queryables; R311r carry closed.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: new module-private free function `fn extract_query_attachment(query: &Query) -> Option<&[u8]>` walks `query.extensions.as_ref()` and matches each `ExtEntry` against the zenoh-pico query-attachment wire shape (`ext_id == 0x05` low-nibble of header + `body == ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf`). First matching entry's `zbuf.value.as_slice()` is returned; absent extensions vec or no-attachment chain yields `None`. The mandatory bit (`_Z_MSG_EXT_FLAG_M = 0x10`) is intentionally NOT required to match because zenoh-pico's `_z_query_decode_extensions` falls into the `default` arm silently when M is clear (no `_z_msg_ext_unknown_error`), which is the encode-side behaviour we mirror at decode-side.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: `fire_matching_queryables` body augmented — the existing `let parameters_view = query.parameters.as_deref();` line is followed by `let attachment_view = extract_query_attachment(query);` so the view is computed ONCE per inbound query (the chain walk is O(n) on ext count which the zenoh wire format caps at 8 per `Query::decode` line 109). Asymmetric by design: local.diff(remote) surfaces only what remote has that local differs on or lacks; local's own extras are found when remote runs remote.diff(local). Each replica diffs the received digest, so every divergence is found once on the side that must pull.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_aligner.rs (NEW, storage-aligner feat): Action{Put,Delete} + EventMetadata{key,timestamp,action}, a faithful mirror of zenoh log.rs:43-49 (Action) / :98-128 (EventMetadata). EventMetadata::fingerprint delegates to storage_replication::event_fingerprint (the digest SSOT, Event::compute_fingerprint log.rs:232-244); the action is NOT hashed (log.rs:226-231), so an event and a peer's copy of it agree, which is what makes the digest buckets compare.

storage-aligner TRACK plan (faithful mirror of zenoh aligner_query.rs + aligner_reply.rs + core.rs spawn_aligner_queryable/spawn_query_replica_aligner): A1 metadata types (vr DONE) -> A2 snapshot answer primitives (cold-era per-interval fp + per-sub-interval fp + events_metadata extraction from the StorageState latest+backend snapshot; factor a bucketing SSOT shared with build_digest) -> A3 AlignmentQuery/AlignmentReply enums (Discovery/All/Diff/Intervals/SubIntervals/Events ; Discovery/Intervals/SubIntervals/EventsMetadata/Retrieval) -> A4 wire codec (bincode-1.3 byte-exact incl EventMetadata/Action/Timestamp, twin of storage_replication::wire) -> A5 answer engine answer_alignment_query(state,config,query) -> A6 pull/convergence engine process_alignment_reply (Intervals->SubIntervals->Events->Retrieval drill-down + apply via StorageState) -> A7 driver: aligner queryable (answer) + query_replica_aligner (get-with-attachment, ask) and WIRE the on_diff seam (storage_replication_service.rs DigestSubscriber callback) to spawn_query_replica_aligner(replica_aligner_ke, AlignmentQuery::Diff(diff)) -> A8 facade forward (wz storage-aligner = [storage-replication, wz-runtime-tokio?/storage-aligner]) + inventory storage-aligner reserved->active + full run-ci -> A9 cross-impl byte interop (AlignmentQuery/Reply vs real bincode 1.3) -> A10 two-replica e2e convergence (the long-promised live test) + 4-agent adversarial review remediation.

Aligner keyexpr (A7) = @zid/<zid>/<config-fp>/aligner (zenoh aligner_key_expr_formatter core.rs:47); reply attachment carries AlignmentReply, payload carries the value (aligner_query.rs reply_to_query :340-363).

Round 311vu.decision_summary: R311vu: storage-aligner EventMetadata wire codec atom (aligner 4/N) -- byte-exact encode/decode of EventMetadata (with the uhlc Timestamp + Action it embeds) to zenoh's bincode 1.3 format, proven byte-identical to the real bincode 1.3 lib and bidirectionally readable; the AlignmentQuery/AlignmentReply envelopes are the next atom.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_aligner.rs: new `pub mod wire` (the twin of storage_replication::wire) -- pub encode_event_metadata / decode_event_metadata + AlignmentDecodeError, built on private push_*/Reader helpers the AlignmentQuery/Reply envelope codec (next atom) reuses.

Byte layout (verified by reading uhlc-0.8.1 Timestamp/NTP64/ID derived serde + zenoh OwnedKeyExpr Serialize = Arc<str> -> String): EventMetadata = stripped_key Option(u8 tag 1=Some, then String[u64 len + utf8]) + timestamp Timestamp(NTP64 u64 LE 8B + ID [u8;16] 16B via zid_to_le_array SSOT) + timestamp_last_non_wildcard_update Option<Timestamp> + action Action(u32 LE variant index). bincode Option = u8 tag (NOT u32); a plain enum index = u32.

wz emits stripped_key=Some(key) (no strip_prefix) + tlnwu=Some(timestamp) (re-supplies the field the kernel type omits) + action 0/1 (Put/Delete). decode discards tlnwu (wildcard-only), trims the 16-byte id back to wz's length-trimmed zid (inverse of zid_to_le_array, round-trip exact), and rejects an inbound wildcard action 2/3 (UnsupportedAction), a None stripped_key (MissingKey), bad UTF-8, trailing bytes, or a hostile length -- the named non-converging residuals until wz storage gains wildcard updates / strip_prefix.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-session-core --features storage-aligner: storage_aligner::wire 6/6 -- encode_event_metadata_is_byte_identical_to_bincode_1_3 (THE fidelity test: wz's hand-rolled bytes == the real bincode 1.3 the version + default config zenoh uses, for the equivalent EventMetadata, across Put + Delete + a full 16-byte zid) and wz_and_bincode_1_3_read_each_others_event_metadata (both directions), plus round-trip, wildcard-action-unsupported, trailing+truncation, none-stripped-key rejections. Feature total 228.

The cross-check EMPIRICALLY confirms the byte spec inferred from the uhlc/zenoh source: bincode 1.3 renders an Option as a single u8 tag, a plain enum's variant index as a u32, a uhlc Timestamp as 24 bytes (NTP64 u64 + ID 16-byte array), and a String as a u64 length + bytes.

carry_forward_bullets: R311vy = storage-aligner session-review remediation 1/N. On the user's "textbook/SSOT/north-star/cost-irrelevant" trigger, ran a 4-agent adversarial review of R311vr..vx (fidelity/correctness/structure-SSOT/honesty) then ARBITRATED every finding by direct read (agents over-flag; direct read is the arbiter). VERDICT: NO critical defect; kernel convergence is self-proven; wire is byte-exact; structure is portfolio-grade. Direct-read arbitration CONFIRMED one real fidelity+SSOT bug -- in the PUSHED digest track, not the aligner: the digest keyexpr rendered the zid as per-byte hex ("1a2b3c") while zenoh's keformat renders ${zid} via ZenohId Display ("3c2b1a"), which ALSO disagreed with the aligner's own (correct) Discovery zid hex. FIXED here: zid_to_zenoh_hex/zenoh_hex_to_zid unified into storage_replication as the single SSOT, used by BOTH the digest keyexpr and the aligner Discovery; digest keyexpr corrected; test corrected.

REMAINING review findings to remediate (R311vz, wa, ...): (B) FIDELITY: process_alignment_reply's Intervals arm compares peer cold fingerprints against the era-BOUNDED cold_era_fingerprints, but zenoh compares the era-INDEPENDENT interval fingerprint (core/aligner_reply.rs:145 -> intervals.get(idx).fingerprint(); rationale core/aligner_query.rs:179-186). Under clock skew across the warm/cold boundary wz makes a spurious re-request (convergence still holds, just an extra round-trip). Fix: add EventBuckets::interval_fingerprints(&set) (era-independent, XOR of all events in each present interval) and use it in the Intervals arm. (C) DRY/SSOT: storage_replication::wire and storage_aligner::wire each hand-roll the SAME bincode-1.3 primitives (Reader{buf,pos}, check_len, push_u64/u32, read_u64/u32/u8/bytes, remaining) -- extract a shared no_std bincode-cursor module returning a minimal shared error each maps into its typed enum. (D) STRUCTURE: AlignmentResponse.value + the process_alignment_reply `value` param use an anonymous (Vec<u8>, Option<EncodingHint>) tuple -- name it (e.g. RetrievedValue{payload, encoding}). (E) HONESTY/coverage: two_replicas_converge_via_the_aligner only covers local-subset-of-peer one-directional pull -- add bidirectional + equal-timestamp-contention (zid tiebreak) cases so the "converges" claim is true in general, not just the happy path. (F) polish: named consts for the wire min-entry sizes (38 = EventMetadata min, 16/8 = pair/u64), citation precision (the aligner files are under replication/core/; the SubInterval XOR-on-insert is classification.rs:378 not :353), and the read_string "before allocating" comment (read_bytes borrows, the alloc is String::from).

HONEST framing to carry (the frozen vu/vv/vx entries' headlines slightly overstate; recorded here as the correction): "byte-proven both directions" = the bincode FRAMING is proven against the real bincode 1.3.3 lib + a serde mirror, and the embedded uhlc Timestamp 24-byte layout is verified by READING uhlc's derived serde (not by round-tripping a real uhlc::Timestamp); "entire aligner wire byte-interop with real zenoh" = codec-level (vs the lib + wz's serde mirror of zenoh's types), a LIVE zenoh-plugin-storage-manager exchange remains a named residual (A11); "two replicas converge" currently = the local-subset one-directional case (E broadens it).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/wire_bincode.rs (NEW, pub(crate), gated storage-replication): the genuinely-shared bincode-1.3 framing primitives -- WireError{UnexpectedEof, LengthOverflow} + push_u64 + Reader{new, remaining, read_bytes, read_u64} + check_len. The single place the bincode-1.3 LE-fixint / u64-length-prefix contract lives.

storage_replication::wire (digest codec): removed its private push_u64 / Reader / read_u64 / remaining / check_len; uses the shared ones; impl From<WireError> for DigestDecodeError lifts the two structural errors through `?`.

storage_aligner::wire (aligner codec): removed its private push_u64 / Reader / read_u64 / read_bytes / remaining / check_len; uses the shared ones; impl From<WireError> for AlignmentDecodeError. The aligner-only widths (push_u32, push_string, read_u8, read_u32, read_string) stay as aligner-local fns / inherent methods ON the shared Reader -- the digest codec never had them, so they were never a duplication (sharing them would make them dead code in the digest-only build). lib.rs: pub(crate) mod wire_bincode gated storage-replication.

Round 311we.decision_summary: R311we: storage-aligner A8c-1 -- relax the query-attachment 32-byte cap (QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN) to no_std-only. The cap is the shared ExtZbuf value carrier's heapless<32> bound; under alloc the carrier is an unbounded Vec (matching zenoh's unbounded query ZBytes), so the over-conservative builder assert is now gated not(alloc) -- letting a storage AlignmentQuery (Diff/Intervals/Events > 32 bytes) ride the query attachment intact. The aligner is alloc-only and never targets a no_std wz peer, so no cross-impl fidelity is lost.
changes_bullets: request_build.rs: RequestQueryBuilder::query_attachment's `len <= QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN` assert is now #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))] (the non-empty assert stays unconditional). Under alloc the ExtZbuf value carrier is an unbounded Vec, so no cap; under no_std it is heapless::Vec<u8, 32> and the assert fails fast at the call site. Docs on the setter, the QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN constant, and build_request_query_with_attachment updated to state the alloc-unbounded / no_std-32 split and why it is interop-safe (zenoh + alloc-wz peers accept arbitrarily large ZBuf; only a no_std wz peer -- which never runs the alloc-only aligner -- would reject over-32 on decode).
verification_bullets: The should_panic("exceeds .. max-size (32)") test is replaced by build_request_query_with_attachment_carries_over_32_under_alloc: a 200-byte attachment builds under alloc and the encoded Query body carries the full payload on the id-0x05 ext (decode_attachment_ext round-trip). The existing 32-byte byte-exact wire test (build_request_query_with_attachment_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes) and the empty-slice should_panic still pass -- the relaxation changes only the over-32 alloc path, no wire bytes change for <= 32 byte attachments.

Round 311wm.decision_summary: R311wm: A8c-2 session-review remediation. A 4-agent adversarial review of wh..wl (fidelity / SSOT-structure / correctness-edge / honesty-northstar) + direct-read arbitration; verdict: NO critical defect, structure/fidelity/honesty textbook-grade. 6 confirmed items fixed: 1 HIGH -- issue_and_collect now wraps the on_final await in a tokio backstop so the pull loop is self-bounded (the wire with_timeout_ms's reply-timeout sweep is a SEPARATE task, R268 moved it out of drive_session_until_terminal, so an unreachable peer + no sweep would hang final_rx.await and leak the detached task; the prior doc overclaimed). 2 MEDIUM -- digest_keyexpr_zid_hex hex-validates the zid (blocks a wildcard keyexpr-injection into the aligner query keyexpr); run_alignment truncates Discovery replies to the first (zenoh core.rs:567-572). 3 LOW -- MAX_ALIGNMENT_QUERIES followup cap; decode_reply derives value-presence from the event Action (Delete Retrieval -> None); 2 citation fixes + stale module doc. 1 new test + 3 asserts; storage-aligner 315, default 279 no regression; clippy -D + fmt clean; C1z lane green.
changes_bullets: (HIGH) issue_and_collect now wraps the on_final await in a tokio::time::timeout backstop (ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS + ALIGNER_BACKSTOP_SLACK_MS) so a spawned alignment task is SELF-BOUNDED. The prior ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS doc claimed the wire with_timeout_ms guarantees on_final fires when a replica is unreachable, but the reply-timeout sweep (ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out) is a SEPARATE task -- R268 relocated it OUT of drive_session_until_terminal -- so a session without an app-spawned sweep would hang final_rx.await forever on a silent peer, leaking the detached task + its Arc<Mutex<StorageState>> clone per divergence. The backstop resolves regardless; the doc is corrected to state this honestly.

(MEDIUM) digest_keyexpr_zid_hex now requires the zid chunk to be all ascii-hexdigit (exactly what zid_to_zenoh_hex emits, so a legit peer never fails) -- defense-in-depth: a crafted/non-conformant peer keyexpr like @-digest/a$*/<fp> would otherwise splice a keyexpr WILDCARD into the aligner query keyexpr (aligner_keyexpr_for_hex), fanning a targeted Diff pull (and this replica's DigestDiff) out to many replicas. +3 rejection asserts.

(MEDIUM) run_alignment now truncates a Discovery query's replies to the first (replies.truncate(1)): zenoh defensively stops after the FIRST Discovery reply (core.rs:567-572) because Monotonic may still deliver several; without the guard several Discovery replies fanned into several All pulls.

(LOW) run_alignment now bounds the followup queue with MAX_ALIGNMENT_QUERIES (100k). A conformant peer's refinement tree stays far below; a hostile peer answering ANY query with fresh Discovery replies can no longer grow the queue unbounded (zenoh has the same exposure via unbounded task spawns; wz's single-task drain makes a cheap cap natural). Hitting it abandons THIS pass -- the next digest tick re-triggers if still diverged, so a deep alignment still converges over ticks.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/query_reply_e2e.rs (NEW): the FIRST in-process Session::query -> remote declare_queryable -> reply -> on_final e2e over a real loopback TCP link. Two sessions, each sharing ONE Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>> between its TokioSession and its drive-loop dispatch closure -- the high-level query/queryable callbacks are STAGED on the session's shared (Arc-backed) DeferredFireQueue and run only by Session::dispatch_iteration_event's drain, so a bare observer.dispatch_event (the pub/sub pattern) only stages and never fires. The asker re-issues the query on a poll cadence until a reply lands, holding each ReplyHandle, so Declare propagation is absorbed without a racy fixed sleep. Gated on query-get/query-queryable/query-reply/transport-link-tcp/transport-unicast (all default -> runs in Layer C1).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/storage_aligner_convergence_e2e.rs (NEW): A11 -- two replicas over a real TCP link. Source A seeds demo/x (wall_clock_ntp64 timestamp), declares AlignerService + spawns DigestPublisher; empty dest B calls spawn_digest_aligner; both drive continuously and the scenario polls B's store until it holds A's value (monotonic convergence). Strong assert: B holds A's value AND the two replicas' replication_digests are byte-identical at a single shared now. Gated on storage-aligner/transport-link-tcp/transport-unicast.

verification_bullets: PROVEN cross-impl facts (the whole point of A10), each observed directly against a real zenohd 1.5.0 + zenoh-plugin-storage-manager: (1) config fingerprint PARITY -- wz ReplicationConfig::new("data/test/**", None, 1000, 5, 6, 30, 250) hashes to 3912446778783065544, the literal a real zenohd emits in its "Published Digest" trace; the test pins this golden as a hard assert before any I/O. (2) wz DECODES zenohd's Digest (received + bincode-decoded cleanly, era buckets correct). (3) wz's AlignmentQuery (Diff THEN the Events followup) interoperates -- zenohd's aligner logs "Processing AlignmentQuery::Diff" + "Processing AlignmentQuery::Events". (4) wz DECODES zenohd's aligner reply + process_alignment_reply applies it -- the wz replica store gains data/test/x with zenohd's stored bytes verbatim.
A10 test: 12/12 runs green (non-flaky). Convergence is poll-on-condition (the replica gains the entry), monotonic, generous budget over zenohd's 1s digest interval; converges in ~1.4s.

Plugin ABI: the checkout-built libzenoh_plugin_storage_manager.so (1.5.0, rustc 1.85.0) loads into the zenohd binary -- zenohd logs "Starting required plugin storage_manager" + "Plugin compatibility record" match; the storage spawns + publishes digests every 1s + declares its aligner queryable.

Layer Z A10 leg green end-to-end (WZ_ZENOHD_BIN + WZ_STORAGE_MANAGER_SO, --test-threads=1). clippy -p wz-integration-tests --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean; bash -n run-ci.sh + build-zenohd.sh OK.

No C1 regression: wz-runtime-tokio default 279 (the storage-aligner dev-dep does NOT leak into wz-runtime-tokio's own workspace test build under resolver=2); wz-integration-tests non-ignored suite unaffected.

The fixture_session_init_params (version 0x05 / batch_size 0 -- wz-internal-test values) is REJECTED by a strict zenohd at InitSyn; A10 dials with interop params (version 0x09, batch 65535, seq_num_res/req_id_res 2) mirroring wz-ap-demo's demo_session_init_params. A wz CLIENT publish to the router returns Ok(0) (it forwards only to known subscriptions, and a client is not told the router's storage subscription), so the seed is a foreign pico z_pub; a single z_put races its session teardown and does not land, while a bounded z_pub burst's earlier (1s-spaced) Puts land and settle.

PROVEN against the reference Rust zenoh: config-fingerprint parity (golden 3912446778783065544), wz decodes zenohd's Digest, wz's AlignmentQuery (Diff+Events) interoperates with zenohd's aligner, wz decodes zenohd's aligner reply + lands the entry. The storage replication track is now cross-impl-validated end-to-end, not just wz<->wz.

PROVISIONING: scripts/build-zenohd.sh now builds the storage-manager plugin cdylib alongside zenohd (source A / checkout only; source B / crates.io cannot, and the test SKIPs). The plugin must share zenohd's zenoh version + rustc so its ABI-compat hash matches. Layer Z runs the A10 leg when the plugin is present.

DURABLE LESSONS: (1) the wz<->zenohd handshake needs INTEROP params (version 0x09, batch_size 65535, seq_num_res/req_id_res 2 -- wz-ap-demo's demo_session_init_params), NOT fixture_session_init_params (version 0x05 / batch 0, a wz-internal-test shape a strict zenohd rejects at InitSyn). (2) A wz CLIENT publish returns Ok(0) routing to nobody when it does not know a matching remote subscription -- so seeding a foreign router's storage needs a foreign client (pico z_pub), not a wz-side Put. (3) pico z_pub prepends "[ N] " to its value (assert CONTAINS, not exact); a single pico z_put races its close and does not land.

Finding: already COMPLETE (the storage-aligner forward from R311wl + the wz::runtime_tokio re-export exposing storage_service/storage_replication_service/storage_aligner_service + the domain-storage aggregate + the preset-ap-full/preset-zenoh-cpp presets all compose the four storage features), so A9 needed no new feature/re-export (the carry's 'if needed' resolves to not-needed). changes_bullets: scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer C1z's facade-build step gains `cargo build -p wz --features storage-history` (and a comment). This was the ONE storage facade forward not CI-built: storage-aligner implies backend + replication + aligner (so its existing facade build covers those three forwards), but storage-history is ORTHOGONAL -- replication runs on a Latest store, so storage-aligner does NOT imply storage-history -- so the wz facade's `wz-runtime-tokio?/storage-history` forward needs its own facade build to stay guarded.

No source change: A9 is an AUDIT of the facade's storage-track composition plus the one CI guard above. The facade already composed the track (the storage-aligner forward landed in R311wl; the wz::runtime_tokio re-export already exposes the storage driver modules; the domain-storage aggregate and the preset-ap-full / preset-zenoh-cpp presets already list all four storage features), so no new feature/re-export was needed.
verification_bullets: A9 audit -- the wz facade FULLY composes the storage-aligner track, verified on four axes: (1) feature forward -- storage-aligner = [storage-replication, wz-runtime-tokio?/storage-aligner] (R311wl), storage-history = [storage-backend, wz-runtime-tokio?/storage-history]; (2) re-export -- the facade re-exports `wz_runtime_tokio as runtime_tokio`, so wz::runtime_tokio::storage_{service,replication_service,aligner_service}::* (StorageService, DigestPublisher, spawn_digest_aligner, AlignerService, ...) are reachable through the facade; (3) domain aggregate -- domain-storage lists all four storage features; (4) presets -- preset-ap-full and preset-zenoh-cpp both list all four.

Builds clean: cargo build -p wz under --features storage-aligner, under --features storage-history (the newly-guarded forward), AND under --features preset-ap-full (storage-aligner bundled with ~123 features -- proves no feature-unification conflict in a real preset).

C1z lane green end-to-end with the added storage-history facade build (storage-aligner --lib storage 36 + the A11 e2e 1 + storage-history --lib storage 10 + clippy x3 + facade build x2). bash -n scripts/run-ci.sh OK.

Scope discipline: A9 added NO curated `wz::storage` re-export or new preset -- the facade already exposes the drivers via wz::runtime_tokio and the presets already include storage; adding more would be speculative (YAGNI). The "if needed" in the carry resolved to not-needed beyond the one CI guard.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/query.rs: Queryable::matches now matches an inbound query by keyexpr INTERSECTION (keyexpr_intersects_target -- the seam declared_intersects already uses) instead of keyexpr_pattern_matches, which matched the queryable pattern against the query as a concrete LITERAL, so a wildcard query selector's `*` was matched character-literally and never reached a concrete queryable. For a concrete query the result is identical -- no regression. Removed the now-unused keyexpr_pattern_matches import.

crates/wz-session-core/src/query.rs: NEW unit test concrete_queryable_answers_wildcard_query_selector -- a concrete queryable answers an intersecting wildcard selector and does NOT answer a non-intersecting one (the regression guard for the fix).

An empty zenohd replica converges to a wz replica that holds an entry, via zenohd's initial-alignment Discovery (the wildcard @zid/*/<fp>/aligner which wz now answers) then a concrete All; witnessed by a foreign pico z_get against zenohd. Module doc updated to cover BOTH directions.
verification_bullets: The wz fidelity gap was DIAGNOSED, not assumed: direct read + zenohd trace logging showed the wildcard Discovery propagated to wz's face (Propagate query to Face{3,100a0c}) but wz's answer callback never fired; a client-vs-peer hypothesis was REFUTED (peer mode gave the identical result). Root cause: Queryable::matches matched the query selector as a literal.

ANSWER e2e converges 5/5 runs, all 0.71s (non-flaky): zenohd's empty-replica initial-alignment Discovery is the fast path; the steady-state digest-diff path is the fallback, both inside the ~52s z_get poll budget.

No regression from the matcher change: wz-session-core query module 269, wz-runtime-tokio default 279, storage-aligner 315 + A11 two_replicas_converge, A10 wz_replica_converges (ASK) all green; no_std + minimal (--no-default-features [+query-queryable]) builds compile; clippy -D + fmt clean.

The storage replication+aligner track is now cross-impl-validated in BOTH directions (A10 wz pulls from zenohd; A12 zenohd pulls from wz).

THE FIX (general, NOT aligner-specific): wz Queryable::matches matched an inbound query SELECTOR as a concrete literal, so a wz queryable could not be reached by ANY wildcard query selector -- e.g. a foreign z_get -k 'demo/*', or zenohd's initial-alignment @zid/*/<fp>/aligner Discovery. Now keyexpr INTERSECTION (zenoh query routing). A11 never hit this (it sent only concrete Diff queries).

CONVERGENCE MECHANISM: an empty zenohd bootstraps via a one-shot initial-alignment Discovery (storages_mgt service.rs:13-26 awaits it BEFORE the steady digest pub/sub starts) -- a WILDCARD @zid/*/<fp>/aligner GET; wz answers Discovery(wz-zid); zenohd then GETs the concrete @zid/<wz-zid>/<fp>/aligner with All. The digest-diff path (wz DigestPublisher -> zenohd @-digest/* subscriber -> concrete Diff) is the fallback once the Discovery GET times out.

The A10 ASK pico-seed rationale otherwise stands (the wz session there is the empty replica under test + a single Put races teardown); only the "route to nobody" framing is imprecise.

Round 311xh.decision_summary: R311xh: close the R311xg disclosed gap #1 -- mandatory-method-presence. A configured auth RESPONDER now REQUIRES the peer to present the method's sub-ext on InitSyn (accept_recv_init_syn Errs on a None offer) instead of silently degrading to no-auth, matching zenoh (usrpwd.rs:372 / pubkey.rs:558 bail on a missing ext). Enforcement is method-level (configured = mandatory, AND across methods) and the accept_* stages run only on the accept side, so the offer is required there; usrpwd gates on a non-empty lookup (responder), pubkey unconditionally. Happy paths are unaffected (the initiator offers); + 2 new require-offer reject tests. No inventory change.

An empty-lookup initiator-role method does not enforce. + a test (responder rejects a no-offer InitSyn; initiator does not).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/extauth_pubkey.rs: accept_recv_init_syn now REQUIRES the InitSyn pubkey offer -- a missing/malformed offer is Err("pubkey: missing InitSyn offer"), not a silent degrade (zenoh pubkey.rs:558 bails "Missing PubKey extension"). Round 311xi.decision_summary: R311xi opens the transport-advanced track: a Unix-domain-stream link backend (transport-link-unixsock), the wz mirror of zenoh's unixsock_stream link, mirroring the proven TCP/TLS stream pipeline seam. A unix socket is a reliable byte STREAM (is_streamed/is_reliable true, MTU 65535), so it reuses the stream_link StreamEnvelope SSOT UNCHANGED over a tokio UnixStream (into_split owned halves, like TCP) -- no new codec and no new dependency (tokio's net feature already carries UnixStream/UnixListener on Unix, unlike tls's tokio-rustls / ws's tungstenite). The unixsock-stream/... locator leaf is ungated/foundational (like serial -- a non-IP filesystem-path endpoint, the AnyLocator::Unixsock variant); only the dial/accept BACKEND is the cfg gate. wz<->wz e2e over a real loopback unix socket reaches Established and delivers a Put byte-exact, zero-flake 3/3. transport-link-unixsock reserved->active (atom 83). The wz<->zenohd unixsock cross-impl leg is deferred to a follow-up (R311xj), the same kernel->cross-impl split as storage A10/A12 and usrpwd R3b-1/R3b-2.

Module doc updated (Two->Three leaves; unixsock dropped from the not-yet-wired list).

crates/wz-session-core/src/reconnect.rs: NotReconnectable::Unixsock + the TryFrom<AnyLocator> arm. A unix socket is non-IP (outside the IP-family reconnect set the supervisor models; pico's Z_FEATURE_AUTO_RECONNECT is tcp/udp/tls/ws and pico has no unixsock), so it is rejected at the narrowing boundary like serial -- a path-bearing ReconnectLocator arm is a clean extension point. + a reject test.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: #[cfg(feature=transport-link-unixsock)] pub mod unixsock_pipeline + doc.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: DialedLink::Unixsock(UnixStream) (not Box'd -- a thin fd wrapper) + transport_name; dial_locator Unixsock arm (gated wired via dial_unixsock + cfg(not) typed Unsupported, like serial); bind_locator Unixsock arm (Unsupported -- the listen side is a UnixListener owned by the acceptor, not the TcpListener this seam returns); InboundLink::Unixsock(UnixsockReadDriver) + the 4 LinkDriver dispatch arms; wire_dialed_link Unixsock arm.

LOCATOR through connect_and_open_session; both reach Established and a Put is delivered byte-exact over the StreamEnvelope-framed unix stream.

Round 311xk.decision_summary: R311xk completes the link-kind family (tcp/udp/tls/ws/serial/unixsock/vsock + quic): a QUIC link backend (transport-link-quic), the wz mirror of zenoh-link-quic. zenoh carries a zenoh batch over ONE bidirectional QUIC stream per connection (uni rejected, max_concurrent_bidi=1) with the SAME StreamEnvelope length-prefix as TCP/TLS (is_streamed=true, MTU BatchSize::MAX), so it reuses the stream_link SSOT UNCHANGED over a quinn SendStream/RecvStream pair -- which are ALREADY split (no into_split / tokio::io::split). NEW dep quinn 0.11 (default-features=false, ring+rustls+runtime-tokio) -- front-load-verified to share a single rustls 0.23.40 with the existing tokio-rustls 0.26 (no version conflict), so QuicClientConfig::try_from(rustls::ClientConfig) type-checks. Proto::Quic is IP-family (numeric host:port, like tls/ws -- NOT a new AnyLocator variant); the cert (TLS-1.3 + ALPN hq-29, built by quic_config reusing the tls_config PEM loaders) is threaded via DialConfig.quic, the tls pattern. UNLIKE vsock, QUIC loopback needs no special kernel support, so the wz<->wz e2e is FULLY RUNNABLE (self-signed rcgen, no #[ignore]) -- the fully-verified link round closing vsock's #[ignore] gap. transport-link-quic reserved->active (atom 85).

Round 311xq.decision_summary: R311xq implements the foundational predefined Encoding constants + the MIME id<->str table (the §5.19 encoding domain), the wz mirror of zenoh's high-level Encoding API (api/encoding.rs), layered on the already-active pubsub-encoding wire field codec. DIRECT-READ DECISION: the 7 encoding atoms are NOT cfg-toggleable -- encoding identity is a DATA value (a numeric id + a free-form schema string), and the §5.19 audit (R311cg/R311hr) + the audit-catalog-status.sh A3 rule (active <=> a real cfg toggle; an always-on FOUNDATIONAL capability = status=reserved + a FOUNDATIONAL reason, the keyexpr-canon precedent) mean cfg-gating an encoding NAME is a dead-code stub. So the constants are IMPLEMENTED ungated-foundational and the 7 atoms STAY status=reserved with a FOUNDATIONAL reason -- NOT flipped to active (they are not knobs). This CORRECTS the user's chosen-option label (\"reserved->active-foundational\") to the audit-faithful \"reserved-FOUNDATIONAL\" (active is reserved for real toggles -- keeps the active set honest). The active-atom count is UNCHANGED (90); the atoms moved inert-reserved -> FOUNDATIONAL-reserved (implemented).

Round 311xr.decision_summary: R311xr -- 3-agent adversarial-review remediation of the transport-advanced track (R311xl..xq). The reviews (refactoring-expert SSOT/smell + general-purpose faithfulness + system-architect long-term), arbitrated by direct-read, CONVERGED independently on ONE real structural debt: the unit-ext negotiation MECHANISM replicated across the 3 capabilities -- in direct tension with the project's own SSOT-over-DRY north star. Fixed: (1) extracted the unit-ext encode/detect SSOT (crate::unit_ext) + a generic stage_capability, the 3 ext modules + 6 send sites delegate (the named per-capability id + encoder wrapper KEPT for discoverability); (2) extracted the 3 byte-identical e2e establish_pair helpers into ONE establish_capability_pair in test-support (the offer is a closure); (3) added transport_compose_e2e proving all 3 negotiate + LAYER (compression(lean(shm-descriptor))) on one session -- the composition the single-mode e2e could not prove; (4) made the SHM no-resolver drop OBSERVABLE (a counter + getter, was a bare silent return). DECLINED with rationale: the Mutex<bool>->AtomicBool is_X change (slot consistency with every other R::Mutex per-session slot > a sub-us non-hot-path gain + portable_atomic gating cost; rated RECONSIDER, not debt). DEFERRED (YAGNI, the review agreed): the RX transform-pipeline abstraction -> at the 4th mode. The faithfulness review confirmed byte-faithfulness + honest scoping, so this is STRUCTURE-only, no behavior change.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/unit_ext.rs (NEW): the zero-payload UNIT capability-ext mechanism SSOT -- encode_unit_ext(id) + chain_has_ext_id(exts, id). extlowlatency / extcompression / extshm's encode_X_ext + peer_offered_X + body_has_shm_marker now DELEGATE (the named id constant + wrapper kept per-capability); the struct-literal + any() body (written 4x) collapses to 1. + 1 unit test.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: the 3 byte-identical stage_X_send replaced by ONE generic stage_capability(role, offer, build: fn() -> ExtEntryOwned) -- `build` is the per-capability named encoder (the single source of both the id, for the idempotent retain, and the content); the 6 InitSyn/InitAck send sites call it directly. is_X kept R::Mutex<bool> (the AtomicBool change declined for slot consistency).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio-test-support/src/lib.rs: establish_capability_pair(init_offer, resp_offer, apply_offer: impl Fn) + EstablishedPair + fixture_params_with_zid -- the shared recording-driver handshake driver extracted from the 3 byte-identical e2e establish_pair helpers (the offer is the closure; the feature-gated setter stays in the e2e crate, so test-support carries none of it).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/{lowlatency,compression,shm}_e2e.rs: deleted the local establish_pair + params helpers; Test 2 now calls establish_capability_pair with the per-capability offer closure (EstablishedPair.init_actions / .init_driver). The single-mode proofs unchanged.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/transport_compose_e2e.rs (NEW): a session negotiates lowlatency + compression + shm; an SHM Put's captured wire shows the LAYERING -- compression BatchHeader (outermost) || lean bare N_MID_PUSH (inside, carrying the shm descriptor). The 3-way composition single-mode e2e could not prove.

crates/wz-session-core/src/pubsub.rs: the SHM RX un-swap's unresolvable-descriptor path increments an observable shm_unresolved_drops counter (+ a getter) instead of a bare silent return (fail-OBSERVABLE on a missing set_shm_resolver). + a unit test (a marker Put with no resolver drops nothing AND counts).
scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer C1ag (unit_ext SSOT test + the SHM-drop observability test + transport_compose_e2e + the combined three-feature --all-targets clippy).
verification_bullets: All single-mode e2e unchanged + green after the refactor: lowlatency/compression/shm_e2e 2 each (now via establish_capability_pair); the 21 ext-module unit tests; transport_compose_e2e 1 (the 3-way layering); shm_put_with_no_resolver_drops_observably 1 (fail-observable: delivers 0 + counter 1). Zero behavior change.

clippy -D warnings green on ALL configs: the combined transport-lowlatency,session-extcompression,session-extshm,transport-unicast,transport-link-tcp --all-targets (the compose test + the shared helper + all 3 data paths together); bare transport-lowlatency (the unit_ext consumer); OFF default (session-core 177 lib + runtime-tokio --all-targets + test-support 7). facade wz --features <all 3> builds. Full C1ag chain + the regressed C1ad/ae/af (extlowlatency 4 / compression 6 / shm 5) green. run-ci.sh bash -n OK.

The 3-agent adversarial review arbitrated by direct-read: the SSOT review + the arch review CONVERGED independently on the negotiation-machinery replication as the #1 real debt (convergence = real, not agent over-flag); the faithfulness review (which RAN the 22 unit + 6 e2e tests) confirmed byte-faithfulness (all 53 encoding MIME mappings, the lowlatency/compression/shm wires) + honest scoping (no doc-around-a-hack, no fidelity bug). So the remediation is structure-only, not a correctness fix.
carry_forward_bullets: R311xr = 3-agent review remediation of the transport-advanced track: the unit-ext negotiation MECHANISM is now one SSOT (unit_ext + stage_capability; per-capability id/encoder/wrapper kept), the 3 e2e handshake drivers are one (establish_capability_pair in test-support), the 3-way composition is PROVEN (transport_compose_e2e), and the SHM no-resolver drop is OBSERVABLE (a counter). No wire/behavior change; inventory unchanged.

DECLINED (documented, not debt): the Mutex<bool>->AtomicBool is_X consolidation (slot consistency with every other R::Mutex per-session slot > a sub-us non-hot-path gain + the portable_atomic feature-gated-import cost). DEFERRED (YAGNI, the review agreed): the RX transform-pipeline abstraction -> extract when the 4th transport mode lands (the trigger), not before.

Round 311xt.decision_summary: R311xt implements the §5.18 time-hlc atom -- the ACTIVE Hybrid Logical Clock timestamp source, the wz mirror of zenoh's Option<Arc<uhlc::HLC>> on the Runtime (net/runtime/mod.rs:147, an HLC created when timestamping is enabled). DIRECT-READ CORRECTION (the front-loaded highest-risk unknown): zenoh's HLC WRAPS the physical/system clock (HLCBuilder default clock = system_time_clock), it is NOT an alternative to wall-clock, so the prior inventory framing ("HLC = opt-in alternative to wall-clock" / "system-clock mutually-exclusive-with-HLC") was wrong and is corrected. wz reuses the uhlc crate verbatim (the algorithm SSOT, zenoh's 0.8 pin, the same reuse stance as lz4_flex/memmap2) and injects wz's own wall_clock_ntp64 as the HLC physical clock via HLCBuilder::with_clock, so the HLC wraps wz's existing wall-clock SSOT and produces the same NTP64 magnitude the digest/aligner use. The HLC lives in wz-runtime-tokio (the AP runtime, where zenoh puts it + where its sole consumer + physical source live), gated behind the new non-default time-hlc feature, and is wired LIVE into the storage capture fallback (wz's only auto-stamp site) via a FallbackStamp source seam: time-hlc ON stamps an un-timestamped sample with the HLC (logical counter + monotonicity + drift over the wall clock), OFF uses the bare wall_clock_ntp64 (byte-identical to prior behavior). A3 verdict: time-hlc is a genuine cfg-toggle gating real BEHAVIOR (unlike encoding, where gating a name was a dead stub) -> reserved->ACTIVE (active 90->91); the other 3 §5.18 atoms are FOUNDATIONAL (time-ntp64 word+codec, time-system-clock the physical layer the HLC wraps, time-timestamp-source the FallbackStamp seam) with reasons updated to the FOUNDATIONAL prefix.

Round 311xv.decision_summary: R311xv -- P4 A3 remediation. The concurrent R311xu P4-scoping round (d3862f3) added 64 LAYER-3 catalog atoms to the inventory (§5.21-§5.27 + §5.1+4) via add-inventory-entry but did NOT declare them as cargo features, so the Layer A3 catalog-status gate's invariant #1 (every catalog atom is a [features] key in some crates/**/Cargo.toml) FAILED with 64 phantom atoms. This was caught by a full run-ci this session (RUNCI_EXIT=1, Layer A3 FAIL); R311xu's recorded run-ci-green was inaccurate -- A3 was red. FIX: declared all 64 as no-op `[]` cargo features in the facade crates/wz/Cargo.toml, grouped by P4 family (router 16 / plugin 6 / adminspace+config 11 / storage-backend+mgr 13 / ext-pubsub 10 / rest 2 / api-compat 2 / transport+4), the established reserved-atom marker pattern (like time-ntp64 = []). All reserved -- no code, no cfg gate -- so A3 invariant #2 (reserved => not gated) holds trivially and #4 (section_ref to §5.21-§5.27) was already set by R311xu. Pure declaration: no inventory mutation, no code behavior change. This is the missing half of R311xu (catalog atoms must be declared as cargo features, not only registered in the inventory).

Round 311xx.decision_summary: R311xx -- liveliness-history correctness fix (small-track A3 read-first surfaced two real fidelity bugs the absent integrated proof had hidden, NOT a cfg flip). Bug #1 (subscriber): history_complete was wired to flip on an inbound Interest(Final) -- which the responder never sends -- so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted); the R281 wire-up had cited the no-op pico _z_interest_process_interest_final (interest.c:524) instead of the real terminator handler _z_interest_process_declare_final (interest.c:508). Fixed: dispatch_messages now flips history_complete on the responder's Declare(DeclFinal) whose interest_id echoes a history-subscriber slot (mirror of the liveliness-get registry's fire_final_for), and ignores inbound Interest (the responder's concern). Bug #2 (responder): respond_to_interest gated the current-token replay on non-final (C|F), so a FUTURE-only (history=false) subscriber wrongly received the current tokens as spurious Put samples; fixed to gate on the CURRENT bit (zenoh `if mode.current()`, hat/client/token.rs:354) -- a FUTURE-only interest now stages nothing (future updates ride the declarer's proactive declare). Both bugs confirmed diagnose-first with failing guards before the fix; an integrated responder->subscriber test now proves the current-token Put AND history_complete together (the integrated proof the §5.10 review flagged as absent). STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory UNCHANGED -- liveliness-history stays reserved (R311xx adds no cfg gate), the cfg-gate->active promotion (R311cl's "careful per-call cfg-gate, not field gate") + liveliness-historical-samples FOUNDATIONAL reclassification are the R2 follow-up. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

The prior R281 wire-up flipped history_complete on an Interest(Final) the responder never sends, so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted). dispatch_messages doc-comment corrected.

Mirror of zenoh `if mode.current()` (hat/client/token.rs:354). The pre-fix gate wrongly replied to FUTURE-only interests, so a history=false subscriber received the current tokens as spurious Put samples.

Round 311xx.publishable_decision_summary: R311xx -- liveliness-history correctness fix (small-track A3 read-first surfaced two real fidelity bugs the absent integrated proof had hidden, NOT a cfg flip). Bug #1 (subscriber): history_complete was wired to flip on an inbound Interest(Final) -- which the responder never sends -- so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted); the R281 wire-up had cited the no-op pico _z_interest_process_interest_final (interest.c:524) instead of the real terminator handler _z_interest_process_declare_final (interest.c:508). Fixed: dispatch_messages now flips history_complete on the responder's Declare(DeclFinal) whose interest_id echoes a history-subscriber slot (mirror of the liveliness-get registry's fire_final_for), and ignores inbound Interest (the responder's concern). Bug #2 (responder): respond_to_interest gated the current-token replay on non-final (C|F), so a FUTURE-only (history=false) subscriber wrongly received the current tokens as spurious Put samples; fixed to gate on the CURRENT bit (zenoh `if mode.current()`, hat/client/token.rs:354) -- a FUTURE-only interest now stages nothing (future updates ride the declarer's proactive declare). Both bugs confirmed diagnose-first with failing guards before the fix; an integrated responder->subscriber test now proves the current-token Put AND history_complete together (the integrated proof the §5.10 review flagged as absent). STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory UNCHANGED -- liveliness-history stays reserved (R311xx adds no cfg gate), the cfg-gate->active promotion (R311cl's "careful per-call cfg-gate, not field gate") + liveliness-historical-samples FOUNDATIONAL reclassification are the R2 follow-up. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/declare/liveliness_subscriber.rs: dispatch_messages now flips history_complete on an inbound Declare(DeclFinal) whose interest_id echoes a history-subscriber slot (mirror of the liveliness-get registry's fire_final_for + pico _z_interest_process_declare_final, vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/interest.c:508) and IGNORES inbound Interest messages (the responder's concern; pico _z_interest_process_interest_final, interest.c:524, is a TODO no-op). The prior R281 wire-up flipped history_complete on an Interest(Final) the responder never sends, so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted). dispatch_messages doc-comment corrected.

crates/wz-session-core/src/declare/local_token.rs: respond_to_interest gates the current-token replay on the CURRENT bit (new INTEREST_CURRENT_MASK 0x20) instead of the prior non-final (C|F) mask; a FUTURE-only Interest (the history=false subscriber's declare) now stages nothing -- future updates are covered by the declarer's proactive Declare(DeclToken), not by replaying current state. Mirror of zenoh `if mode.current()` (hat/client/token.rs:354). The pre-fix gate wrongly replied to FUTURE-only interests, so a history=false subscriber received the current tokens as spurious Put samples.
