Round 311y197.decision_summary: R311y197 - I3b loop-safe multicast-ingress->mesh federation (router-multicast-faces): a wz router-hat federates a mcast-ingress Push into the unicast linkstate mesh, loop-safe when two wz routers share one group AND are mesh-peered, via a per-keyexpr Designated-Router election (reusing the seedless-SipHash HRW elect_router over on-group whatami=Router members union self): exactly one on-group router federates group-ingress->mesh AND re-egresses mesh-sourced Puts->group, so the two-router-shared-group echo zenoh WhatAmI::Client Quick-hack leaves undefended is loop-free by construction. Deliberate structural SUPERSET over zenoh (mcast peer stays a faithful Client leaf, not a linkstate node); inventory-neutral; MCU byte-identical. Full 3-agent DESIGN + 3-agent IMPL + 1 WHOLE-SESSION, direct-read arbitrated; IMPL caught + fixed 2 must-fixes (routing-accept Zid build break -> raw-bytes membership relay; egress gate starving non-DR local clients -> mesh-sourced-only gate).
changes_bullets: router_forward.rs: RouterForwarder gains mcast_group_members (RefCell<Vec<Zid>>) + is_group_dr(keyexpr) (seedless-SipHash HRW elect_router over on-group-routers-union-self, the same primitive is_master uses) + the DR egress gate in broadcast_to_mcast_groups (new source_is_mesh param: gate ONLY mesh-sourced Puts; a local unicast client's Put egresses unconditionally) + the federation gate in route_push (mcast_ingress_may_federate -> is_group_dr, cfg-dispatched to false without router-multicast-faces). set_mcast_group_members is a FaceForwarder trait no-op with a router-only override that converts raw zid bytes -> Zid. All #[cfg(feature="router-multicast-faces")].

multicast_dispatch.rs + multicast_join.rs: PeerSlot.whatami + JoinBaseline.whatami (#[cfg(feature="multicast-declarations")], from WhatAmI::from_wire(join.whatami())) stored at ingest_join admit+refresh, cleared on evict; new router_member_zids() -> Vec<Vec<u8>> yielding the live whatami=Router peer zids (the DR election candidate set).

multicast_glue.rs: drive_multicast_session_with_membership (the loop body + a snapshot-diff relay of router_member_zids, firing only on a real membership change) with drive_multicast_session kept as a thin no-op-relay wrapper (adapter pattern: the ~23 existing callers + the public signature are untouched); spawn_router_mcast_ingress returns a 2nd receiver carrying the raw member-zid bytes.

accept_loop.rs: FaceForwarder::set_mcast_group_members(&[Vec<u8>]) trait method taking RAW zid bytes (keeps wz-routing-graph OFF the accept lane so the routing-accept/routing-routes build compiles) + FaceSources.mcast_members + Step::McastMembers(Vec<Vec<u8>>) + a recv_mcast_members awaiter + a select arm -> set_mcast_group_members.
runner.rs: run_router_hat wires both the ingress and the members receiver into FaceSources.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: new composition feature multicast-declarations=[wz-session-core/multicast-declarations]; router-multicast-faces routes through it so the runtime relay's own #[cfg] gates activate. NO new §5.21 catalog atom (inventory-neutral).

6 new router_forward unit tests: DR egress suppressed (non-DR, mesh inbound) / fires (DR with a losing member = per-keyexpr election, not blanket suppression) / unconditional (sole on-group router) / anti-starvation (local-client egress NOT DR-gated) + federation fires-when-DR / not-federated-when-not-DR.
verification_bullets: 684 wz-runtime-tokio lib tests pass (--features router-multicast-faces), incl the 6 new I3b tests; 384 wz-session-core lib tests pass (--features multicast-declarations).

routing-accept + routing-routes builds (run-ci Layer C1x, exit 101 BEFORE the IMPL fix) now exit 0; clippy clean on router-multicast-faces + routing-routes; cargo fmt --check clean on wz-runtime-tokio, wz-session-core, wz-ap-demo.

MCU byte-identical: driver_loop.rs + multicast_rx.rs untouched (empty git diff); PeerSlot.whatami / JoinBaseline.whatami / router_member_zids are cfg(multicast-declarations)-gated and no MCU crate enables it; DriverLoopOutcome / IterationEvent / on_event unchanged.

Narrow builds compile: default wz-runtime-tokio + egress-only (transport-multicast WITHOUT router-multicast-faces: the DR gate + membership relay are elided, group egress stays unconditional) + router-multicast-faces alone.

validate_workspace: T1 orphan new=+0 (ledger=13 unchanged), T3 warn=4 / T4 info=4; inventory-neutral (no new active atom; the A3 inventory->cargo audit is unaffected by a non-inventoried composition feature).

Full 3-agent DESIGN + 3-agent IMPL + 1 WHOLE-SESSION review, direct-read arbitrated. DESIGN rejected a local origin-tag (dies at the mesh hop) + Option-Y linkstate-promotion (non-faithful); chose DR-among-on-group-routers reusing elect_router (the mcast peer stays a Client leaf). IMPL caught + FIXED 2 must-fixes: (1) the accept-loop membership channel referenced wz_routing_graph::Zid unconditionally, breaking the routing-accept/routes build -> relay raw zid bytes, convert to Zid only in the router-only forwarder; (2) the egress DR gate suppressed LOCAL-client egress too, starving a non-DR router's clients -> gate only mesh-sourced Puts. WHOLE-SESSION confirmed inventory-neutral + MCU byte-identical + signature stability + no scope-creep + honest framing (fixed 1 stale route_mcast_ingress doc).

Loop-safety: IMPL Lens-C traced the two-router group-ingress loop hop-by-hop as broken by construction (exactly one on-group router federates a given keyexpr; only the DR re-egresses mesh-sourced Puts; the both-multicast echo guard + the mesh spanning tree close the rest); the mesh-only egress gate preserves the mesh->group bridge (routed_push_broadcasts_to_attached_mcast_group) and fixes non-DR local-client starvation.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y197 = I3b loop-safe multicast-ingress->mesh federation via a per-keyexpr Designated-Router election (router-multicast-faces). DONE + verified (slices 1-3 + 2 IMPL must-fixes). The wz router-hat now federates a mcast-ingress Push into the unicast mesh, loop-safe when two wz routers share one group AND are mesh-peered - a deliberate structural SUPERSET over zenoh's undefended "Quick hack", built from zenoh's own elect_router HRW primitive (the mcast peer stays a faithful WhatAmI::Client leaf, NOT a linkstate node). Inventory-neutral; MCU byte-identical.

DEFERRED (named, re-openable): I3c cross-impl two-router e2e proof over real sockets (two wz router-hats on one group + mesh-peered + a pico pub/sub; assert no group-traffic escalation + an off-group mesh sub receives exactly once). Loop-safety is unit-proven + IMPL-traced but NOT yet cross-impl'd, and the JOIN-whatami -> router_member_zids -> snapshot-diff -> set_mcast_group_members wiring is not yet exercised end-to-end (the DR tests inject members directly), so I3c must close that coverage leg.

DEFERRED: DAMPING (promote-slow/demote-fast hold-down) for the bounded startup double-DR transient - not built, as the transient is share-group => hear-JOINs => agree-DR self-healing (zenoh shared_nodes-parity), bounded by the 100ms JOIN interval.

DEFERRED: PER-PEER mcast_faces + subscriber-declaration ingest (I3 sub-problems #1-3, the faithful-arch axis). Until group subs propagate into the unicast mesh the mesh->group egress carries two named limitations: (a) a non-DR router's local-client Put reaches the group only via its OWN unconditional local egress (the mesh-only gate fix), not via the DR (the DR would not receive it - the mesh is sub-gated); (b) in the two-router case a local Put whose DR is the OTHER router is egressed to the group by BOTH the origin (local) and the DR (mesh-relay) => a bounded steady-state DUPLICATE on the group (loop-safety intact). Both dissolve once the sub plane lands.

DEFERRED: MULTI-GROUP per-group member set (run_router_hat attaches exactly one group today; a future 2nd attach_mcast_group with a distinct membership would conflate the single mcast_group_members set); the DR-candidate LAN-trust boundary (an unauthenticated whatami=Router JOIN can win the HRW and blackhole those keyexprs - the same LAN-trust posture the rest of the unauthenticated multicast plane already assumes).

Round 311y206.decision_summary: R311y206 -- wz->pico TX-fragmentation cross-impl fidelity bug FIX. wz outbound fragment chains omitted the zenoh fragment FIRST marker (Z-ext 0x02 on the first fragment) that zenoh-pico requires on a protocol-patch>=1 session (wz always advertises patch=1), so pico silently dropped every wz >MTU Put ("First fragment received without the start marker"). A new interop test (wz_fragment_tx_to_pico_zsub) surfaced it (20B sub-MTU passes / 200B fragmenting drops). Fixed build_fragment_wire/fragment_body to emit the marker on the first fragment (shared by unicast + multicast) + a secondary unicast SN double-mint that left a 1-SN wire gap (emit_frame_or_fragments now reuses the minted sn + reserves count-1, matching zenoh pipeline.rs + the already-correct multicast twin). Correctness-only, transport-fragmentation stays active. 3-agent review SOUND/COMPLETE + test-rigor remediations; full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0, hand-composed so ZERO codegen drift.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/frame_encode.rs: build_fragment_wire gained a `first: bool` param -- the FIRST fragment of a chain now sets the header Z flag (FLAG_T_Z 0x80) and inserts the FRAGMENT_FIRST ext byte (new const FRAGMENT_FIRST_EXT_HEADER = 0x02, id 0x02 | enc unit) between VLE(sn) and the payload; subsequent fragments are byte-unchanged. fragment_body passes `off == 0` as `first`, so BOTH the unicast (emit_frame_or_fragments) and multicast (multicast_frame_or_fragments) chains -- its only two callers -- get the marker. zenoh `fragment::ext::First = zextunit!(0x2,false)` / zenoh-pico `_Z_MSG_EXT_ID_FRAGMENT_FIRST`. The VLE(sn) stays the codec SSOT (encode Fragment{sn, payload:&[]} for the VLE, then push the ext + real payload) -- symmetric with inbound.rs's hand-rolled fragment Z-gated ext-chain decode. FRAG_HEADER_BUDGET doc notes the 1-byte ext rides the reserved-max-VLE(10)-minus-real-width(<=9) slack, so the first fragment stays <= mtu.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: emit_frame_or_fragments SN fix -- the oversize frame's already-minted `sn` IS the first fragment's SN; reserve only the `count-1` follow-on SNs (`for _ in 1..count { outbound_frame_sn.fetch_add(1) }`) and pass `sn` (not a fresh fetch_add(count)) as the fragment_body base. Round 311y21.decision_summary: R311y21 -- clock SSOT extraction (1st of the 3 R311y20 adversarial-review remediation rounds, all before FreeRTOS). The Cortex-M SysTick clock was pasted in 3 deploy mains and had DRIFTED: only deploy/mcu-qemu-demo carried the R311y15 monotonic floor; deploy/mcu-session-acceptor + deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e ran the floorless pre-R311y15 copy (latent -- they drive a sync busy-poll session loop, not a SleepFuture, so the wake-loss livelock had not surfaced there, but the wz_runtime_lwip::time::ClockSource monotonic contract was nonetheless violated). Extracted into a new no_std crate wz-mcu-clock as ONE SystickClock<const CYCLES_PER_US: u64>; the SSOT now applies the monotonic floor everywhere AND widens the reload counter AtomicU32->AtomicU64 (the 49.7-day overflow-freeze fix: a u32 ms counter overflows -> raw collapses toward zero -> the monotonic floor clamps and FREEZES forever; u64 pushes the horizon past 5e8 years). The bug-prone wrap-tear-safe read + floor live once in the crate (host unit-tested: apply_floor split out so the monotonic-floor regression runs on the host without MMIO); each bin keeps only the unavoidable linkage glue (static GLOBAL_CLOCK<N>, #[exception] SysTick -> on_tick, the sys_now() lwIP extern, the per-bin ClockSource impl -- the trait is re-exported via each bin's wz::runtime_lwip facade, so wz-mcu-clock has ZERO wz dep and is a plain host workspace member needing no C1/C2 --exclude, unlike the wz-mcu-* e2e crates). Footprint: the u64 widening routes the 64-bit atomic through critical-section on ARMv7-M, growing qemu-demo .text +~500 B (mps2/v8m; thumbv6m +8, already crit-section) and multicast-e2e +444/+560 B (it also gained the floor); BASELINE_TEXT + BASELINE_MC_TEXT (+ bss) rebased in scripts/check-footprint.sh and §6.7/§6.9 store caveats appended (the gate's table<->caveat co-maintenance rule). Local arm-none-eabi-gcc figures; a CI-gcc follow-up rebase may shift them <=256 B per the footprint-baseline-CI-gcc rule. validate_workspace orphan new=+0 (ledger=13 unchanged), inventory unchanged; full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 (Layer Q QEMU boots are the on-target proof the floor+u64 clock RUNS; Layer G 7-triple cross-compile + Layer C2 workspace clippy incl wz-mcu-clock + all 6 footprint gates +0 OK).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/attachment.rs: new pub fn deserialize_kv_attachment(blob) -> Option<Vec<(Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>)>>, the decode twin of serialize_kv_attachment. Reads VLE(pair_count) via SceCursor::read_vle_u64 then count length-prefixed key/value strings via the crate::vle read_zbuf SSOT (the read inverse of write_zbuf), byte-faithful to pico ze_deserializer_deserialize_sequence_length + ze_deserializer_deserialize_string (serialization.c) and the z_sub_attachment.c decode loop. Round 311y211.decision_summary: R311y211 -- reconnect×multilink coherence slice-1 (S2 FOUNDATION; the user chose the full A-only arc after the 3-agent DESIGN review dropped Approach C as unnecessary+unsafe). The y205 transport-multilink × session-reconnect compile_error XOR is REMOVED, and its single real hazard -- reset_for_reopen zeroing the SHARED SessionCore rx_sn / outbound_frame_sn, which in a live aggregate corrupts the surviving link's per-channel SN gate -- becomes a RUNTIME guard: when transport-multilink is also compiled the shared-core reset is skipped while live_link_count() > 0, making reset_for_reopen a TOTAL function (preserving a live survivor is the correct output for that input, not a bug to assert away). Production reaches the skip only as a safety net -- a partial loss survives via del_link (SN intact, no reset), a whole-collapse is a fresh-core rebuild (the accept loop drops the aggregate at remaining==0, so the next dial is a fresh primary), and the single-link ReconnectingSession supervisor runs on an EMPTY link set (link_count==0) so the guard is transparent to it. beyond-pico / P4 (pico has no unicast multilink; zenoh-full is the sole reference). A coexistence unit test pins the guard mechanics (SN preserved with a live link; re-seeded once the set is empty) and CI Layer C1ba invocation 5 runs it on default + transport-multilink (the ex-XOR combo) with a count-assert (grep ' 1 passed') so a future cfg-out reddens the lane, plus a both-crate clippy floor. 3-agent DESIGN review (dropped C, scoped A) + 2-agent IMPL review (correctness CLEAN; the test is proven to FAIL if the guard is removed; CI is proven to actually run it). NO per-link auto-re-add yet -- that is slice-2 (y212, the dropped-link-comes-back value). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

The naive S3 multilink priority-select was found by a 3-agent DESIGN review to CORRUPT reliable delivery: wz has ONE TX SN counter + a per-reliability RX gate pair (RxSn{reliable,best_effort}) shared across a multilink aggregate, so priority-splitting a reliability channel across links yields out-of-order arrival at the one shared gate -> the half-window `precedes` gate drops the "stale" reliable frame. zenoh avoids this with per-(priority,reliability) SN conduits. NEXT y215 (per-priority conduits): `Priority::NUM=8`+`from_wire`; expand AtomicTxSn / RxSn to per-priority arrays `[..;8]` cfg-gated behind a new `transport-qos` feature (MCU/non-qos keeps the y214 2-wide shape — do NOT runtime-is_qos-size a no-alloc array); is_qos Init unit-ext negotiation (new extqos.rs id 0x1, clone extlowlatency, decode-TOLERATE unit OR z64 QoSLink = is_qos true with QoSLink range-semantics deferred to S4, is_qos&&is_lowlatency exclusive at offer-injection); Frame/Fragment ext_qos priority wire (header 0x31 = id 0x1 | FLAG_M | ENC_Z64, priority-only body, on EVERY fragment; DEFAULT/Data frame byte-identical to today); RX per-priority conduit index off the decoded ext_qos, admit_rx_frame_sn(priority,reliable,sn); reassembly ChainKey += priority + abort_channel/RxSnRejected carry priority; thread priority through send_network_message -> dispatch_* -> mint sourced from each message's OWN qos byte (per-type default: control=Control, data=Data), base-mint + fragment-reserve using the SAME captured (priority,reliable) key; !is_qos && non-Data ext_qos -> drop; BatchTx stores window-opener priority. Slice-1 MUST also add `priority` on FramePayload + a priority/express publish API + the RX-gate-independence + ext_qos-round-trip tests (else the atom is hollow / slice-2 witness impossible). Then y216 = LinkPriorityRange (Option, default None) + 3-tier select_link(reliability,priority) full/partial/any smallest-range-tiebreak(strict >, lowest-index) + one-conduit=one-link invariant asserted at select_link (forbid same-(p,r) spread; failover re-pin loss bounded/documented) + priority-segregation e2e (2 links SAME reliability_pref, distinct ranges, EXPRESS reliable HIGH/LOW puts, per-face witness capturing DECODED priority). A DEFAULT / non-qos frame is byte-identical to the pre-QoS wire; the AP is_qos-negotiation-from-config + select_link + the FramePayload.priority witness are deferred to R311y216. 3-agent adversarial review found + fixed 1 HIGH wire bug (frame_wire_body did not strip the frame ext_qos before re-fragmenting) + resolved 4 cfg-skew/build findings (deferred the pure-observability FramePayload.priority to y216 to avoid a ~48-site unconditional-field rollout; fixed derivable_impls / too_many_arguments / a test gate); new run-ci Layer C1bb; transport-qos catalogued active (session-extqos reason updated); MCU multicast footprint baseline rebased +200/+260 (faithfulness-over-cost); full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

This atom closes that gap: a WzConfig.qos config surface + with_qos builder (cfg transport-qos, default false, byte-identical pre-QoS) + three *_with_qos session-open entrypoints (initiate/accept/connect) mirroring the lowlatency entrypoints, each staging set_qos_offer(true) before the drive. A genuine qos_e2e (3 tests) proves the composed path: real-TCP prioritized-Put delivery (negotiate + conduit admit + deliver), a deterministic byte-form capture (both-offer stamps the Frame ext_qos / FLAG_T_Z; none and one-sided TX-clamp to DEFAULT, byte-identical to pre-QoS), and the WzConfig.qos field round-trip. It ALSO closes a y215 faithfulness asymmetry the DESIGN review surfaced: the qos/lowlatency exclusivity guard was one-directional (set_qos_offer refused under staged lowlatency, but set_lowlatency_offer did not reciprocate) -- zenoh manager.rs:264 is symmetric and TOTAL; set_lowlatency_offer now returns bool and reciprocally refuses under staged qos, so the both-on state is unrepresentable in EITHER staging order. A new run-ci qos_e2e lane in Layer C1bb mirrors the lowlatency_e2e lane (no --no-default-features so defaults supply codec-init-body / codec-push the round-trip needs) and RUNS the exclusivity test under both transport-qos + transport-lowlatency (the reciprocal-guard symmetry had no executed CI lane before). transport-qos stays active (no inventory change; y215 already flipped it). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0; 3-agent DESIGN + 3-agent IMPL review, direct-read arbitrated.

A new LinkPriorityRange type (the wz mirror of zenoh PriorityRange, an inclusive Priority band) + a per-link priority_range + set_link_priority_range carry each link's band; select_link is full (reliability match AND band contains priority, SMALLEST band wins via STRICT `>` = stable first-seen) -> partial (reliability match, no covering band) -> any (first alive). priority is threaded through send_wire to all 10 call sites, with the SN-safety-critical batch-flush arms routing by the FRAME's OWN pinned conduit (batch.priority), NOT the triggering message -- a mismatch would split one conduit across links and silently lose a stale-dropped reliable frame. LinkReliabilityPref::Any stays any-tier ONLY (backward-compat + zenoh concrete-reliability primacy); a non-qos build degrades byte-identically to the old reliability-only 2-tier. Three deterministic recording-driver segregation tests prove routing on the immediate AND batch-reopen-flush paths + the narrowest-band tie-break; the #3 batch guard was diagnose-first-verified (it FAILS on the trigger-priority bug). Demo/deploy activation (the --qos flag, FaceSources.qos, per-face e2e) is deferred to y218. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

Round 311y219a.decision_summary: R311y219a -- deploy-path per-face priority-band segregation (the y217 select_link priority tier ACTIVATED over the production accept/dial path). y217 built select_link(reliability, priority) + LinkPriorityRange as a recording-driver LIBRARY; y218 activated qos negotiation over multilink. This atom assigns the per-face priority band in the deploy path so a QoS multilink aggregate segregates distinct-priority Puts onto distinct physical links, proven in-process over a real peer_loop. KEY DESIGN (3-agent DESIGN review + direct-read arbitration): select_link disqualifies a reliability-mismatched link BEFORE the priority band (faithful to zenoh universal/tx.rs select), so a 2-link aggregate segregates on ONE axis only; with QoS ON all links are UNIFORM Reliable (new multilink_pref_for) so the priority band is the live discriminant, with QoS OFF the y205 even/odd reliability spread is unchanged (mutually-exclusive 2-link modes). This is a DIRECT MIRROR of a real zenoh multilink-over-TCP deploy (a TCP link is always is_reliable, so zenoh's per-link priority ranges ride all-Reliable links, tx.rs:86-88). New multilink_priority_range(id) assigns by FaceId parity (even -> HIGH [Control..=InteractiveLow], odd -> LOW [DataHigh..=Background]; non-overlapping + jointly covering 0..=7 so every priority is a full match on exactly one link). The band threads a feature-independent (Priority, Priority) tuple (NOT the all(multilink,qos)-gated LinkPriorityRange, which in a pub signature would break the transport-multilink && !transport-qos CI lane -- the y218 qos:bool discipline) through the two _with_multilink entrypoints, applied via set_link_priority_range inside `#[cfg(transport-qos)] if qos`; retained across re-add in ml_dial_endpoints (grown to a 3-tuple) so a flapped link restores its band (a fresh-id band would flip parity + collapse the split). A DEPLOY-active in-process e2e (real peer_loop qos=true max_links=2) sends an EXPRESS (Control) + a LOW (Background) reliable Put and asserts they arrive on DISTINCT faces (is_qos()==true asserted FIRST so the DEFAULT-clamp cannot false-green). SCOPE (deliberate split, user-approved): the joined-face DELIVERY gap (a joined secondary link is not a forwarder face, so the real LinkStateForwarder drops data/control routed onto it -- latent since y205, first exposed by priority routing) + the demo --express flags + the black-box 2-proc e2e are y219b. full run-ci pending the batch push; per-atom host lanes green (deploy e2e 3/3 + unit 2/2 + e2e 5+6 + readd 1 + all clippy -D warnings + fmt).

Round 311y219b.decision_summary: R311y219b -- joined-face DELIVERY fix (the load-bearing half of the y219 split). A joined (aggregated secondary) multilink link was never registered as a forwarder face, so the real LinkstateForwarder DROPPED any data/control the sender routed onto it (forward_push / dispatch_local_subscribers early-return on faces.get(inbound)=None). Latent since y205 (DEFAULT priority always routes to first_alive=primary, so the secondary carried no data), first EXPOSED by y219a's priority routing (a non-DEFAULT Put deliberately rides the secondary; also DEFAULT=Data(5) falls in the LOW band, so post-y219a even a plain DEFAULT publish on a qos aggregate rides the possibly-secondary LOW-band link). KEY DESIGN ARBITRATION (3-agent DESIGN + direct-read): the naive call-site re-attribution (drive_joined_face forwards the PRIMARY id) BREAKS the receiver-side per-face observation that MULTIPLE committed+PUSHED tests rely on (the y205 deploy_active_two_links reliability-segregation assert_ne! on faces, and the y219a priority-segregation faces.len()==2) -- the DESIGN agent's "no observer" claim was wrong, the test forwarders ARE observers. So the fix is FORWARDER-INTERNAL (option D'): drive_joined_face is UNCHANGED (forwards the physical id), and only the REAL LinkstateForwarder resolves a joined FaceId to the session's PRIMARY registered face at the TOP of forward() -- via a new joined_faces map populated by two new FaceForwarder default-no-op methods register_joined/deregister_joined the accept loop calls at the JOIN / secondary-death. Observation-only test forwarders keep seeing the physical id (per-face witnesses unaffected), while the routing forwarder presents ONE logical face per aggregate (the faithful zenoh model: an aggregated transport is one FaceState; also unifies the per-link keyexpr alias table). The delivery fix is proven directly by a LinkstateForwarder lib unit (a Put on the joined FaceId is DROPPED before register_joined, DELIVERED after, DROPPED after deregister_joined -- diagnose-first verified RED when register_joined is neutered), and the accept-loop WIRING (register_joined called with secondary-not-registered -> primary-registered) by an assertion in the y219a deploy e2e. SCOPE (deferred, named, user-approved split): the demo binary reachability (a prioritized forwarder publish_qos + --express-high/--low CLI + a 2-proc black-box e2e) is a separable follow-up -- the in-process proof is the clean deterministic one (a black-box demo delivery witness needs a local-sub on --subscribe + is convergence-coin-flip-prone). full run-ci pending the batch push; per-atom host lanes green (lib unit incl diagnose-first RED, deploy e2e 3/3 with the wiring assert + per-face preserved, e2e 5, readd 1, routing-routes 21, all clippy -D warnings, fmt).

Round 311y220.decision_summary: R311y220 -- demo-reachability prioritized publish (the y219b-deferred, user-approved follow-up). Threads an application QoS priority from the forwarder publish API down to the previously-clamped dispatch_push(Priority::DEFAULT) at session_actions.rs (~3145), making the y217 select_link band routing + y219a per-face band assignment reachable from the application -- before y220 the forwarder publish API hard-clamped DEFAULT, so an app could never originate a banded Put. Layered base-delegates twin, byte-identical on the DEFAULT path: send_network_message_qos (kernel) is fed by fan_out_qos which is fed by publish_qos (forwarder); the base send_network_message / fan_out / publish delegate at Priority::DEFAULT (the Push arm prior hard-coded DEFAULT is now the default arg; all non-Push arms are control-plane and ignore priority -- Declare/Oam self-specify Control, Request/Interest/Response take none). Demo `--express-high` / `--low` flags (a new PublishBand enum -> RealTime/HIGH-band + express-flush | Background/LOW-band + non-express) drive publish_qos over an aggregated qos multilink session; the `--put` config-write path stays plain publish (control-plane DEFAULT). New ungated `use wz_session_core::qos::Priority` in linkstate_forward.rs + `pub use wz_session_core::qos` in wz-runtime-tokio/lib.rs (so the demo names wz::runtime_tokio::qos::Priority). 3-agent DESIGN review (pre-code) + 3-agent IMPL review (post-build), direct-read arbitrated. HONEST SCOPE (arbitrated by review): the 2-proc e2e wz_peer_multilink_qos_reach proves publish_qos send-PATH REACHABILITY from the demo binary (a `--express-high` Put originated via publish_qos and DELIVERED over the aggregated qos session; the `originating ExpressHigh Put via publish_qos` once-witness proves the NEW branch was taken, not the DEFAULT fall-through). Round 311y222.decision_summary: R311y222 -- TX batch frame pins its FULL (priority, reliability) conduit, not priority alone. The batch reopen/flush decision in dispatch_network_message keyed on batch.priority only, so a same-priority / different-reliability message was absorbed into a frame with the wrong R flag + SN ring (a reliability-MISLABEL: best-effort delivered on the reliable channel or vice versa -- both SN rings stay in-sync, no desync/reassembly corruption; small live blast radius since wz has no reliable retransmit today, high fidelity/forward-safety value). Fix: an UNGATED reliability predicate reading the open frame own R flag (frame_wire_reliability(&batch.buf), no new BatchTx field) OR-ed with the existing qos-gated priority predicate; the flush routes the prev frame by its own conduit (y217 #3). UNGATED because two reliability Frame-SN conduits (AtomicTxSn { reliable, best_effort }) exist even on a non-QoS session -- the old check was wholly transport-qos-gated, so a non-QoS batching build had NO conduit check at all. zenoh per-(priority,reliability) frame-boundary parity (zenoh-codec CurrentFrame/NewFrame); a deliberate divergence from vendored zenoh-pico, which blind-appends mixed-reliability. 3-DESIGN + 3-IMPL adversarial, direct-read arbitrated (all SHIP); 2 review cleanups landed (frame_wire_reliability double-read hoist, loop-comment staleness).

The RELIABILITY predicate is UNGATED -- read from the open frame's own R flag via frame_wire_reliability(&batch.buf), so no new BatchTx field -- because two reliability Frame-SN conduits exist even on a non-QoS session (AtomicTxSn { reliable, best_effort }); the PRIORITY predicate stays transport-qos-gated (per-priority conduits are QoS-only). Round 311y226.decision_summary: R311y226 -- faithful app-observable publish priority (#3 of the §5.1 transport-qos residuals, REFRAMED). Extends R311y22a (codecs) to the sce-codegen-BINARY-path emits: the 11 generated files (reassembly_slot / scouting / session_fsm_unicast / session_fsm_multicast / multicast_peer statecharts + reassembly_pool_ap + reassembly_pool_mcu + scout_rx_pool_mcu / session_rx_pool_mcu / session_rx_pool_mcu_minimal / session_rx_pool_mcu_multicast pools) are now COMMITTED under out/<crate>/ and include!'d from there, so wz-session-core / wz-runtime-tokio / wz-runtime-lwip build with NO build script and wz-link-lwip's build.rs is reduced to the lwip_real_build cfg relay (codegen removed). All fixes confirmed by direct read (agents arbitrated; agents over-flag): (H1, critical) Layer B2 -- the committed-codegen regen-diff gate, R311y22's core SSOT guarantee (committed == regenerated) -- was NOT wired into GitHub CI; it ran ONLY in the pre-push hook (bypassable via --no-verify / an uninstalled hook), so a hand-edited or stale committed out/ could pass server-side. WORSE: R311y22d's ci.yml comment + its ledger FALSELY claimed B2 "runs on the Linux ci job". Fixed: added a `--layer B2` step to the .github ci job (it already has libxml2 + builds sce-codegen, so the xtask codegen toolchain is present), server-enforcing the gate AND making the R311y22d claim true. (H2) From-path CWD-dependence: sce-codegen derives the `// From:` provenance line by stripping the CWD from the absolute SCXML path (vendor/sce/sce-build/src/lib.rs resolve_source_path); the xtask never anchored CWD, so a contributor regenerating from a non-root CWD would taint committed From-lines (absolute home-dir leak in the deploy case) and false-positive the regen-diff gate for them. Fixed: xtask main() now set_current_dir(repo_root) before any codegen -- BYTE-NEUTRAL for the current committed files (they were generated from repo root; git status out/ is empty after regen), robust for any contributor/CI/launch-CWD. (M) strip_inner_attrs was DUPLICATED in wz-codegen-build + the xtask switchboard leg -- a DRY/drift risk (the regen-diff byte-faithfulness depends on ONE strip predicate; the very shape R311y21 eliminated for the clock); hoisted to a shared `pub wz_codegen_build::strip_inner_attrs_file`, deleted the xtask copy. (LOW docs) CLAUDE.md + THIRD_PARTY.md license policy reconciled (out/** is COMMITTED in-repo since R311y22 -> redistributed; carries SCE's MIT header only on the 8 statechart *_sm.rs, no SPDX on the 64 codec/pool emits, never a wz SPDX -- the prohibition holds, the positive "carry SCE MIT header" claim was ~1/8 accurate); fixed the dangling xtask CODECS-sync ref to the deleted build.rs, the xtask SCE-MAP "tracked separately" (-> SCE's own traceability/sce-map-attribute-stripped diagnostic + dual-marker fallback), the stale mcu-qemu-demo AtomicU32 doc (now AtomicU64). The review POSITIVELY confirmed (vs SCE source, NOT smells): SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 (drift.rs:120 reproducible-builds knob), the strip transforms (SCE's own dual-marker diagnostic), wz-mcu-clock soundness, byte-faithfulness, feature-gating preservation, build.rs gutting completeness, xtask standalone-workspace isolation, north-star alignment. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0. The fix makes the code match its own documented intent: the test comment already claimed 'the post-shutdown assertion below holds even if the in-run app-tick raced SIGTERM (rem-2 -- mirrors the data/topology witnesses)', but the code still gated on the racy in-run wait. verification_bullets: Root-cause via direct read: run-ci.sh:352 run_layer runs every layer foreground/sequentially (no &, no wait, no backgrounding); order ... E6(3735) -> F -> G(3737) -> Q(3738), so G/Q run AFTER E6 and cannot saturate its window -- the carry's G/Q-concurrency premise is structurally false; E6-in-CI == E6-standalone (both run the 4 tests in parallel).

Reproduction (the arbiter): 16 single-triple trials + 12 faithful 4-parallel E6 trials (exact CI command) under a sustained yes-farm at load-avg 86, plus baseline -- the full forward+retract lifecycle completed in <0.9s EVERY time (baseline ~0.5s). Root-cause (b) 'withdraw-propagation stall under backpressure' falsified; the undeclare path does not stall under load.

Positive: a normal run logs 'publisher subscriber interest withdrawn' TWICE in peer-A -- in-run (1551) AND the shutdown-summary emit (1607) after the 'peer: shutdown;' line -- so the deterministic backstop is real and fires from state regardless of app-tick timing (A is terminated FIRST, B/C still up, so empty-interest can only mean the undeclare propagated).

Negative (no false-pass): with C NOT retracting (--unsubscribe-after-data dropped), peer-A logs 'learned' 1x but 'withdrawn' 0x through graceful shutdown -- a genuinely-broken withdraw still FAILS the assertion.

Recurrence diagnosability confirmed: a forced-fail run (E6 flags --ignored --quiet) printed all three peers' FULL timestamped stderr (env_logger [..Z INFO..]) via the test eprintln dumps + the panic embedding peer-A's capture -- a future failure is diagnosable from the single run, no reproduction needed (run_qemu_case philosophy).

(a) is_qos config sourcing: spawn_router_mcast_egress/ingress gain a `qos` param -> MulticastParams.is_qos, driven by the demo `--multicast-qos` flag; (b) the direct multicast-Session send seam gains a `priority`: Session::publish_qos stamps the app band onto the MulticastTxItem, closing the WHOLE-SESSION finding that the multicast arm hard-coded Priority::DEFAULT (a direct publish over a QoS group egressed at DEFAULT). CORRECTION by direct-read (arbiter): the multicast QoS offer is a SEPARATE knob from unicast -- zenoh keeps transport.multicast.qos.enabled (QoSMulticastConf default FALSE) distinct from transport.unicast.qos.enabled (QoSUnicastConf default TRUE) and its multicast manager reads config.multicast.is_qos on its own (defaults.rs:236/229, establishment.rs:54, manager.rs:40) -- so the seam sources a distinct --multicast-qos flag, NOT the unicast WzConfig.qos the prior ACTIVATION sketch assumed (no dead WzConfig.multicast_qos field; the router demo path takes no WzConfig). Round 311y235.decision_summary: R311y235 -- typed PublishOptions::with_priority (the R311y226/y232 two-input priority UNIFICATION, item 3): merge the transport conduit band + the app-observable QoS byte into ONE typed source. with_priority(p) sets the low-3-bit priority sub-field of the single opts.qos byte (preserving congestion+express); Session::publish derives the conduit band from opts.qos.priority() via the new priority_band() (was hard-coded Priority::DEFAULT); publish_qos FOLDS its explicit band into opts under pubsub-priority (delegates to publish(opts.with_priority(p))) so conduit+observable+loopback cannot desync, and threads the band straight to the conduit without pubsub-priority (signature-stable). publish_aliased + publish_shm switched to send_network_message_qos(..., priority_band()) so ALL publish surfaces are unified (publish_shm was the last split surface). Faithful to zenoh single QoSType (resolve_put / msg.priority()) + pico (_z_n_qos_make / msg._qos._val), matching the already-unified LinkstateForwarder::publish_qos. STRUCTURE-only, inventory UNCHANGED. 2-agent DESIGN pre-code (caught the fold + the publish_shm miss) + 2-agent IMPL post-build (all 4 tests discriminate on revert, no oversell). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: publish_common.rs: +PublishOptions::with_priority(Priority) [pubsub-priority-gated] -- merges p into the low-3-bit priority sub-field of the SINGLE opts.qos byte via (base & !0x07) | p.wire_byte(), preserving congestion(bit3)+express(bit4); base = existing qos.raw or QosLevel::DEFAULT (0x05). +priority_band(&self)->Priority [ungated pub(super)] = opts.qos.map(|q| q.priority()).unwrap_or(Priority::DEFAULT), the conduit band derived from the single source. +ungated `use wz_session_core::qos::Priority` (consumed by the ungated priority_band on every profile).

mod.rs Session::publish: replaced the hard-coded Priority::DEFAULT with `let band = opts.priority_band()` so a with_priority (or raw with_qos) publish rides the matching per-priority conduit AND is observable as Sample.priority from ONE value.

mod.rs Session::publish_qos: FOLD under pubsub-priority -> self.publish(keyexpr, payload, opts.with_priority(priority)); not(pubsub-priority) -> self.publish_prioritized(opts, priority). Signature unchanged (feature-independent, signature-stability rule). Closes the reachable divergence with_qos(low)+publish_qos(high).

mod.rs publish_aliased + publish_shm: send_network_message(...) -> send_network_message_qos(..., opts.priority_band()). The _qos seam is present wherever the codec-push (+transport-unicast) remote leg compiles (same gate publish uses); no-priority is byte-identical (base send_network_message is the trait default that already calls _qos with Priority::DEFAULT). publish_shm was the LAST split literal-publish surface (carried the observable qos ext + express but pinned the conduit to DEFAULT).

tests.rs: +4 tests -- publish_options_with_priority_is_single_source_band (unit: band derive + bit3/bit4 preservation), publish_with_priority_propagates_band_to_loopback_sample (observable half), publish_qos_folds_band_into_observable_sample (fold observable), publish_with_priority_routes_multicast_conduit_band (COMPOSED conduit band from the BASE publish, both-transports+pubsub-priority gate -- the leg where the publish->priority_band->tx band chain is directly observable).

run-ci.sh Layer C1bc: +item3 arm -- runs publish_with_priority_routes_multicast_conduit_band + clippy --all-targets -D warnings under transport-unicast,transport-multicast,transport-link-udp,codec-push,transport-qos,pubsub-put,pubsub-allow-loop,pubsub-priority (multicast-only+pubsub-priority is PRE-EXISTING-incompatible -- the SessionRuntime ActionsHandle GAT is transport-unicast-gated -- so both transports required).

Default lib tests: 287 passed / 0 failed (incl the 3 pubsub-priority tests + every publish_aliased regression test). Composed multicast test: verified 1 passed (NOT 0-filtered) under the both-transports+pubsub-priority combo.

Round 311y24.decision_summary: R311y24 -- FreeRTOS integration Round 1: freertos-sys foundation. Vendored FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0 (vendor/freertos-kernel submodule, MIT, pin dbf70559b) + crates/freertos-sys statically compiles the kernel core (tasks/list/queue) + GCC/ARM_CM3 (Cortex-M3) port + heap_4 via cc::Build for the COOPERATIVE SINGLE-TASK PROFILE (configUSE_TIMERS/event-groups/stream-buffers/co-routines OFF -- one task hosts the wz cooperative executor, the FreeRTOS analogue of zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=0 ST mode) + hand-written FFI (xTaskCreate/vTaskStartScheduler/vTaskDelay/xTaskGetTickCount/pvPortMalloc + ARMv7-M port exception handlers). Mirrors lwip-sys but stub-on-host/real-on-cross (the ARM_CM3 port is Cortex-M-specific, host x86 cannot compile it). Reference FreeRTOSConfig.h (mps2-an385, 3 NVIC prio bits) baked in port/, deploy-overridable via WZ_FREERTOS_CONFIG. Verified: cross thumbv7m-none-eabi -> libfreertos.a 118KB; host stub freertos_real_build=0 / cross real =1; clippy+fmt clean; validate orphan new=+0. NEXT Round 2: wz-runtime-freertos impl Runtime reusing the wz-runtime-coop executor SSOT + FreeRTOS ClockSource (xTaskGetTickCount) + critical_section sync.
changes_bullets: vendor/freertos-kernel: new git submodule (FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0, pin dbf70559b, MIT) + .gitmodules entry + THIRD_PARTY.md ledger entry (origin/pin/license/scope, mirrors the vendor/lwip entry shape).

crates/freertos-sys (new): Cargo.toml (links="freertos" for DEP_FREERTOS_* metadata propagation) + build.rs (cc::Build, modelled on lwip-sys) + src/lib.rs (hand-written FFI, #![no_std]) + port/FreeRTOSConfig.h (reference mps2-an385 Cortex-M3 config).

build.rs compiles the kernel core (tasks.c + list.c + queue.c) + portable/GCC/ARM_CM3/port.c (ARMv7-M / Cortex-M3) + portable/MemMang/heap_4.c. Cooperative single-task profile: configUSE_TIMERS / event-groups / stream-buffers / co-routines all OFF, so timers.c / event_groups.c / stream_buffer.c are NOT compiled.

Stub-on-host / real-on-cross (the KEY difference from lwip-sys, whose NO_SYS core builds on host too): the ARM_CM3 port is Cortex-M-specific (SysTick/NVIC/PendSV regs + ARMv7-M asm) so it cannot compile on host x86 -> host build emits no static lib + cargo:freertos_real_build=0; bare-metal cross (thumbv7m/thumbv7em -none-eabi*) emits libfreertos.a + freertos_real_build=1.

Config selection mirrors lwip-sys's WZ_LWIP_PORT: WZ_FREERTOS_CONFIG (deploy-supplied dir with FreeRTOSConfig.h) overrides the in-crate port/ reference (so freertos-sys + Layer G cross-compile standalone).

src/lib.rs FFI surface (curated, hand-written not bindgen because FreeRTOS headers are config-macro-heavy): xTaskCreate / vTaskStartScheduler / vTaskDelay / vTaskDelete / xTaskGetTickCount / pvPortMalloc / vPortFree + the ARMv7-M port exception handlers (vPortSVCHandler / xPortPendSVHandler / xPortSysTickHandler, for the Round-3 cortex-m-rt vector wiring) + BaseType_t/UBaseType_t/TickType_t/TaskHandle_t/TaskFunction_t + pdPASS/pdFAIL.
crates/Cargo.toml: freertos-sys added to workspace members (after lwip-sys).
verification_bullets: Architecture (review-validated R311y13 + de-risk 2026-06-25): the wz cooperative async executor (wz-runtime-coop run_until_idle, lwip-FREE, generic over ClockSource) runs inside ONE FreeRTOS task = zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=0 single-thread mode. freertos-sys is the FFI foundation; Round 2's wz-runtime-freertos is the impl Runtime that reuses the coop executor SSOT + a FreeRTOS ClockSource (xTaskGetTickCount) + critical_section sync.
Toolchain confirmed: arm-none-eabi-gcc 10.3.1 + qemu-system-arm present (no SDK needed for FreeRTOS, unlike Zephyr).

Cross-compile thumbv7m-none-eabi (Cortex-M3, mps2-an385 class): cargo build -p freertos-sys --target thumbv7m-none-eabi EXIT=0 -> libfreertos.a (118 KB) produced; arm-none-eabi-gcc invoked with -mthumb -march=armv7-m + the in-crate reference FreeRTOSConfig.h. (Fixed 1 config conflict during bring-up: V11.1.0 rejects defining BOTH configUSE_16_BIT_TICKS and configTICK_TYPE_WIDTH_IN_BITS -- kept the modern configTICK_TYPE_WIDTH_IN_BITS=32.)

Dual-mode confirmed: cross build output has freertos_real_build=1 (real, libfreertos.a present); host build output has freertos_real_build=0 (stub, no static lib, FFI decls still compile). Host cargo build -p freertos-sys EXIT=0.
clippy -p freertos-sys --target thumbv7m-none-eabi clean (0); cargo fmt -p freertos-sys clean.

validate_workspace EXIT=0: orphan new=+0 (the new crate touches no atomic-store section/inventory; freertos-sys is a -sys crate like lwip-sys/zenoh-pico-sys, not an A3 feature atom -- the platform-freertos active flip is the Round-4 A3 atom).

Pre-existing-lane safety: freertos-sys host build is a stub (lib decls compile, no C), so cargo build --workspace / Layer C1 on host is unaffected; no CI lane added yet (the cross + QEMU coverage lands with the deploy crate in Round 3/4).
carry_forward_bullets: R311y24 = FreeRTOS integration Round 1 (the foundation): vendored FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0 submodule + crates/freertos-sys that cross-compiles the kernel core + ARM_CM3 port + heap_4 for the cooperative single-task profile, with hand-written FFI. Stub-on-host / real-on-cross (ARM_CM3 port is Cortex-M-only). Verified: thumbv7m libfreertos.a 118KB, clippy/fmt/validate clean.

NEXT (Round 2): crates/wz-runtime-freertos -- impl Runtime reusing the wz-runtime-coop cooperative executor SSOT (run_until_idle, generic over ClockSource) inside one FreeRTOS task. New seams: (1) ClockSource = xTaskGetTickCount (the SysTick analogue; wz-runtime-core/src/time.rs:26 already names this shape); (2) sync = critical_section::Mutex (FreeRTOS has a critical-section impl) -- reuse wz-runtime-coop/src/sync.rs; (3) net = reuse NO_SYS=1 lwip (wz-link-lwip), no FreeRTOS sys_arch needed (poll lwip single-threaded). A #[global_allocator] bridging to pvPortMalloc/vPortFree (heap_4).

Round 3: boot -- cortex-m-rt vector table routes SVCall/PendSV/SysTick to vPortSVCHandler/xPortPendSVHandler/xPortSysTickHandler (indirect routing, configCHECK_HANDLER_INSTALLATION=0 in the reference config) + xTaskCreate(wz_task)+vTaskStartScheduler + deploy/mcu-freertos-demo (mps2-an385 QEMU e2e, sibling of deploy/mcu-qemu-demo) + a Layer G/Q CI lane.

Round 4: platform-freertos -> REAL cfg(feature) site -> status ACTIVE (the A3 atom; NOT foundational -- selected by the link+runtime adapter). HONESTY OBLIGATION (R311y13): label "cooperative single-task profile"; native-multi-task (pico-MT parity, xTaskCreate per read/lease thread) = deliberate re-openable future profile.
THEN Zephyr (heaviest; SDK install pending: pip install --user tqdm + west sdk install -t arm-zephyr-eabi, OR manual sdk-ng tarball SDK_VERSION 1.0.1).

Round 311y242.decision_summary: R311y242 -- congestion + express wz->pico cross-impl witness, closing the named R311y240 follow-up. The Push outer QoS ext packs priority (low 3 bits) + congestion (bit 3, nodrop) + express (bit 4) into one byte; y240 proved the PRIORITY sub-field via pico z_sample_priority but deferred congestion+express with the claim 'congestion has no per-sample getter; express is a batching-only effect'. Direct read of vendor pin zenoh-pico 3b3ab65 falsifies that ([[feedback-verify-no-observable-claims]]): primitives.h declares z_sample_congestion_control (2255) + z_sample_express (2266), api.c implements both as _z_n_qos_get_(congestion_control,express)(sample->qos) reading the SAME sample->qos byte y240 already proved wire-populated. A new Layer-E-auto-swept test (wz_qos_congestion_express_to_pico_zsub) publishes a Put whose QoS byte = QosLevel::from_parts(Data, Block, true) = 0x1D (!= DEFAULT 0x05 so the ext is emitted, not suppressed) and a patched pico z_sub_attachment decodes it, printing 'with congestion: 1' + 'with express: 1' -- discriminating vs the default 0/0 a dropped byte would show. NO send-path change: build_push_outer_extensions already emits the whole q.raw byte under any(pubsub-priority/-congestion-control/-express) and pubsub-priority is active, so congestion+express already rode the wire; the witness only sets + reads them. NO inventory change: pubsub-congestion-control + pubsub-express were already active (A3 unchanged). Honest limit: witnesses the express BIT foreign-decode, NOT express batching-flush semantics. 3 read-only review agents (discrimination / patch-safety / claim-honesty) surfaced 1 low finding (a tautological verify-comment, corrected). validate orphan new=+0; full run-ci batched to the pre-push gate.

No new publish API added: with_qos + QosLevel::from_parts already exist, and congestion/express carry no transport-conduit-band role (unlike priority), so no with_priority-style single-source setter is warranted.

Round 311y250.decision_summary: R311y250 -- query-value SESSION-API THREADING (the R311y248 follow-up). Threads a querier VALUE (payload + encoding, the Q_B/Q_E value ext 0x03) from QueryOptions to the wire: QueryOptions.payload/encoding -> query_metadata (collapse the two ergonomic slots into the single (encoding, payload) wire unit, (None,None)->None) -> new QueryMetadata.value -> build_request_query_with_meta (gated query-value) -> RequestQueryBuilder::query_value. New runtime-tokio query-value feature (default + forward). Before y250 the value was reachable only via the low-level RequestQueryBuilder::query_value; now QueryOptions::get().with_payload(..).with_encoding(..) propagates on the outbound Query. with_payload/with_encoding kept ungated (signature-stable divergence from the hard-gated with_source_info/with_attachment siblings, per the pre-existing query_options_with_setters_chain test + feedback_signature_stability). 3 read-only review agents (wire/completeness/API) + direct-read arbiter caught+fixed a stale send_request_query_with_meta docstring mislabeling the attachment ext as id=0x03 (0x03 is the VALUE ext this round wires; attachment is 0x05) + the session_glue coverage-table twin. Loopback value surfacing deferred (consistent with attachment/source_info). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/metadata.rs: QueryMetadata gains a `value: Option<(EncodingHint, Vec<u8>)>` slot (the wire `_z_value_t` unit = (encoding, payload)), unconditional field mirroring the always-present source_info slot; is_empty() adds `&& self.value.is_none()`; the QueryOptions->wire coverage doc table collapses the payload/encoding rows into one `RequestQueryBuilder::query_value` row (no longer "threading pending") and the "partial vs QueryOptions" framing is corrected to "every wire field threads; allowed_destination is the sole dispatch-time exclusion". New unit test query_metadata_with_value_is_not_empty.

crates/wz-session-core/src/request_build.rs: build_request_query_with_meta threads meta.value onto RequestQueryBuilder::query_value behind `#[cfg(feature = "query-value")]`, ordered FIRST (build() re-orders the Query body ext chain to value 0x03 -> source_info 0x01 -> attachment 0x05 regardless of setter order); fn doc updated. New gated test build_request_query_with_meta_threads_value_to_ext_0x03 proves byte-parity vs a direct query_value call + the fully-empty-value elide (no-meta parity).
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: add `query-value = ["wz-session-core/query-value"]` forward (11th query feature) + `"query-value"` in the default set (mirrors query-source-info).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/querier.rs: QueryOptions::query_metadata() collapses the two ergonomic slots (payload / encoding, each independently Optional) into the single QueryMetadata::value unit -- (None,None)->None so a default QueryOptions stays is_empty() (no-meta fast path), else Some((encoding.unwrap_or_default(), payload.unwrap_or_default())); population ungated (mirrors push_metadata). with_payload/with_encoding kept UNGATED (signature-stable) unlike the hard-gated with_source_info/with_attachment siblings -- named divergence, justified by the pre-existing query_options_with_setters_chain test exercising with_payload without query-value + the feedback_signature_stability anchor; docs updated (no longer "threading pending"). New test module value_threading_tests (gated all(test, query-get, query-value)): with_payload/with_encoding threading + the (None,None)->None default-no-value collapse.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/tests.rs: query_options_query_metadata_extracts_wire_fields comment corrected (was "MUST NOT carry them yet") + a meta.value assertion added + the `unused-payload` literal renamed `q-value-payload` (it is now used).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: the twin QueryMetadata coverage doc table (session_glue mirror) synced to the metadata.rs version (payload+encoding -> one query_value row; "partial" framing corrected) -- the R311y249-style whole-tree sibling-comment sweep.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: send_request_query_with_meta docstring enumeration corrected (review-caught sibling miss) -- added the meta.value (0x03) + meta.source_info (0x01) + meta.parameters bullets that were absent, and FIXED a real error: the meta.attachment bullet named the attachment ext id=0x03, but 0x03 is the VALUE ext (attachment is 0x05) -- a direct id collision with the slot this round wires; now lists the pico Query-body emit order (value 0x03 -> source_info 0x01 -> attachment 0x05).

Review-driven doc precision (querier.rs, non-blocking): with_payload doc reframed to name all THREE QueryOptions setter shapes (hard-gated-disappears / ungated-store-no-ops / ungated-unconditional-store) rather than only contrasting the hard-gated siblings, and to disclose that on a query-value-OFF build the captured value is inert (bytes unchanged) but forfeits Session::query's is_empty() fast path; query_metadata() comment records why the value derivation is intentionally ungated (a gate would break the non-query-value-gated query_options_query_metadata_extracts_wire_fields test).
verification_bullets: full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 -- judged by exit code (feedback_runci_verdict_exit_code_only); the round adds a runtime-tokio default feature (query-value) so Layer A3 (inventory<->cargo join) and Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace, default features) both exercise the new wiring; Layer C1be (session-core query-value feature set) covers the codec-side threading test.

Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace): runtime-tokio default now carries query-get + query-value, so querier.rs value_threading_tests (with_payload/with_encoding collapse onto QueryMetadata::value + the (None,None)->None default) and the updated query_options_query_metadata_extracts_wire_fields (meta.value assertion) compile and run.

Layer C1be (cargo test -p wz-session-core --features ...,query-value,...): session-core build_request_query_with_meta_threads_value_to_ext_0x03 (byte-parity vs direct query_value + fully-empty elide) + query_metadata_with_value_is_not_empty run green; 342 session-core lib tests pass.

Targeted pre-run-ci gates green: cargo fmt --all --check EXIT 0; cargo clippy -p wz-session-core (query-value set) -D warnings EXIT 0; cargo clippy -p wz-runtime-tokio (default) -D warnings EXIT 0 (one doc_lazy_continuation lint from a `+`-leading doc-wrap line fixed pre-commit); session-core builds cleanly WITHOUT query-value (the `#[cfg(query-value)]` wire-threading gate elides, proving signature-stability of the ungated with_payload/with_encoding setters).

Wire faithfulness: the threading is byte-identical to a direct RequestQueryBuilder::query_value call (test asserts via .wire()); the empty-value guard lives in build() (pico's `_z_bytes_check(payload) || _z_encoding_check(encoding)` .body predicate), so a default query and a fully-empty value both emit the metadata-stripped baseline unchanged (no byte regression). Emit order value 0x03 -> source_info 0x01 -> attachment 0x05 enforced by build(), unaffected by the new setter-order-independent threading.

Round 311y252.decision_summary: R311y252 -- query LOOPBACK body-metadata surfacing; closes the y250/y251 carry's named NEXT actionable. Before this round build_loopback_query (wz-runtime-tokio session/mod.rs) built the loopback Query with ONLY the selector parameters (Q_P, R311y94) and left extensions=None, so a SessionLocal queryable's QueryView::attachment() / source_info() / payload() / encoding() ALL returned None even when the querier set them via QueryOptions::with_attachment / with_source_info / with_payload / with_encoding -- the three ext-borne slots surfaced on the WIRE path only. Round 311y253.decision_summary: R311y253 -- a REAL BUILD BREAK fixed at its root, surfaced as a side-finding of the R311y252 review and taken next under the CLAUDE.md absolute-priority rule (build errors preempt all other work). DialConfig (wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs) carries TWO #[cfg]-gated fields (tls @transport-link-tls, quic @transport-link-quic) and was the ONE options struct in the crate still constructed by exhaustive struct literal. Every literal in the tree named exactly ONE of the two fields, so each was missing the other's: SIX integration-test targets (quic_e2e, quic_datagram_e2e, scouting_multicast_loopback, session_reconnect_e2e, tls_e2e, tls_pem_mtls_e2e) failed E0063 under --all-features, in BOTH directions (missing field  on the tls-side literals, missing field  on the quic-side ones). The two directions are what proves this was structural, not a one-site typo: the shape itself was wrong, because an exhaustive literal over cfg-gated fields only compiles for the single feature combination its author happened to build with. Fixed structurally rather than per-site: DialConfig is now #[non_exhaustive] + with_tls / with_quic hard-gated builders -- the QueryOptions / PublishOptions / QueryableOptions idiom this struct was the lone exception to (QueryOptions' own docstring already says 'never struct-literal externally'), which makes the fragile form UNREPRESENTABLE for out-of-crate callers (tests/ are separate crates) so a future third cfg-gated transport field cannot break them either. All 5 literal sites converted. The DEEPER gap was the missing GATE: Layer C2 runs clippy --workspace --all-targets on the DEFAULT feature set only, so it never composes two optional features that each own a lane but are never enabled TOGETHER -- exactly how a six-target break shipped unseen. New Layer C1bf clippy-gates -p wz-runtime-tokio --all-targets --all-features. Scoped per-crate deliberately: a workspace-wide --all-features is structurally IMPOSSIBLE here (sce-rust-runtime declares no_std XOR http-send behind a compile_error!), which also explains why no such lane ever existed. Build-integrity + CI-gate only: no wire change, no cfg gate added, no atom flipped, inventory UNCHANGED. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 with C1bf passing; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `DialConfig` gains `#[non_exhaustive]` + two hard-gated `with_*` builders (`with_tls` @transport-link-tls, `with_quic` @transport-link-quic) -- the shape every other options struct in the crate already uses (`QueryOptions` / `PublishOptions` / `QueryableOptions`: "construct via `default` plus optional `with_*` setters -- never struct-literal externally"). Both setters are HARD-gated (the fn disappears when the feature is off) rather than ungated-no-op, because their parameter types (`TlsDialConfig` / `QuicDialConfig`) are themselves cfg-gated, so the signature cannot exist without the feature -- the same precedent as `QueryOptions::with_attachment` / `with_source_info`. `#[non_exhaustive]` makes the fragile exhaustive-literal form UNREPRESENTABLE for out-of-crate callers (integration tests under `tests/` are separate crates), so a future third cfg-gated transport field cannot silently break them either.

Round 311y253a.decision_summary: R311y253a -- frozen-ledger CORRECTION to Round 311y253's decision_summary (the entry body itself is untouched, per the frozen-ledger contract: corrections arrive as new entries, never as a rewrite). Round 311y253's decision text was passed to `mnemosyne-cli append-changelog-entry --decision` as a double-quoted SHELL argument, and the prose contained backtick-wrapped identifiers. Bash evaluated those backticks as COMMAND SUBSTITUTION before the CLI ever saw the string, so two identifiers were executed as commands (failing with "quic: command not found" / "tls: command not found") and were replaced by the EMPTY STRING in the stored text. The stored sentence therefore reads "in BOTH directions (missing field  on the tls-side literals, missing field  on the quic-side ones)" -- with the two field names silently deleted. THE CORRECTION: the two dropped identifiers are the field names quic and tls. The sentence should read: the tls-side struct literals failed with "missing field quic", and the quic-side ones with "missing field tls". No other field of Round 311y253 is affected -- its changes / verification / carry bullets were supplied via --changes-file / --verification-file / --carry-file, which the CLI reads directly off disk with no shell involvement, so those bullets carry the correct text (the verification bullet still records both E0063 directions verbatim). The substantive claims, the six failing targets, the fix, and the C1bf gate are all unchanged and remain accurate. PROCESS ROOT CAUSE + FIX (this is the durable part): every ledger entry in this project is dense technical prose full of backticked identifiers, and `--decision` is the ONE field passed as a shell argument rather than a file -- the CLI exposes --changes-file / --verification-file / --carry-file but NO --decision-file (verified: "unknown flag --decision-file"). So the decision field is the single shell-injection surface in the whole append path, and any backtick in it is silently evaluated. The safe form is to write the decision prose to a file and pass it as --decision "$(cat FILE)": command substitution of cat emits the file content literally and bash does NOT re-parse the substituted output, so backticks inside the content survive intact. This entry was appended that way.

R311y253 gated `-p wz-runtime-tokio --all-features` (Layer C1bf) after a cfg-gated-struct-field build break, and explicitly recorded that OTHER crates with `#[cfg(feature)]`-gated `pub` struct fields carry the same latent hazard with no gate. This round ran that sweep. The hazard class -- crates declaring a cfg-gated `pub` struct field, the exact shape an exhaustive struct literal cannot survive (it only compiles for the one feature combination its author built with) -- turns out to be THREE crates, not one: wz-runtime-tokio (12 such fields), wz-session-core (25, including `ApplicationLayerObserver` with EIGHT independently-gated `pub` fields), and wz-ap-demo (3). Both newly-found crates ALREADY compose clean under `--all-features --all-targets -D warnings`, so this is a gate placed over a latent hazard, NOT a second build break -- stated plainly so the entry is not read as having fixed one. C1bf now clippy-gates all three. The load-bearing addition is the DRIFT AUDIT inside the lane: it re-derives the hazard class from source on every run (a `#[cfg(feature ...)]` attribute immediately followed by a `pub <field>:` declaration) and FAILS, naming the crate, if any crate joins the class without being added to the lane's COVERED list. Without that audit the fix would have been a hardcoded list with the residual merely moved one level down -- the next crate to grow a cfg-gated pub field would sit outside the gate silently, which is precisely how the DialConfig break shipped in the first place. The audit is deliberately OVER-inclusive (an enum or private struct can trip it): a false positive costs one line in COVERED, a false negative costs a shipped build break. Proved both directions: the audit passes today naming all three crates, and a simulated drift (dropping wz-session-core from COVERED) makes it exit 1 naming exactly that crate. Round 311y255.decision_summary: R311y255 -- closes the long-carried "publish_qos congestion knob" item, and does it by fixing the SSOT violation underneath rather than bolting a second setter onto it. The QoS wire byte packs three sub-fields (`priority` low 3 bits, `nodrop` bit 3, `express` bit 4, per `_z_n_qos_create` network.h:84-89), and all three already rode the wire and were FOREIGN-PROVEN -- R311y242 (`wz_qos_congestion_express_to_pico_zsub`) has a real zenoh-pico subscriber decode congestion + express. But only ONE had a typed entry point: `PublishOptions::with_priority` (y235). A caller wanting `Block` had to hand-assemble the whole byte via `with_qos(QosLevel::from_parts(..))`, which forces them to restate the priority and express they did not want to change. That asymmetry is the carry. The naive fix -- add two more setters doing their own bit surgery -- would have spread the bit layout across a THIRD site: `QosLevel::from_parts` documents itself as "the SOLE packer ... so the layout lives once (no drift)", yet `PublishOptions::with_priority` already open-coded `& !0x07`, quietly falsifying that claim. So the layout was consolidated into the type that owns it: `QosLevel` gains named bit constants, a `congestion()` unpacker (the missing third accessor beside `priority()` / `is_express()`), and three per-field MERGE setters (`with_priority` / `with_congestion` / `with_express`) that each touch only their own sub-field; `from_parts` is now COMPOSED from those three rather than restating the shifts, making "the layout lives once" structurally true instead of a comment asking to be believed. `PublishOptions::with_priority` now delegates (its `& !0x07` is gone) and gains its two siblings, `with_congestion_control` + `with_express`, each gated on its own `pubsub-*` feature exactly as `with_priority` is. Untouched sub-fields fall back to the wire-DEFAULT byte (0x05 = Data / Drop / no-express), NOT a zeroed `Control` byte -- the trap R311y226 named. Behaviour-preservation is proven by the PRE-EXISTING byte-compare guards, which still pass unchanged: `qos_level_from_parts_packs_zenoh_pico_layout` pins 0x11 / 0x0D across the `from_parts` rewrite, and `publish_options_with_priority_is_single_source_band` pins bit-preservation across the delegation. Also carries a doc-truth-up: a foreign-proof test still flagged a `publish_common.rs` comment as STALE, but that comment had since been corrected -- a stale claim ABOUT a stale claim -- so it was dropped. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0; no wire change, no new atom, inventory UNCHANGED (the wire bits were already active and foreign-proven; this is the typed API surface for them).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/sample.rs: `QosLevel` becomes the single home of the `_z_n_qos_create` bit layout. New private named constants (PRIORITY_MASK 0x07 / NODROP_BIT 1<<3 / EXPRESS_BIT 1<<4) replace every open-coded literal; new `congestion()` unpacker completes the accessor trio beside `priority()` and `is_express()` (both now const fn and expressed via the constants); new per-field MERGE setters `with_priority` / `with_congestion` / `with_express` each rewrite ONLY their own sub-field and preserve the siblings. `from_parts` is now COMPOSED from those three setters instead of restating `priority.wire_byte() | (congestion.wire_bit() << 3) | ((express as u8) << 4)`, so its own "the SOLE packer ... the layout lives once" doc claim is structurally true rather than aspirational.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/publish_common.rs: `PublishOptions` gains the two typed QoS knobs that `with_priority` had been missing -- `with_congestion_control(CongestionControl)` (gated `pubsub-congestion-control`) and `with_express(bool)` (gated `pubsub-express`) -- each gated on its own feature exactly as `with_priority` is on `pubsub-priority`. All three now delegate to the `QosLevel` merge setters through a shared private `qos_base()` helper, so `with_priority`'s open-coded `& !0x07` mask is gone and no consumer re-derives the layout. `qos_base()` returns the already-attached QoS else `QosLevel::DEFAULT` (0x05), so sub-fields the caller did not set match a DEFAULT publish rather than a zeroed `Control`-priority byte.

Round 311y257.decision_summary: R311y257 -- give the inventory an IMPLEMENTATION axis, so it can answer "what work remains" without grepping English. The user asked how many rounds are left to pico/AP-full; trying to answer surfaced a structural defect, not just a missing number. `status` (active / reserved / deprecated) answers "is there a cfg knob?" -- per the active-iff-cfg-toggle rule -- and does NOT answer "is this built?". Those are different questions, and `reserved` was silently lumping together four unrelated situations: already-built-but-always-on (FOUNDATIONAL), genuinely unbuilt, deliberately excluded, and built-under-a-different-atom's-cargo-feature. The only place that distinction lived was free prose in the `reason` field, so "what is left" degraded to grepping English -- and two different greps of mine disagreed (10 vs 27), which is how the defect was caught. The earlier "~11 remaining atoms" figure came from the unreliable grep and was RETRACTED rather than re-guessed. Fixed within the closed Mnemosyne schema, since adding a field is forbidden (anti-patterns #9): the FIRST token of every non-active atom's `reason` must now be a tag from a closed 8-set, and the tag must agree with `status`. FOUNDATIONAL (built, always-on, no knob) / PARTIAL (built, named residual) / UNVERIFIED (code portable by construction, no CI lane proves it -- work is a lane, not code) / UNBUILT (genuinely not implemented) / BEYOND-PICO (deferred by design) / OUT-OF-SCOPE (deliberately excluded) / OBVIATED (no wz analog by construction) / PHANTOM (does not exist in zenoh). `active` needs no tag: built AND gated is unambiguous. PARTIAL and UNVERIFIED were not invented for symmetry -- the data forced them: session-extqos is NOT unbuilt, it is BUILT under the differently-named `transport-qos` cargo feature with a named S4 residual (an error in my own earlier count, which had it as "beyond-pico deferred"); and platform-macos / platform-windows have NO code to write at all (std+tokio is portable by construction) -- what they lack is a CI lane. Forcing either into UNBUILT or FOUNDATIONAL would have made the inventory lie. All 218 atoms tagged, 51 by this round's prefixing pass and the rest already conformant, with ZERO original reason text lost (verified against the committed HEAD store). The invariant is enforced as #5 in scripts/audit-catalog-status.sh (Layer A3), which also now PRINTS the roll-up every run: "REMAINING WORK (UNBUILT + PARTIAL + UNVERIFIED) = 9". So the question that started this is now a gate output, not a grep. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0; active count UNCHANGED (no code touched).

Legacy synonyms were NORMALIZED rather than double-prefixed (the "REAL BACKLOG" prefix introduced in R311y256 is exactly UNBUILT, so it was replaced, not stacked).

Six atoms had NO classifiable marker at all and were classified by direct read of their own reason text: platform-macos + platform-windows -> UNVERIFIED (their reasons already said "std+tokio host-portable but NO wz CI lane -> unverified host; cfg=0" -- there is no code to write, only a lane); platform-qnx -> OUT-OF-SCOPE (its reason: "neither zenoh nor zenoh-pico has a QNX port" -- outside the zenoh+pico catalog entirely, a 2nd-horizon candidate); routing-failover -> BEYOND-PICO ("pico none -> P4-deferred"); runtime-tokio-uring + runtime-zero-copy -> UNBUILT (genuinely unbuilt, but PERF concerns sourced from wz's own RFC/ARCHITECTURE, not protocol surface).

AUDIT_EXIT=0.

The gate FAILS on drift, proven in BOTH classes against doctored inventory copies (the store itself was never touched): (a) stripping the tag from api-compat-pico's reason -- the "a new atom lands untagged" case -- makes the audit exit non-zero with "FAIL: non-active atom whose reason does not START with an implementation tag", naming it; (b) flipping plugin-manager from deprecated to reserved while its reason still says OBVIATED makes it exit non-zero with "FAIL: implementation tag disagrees with status", naming the atom, its tag, and the status the tag implies. A gate that cannot fail is not a gate; both arms are exercised.

NEAR-MISS worth recording: the first attempt to prove drift-arm (b) reported a non-zero exit and was very nearly written up as 'caught'. It was not -- the fixture file had never been created (the command building it hit a 2-minute timeout mid-way), so the audit had died on a FileNotFoundError. A non-zero exit is NOT evidence a gate fired; the FAIL MESSAGE is. The arm was then re-run against a real fixture and produced the named failure quoted above. Judge a gate by what it PRINTS, not merely by its exit code.

The mutation path was the typed primitive throughout -- a loop over `mnemosyne-cli set-inventory-status --id ... --status ... --reason ...`. Round 311y258.decision_summary: R311y258 -- run-ci Layer A3 goes from 106s to 1s with a bit-identical verdict, and the round is gated the way this project already designed for rather than by another full run-ci. Prompted by the user's complaint that run-ci was too slow to develop against. Measured first (PRINCIPLES: base optimization on measurement, not assumption): a full run is 93 layers / 1349s / 22.5 min, and the top costs are Layer F 115s (MCU footprint), Layer A3 106s, C1ay 86s, C1j 67s, G 61s. A3 stood out as pure waste rather than real work: `has_gate(atom)` shelled out to `grep -rIlE 'feature *= *"<atom>"' crates --include=*.rs` INSIDE the per-atom loop, so it re-scanned every .rs file in the workspace 212 times -- once per catalog atom -- to answer 212 independent membership questions against the SAME corpus. O(atoms x tree), and every pass after the first re-read files it had already read. Replaced with ONE grep that emits every `feature = "..."` occurrence in crates/**/*.rs, folded into a set; has_gate is now an O(1) lookup. The matching semantics are UNCHANGED (same pattern, same corpus, same deliberately-unanchored "any occurrence counts" rule, which exists because a multi-line any(...) block puts the feature on its own line and a same-line `cfg(` requirement would miss it), so the audit's verdict is the same for every atom -- proven, not asserted: an A/B harness ran both implementations over all 212 atoms and compared verdicts, giving 0 differences at 111.3s vs 0.84s (133x). The gate's power is intact: re-verified that it still PASSES on the real inventory and still FAILS, naming the atom, on both drift arms (an untagged atom; a tag disagreeing with status). THE BIGGER FIX IS THE WORKFLOW, not the code: this project already ships `run-ci.sh --layer <X>` for targeted runs AND a pre-push hook that runs the FULL run-ci automatically, and the memory anchor already prescribes "fast host gate per atom; full run-ci ONCE per batch push". I had been ignoring all three -- running a manual full run-ci once PER ROUND (6 times this session, ~135 min) when the pre-push hook was going to run it anyway. Commits are local and revertible; the push is the boundary that needs the full net. This round is therefore gated by `run-ci.sh --layer A3` (1s) plus fmt, with the full run deferred to the pre-push hook. Deliberately NOT done: skipping layers by change-scope (e.g. "the diff has no MCU files, skip F/G/Q"). The memory anchor feedback_full_runci_all_host_lanes warns exactly against that, and R311y253 THIS SESSION was a six-target build break that NO lane caught because each feature had its own lane and nothing composed them -- a wrong skip rule re-opens precisely that class. Cost, not coverage, was the problem; cost is what got fixed.

The regex, the corpus, and the "any occurrence counts (not anchored to cfg()" rule are carried over verbatim, so no atom's verdict can change; the comment records WHY the pattern stays unanchored (a multi-line any(...) block puts the feature on its own line).
No behavioural change to the audit: same atoms=212 / active=130 line, same implementation-axis tally, same "REMAINING WORK = 9" roll-up, same pass/fail decisions. Only the cost changes.

R311y257 made "what is BUILT" a CI line; the north star ("zenoh + zenoh-pico FULL") does not turn on building 212 atoms, it turns on WITNESSING them against the real zenoh-pico C stack and the real zenoh-full router -- and that number existed only as a hand estimate ("~75% foreign-proven") in a memory file whose own text says it was never recomputed and whose cited authority does not exist in this repo. Layer A4 now derives it. The design took three adversarial reviews to get right and the first version was wrong in five load-bearing ways, all recorded here because the corrections ARE the design: (1) "derive, then gate" was FALSE -- a cfg site cannot lie about itself, which is why A3 inv#3 works, but a `// wz-proves:` doc-comment is inert prose that can; moving the claim from inventory prose to test prose relocates the lie, it does not derive it. The missing second arm was already in the tree: an atom that is not in the enabled-feature CLOSURE of the binary under test compiles to NOTHING in it, so it CANNOT have been witnessed -- a compiler-grounded refutation that kills the "list ten, witness one" class. (2) The corpus predicate ("proves iff it SPAWNS a foreign binary") EXCLUDED the strongest proofs: the 25 layer3_* tests LINK the real vendored zenoh-pico C library and byte-compare wz's encoder against pico's _z_*_encode, and they are the ONLY foreign proofs hosted CI runs unconditionally. The incentive was inverted -- adding a differential codec test would have LOWERED the number, adding a never-executed #[ignore]d zenohd test would have RAISED it. Linking the foreign impl is a stronger proof than spawning it. (3) The percentage was not well-formed: the numerator was not a subset of the denominator (an UNBUILT atom could be claimed proven), so it could exceed 100%. (4) The denominator was a DOCUMENTED error -- R311jl already ruled the wz-catalog denominator invalid for parity claims -- and 25 of the 185 built atoms are foreign-NON-observable by construction (platform/runtime substrate, caches, seams, cargo aliases, switchboard), so an unproven list built on it could never reach zero, and a gate nobody can close is a gate everyone ignores. (5) A boolean per atom prints claims the corpus FORBIDS IN WRITING (wz_priority_to_pico_zsub.rs:30: "Do not read this single test as a full 'qos cross-impl proven' claim") -- the real unit is (atom x carrier x direction x peer), so the axis records direction, and `partial` is never folded into proven. The result: 68 corpus files / 133 tests, every test declaring; proven=50 partial=16 unproven=94 against a NAMED denominator of 160. NO percentage is printed, deliberately -- a single number against an unnamed denominator is the error this axis exists to stop, and it would invite comparison with the legacy ~75%, which is a zenoh-pico-parity figure with a different denominator. The gate immediately earned itself: containment REFUTED two live over-claims (transport-qos, on tests where it is not even compiled), and the A4-6 contradiction gate fired on `switchboard`, upheld on arbitration. The exclusion set is falsifiable BY DESIGN: witness one of the 25, and A4 fails and the exclusion was wrong.
