KEY CORRECTION for whoever picks the backlog up: "pico does not implement mechanism X" does NOT mean "pico cannot witness X". The canonical proof of routing-routes (which pico has no analog of) is pico-publisher -> wz-router -> pico-subscriber; pico plays both ends. Same for the access-* interceptors (pico is the traffic source whose Put gets dropped), adminspace-read/-write (pico is a fully capable z_get querier), storage-backend (pico z_put then z_get sees the replay), and time-hlc (a pico subscriber can observe strictly-increasing stamps within one millisecond vs ties). Genuinely zenohd-only = a second ROUTER or a link pico cannot speak: router-hat-router, routing-router, routing-token-tables, router-multicast-faces, scouting-gossip/-autoconnect, storage-aligner/-replication, rest-*, session-ext{auth,compression,shm}, transport-{shm,compression,lowlatency,multilink}, transport-link-{quic,unixsock,vsock,unixpipe}.

Round 311y26.decision_summary: R311y26 -- FreeRTOS integration Round 2: crates/wz-runtime-freertos, the cooperative single-task PROFILE. Does NOT reimplement the executor or impl Runtime -- FreertosRuntime is a type alias for CoopRuntime<FreertosClock> (the audited wz-runtime-coop executor SSOT -- task pool/waker/timer queue -- reused verbatim, parameterised by the clock). Supplies ONLY the FreeRTOS seams: FreertosClock<TICK_HZ> (ClockSource over xTaskGetTickCount, const-generic over configTICK_RATE_HZ, mirrors SystickClock<CYCLES_PER_US>) + FreertosAllocator (GlobalAlloc over heap_4 pvPortMalloc/vPortFree, over-align-safe; deploy declares #[global_allocator]). Sync needs nothing (CoopRuntime uses critical_section; deploy supplies impl); net reuses NO_SYS lwip. Per the R311y25 lesson the CI lane (Layer G G.15, thumbv7m + WZ_FREERTOS_CONFIG) lands THIS round. Verified: cross-compile thumbv7m EXIT=0 + Layer G pass (G.14 + G.15 OK) + clippy(deny) + fmt + validate orphan new=+0. NEXT Round 3: boot + deploy/mcu-freertos-demo + QEMU mps2 e2e.

FreertosRuntime<const TICK_HZ: u32> = type alias for CoopRuntime<FreertosClock<TICK_HZ>> — the executor is NOT reimplemented; the audited wz-runtime-coop task pool / waker / cancel / timer queue (the SSOT) is reused verbatim, parameterised only by the clock seam. = zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=0 ST mode (one task hosts run_until_idle).

FreertosClock<const TICK_HZ: u32>: impl wz_runtime_coop::ClockSource; now_us() = xTaskGetTickCount() as u64 * 1_000_000 / TICK_HZ (multiply-before-divide = exact for any tick rate; ticks*1e6 < 2^52 so no u64 overflow). Const-generic over configTICK_RATE_HZ — mirrors the bare-metal wz_mcu_clock::SystickClock<CYCLES_PER_US> const-generic timebase shape. ZST + Copy.

FreertosAllocator: unsafe impl GlobalAlloc over freertos-sys pvPortMalloc/vPortFree (heap_4). Direct for align<=8 (heap_4's portBYTE_ALIGNMENT on ARMv7-M); over-aligned requests over-allocate (size+align+usize), align up, and stash the heap_4 base pointer in the usize slot below the returned address so dealloc recovers it. Lives in the profile crate (not the deploy) because the FreeRTOS heap IS the kernel's — unlike the bare-metal profile's free embedded_alloc choice; the deploy declares #[global_allocator] static = FreertosAllocator.

Seams NOT needed here: sync (CoopRuntime already uses critical_section::Mutex; the deploy supplies the critical-section impl), net (reuses NO_SYS=1 lwip via wz-link-lwip, no FreeRTOS sys_arch — the executor polls lwIP single-threaded).

Round 311y260.decision_summary: R311y260 -- close the ENCODING cluster of the y259 unproven backlog by proving the WHOLE 53-entry encoding table against real zenoh-pico on a socket, not one entry of it. Picked from the 94-atom list by the rule y259 established: a proof that hosted CI actually RUNS is worth more than one it does not, and a pico-CLI witness lands in Layer E (every push) whereas a zenohd witness lands in Layer Z (which hosted CI never even builds). R311y207 had proved exactly ONE encoding id (text/plain = 4), which established that the encoding field crosses the wire at all but left the TABLE unproven -- 52 further ids, each an independent chance for wz and zenoh-pico to disagree about what a number MEANS. That failure mode is silent and nasty: the payload arrives intact and is labelled the wrong media type, so an application/cbor sample surfaces as application/cdr in the foreign consumer. The new test publishes one Put per id 0..=52 and pairs pico's two consecutive output lines (`Received ('demo/enc': 'enc-<id>')` then `with encoding: <mime>`, z_sub_attachment.c:59,61) to correlate each id to the MIME zenoh-pico's OWN table resolved for it, then checks every one against wz's `mime_for_id`. Pairing rather than set-comparison is deliberate: asserting only that the SET of printed MIMEs equals wz's 53 would pass a table PERMUTATION. wz's table is the expected-value SSOT -- the test never restates it, so it cannot drift from the implementation it checks. Result: all 53 agree; wz and zenoh-pico share one encoding table, proven on a real socket. Grading is deliberately NOT uniform: the 52 non-default ids are DISCRIMINATING (a dropped encoding field would make pico print the default zenoh/bytes instead of the expected MIME), but id 0 (`encoding-empty`) is not -- pico prints zenoh/bytes both when wz sends id 0 explicitly and when the field is absent -- so encoding-empty is claimed `partial` with that stated in the header, even though wz demonstrably does put id 0 on the wire (push_build.rs::gated_encoding_field special-cases nothing). `pubsub-encoding wz->pico` also stays `partial`: the SCHEMA sub-field (id << 1 | 1, then schema bytes) is exercised only pico->wz, by pico_pub_attachment_to_wz_sub, and this test does not close it. An adversarial post-build review then forced the grading tighter twice, and both corrections are the point of the round rather than a footnote. FIRST: the five per-family atoms (encoding-utf8/-json/-cbor/-protobuf/-bytes) are DEFINED in the inventory as their `EncodingHint::<NAME>` const, and the sweep had been building `id << 1` by hand -- so re-pointing `ID_APPLICATION_JSON` from 5 to 6 would have left the test PASSING while every caller of `EncodingHint::APPLICATION_JSON` silently mislabelled its payload as `text/json`, and Layer A4 kept reporting the atom foreign-proven. A claim has to bind to the code the atom IS, so the sweep now publishes the named constants themselves against the MIME each one promises. SECOND: `encoding-mime` was graded full, but that atom is the whole MIME subsystem -- `mime_for_id` AND `id_for_mime` AND the `"mime;schema"` parse (`encoding_from_mime` / `encoding_to_mime`) AND the ID_CUSTOM 0xFFFF fallback -- of which this test witnesses exactly one half of one function; it is downgraded to `partial`, on the same reasoning the file already used to keep `pubsub-encoding` partial. Also hardened: `observed_pairs` now drops a torn trailing line and the mismatch branch re-reads once before declaring a divergence, because that branch was FATAL while `missing` merely retried -- an asymmetry that could have surfaced a transient short read as the alarming "wz and zenoh-pico DISAGREE on the encoding table". Picked from the 94-atom list by the rule y259 established: a proof that hosted CI actually RUNS is worth more than one it does not, and a pico-CLI witness lands in Layer E (every push) whereas a zenohd witness lands in Layer Z (which hosted CI never even builds). R311y207 had proved exactly ONE encoding id (text/plain = 4), which established that the encoding field crosses the wire at all but left the TABLE unproven -- 52 further ids, each an independent chance for wz and zenoh-pico to disagree about what a number MEANS. That failure mode is silent and nasty: the payload arrives intact and is labelled the wrong media type, so an application/cbor sample surfaces as application/cdr in the foreign consumer. The new test publishes one Put per id 0..=52 and pairs pico's two consecutive output lines (`Received ('demo/enc': 'enc-<id>')` then `with encoding: <mime>`, z_sub_attachment.c:59,61) to correlate each id to the MIME zenoh-pico's OWN table resolved for it, then checks every one against wz's `mime_for_id`. Pairing rather than set-comparison is deliberate: asserting only that the SET of printed MIMEs equals wz's 53 would pass a table PERMUTATION. wz's table is the expected-value SSOT -- the test never restates it, so it cannot drift from the implementation it checks. Result: all 53 agree; wz and zenoh-pico share one encoding table, proven on a real socket. Grading is deliberately NOT uniform: the 52 non-default ids are DISCRIMINATING (a dropped encoding field would make pico print the default zenoh/bytes instead of the expected MIME), but id 0 (`encoding-empty`) is not -- pico prints zenoh/bytes both when wz sends id 0 explicitly and when the field is absent -- so encoding-empty is claimed `partial` with that stated in the header, even though wz demonstrably does put id 0 on the wire (push_build.rs::gated_encoding_field special-cases nothing). `pubsub-encoding wz->pico` also stays `partial`: the SCHEMA sub-field (id << 1 | 1, then schema bytes) is exercised only pico->wz, by pico_pub_attachment_to_wz_sub, and this test does not close it. An adversarial post-build review then forced the grading tighter twice, and both corrections are the point of the round rather than a footnote. FIRST: the five per-family atoms (encoding-utf8/-json/-cbor/-protobuf/-bytes) are DEFINED in the inventory as their `EncodingHint::<NAME>` const, and the sweep had been building `id << 1` by hand -- so re-pointing `ID_APPLICATION_JSON` from 5 to 6 would have left the test PASSING while every caller of `EncodingHint::APPLICATION_JSON` silently mislabelled its payload as `text/json`, and Layer A4 kept reporting the atom foreign-proven. A claim has to bind to the code the atom IS, so the sweep now publishes the named constants themselves against the MIME each one promises. SECOND: `encoding-mime` was graded full, but that atom is the whole MIME subsystem -- `mime_for_id` AND `id_for_mime` AND the `"mime;schema"` parse (`encoding_from_mime` / `encoding_to_mime`) AND the ID_CUSTOM 0xFFFF fallback -- of which this test witnesses exactly one half of one function; it is downgraded to `partial`, on the same reasoning the file already used to keep `pubsub-encoding` partial. Also hardened: `observed_pairs` now drops a torn trailing line and the mismatch branch re-reads once before declaring a divergence, because that branch was FATAL while `missing` merely retried -- an asymmetry that could have surfaced a transient short read as the alarming "wz and zenoh-pico DISAGREE on the encoding table". Round 311y261.decision_summary: R311y261 -- close the QUERY-KNOB cluster of the A4 backlog, and do it in the STRONGEST execution class available. The y260 selection rule says pick the next cluster by whether hosted CI would actually RUN the witness; this round pushes that rule one notch further. A pico-CLI proof lands in Layer E, which hosted CI runs but only via --ignored; a CODEC-PARITY proof links the real vendored zenoh-pico C encoder in-process and runs in Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace) with NO #[ignore] at all -- on every push, unconditionally, with no external binary to provision. So the six query knobs, all of which are codec surface, were proven that way rather than through a CLI. Diagnosis first, per the rule that direct read is the arbiter: zenoh-pico DOES decode the Request exts (_ext_target / _ext_budget / _ext_timeout_ms, network.h:139-141) and the Query body fields (_consolidation / _parameters / _ext_attachment, message.h:104-111) and it DOES have the Response ERR arm (_Z_RESPONSE_BODY_ERR) -- but it exposes NO public getter for target/timeout on z_loaned_query_t, so a stock z_queryable CANNOT print them and the CLI route would have needed an invasive example patch to witness what the C encoder can byte-compare directly. wz's side is the production path, not a test-only shim: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/querier.rs drives the same RequestQueryBuilder these tests exercise. What the round proves: wz's REQUEST-level target ext and timeout ext, the QUERY-body consolidation (Q_C flag + mode byte), selector parameters (Q_P flag + length-prefixed slice) and attachment ext, and the RESPONSE(Err) arm, are each byte-identical to what zenoh-pico's own C encoder emits for the same value. Each test carries an ANTI-VACUITY guard asserting the knob-bearing encoding differs from the bare default envelope -- without it, a wz that silently DROPPED a knob and a pico whose sentinel logic emitted nothing would agree by both encoding the same 4 bytes, and the compare would pass proving nothing. The err arm matters disproportionately: every prior Layer 3 response compare drives the REPLY arm, so wz's ERROR path -- the one a queryable takes when it cannot answer -- was structurally unproven against zenoh-pico, and a disagreement there is worst-case invisible (the happy path interoperates; only failures mis-decode). An adversarial post-build review then downgraded ALL SIX claims from full to PARTIAL, and that downgrade is the honest result rather than a footnote. The tests are ENCODE-ONLY byte differentials, and -- except query-attachment -- they never compile the code the atom is DEFINED as: `query-target`'s cfg sites are in querier.rs (QueryOptions::with_target), while RequestQueryBuilder::request_target is UNGATED, so turning the query-target feature OFF leaves the test compiling and passing while still claiming the atom foreign-proven. A4's containment arm cannot catch this (the feature IS in the closure); only reading the test can. The same class the y260 EncodingHint over-claim fell into, and the sibling `query-value` -- same file, same shape, with STRICTLY MORE evidence (a codec-parity byte test AND a live pico-queryable test) -- is itself graded partial, which settles it. The atoms' own definitions confirm the grade: query-selector-parameters is `F=selector param PARSE` (a DECODE-side concern an encode test cannot reach); query-consolidation is `C=indep reply dedup` and query-target `C=indep query routing knob` -- neither of which a byte comparison exercises. The review also forced three real FIXES: (a) the magic enum literals (1 / 2 / _tag = 1) were hand-transcribed copies of pico's constants, so an upstream renumbering would have degraded the differential from "wz vs pico" to "wz vs my copy of pico" -- they now import the bindgen consts; (b) NOTHING pinned the knob-LESS builder against pico's default, so a builder that spuriously emitted a sentinel-valued ext would have broken a real pico queryable with zero test failures -- a converse test now closes it; (c) the err test drove `build_response_err_empty`, a shape PRODUCTION NEVER EMITS -- the real reply_err path requires a literal keyexpr (mapping_id=0 panics without a suffix) and always stamps an encoding, so a second test now byte-compares that N-flag + E-flag shape, which is the branch that actually crosses the wire. Net Layer A4 movement: the six atoms go UNPROVEN -> PARTIAL, not -> proven. All-lanes unproven 87 -> 81 and hosted-CI-executed unproven 108 -> 102; `proven` correctly does NOT move, because encode-side byte parity is not full cross-impl proof of a behavioural knob.

One shared `PicoQueryKnobs` patch-set + one audited unsafe helper instead of five near-duplicate blocks.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_response.rs: +1 codec-parity differential for the RESPONSE(Err) arm (`_tag = _Z_RESPONSE_BODY_ERR`), across empty / short / long payloads. Every prior compare in that file drives the REPLY arm; the err arm had never met a foreign encoder.

A pico-CLI proof lands in Layer E, which hosted CI runs but only via --ignored; a CODEC-PARITY proof links the real vendored zenoh-pico C encoder in-process and runs in Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace) with NO #[ignore] at all -- on every push, unconditionally, with no external binary to provision. So the six query knobs, all of which are codec surface, were proven that way rather than through a CLI. Diagnosis first, per the rule that direct read is the arbiter: zenoh-pico DOES decode the Request exts (_ext_target / _ext_budget / _ext_timeout_ms, network.h:139-141) and the Query body fields (_consolidation / _parameters / _ext_attachment, message.h:104-111) and it DOES have the Response ERR arm (_Z_RESPONSE_BODY_ERR) -- but it exposes NO public getter for target/timeout on z_loaned_query_t, so a stock z_queryable CANNOT print them and the CLI route would have needed an invasive example patch to witness what the C encoder can byte-compare directly. wz's side is the production path, not a test-only shim: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/querier.rs drives the same RequestQueryBuilder these tests exercise. What the round proves: wz's REQUEST-level target ext and timeout ext, the QUERY-body consolidation (Q_C flag + mode byte), selector parameters (Q_P flag + length-prefixed slice) and attachment ext, and the RESPONSE(Err) arm, are each byte-identical to what zenoh-pico's own C encoder emits for the same value. Each test carries an ANTI-VACUITY guard asserting the knob-bearing encoding differs from the bare default envelope -- without it, a wz that silently DROPPED a knob and a pico whose sentinel logic emitted nothing would agree by both encoding the same 4 bytes, and the compare would pass proving nothing. The err arm matters disproportionately: every prior Layer 3 response compare drives the REPLY arm, so wz's ERROR path -- the one a queryable takes when it cannot answer -- was structurally unproven against zenoh-pico, and a disagreement there is worst-case invisible (the happy path interoperates; only failures mis-decode). An adversarial post-build review then downgraded ALL SIX claims from full to PARTIAL, and that downgrade is the honest result rather than a footnote. The tests are ENCODE-ONLY byte differentials, and -- except query-attachment -- they never compile the code the atom is DEFINED as: `query-target`'s cfg sites are in querier.rs (QueryOptions::with_target), while RequestQueryBuilder::request_target is UNGATED, so turning the query-target feature OFF leaves the test compiling and passing while still claiming the atom foreign-proven. A4's containment arm cannot catch this (the feature IS in the closure); only reading the test can. The same class the y260 EncodingHint over-claim fell into, and the sibling `query-value` -- same file, same shape, with STRICTLY MORE evidence (a codec-parity byte test AND a live pico-queryable test) -- is itself graded partial, which settles it. The atoms' own definitions confirm the grade: query-selector-parameters is `F=selector param PARSE` (a DECODE-side concern an encode test cannot reach); query-consolidation is `C=indep reply dedup` and query-target `C=indep query routing knob` -- neither of which a byte comparison exercises. The review also forced three real FIXES: (a) the magic enum literals (1 / 2 / _tag = 1) were hand-transcribed copies of pico's constants, so an upstream renumbering would have degraded the differential from "wz vs pico" to "wz vs my copy of pico" -- they now import the bindgen consts; (b) NOTHING pinned the knob-LESS builder against pico's default, so a builder that spuriously emitted a sentinel-valued ext would have broken a real pico queryable with zero test failures -- a converse test now closes it; (c) the err test drove `build_response_err_empty`, a shape PRODUCTION NEVER EMITS -- the real reply_err path requires a literal keyexpr (mapping_id=0 panics without a suffix) and always stamps an encoding, so a second test now byte-compares that N-flag + E-flag shape, which is the branch that actually crosses the wire. Net Layer A4 movement: the six atoms go UNPROVEN -> PARTIAL, not -> proven. All-lanes unproven 87 -> 81 and hosted-CI-executed unproven 108 -> 102; `proven` correctly does NOT move, because encode-side byte parity is not full cross-impl proof of a behavioural knob.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_request.rs: +5 codec-parity differentials against zenoh-pico's real `_z_request_encode` -- request target ext (QueryTarget::All + AllComplete), request timeout ext (1 / 5000 / 2^32 ms, spanning the VLE width boundaries), Query-body consolidation (None / Monotonic / Latest -- AUTO is pico's sentinel and emits nothing, so those three are the discriminating set), Query-body selector parameters (short + a `_time=[..]`-bearing selector), and the Query-body attachment ext. One shared `PicoQueryKnobs` patch-set + one audited unsafe helper instead of five near-duplicate blocks.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_response.rs: +1 codec-parity differential for the RESPONSE(Err) arm (`_tag = _Z_RESPONSE_BODY_ERR`), across empty / short / long payloads. Every prior compare in that file drives the REPLY arm; the err arm had never met a foreign encoder.
Each of the 6 tests carries an anti-vacuity assertion (`assert_ne!(pico, <bare default>)`) so that neither side can "agree" by emitting nothing for the knob under test.
No production code changed -- this round adds PROOF, not behaviour.

Post-build review corrections, all tightening: ALL SIX claims downgraded full -> partial (encode-only differentials that, except query-attachment, never compile the atom's own cfg-gated code -- the same over-claim class as y260's EncodingHint consts; the sibling query-value carries strictly more evidence and is itself partial). The hand-transcribed pico enum literals (1 / 2 / 0,1,2 / _tag = 1) replaced with the bindgen consts (z_query_target_t_Z_QUERY_TARGET_ALL etc.) so an upstream renumbering cannot silently degrade the differential into "wz vs my copy of pico". New `layer3_response_err_with_encoding_byte_equivalent`: the err shape PRODUCTION actually emits -- literal keyexpr (N flag; ResponseErrBuilder panics on mapping_id=0 without a suffix) + E-flag encoding -- because the original err test drove `build_response_err_empty`, a shape the production reply_err path never sends. query-attachment extended to 1 / 22 / 32 (QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN) bytes so the ext's length prefix is exercised at its boundary. Doc-comment ext ids corrected (target 0x04, timeout 0x06 -- 0x05 is BUDGET; the original said 0x05/0x07) and a SAFETY-comment typo fixed.

Anti-vacuity holds: every knob's pico encoding is asserted DIFFERENT from the bare default envelope, so a both-sides-emit-nothing pass is impossible.
Production-path bound, not a test-only shim: wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/querier.rs drives the same `RequestQueryBuilder` these tests exercise.

THE RESIDUAL THAT KEEPS THEM PARTIAL, and the next round's work if the cluster is to close: these atoms' cfg-gated code lives in querier.rs (QueryOptions::with_target / with_timeout_ms / with_consolidation) and query.rs (selector-param PARSE, reply_err), NOT in the ungated RequestQueryBuilder the byte tests drive -- so a live wz<->pico leg through Session::get / QueryResponder::reply_err is what would earn a full grade. Also still open: the err response's `responder` envelope ext.
SELECTION RULE, sharpened (this is the reusable part): rank the remaining clusters by EXECUTION STRENGTH, not just by "does hosted CI run it".
1. codec-parity (layer3_*): links pico's C encoder in-process, NOT #[ignore]d -> Layer C1, every push, no external binary. STRONGEST.
2. pico CLI (Layer E): hosted CI runs it, but via --ignored and it needs the pico CLI provisioned.
3. zenohd (Layer Z): hosted CI never builds zenohd -> local-only, raises the all-lanes number but NOT the number that gates merges.

Prefer (1) whenever the atom is codec surface. It was the right call here even though the pico CLI route looked more "end-to-end": zenoh-pico decodes the request exts but exposes NO public getter for target/timeout on z_loaned_query_t, so a stock z_queryable cannot print them and the CLI route would have needed an invasive example patch to witness what the C encoder byte-compares directly.

NEXT CLUSTERS, in that order: keyexpr-includes + keyexpr-mapping (codec-parity: pico has `_z_keyexpr_includes` and the resource/alias table -> class 1) · ext-pubsub advanced (7 atoms; pico HAS Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION/SUBSCRIPTION, and the `@adv` keyexpr prefix is on the wire) · adminspace (8; pico HAS Z_FEATURE_ADMIN_SPACE + src/api/admin_space.c, so a pico z_get can witness wz's adminspace -- long mis-scoped as zenohd-only) · the locator family · scouting.

RESIDUAL named, not closed: the request BUDGET ext (`_ext_budget`) is encodable by wz (`RequestQueryBuilder::request_budget`) and decoded by pico, but no catalog atom names it -- the same shape as the OAM / ext-TLV envelope gap y259 surfaced. If an atom is ever added, the differential is a 10-line addition to the same PicoQueryKnobs helper.

LESSON (second consecutive round it has bitten, now doubly memorised): a codec-parity byte differential proves the WIRE, not the ATOM. Before grading such a claim full, grep the atom's `#[cfg(feature = "<atom>")]` sites and check the test actually compiles them. Five of six knob atoms here gate their code in querier.rs while the builder the test drives is ungated -- so the feature could be turned OFF and the test would still pass, still claiming the atom proven. A4's containment arm structurally cannot see this (the feature IS in the closure). Only a reader can. [[feedback_claim_binds_to_atom_code]].

Round 311y262.decision_summary: R311y262 -- close keyexpr-includes and keyexpr-mapping, and pick them by the rule y261's failure taught: check FIRST that the test will compile the code the atom is DEFINED as. y261 downgraded six query atoms because their codec-parity byte differentials never crossed the atoms' own cfg gates (the gates live in querier.rs; the builder the tests drove is ungated), so this round front-loaded that check: keyexpr-includes is ACTIVE and its entry point `keyexpr_includes_patterns` is ITSELF `#[cfg(feature = "keyexpr-includes")]` (keyexpr_match.rs:567) -- turn the feature off and the differential does not compile, let alone pass. The claim binds. WHY THE ATOM NEEDED ITS OWN WITNESS, and why the sibling intersects differential was not enough: INCLUDES IS DIRECTIONAL WHERE INTERSECTS IS SYMMETRIC. `a ∩ b` asks whether some key matches both; `a ⊇ b` asks whether EVERY key b matches is also matched by a. An implementation can agree with zenoh-pico on every intersects answer and still get the subsumption backwards -- `*` and `**` intersect in both directions, but `**` includes `*` while `*` does NOT include `**`. Nothing in the repo had ever checked that asymmetry against a foreign implementation, and the corpus here contains the pairs where includes and intersects genuinely disagree, so an includes-aliased-to-intersects wz FAILS (3 of the 5 tests, first at the pair ("a","*")). The witness is zenoh-pico's real `_z_keyexpr_forward_includes`, the worker `_z_keyexpr_includes` dispatches into -- emitted by the SAME macro-template instantiation that produces the intersects worker the sibling test already uses (keyexpr.c:565-568), so it is exposed the same way (a hand-written forward decl in the sys wrapper header + one allowlist line) and it runs in Layer C1 on every push, unconditionally, with no external binary to provision. keyexpr-mapping was not a new test at all but an UNDER-CLAIM: pico's z_put calls z_declare_keyexpr and then Pushes by mapping id with NO suffix on the wire, so wz's alias table MUST resolve it or `SUBSCRIBER FIRED` is unreachable (a table miss returns None and the dispatch is dropped silently) -- ap_demo_round_trip has been witnessing wz's resolver against a FOREIGN-declared mapping all along, and wz_publisher_aliased_to_zsub the reverse, and neither said so. Under-claiming makes the unproven list wrong in the same way over-claiming makes the proven list wrong. An adversarial review then caught three real defects, all fixed: the algebra test was NOT a differential (it checked wz=>wz and pico=>pico independently and never compared the two -- a wz returning `false` unconditionally passed it, and its doc-comment asserted the opposite); the `$*` corpus never reached the ordered sub-part walk, which is exactly where includes and intersects diverge (a bare `a$*` short-circuits on both sides); and one input, a lone `$*` chunk, is NON-CANONICAL -- both canonizers rewrite it to `*`, so it sits outside both matchers' stated "assume canonized chunks" precondition and no production path can emit it. Layer A4: unproven 81 -> 79, partial 27 -> 29 (hosted-CI-executed unproven 102 -> 100). Both atoms are `partial`, honestly: the corpus is a bounded alphabet with no @-verbatim chunks, and the mapping claims witness the alias table's PRESENCE, not its content.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_keyexpr_includes.rs (NEW): 5 cross-impl differentials against zenoh-pico's real `_z_keyexpr_forward_includes` C matcher, linked in-process -- literal pairs, single-chunk wildcard, the `**` ASYMMETRY (the case an intersects-only differential structurally cannot catch), the `$*` DSL including the ordered sub-part walk, and the algebra (inclusion implies intersection) checked in both implementations AND cross-compared between them. Every pair is asserted in BOTH directions, because inclusion is directional.

crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h + build.rs: expose `_z_keyexpr_forward_includes` to bindgen. It has no public header declaration -- it is emitted by the `keyexpr_match_template.h` macro instantiated twice in session/keyexpr.c (once per relation), exactly like the `_z_keyexpr_forward_intersects` worker the sibling test already consumes -- so it gets the same treatment: a hand-written forward decl in the wrapper + one allowlist line. Signature verified byte-exact against the template.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/ap_demo_round_trip.rs + wz_publisher_aliased_to_zsub.rs: +`keyexpr-mapping <dir> partial` on the two tests that were ALREADY witnessing the alias table without claiming it. pico's z_put declares a keyexpr and then Pushes by mapping id with no suffix, so wz's resolver is strictly required for the subscriber to fire; the reverse test has pico resolve wz's mapping id back to the literal it prints.

crates/wz-integration-tests/Cargo.toml: pin `keyexpr-includes` explicitly on the wz-session-core dev-dep. It was riding the crate's default list, so a default-list edit could have silently un-compiled the atom's gated code out from under the differential.

Post-review fixes: the algebra test now runs `assert_includes_agree` on every pair (it was two independent self-consistency checks, not a differential, and its doc said otherwise); the `$*` corpus gained `a$*c` vs `a$*b$*c` and friends so it reaches `_z_chunk_right_contains_all_stardsl_subchunks_of_left`, where INTERSECTS short-circuits and INCLUDES must walk the sub-parts in order; the non-canonical lone-`$*` input was dropped; and the wz->pico mapping claim now discloses that it witnesses the table's presence, not its content.
No production code changed -- this round adds PROOF, not behaviour.
verification_bullets: layer3_keyexpr_includes 5/5 pass against the REAL vendored zenoh-pico C matcher; the whole non-#[ignore]d suite is 95 passed / 0 failed (the sys-crate FFI change is a superset -- no regression in the 25 sibling layer3 differentials).

LOAD-BEARING, verified rather than asserted: the corpus contains pairs where includes and intersects genuinely disagree (`*` vs `**`, `a` vs `**`, `a` vs `*`), so a wz that aliased includes to intersects fails 3 of the 5 tests. The differential cannot pass vacuously.

BINDS TO THE ATOM (the y261 check, run FIRST this time): `keyexpr_includes_patterns` is `#[cfg(feature = "keyexpr-includes")]`, so the feature being off breaks the BUILD -- the test cannot pass while leaving the atom's code uncompiled. The feature is now pinned explicitly in the test crate's dev-dep rather than inherited from a default list.

FFI signature verified byte-exact against `keyexpr_match_template.h`'s `_ZP_CAT(_z_keyexpr_forward, includes)` expansion (same arity/order/types, external linkage, `<stdbool.h>` in scope) -- a wrong signature here would be UB, not a test failure.

Layer A4: all lanes partial 27 -> 29, unproven 81 -> 79. EXECUTED BY HOSTED CI: partial 32 -> 34, unproven 102 -> 100. `proven` unchanged -- both atoms are honestly partial (bounded alphabet, no @-verbatim chunks; the mapping claims witness the table's presence, not its content).

carry_forward_bullets: R311y262 = keyexpr-includes + keyexpr-mapping leave the unproven list (81 -> 79; hosted-CI-executed 102 -> 100). Both land as `partial`.

THE RULE THAT MADE THIS ROUND CLEAN, and it is now front-loaded rather than learned in review: before picking a cluster, check that the test will COMPILE THE ATOM'S OWN cfg-gated code. keyexpr-includes passes that check by construction (its entry point IS the cfg-gated fn); the y261 query knobs did not (their gates live in querier.rs while the builder under test is ungated), which is why six claims had to be downgraded there and none here. [[feedback_claim_binds_to_atom_code]].

UNDER-CLAIMING IS A DEFECT TOO, and this round found one sitting in the tree: keyexpr-mapping had ZERO claims while two existing tests were already witnessing it (pico's z_put declares a keyexpr then Pushes by mapping id with no suffix -- wz's alias table is strictly required for the subscriber to fire). An unproven list that lists an atom nothing has ever failed to prove is as wrong as a proven list that lists one nothing proved. Worth a sweep: re-read the corpus for atoms already witnessed but unclaimed.

RESIDUALS named, not claimed: the includes corpus has no `@`-verbatim chunks (so pico's `_z_keyexpr_parts_includes` and the `can_have_verbatim` backward branch never run) and no multi-`**` patterns (so `_z_keyexpr_special_includes` never runs); the mapping claims witness the alias table's PRESENCE, not its CONTENT (a table resolving 7 -> "wrong/key" would surface as a keyexpr mismatch on pico's side, but nothing asserts the table directly).

NEXT CLUSTERS, by execution strength: ext-pubsub advanced (7 atoms; pico HAS Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION/SUBSCRIPTION and the `@adv` keyexpr prefix is on the wire -- check the cfg-gate binding FIRST) · adminspace (8; pico HAS Z_FEATURE_ADMIN_SPACE + src/api/admin_space.c, so a pico z_get can witness wz's adminspace -- long mis-scoped as zenohd-only) · the locator family · scouting · session-reconnect / -matching / transport-keepalive / -batching.

Round 311y263.decision_summary: R311y263 -- an UNDER-CLAIM sweep of the corpus, and the cross-impl divergence it turned up. Two premises drove the round. FIRST: under-claiming is a defect of the same kind as over-claiming. y262 found keyexpr-mapping sitting at ZERO claims while two tests had been witnessing it all along, and an unproven list that names an atom nothing has ever failed to prove is exactly as wrong as a proven list that names one nothing proved. So the corpus was swept against the 79-atom unproven list under the same bar the claims themselves are held to (foreign participation / DISCRIMINATING witness / crosses the atom's own cfg gate). The sweep's REJECT list is the more valuable half and is recorded here, because it stops twelve future over-claims: time-system-clock (the timestamp test HAND-SETS the value, so wall_clock_ntp64 is never called), ext-pubsub-serde-codec (the attachment tests agree with pico's ze_serializer ON THE WIRE but wz's serialize_kv_attachment is built on crate::vle and never touches serde_codec -- the exact trap that cost y261 six downgrades), transport-keepalive ("the session stayed up" is not discriminating -- nothing asserts a KeepAlive), transport-batching (zero corpus tests call batch_start/batch_end), session-reconnect (no corpus test re-dials against a foreign peer), session-matching (the only matching listener in the corpus is PICO's, not wz's), liveliness-get (its only caller is a wz<->wz test, which A4-3 forbids from claiming), liveliness-history (no corpus binary passes history=true, so the per-call gate is never crossed), scouting-active/-static/-multicast, and locator-tcp/-udp (a locator string is a LOCAL config artifact each side parses with its own parser -- nothing forces the two grammars to agree). Only two atoms were genuinely under-claimed: attachment-bytes (the attachment CODEC -- encode_attachment_ext / serialize_kv_attachment -- is a DISJOINT code body from pubsub-attachment, which gates the field plumbing; both attachment tests IMPORT the gated module and cannot compile without it) and time-ntp64. SECOND: the sweep named a cheap gap in the strongest lane -- every Push/MsgPut differential drove the DEFAULT no-flag shape, so the body-level timestamp and attachment slots had a live wire witness but NO byte-compare against pico's own C encoder. That is now closed against the PRODUCTION builder (build_push_literal_with_meta, the SSOT Session::publish routes through), and it passes byte-for-byte. AND THEN THE REAL FIND. Chasing time-ntp64 to a FULL grade meant proving the other half of the atom -- the word's CONSTRUCTION, `(seconds, nanos) -> secs << 32 | frac`, which a byte-compare of an already-composed word structurally cannot reach -- so a differential was written against zenoh-pico's own composer. IT FAILED, and it was right to: zenoh-pico's `_z_timestamp_ntp64_from_time` (protocol/core.c:66-72) adds `+ 1` to the fraction, which zenoh's own reference does NOT (uhlc-0.8.1/src/ntp64.rs:287-293). wz mirrors uhlc exactly, so wz agrees with zenoh and ZENOH-PICO IS THE OUTLIER: for the same instant a pico stamp sits one NTP64 tick (2^-32 s, ~233 ps) above a wz/zenoh stamp -- including at (0s, 0ns), where zenoh says 0 and pico says 1. The divergence is UNIVERSAL (verified pico == wz + 1 across all 40 (secs, nanos) probes) and wz is pinned to uhlc's formula, recomputed in the test so it binds to the REFERENCE rather than to itself. wz is NOT bent to match: its reference is zenoh, and matching one pico off-by-one would put it out of step with every zenoh peer. The test therefore PINS the anomaly and claims NO atom -- a locked disagreement is the opposite of an interop proof, the same treatment the corpus already gives the known pico canon anomalies -- and time-ntp64 stays `partial` on the wire claim with the composer divergence named as its residual. The codec agreeing does not make the atom whole. Layer A4: unproven 79 -> 77, proven 52 -> 53, partial 29 -> 30 (hosted-CI-executed unproven 100 -> 98).

Round 311y264.decision_summary: R311y264 -- wire the cross-impl proof lanes into hosted CI, and make the number that gates merges converge on the true one. This closes the honesty debt R311y259 named on the day the axis was built. Layer A4 reports the proof axis as TWO populations because a proof that never runs is not a proof: 64 of the corpus's tests are #[ignore]d, and the lanes that execute them -- E2 / E6 / E8 / Z -- were simply not in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The zenohd tier in particular, the ONLY proofs against the canonical Rust implementation, ran on exactly one developer's machine at pre-push. A derived number resting on evidence hosted CI never executes carries MORE false authority than the hand estimate the axis replaced, which is why A4 has always refused to fuse the two counts -- but refusing to fuse them is disclosure, not a fix. This is the fix. A new `interop` JOB (separate from `ci`, so a from-source external build cannot eat the primary job's 30-minute budget) provisions the pico CLIs + zenohd and runs E2 (the six subset binaries, whose pinned atom lists make their proofs tightly bounded) + E6 (peer mesh, 3 pico legs) + E6b + E8 (router-hat vs a real pico subscriber) + Z (zenohd). THE PLUGIN DETAIL IS THE POINT, not a footnote: a hosted runner has no cargo-git checkout, so build-zenohd.sh would have fallen to its crates.io path -- and `cargo install` yields the router BINARY but NOT the storage-manager cdylib, so Layer Z's storage-replication leg would have SKIPped. A SKIP is green. The lane would have "run in CI" while one of its proofs quietly did not execute, manufacturing exactly the false authority this axis exists to destroy. So the script gained a source path (a shallow clone of the pinned tag, opt-in via ZENOHD_ALLOW_CLONE so a developer's machine keeps preferring the checkout it already has), because only a source tree produces the plugin. The clone was verified end to end before wiring: the 1.5.0 tag exists, the tree carries zenohd/Cargo.toml and plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager, and the script's existing version assert reads 1.5.0 off the clone's workspace root. Layer A4's execution model was generalized in the same round, and that matters as much as the yml: it had hardcoded "only Layer E runs ignored tests", so wiring lanes would have moved reality without moving the number. It now DERIVES lane -> test-target from run-ci.sh's `run_layer` registrations and the hosted lane set from ci.yml's `run:` steps, so a lane wired into the workflow moves the reported number with no edit to the gate -- the prose-list-that-rots pattern this axis exists to replace. Result: EXECUTED-BY-HOSTED-CI proven 27 -> 49, unproven 98 -> 81, against all-lanes 53 / 77. Layer M (multicast) is deliberately NOT wired: run-ci.sh marks it an "opt-in environment-flaky lane", and a flaky gate is worse than an honest local-only one (no-flaky-ever). The residual is now exactly one atom, and A4 names it: codec-join, whose only full witness lives in a multicast test.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: new `interop` job (ubuntu-22.04, 60 min) running Layer E2 + E6 + E6b + E8 + Z. Separate from the `ci` job so the zenohd from-source build cannot eat its 30-minute budget. Provisions: the 1.85.0 toolchain (zenoh 1.5.0's pinned channel, which build-zenohd.sh hard-requires), the zenoh-pico CLIs, and zenohd -- the last cached on `target/zenohd` keyed by the pinned version, since a fixed external release's binary is a pure function of that version, so only a cold cache pays a build.

scripts/build-zenohd.sh: new SOURCE path (A2) -- a shallow clone of the pinned tag when no cargo-git checkout exists, opt-in via ZENOHD_ALLOW_CLONE=1 so a developer's machine keeps preferring the checkout it already has and never pays a clone. Without it a hosted runner falls to crates.io, which yields no storage-manager cdylib, and Layer Z's storage-replication leg SKIPs GREEN -- a proof that "runs in CI" without executing. The existing version assert validates the clone exactly as it validates a checkout, so a mis-tagged tree fails fast.

scripts/lib/crossimpl_audit.py: the hosted-execution model is now DERIVED instead of hardcoded. It had assumed "only Layer E runs ignored tests", so wiring lanes into the workflow would have changed reality without changing the reported number. `lane_bodies()` parses run-ci.sh's `run_layer <ID> <fn>` registrations, `lane_test_targets()` extracts each lane's `--test` targets, and `ci_executes()` asks whether ANY hosted lane runs this test's target (or whether Layer E's catch-all does, modulo its --skip filters). A lane wired into ci.yml now moves the number with no edit to the gate.
verification_bullets: Layer A4 after the wiring: EXECUTED BY HOSTED CI proven 27 -> 49, partial 35 -> 30, unproven 98 -> 81, against all-lanes 53 / 30 / 77. The EXECUTION lines flipped accordingly -- "EXECUTION [zenohd]: hosted CI runs Z" where it previously read "NOT RUN in hosted CI", and "[pico]: hosted CI runs E/E2/E6/E8". Both derived from ci.yml, so they cannot drift from the workflow.

Round 311y265.decision_summary: R311y265 -- the whole-session review round (3 independent adversarial agents over y259..y264, pre-push), and it caught the session reproducing its own headline failure mode one lane over. THE FALSE GREEN: R311y264 wired Layer E2 into hosted CI, but E2 was prereq-SKIP on six wz-e2e-* subset binaries that NOTHING builds -- not run-ci.sh, not the workflow. It passed locally only because those binaries linger in target/ from an earlier session; a fresh runner has none. And because Layer A4 derives "this lane runs in hosted CI" from ci.yml, wiring the step made A4 COUNT E2's pico proofs as EXECUTED while a fresh runner would have SKIPped every one of them, green. That is precisely the hazard the same commit's ZENOHD_ALLOW_CLONE comment was written to guard against (a SKIP is green), reintroduced next door -- and it would have shipped. The fix is structural, not a workflow step: a lane now BUILDS its own wz binaries, the way E6 / E8 / Z already build wz-ap-demo, and the rule is stated where it can be applied again -- SKIP on a FOREIGN binary (a machine may legitimately lack the zenoh-pico CLI or zenohd), NEVER on a wz binary we can just build. Layer E was carrying the same latent hole (it SKIPped on a missing wz-ap-demo and was saved only by an explicit workflow step) and now builds its demo too. Layer Z's remaining SKIPs are on genuinely external binaries, so they stay SKIPs on a developer's box -- but the hosted job GUARANTEES them, so it now sets WZ_Z_REQUIRE=1 and every one of them escalates to a FAIL there, the exact shape of the existing WZ_QZ_REQUIRE ("a should-run lane that SKIPs is the burn"). No hosted lane can now SKIP green on anything the job provisions. TWO OVER-CLAIMS, both of the family that has bitten every round of this session, both DOWNGRADED (and both lower the headline number, which is the correct direction): codec-keep-alive was FULL on a comparison of two EMPTY VECTORS -- the atom is a fieldless struct whose encoder is a no-op, so deleting its body leaves the gate green, and the file's own doc concedes the atom's only real wire contribution (the MID byte) is written by the enclosing envelope and out of scope; the irony is that y263 rejected `transport-keepalive` for non-discrimination while `codec-keep-alive` sat at FULL next door. And `pubsub-encoding pico->wz` was FULL from a ONE-VALUE witness whose schema bit is SET, so a decoder that ignored the bit and always parsed a schema string would pass while corrupting every schemaless encoding pico sends -- while the wz->pico sibling, a 53-id sweep with strictly more evidence, is itself graded partial. y261's settling rule applies verbatim. A FROZEN LEDGER CORRECTION, which is why this entry exists rather than an edit: Round 311y263's decision_summary states that `liveliness-history` was rejected because "no corpus binary passes history=true, so the per-call gate is never crossed". THAT IS FALSE. wz_to_zenohd_router.rs:911 passes `--liveliness-subscribe-history`, and wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs:427 sets `liveliness_options.history` from it. The CONCLUSION (leave the atom unproven) stands, but for a different and weaker reason the test's own doc-comment supplies: history was added there to REMOVE AN ORDERING RACE, so the leg passes on the plain live-routing path too, and nothing asserts a REPLAYED token as distinct from a ROUTED one -- the witness is not discriminating. This matters because y263 itself argued its REJECT list is the more valuable half; a reject list whose stated reason is a false claim about the corpus fails OPEN, since a future round would read the frozen reason, see that history=true is now passed, and claim the atom. Also corrected: y263's reject list is thirteen atoms, not "twelve"; y264's "64 of the corpus's tests are #[ignore]d" is 65 on HEAD (the figure was carried over from y259's 64-of-133). The verification bullets of both entries were exact; only the summary prose drifted. carry_forward_bullets: R311y265 = the whole-session review round. It caught the session reproducing its own headline failure one lane over, and that is the durable lesson: WIRING A LANE INTO HOSTED CI IS NOT THE SAME AS MAKING ITS PROOFS EXECUTE. Layer A4 reads "this lane is in ci.yml" as evidence of execution, so any lane that can SKIP green on a missing dependency makes the number lie the moment it is wired. The rule, now applied to every hosted lane: SKIP on a FOREIGN binary (a machine may legitimately lack the zenoh-pico CLI or zenohd), NEVER on a wz binary the lane can build; and where the hosted job GUARANTEES an external binary, escalate the SKIP to a FAIL there (WZ_Z_REQUIRE, mirroring WZ_QZ_REQUIRE).

THE OVER-CLAIM FAMILY HAS NOW BITTEN IN EVERY ROUND OF THIS SESSION (y260 constants, y261 cfg gates, y265 tautologies), which is a pattern, not bad luck. The check that catches it every time: BREAK THE ATOM'S CODE IN YOUR HEAD -- if the test still passes, the claim is not a proof. `codec-keep-alive` was full on `vec![] == vec![]`; `pubsub-encoding pico->wz` was full on a single value whose schema bit was always set. Both are now partial. Corollary that settles most arguments cheaply: if a SIBLING atom with MORE evidence is graded partial, a claim with LESS cannot be full.

A REJECT LIST FAILS OPEN. y263's frozen reject reason for `liveliness-history` ("no corpus binary passes history=true") is FALSE -- wz_to_zenohd_router.rs:911 passes it. The conclusion holds but the reason does not, and a future round reading that frozen reason would see the condition satisfied and claim the atom. The REAL reason is in the test's own doc: history was added to remove an ordering race, so the leg passes on the plain routing path and nothing asserts a REPLAYED token as distinct from a ROUTED one. When a reject list is the deliverable, its REASONS carry the same weight as claims and need the same scrutiny.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311y265 = the whole-session review round. It caught the session reproducing its own headline failure one lane over, and that is the durable lesson: WIRING A LANE INTO HOSTED CI IS NOT THE SAME AS MAKING ITS PROOFS EXECUTE. Layer A4 reads "this lane is in ci.yml" as evidence of execution, so any lane that can SKIP green on a missing dependency makes the number lie the moment it is wired. The rule, now applied to every hosted lane: SKIP on a FOREIGN binary (a machine may legitimately lack the zenoh-pico CLI or zenohd), NEVER on a wz binary the lane can build; and where the hosted job GUARANTEES an external binary, escalate the SKIP to a FAIL there (WZ_Z_REQUIRE, mirroring WZ_QZ_REQUIRE).

THE OVER-CLAIM FAMILY HAS NOW BITTEN IN EVERY ROUND OF THIS SESSION (y260 constants, y261 cfg gates, y265 tautologies), which is a pattern, not bad luck. The check that catches it every time: BREAK THE ATOM'S CODE IN YOUR HEAD -- if the test still passes, the claim is not a proof. `codec-keep-alive` was full on `vec![] == vec![]`; `pubsub-encoding pico->wz` was full on a single value whose schema bit was always set. Both are now partial. Corollary that settles most arguments cheaply: if a SIBLING atom with MORE evidence is graded partial, a claim with LESS cannot be full.

A REJECT LIST FAILS OPEN. y263's frozen reject reason for `liveliness-history` ("no corpus binary passes history=true") is FALSE -- wz_to_zenohd_router.rs:911 passes it. The conclusion holds but the reason does not, and a future round reading that frozen reason would see the condition satisfied and claim the atom. The REAL reason is in the test's own doc: history was added to remove an ordering race, so the leg passes on the plain routing path and nothing asserts a REPLAYED token as distinct from a ROUTED one. When a reject list is the deliverable, its REASONS carry the same weight as claims and need the same scrutiny.

Expect the cold zenohd build to dominate; it caches on target/zenohd keyed by the pinned version. If it overruns the 60-minute budget, RAISE THE TIMEOUT; do not fall back to the crates.io zenohd, which yields no storage-manager plugin and would silently SKIP the storage-replication proof (and WZ_Z_REQUIRE now turns that skip into a FAIL, so the lane will tell you loudly instead of lying).

NEXT: adminspace (8 atoms) is unblocked -- E6b is in hosted CI and pico HAS Z_FEATURE_ADMIN_SPACE, so a pico z_get vs wz's adminspace test placed in that lane will EXECUTE. Check the cfg-gate binding first, as always.

Round 311y266.decision_summary: R311y266 -- the gate-integrity half of the whole-session review, and it found that the gate was lying in a way nobody was watching. Layer A4's disclosure line read "E7/M only in the local full run-ci (pre-push)". FALSE FOR M: Layer M guards itself with `ONLY_LAYER != "M" && WZ_RUN_LAYER_M != 1`, and the pre-push hook invokes run-ci.sh with neither -- so M runs on NO default path at all, hosted or local. Three atoms (router-multicast-faces, transport-link-udp, transport-multicast) were sitting inside the headline `proven` on the strength of tests that execute NOWHERE, and nothing named them: `promoted_by_unrun` only catches the partial->full promotion case, so the strictly worse population -- proven with ZERO hosted-CI witness of any kind -- was visible only as an unexplained delta between the two headline counts. Both are fixed: the roll-up now prints PROVEN WITH NO HOSTED-CI WITNESS AT ALL and names them, and `opt_in_lanes()` derives "runs nowhere" from the guard itself, so the disclosure cannot drift back into a lie. THE GATE'S KILL SWITCH WAS ONE NETWORK BLIP AWAY. audit-crossimpl-proof.sh exits 0 when mnemosyne-cli is absent, and hosted CI installs it behind a deliberately fault-tolerant `|| { warning; skip }` fallback -- so a transient upstream failure would have left EVERY invariant unchecked (a malformed claim, an atom renamed out of the inventory, a wz<->wz test claiming foreign proof) on a green build. WZ_A4_REQUIRE=1 in the workflow turns that skip into a failure. THE SAME SHAPE, ONE LEVEL DOWN, ACROSS EVERY HOSTED PROOF LANE: E / E2 / E6 / E8 all SKIP green on a missing zenoh-pico CLI, and E6's three pico legs skip INDIVIDUALLY, so deleting one workflow step would have taken every pico proof out of hosted CI while A4 -- which reads "this lane is in ci.yml" as evidence its proofs executed -- kept counting them. A shared `_pico_cli_unavailable` helper now escalates under WZ_PICO_REQUIRE, set on the interop job. The rule these three fixes share, and the one worth carrying: a SKIP on a binary the job PROVISIONS is a provisioning regression wearing a green badge (WZ_QZ_REQUIRE's "a should-run lane that SKIPs is the burn", now applied to A4, to the pico CLIs, and to Z). Also fixed, each a latent false-green rather than a live one: the zenohd cache was keyed on the version alone with no content hash of the build script, so a cache once populated WITHOUT the storage-manager plugin would have stranded that proof behind a green SKIP for the life of the key -- it is now keyed on hashFiles(build-zenohd.sh) and a step ASSERTS both artefacts are present after restore rather than trusting it; `cf.binary`'s ternary had two IDENTICAL branches, so a file driving several wz binaries silently got the alphabetically-first (wz-ap-demo, the fattest 110-feature closure) and its claims would have been validated against a union it does not have -- the audit now unions the closures of every binary a file drives, which is a superset and so can never false-FAIL; `#[ignore]` written ABOVE `#[test]` left has_ignore False, so a skipped test counted as "runs on every push via C1"; and helper_classes() splits lib.rs on a hard 4-space fn indent, so a reformat would have silently returned {} and shrunk the corpus AND every derived number with it, still green -- it now raises instead. The interop job's timeout goes 60 -> 120: a cold cache must build the pico CMake tree, the whole zenoh workspace in release, four differently-featured wz-ap-demo builds, six wz-e2e-* binaries and then Layer Z's serial sweep. DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED: `ci_executes` is still derived from what the shell INTENDS to run, not what it DID run. The SKIP holes it could not see are closed by escalation rather than by modelling, and the only sound version of that predicate joins the claims to libtest's actual `test <name> ... ok` output. Until then, "executed by hosted CI" is a well-guarded assertion, not a measurement. Round 311y267.decision_summary: R311y267 -- the footprint gate was measuring its own build directory's path length, and hosted CI had been RED for ~20 pushes because of it. The kickoff read of `gh run list` (not of run-ci, which was green) found the last green at 99e42828 and every push since e81d7a50 (2026-07-09) failing on Layer Q's mcu-multicast-e2e footprint. The code never regressed: a clean local build of HEAD reads 51116 at rustc 1.96 -- byte-identical to the CI number of the last GREEN run. TWO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES WERE BEING GATED AS IF THEY WERE CODE. (1) rustc floats: every job used dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, and stable went 1.96.1 -> 1.97.0 on 2026-07-09 -- the exact day the red streak begins -- moving codegen ~+48 B on this binary. The workspace rust-version field is an MSRV LOWER BOUND and never pinned the build compiler, which is what a byte-exact ROM gate needs; the project already knew this (build-zenohd.sh pins zenoh's 1.85.0 channel with the comment that building on another channel "is not a reproducibility trade this project makes") and had simply never applied it to its own build. (2) rustc embeds ABSOLUTE BUILD PATHS (panic Location strings, cargo registry sources) in .rodata, and `size --format=berkeley` counts .rodata inside its `text` column -- so the gated number encodes the length of the path it was built at. Proven by construction, not inferred: the same commit and same rustc measured 50964 built at /w, 51164 at /home/coin/watching-zenoh, and 51344 at the runner's /home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh -- a 380 B spread on identical code against a +/-256 B band, ordered exactly by path length. An ubuntu:22.04 container mounted at the runner's path reproduced CI's 51344 to the byte, which is what turned a theory into a diagnosis. THE PRIOR EXPLANATION WAS FALSE AND HAD TO GO: the standing "footprint baseline is CI-arm-gcc-specific, local gcc emits less" rule (§6.7 caveat (r), and the recipe of rebasing baselines from CI log numbers) blamed arm-gcc -- but CI and this host carry byte-identical gcc 10.3.1 / binutils 2.38 / newlib 3.3.0 packages, and following that recipe would have pinned a number produced by a floating compiler at one machine's path, going red again at the next rustc and leaving the local gate 4 bytes from red. FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY REBASING THE NUMBER: rust-toolchain.toml pins rustc 1.97.0 and owns components + targets (they must follow the PINNED toolchain -- left on a floating stable they would install on a toolchain cargo does not use, and run-ci.sh SKIPs a target it cannot find, so the footprint gate would have gone quietly green having measured nothing: a SKIP is green, one lane over); Layer Q exports --remap-path-prefix for every MCU build; and check-footprint.sh now re-asserts path purity on the ARTIFACT, FAILing a binary that still embeds the repo root or CARGO_HOME rather than measuring it. Verified: host and runner-path container now agree byte-for-byte (50956), and the negative test confirms the new gate actually fires. Baselines rebased once onto the reproducible measurement; all six deltas +0. Layer Q pass, RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: rust-toolchain.toml (NEW): pins channel 1.97.0 and owns components (rustfmt, clippy) + the 8 embedded targets. The pin is the SSOT: components/targets declared in ci.yml would attach to whatever toolchain the action installs while cargo resolves the pinned one from this file, leaving the real build toolchain without the embedded targets -- and run-ci.sh SKIPs a target it cannot find, so Layer Q would report green having measured nothing. Bumping the pin is now an explicit round that must carry the footprint rebase in the same commit.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: all five dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable steps (ci / interop / cross-mcu / zephyr-mcu / portability) replaced with `run: rustup show`, which materialises the pinned toolchain (channel + components + targets) from rust-toolchain.toml. The embedded-target and component inputs are deleted (the pin owns them). zenohd's separate 1.85.0 install is untouched -- build-zenohd.sh selects it with an explicit `cargo +1.85.0`, which overrides the toolchain file.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new footprint_remap_rustflags() SSOT helper; layer_q_qemu_mcu_e2e() exports it as RUSTFLAGS for every MCU build, so the footprint artifacts are path-normalised. Safe over the deploy crates' .cargo/config.toml target.*.rustflags (env RUSTFLAGS replaces rather than merges them): every deploy MCU build.rs already emits -Tlink.x via cargo:rustc-link-arg, and those config entries are documented duplicates of exactly that.

scripts/check-footprint.sh: new path-normalisation gate -- FAILs (exit 1, naming the leaked prefix) if the measured ELF still embeds the repo root or CARGO_HOME, so a binary built outside Layer Q's export cannot be silently measured against a baseline it is not comparable to. Also prints the measuring toolchain (rustc + arm-gcc) with each measurement: the gate now records its own provenance.

scripts/check-footprint.sh: BASELINE_TEXT rebased to the reproducible figures (v6m 19780 / v7m 25296 / v7em-hf 25360 / v8m 26148) and BASELINE_MC_TEXT to (v7m 50956 / v7em-hf 51096). Round 311y267.publishable_decision_summary: R311y267 -- the footprint gate was measuring its own build directory's path length, and hosted CI had been RED for ~20 pushes because of it. The kickoff read of `gh run list` (not of run-ci, which was green) found the last green at 99e42828 and every push since e81d7a50 (2026-07-09) failing on Layer Q's mcu-multicast-e2e footprint. The code never regressed: a clean local build of HEAD reads 51116 at rustc 1.96 -- byte-identical to the CI number of the last GREEN run. TWO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES WERE BEING GATED AS IF THEY WERE CODE. (1) rustc floats: every job used dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, and stable went 1.96.1 -> 1.97.0 on 2026-07-09 -- the exact day the red streak begins -- moving codegen ~+48 B on this binary. The workspace rust-version field is an MSRV LOWER BOUND and never pinned the build compiler, which is what a byte-exact ROM gate needs; the project already knew this (build-zenohd.sh pins zenoh's 1.85.0 channel with the comment that building on another channel "is not a reproducibility trade this project makes") and had simply never applied it to its own build. (2) rustc embeds ABSOLUTE BUILD PATHS (panic Location strings, cargo registry sources) in .rodata, and `size --format=berkeley` counts .rodata inside its `text` column -- so the gated number encodes the length of the path it was built at. Proven by construction, not inferred: the same commit and same rustc measured 50964 built at /w, 51164 at /home/coin/watching-zenoh, and 51344 at the runner's /home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh -- a 380 B spread on identical code against a +/-256 B band, ordered exactly by path length. An ubuntu:22.04 container mounted at the runner's path reproduced CI's 51344 to the byte, which is what turned a theory into a diagnosis. THE PRIOR EXPLANATION WAS FALSE AND HAD TO GO: the standing "footprint baseline is CI-arm-gcc-specific, local gcc emits less" rule (§6.7 caveat (r), and the recipe of rebasing baselines from CI log numbers) blamed arm-gcc -- but CI and this host carry byte-identical gcc 10.3.1 / binutils 2.38 / newlib 3.3.0 packages, and following that recipe would have pinned a number produced by a floating compiler at one machine's path, going red again at the next rustc and leaving the local gate 4 bytes from red. FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY REBASING THE NUMBER: rust-toolchain.toml pins rustc 1.97.0 and owns components + targets (they must follow the PINNED toolchain -- left on a floating stable they would install on a toolchain cargo does not use, and run-ci.sh SKIPs a target it cannot find, so the footprint gate would have gone quietly green having measured nothing: a SKIP is green, one lane over); Layer Q exports --remap-path-prefix for every MCU build; and check-footprint.sh now re-asserts path purity on the ARTIFACT, FAILing a binary that still embeds the repo root or CARGO_HOME rather than measuring it. Verified: host and runner-path container now agree byte-for-byte (50956), and the negative test confirms the new gate actually fires. Baselines rebased once onto the reproducible measurement; all six deltas +0. Layer Q pass, RUNCI_EXIT=0.

Round 311y268.decision_summary: R311y268 -- the read-back round, and it caught R311y267 over-claiming. R311y267 shipped and WORKED: the hosted runner's Layer Q went green on the first attempt after ~20 red pushes, with qemu-demo x4 and multicast thumbv7m all reading +0 against the rebased baselines and the pin confirmed active on the runner (rustup: "overridden by /home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh/rust-toolchain.toml"). But reading the runner's own numbers back -- rather than trusting the claim -- surfaced one axis that does NOT match: multicast thumbv7em-none-eabihf reads 51100 on the runner against 51096 here, a +4 B residual. R311y267 asserted the figures were "byte-identical on this host and on the runner"; that assertion was extrapolated from ONE container-verified target (thumbv7m) onto all six, and it is false for thumbv7em-hf. Frozen-ledger: R311y267's body stands, this entry corrects it. ROOT-CAUSED, not waved through: a container at the HOST path reproduces 51096 and the same container at the RUNNER path reproduces 51100, so the residual is genuinely path-correlated -- but an ELF diff of the two (Q.5 artifacts, after first discovering the on-disk binary was Q.6's loopback-multicast variant overwriting the same path) shows .rodata BYTE-IDENTICAL and the entire 4 B living in .text. So the path-LENGTH term -- the 380 B one that caused the incident -- really is fully eliminated by --remap-path-prefix; what remains is .text alignment jitter, because cargo derives each crate's metadata hash from its package PATH, which perturbs symbol hashes and hence padding. It is not proportional to path length (5 of the 6 gated axes are +0 across environments), it is 1.5% of the +/-256 B band, and eliminating it would require building at a canonical path (a containerised footprint build) -- disproportionate. CARRIED as a named residual, with the honest framing recorded where it will be read: "reproducible" does NOT mean "bit-identical" here; the unbounded term is gone, a few bytes of layout jitter are not.

Round 311y269.decision_summary: R311y269 -- Layer Q.6's ELF stops overwriting Layer Q.5's footprint artifact, and the comment that claimed it never did is retracted. Q.6 (the loopback-multicast QEMU runtime proof) builds the SAME crate, triple, profile and --bin as Q.5 (the footprint artifact), differing only in --features loopback-multicast and WZ_LWIP_PORT. Cargo keys a binary's FINAL path on (target dir, triple, profile, bin name) ONLY: the feature set is hashed into the intermediate deps/<bin>-<hash>, and the last build then UPLIFTS (hard-links) over the same stable path. Demonstrated on disk -- two feature-hashed intermediates coexist in deps/ while the final path shares an inode with whichever built last, and after a full Layer Q that is always Q.6's (bss 287244, against the footprint bin's 272268). Q.6's own comment asserted "a SEPARATE ELF ... so the Q.5 baseline stays byte-identical"; the ELF was never separate. THE MEASUREMENT WAS NEVER WRONG -- Q.5 gates immediately after its own build, before Q.6 runs -- but that made the gate's correctness rest on LANE ORDERING, an invariant nothing enforced and nothing stated: a future round reordering the lanes, or footprinting anything after Q.6, would have silently measured the wrong binary. This is the same shape as the defect R311y267 fixed (a gate whose number depends on something nobody declared), and it was found only because R311y268's post-hoc ELF diff picked up the Q.6 variant and produced garbage. Q.6 now builds into its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR (deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e/target-loopback), so the collision is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely unreached; it also ends a per-run rebuild thrash, since the two lanes flip WZ_LWIP_PORT (which lwip-sys declares rerun-if-env-changed) and each was invalidating the other's C build. Round 311y270.decision_summary: R311y270 -- §5.23 adminspace gets its first FOREIGN witness: a real zenoh-pico z_get CLI queries a wz routing peer's admin space and decodes the two bodies wz serves there. Until now every adminspace atom sat `unproven` on the cross-impl proof axis, and the reason recorded in Layer E6b was that an admin GET "adds no wire format, so no cross-impl leg is needed" -- which is an argument about the ENVELOPE (an admin GET is an ordinary Query, its replies ordinary Put bodies) and says nothing about the KEYS and BODIES a foreign client actually has to agree with in order to use the admin space at all. This closes that. The E6b binary is unchanged (--features routing-peer,adminspace-introspection-handlers); only the client changes, from a wz demo to pico. One root GET at `@/<A_zid>/peer/**` returns three replies, all decoded by pico's C stack: the node record at the bare root (`{"locators":["tcp/<the actual reserved port>"],"plugins":null,"sessions":[],"version":"0.1.0","zid":"<A_zid>"}`), the config leg, and the per-entity subscriber leg keyed by A's LIVE declared keyexpr (`@/<A_zid>/peer/subscriber/demo/data`) carrying the zenoh Sources body. THE TWO CLAIMS ARE NOT EQUALLY BOUND, AND ARE STATED APART RATHER THAN FUSED. adminspace-introspection-handlers has an EXECUTED counterfactual: rebuilding the demo `--features routing-peer` alone drops the subscriber leg from pico's reply set and the test FAILS -- run, not asserted. adminspace-core has NO counterfactual build that can exist: the demo's routing-peer hard-pulls wz/adminspace-core (a routing peer hosts its own admin space, wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml:179), so no --peer binary with the atom off is buildable; its binding is instead structural and total -- the ENTIRE wz_session_core::adminspace module, where the local_data JSON builder lives, is #[cfg(feature = "adminspace-core")] (wz-session-core/src/lib.rs:492), so with the atom off the body cannot be produced. Strong, but READ rather than RUN, and the test docstring grades it that way. THE NEGATIVE TEST EARNED ITS KEEP: it was run BEFORE the claim was written, and it caught the first draft of this round asserting the metrics-absence as its discriminator while the adminspace-core assertion would in fact have passed against a binary with every adminspace feature off -- because routing-peer pulls core regardless. The claim was re-grounded on the module cfg gate (direct read) instead of a counterfactual that does not exist. Axis: proven 51 -> 53 all-lanes and 47 -> 49 executed-by-hosted-CI (E6b is a hosted lane since R311y264, so these proofs RUN); adminspace-core and adminspace-introspection-handlers leave the unproven list.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_peer_adminspace_to_pico_zget.rs (NEW): peer A is the existing E6b wz-ap-demo (--peer --config-queryable --subscribe demo/data), the client is the real zenoh-pico z_get CLI dialing tcp/<addr> as a client and GETting `@/<A_zid>/peer/**`. Asserts (1) the adminspace-core node record at the bare root, pinned on A's live zid AND its ACTUAL bound locator (the port the test reserved at runtime, so a static fixture cannot satisfy it) plus the version/sessions fields of its F=; (2) the adminspace-introspection-handlers subscriber leg keyed by the LIVE declared keyexpr with the zenoh Sources body naming A as source peer; (3) that the `@/<zid>/peer/metrics` leg is ABSENT -- adminspace-metrics is not in this binary's features, so a reply set that ignored the cfg gates could not pass. Until now every adminspace atom sat `unproven` on the cross-impl proof axis, and the reason recorded in Layer E6b was that an admin GET "adds no wire format, so no cross-impl leg is needed" -- which is an argument about the ENVELOPE (an admin GET is an ordinary Query, its replies ordinary Put bodies) and says nothing about the KEYS and BODIES a foreign client actually has to agree with in order to use the admin space at all. This closes that. The E6b binary is unchanged (--features routing-peer,adminspace-introspection-handlers); only the client changes, from a wz demo to pico. One root GET at `@/<A_zid>/peer/**` returns three replies, all decoded by pico's C stack: the node record at the bare root (`{"locators":["tcp/<the actual reserved port>"],"plugins":null,"sessions":[],"version":"0.1.0","zid":"<A_zid>"}`), the config leg, and the per-entity subscriber leg keyed by A's LIVE declared keyexpr (`@/<A_zid>/peer/subscriber/demo/data`) carrying the zenoh Sources body. THE NEGATIVE TEST EARNED ITS KEEP: it was run BEFORE the claim was written, and it caught the first draft of this round asserting the metrics-absence as its discriminator while the adminspace-core assertion would in fact have passed against a binary with every adminspace feature off -- because routing-peer pulls core regardless. The claim was re-grounded on the module cfg gate (direct read) instead of a counterfactual that does not exist. Axis: proven 51 -> 53 all-lanes and 47 -> 49 executed-by-hosted-CI (E6b is a hosted lane since R311y264, so these proofs RUN); adminspace-core and adminspace-introspection-handlers leave the unproven list.

Round 311y271.decision_summary: R311y271 -- adminspace-plugins-handlers gets a pico witness, and wiring it exposed that the axis's own EXECUTION disclosure had rotted. THE PROOF: pico's z_get reads wz's `@/<zid>/peer/plugins/**` leg and decodes the compiled-subsystem record (`{"name":"storage_manager","id":"storage_manager","version":"0.1.0","path":"__static__","state":"Loaded","report":{"level":"Info"}}`) -- the `__static__` marker being wz's superset signal that this registry is the cfg!-driven compiled-subsystem set, NOT a dlopen PluginsManager (§5.22 stays reserved). It rides Layer E6e's EXISTING binary (routing-peer,adminspace-plugins-handlers,storage-backend), the same shape R311y270 used on E6b. GRADED PARTIAL, DELIBERATELY: the atom's F= has three surfaces and only one is witnessed. The `status/plugins/**` legs and the node record's `plugins` field both report STARTED plugins, and nothing starts storage_manager here (no storage is configured), so they are faithfully EMPTY -- correct behaviour, but unproven; a live-storage witness is adminspace-config-hotreload territory and would upgrade this to full. Both failure modes were RUN, not argued: rebuilding the demo `--features routing-peer,storage-backend` -- subsystem still compiled in, only the ATOM removed -- makes the test FAIL with no plugins leg at all (so the witness binds to the atom, not to storage-backend), and the feature ON without storage-backend answers with an empty registry (so the asserted body is non-empty and subsystem-specific, not the `vec![] == vec![]` tautology that once graded codec-keep-alive full). THE ROUND'S SECOND, UNPLANNED FINDING: adding the proof moved `proven/partial [all lanes]` but left `[executed by hosted CI]` FLAT -- because Layer E6e was not in the workflow. That gap is exactly the signal Layer A4 splits its two populations to produce, and it worked. E6e is now wired into the hosted interop job. Chasing it further surfaced that CLASS_LANES -- the map behind the EXECUTION disclosure -- was HARDCODED and had already rotted: it printed "hosted CI runs E/E2/E6/E8" while E6b's pico proofs had been running there since R311y264, and the comment directly above it claimed the opposite ("the printed line moved with it without an edit here"). The COUNTS were never wrong (ci_executes derives them end to end); only the sentence describing them lied. CLASS_LANES is now DERIVED from the same two sources ci_executes uses -- the corpus's per-file class and run-ci.sh's lane -> --test map -- so wiring a lane moves the disclosure as well as the number. The corrected line reads E/E2/E6/E6b/E6e/E8/Z, and it also drops E7 (a wz<->wz lane the hardcoded list wrongly counted as a pico lane) and surfaces Z (which runs the 3 dual-class pico+zenohd files). Axis: partial 32 -> 33 all-lanes AND 32 -> 33 executed-by-hosted-CI; adminspace-plugins-handlers leaves the unproven list; §5.23 now has 3 of 8 atoms with a foreign witness.

THE ATOM IS THE GATE, NOT THE WRITE. adminspace-write's F= is the `permissions.write` gate on the config-write PUT path (zenoh adminspace.rs:396, default-DENY per PermissionsConf), so a test that merely showed a write LANDING would witness the plumbing while saying nothing about the atom. Round 311y273.decision_summary: R311y273 -- adminspace-router-linkstate gets a foreign witness: a real zenoh-pico z_get reads a wz ROUTER's admin topology across a two-router federation, and this round required a hosted-CI wiring decision the user approved. THE PROOF: R1 (--router-hat --config-queryable) + R2 (--router-hat --connect R1) federate; pico z_gets `@/<R1_zid>/router/**` and decodes all three F= legs -- linkstate/routers + linkstate/peers (GraphViz DOT of the two link-state nets) and route/successor/** (the computed (src,dst)->next-hop table). FULL, not partial, and the topology is WHY: the successor table renders from the ROUTERS net (zenoh hat/router/mod.rs:910), so it is empty on a lone router OR a router-with-peers -- a next hop exists only once a SECOND router is present. Probed before the round: one router alone gives non-empty DOT but an EMPTY successor table; two federated routers give a successor entry keyed `.../src/<R1>/dst/<R2>: "<next-hop>"`, which the test pins (a key built from two runtime zids cannot be a fixture). EXECUTED COUNTERFACTUAL: rebuild the binary at E7's PRIOR feature set (router-hat-router alone, adminspace-router-linkstate OUT) and the test FAILS at the barrier -- the router hosts no `@/<zid>/router/**` queryable at all, since every leg is #[cfg(feature="adminspace-router-linkstate")]. THREE HARNESS TRAPS CAUGHT AND FIXED, none by eye: (1) the first barrier waited for R2's zid string in R1's log, which never appears -- wz logs faces in raw little-endian zid bytes while the admin space renders zenoh-hex (byte-reversed); replaced with R1's own deterministic `routers-net converged (2 node(s))` edge (the y124-class fix: a convergence-count witness, not a string match). (2) A4-4 rejected the first draft -- the wz-proves line sat above a helper fn, unattached; moved onto the #[test]. (3) the fn name carries the `wz_router_` prefix Layer E's catch-all skips (`--skip wz_router`), so E does not double-run it on an arbitrary-feature binary. THE WIRING DECISION: E7 was NOT in hosted CI (local pre-push only), so before wiring, adding the proof moved A4's all-lanes count while the executed-by-hosted-CI count stayed flat -- the same signal E6e surfaced in y271. E7's one historical flake (an in-run convergence tick-race) was fixed to a deterministic shutdown-peak assertion in R311y124; verified stable across 3 repeated full-lane runs on the new feature set before wiring; user approved adding it to the interop job. Axis: proven 54 -> 55 all-lanes AND 50 -> 51 executed-by-hosted-CI (the wiring is why the second moved). §5.23 now has 5 of 8 atoms foreign-witnessed.
