Round 311y274.decision_summary:
R311y274 -- the whole-session review round (3 independent adversarial read-only agents over y267..y273, arbitrated by direct read), and it closes the session's own doctrine where the session had left it open. THE HEADLINE FINDING: the footprint gate -- the entire subject of R311y267 -- was the ONE provisioned CI lane with no WZ_*_REQUIRE backstop. Every other provisioned lane escalates a prerequisite SKIP to a FAIL (WZ_A4_REQUIRE, WZ_PICO_REQUIRE, WZ_Z_REQUIRE, WZ_QZ_REQUIRE), on the stated rule "a SKIP is green; escalate wherever the job provisions the thing." The mcu job's Layer Q step had neither an env nor a post-build assert (ci.yml:631 bare run), and every SKIP beneath it exits 0: target-absent (continue), nothing-built (return 0), and check-footprint's binary/size-missing (exit 0). Its only defense was rust-toolchain.toml provisioning the targets via `rustup show` -- and rustup regressed exactly that auto-install in 1.28.0, so the failure mode is real, not hypothetical: if a future runner image loses a target, `rustup show` succeeds, the target is absent, every Q sub-lane continues, and the mcu job is green having measured zero bytes -- the precise 20-push regression R311y267 exists to catch, sailing through. FIXED: WZ_Q_REQUIRE=1 on the mcu job (ci.yml), and the five SKIP branches escalate to FAIL under it -- the two check-footprint prereqs (binary/size missing), the two run-ci target-absent sub-lanes (Q.1/Q.3 machine, Q.5 mctarget), and the nothing-built aggregate backstop; off (a dev host without the cross toolchain) all stay soft SKIPs. SECOND FINDING (B2), the path-purity gate's own detector was unguarded: check-footprint verifies remap purity with `strings`, but unlike `arm-none-eabi-size` (command -v guarded) `strings` was not -- proven by the agent that with `strings` off PATH the gate reported a clean +0 on a binary carrying the repo path. Now an absent `strings` FAILs unconditionally (no legitimate "measure without the detector" mode). Both fixes verified with executed negative tests: strings-absent -> FAIL exit 1; WZ_Q_REQUIRE + missing binary -> FAIL exit 1 (soft SKIP exit 0 without the require); and the normal Layer Q still passes +0 on all six axes under WZ_Q_REQUIRE. ALSO CORRECTED (documentation, no behavior): the interop job name (ci.yml) said "(E2 + E6 + E6b + E8 + Z)" -- stale since y271/y273 added E6e + E7 steps, the same prose-rots-below-the-derived-layer problem y271's class_lanes() de-hardcode fixed one level down; and the y273 test docstring said the adminspace-router-linkstate counterfactual fails because "pico's GET returns nothing" when it actually fails earlier, at the admin-root log scrape (the barrier) before pico is spawned -- same outcome, corrected mechanism (both A and C agents flagged it). THE REVIEW'S HEALTH SIGNAL: zero over-claim defects (agent A re-ran the counterfactuals, one empirically), zero frozen-ledger violations (agent C's structural JSON diff: 7 entries added, 0 bodies mutated), workspace clean -- the findings are all gate-hardening and doc precision, not correctness regressions.

Round 311y277.decision_summary: R311y277 -- adminspace-config-hotreload cross-impl witness via a NEW storage-hosting demo run-mode (--storage-host). A stock zenoh-pico client drives the config-diff storage lifecycle END-TO-END: a pico z_put @/<zid>/peer/config/storage-add demo:demo/** makes wz call RuntimeStorageManager::add_storage (a LIVE storage), and a subsequent pico z_get @/<zid>/peer/plugins/** decodes storage_manager state Started (Loaded before); storage-del reverses it. This closes §5.23 -- all 8 adminspace atoms are now foreign-witnessed. The witness binds to the atom's REAL code, NOT a bool flip: the host GET handler reads compiled_plugins_dyn(&version, storage_started), storage_started tracks !manager.is_empty(), and the test waits on the host's spawned-live-storage log emitted ONLY in the Ok arm of a real add_storage (runner.rs) before asserting Started -- so Started cannot appear without a live manager-hosted storage. DESIGN-REVIEWED PRE-CODE by 3 independent adversarial agents (the recurring review trigger, DESIGN phase): agent 1 confirmed the StorageService survives its transient client Session drop (Arc-all-the-way, panic/UAF-free); agent 3 confirmed bare-Session GET reachability (intersection), the Send+'static handler bound (-> Arc state, manager task-local), and the dispatch-drain hook (after dispatch_iteration_event_with, not under_lock); agent 2 found a simpler run_peer bool-flip but flagged it OVER-CLAIMS (reports Started without add_storage) -- REJECTED because the claim must bind to the atom M=/C= code (feedback-claim-binds-to-atom-code). ARCHITECTURE: stock pico z_put and z_get are separate one-shot processes, so a single 1:1 unicast Session cannot serve them; the host MULTI-ACCEPTS per-client Sessions (bind once, loop accept->open->declare admin GET queryable + config-write subscriber->drive->re-accept) with the manager + storage_started + pending stash HOISTED above the loop. NAMED BOUND: the hosted storage is a ZOMBIE -- declared on the transient z_put client Session, it survives (manager hoisted) as STATE-OBSERVABLE (keeps !is_empty() -> Started) but is NOT data-serving across the session boundary; the witness asserts only the plugins STATE flip, not cross-connection data. A4: proven 57->58 all-lanes AND 53->54 executed-by-hosted-CI (+1 both, config-hotreload executed via the hosted E6h). full run-ci deferred to push (pre-push hook covers Layer A3 catalog + C1/C2 workspace).

Round 311y279.decision_summary: R311y279 -- storage-backend-filesystem BUILT (reserved/UNBUILT -> active): a durable, filesystem-backed Volume/StorageBackend in wz-runtime-tokio (FilesystemVolume / FilesystemStorage), the wz counterpart of zenoh's zenoh-backend-filesystem, on std + the log facade only (no new third-party dep). The reserved platform-freertos atom is promoted to active by a GENUINE cfg(feature = "platform-freertos") site in crates/wz/src/lib.rs (`pub use wz_runtime_freertos as runtime_freertos`) -- the ONE platform-* that gates real code, because target_os CANNOT distinguish a FreeRTOS deploy from bare-metal (both are target_os = "none" on thumbv7m-none-eabi); so unlike platform-bare-metal (target-triple+no_std-selected = FOUNDATIONAL) the RTOS is an opt-in cfg knob (A3 active<=>cfg). Round 311y280.decision_summary: R311y280 -- storage-backend-filesystem COMPOSITION + DURABILITY proof (test-only, additive; NO inventory change -- the atom is already active from y279). Closes the composition-over-isolated-atoms gap: y279's backend unit test proved FilesystemStorage round-trips on disk IN ISOLATION, but nothing proved it works through the LIVE service path. A new wz-runtime-tokio test drives the REAL path -- RuntimeStorageManager::add_storage with a FilesystemVolume registered under volume_id "fs" -> a live StorageService (capture subscriber + queryable) -> FilesystemStorage -> disk -> the manager+session are DROPPED -> a FRESH manager+session+FilesystemVolume on the SAME dir re-hosts the storage -> a loopback GET serves the value persisted before the restart, with NO new put (so it can only come from load-on-open). A MemoryVolume negative control runs the identical flow and proves the Volatile backend LOSES the value across the same restart -- the discriminator that makes the fs PASS mean durability, not a one-session round-trip. RuntimeStorageManager / VolumeRegistry already accept any Box<dyn Volume>, so FilesystemVolume composes with ZERO API change; this round is the missing PROOF, not new production logic. CI Layer C1bg extended to run both tests under storage-mgr-multi-storage-host + storage-backend-filesystem + pubsub-allow-loop + declare-subscriber, each with a >=1-passed guard. A focused adversarial review (1 agent, direct-read arbitrated) verified the proof discriminates + is non-vacuous (SOUND-PROOF; session 1 fully dropped, session 2 opens a fresh backend that load-on-opens from disk, the reply is read straight from backend.get_all_entries/get). validate_workspace orphan new=+0. NOT pushed.

Round 311y285.decision_summary: R311y285 -- api-compat-pico R1 IMPL-review fixes (§5.27). A 3-agent independent adversarial IMPL review of R311y284 (memory-safety/UB, ABI-fidelity vs ~/zenoh-pico, correctness/integration/honesty), arbitrated by direct source read + an empirical test. The most damaging flagged item -- "z_put from inside a subscriber callback panics on Handle::block_on and poisons the driver mutex, killing the session" -- is REFUTED empirically: a new echo test publishes from within the callback and the sample is delivered; the reviewer traced pico's scouting/response send_blocking(block_on) path, but the unicast pub path enqueues via the writer channel (the same path the in-runtime drive loop uses, which is why it never panics). Real fixes applied: (1) SessionState::close now uses tokio Notify::notify_one instead of notify_waiters -- a CONFIRMED lost-wakeup hang, since the drive task parks its .notified() waiter only after z_open returns, so a fast z_close/z_session_drop could drop the signal and block on join() forever on a healthy link; notify_one stores a permit so the shutdown is never lost. (2) The outbound C subscriber callback is now wrapped in catch_unwind so a panicking callback cannot unwind across the extern "C" boundary and tear down the drive thread. (3) z_open always-initializes its *zs out-param before any fallible work (pico contract). (4) Nine compile-time size_of static_asserts turn the byte-match claim into a build-enforced gate. (5) The wz api-compat-pico feature now also enables runtime-tokio, so the runtime-XOR compile_error fires for api-compat-pico + runtime-coop (previously it silently linked both runtimes). (6) z_string_take_from_loaned added, completing pico's string full-DEF family. (7) Docstrings corrected: the z_open listener blocks uncancellably until a peer connects (an R2 non-blocking-accept item), and the binary-drop-in claim is qualified (architecturally sound because pico defines the owned-type ops as EXTERN symbols in api.c not static inline, but R1 validates only wz-to-wz loopback; real pico-binary interop is deferred to a cc round-trip). No behavior regression: both #[test]s green (2/2, 3x stable), clippy -D warnings + fmt clean, A3/validate_workspace consistent. NOT pushed (local; awaiting push consent).

The most damaging flagged item -- "z_put from inside a subscriber callback panics on Handle::block_on and poisons the driver mutex, killing the session" -- is REFUTED empirically: a new echo test publishes from within the callback and the sample is delivered; the reviewer traced pico's scouting/response send_blocking(block_on) path, but the unicast pub path enqueues via the writer channel (the same path the in-runtime drive loop uses, which is why it never panics). (3) z_open always-initializes its *zs out-param before any fallible work (pico contract). (4) Nine compile-time size_of static_asserts turn the byte-match claim into a build-enforced gate. Round 311y288.decision_summary: R311y288 -- api-compat-pico R2: non-blocking multi-peer listener (Option C). A 4-agent DESIGN review established that pico's listener holding up to Z_LISTEN_MAX_CONNECTION_NB=10 CONCURRENT inbound peers is pico's tested BASELINE (its own tests/z_test_peer_unicast.c pins it), not a superset -- so the naive single-peer non-blocking listener (Option B) would have shipped BELOW baseline, and no-cost-deferral pointed to Option C. Built (git y287 build + y288 IMPL-review fixes): z_open(listen) now binds and returns immediately with zero peers and no error, killing R1's uncancellable-hang divergence (R1 awaited the first peer inside a blocking open with no SessionState yet, so z_close could not interrupt it); wz_runtime_tokio::accept_loop (feature routing-accept, added to the crate's wz-runtime-tokio dep -- it is NOT in the default bundle) holds N concurrent inbound peers, each as a face. Because a wz unicast Session is one-peer-by-construction, the C z_owned_session_t handle is NOT a wz session but a face REGISTRY + subscription SSOT (new src/faces.rs); each face gets its OWN TokioSession+observer, which makes the per-peer keyexpr-alias id space unrepresentably-collidable rather than merely untested (a shared observer would conflate peer A's expr-id=7 with peer B's). declare-before-peer is the SSOT recorded unconditionally + replayed onto each face at FaceUp (pico accept.c:148-149); z_put/z_publisher_put fan out to every face; per-session random zid via getrandom (pico Z_ZID_LENGTH=16 default path, api.c:846-855) replacing R1's fixed per-role zid; Z_CONFIG_MODE_KEY honoured for the dial role (mode=peer -> dialing PEER, else CLIENT, pico session.c:120-140); connect+listen together rejected Z_ERR_INVALID (the dual-role listen+dial hybrid deferred, not silently dropped). A 3-agent IMPL review (concurrency / pico-fidelity / proof-honesty) found ONE HIGH blocker, fixed here: unsafe impl Sync for CClosure was unsound because the pubsub-allow-loop loopback drain runs the C callback on the CALLING (C app) thread, and per-face cells no longer serialized it against the drive thread's inbound dispatch -- two call(context) at once on one C context. Fixed by making the fan-out publishes Locality::Remote, which ALSO removed a second latent bug the review structure surfaced (a single z_put fired the one C callback once per face = N duplicate local deliveries); local self-delivery (Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_SUBSCRIBER, never implemented in this crate) is now a named deferred divergence. Also fixed from the fidelity review: publish_all iterates all faces best-effort (swallows per-face transient TransportUnavailable, surfaces only deterministic ExceedsCapacity, matching pico's discard-per-peer-send tx.c:92-95) rather than early-returning on the first face's error; declare_subscriber records the SSOT entry unconditionally (pico registers locally first, primitives.c:209-248) rather than discarding it when all live faces reject. NO inventory status change (api-compat-pico stayed active from R1); STRUCTURE/behavior refinement. NAMED divergences deferred: the 10-peer cap (an embedded static-array artifact; accept_loop is unbounded here, no hosted rationale to cap), the Z_CONFIG_SESSION_ZID_KEY override, local self-delivery, and the connect+listen dual-role hybrid. Reviews arbitrated by direct source read of both trees + falsification (forcing a single face made the multi-peer gate test fail with the exact cross-face-fanout message).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/faces.rs (NEW): SharedSession = face registry (BTreeMap<u64, FaceEntry>) + subscription SSOT (Vec<SubEntry>); CApiForwarder: FaceForwarder landing each accept_loop face in the registry (register->face_up builds a per-face TokioSession+observer and replays the SSOT; forward->dispatch into that face's session; deregister->face_down). publish_all fans out best-effort (swallows TransportUnavailable, surfaces ExceedsCapacity). declare_subscriber records the SSOT entry unconditionally. Locking: every C-invoking path (dispatch / drop) moves data out of the registry lock before calling into C (callback re-entrancy via z_put-in-callback is supported).

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: z_open(listen) binds via bind_endpoint and returns immediately, then runs accept_loop racing a cancellable shutdown (AtomicBool stop-latch + Notify); z_open(connect) dials one face (DIAL_FACE_ID). SessionState now holds Arc<SharedSession>. fresh_zid() (getrandom, 16 bytes) per session; None on entropy failure fails the open before the success signal. dial whatami from Z_CONFIG_MODE_KEY; connect+listen both set -> Z_ERR_INVALID. zp_*_task shims unchanged (pico-faithful).

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: CClosure is Arc-shared across per-face callbacks (C drop(context) fires once at refcount 0); make_subscriber_callback builds one wz callback per face from the shared closure; unsafe impl Sync justification rewritten around the single-drive-task + Remote-only-fan-out invariant. put_options() = Locality::Remote (no per-face loopback). z_put/z_publisher_put fan out via SharedSession::publish_all; z_declare_subscriber records the SSOT; SubscriberState::drop retracts via SharedSession::undeclare_subscriber.

A 4-agent DESIGN review established that pico's listener holding up to Z_LISTEN_MAX_CONNECTION_NB=10 CONCURRENT inbound peers is pico's tested BASELINE (its own tests/z_test_peer_unicast.c pins it), not a superset -- so the naive single-peer non-blocking listener (Option B) would have shipped BELOW baseline, and no-cost-deferral pointed to Option C. Built (git y287 build + y288 IMPL-review fixes): z_open(listen) now binds and returns immediately with zero peers and no error, killing R1's uncancellable-hang divergence (R1 awaited the first peer inside a blocking open with no SessionState yet, so z_close could not interrupt it); wz_runtime_tokio::accept_loop (feature routing-accept, added to the crate's wz-runtime-tokio dep -- it is NOT in the default bundle) holds N concurrent inbound peers, each as a face. Because a wz unicast Session is one-peer-by-construction, the C z_owned_session_t handle is NOT a wz session but a face REGISTRY + subscription SSOT (new src/faces.rs); each face gets its OWN TokioSession+observer, which makes the per-peer keyexpr-alias id space unrepresentably-collidable rather than merely untested (a shared observer would conflate peer A's expr-id=7 with peer B's). declare-before-peer is the SSOT recorded unconditionally + replayed onto each face at FaceUp (pico accept.c:148-149); z_put/z_publisher_put fan out to every face; per-session random zid via getrandom (pico Z_ZID_LENGTH=16 default path, api.c:846-855) replacing R1's fixed per-role zid; Z_CONFIG_MODE_KEY honoured for the dial role (mode=peer -> dialing PEER, else CLIENT, pico session.c:120-140); connect+listen together rejected Z_ERR_INVALID (the dual-role listen+dial hybrid deferred, not silently dropped). Fixed by making the fan-out publishes Locality::Remote, which ALSO removed a second latent bug the review structure surfaced (a single z_put fired the one C callback once per face = N duplicate local deliveries); local self-delivery (Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_SUBSCRIBER, never implemented in this crate) is now a named deferred divergence. NO inventory status change (api-compat-pico stayed active from R1); STRUCTURE/behavior refinement. NAMED divergences deferred: the 10-peer cap (an embedded static-array artifact; accept_loop is unbounded here, no hosted rationale to cap), the Z_CONFIG_SESSION_ZID_KEY override, local self-delivery, and the connect+listen dual-role hybrid. Reviews arbitrated by direct source read of both trees + falsification (forcing a single face made the multi-peer gate test fail with the exact cross-face-fanout message).

Round 311y289.decision_summary: R311y289 -- api-compat-pico R2 whole-session-review nit fixes. A 3-agent independent adversarial WHOLE-SESSION review of the cumulative origin/main..HEAD diff (R311y287 build + R311y288 IMPL-review fixes) returned SHIP across all three lenses (CI-hosted-green: no lane-coverage gap and no MCU/cross/QEMU/Zephyr/macOS/Windows lane builds the std-only cdylib, verified zero --workspace+--target combos; SSOT/ledger/honesty: frozen-ledger clean (56 insertions 0 deletions), every ledger claim binds to code, all four named divergences stated as divergences not mirrored, no SKIP-is-green trap; correctness/completeness: the y288 Locality::Remote fix genuinely removes the unsound C-thread callback path, the unsafe impl Sync justification holds, best-effort publish_all swallows exactly the one transient variant, entropy-failure fails cleanly for both roles, 7/7 tests pass). Two actionable LOW findings fixed here: (F1) SharedSession::undeclare_subscriber dropped the matched SSOT SubEntry -- which can hold the LAST Arc<CClosure> when no live face exists (a listener that never had a peer, or one whose per-face declares all failed) -- INSIDE the registry StdMutex via subs.retain(), so the C drop(context) could run under the lock and deadlock a drop that re-enters the session; fixed by removing the entry into a binding and dropping it after the lock scope, matching the module's own stated lock discipline (harmless for the tested N>=1-face paths, latent otherwise). (F2) z_declare_subscriber was infallible after the y288 SSOT-first change, so a non-canonical / pico-unsafe keyexpr (the **/c/* three-family bug) was silently recorded as a dead subscription reporting Z_OK -- a regression from R1, which surfaced the wz outbound-gate reject as an error; fixed by hoisting wz's own check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe gate (wz_runtime_tokio::keyexpr_canon, a standalone &str validator needing no peer) to the C boundary before recording the SSOT, returning Z_ERR_INVALID uniformly whether or not a peer is connected (the per-face declares are best-effort, so a per-face reject would otherwise be swallowed). A new gate test proves the reject AND that the moved closure is still consumed (C drop runs) on the reject path (consume-on-all-paths). F3 (no local self-delivery) is a named, sound divergence -- no change. LOW L1 (the api-compat-pico inventory reason prose is round-stamped R311y284 and now lags the R2 listener behavior -- honest, not false) is DEFERRED to a follow-up rather than risk an error-prone full-reason rewrite here; the Round 311y288 ledger entry documents the current R2 state. No behavior regression: 8/8 tests green (6 listener_multipeer + 2 pubsub_roundtrip), clippy -D warnings + fmt clean. Reviews arbitrated by direct source read of both trees.

Both the per-face subscribers and the SSOT entry now release outside the lock, so the C drop(context) never runs under the non-reentrant mutex.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: z_declare_subscriber now rejects a non-canonical/pico-unsafe keyexpr up front via wz_runtime_tokio::keyexpr_canon::check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe(&ke) -> Z_ERR_INVALID (the cclosure is already owned, so the early return drops it and runs the C drop -- consume-on-all-paths), before recording the SSOT. Restores R1's error-surfacing for invalid keyexprs, uniform across the peer/no-peer cases (per-face declares are best-effort and would otherwise swallow the reject).

The fix moves query's first drain inside the existing `if allows_local` block, preserving the local path's drain -> deliver_local_final -> drain ordering byte-for-byte; same for query_aliased. PROVABLY a no-op for the current tree: no existing caller passes Locality::Remote to query (every Locality::Remote in the tree is a PublishOptions), so the gate is true for every current call site. The owned-query + owned-reply families and z_query_take_from_loaned are LOUD-withheld -- pico's channel handlers are static inline (nm -D shows zero handler symbols; they compile into the USER's object and call z_query_take_from_loaned), so EXPORTING the owned family without a deferral seam makes every channel-based queryable compile, link and SILENTLY break, whereas withholding it yields an undefined-symbol link error -- loud, and the same round boundary R1 set. RULE: export owned-query <=> build the seam; R3 does neither. The seam is a NEW wz CORE concept for R3b: ReplyOut is a borrowed-&mut reply ACCUMULATOR (wz-session-core/src/query_sink.rs:123) whose with_responder/clear_responder/responder only stamp a responder IDENTITY (zid+eid), NOT detachment; nothing in the tree owns a responder past the callback and wz sends the ResponseFinal after the callback returns.

Mirror pico's api.c feature gates, not the header (the header declares all ops unconditionally). timeout_ms == 0 -> Z_GET_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 10000. Cross-face consolidation (AUTO resolves to LATEST, client-side) is a named divergence unless cheap.

Round 311y291.decision_summary: R311y291 -- R311y290 session-review fixes: a C1j build break + a CORRECTION of R311y290's false "provably a no-op" claim. A 3-agent independent adversarial session review of the unpushed R311y290 diff returned REVISE from all three lenses, converging on ONE build blocker and independently refuting one headline claim. (1) BUILD BREAK (absolute-priority class): the new regression test carried NO cfg gate while calling super::publish_common::build_loopback_sample, which is #[cfg(feature = "pubsub-allow-loop")] -- and run-ci Layer C1j compiles wz-runtime-tokio's TESTS under 10 consumer-plane subsets, NONE of which enable pubsub-allow-loop (run-ci.sh says so outright), so the lib-test target failed E0425 in every subset. R311y290's verification ran only `cargo test --lib` and Layer C1 -- both DEFAULT-features lanes where pubsub-allow-loop is ON -- so the lane that catches this class was never run: green-local-gate-is-not-green, one layer down. The pre-push hook runs the full sweep, so the push would have been BLOCKED (note the inversion: hosted ci.yml does not run C1j at all, so hosted would have been green -- C1j/C4c/C4d/C4e are push-gated but not hosted-gated, a pre-existing mirror gap this round did not create and does not fix). Fixed with #[cfg(all(feature = "query-get", feature = "declare-subscriber", feature = "pubsub-allow-loop"))]: pubsub-allow-loop is the COMPILE need, the other two are RUNTIME needs (both methods are signature-stable and return FeatureDisabled when off, so the test would compile and then fail at .expect / assert!(issued.is_ok())). Verified C1j pass AND that the test still RUNS in the default lane -- a cfg gate that silently deletes the test everywhere would itself be the a-SKIP-is-green trap. (2) FALSE CLAIM CORRECTED: R311y290's decision_summary and its code comment claimed "PROVABLY a no-op for the current tree: no existing caller passes Locality::Remote to query (every Locality::Remote in the tree is a PublishOptions)". FALSE, confirmed by direct read: with_allowed_destination (querier.rs:130) is the QUERY-side setter while with_locality (publish_common.rs:171) is the PUBLISH-side one -- two different methods -- and the R311y290 grep only searched the latter, missing ~19 in-tree TEST callers that do pass Locality::Remote to query/query_aliased/declare_querier. The claim was also self-refuting: R311y290's own new test IS a Remote query caller where the gate is false AND behaviour differs -- that difference is the falsification the entry cites as its proof. Two further counterexamples to the "every Remote is a PublishOptions" half are production but are not query callers (storage_aligner_service.rs:295 QueryableOptions, storage_replication_service.rs:283 SubscribeOptions). The CONCLUSION survives -- no in-tree PRODUCTION caller passes Remote to query, and the ~19 test callers stage nothing before the drain, so draining an empty queue left the gate observably inert (294/294 lib, 72/72 query-filtered) -- but that is an EMPIRICAL result, not a proof, and not even a static guarantee: GroupOptions::with_get_locality (group.rs:145) and AdvancedSubscriberOptions::get_locality (advanced_subscriber.rs:287/344) are PUBLIC knobs that forward a user-settable Locality into query, which no grep can see. Per frozen-ledger the R311y290 entry is not rewritten (there is also no primitive to rewrite one -- append is the only mutate path, and a direct JSON edit is anti-pattern #8); this entry is the correction, and the false sentence baked into session/mod.rs was fixed in source (comments are not frozen). Also corrected: R311y290 said "z_put (their only C-thread path)" -- z_publisher_put is a second one; both ride put_options() = Locality::Remote, so the safety conclusion holds but "only" was wrong. (3) NAMED, NOT FIXED (R3 design input): Session::sweep_expired_queries (mod.rs:961-970) drains UNGATED at :968 and is pub -- so R3's planned sweep, if spawned as its own task per the wz-rest precedent, would run a face's subscriber CClosure::call on the sweep thread concurrently with the drive task, re-opening through a different door the exact race R311y290 closed for z_get (the precedent is sound for wz-rest only because Rust closures are Send+Sync; a C context is not). R3 must drive the sweep FROM the drive task, or gate that drain the way R311y290 gated query's. Recorded in the api-compat-pico plan. Adversarial cross-check that HELD: a reviewer tried to refute R311y290's rationale via DeferredListenerCell's backlog serialization and could not -- the backlog serializes per CELL, and each face registers the SAME Arc<CClosure> into its OWN session (hence its own cell) while drain runs jobs OUTSIDE the mutex, so two concurrent call(context) on one C context is genuinely reachable.

Round 311y292.decision_summary: R311y292 -- api-compat-pico R3a: the QUERYABLE (responder) half of the pico query plane, built as a SECOND SSOT in the C session registry and proven over the wire against a wz-native querier. The R3 design (settled by a prior 3-agent DESIGN review that returned REVISE/REVISE/MUST-EXPAND) scoped get+queryable as one round; this round ships the queryable half, because the mid-round finding was that the two halves have DIFFERENT readiness: the queryable half needs no new upstream concept, while the get half needs a reply-registry sweep whose only sound driver is the drive task (the R311y291 session-review Finding 3 -- Session::sweep_expired_queries drains UNGATED at session/mod.rs:968, so a separate sweep task would run a face's C callback on the sweep thread and re-open, through a different door, the exact race R311y290 closed for z_get). Splitting there keeps every commit proven rather than shipping an untested intermediate. WHAT LANDED: faces.rs gains qbls (the responder SSOT) + FaceEntry.queryables, replayed onto every face by face_up exactly as the subscription SSOT is (pico declare-before-peer); a new src/query.rs exports the closure_query family, z_declare_queryable / z_declare_background_queryable / z_undeclare_queryable + the 7 no-copy ownership ops, z_queryable_keyexpr, the loaned-query accessors, and z_query_reply / _del / _err with their options structs. DESIGN CALLS, each grounded by direct read: (1) replies ACCUMULATE in the query marshal and flush into the wz ReplyOut when the C callback returns -- observably identical because wz's own QueryResponder already only accumulates into a Vec<QueryReply> that into_response drains (wz-session-core/src/query.rs:884-895, read to verify rather than cited from the design note), and it avoids erasing a &mut dyn ReplyOut lifetime through a transmute; (2) the marshal carries an AtomicBool valid flag cleared before the frame returns, so a stashed pointer is a loud Z_ERR_INVALID rather than a silent write -- Atomic not Cell because a Cell read from another C thread would itself be UB; (3) option structs mirror pico's api.c FEATURE GATES, not its header -- Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE defaults to 0 (CMakeLists.txt:353), so z_queryable_options_t is { bool complete; } with no allowed_origin. TWO LOUD WITHHOLDS (undefined symbol = link error, the R1 precedent; a stub would be a silent lie): the owned-query family + z_query_take_from_loaned (pico's channel handlers are static inline and call it from the USER's object, so exporting it without the retained-responder seam wz lacks would make every channel-based queryable link and silently fail), and z_query_encoding (needs the encoding type family, a separate round). ONE NAMED DIVERGENCE: z_query_reply_del with a keyexpr DIFFERENT from the query's returns Z_ERR_INVALID -- wz's ReplyOut::reply_del takes no keyexpr and always emits under the bound key, so the faithful shape is unrepresentable; a loud reject beats replying under the wrong key. Inventory UNCHANGED (api-compat-pico stays active; R3a adds no cfg gate).

NEXT = R3b, the GET half (z_get + the reply fan + the sweep). The design is settled and recorded in the session plan; the whole remaining risk is the SWEEP. Its shape is NOT yet decided and must not be guessed: Session::sweep_expired_queries (wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs:961-970) drains UNGATED at :968 and is pub, so a sweep task on its own thread would run a face's subscriber CClosure::call on the SWEEP thread concurrently with the drive task -- re-opening through a different door the exact race R311y290 closed for z_get. The wz-rest / ap-demo tokio::spawn(loop{sleep;sweep}) precedent is sound THERE only because Rust closures are Send+Sync; it is NOT sound for a C callback context. So the sweep must be driven BY the drive task. A promising shape found this round by direct read but NOT yet built or reviewed: drive_session_until_terminal already select!s the link poll against a clock.sleep wake arm and calls on_event on every lease/keepalive wake (session_glue.rs:807-867), and wz-capi-pico ALREADY passes its dispatch closure as that on_event -- so the sweep could ride the existing drive-thread callback with no upstream change. The open question is CADENCE: the loop wakes on the lease/keepalive deadline (lease_ms=10_000 here), while pico's is 1000 ms, so a get with timeout_ms=1000 could fire its final late. The textbook fix is likely to teach the drive loop's wake deadline about the reply-registry deadline (an upstream change); the alternative the design named was gating sweep_expired_queries' drain the way R311y290 gated query's. DECIDE THIS WITH A DESIGN REVIEW BEFORE CODING -- it is exactly the class the R3 DESIGN review already caught twice.

R3b also carries, from the settled design: completion = the Arc<CReplyClosure> REFCOUNT alone, NOT an AtomicUsize counter (a dead face's Pending is dropped, not swept, and dropping it never fires on_final -- so any N-final counter hangs forever on face death); the C thread must hold its OWN Arc guard across the whole fan loop; fan the get OUTSIDE the registry lock (the publish_all snapshot pattern) with Locality::Remote.

UPSTREAM DEBT surfaced by R3a (new, not previously tracked): wz's ReplyOut has no keyed Del -- reply_del() takes no keyexpr and always emits under the responder's bound key, while pico's z_query_reply_del accepts an arbitrary one. R3a rejects the differing-keyexpr case with Z_ERR_INVALID (loud) rather than replying under the wrong key. Closing it needs a reply_keyed_del on the wz-session-core seam + its codec arm -- an upstream round. The sibling reply_keyed / reply_keyed_stamped / reply_keyed_encoded family already exists for the Put form, so the Del gap is an asymmetry in that family, not a missing concept.

STILL WITHHELD after R3a (loud, re-openable, both named in src/query.rs's module doc): the owned-query family + z_query_take_from_loaned (needs a retained-responder + deferred-final concept in wz-session-core -- ReplyOut's with_responder only stamps a responder IDENTITY, it does not detach one, and wz sends the ResponseFinal once the callback returns); z_query_encoding (needs the encoding type family).

Round 311y294.decision_summary: R311y294 -- api-compat-pico R3a review remediation: the 3-agent IMPL review of R311y292 returned MUST-REVISE from all three lenses (unsafe-soundness / pico-faithfulness / SSOT-structure), and this round closes every finding plus corrects two FALSE claims R311y292 froze into the ledger. Direct read arbitrated throughout, and it overruled a reviewer once. THE ROOT PATTERN across the findings: R3a stated correct principles and then did not apply them -- the reviewers' phrase, and it holds. FIXED HERE. (1) FIDELITY, the big one: pico ENFORCES zenoh's reply-subset-of-query contract -- `!query->_anyke && !_z_declared_keyexpr_intersects(&query->_key, keyexpr)` -> _Z_ERR_KEYEXPR_NOT_MATCH (src/net/primitives.c:437-440) -- while R311y292's comment asserted the OPPOSITE ("pico lets the queryable pass any keyexpr") and forwarded any key with Z_OK. Now enforced. The `_anyke` half needed no upstream change once read properly: it is not a wire field but a SELECTOR PARAMETER (Z_SELECTOR_QUERY_MATCH "_anyke", api/constants.h:18) -- the sender appends it when accept_replies==Z_REPLY_KEYEXPR_ANY (codec/message.c:399-423), reception forces _implicit_anyke=false (codec/message.c:488-490), so the responder derivation collapses to `_anyke = _z_parameters_has_anyke(parameters)` (net/query.h:104), and QueryView::parameters() already carries them. pico's boundary-checked parse is ported verbatim (query_params.c:46-70). (2) The related z_query_reply_del STRING-EQUALITY reject was the wildcard-match-by-equality anti-pattern breaking the COMMON case (a wildcard queryable's query key is a PATTERN), and R311y292 dressed it as a "named divergence" whose stated cost was FALSE -- the reviewer proved the codec arm needs NO change, so wz-session-core gained send_reply_keyed_del + the ReplyOut::reply_keyed_del default (~10 lines, the Del-arm mirror of the Put arm's long-existing keyed family). It was a cost-deferral wearing a divergence's clothes; the seam is built and the divergence is GONE. (3) SOUNDNESS made mechanical: queryable_options now pins Locality::Remote. Locality::Any::allows_local() is TRUE (locality.rs:70-72), so an Any queryable would have made `unsafe impl Sync for CQueryClosure` FALSE the moment R3b's z_get lands with default locality -- a C-thread get would drain a local queryable job on the C thread while a drive thread ran call on another face, the exact unsound-Sync bug R311y288 fixed on the publish plane. R311y292's faces.rs doc argued FOR Any in the same commit whose Sync impl depended on local never happening. Remote is also pico-FAITHFUL: Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE defaults to 0 (CMakeLists.txt:353). (4) The moved options->attachment was LEAKED and silently dropped (z_bytes_* IS exported, so a C program can build one) -- now consumed on every path and carried via ReplyOut::reply_keyed_attached. (5) Two more FALSE comments corrected: a NULL reply keyexpr does NOT mean "reply under the query's key" (pico has no null handling and SEGFAULTS) -- now a defined Z_ERR_NULL; and congestion_control's default is Z_CONGESTION_CONTROL_BLOCK=1 (api.c:2118,2181), not 0 (=DROP). (6) The valid/AtomicBool tripwire is REMOVED: its doc claimed multi-threaded C while the sibling UnsafeCell doc claimed pico's single-thread contract -- mutually exclusive anchors -- and with a callback-scoped marshal the flag can never usefully fire, since after the frame dies READING it is the use-after-free it meant to catch. It documented a protection that did not exist. (7) z_query_accepts_replies EXPORTED (it is the _anyke accessor governing #1, and was missing); z_query_source_info disclosed as withheld (needs the source-info family). DIRECT READ OVERRULED THE REVIEWER on z_queryable_id: it is #if defined(Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API) (primitives.h:2884) which defaults 0 (CMakeLists.txt:316), so a default build has no such symbol and it is NOT a missing export. (8) SSOT: session_state deduplicated into session.rs (it cast types owned by neither pubsub nor query); CClosure/CQueryClosure unified onto ONE generic ffi::CClosure<C> owning the drop-once Drop, with Sync deliberately NOT blanket-implemented so each plane still writes its own proof and R3b's reply plane cannot inherit one silently. (9) NO-FLAKY-EVER: the wire test's 300ms-sleep + single-query bet replaced by the sibling pubsub_roundtrip's bounded convergence loop (a get is idempotent, so re-asking is convergence on declaration propagation, not a retry-pass); it now finishes in 0.10s instead of always burning 5.00s. Inventory UNCHANGED (no cfg gate added).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/query.rs: parameters_has_anyke (pico's boundary-checked selector parse, query_params.c:46-70) + reply_keyexpr_is_covered (the !_anyke && !intersects gate, routed through the keyexpr_match SSOT -- never string equality); QueryMarshal gains `anyke`, derived at marshal time; z_query_reply / _del now enforce coverage and return the EXACT pico code Z_ERR_KEYEXPR_NOT_MATCH; both consume options->attachment on every path (z_query_reply carries it via reply_keyed_attached; the Del arm takes-and-drops, a named gap); a NULL reply keyexpr is Z_ERR_NULL, not a silent substitution; the valid/AtomicBool tripwire REMOVED with the honest callback-scope contract documented; z_query_accepts_replies + z_reply_keyexpr_t/Z_REPLY_KEYEXPR_* exported; congestion_control/priority defaults via the new Z_CONGESTION_CONTROL_BLOCK=1 / Z_PRIORITY_DEFAULT=5 consts; PendingReply::Del carries a keyexpr; CQueryClosure is now a ffi::CClosure alias keeping its own unsafe impl Sync.

crates/wz-session-core/src/query.rs + query_sink.rs: NEW QueryResponder::send_reply_keyed_del + the ReplyOut::reply_keyed_del trait method (defaulting to reply_del, so every existing impl stays valid) -- the Del-arm mirror of the Put arm's keyed family, closing the asymmetry that a wildcard-answering queryable could not retract a concrete key. No codec change: into_response's Del arm already encodes under the record's keyexpr_literal.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: `pub use wz_session_core::keyexpr_match;` on the keyexpr_canon precedent -- an AP consumer needing "does A intersect B?" must reach the ONE matcher rather than re-derive it.
crates/wz-capi-pico/src/faces.rs: queryable_options pins Locality::Remote (soundness made mechanical + pico-faithful per Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE=0); the doc that argued the opposite is replaced.
crates/wz-capi-pico/src/ffi.rs: NEW generic CClosure<C> owning the {context, call, drop} shape + the one panic-guarded drop-once Drop; Sync deliberately left to per-plane concrete impls.
crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: session_state lands here (beside both types it casts) with a # Safety doc; the byte-identical copies in pubsub.rs + query.rs are gone.
crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: CClosure is now a ffi::CClosure alias keeping its own unsafe impl Sync; z_internal_closure_sample_check gained the panic guard its query sibling already had.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/lib.rs: byte-compat guard gains z_query_reply_options_t == 40 + z_query_reply_del_options_t == 32 -- the two whose layout is Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API-conditional, and so the two most likely to drift.
crates/wz-capi-pico/tests/queryable_roundtrip.rs: the fixed-sleep bet replaced by a bounded query-until-received convergence loop racing the pump.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-capi-pico: 13/13 pass (3 lib unit + 6 listener_multipeer + 2 pubsub_roundtrip + 2 queryable_roundtrip); wz-session-core 207/207; wz-runtime-tokio 294/294 (the reply_keyed_del trait default is additive, so no existing ReplyOut impl changed).

FALSIFIED, and the falsification CHANGED the fix: the first gate for the R311y293 dangling-handle bug asserted the payload BYTES read back correctly -- and it PASSED with the bug deliberately restored, because the dead frame still held the old Vec. Rewritten to assert the ADDRESS invariant (bind_points_the_cached_views_at_this_marshals_own_fields), it FAILS on the same falsification with a 208-byte delta (the exact struct move) and passes when fixed. Reading a dangling pointer is UB that routinely appears to work; only the address is deterministic. Recorded as a durable lesson.

New unit gates, both binding to the fidelity fix: anyke_parses_with_picos_parameter_boundary_rules (asserts the decoys "no_anyke" / "_anykey=1" / "xx_anyke_yy" are NOT read as the flag -- the boundary rules are what make it a parse, not a substring search -- and that a real flag after a decoy is still found); reply_coverage_is_intersection_not_string_equality (asserts a/** covers a/b, which the R311y292 string-equality cut REJECTED, and that _anyke short-circuits a disjoint reply exactly as pico's !_anyke && !intersects does).
cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings on all 3 touched crates: CLIPPY_EXIT=0. cargo fmt --all --check: FMT_EXIT=0.
run-ci.sh --layer A3: pass -- atoms=212 active=132 UNCHANGED (R311y294 adds no cfg gate); REMAINING WORK = 7.

Every fidelity claim above re-verified by direct read of ~/zenoh-pico this round, not carried from the review: primitives.c:437-440 (the enforced gate), net/query.h:104 (the _anyke derivation), codec/message.c:488-490 (why reception forces implicit=false), query_params.c:46-70 (the boundary rules), constants.h:18 / :216 / :247-250, CMakeLists.txt:316 (UNSTABLE_API=0) + :353 (LOCAL_QUERYABLE=0), primitives.h:2884 (the z_queryable_id gate that overruled the reviewer).
carry_forward_bullets: R311y294 = the R3a review remediation: every IMPL-review finding closed, and two FALSE claims R311y292 froze are corrected here (frozen-ledger: a new entry, never a rewrite). CORRECTION 1 -- R311y292's changes_bullets said "query.rs (NEW, ~700 lines)"; it was 941 at that commit. Estimated instead of measured; use wc -l. CORRECTION 2 -- R311y292's carry said closing the Del-keyexpr gap "needs a reply_keyed_del on the wz-session-core seam + its codec arm"; the codec arm claim is FALSE (into_response's Del arm already encodes under the record's keyexpr_literal, wz-session-core/src/query.rs:487-493), and the whole fix was ~10 lines. That inflated cost is what made the deferral look justified -- the tell was R311y292's own words, "an asymmetry in that family, not a missing concept". Contrast the owned-query withhold, which genuinely needs a NEW concept and remains a real divergence.

R3a is now COMPLETE and reviewed-clean. NEXT = R3b, the GET half. The design is settled (see the session plan memory); the whole remaining risk is the SWEEP, and it is NOT yet decided -- do not guess it. Session::sweep_expired_queries (wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs:961-970) drains UNGATED at :968 and is pub, so a sweep task on its own thread would run a face's C callback on the SWEEP thread concurrently with the drive task, re-opening through a different door the race R311y290 closed. The wz-rest / ap-demo tokio::spawn(loop{sleep;sweep}) precedent is sound THERE only because Rust closures are Send+Sync. So the sweep must be driven BY the drive task. Promising shape found by direct read but NOT built or reviewed: drive_session_until_terminal already select!s the link poll against a clock.sleep wake arm and calls on_event on every lease/keepalive wake (session_glue.rs:807-867), and wz-capi-pico ALREADY passes its dispatch closure as that on_event -- so the sweep could ride the existing drive-thread callback with no upstream change. Open question is CADENCE (the loop wakes on the lease/keepalive deadline, lease_ms=10_000 here, vs pico's 1000 ms, so a get with timeout_ms=1000 could fire its final late); the textbook fix may be teaching the drive loop's wake deadline about the reply-registry deadline. DECIDE WITH A DESIGN REVIEW BEFORE CODING.

R3b also carries, from the settled design: completion = the Arc<CReplyClosure> REFCOUNT alone, NOT an AtomicUsize counter (a dead face's Pending is dropped, not swept, and dropping it never fires on_final, so any N-final counter hangs forever on face death); the C thread must hold its OWN Arc guard across the whole fan loop; fan the get OUTSIDE the registry lock (the publish_all snapshot pattern) with Locality::Remote. R3b's reply closure gets a THIRD ffi::CClosure<C> instantiation and MUST write its own unsafe impl Sync -- the generic deliberately does not blanket-grant it.

STILL WITHHELD after R3a (loud = link error, re-openable, all named in src/query.rs's module doc): the owned-query family + z_query_take_from_loaned (needs a retained-responder + deferred-final concept in wz-session-core -- ReplyOut::with_responder only stamps a responder IDENTITY, it does not detach one, and wz sends the ResponseFinal once the callback returns); z_query_encoding (encoding family); z_query_source_info (source-info family). NOT a gap: z_queryable_id is Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API-gated (default 0), so a default pico build has no such symbol.

NAMED GAPS in the reply options, both dropped rather than silently mis-honoured: is_express (wz's ReplyOut has no express arm on any reply form -- a batching hint, no delivery/content effect) and the Del arm's attachment (consumed so nothing leaks, but wz's Del reply carries none). Local self-delivery for queryables is now an explicit divergence too (queryable_options pins Locality::Remote), matching pico's Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE=0 default.

Round 311y295.decision_summary: R311y295 -- correct R268's stale cancel-safety rationale on drive_session_until_terminal. DOC-only; no code, no behavior, no inventory change. Surfaced by the R3b DESIGN review and then arbitrated by direct read, which went FURTHER than the review did. R268 removed the per-iteration on_tick hook and justified it two ways: (a) YAGNI -- every caller passed a no-op, so it was dead surface; (b) a HAZARD -- "sub-second sweep cadence belongs in a peer task that does not race poll_and_dispatch_one (which is not cancel-safe for length-prefixed drivers -- cancelling between the u16 length read and the payload read drops captured bytes)". Reason (a) stands and is untouched. Reason (b) is FALSE as of R311et and is corrected. Two independent falsifiers, both direct-read: (1) the ONE length-prefixed driver was FIXED -- R311et hoisted the partial-read buffers into &mut self (ReadState, lib.rs:1321-1339) over cancel-safe AsyncReadExt::read, and its own doc (lib.rs:1309-1318) names R264's "sub-second sweep cadence inside drive_session_until_terminal race-cancelled poll_and_dispatch_one 10x/s" as the fixture that surfaced it -- so the hazard R268 cites is precisely the hazard R311et closed, and two files in one crate have contradicted each other since; (2) NO OTHER driver is length-prefixed -- udp_pipeline:179 / ws_pipeline:138 / quic_datagram_pipeline:127 are datagram flows with no reassembly (ws's own comment says "datagram flow, no length-prefix reassembly"), serial_pipeline:282-288 documents its own cancel-safety ("Cancel-safe: the only .await is the single read... a dropped read consumes no bytes"), and quic_pipeline:102 delegates inward -- so the clause never applied to them at all. This is stronger than the review's position, which conservatively verified only TCP and proposed relying on capi-pico being TCP-only as containment-by-convention; direct read shows no containment is needed because the hazard class is empty. Also recorded: cancellation is neither new nor hypothetical -- this loop's own tokio::select! (session_glue.rs:811-867) ALREADY drops an in-flight poll_and_dispatch_one on every lease/keepalive wake, so a finer wake deadline changes that cancellation's FREQUENCY, not its correctness. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROUND rather than a comment fixed in passing: the stale prose was not inert. It had already propagated -- it shaped this session's own R3b carry ("poll_and_dispatch_one is not cancel-safe, so do not just add a select! arm"), steering the next round away from the correct shape toward a sweep task that would be UNSOUND for a C-ABI callback context. A false rationale in a doc that a future round must consult is a trap, and it fires exactly when someone trusts the codebase. R268's live clause ("can re-introduce a similar hook when an actual consumer materialises") is preserved and now points a future consumer at folding its deadline into the loop's existing wake min.

Round 311y296.decision_summary: R311y296 -- api-compat-pico R3b: the get (querier) half of the pico query plane, plus the drive-loop seam it needed. New crates/wz-capi-pico/src/get.rs exports z_get / z_get_with_parameters_substr, z_get_options_t (+ _default), the z_closure_reply ownership family, the loaned-reply accessors (z_reply_is_ok / _ok / _err / _err_payload), the target + consolidation enums, and pico's 7 query-option constructors; pubsub.rs gains z_sample_kind (load-bearing once R3a's z_query_reply_del can answer a get). COMPLETION is the shared Arc<CReplyClosure> REFCOUNT alone, never a finals counter: a dead face's pending entry is DROPPED not swept, so it fires no final and any counter hangs forever, while the refcount ends the get uniformly and promptly on a real final / timeout sweep / face death / per-face issue error / zero faces; the C thread holds its own clone across the fan loop so face 1's early final cannot complete the get mid-fan. The sweep rides the EXISTING on_event drive-thread callback (SharedSession::dispatch) -- structurally, not by convention: the drive future is !Send (the SCE Engine owns bare Box<dyn FnMut()>), so a per-face sweep task cannot compile, while it would compile and be unsound. The DESIGN plan's fold-the-deadline-into-the-wake-min was NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and the test caught it at 3.11s (exactly the ~3333ms keepalive cadence): z_get runs while the loop is already parked in select! on the OLD deadline, so next_extra_deadline() is not re-read until that wake. ExtraDeadline therefore carries BOTH halves -- next_ms plus a revised Notify -- and the loop gained a precondition-gated re-arm branch; revised is Option so tokio never constructs the future for the ~97 pre-existing callers, keeping the delegation genuinely free rather than costing them 2 waiter-lock acquisitions per frame. drive_session_until_terminal keeps its exact signature (all ~97 call sites untouched) and delegates. 3-agent adversarial IMPL review: the Sync proof and the whole upstream seam (min equivalence, select fairness, cancel-safety, cfg parity, CLOCK EPOCH on both roles) were independently verified CLEAN; 8 real defects were found and ALL are fixed. Chief among them, honestly: consolidation. get.rs claimed the mode was "honoured" and the AUTO resolution "ported" -- FALSE. pico's LATEST suppresses the per-reply callback entirely and flushes a keyexpr-deduped cache at the last final (query.c:178-181, 143-172, 239-247), and AUTO defaults to LATEST, so the gap is the DEFAULT get path: pico delivers one reply where wz delivers two. It is NOT fixed here because it is a wz CORE gap, not a binding one -- Session::query already takes with_consolidation, so wz's own Rust API has it too -- and the inventory's query-consolidation atom was itself asserting C=indep reply dedup, a behaviour no code implements. That SSOT claim is corrected, the divergence is named at every site that touched it, and the core build is a design-review-first follow-up blocked on two real seams (a ReplyView timestamp the wire decode discards; a BoundedVec-safe per-pending cache for the no_std MCU profile). Every gate was FALSIFIED, not merely observed green.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/get.rs (NEW, ~1100 lines): the querier plane. z_get + z_get_with_parameters_substr (the latter is the real body; z_get is pico's own strlen delegation, api.c:1743-1746); z_get_options_t = the DEFAULT-build layout (64 B / align 8 compile-time asserted -- allowed_destination is Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE-gated and source_info/cancellation_token Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API-gated, all 0 by default); z_get_options_default mirroring api.c:1723-1741 (accept_replies = MATCHING_QUERY not ANY; congestion = BLOCK not DROP); the z_closure_reply family (24 B, non-const reply ptr per session.h:159 + examples/unix/c11/z_get.c:35); z_reply_is_ok / _ok / _err / _err_payload; the target + consolidation enums (AUTO = -1); pico's 7 ungated query-option constructors (z_query_target_default, z_reply_keyexpr_default, z_query_consolidation_auto/latest/monotonic/none/default, api.c:442-462) -- six sit in the basic z_get flow and the crate's own docs cited two of them as the authority for the defaults while not exporting them.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/get.rs: get_timeout_ms applies pico's timeout_ms==0 -> Z_GET_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT=10000 rewrite (api.c:1762-1764), saturating u64->u32. Routing C's 0 into wz's timeout_ms=0 would mean the OPPOSITE (deadline_ms=None, never expires) and the get's completion would never fire. transmit_parameters ports pico's implicit-_anyke append (primitives.c:575-578 + codec/message.c:399-425), making wz's plain parameters bytes byte-identical to pico's encode with no implicit_anyke concept upstream. ReplyGate ports the RECEIVE half (query.c:121): !anyke && !intersects -> the reply is dropped before the C callback sees it, routed through R3a's reply_keyexpr_is_covered so the two halves cannot drift. get_options pins Locality::Remote (fidelity AND the mechanical half of the Sync proof) and ports pico's client-side AUTO resolution (_time= -> NONE else LATEST, unanchored _z_strstr per string.c:75-79, so a decoy matches -- fidelity, not a bug).

crates/wz-session-core/src/reply.rs: ReplyRegistry::next_deadline_ms() -> Option<u64> (additive; deadline_ms is private and no accessor existed) + 2 unit tests (earliest-wins regardless of insertion order, None entries impose no wake, re-arm after a sweep).
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: Session::next_reply_deadline_ms(), query-get-gated exactly like its sibling sweep_expired_queries.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: new ExtraDeadline { next_ms, revised: Option<&Notify> } + drive_session_until_terminal_with_extra_deadline, folding the caller deadline into the EXISTING (lease_dl, ka_dl) min and adding a precondition-gated re-arm select branch. drive_session_until_terminal keeps its signature and delegates with next_ms=||None / revised=None, so all ~97 call sites are untouched and pay nothing per iteration. R268's hook was pre-authorised for exactly this consumer (y295 corrected its stale cancel-safety reason).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/accept_loop.rs: FaceForwarder::next_extra_deadline_ms + deadline_revised, both default-None (the tick_period extension-point precedent); drive_face threads them. drive_joined_face stays on the plain drive (a joined link shares the primary's session and is never registered as its own face), so the plain fn's import is cfg(any(test, transport-multilink)).

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/faces.rs: SharedSession::dispatch now sweeps (the on_event drive-thread path for BOTH roles -- the only thread a C closure may run on; sweep_expired_queries' drain is UNGATED, so the caller is the whole safety argument); next_reply_deadline_ms + deadline_revised + face_sessions_with_wake; per-face revised Notify; face_sessions dedups publish_all's snapshot. NEW clear_faces() -- pico's _z_session_close -> _z_flush_pending_queries (utils.c:194).

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: SessionState::close() calls clear_faces AFTER joining the driver, so z_close ENDS every in-flight get and a get issued after z_close sees an empty peer set instead of hanging forever. The accept loop's shutdown never deregisters its faces (deregister runs only in Step::Driven), so the listen role leaked where the dial role already did the right thing -- identical C code completed on connect and hung on listen. drive_dial threads its own ExtraDeadline (it does not go through accept_loop).

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: SampleMarshal refactored to R3a's proven new()+bind()-at-the-final-address shape and shared with the reply plane (z_reply_ok must hand back a z_loaned_sample_t); new z_sample_kind + z_sample_kind_t. R1 shipped only keyexpr/payload because pub/sub had no Del to observe; R3a's z_query_reply_del made that a hole the moment the planes composed.

crates/wz-capi-pico/Cargo.toml: query-timeout selected EXPLICITLY. query-get does NOT imply it (the edge runs query-timeout = [query-get]), so with_timeout_ms is a signature-stable NO-OP without it -- and losing it is SILENT: the crate still compiles, the get_timeout_ms unit test still passes, and every get to a silent peer simply never completes. Contrast sweep_expired_queries, which is query-get-gated and fails loudly.
crates/wz-capi-pico/tests/get_roundtrip.rs (NEW): 7 e2e gates against a wz-native far end. docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json: the query-consolidation inventory reason corrected.
verification_bullets: wz-capi-pico 25/25 green: 8 unit + 7 get e2e + 6 listener_multipeer + 2 pubsub_roundtrip + 2 queryable_roundtrip. R1/R2/R3a all unchanged (no regression).
Upstream regression across the ~97 drive_session_until_terminal call sites: wz-runtime-tokio 294/294, wz-session-core 207/207.

EVERY new gate was FALSIFIED, not merely observed green. (a) Remove the dispatch sweep -> c_get_completes_at_its_timeout FAILS. (b) The re-arm signal was falsified BEFORE it existed: the same test failed at 3.114s, which is exactly the ~3333ms keepalive cadence (adopted_lease_ms/3, LEASE_EXPIRE_FACTOR=3 at lease.rs:20, capi lease_ms=10_000) -- i.e. the fold-into-min alone does not re-read the deadline while the loop is parked. (c) Neuter clear_faces' body -> c_close_completes_an_in_flight_get FAILS with its own message.

The timeout gate binds on BOTH halves of ExtraDeadline by construction: bounds [400ms, 2500ms) for a 500ms timeout, where without next_ms OR without revised the completion lands at ~3113ms. An independent reviewer re-derived both numbers and confirmed the margin only widens under load (the without-hook time is timer-driven), so it is not flaky in the dangerous direction; the lower bound is safe to sub-ms (now_monotonic_ms floors).

Both ROLES are gated separately: c_get_completes_at_its_timeout (listen, via the FaceForwarder hooks) and c_dialed_get_completes_at_its_timeout (connect, via drive_dial's own hand-rolled wiring). Either can regress alone and the Option-threading means a missing signal no longer degrades silently.

The other 5 gates: happy path (reply lands + exactly one completion + NOT on the timeout); face death (peer's socket closes -> face_down; bound 2s, deliberately below the ~9800ms lease fallback so a socket-close regression cannot pass via lease expiry); z_close ends an in-flight get AND a post-close get completes immediately; zero faces (immediate, reply cb never fires, 30s timeout unused); multi-face (both replies, ONE completion -- pins the C thread's fan-loop Arc guard).

The reply callback RECORDS failures instead of asserting: fire_reply's catch_unwind (required -- unwinding across extern "C" is UB) would swallow a panic and report the indistinguishable "no reply arrived". This was not theoretical: it hid a type-confusion in the first cut of the test's own payload read.

clippy -D warnings clean on all 3 touched crates (--all-targets); cargo fmt --all applied. run-ci Layer A3 pass: atoms=212 active=132, REMAINING WORK=7 unchanged (R3b adds no cfg gate; api-compat-pico was already active). run-ci Layer C1w pass (routing-accept accept_loop). validate_workspace: T1 orphan new=+0 (ledger=13 unchanged), style unchanged (T3 warn=4 / T4 info=4).

Direct read is the arbiter throughout: every pico constant, layout, gate and semantic was verified against ~/zenoh-pico rather than taken from memory or from the reviewers. Two reviewer findings were confirmed by reading pico myself before acting (query.c:121 the reply filter; query.c:178-181 the LATEST callback suppression); the pico timeout sweep was found to be a 1000ms fixed poll (query.c:64-69), so the deadline-driven re-arm is a superset, not a mirror.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y296 = api-compat-pico R3b (get), the last of the R3 split. R1 (binary drop-in pub/sub) + R2 (non-blocking multi-peer listener) + R3a (queryable) + R3b (get) are all BUILT and 3-agent-IMPL-reviewed. The api-compat-pico TRACK's core is now closed; what remains on it is the withheld set below, not a missing plane.

NEXT (highest value, design-review-first): wz-CORE consolidation. The inventory's query-consolidation atom is active and, until this round, claimed C=indep reply dedup -- a behaviour NO code implements. wz only transmits the Q_C wire ext. pico's LATEST suppresses the per-reply callback entirely, dedups by keyexpr keeping the newest timestamp, and flushes at the last final (query.c:143-181, 239-247), and AUTO resolves to LATEST absent a _time= selector, so this is the DEFAULT get path: pico delivers ONE reply where wz delivers two. This is NOT a capi-pico gap -- Session::query already takes with_consolidation, so wz's own Rust API is equally unfaithful, and the fix belongs in ReplyRegistry (where pico puts it). Blocked on 2 real core seams: (1) a ReplyView TIMESTAMP -- the wire decode has it and discards it (reply.rs, `timestamp: _`) -- without which "keep the newest" is undecidable; (2) a BoundedVec-safe per-pending reply cache the no_std MCU profile can carry. Under the Arc-refcount completion design the flush must run in a Drop that fires `call` for each cached reply BEFORE drop(context). MONOTONIC is NOT part of this (pico's drop flag gates only its cache, never the callback -- wz matches). Do NOT bolt this onto the binding.

A3 grammar note for that round: query-consolidation stays `active` (the Q_C ext IS a real cfg knob, so invariant #3 holds) -- the grammar cannot express "active but half-built" (PARTIAL requires reserved, and reserved requires zero cfg sites). If that is judged a real gap in the model, it is a separate audit round, not a status hack.

R3b's own NAMED DIVERGENCES (re-openable): (a) consolidation apply-half, above. COMPLETION is the shared Arc<CReplyClosure> REFCOUNT alone, never a finals counter: a dead face's pending entry is DROPPED not swept, so it fires no final and any counter hangs forever, while the refcount ends the get uniformly and promptly on a real final / timeout sweep / face death / per-face issue error / zero faces; the C thread holds its own clone across the fan loop so face 1's early final cannot complete the get mid-fan. The sweep rides the EXISTING on_event drive-thread callback (SharedSession::dispatch) -- structurally, not by convention: the drive future is !Send (the SCE Engine owns bare Box<dyn FnMut()>), so a per-face sweep task cannot compile, while it would compile and be unsound. The DESIGN plan's fold-the-deadline-into-the-wake-min was NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and the test caught it at 3.11s (exactly the ~3333ms keepalive cadence): z_get runs while the loop is already parked in select! on the OLD deadline, so next_extra_deadline() is not re-read until that wake. It is NOT fixed here because it is a wz CORE gap, not a binding one -- Session::query already takes with_consolidation, so wz's own Rust API has it too -- and the inventory's query-consolidation atom was itself asserting C=indep reply dedup, a behaviour no code implements. Round 311y297.decision_summary: R311y297 -- hosted-CI runner disk headroom for the feature-matrix job. LEDGER ENTRY WRITTEN RETROACTIVELY at the R311y298 session: the fix shipped and pushed as 0bd9952 without an entry, because the red-CI fire drill ended the prior session before the ledger step. The commit itself is unchanged and stays the record of what landed; this entry is the audit trail it never got. WHAT HAPPENED: the y296 push died with "No space left on device" while the Actions runner was writing its OWN diagnostic log, at Layer F, AFTER every wz gate through E5 had passed -- no wz gate failed, the runner ran out of disk. The "validate + verify + test" job builds the whole workspace and then ~20 more feature-subset lanes (C1b..C1i, C4, C4b), each a DISTINCT feature set and so a DISTINCT artifact set in crates/target, plus zenoh-pico's CLI binaries and wz-ap-demo for the Layer E interop lanes; debug artifacts dominate and the total grows monotonically as atoms land. y292-y296 tipped it. FIX: a first step in that job prunes the ubuntu-22.04 preinstall the job never uses (dotnet, android, ghc, boost, CodeQL, docker images), each with `|| true` so a path absent on a future image is headroom-not-a-gate, bracketed by `df -h /`. Scoped to this job deliberately, not hoisted: it uses only actions/checkout + Swatinem/rust-cache with rustup Rust and apt python3, so nothing it needs lives in the hosted tool cache (the Zephyr job DOES use actions/setup-python, which is why a shared step would be wrong).
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: new first step "Free runner disk space (headroom for the feature-matrix lanes)" in the `validate + verify + test` job (41 lines added, the only change in the commit) -- prunes /usr/share/dotnet, /usr/local/lib/android, /opt/ghc, /usr/local/share/boost, /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL and runs `docker image prune --all --force`, every removal `|| true` so a path missing on a future runner image cannot fail the build.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: the prune is bracketed by `df -h /` BEFORE and AFTER, so the job's starting headroom is reported in the log; the y296 failure was undiagnosable precisely because nothing ever reported free space.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: the step carries an in-yaml rationale comment recording why the job has no other headroom (~20 distinct feature-set artifact sets + pico CLI binaries + wz-ap-demo), why y296 tipped it, and why the step is job-scoped rather than hoisted (the Zephyr job's actions/setup-python needs the tool cache this job does not).
verification_bullets: Hosted CI run 29347159829 on 0bd9952: ALL 6 jobs green -- validate + verify + test (26m25s), cross-impl proof lanes E2/E6*/E7/E8/Z (5m0s), portability windows-latest (9m13s), portability macos-latest (1m53s), cross-compile + QEMU Layer G+Q (10m7s), Zephyr Layer Qz (2m43s). The disk failure did not recur.

MEASURED from the run's own df bracket (job 87133762657): BEFORE prune /dev/root 146G size, 57G used, 89G avail, 39% use; AFTER prune 40G used, 106G avail, 28% use. So the prune freed 17G and cost ~27s (15:51:24 -> 15:51:51).

HONEST CORRECTION to the commit message: it claimed "prune ~25GB of unused preinstall"; the measured figure is 17G. The claim was written from the standard-remedy estimate, not from a measurement -- the measurement only existed after the run the commit enabled. 17G is the number.

CLAIM BOUNDED -- what this run does NOT prove: the df bracket wraps the PRUNE STEP ONLY (ci.yml:102 and ci.yml:112; grep `df -h` finds no other call site). Nothing reports disk at the lanes, at Layer F, or at the peak. So the commit's stated goal -- "a future squeeze should be visible BEFORE it is fatal" -- is delivered only as a starting number; a re-overflow at Layer F would still show 106G avail at minute 1 and then nothing. The headroom is real; the visibility is half-built.

INFERENCE (labelled as such, not measured): the y296 run had no df step, but it ran the same job on the same runner image, which the y297 measurement shows starts at ~89G avail. That the y296 job still overflowed therefore implies its own artifacts consumed on the order of 89G, and that the +17G this fix buys is roughly a 19% headroom increase on a workload that already exceeded the disk -- a thin margin, not a comfortable one.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y297 = hosted-CI runner disk headroom: the feature-matrix job prunes ~17G (MEASURED; the commit message's "~25GB" was an unmeasured estimate) of unused ubuntu-22.04 preinstall before building, taking the job's starting headroom 89G -> 106G. CI-infrastructure only -- no wz code, no Cargo, no inventory, no behavior change. Hosted CI run 29347159829 green on all 6 jobs.

OPEN (this fix's own named gap): the `df -h` bracket wraps the prune step ONLY, so disk is never reported at the lanes or at Layer F where y296 actually died. The commit's "visible BEFORE it is fatal" goal is half-delivered. A real fix reports df AFTER the lane block (or per-lane), which is where a squeeze would show as a trend rather than a single starting number.

OPEN (second ceiling, approached and unaddressed): the main job took 26m25s against `timeout-minutes: 30` = 88% of the budget, and it is SLOWER than the last green run before the overflow (y291, 25m31s) because the prune itself costs ~27s. y297 bought disk headroom and spent time headroom. Both ceilings are being approached at once and only the disk one was addressed; nothing reports or gates the time margin either.

OPEN (the underlying cost driver, untouched): the job's disk+time growth is monotonic in atom count because each feature-subset lane materialises a DISTINCT artifact set in crates/target. Pruning the runner image is a one-off constant (~17G, now spent) against a growing workload -- it does not change the slope. The structural options (a shared/incremental target dir across lanes, splitting the feature matrix into parallel jobs, or trimming the lane set) are unexamined; the next squeeze arrives on schedule.

Round 311y299.decision_summary: R311y299 -- A3 impl-axis grammar: stop asserting a completeness the audit never checked. The A3 gate printed "REMAINING WORK = 7 ... OK" while EXEMPTING all 132 active atoms from the implementation axis by construction (audit-catalog-status.sh :212 required a tag only of non-active atoms, :228-230 skipped actives in the tally, :235 excluded them from REMAINING WORK). The false premise was :175 -- "active needs no tag: it means built AND cfg-gated" -- which contradicted :39-43 of the same file ("active means EXACTLY a real composition toggle -- nothing else"). Invariant #3 pins active <=> >=1 cfg site: it asserts A KNOB EXISTS, never that the capability behind it is finished. The grammar then made the truth unsayable: IMPL_TAGS mapped each tag to exactly ONE status (a function), PARTIAL mapped to reserved, and reserved requires ZERO cfg sites -- so an atom with a real knob COULD NOT be marked PARTIAL. R311y296 found query-consolidation half-built, had nowhere to put it, and wrote it into prose. FIX: tag->status becomes a RELATION (set-valued); COMPLETE (new) is legal on active; PARTIAL widens to {reserved, active}. query-consolidation is the FIRST atom tagged under it -- code-verified, not transcribed (8 cfg sites; transmit = request_build.rs:75 emits the Q_C ext; apply = ZERO ConsolidatingSink/consolidat hits in reply_sink.rs) -- taking REMAINING WORK 7 -> >=8, the first active atom ever counted. WHAT THIS ROUND DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO, and why: it did NOT mass-tag the other 131. Three adversarial design reviews + direct-read arbitration refuted the plan this round started with. The inventory reason prose has ROTTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- storage-aligner says "driver A8 + facade forward A9 pending" against a live 1178-line storage_aligner_service.rs and a shipped facade forward (wz/Cargo.toml:639); keyexpr-includes says "no internal consumer yet" against 6 live consumers (linkstate_forward.rs:1550, router_forward.rs:4816, ...). 2 of the 7 atoms the carry named as half-built were STALE = a 29% error rate on the most-curated list available, which extrapolates to ~38 wrong tags over 132. Transcribing that prose into a typed tag would launder stale prose into a field that LOOKS authoritative -- prose rots, and a typed tag certified by prose rots just as fast, only louder. So the active arm is OPTIONAL-BUT-COUNTED: untagged actives report as UNAUDITED (131 of 132) and REMAINING WORK prints as ">= N [LOWER BOUND]". Green and TRUE at every step; tags are earned a batch at a time by code read; at UNAUDITED=0 the arm promotes to fail_untagged and the bound becomes exact. Two carry claims were also REFUTED and must not be re-quoted: the "C= clause required on every active atom" move is a NULLITY (83 of 92 existing C= clauses contain no .rs reference at all -- C= as practiced asserts "a cfg knob exists", which has_gate() already proves mechanically for free), and "REMAINING WORK = 7 vs 7 half-built actives" was a CARDINALITY COINCIDENCE across disjoint sets (the audit's 7 are all reserved; the carry's 7 are all active; zero overlap). Also: A3 had NO require-mode and exited 0 on a missing mnemosyne-cli, and release.yml ran it UNGUARDED with no A4 step at all -- one network blip forfeited the only gate joining the inventory to the source tree, on a green badge. WZ_A3_REQUIRE now mirrors WZ_A4_REQUIRE (R311y266). And this file's own normative prose had rotted: :57-63 listed keyexpr-includes / -wildcard-single / -wildcard-double / -dollar-star as FOUNDATIONAL-reserved examples while all four are live status=active with 11/7/17/7 cfg sites -- 4 of 12 examples wrong, in the file whose entire purpose is to stop the impl axis living in unchecked prose. A4 UNCHANGED: built(187), denominator=162, proven=58/partial=33/unproven=71, verified empirically after the real mutation, not argued.

Round 311y300.decision_summary: R311y300 -- R311y299 review remediation, and a CORRECTION of R311y299's own false claim (frozen-ledger path: R311y299's body stands; this entry supersedes the two clauses named below). THE CORRECTION, and it is the important half: R311y299's decision/carry asserted that keyexpr-includes' reason is FALSE -- "no internal consumer yet" against "6+ live consumers (linkstate_forward.rs:1550, router_forward.rs:4816, ...)". THAT ASSERTION IS ITSELF FALSE, and the reason is CORRECT. The atom's cfg gates TWO functions in keyexpr_match.rs: keyexpr_includes_target (:433) and keyexpr_includes_patterns (:567). The reason's C= clause NAMES keyexpr_includes_patterns specifically, and that function has ZERO src consumers (2 test sites) -- "no internal consumer yet (exposed+tested)" is precisely true of the function it names. The 13 src consumers are of the OTHER function, keyexpr_includes_target. The error was a loose `grep keyexpr_includes` that conflated the two without reading which symbol the C= clause binds to -- i.e. exactly the violation of [[feedback-claim-binds-to-atom-code]] that R311y299 itself shipped a memory about, committed in the same session. CONSEQUENCE for the headline number: R311y299's "2 of 7 stale = 29% error rate" is WRONG; only storage-aligner is stale, so it is 1 of 7 = ~14%. storage-aligner's staleness is RE-CONFIRMED at symbol precision (both named residuals are done: `pub mod storage_aligner_service` exported at wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:1105 = 1178 lines with `pub struct AlignerService`, plus a storage_aligner_convergence_e2e.rs; facade forward present at wz/Cargo.toml:645). WHY THE THESIS SURVIVES AND IS STRENGTHENED, NOT WEAKENED: three INDEPENDENT parties -- the implementing agent and BOTH adversarial review agents (design-scope and whole-session) -- graded keyexpr-includes identically wrong, each by the same loose grep, and the whole-session reviewer offered it as independently "confirmed". 3 of 3 failed on the FIRST atom examined. So the danger is not merely that reason prose rots; it is that GRADING reason prose requires binding to the exact symbol its C= names, and a majority of careful readers do not do that unprompted. A prose-driven mass re-tag would therefore have been MORE dangerous than R311y299 estimated, not less -- the corrected 14% is a measure of prose staleness, while the 3-of-3 misgrade is a measure of AUDITOR error, which is the compounding one and which no amount of review consensus catches (consensus was the thing that was wrong). REMEDIATION of the two reviews: (1) the real defect -- release.yml's Layer A3 `if: env.MNEMOSYNE_SKIP != '1'` guard, added by R311y299, made WZ_A3_REQUIRE UNREACHABLE and preserved the exact forfeit R311y299 claimed to close: MNEMOSYNE_SKIP is set ONLY by the install fallback (:88-90), so guard and require are DISJOINT -- install fails => step skipped => require never evaluates => green release with A3 never run, on a workflow with no A4 step to notice. Only the step icon changed. Guard REMOVED; release.yml now matches ci.yml, which had it right. (2) ">= N [EXACT]" printed an inequality asserting exactness -- the `>=` was outside the conditional; the operator now lives inside it. (3) crossimpl_audit.py's new comment said a mis-scoped COMPLETE would "INFLATE the proven percentage"; A4 prints COUNTS, never a percentage (R311jl). (4) feature_closure.py:29 hardcoded "37 of the 160 denominator atoms" while the live denominator is 162 -- pre-existing rot, but R311y299 swept two other files for exactly this class and skipped it; the count is REMOVED rather than refreshed (A4 prints the live denominator every run; a prose count nothing gates only rots again), and the bullet's "compiled whether or not the feature is enabled" premise is annotated as NARROWER than phrased, since session-extqos is reserved with 0 own cfg sites yet elidable behind 155 transport-qos sites.
