Round 311y307.decision_summary: R311y307 -- pubsub QoS-byte merge: the three per-field features become ONE compile unit (pubsub-qos), dissolving a verified wire-fidelity defect rather than masking it. FOUND (batch-6 A3 read-first, direct read): pubsub-priority / -congestion-control / -express each gated ONLY their typed PublishOptions setter, while the encode (build_push_outer_extensions) and decode (dispatch_push -> extract_qos) paths gated on their any(...) UNION and QosLevel::from_parts / with_priority / with_congestion / with_express are entirely ungated (module qos is unconditional). So composing ANY ONE sibling put ALL THREE sub-fields on the wire -- falsifying each atom's own doc claim "Without it the <field> sub-field cannot ride the wire" (publish_common.rs:283-286 / :312-313 / :326) in every mixed subset; the mixed subset was verified to build (cargo check exit 0). DESIGN REVIEW (3 independent adversarial agents, arbitrated by direct read) KILLED my first design (a QosLevel::gated() per-field mask applied at encode + decode + conduit band): all 3 converged on dropping the band gate -- masking priority_band would permanently clamp publish_shm / publish_aliased, which have NO _qos variant, and would make the drive.rs:402 conformance guard constant-false while collapsing the 8 per-priority RxSn conduits (sn.rs:179-195); 2 of 3 killed the decode mask as a protocol LIE (the bits already arrived; rewriting one makes wz report a QoS the peer never sent, a divergence the all-features-on cross-impl proofs can never observe); and a public QosLevel::gated() would have been reachable from the SHARED Request path (request_build.rs:365), where the natural default is Block (0x0D) not Drop (0x05), silently degrading queries. The review also REFUTED my own diagnosis twice: run-ci C1bb ALREADY builds+tests a mixed subset (pubsub-priority alone), so the leak escaped for want of a NEGATIVE assertion, not for want of a subset; and my "wz is pico-faithful 2-channel" premise was false (wz has per-priority conduits under transport-qos). CHOSEN instead (user directive: ignore cost, take the long-term-correct path): MERGE. Measured, the split had no slimming value -- solo cfg sites were priority=2 production / congestion=2 / express=1, everything else union or ungated -- so the three were one atom plus three API subsetters, not three composable atoms; Sample carries a single Option<QosLevel> in which a per-field "absent" is unrepresentable. Merging makes union == feature, so the un-composed state cannot be expressed and there is nothing left to mask: the defect stops existing rather than being handled (unrepresentable-by-construction, achieved by deleting a false distinction rather than adding machinery). The three keep their cargo keys as aliases composing pubsub-qos (so --features pubsub-priority still works) and become catalog atoms with no own cfg site -- reserved + FOUNDATIONAL, the liveliness-historical-samples / pubsub-sample precedent, which the A3 gate itself prescribed in its FAIL text. All three RUNTIME knobs survive as pubsub-qos-gated setters, signature-stable; wz stays a superset (zenoh/pico expose all three as runtime options with NO compile knob, so wz = 1 compile knob + 3 runtime knobs). NO masking anywhere: a decoded byte is recorded exactly as the peer sent it. A3: atoms 212->213, active 132->130, COMPLETE 29->30 (pubsub-qos EARNED by code read), FOUNDATIONAL 54->57, UNAUDITED 83->80, REMAINING WORK >= 27 unchanged (the trio were never in it). NOT pushed.

Round 311y308.decision_summary: R311y308 -- Push loopback metadata gates + the §5.8-pubsub burn-down batch COMPLETE (the domain now has ZERO unaudited atoms). FIXED, the defect the batch-6 read named: build_loopback_sample (publish_common.rs) copied all five metadata fields into the loopback Sample UNGATED w.r.t. their own features, while the wire leg gated each at its SSOT point. Since PublishOptions' fields are pub and #[non_exhaustive] blocks only struct-literal construction (NOT field assignment), a value written through the pub field -- the gated with_* setter being absent in that subset -- reached a loopback subscriber in a build that never composed the feature, falsifying the manifest's "Feature-off: nothing is set nor written". Loopback-only / process-local; the wire leg was always correct. The fix mirrors the ALREADY-CORRECT Reply-side idiom (reply.rs loopback_put_attachment:366 / loopback_put_encoding:384) that the Push path never received -- verified the template first rather than copying it blind, and it verifies: its own doc states its parity claim narrowly (content when both legs exist, not which legs a subset compiles), which this round inherits verbatim. Five loopback_* gates now stand between opts and the Sample; since push_metadata (wire) and build_loopback_sample (loopback) are the ONLY two consumers of those fields, they are now INERT feature-off on BOTH legs, so privatising the pub fields would add nothing behavioural and was NOT done (priority_band also reads qos and stays ungated -- the independent transport-qos conduit axis, per y307). TWO PRE-EXISTING LATENT DEFECTS surfaced by the new lane and fixed: (a) pubsub.rs gated `use alloc::vec::Vec` on any(pubsub-put, pubsub-delete) with a comment claiming the opposite of the truth -- `Vec` is NAMED only by the pubsub-delete arm's Vec::new() and by the not(pubsub-attachment) type annotations (the ON arm's .map(<[u8]>::to_vec) never names it) -- so alloc+put+attachment failed on an unused import; (b) push_build.rs gated `use ExtEntryOwnedVariant` on any(pubsub-source-info, <QoS>) with a comment that went stale at R311ek (which moved source_info's full-entry construction behind encode_source_info_ext_entry, after which source_info never names the variant) -- so source-info ON + qos OFF failed the same way. Both are the SAME class: an import gate that encodes *which cfg arm happens to name a type* drifts the moment that arm is refactored, and only an unbuilt subset pays. Fixed by removing the coupling (fully qualifying) rather than restating it in a longer cfg. Also cleaned a y307 rewrite artifact: its regex matched only exact-3-feature unions, so a 4-entry any() became pubsub-qos x3 duplicated; swept the workspace -- 0 duplicated-union and 0 singleton-any sites remain. Round 311y310.decision_summary: R311y310 -- pay down the §5.8 citation rot y309 named and deliberately deferred: rebuild the seven remaining COMPLETE reasons (pubsub-qos / -put / -delete / -encoding / -timestamp / -attachment / -source-info) symbol-first, following the pubsub-allow-loop template y309 built. The substance of all seven was already independently re-verified by y309's tag-vs-code review; this round rebuilds POSITIONS, and it found more than positions. THE HEADLINE FINDING, which upgrades the lesson rather than just applying it: four reasons cited the loopback gate as `loopback_encoding` / `loopback_timestamp` / `loopback_attachment` / `loopback_source_info` -- names that exist under NO symbol anywhere in the tree. The real gates are `gated_*`, generated by the metadata_gated! macro in publish_common.rs, so even `grep "fn gated_timestamp"` misses them. The wrong name has a traceable origin: build_loopback_sample's own doc comment says "every metadata field now flows through its `loopback_*` gate above", and the reasons copied the comment. So y309's rule "CITE SYMBOLS, NOT LINES" is necessary but NOT sufficient -- a symbol-first citation is only durable if the symbol was actually grepped; naming one that never existed is the same failure as a stale line, wearing better clothes. The rule is now: name the symbol AND grep it. The code comment is fixed too, at the source, so the next session cannot re-copy the wrong name. THE MECHANISM, MEASURED rather than asserted: rot is confined exactly to the four files R311y307-y309 touched (push_build.rs / pubsub.rs / publish_common.rs / session/mod.rs) -- build_push_outer_extensions had moved 412 -> 406, dispatch_push's `_ => return` 761 -> 771, publish_qos 676 -> 659 -- while every cite into an untouched file was re-measured EXACT (flush_batch_if_express at session_actions.rs:3446, the drive.rs:402 is_qos() guard, build_body_extensions:349 and build_push_del_literal:230, both above the edit point). That is the mechanism y309 hypothesised, now confirmed by measurement on both arms. The three individual errors y309 named are also paid, and two were worse than named. (1) pubsub-encoding cited "adminspace-core force-enables pubsub-encoding (wz/Cargo.toml)": wrong manifest AND an incomplete set -- THREE features imply it, none of them in wz/Cargo.toml's own feature body: adminspace-core (wz-session-core), storage-backend (wz-runtime-tokio), rest-http-bridge (wz). (2) pubsub-source-info cited "an acknowledged asymmetry (wz/Cargo.toml)": the asymmetry is real and re-verified, but wz/Cargo.toml acknowledges nothing of the kind -- its only source-info line is a bare forward. The real acknowledgement is in wz-session-core/Cargo.toml on the reply-source-info feature. A true claim filed against a manifest that does not make it is unfalsifiable by the reader who checks -- worse than an uncited claim, because it survives the check by exhausting the checker. (3) pubsub-timestamp credited "C1d arm1 (metadata-OFF subset)" as its gate proof: measured against scripts/run-ci.sh, arm 1 composes pubsub-timestamp, so it is metadata-off for encoding / source-info / qos and proves NOTHING about this atom's OFF path; the timestamp-OFF C1d arms are 3 and 4, and the behavioural NEG is C1bj. Crediting a feature-ON arm as a gate proof is "a SKIP is green" in its inventory form. Also corrected, found this round: pubsub-put sourced its RX-only contract partly to an in-code note that the bare position hid the location of -- it is the doc of push_with_keyexpr inside `mod push_fixtures`, a `#[cfg(all(test, ..))]` module, so it corroborates the contract but is test-side prose, not production-code evidence; and pubsub-qos cited extract_qos to pubsub.rs, which only CALLS it (it is defined in sample.rs). All ci.yml positions are replaced by job + step names for the same durability reason. NOT done here, deliberately, and carried: the §5.8 section prose still states the pre-y307 union claim, pubsub-qos still carries no wz-proves tag, and the FOUNDATIONAL tag on the reserved trio is still arguably a category error -- those are the y309 gate-review items and they are a section-prose round, not a citation round.

Round 311y312.decision_summary: R311y312 -- bind the QoS foreign proof to the atom that gates it, closing the LAST y309 gate-review item. Before this round the merge y307 performed was reflected in the code, the inventory reasons (y310) and the section prose (y311), but NOT in the proof axis: the sole atom gating the QoS byte, pubsub-qos, sat in audit-crossimpl-proof.sh's actionable UNPROVEN list of 72, while its three RESERVED aliases carried the proofs. An atom with zero cfg sites of its own cannot be what a test proves -- a claim binds to the atom's own gated code, and after y307 the only gated code is pubsub-qos's. THE FIX IS FOUR COUPLED EDITS IN ONE COMMIT, and the coupling is forced, not stylistic: (a) the trio join FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE under the EXISTING category "Pure cargo aliases / re-views of an atom that is itself counted", where link-frame ("would double-count"), link-fragment and link-batching already sat -- the repo had already ruled on this exact shape two rounds before y307, which is the strongest argument that this is a correction and not a novelty; (b) the claims re-point onto pubsub-qos; (c) the priority test's claim becomes `partial`, because it witnesses bits 0-2 only; (d) the congestion+express test is promoted to assert all three sub-fields, which makes ONE claim full. (a) and (b) MUST land together because A4-6 rejects a claim on an excluded atom and fires BEFORE A4-2/A4-5 -- split them and the gate goes red. (d) is not polish: partial claims never aggregate (full = set(proven_full); partial = proven_partial - full), so leaving the byte's proof split across two tests would have capped the merged atom at `partial` forever. The promoted test pins Priority::RealTime(1) instead of Data(5) for the reason its sibling already documents: Data IS pico's default, so asserting it is a tautology that passes whether or not propagation works. PROVEN BY FALSIFICATION, not by the assertion's existence: reverting the priority to Data turns the test red with pico printing "with priority: 5" against the expected 1. MEASURED, against the run captured before any edit: denominator 163 -> 160 (FNO 25 -> 28), proven 58 -> 58, partial 33 -> 31, unproven 72 -> 71, and pubsub-qos is gone from the UNPROVEN list. The count did not merely move -- three alias slots left a denominator they were double-counting and the real atom entered as proven. WHAT THIS ROUND ALSO CAUGHT, unplanned: the gate caught ME. A first attempt wrote the literal marker `wz-proves:` into the promoted test's module prose; A4-4 (no silent contribution) flagged it as a malformed/unattached claim line and the audit went red until it was reworded. The invariant that exists to stop a test contributing silently also stops prose contributing accidentally -- worth recording as evidence the arm is live rather than decorative. Also fixed here, named by the design review and true independently of this change: crossimpl_audit.py justified exempting non-active atoms from A4-5 containment because "its code is compiled unconditionally, whether or not its `= []` cargo key happens to be enabled". That premise is FALSE of every alias-shaped FOUNDATIONAL in the tree -- 18 of 57 -- whose key is not `= []` and whose vehicle's code IS elided when the vehicle is off. The exemption is still right, but for the narrower reason now stated: the atom names no cfg site, so containment over ITS name is vacuous either way. And the promoted test's own module doc still described the ext as "gated on any(pubsub-priority / pubsub-congestion-control / pubsub-express)" -- the pre-y307 union claim, in a THIRD location after the inventory reasons (y310) and the section prose (y311). NAMED, not paid: FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE is falsifiable ONLY through A4-6, so excluding the trio AND removing their claims leaves nothing in the corpus able to refute the exclusion. That cost is real and is the price of not double-counting; the mechanism stays armed for any future test that claims one.

Round 311y314.decision_summary: R311y314 -- whole-session review remediation for the R311y310-y313 arc, and a RETRACTION. Three independent adversarial reviews, every finding arbitrated by direct read; one finding was fabricated and discarded, the rest were real and most were mine. THE RETRACTION FIRST, because it is the round's point: R311y312's carry claimed "§5.8 IS CONSISTENT WITH THE y307 MERGE ON ALL FOUR LEGS" and "every y309 gate-review item is now closed". That is FALSE and it is frozen. Leg 1 -- the code -- still carried the pre-merge claim in three places, and the falsifying subset is a lane I hosted MYSELF in y309: session/mod.rs's publish_qos rustdoc said "under pubsub-priority the explicit band is FOLDED" and "Without pubsub-priority there is no observable qos byte", while the arm 11 lines below reads #[cfg(feature = "pubsub-qos")]; Layer C1bi composes pubsub-qos WITHOUT pubsub-priority and the whole byte rides. session/tests.rs said the same twice, and run-ci.sh's C1bc comment named a "pubsub-priority arm of the publish_qos fold" that does not exist. Worse, pubsub-qos's own inventory reason cites that rustdoc as evidence OF ITS GATE -- so y310 read the code at the cited site, rebuilt the citation, and never read the prose it was pointing at. The four-legs thesis was right; the claim that I had finished all four was an aspiration written as a fact, which is exactly what the ledger-claims-conservative rule exists to stop. WHAT ELSE THE REVIEWS CAUGHT, all verified: (1) y310's SCOPE was wrong. It rebuilt "the seven remaining COMPLETE reasons" -- a phrase taken from y309's carry PROSE -- while the store returns TWELVE §5.8 atoms, so the three reserved aliases kept the identical pre-y307 positions y310 was paying down (build_push_outer_extensions 412->406, with_qos 283->267, with_priority 292->310, with_congestion_control 314->335, with_express 327->350; QosLevel::from_parts in the untouched sample.rs re-measured EXACT). with_priority is the instructive one: the cited position pointed EARLIER than the symbol, so following it lands in a different function. I violated derive-the-set-from-the-store in the session where I preached it, and again in (2). (2) y313's carry said "§5.9 now 9 unaudited of 10". Store-derived: ELEVEN atoms, 9 untagged. The 10 came from stale prose -- the same census error y309 logged against y308. (3) THREE un-grepped numbers, in the arc whose whole thesis is that un-grepped citations rot: crossimpl_audit.py's header said "25 of those atoms" while y312 made it 28 and the script PRINTS 28 four lines into its own stdout; the alias enumeration I wrote in two files said "the 9 locator-* forwards" for 8 and omitted four members (keyexpr-canon, liveliness-historical-samples, scouting-gossip, scouting-multicast) -- and I had the correct 18-item list printed in front of me when I wrote it. Counts and lists are citations. Both are now DERIVED or deleted; the FNO header no longer states a count at all, because len() is the SSOT. (4) y310's pubsub-encoding force-enable claim was wrong three ways: it said "THREE features imply it, none in wz/Cargo.toml's own feature body" and then listed rest-http-bridge, which IS in wz/Cargo.toml; it wrote no carve-out down, so the count was false as frozen; and it called the set "completed". Derived: TWELVE feature bodies name it directly, plus wz-rest/Cargo.toml hard-enables it on its dependency unconditionally -- not a feature at all, so no knob turns it off. (5) y310's pubsub-timestamp correction fixed an arm-ordinal miscredit and introduced a NEW one in the next clause ("second arm" for arm 1) -- an ordinal IS a position, and the five C1bj arms are order-independent. (6) y313's query-reply reason said "four production sites" and MEASURED was the word it used; there are six -- put_reply_attachment and put_reply_encoding are production fns on any(pubsub-put, query-reply). (7) y313 granted COMPLETE citing a "real gate-proof PAIR" whose two arms were bare whole-crate cargo test invocations -- zero surviving tests exits 0, the construction C1bi's own comment (written this same session) defines as "a skip reporting green". FIXED PROPERLY rather than by downgrading the tag: C1e arm 2 now asserts its 2 NEGs survive, and C1f arm 2 asserts reply::tests is non-empty with query-reply and EXACTLY ZERO without it (measured 32 vs 0) -- which is what makes the pure-getter arm falsifiable. (8) pico's network.c cite was AMBIGUOUS, not stale: two vendored files share the basename, and definitions/network.c:44 is `ret.n += 1;`. The symbol-first rule exempted vendored cites because they do not MOVE; it never considered that a basename can be ambiguous. (9) wz/Cargo.toml's pubsub domain header still read "(11 atomic, 10 active / 1 reserved)" -- a FOURTH location of the dissolved count, and the one §5.8's own rebuilt bullet points a reader at. (10) y311 deleted the any-of outputs bullet while appending a caveat that says it "supersedes the any-of bullet"; caveats are append-only, so a corrective caveat now says that reference is history. Also reconciled: FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE's stated predicate ("no foreign peer can produce or observe ANY difference") is FALSE of its alias entries and has been since link-fragment/link-batching landed -- toggling an alias demonstrably changes the wire, because the alias pulls its vehicle. The set holds TWO categories and only the first matches the predicate; the second is DE-DUPLICATION. That divergence is now stated in the file, along with the honest cost y312 claimed to have named and did not: a category-2 entry CAN be witnessed, so A4-6 cannot refute it -- the trio's witness exists in this tree and simply reports as pubsub-qos. y312 named a sequencing constraint and called it a cost.

Round 311y317.decision_summary:
R311y317 -- a REAL wire-observable gate hole, found by testing y316's own carry
instead of trusting it, and closed. Three atoms (query-target /
query-consolidation / query-timeout) were emitting their wire bytes in builds
that do not contain them. MEASURED, not argued: with each atom off, assigning
the `pub` field on QueryOptions -- rather than calling the gated `with_*`
setter -- put Q_T (0x34, header 124->252), Q_C (0x23) and the timeout ext
(0x26, varint 1000) on the wire. `#[non_exhaustive]` blocks struct-literal
construction, NOT assignment onto a `QueryOptions::get()` value, so the
setter's body gate was never the enforcement point it was documented to be.
ROOT CAUSE, and it is structural rather than a per-slot oversight: the split is
exact. `build_request_query_with_meta` (session-core, the TX SSOT) cfg-gates 4
of 7 metadata slots -- value / source-info / attachment / selector-parameters --
and threads 3 ungated. Every gated one forwards to a same-named wz-session-core
feature; every ungated one (query-target / -consolidation / -timeout) is
runtime-tokio-TERMINAL, so session-core cannot name the atom, let alone gate it.
The runtime layer is the last hop that knows these three exist. THE TRAP I WOULD
HAVE WALKED INTO: gating only the wire threading fixes the bytes and leaves the
local ReplyRegistry deadline armed, because `Session::query` reads
`opts.timeout_ms` DIRECTLY at two sites that never touch `query_metadata()` --
and my wire-byte test would have gone GREEN while it happened. Two adversarial
reviews caught it independently; I then falsified it by hand (reverting only the
deadline half makes the wire assertion pass and the deadline assertion fail).
PRECEDENT, which I had backwards: I argued this against y316's BorrowedQuery
ruling. Review found y316 contains no such ruling, and that the governing
precedent is R311y308/y309 -- which adjudicated THIS EXACT SHAPE on the pubsub
side (an ungated pub-field `qos` reaching a subscriber / changing Frame count +
SN) and closed it with `metadata_gated!` + `push_metadata`. The query side never
followed. querier.rs even claimed it "mirrors push_metadata verbatim" -- a
fossil, false since y309. RETRACTED FROM y316: its carry (a) called
queryable.rs's ungated re-projection "the strongest remaining query-value gap".
It is not a gap: that file gates on query-queryable / transport-unicast only and
names NONE of the four metadata atoms -- OwnedQueryEvent relays all four
identically. It is a uniform relay design, not a query-value hole. I took one
reviewer's framing and froze it as fact; that is the same failure this round's
predecessors kept making.

Round 311y318.decision_summary:
R311y318 -- read the leg y317 refused to tag on, and it turned out CORRECT, so
two atoms are now COMPLETE and the round's real work was hosting the gate rather
than fixing anything. WHAT WAS ASKED: y317 closed a wire-observable hole
(query-target / -consolidation / -timeout emitted their bytes on builds without
them) but declined to tag, because a tag needs both legs and the router leg was
unread. y315's query-reply-err reason had flagged that routing-peer synthesizes a
Timeout Err, so query-timeout might carry a router-side leg gated on the wrong
atom. WHAT THE READ FOUND: the opposite of a hole. These atoms have NO
queryable-seam leg by design -- QueryTarget appears nowhere in query.rs /
query_sink.rs and QueryView exposes neither accessor, because a target is a
ROUTING hint, not handler input. The consumers are two routers,
linkstate_forward (gated routing-peer) and router_forward (gated
routing-router-hat), reading through request_routing_context's ungated readers.
NEITHER router file names any of the three atoms: 0 occurrences, measured. That
is exactly R311y315's ruling -- gate the atom that OWNS the route -- and it is
right: a relay must honour a peer's target/timeout regardless of whether THIS
build can emit one, the same reason InboundReplyBody::Err must decode a foreign
Err. So the legs are: EMIT gated on the atom (y317), CONSUME gated on the router
atom, and for query-timeout a THIRD leg -- the local deadline -- also gated on
the atom (y317). query-timeout is the atom with more than two legs, which is why
the obvious fix would have missed one. THE ROUND'S ACTUAL DELIVERABLE: y317's
gate was LOCAL-ONLY. Layer C1j (the consumer-plane behaviour matrix that runs
the zget-reply-only subset) is absent from ci.yml, and no other hosted lane
composes query-get WITHOUT the three atoms -- Layer C1's --workspace unifies them
ON, which cfg's all three NEGs out. So the fix was proven by falsification and
then guarded by nothing. The precedent settled it without my having to invent
anything: the feature-gates job exists because R311y309 hosted C1bi + C1bj -- the
PUBSUB-side gates of this exact shape -- and its comment states the rule
verbatim: "a gate that never runs hosted reports success by silence". Layer C1bk
is the query twin, hosted there. It compares the NEG test SET rather than a
count, because R311y315 shipped a gate whose CARRY pinned len() and a rename
passed green; the set-comparison is itself falsified both ways (rename a guard ->
red, cfg-elide one -> red). ALSO: the feature-gates job NAME enumerated its lanes
("C1bi + C1bj") and went stale the moment C1bk landed -- it names the genre now.

Round 311y319.decision_summary:
R311y319 -- the whole-session review, and it caught me shipping a COMPILE BREAK
into five hosted-adjacent lanes. THE HEADLINE, because it is the worst defect of
the session and it was mine: inserting the effective_* accessors into querier.rs
STRANDED query_metadata's #[cfg(feature = "query-get")]. Rust lets doc comments
and attributes interleave, so the attribute bound to my new accessor (a harmless
duplicate) and query_metadata was left UNCONDITIONAL -- it then called three
query-get-gated methods and named a query-get-gated type. Any subset with
transport-unicast ON and query-get OFF failed to compile: five layers red (C4b,
C4c, C4d, C1j, C1bj), including C1bj, which is HOSTED. Every default-feature
gate was green; the damage was confined to subsets nobody builds by default --
the exact shape y317/y318 exist to prevent, committed by the round that
prevented it. An existing lane I did not write caught it, and an independent
code review reached the same diagnosis and measured the blast radius I had
under-counted (I found C1bj; it found five). The invariant was documented three
lines from the break: session/mod.rs's import gate says QueryMetadata "is only
returned by the private query_metadata helper WHICH STAYS GATED ON query-get".
It stopped being gated. THE PATTERN THE REVIEW NAMED, and it is the session's
real lesson: a retraction lands where the author is LOOKING and misses the same
claim's second home. Three instances, all mine, all live surfaces (not frozen
history): (1) y317 retracted the "future R240+ sweep" fossil on the field doc
and missed the IDENTICAL claim on the setter doc 144 lines up. (2) y316

put query-value in wz-runtime-tokio's default, flagged as y315 carry (d) and
carried unpaid through y316/y317/y318. Now paid, and the lane's real narrower
value stated instead. (3) y317 retracted the queryable.rs "strongest remaining
gap" claim in its CARRY but left it in query-value's store reason, where it read
as an open debt against a COMPLETE tag -- its sibling query-source-info's reason
never carried it, and that asymmetry was the tell. ALSO SELF-FOUND: §5.9's
impl-axis census survived in a rationale bullet after I removed it from the
intent -- a fix that reads complete while the census lives in the next field
down; y315 had flagged that same bullet as stale-prone and left it a list. And

whose name carries a digit, leaving it set-unverified while green. Correcting a
false claim, I wrote another: my first C1be header fix asserted the lane runs
--no-default-features. It does not. Measured, then corrected in place.

Round 311y321.decision_summary:
R311y321 -- the user's carry asked two questions and the answer to both was YES,
so both atoms stay PARTIAL and the apply work is real. Then the user rejected my
framing twice, correctly, and the round grew into the apply half itself.
WHAT I GOT WRONG FIRST: I wrote that wz "structurally cannot" convey target to a
loopback queryable and that the consolidation accumulator was separate work. Both
were cost-deferral wearing a design word. zenoh's handle_query takes target as a
plain parameter for exactly the reason I called impossible; QueryableOptions.complete
ALREADY exists and already flows to the declare wire (mod.rs:2934/2950) -- the
dispatch registry simply does not retain it; and ReplyView already has an Err
discriminant + err_encoding, so synthesizing Err(Timeout) needs no new shape.
Nothing was a wall. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLED SCOPE: the consolidation gap is
a LIVE pico break on the C API's DEFAULT path, not a north-star aspiration --
z_get_options_default is AUTO (pico api.c:1725 -> :462 -> :446), wz-capi-pico
resolves AUTO -> LATEST exactly as pico does, and wz applied nothing. get.rs's
own module doc had confessed it as "A NAMED DIVERGENCE" for rounds.
THE ANSWERS, both by direct read of the registry cache, never memory: (1) zenoh
DOES synthesize Err("Timeout") -- api/session.rs:2264-2285 removes the query,
flushes the Latest cache, then calls back Err(ReplyError::new("Timeout")). wz's
sweep_timed_out fires on_final only (0 occurrences of Timeout in reply.rs), so a
caller cannot distinguish a timeout from a peer's Final. The divergence has TWO
legs and they split cleanly: the Err synthesis is query-timeout's, the flush is
query-consolidation's -- and the flush was unbuildable until this round, because
there was no cache. (2) zenoh DOES apply QueryTarget to session-local queryables
-- handle_query's filter applies (queryable.complete || target != AllComplete)
UNCONDITIONALLY; its `local` flag gates only the LOCALITY leg, and the local call
site passes the caller's real target. So querier.rs's "loopback-inert by design
(single-host fan-out has no selection axis)" is REFUTED.
WHAT LANDED: R1, the ReplyView timestamp seam -- which turned out to close a leg
pubsub-timestamp was tagged COMPLETE without. That reason's own enumeration
showed the asymmetry (push send + push receive + loopback + reply SEND; no reply
receive), the fourth sibling-asymmetry hit of the session. R3, the
ConsolidatingSink decorator: Latest + Monotonic + None-passthrough, wired through

Round 311y322.decision_summary:
R311y322 -- the whole-session review of R311y321 landed after y321 was frozen. It
found a REAL DATA-LOSS BUG in the feature y321 shipped, plus three false claims
y321 froze into the ledger. This entry exists because y321's body cannot be
rewritten. Three independent adversarial reviewers, ZERO fabricated findings,
and every finding below was verified by my own direct read before I acted on it.
THE BUG -- ConsolidatingSink consolidated Err replies. zenoh cannot, and does not
express that as a rule but as STRUCTURE: its consolidation match lives entirely
inside send_response's ResponseBody::Reply arm, while ResponseBody::Err is a
DISJOINT arm that calls callback.call(new_reply) directly. It could not
consolidate an Err if it tried -- Reply.result's Err variant is a bare
ReplyError { payload, encoding } with NO keyexpr, and the consolidation arms key
on result.unwrap().key_expr, unreachable for an Err by construction. wz cannot
borrow that structure: the wire dispatcher resolves keyexpr_literal BEFORE the
body match, so every InboundReply arm has a keyexpr and an Err arrives fully
cache-able. Consequences on the DEFAULT pico path (AUTO -> LATEST), both
directions: against a stamped Put the Err failed displaces_cached and was
silently swallowed; against an unstamped Put it won the tie and EVICTED the good
reply. Guarded now -- ReplyKind::Err forwards before the mode match and never
caches. WHAT HID IT: my own comment, which asserted an Err "ties with an
unstamped Put and is forwarded -- matching zenoh, which runs every reply through
the same match". zenoh does not run every reply through the same match. The
comment reasoned from the tie rule and never read the upstream arm split, and
mod consolidating_sink_tests had no Err test at all -- its only fixture was
fn put(). A claim I wrote became the reason I did not look.
THE FROZEN FALSEHOODS IN y321, each now corrected in the live surfaces:
(1) "wz's sweep_timed_out fires on_final only, so a Latest query that times out
drops its whole cache" -- FALSE. sweep_timed_out fires the swept entry's
on_final; the AP sink IS the ConsolidatingSink; its on_final drains the cache. A
reviewer probe measured it. y321 BUILT the timeout flush and then booked it as
owed work; its carry item (1) directs the next round to build what already
works. Only the Err(Timeout) synthesis is genuinely missing, and it is
query-timeout's leg.
(2) "QueryableOptions.complete ... already flows to the declare wire
(mod.rs:2934/2950)" -- a DEAD citation, cited 3x including in a carry that
instructs a future round. Those lines are map_queryable_err and
SendDeclareError::RequiresUnicast. The real sites are :2968/:2984 -- a uniform
34-line offset, because MY OWN EDITS added 34 lines above them between the read
and the write. Read before editing, cited after: the exact R311y309 lesson, in
the round that quotes it.
(3) "1135 session-core + 296 runtime tests green" -- unreproducible as written
because it names no feature profile. The real figures are 1137 --all-features
and 296 default. A count without its profile is not a citation.
ALSO FIXED: a FIFTH surviving instance of the emit-only claim, inside
build_loopback_query, which y321's own retraction commit missed while rewriting
the doc comment directly above it -- and which deferred to "the doc note" that
now refutes it. And register_consolidating, a public API y321 invented for a
caller that does not exist: grep found no non-None caller, none was possible
(the z_get path holds a built sink, not the closures it takes), and two comments
claimed it was the mechanism. Deleted rather than documented.
THE LESSON, and it is the same one three times: my prose is where my errors hide.
The Err bug, the timeout residual, and the dead citation were each PROTECTED by a
sentence I wrote asserting the thing I had not checked.

id.to_le_bytes()[..id.size()] and size() strips trailing zeros), so it needs a
hostile peer and only moves a same-instant tie. Named, not fixed.

z_get task off state.queries and a twin off state.liveliness_queries, both
calling back Err(ReplyError::new("Timeout", Encoding::ZENOH_STRING)). wz mirrors
the split exactly (ReplyRegistry vs LivelinessGetRegistry, two tables, two
sweeps), so fixing only z_get would have manufactured the asymmetry this session
keeps catching in other people's work. Both legs land here.
THE ASYMMETRY THAT WAS ALREADY IN THE TREE, unnamed by any round: the RELAY leg
already emitted the Err. synthesize_expired_query_returns builds
build_response_err_empty(rid, b"Timeout") toward the inbound face on a reaped
branch and cites zenoh's QueryCleanup::run in its own doc. So a wz querier

behaviour. I went looking for a residual to justify keeping PARTIAL and found
instead that the residual I feared was already paid, and that the hole was on

THE SEAM. ReplySink gains on_timeout(rid) with a DEFAULT of synthesize-then-
final. The default is the whole contract for a stateless sink -- the AP closure
adapter, an MCU closed enum, the liveliness sinks -- which is why this is a
defaulted method and not a breaking addition. ConsolidatingSink OVERRIDES it,
because ORDER is observable: zenoh flushes the Latest cache BEFORE the error
(data first, then the reason the stream stopped), and the default's
on_reply->on_final would emit the error FIRST and the cached data after it, so a
caller treating an error as terminal would lose data it had already earned.
flush_latest is extracted so the normal-final path and the timeout path cannot
drift apart on the Latest condition.
NO GATE, AND NONE IS POSSIBLE. wz-session-core does not declare query-timeout
(measured via cargo: it and query-consolidation are both wz-runtime-tokio

need to: the runtime gates by ARMING -- effective_timeout_ms() reads 0 with the
feature off, deadline_ms stays None, and the sweep loop is empty by
construction. The gate is the arming, not the sweep. Same shape as y321's
consolidation wiring: gate at the runtime, drive session-core by DATA.

client-side synthesis carries ZENOH_STRING (packed_id 2: zenoh's ZENOH_STRING is
{id:1,schema:None} and wz packs id<<1|schema_bit); the router leg carries
err_body's encoding:None. zenoh does exactly this -- ReplyError::new(.., 
Encoding::ZENOH_STRING) on the client, Encoding::default() in QueryCleanup. wz
reproduces the upstream's own inconsistency rather than tidying one leg into a
divergence.
FALSIFICATION EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN. Neutering the trait DEFAULT left all 12
tests GREEN -- because every test drove ConsolidatingSink, which overrides it,
and nothing exercised the default the LIVELINESS leg actually rides. That is the
y321 Err bug's shape verbatim: one fixture shape, and the arm it never builds is
the arm that breaks. The missing test was added and then re-falsified red.

Round 311y324.decision_summary:
R311y324 -- the review of R311y323. Two independent adversarial reviewers, ZERO
fabricated findings, and the verdict on the CODE was clean on every lens: the
flush-before-Err order matches zenoh, packed_id 2 is right (verified through
zenoh-codec's `(id as u32) << 1 | flag::S`, not through my comment), the
no-gate-needed claim survived a deliberate falsification attempt, no residual
could be constructed, no double-fire, and every consumer handles Err. y323's
code stands. Its PROSE did not.
WHAT THEY FOUND -- one class, six sites, and the worst one is a trap the file
itself warns about. y323 wrote careful new comments AT the edit points and left
the refuted claims in the DOC HEADERS of the very functions it edited:
(1) ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out's rustdoc still said "the callback cannot
distinguish 'timed out' from a normal Final ... Future rounds may extend
FinalCallback to carry an explicit FinalCause enum if a concrete user need
arises (R261 carry)". y323 IS that future round. It reversed R261's opaque-cause
architectural pick and recorded the reversal nowhere -- while the doc went on
proposing it as open work. The reversal also did NOT take R261's shape: a
FinalCause enum would have been a wz invention; zenoh models the cause as a
synthetic Err REPLY preceding the terminator, so on_timeout does that instead.
Now stated where R261's pick was stated.
(2) liveliness_get's sweep doc + (3) its PendingGet::deadline_ms field doc said
the same ("cannot distinguish", "firing on_final exactly as a real terminator
would") -- the second is 211 lines above the edit.
(4) querier.rs's timeout_ms field doc carried R311y317's OWN correction text,
"fires on_final synthetically", which y323 falsified. This is the trap: 144 lines
below it, R311y318 wrote "R311y317 retracted the SAME fossil on the field doc 144
lines up and missed this one -- a retraction lands where the author is looking."
The file carries the lesson and y323 walked into it anyway, on the same field.
(5) LivelinessGetOptions::timeout_ms and (6) Session::liveliness_get's public API
doc, same claim.
ALSO: reply_sink's Latest arm said the timeout path was covered "for free"
because the sweep fired on_final -- which is precisely the reasoning on_timeout's
override exists to REFUTE. A comment describing a bug as a convenience is how the
y321 Err bug shipped.
AN OVERSTATEMENT OF MINE, and it is the session's own lesson landing on me:
y323's entry says the relay Err was "unnamed by any round". FALSE. R311y315's
query-reply-err reason names it exactly -- "the routing-peer-gated query-timeout
path emits an Err through the same primitive (LinkstateForwarder::
synthesize_expired_query_returns calls build_response_err_empty with a b'Timeout'
payload)". The fact was one store row away, in a SIBLING's reason, and I did not
read it. What was genuinely unnamed is the ASYMMETRY (relay emits, local did
not), not the relay fact.
AND A COVERAGE GAP THEY LOCATED PRECISELY: timeout_reply's doc justifies the
design as "ungated and no-alloc-safe ... so the MCU profile gets the same timeout
signal as AP", but y323's only default-on_timeout test lived in
consolidating_sink_tests, which is alloc-gated. The profile the claim is ABOUT
had zero coverage. Moved to the ungated `mod tests`, whose CountingReplySink
exists for exactly that, and it now runs under --no-default-features.

fabricated findings, and the verdict on the CODE was clean on every lens: the
flush-before-Err order matches zenoh, packed_id 2 is right (verified through
zenoh-codec's `(id as u32) << 1 | flag::S`, not through my comment), the
no-gate-needed claim survived a deliberate falsification attempt, no residual
could be constructed, no double-fire, and every consumer handles Err. y323's
code stands. Its PROSE did not.
WHAT THEY FOUND -- one class, six sites, and the worst one is a trap the file
itself warns about. y323 wrote careful new comments AT the edit points and left
the refuted claims in the DOC HEADERS of the very functions it edited:
(1) ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out's rustdoc still said "the callback cannot
distinguish 'timed out' from a normal Final ... Future rounds may extend
FinalCallback to carry an explicit FinalCause enum if a concrete user need
arises (R261 carry)". y323 IS that future round. It reversed R261's opaque-cause
architectural pick and recorded the reversal nowhere -- while the doc went on
proposing it as open work. The reversal also did NOT take R261's shape: a
FinalCause enum would have been a wz invention; zenoh models the cause as a
synthetic Err REPLY preceding the terminator, so on_timeout does that instead.
Now stated where R261's pick was stated.

the same ("cannot distinguish", "firing on_final exactly as a real terminator
would") -- the second is 211 lines above the edit.

lines up and missed this one -- a retraction lands where the author is looking."

synthesize_expired_query_returns calls build_response_err_empty with a b'Timeout'
payload)". The fact was one store row away, in a SIBLING's reason, and I did not

not), not the relay fact.

Round 311y325.decision_summary:
R311y325 -- the (i) attack R311y324's carry demanded, and it REFUTES the
enumeration. The carry was explicit: do not re-check the legs query-timeout's
reason lists; try to NAME one it never listed. Two were named, so the tag does
NOT move to COMPLETE. No code defect was found -- this is an accounting round.

LEG A, and it is bigger than the one I went looking for. Legs (1)/(2) and the
gate all take timeout_ms's VALUE as given; NO leg asks what the value is when
the caller sets nothing. It is 0 -- QueryOptions derives Default
(session/querier.rs:58) -- and 0 is never-expire, so a DEFAULT Session::query
never expires and the Err("Timeout") machinery y323 built is UNREACHABLE on the
default client path. zenoh does the opposite: get() reads
conf.queries_default_timeout() unconditionally (zenoh-1.5.0 api/session.rs:
1209-1212), default 10000 (zenoh-config-1.5.0 defaults.rs:151). AND IT IS THE
SAME SIBLING ASYMMETRY y323 CLOSED, one level up: wz's own RELAY mirrors the 10s
default (linkstate_forward.rs:661). y323 wrote "one atom, two legs, opposite
behaviour" about the Err leg and did not look at the default leg, which has the
identical shape. The store had booked this root cause FOUR times (y89, y290,
y295, y296) without ever binding it to the atom, and FIVE consumers hand-patch a
default instead of inheriting one. Not a typo and not clearly a bug: 0 is
double-loaded as the wire-elision sentinel AND never-expire, so a 10s default is
not expressible without Option<u32> or a client config plane. It is an UNTAKEN
design decision -- which is exactly why the enumeration is not exhaustive.

LEG B -- the reason contradicts ITSELF, no external evidence needed. Its C=
clause says the knob gates "its own deadline arming -- not the sweep"; three
sentences later y323 annexes BOTH sweeps. And "exactly TWO arming sites ... Both
read effective_timeout_ms" is false: session/mod.rs:3901 arms a liveliness
deadline off a raw field under liveliness-get's cfg alone, and
wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs:278-281 arms a ReplyRegistry deadline off a CLI flag
through the pub ungated register(). By y323's OWN arming test the liveliness
sweep is liveliness-get's leg, not this atom's. MOVED, not deleted --
liveliness-get's reason was a stub naming no timeout, so y323 covered a leg
nobody covered and a delete would leave it uncovered.

TWO OF MY OWN ARGUMENTS DIED IN REVIEW, and both are recorded so nobody
re-derives them: "the liveliness arm BYPASSES the accessor" is a category error
(none existed to bypass; effective_timeout_ms is itself query-get-gated, so on
the liveliness-get-only lane it does not exist at all), and "all 5 proofs live in
a crate that cannot declare query-timeout, so none bind" is NON-DISCRIMINATING --
it strips this atom's legitimate z_get proof identically. Gate-at-the-last-hop-
that-KNOWS forces that crate placement; it is not a defect.

fabricated findings, and they broke two of my four arguments; the grep broke
their verdict on the fifth.

ledgered before I re-found it.

citing this module AND this lane by name), rode nothing. Measured, not argued:

RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" -- every fixture is co-located and vanishes with the module.
Silently green, the exact construction y314 named. Both modules are now pinned as
SETS (y315's lesson: a rename passed a len() gate). Falsified both ways.

THE REVIEW BROKE MY ARTIFACT AGAIN, 3 for 3 rounds. Reviewer 1+2 independently found
the same defect and it was in MY PROSE, protecting a correct guard: the comment
claimed one widening mechanism for all three atoms, false for query-source-info,
which is NOT in the module cfg (query.rs:3374-3379 has two not()s) -- its test
self-gates at :3516/:3542, so widening it elides one test, not the module. Measured
both paths, corrected (5fab0bc). Reviewer 2 also named two limits I closed (f3c69a7):
`[^:]*` made a NEG added in a submodule INVISIBLE to the compare, and a build break
read as the listed module's fault when `--lib <m>` filters what RUNS, not what BUILDS.

REVIEWER 3 FOUND THE ROUND'S REAL DEFECT, and it is why the tag moved on the review
rather than on my read: query-attachment's drop proof was VACUITY-EXPOSED. Its
fixture (query.rs:3407) hand-writes set_ext_id(0x05) with the constant's name only in
a comment -- the isolation module's own not(query-attachment) gate cfg's the SSOT out
of the build that must not decode -- while extract_query_attachment's OFF arm returns
None WITHOUT walking the chain, so a malformed ext satisfies it identically. The tree
already ratified the rule (query-value carries this twin since y316; query-source-
info's reason names it) and attachment alone lacked it. PAID (d59305a) and FALSIFIED:
0x05 -> 0x06 makes the twin FAIL rc=101 while the drop proof still PASSES rc=0. The
vacuity is demonstrated, not theorised.

THE ASYMMETRY IS NOT A DEFECT -- reviewer 3's read beat mine: `pub mod attachment` is
#[cfg(all(alloc, attachment-bytes))] (lib.rs:737) and query-attachment implies
attachment-bytes, so its gate is COMPILE-EXISTENCE NECESSITY. Q_P is a native
Query-body bit with no module to gate. y318 governs: build_request_query_with_target/
_with_timeout_ms are pub+ungated+codec-request-re-exported too, and both are COMPLETE.
Measured: those low-level helpers have ZERO production callers; session_glue's
"session.rs z_get" comment is a fossil.

ANYKE IS NOT A HOLE -- my third dead hypothesis. _implicit_anyke is not a wire field
(pico message.c:488-490 sets it false on receive: "signaled by the presence of the
_anyke key"). It is encode-time sugar off accept_replies, wz expresses every byte via
with_parameters(b"k=v;_anyke"), and wz DOES implement anyke at wz-capi-pico/src/
query.rs:139/169/934 -- a file naming NEITHER atom, i.e. owned elsewhere per y315.

Round 311y330.decision_summary:
R311y330 -- §5.9-query is FULLY AUDITED (UNAUDITED 0 of 11; re-derived, not
quoted). I proposed COMPLETE for both remaining atoms and the review REFUTED
BOTH. They are PARTIAL, and the round is a case study in my proposals being
wrong while my fixes were right.

WHAT I PROPOSED AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. query-queryable: I read session/mod.rs's
R311y321 note assigning the loopback selection gap to "the query-target atom's
PARTIAL residual" and concluded `complete` was not this atom's problem. That
note names only HALF the predicate. zenoh's rule is (queryable.complete ||
target != AllComplete): `target` is the REQUESTER-side operand and is
query-target's; `queryable.complete` is the RESPONDER-side operand, which is
verbatim this atom's C= ("indep responder-side"). Plumbing target alone could
never close it -- the predicate would have no `complete` to read. Measured:
wz-session-core/src/query.rs contains ZERO occurrences of `complete`;
QueryableOptions::complete reaches the wire declare (mod.rs:2999/:3015) and never
the local registry, so a SessionLocal queryable with .with_complete(true) is a
SILENT NO-OP. pico keeps the sibling wz drops -- _z_session_queryable_t stores
`bool _complete` ADJACENT to _allowed_origin (session.h:129/130) and reads it
locally (filtering.c:148, queryable.c:189/:286). A prose sentence assigning the
gap elsewhere is what would have let this atom be tagged COMPLETE with its own
C= surface unbuilt.

query-get: two independent blockers, neither mine. (1) Its OFF arm is
COMPILE-ONLY. Exactly three not(query-get) sites exist and all three are the
production arms; ZERO tests carry that gate. On the `queryable-only` lane -- the
very subset where this atom is off -- SEVEN sibling atoms' OFF guards run
behaviourally and its three do not. The standard is the repo's own
(session_glue.rs:1445-1452, R311hw/R311hx): a compile/footprint proof "does NOT
prove the consumer-side signature-stable emit path BEHAVES correctly when off".
(2) A homeless RX default divergence, the LEG A shape that refuted query-timeout
at y325: zenoh defaults accept_replies to MatchingQuery and states it as a
GUARANTEE (session.rs:1181); pico agrees (constants.h:291). wz NATIVE has no
reply-keyexpr gate at all -- Session::query is hard-wired to ANY, the upstreams'
OPT-IN, delivering replies both upstreams' default get would DROP. R311y329
examined _anyke, ruled it "owned elsewhere", and that ownership deferral has
never landed on any atom. It is homeless.

WHAT I ACTUALLY FIXED, and it started as a note. tests.rs said a
query-queryable-OFF UNIT run was "blocked until the test-support dev-dep stops
force-enabling default features (the C1j isolation carry)". STALE: the sibling
already sets default-features = false, this file's fixtures come from the
crate-LOCAL crate::test_fixtures, and the OFF build compiles and runs 126 unit
tests. Nothing blocked the proof but the note claiming it was blocked. Wrote the
two NEGs the atom never had (typed Err AND frame_count unchanged, per the
doctrine above) -- and in doing so found TWO POS tests that were VACUOUS on that
build: both were ungated and DISCARDED the declare's Result, so the reject
emitted nothing, the assert held trivially, and no queryable existed at all.
Their sibling twelve lines up already carried the fix (gate + .expect).

THE REVIEW BROKE MY ARTIFACT, 4 rounds running, and one finding is pure irony: I
retracted Session::query's implication-chain claim (query-get does NOT imply
query-queryable; the manifest says [query-reply, codec-request], and the body DOES
hold a further cfg at the loopback fan) -- then did not sweep the sibling file,
where QueryOptions' R307 doc claimed "the struct + impl + every setter elide when
query-get is off", false and self-contradicted by the R311o paragraph three lines
below it. That is retraction-lands-where-you-look, committed one commit after I
wrote a retraction about the same class.

MY OWN EVIDENCE HAD THREE ERRORS, all counts or hosting. "24 production cfg
sites" was a raw grep sweeping doc comments and cfg(test) gates. "58" for
query-queryable did not reproduce and MISSED reply.rs's 6 gates entirely. "The
subset feeds C1h + C4b" is structurally impossible -- C1h builds -p
wz-session-core, which does not declare query-get at all. Derive the SET.

Round 311y332.decision_summary:
R311y332 -- the proofs run now. Two rounds' feature-OFF NEGs were written into a
lane no hosted job executed, and this round stopped that from being a thing I do.

THE SELF-DEFEAT, named plainly. R311y330 wrote declare_queryable{,_aliased}'s
drop proofs; R311y331 wrote query{,_aliased,_aliased_auto}'s. Both rounds
falsified them locally, tagged the atoms on them, and shipped them into Layer
C1j -- which is ABSENT from ci.yml. Two rounds of "proven by falsification
locally" is exactly the silence the feature-gates job exists to break; its own
comment has said so since R311y309: "a gate that never runs hosted reports
success by silence". I hosted C1bk on that reasoning at y318 and then wrote two
rounds of proofs into an unhosted lane anyway.

THE FIX, and it is the y309 precedent applied verbatim: C1j is a step on
feature-gates now. Cost measured, not guessed -- C1j's worst recorded local wall
time is 193s (typical 54-87s) across 214 run-ci logs, against that job's
30-minute budget, whose three existing lanes total ~24s warm. It shares the
_wz_consumer_plane_subsets feature sets with C4c/C4d, so its distinct-artifact
cost is the rows themselves, once. The `ci` job could NOT have taken it (26m22s
vs timeout-minutes: 30, and its own comment declares no disk headroom) -- which
is why y309 built a parallel job rather than growing that one.

THEN THE SAME TRAP ONE LEVEL UP, which is the part worth reading. C1j runs
`cargo test --quiet` and reads only the exit code. Its rows are 100+ tests each,
so a round that silently cfg'd my five NEGs out would change no visible number
and the lane would stay GREEN. That is verbatim y314's "skip reporting green" --
the defect I fixed in C1e at y329 -- sitting directly above the lane I had just
hosted. Hosting alone would have been half a fix: the proofs would run, and
could vanish without a word. So C1j now pins each row's REQUIRED feature-OFF NEG
set (_c1j_required_negs), as SETS not counts, because R311y315 shipped a
len()-pinned gate that a rename passed green.

FALSIFIED FOUR WAYS, including the path I nearly left unproven: green baseline
(the two pinned rows report themselves); cfg-elide one guard -> RED with the
drifted set printed; a whole-crate compile break -> the first row reports it
through the pre-existing path with cargo's real error visible; and a break
scoped to a PINNED row only (cfg(all(query-get, not(query-queryable)))) ->
"subset zget-reply-only did not BUILD (exit 101) -- not a drift verdict". That
fourth one exists because the third did not exercise my new BUILD branch at all
-- an unproven error path is a guard that never runs, which is the whole subject
of this round.

they guard deny(warnings) dead-code regressions per subset -- but hosting them
is its own runtime call, not a side-effect of unblocking two rounds' proofs.

Round 311y333.decision_summary:
R311y333 -- two corrections to R311y331/y332's METHOD prose, both review-found,
both measured. Frozen entries stand; this supersedes their evidence citations.

CORRECTION 1 -- the E0308 attribution is FALSE. R311y331's decision says
"neutering the arm to a non-existent variant produced E0308". Measured with a
throwaway probe crate, both directions:
  - an EXISTING tuple variant used without its payload (`UnknownMapping` sans
    `(0)`) -> error[E0308]
  - a variant that does NOT exist (`Nonexistent`) -> error[E0599]
So what I actually hit was an ARITY error on a real variant, not a non-existence
error. The METHOD lesson the paragraph draws ("a falsification that dies at
COMPILE time is not a falsification") survives intact -- only its diagnosis of
WHY the compile failed was wrong.

CORRECTION 2 -- and this one voids the evidence, not just the label. R311y331 and
R311y332 both cite `rc=101` as the signature that a falsification BIT. Measured:
  - `cargo test` on a crate with `compile_error!`  -> rc=101
  - `cargo test` with a genuinely failing #[test]   -> rc=101
`rc=101` therefore CANNOT distinguish the two. I cited it as proof of exactly the
distinction it cannot make, in the same paragraph where I declared that
distinction the round's lesson. The claims are still TRUE -- the verification
bullets name the failing test and the runs grepped `FAILED|panicked at`, which IS
discriminating -- but the cited signal was the wrong one, and a future round
copying the citation rather than the grep would prove nothing.
THE DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE, for anyone repeating this: the `test result: FAILED`
line, or the `panicked at <file>:<line>` message naming the assert. Never the exit
code alone. `--list`-mode rc IS sound (nothing runs, so non-zero means the build
failed) -- that is why the C1j / C1e set-pin guards check it there and only there.

WHAT THE REVIEW ALSO FOUND, and it is worth recording because it cuts the other
way: R311y331's falsification was UNDERSTATED. It falsified arm 1 only. The
review falsified all three independently and each killed ONLY its own guard --
so the trio is a genuine 1:1 proof set, stronger than the round claimed.

AND THE PROCESS FIX FROM R311y330 PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY. y330's review was
ungradable because I edited the tree under it. y331's review was told "grade
commit a4809a0" by sha -- and when I moved HEAD anyway (y332 landed mid-review),
the reviewer noticed, said so, and graded a4809a0 via `git show` regardless. The
sha did the work the freeze failed to do. I still moved the tree under a reviewer
for the second round running; naming the sha is what made that survivable, not a
licence to keep doing it.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE REVIEW HELD: the three OFF arms were the only
not(query-get) sites with zero tests; typed Err + frame delta both pinned, no
async race (the guards are plain #[test] and the OFF arm never touches the
driver); `matches!` pins a unit variant exactly; the doctrine quote at
session_glue.rs:1445-1452 is verbatim; "seven sibling atoms" is exactly seven,
and correctly EXCLUDES codec-request (it is IN the subset, so its guard does not
run); PARTIAL=24 re-derived and correct. No third blocker exists -- the review
hunted one (liveliness-get's deadline vs a query-get-gated sweep) and the code
refuted it: liveliness gets ride their own `liveliness_gets` registry and are
swept independently.

Round 311y334.decision_summary:
R311y334 -- wire queryable.complete into the LOCAL query dispatch, closing
query-queryable's primary C= blocker (residual 1) and query-target's loopback
residual; a review-found feature-gate bug on the new loopback leg was caught and
fixed before landing.

THE GAP. options.complete reached only the wire declare (the QueryableInfo ext)
and NEVER the local dispatch table: Queryable<C> stored id/pattern/allowed_origin
/sink with no `complete`, and fire_matching_queryables selected purely on
matches(keyexpr, is_remote). A SessionLocal queryable declared .with_complete(true)
was a silent no-op. Symmetrically, build_loopback_query DROPPED the query target,
so an AllComplete self-get fired every matching local queryable, complete or not.

UPSTREAM, read directly (zenoh 1.5.0 src/api/session.rs:2427-2431, handle_query):
the filter is `(origin==Any || local==(origin==SessionLocal)) && (queryable.complete
|| target != AllComplete) && key_expr.intersects(..)`. The `local` flag gates ONLY
the locality conjunct; the completeness conjunct applies on the loopback path too,
and the SessionLocal call site passes the caller's real target. So the old loopback
drop was NOT faithful -- both operands are real on one host: `complete` is the
RESPONDER-side operand (query-queryable's C=), `target` the REQUESTER-side operand
(query-target's).

THE FIX. Queryable<C> stores `complete`; register_sink (the SSOT) threads it, and
the convenience wrappers default it false (zenoh builder default). matches() gains
`target: Option<QueryTarget>` and the middle conjunct as `!self.complete && target
== Some(AllComplete) -> reject` (the exact negation of zenoh's term). target threads
through fire_matching_queryables / local_query / dispatch_borrowed (the MCU no-heap
sibling, swept, not left behind); dispatch_request reads it off the wire via
read_request_target (no signature change -- target rides the Request envelope).
Session::declare_queryable registers via register_sink with options.complete -- the
SAME value stamped onto the wire ext, so table and wire agree by construction. The
handler still never sees target (QueryView exposes no target accessor); target
reaches only the dispatch predicate, exactly as zenoh's handle_query does. The pico
C-API funnels through the same runtime declare_queryable (faces.rs), covered without
a separate edit.

THE REVIEW-FOUND BUG (two of three adversarial reviewers, independently). The first
cut of the loopback fed the RAW pub field opts.target into local_query. But target /
consolidation / timeout are runtime-tokio TERMINAL features gated by the accessor
QueryOptions::effective_target() (the last-hop-that-knows), NOT by a session-core
forward -- and QueryOptions.target is an ungated pub field whose write bypasses the
cfg gate (R311y317 litigated exactly this on the wire side). query-target = ["query-get"]
and neither query-get nor query-queryable pulls it, so {query-get, query-queryable,
query-target OFF} is a reachable build; there the wire leg (effective_target()->None)
fires both queryables while the raw-field loopback applied AllComplete and skipped the
incomplete one -- the two legs disagree, re-opening the y317 bypass on a new leg. FIX:
both loopback sites now pass opts.effective_target(), mirroring the wire path; the
querier.rs target-field doc is corrected (never read self.target on a dispatch path).

TAGS STAY PARTIAL, deliberately. query-queryable: residual 1 closed, but residual 3
(take_pending_final_rids fn-level cfg asymmetry, observer.rs) is untouched, and (2)
hosting / (4) count stand. query-target: the loopback branch is now correct in code
and locally guarded, but the guard rides only local Layer C1an; its wire twin is
HOSTED in C1bk. Until the loopback guard is hosted in feature-gates, and the atom's
stale `source` pointer is corrected, query-target stays PARTIAL -- then COMPLETE.

Round 311y334.publishable_decision_summary:
R311y334 -- wire queryable.complete into the LOCAL query dispatch, closing
query-queryable's primary C= blocker (residual 1) and query-target's loopback
residual; a review-found feature-gate bug on the new loopback leg was caught and
fixed before landing.

THE GAP. options.complete reached only the wire declare (the QueryableInfo ext)
and NEVER the local dispatch table: Queryable<C> stored id/pattern/allowed_origin
/sink with no `complete`, and fire_matching_queryables selected purely on
matches(keyexpr, is_remote). A SessionLocal queryable declared .with_complete(true)
was a silent no-op. Symmetrically, build_loopback_query DROPPED the query target,
so an AllComplete self-get fired every matching local queryable, complete or not.

UPSTREAM, read directly (zenoh 1.5.0 src/api/session.rs:2427-2431, handle_query):
the filter is `(origin==Any || local==(origin==SessionLocal)) && (queryable.complete
|| target != AllComplete) && key_expr.intersects(..)`. The `local` flag gates ONLY
the locality conjunct; the completeness conjunct applies on the loopback path too,
and the SessionLocal call site passes the caller's real target. So the old loopback
drop was NOT faithful -- both operands are real on one host: `complete` is the
RESPONDER-side operand (query-queryable's C=), `target` the REQUESTER-side operand
(query-target's).

THE FIX. Queryable<C> stores `complete`; register_sink (the SSOT) threads it, and
the convenience wrappers default it false (zenoh builder default). matches() gains
`target: Option<QueryTarget>` and the middle conjunct as `!self.complete && target
== Some(AllComplete) -> reject` (the exact negation of zenoh's term). target threads
through fire_matching_queryables / local_query / dispatch_borrowed (the MCU no-heap
sibling, swept, not left behind); dispatch_request reads it off the wire via
read_request_target (no signature change -- target rides the Request envelope).
Session::declare_queryable registers via register_sink with options.complete -- the
SAME value stamped onto the wire ext, so table and wire agree by construction. The
handler still never sees target (QueryView exposes no target accessor); target
reaches only the dispatch predicate, exactly as zenoh's handle_query does. The pico
C-API funnels through the same runtime declare_queryable (faces.rs), covered without
a separate edit.

THE REVIEW-FOUND BUG (two of three adversarial reviewers, independently). The first
cut of the loopback fed the RAW pub field opts.target into local_query. But target /
consolidation / timeout are runtime-tokio TERMINAL features gated by the accessor
QueryOptions::effective_target() (the last-hop-that-knows), NOT by a session-core
forward -- and QueryOptions.target is an ungated pub field whose write bypasses the
cfg gate (R311y317 litigated exactly this on the wire side). query-target = ["query-get"]
and neither query-get nor query-queryable pulls it, so {query-get, query-queryable,
query-target OFF} is a reachable build; there the wire leg (effective_target()->None)
fires both queryables while the raw-field loopback applied AllComplete and skipped the
incomplete one -- the two legs disagree, re-opening the y317 bypass on a new leg. FIX:
both loopback sites now pass opts.effective_target(), mirroring the wire path; the
querier.rs target-field doc is corrected (never read self.target on a dispatch path).

(take_pending_final_rids fn-level cfg asymmetry, observer.rs) is untouched, and (2)
hosting / (4) count stand. query-target: the loopback branch is now correct in code
and locally guarded, but the guard rides only local Layer C1an; its wire twin is
HOSTED in C1bk. Until the loopback guard is hosted in feature-gates, and the atom's
stale `source` pointer is corrected, query-target stays PARTIAL -- then COMPLETE.

Round 311y335.decision_summary:
R311y335 -- two METHOD misses from R311y334, both caught by the gates rather than
by me, both recorded here because the round's own prose claimed otherwise.

MISS 1 -- THE CALLER SWEEP WAS crates/-SCOPED. R311y334 changed three public
signatures (QueryableRegistry::register_sink, local_query, dispatch_borrowed) and
swept for callers with `grep -rn ... crates/`. That sweep is structurally blind to
deploy/*, which are SEPARATE CARGO WORKSPACES: no `cargo build` run from crates/
ever compiles them, so every subset build the round cited (no-alloc, alloc-only,
full-query) passed while deploy/mcu-noheap-probe was broken. The pre-push Layer Q
gate caught it: error[E0061] "this method takes 4 arguments but 3 were supplied",
twice per target, on the probe's qs.register_sink / qs.dispatch_borrowed. The probe
is the MCU no-heap exerciser of exactly the un-gated control plane y334 touched --
the one consumer most likely to break, and the one the sweep could not see.
FIXED: /*complete=*/ false + /*target=*/ None at the two sites; semantics unchanged
(an incomplete queryable under a BestMatching/None target still fires, so the
probe's `query_fired == 1` assertion is untouched). R311y334's verification bullet
"subset builds compile" was TRUE of the crates/ workspace and MISLEADING as a
whole-tree claim; this entry is the correction. THE RULE: a signature change is
swept REPO-WIDE (`grep -rn --include=*.rs .`), never crates/-scoped. deploy/* being
separate workspaces was already a recorded fact in this project; the round had it
and did not apply it.

MISS 2 -- `git push 2>&1 | tail` REPORTS THE PIPE'S EXIT CODE. The push was run
through a pipe, the harness reported exit 0, and the round announced the push had
landed. It had not: run-ci had FAILED Layer Q and pre-push rejected the ref. `tail`
exited 0; git push did not. This is the same exit-code-behind-a-pipe trap R311y325
/ y326 recorded, and the y333 rule ("cite the `test result:` / panic line, never the
exit code") is its sibling. THE RULE: never read success from a piped command's
status -- check ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, or read the command's own output for its verdict
(here: "pre-push: CI-equivalent gate failed", plainly in the tail I did print).

NOT A FLAKE. Layer Q carries a known qemu load flake, and the footprint gate is the
documented first check for it -- footprint was clean (text/data/bss all (+0) OK on
every target), which is exactly what proved this was a genuine build break and not
the flake. The diagnosis path worked; the sweep that should have prevented it did
not.

Round 311y336.decision_summary:
R311y336 -- the promotion round for R311y334's two atoms. query-target reaches
COMPLETE; query-queryable does NOT, because the review found a fifth, unledgered
residual on its own C= surface -- one that y334 widened.

WHAT LANDED. (1) query-queryable's residual (3): `take_pending_final_rids` is
signature-stable, the `#[cfg(query-queryable)]` removed. The gate was GRATUITOUS,
verified before touching it: `pending_final_rids` is an UNCONDITIONAL field
(R311r: "staging buffers are unconditional so the observer struct shape is stable
across consumer-feature subsets"), so the body compiles in every subset; only the
populate route is gated, and the field is private, so no subset can hold rids with
the feature off. The asymmetry was inverted from its own description: the PRIVATE
drains kept stable signatures while the PUBLIC accessor vanished. (2)
query-target's hosting residual: the loopback pub-field guard moved from the local
C1an stopgap into Layer C1bk -- the feature-gates job's query pub-field row, beside
the wire twin it mirrors. C1bk's subset now composes `query-queryable` directly and
its `--list` SET pin names four guards, so a rename or cfg elision fails red. Both
were pushed and run GREEN ON HOSTED CI before either tag was written: "HOSTED" had
to be demonstrated, not merely wired.

THREE INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWERS, arbitrated by direct read. The mechanical
halves were clean. They returned three things that changed the outcome:

CHANGE 1 -- query-target's `source` blocker is REFUTED, and it was MY error. y334's
reason closed with "TO CLOSE: host the loopback guard AND fix the source pointer".
The second half regressed against R311y330, which had already ruled the
dead-pointer `source` fields "a schema round, not a side-effect" -- no
`set-inventory-source` primitive exists. The killer is a sibling: `query-timeout`
is ALREADY COMPLETE and its own reason names the identical defect and disposes of
it as a non-blocker. Holding query-target to a bar its identical sibling is exempt
from is a mis-scoped criterion, not an impl residual. Retracted in-reason rather
than dropped silently, so the frozen prose does not contradict itself.

CHANGE 2 -- query-queryable is NOT COMPLETE. RESIDUAL (5): a RESOLVABLE query
matching ZERO queryables gets no ResponseFinal on the wire leg (`if matched > 0`
stages the terminator, conflating "dispatched, zero matched" with the two cases
that legitimately owe nothing). Confirmed against both upstreams by direct read:
zenoh builds `query_inner` unconditionally (session.rs:2440-2450) and
`Drop for QueryInner` (queryable.rs:75-83) sends the Final, gating only the
callback loop; pico is explicit (queryable.c:246-252, `if (qle_nb == 0) { ...
_z_session_send_reply_final(...); }`). And wz's OWN two legs disagree -- the
loopback emits `deliver_local_final` unconditionally, so the wire leg is the
wrong one. y334 WIDENED it: `matched` now flows through the new completeness
filter, so an AllComplete query matching only incomplete queryables newly reaches
matched==0 and starves the requester to timeout. It was protected by wz's own
prose ("no queryable matched ... we owe no Final") and was UNLEDGERED (store grep:
0). A follow-up round owns the fix; it is not folded into a promotion round.

CHANGE 3 -- the doc on the loopback guard named a lane this round DELETED (and had
misnamed local C1an a "feature-gates row" since y334). Fixed. Two reviewers found
it independently; it was, as always, a sentence I wrote.

ALSO MEASURED, not this atom's: C1bk's SET pin cannot catch an `#[ignore]` --
`--list` prints an ignored test identically, so the pin would stay at four while
the run reported `1 ignored` and exited 0. Shared with C1j's y332 pins; a
catalog-wide hardening (assert `0 ignored` on set-pinned lanes), raised as a carry.
And query-queryable's residual (2) prose is now stale in the other direction: C1j
IS hosted and runs this atom's NEG pair green -- re-measured, not quoted.

Round 311y337.decision_summary:
R311y337 -- residual (5) closed: a RESOLVABLE query that matches ZERO queryables
now gets its ResponseFinal. query-queryable reaches COMPLETE.

THE DEFECT, found by the R311y336 review and confirmed by direct read of all four
legs. `dispatch_messages` staged the stream terminator only `if matched > 0`. But
`matched == 0` arises three ways and only two of them legitimately owe nothing: a
non-Query body, and an un-resolvable keyexpr. The third -- a resolvable query that
simply matched NOBODY -- silently inherited "owe nothing", and the requester was
left to wait out its own timeout for an answer that was never coming.

BOTH UPSTREAMS TERMINATE IT, and their structure is the fix's design. zenoh's wire
entry `Primitives::send_request` (src/api/session.rs:2769-2792) reaches
`handle_query` ONLY for a resolvable Query body: a non-Query body never enters the
match arm, and an unresolvable wire_expr takes `Err(err) => error!("Received Query
for unknown key_expr")` and returns. Inside `handle_query`, `QueryInner` is built
WITHOUT consulting the queryable set (:2440-2450); only the callback loop is gated
on `!queryables.is_empty()` (:2451), so a zero-match query never moves the inner
into a `Query`, drops it at scope end, and `impl Drop for QueryInner`
(src/api/queryable.rs:75-83) sends the ResponseFinal. pico states it outright:
`if (qle_nb == 0) { ...; _z_session_send_reply_final(zn, qid, is_local); return
_Z_RES_OK; }` (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/queryable.c:246-252) -- and it passes
`is_local`, so BOTH legs owe it. So the debt is "entered handle_query", NOT the
match count.

AND WZ'S OWN TWO LEGS DISAGREED -- the sibling tell that keeps finding real defects
here. The loopback leg already emitted `deliver_local_final` unconditionally; only
the wire leg keyed on matches. The loopback agreed with both upstreams; the wire leg
was the wrong one.

THE FIX. `dispatch_request` returns `DispatchOutcome { dispatched, matched }` and
the Final keys on `dispatched` -- wz's boundary equivalent of entering
`handle_query`. The two `NOT_DISPATCHED` returns map 1:1 onto zenoh's two
pre-`handle_query` exits. Every path that reaches the table and then fires nothing
-- empty table, locality filter, the y334 completeness filter, a non-intersecting
keyexpr, a chunk overflow -- lives INSIDE `fire_matching_queryables`, i.e. after
`dispatched = true`, so all of them owe a Final; that matches zenoh exactly, where
all three filter conjuncts run inside `handle_query` after the inner is built.
`Option<usize>` was rejected: it is `#[must_use]` and would have churned ~35
statement-position test call sites; a plain outcome struct does not.

R311y334 WIDENED THIS HOLE and that is why it surfaced now: the completeness filter
manufactures `matched == 0` on an ordinary path (ask AllComplete while only an
incomplete queryable is registered). A round closing one gap opened the road into
another.

TWO TESTS PINNED THE DEFECT and both were inverted:
`..._skips_final_when_no_queryable_matched` asserted `finals.is_empty()`, and
`..._emits_final_for_each_matched_request` asserted "unmatched rid 12 dropped".
`..._skips_final_when_keyexpr_unresolvable` was NOT touched -- it guards a real
arm that owes nothing, and it still passes under the reverted predicate, which is
what proves the two categories are distinguished rather than merged.

TWO INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWERS, arbitrated by direct read. Both clean. The
defect hunt found no double-Final: the four Final producers are disjoint (the wire
push is once per Request; the two drains empty the SAME Vec so the second sees it
empty; the loopback is requester-side; the router is a separate plane with its own
pending table), and `expected_finals` still matches the producer count. The COMPLETE
hunt could not refute the tag: wz's `Queryable` fields are 1:1 with zenoh's
`QueryableState` and pico's `_z_session_queryable_t`, the locality conjunct is
equivalent by truth table, replay re-stamps `complete`, and post-y337 the wire and
loopback legs agree.

THE REVIEW ALSO CORRECTED MY OWN PROSE, twice. (a) The reason credited only C1j for
this atom's hosted proofs and omitted C1e -- which matters, because wz-session-core
carries NO query features by default, so a bare `cargo test -p wz-session-core` runs
0 of the 40 query tests; C1e (hosted) is what runs y337's core proofs at all.
(b) My `DispatchOutcome` doc said zenoh builds `QueryInner` "UNCONDITIONALLY"; there
is a third guard at :2421-2423 (`state.primitives()`, a closed session). The claim
that matters -- built without consulting the queryable set -- stands; the wording
was imprecise and is fixed.
