Round 311y338.decision_summary:
R311y338 -- R311y337's fix broke an e2e fixture, because the fixture was built
on the defect. Rebuilt it on a peer that owns its own silence, and the rebuild
found a second, subtler version of the same mistake in my own design.

WHAT HAPPENED. y337 made a resolvable zero-match query get its ResponseFinal.
The pre-push gate then failed Layer E on
wz_ap_demo_query_timeout_fires_final_callback: "FINAL fired too early
(50.5ms)". R264 had built the --query-timeout-ms e2e on an acceptor that
declared no queryable, and documented the mechanism in its own header:
"Inbound Request(Query) has no matching responder, so no Response/ResponseFinal
goes back on the wire ... The Query effectively sinks at the peer." That was
never a property of the acceptor's configuration. It was y337's DEFECT. The
fixture had been standing on it for ~70 rounds, which is precisely why the
defect survived: a test depended on it.

THE RULE THIS ROUND BUYS: A FIXTURE'S PRECONDITION MUST BE OWNED BY THE
FIXTURE. If it is instead an emergent property of the code under test, the day
that code is correctly fixed is the day the test starts lying. R264's
precondition ("no reply ever arrives") was emergent, so the correct fix
inverted it.

THE REBUILD. `wz-e2e-silent-peer` -- a new wz-e2e-* test double whose only job
is to never answer. It completes the handshake, stays transport-alive
(keepalive / lease are driven, so the peer is UP and merely mute -- exactly
what a query timeout defends against), and hands inbound events to nobody. The
three rejected alternatives, each for the same reason: SIGSTOP-ing the acceptor
puts the silence in the OS's hands (racy, Unix-only); an unresolvable-keyexpr
peer puts it in the resolve path's current behaviour (rots when that changes);
a query-queryable-OFF wz-ap-demo puts it in a feature combination AND enshrines
a zenoh divergence as the reference fixture. All three borrow their silence.

THEN THE REBUILD FAILED THE SAME WAY, and this is the round's real finding. The
first cut leaned on the double's MANIFEST: omit codec-response /
codec-response-final / query-queryable and answering is "unrepresentable by
construction". `cargo tree -p wz-e2e-silent-peer -e features` agreed -- no
response plane. The e2e still failed at 50 ms. Cause, measured: I had built it
with `cargo build -p wz-ap-demo -p wz-e2e-silent-peer`, and CARGO UNIFIES
FEATURES ACROSS PACKAGES BUILT IN ONE INVOCATION. The double linked a `wz`
carrying the demo's response plane and answered the query. A manifest describes
a PACKAGE; unification is a property of the BUILD GRAPH. My "unrepresentable"
claim was true only of a solo build -- and the fixture would have gone green as
a happy-path test the first time someone folded the two builds into one line:
the same rot, one level up, in the very crate built to prevent it. (This is also
the project's own `-p A -p B` trap, which I had filed under `--all-features`
only.)

SO THE SILENCE MOVED INTO CODE THE DOUBLE OWNS: `run_silent_acceptor_e2e`
(wz-e2e-harness) drives the FSM with a deliberately empty dispatch closure, so
inbound events reach no application plane whatever the build graph enables.
PROVEN unification-proof: the e2e passes under the adversarial
`cargo build -p wz-ap-demo -p wz-e2e-silent-peer` that defeated the manifest.
The manifest's omission stays as defence in depth, and now says so instead of
claiming to be the guarantee.

ALSO PINNED: the two `DispatchOutcome::NOT_DISPATCHED` arms now have their own
registry-level proofs, so "a non-Query body / an unresolvable keyexpr owes
nothing" is no longer load-bearing for an e2e timeout fixture. The
non-Query-body arm had only a callback-level check; it now has a Final-level
one, completing the truth table: dispatched => exactly one Final whatever
`matched` is; not dispatched => none, ever.

AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN DIAGNOSIS. I first blamed y337 for the Layer E
failure and said so. A bisect in an isolated worktree refuted it: e3926f3,
0ab8657 (y334), 658fac0 (y336) and 99073f7 (y337) ALL pass the original fixture.
y337 did break it in the pre-push run (a wz-ap-demo acceptor legitimately
answers post-y337) -- but by the time I re-ran it, MY OWN unified build was
producing the identical 50 ms symptom from a different cause. Two causes, one
timing signature, and I had asserted the wrong one. Measure per commit; a
matching symptom is not a matching cause.

Round 311y339.decision_summary:
R311y339 -- the FIXTURE RULE audit y338 owed. Three parallel sweeps over the
whole fixture surface (108 e2e files, the 8 wz-e2e-* doubles, the unit and
test-support crates) found it CLEAN of R264's shape. The round's finding is
elsewhere: a claim family that has been retracted three times still had a live
member, sitting in the doc of the test that drives the very method where one of
those retractions landed.

THE AUDIT. R264's tell was never "depends on an absence" -- it was a fixture
header that states current wz behaviour as a RULE and rests its design on it.
Swept for exactly that. The a-m range is structurally incapable of the defect:
28 of its 32 files are layer3_* codec-parity DIFFERENTIALS, where an absence is
either fixture-constructed or the assertion itself, so a broken precondition
points at the disagreement instead of fabricating silence. The w-prefixed e2e
(where absence-shaped preconditions can exist at all) are clean -- every
negative arm gates on a POSITIVE witness first. The doubles are clean;
wz-e2e-silent-peer is the reference shape.

FOUR HYPOTHESES OF MY OWN, ALL REFUTED -- recorded so nobody re-asks them.
(1) The interest plane is the query plane's SIBLING, so it should carry y337's
zero-match-Final defect. It does not: router_forward.rs proves "empty current
dump -> only the terminating DeclareFinal", and local_token.rs stages the Final
OUTSIDE the match loop, documented "even when no token matched". y337's defect
did not generalise. (2) respond_to_interest_borrowed drops its Final under a
full staging buffer (`let _ = pending.push(Final)`). Unreachable:
MAX_LOCAL_TOKENS=8 + 1 <= MAX_PENDING_DECLARES=32, and every drain site drains
per EVENT -- one chain per window. The `let _` is dead defence. (3)
link_emitter_b6's pass-with-warning skip is vacuous in CI. False: the `ci` job
builds sce-codegen before Layer C1, and no sce-less job runs that crate. (4)
Another lane carries y338's `-p A -p B` unification trap. False: no multi-`-p`
single invocation exists in run-ci.sh or ci.yml.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND, and it is not a fixture. reply.rs's sweep_timed_out test
doc said "`effective_timeout_ms()` reads 0 with the feature off, so
`deadline_ms` stays None and this sweep sees nothing". y325 RETRACTED that exact
generalisation -- inside ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out, the very method the
test drives -- and named the shape: "true of the path the author was looking at,
false of its siblings". The retraction then landed only on the code y325 was
reading, and missed the test doc in the same file. The claim is false:
`register` is pub and ungated, and wz-ap-demo arms `deadline_ms` straight off
`--query-timeout-ms` (runner.rs:278-287) carrying ZERO `feature =
"query-timeout"` sites. The family's four other members are healthy -- y326
corrected session/mod.rs and advanced_subscriber.rs, and querier.rs's own doc
records TWO prior retractions plus y318's warning that "a retraction lands where
the author is looking". The rule was written into the code and the copy was
still missed.

AND THE SIBLING ASYMMETRY IT LED TO. query_with_timeout_ms_is_silent_noop_*
argued "one wire-parity assertion is the complete guard", and its assert message
claimed "no local deadline is armed" while observing only the frame. Its own
pub-field twin, 40 lines down, refutes it in prose: "a wire-only fix leaves this
armed and the assertion above still passes -- so the wire check alone cannot
guard this atom". C1j's lane comment repeated the same argued coverage. Of the
three metadata twins ONLY query-timeout has a non-wire observable -- which is
precisely why only its twin had to argue, and it argued wrong. It now OBSERVES.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/reply.rs: the sweep_timed_out test doc's "deadline_ms
stays None and this sweep sees nothing" retracted IN PLACE (y325's convention --
quote it, kill it, cite), naming where y325's own retraction landed and why it
missed this copy.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/tests.rs: the timeout SETTER twin now asserts
next_reply_deadline_ms() == None -- the second observable its own pub-field twin
had already proven the wire assert cannot cover. Its doc no longer argues the
shared-sentinel coupling, and the frame assert no longer claims what it cannot
see.
scripts/run-ci.sh: C1j's zget-reply-only comment claimed the guard "pins that the

Round 311y339.publishable_decision_summary:
R311y339 -- the FIXTURE RULE audit y338 owed. Three parallel sweeps over the
whole fixture surface (108 e2e files, the 8 wz-e2e-* doubles, the unit and
test-support crates) found it CLEAN of R264's shape. The round's finding is
elsewhere: a claim family that has been retracted three times still had a live
member, sitting in the doc of the test that drives the very method where one of
those retractions landed.

THE AUDIT. R264's tell was never "depends on an absence" -- it was a fixture
header that states current wz behaviour as a RULE and rests its design on it.
Swept for exactly that. The a-m range is structurally incapable of the defect:
28 of its 32 files are layer3_* codec-parity DIFFERENTIALS, where an absence is
either fixture-constructed or the assertion itself, so a broken precondition
points at the disagreement instead of fabricating silence. The w-prefixed e2e
(where absence-shaped preconditions can exist at all) are clean -- every
negative arm gates on a POSITIVE witness first. The doubles are clean;
wz-e2e-silent-peer is the reference shape.

FOUR HYPOTHESES OF MY OWN, ALL REFUTED -- recorded so nobody re-asks them.
(1) The interest plane is the query plane's SIBLING, so it should carry y337's
zero-match-Final defect. It does not: router_forward.rs proves "empty current
dump -> only the terminating DeclareFinal", and local_token.rs stages the Final
OUTSIDE the match loop, documented "even when no token matched". y337's defect
did not generalise. (2) respond_to_interest_borrowed drops its Final under a
full staging buffer (`let _ = pending.push(Final)`). Unreachable:
MAX_LOCAL_TOKENS=8 + 1 <= MAX_PENDING_DECLARES=32, and every drain site drains
per EVENT -- one chain per window. The `let _` is dead defence. (3)
link_emitter_b6's pass-with-warning skip is vacuous in CI. False: the `ci` job
builds sce-codegen before Layer C1, and no sce-less job runs that crate. (4)
Another lane carries y338's `-p A -p B` unification trap. False: no multi-`-p`
single invocation exists in run-ci.sh or ci.yml.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND, and it is not a fixture. reply.rs's sweep_timed_out test
doc said "`effective_timeout_ms()` reads 0 with the feature off, so
`deadline_ms` stays None and this sweep sees nothing". y325 RETRACTED that exact
generalisation -- inside ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out, the very method the
test drives -- and named the shape: "true of the path the author was looking at,
false of its siblings". The retraction then landed only on the code y325 was
reading, and missed the test doc in the same file. The claim is false:
`register` is pub and ungated, and wz-ap-demo arms `deadline_ms` straight off
`--query-timeout-ms` (runner.rs:278-287) carrying ZERO `feature =
"query-timeout"` sites. The family's four other members are healthy -- y326
corrected session/mod.rs and advanced_subscriber.rs, and querier.rs's own doc
records TWO prior retractions plus y318's warning that "a retraction lands where
the author is looking". The rule was written into the code and the copy was
still missed.

AND THE SIBLING ASYMMETRY IT LED TO. query_with_timeout_ms_is_silent_noop_*
argued "one wire-parity assertion is the complete guard", and its assert message
claimed "no local deadline is armed" while observing only the frame. Its own
pub-field twin, 40 lines down, refutes it in prose: "a wire-only fix leaves this
armed and the assertion above still passes -- so the wire check alone cannot
guard this atom". C1j's lane comment repeated the same argued coverage. Of the
three metadata twins ONLY query-timeout has a non-wire observable -- which is
precisely why only its twin had to argue, and it argued wrong. It now OBSERVES.

R311y340 -- three adversarial reviewers took y339 apart within the hour. Its
headline survives; almost everything I built around it does not. This entry
retracts y339's verdict, reverts its test change, and records the REAL defect my
own refutation buried.

WHAT SURVIVES. The y323 sentence in reply.rs ("`deadline_ms` stays None and this
sweep sees nothing") was genuinely false, and the retraction stands. A reviewer
tried the scope defence I invited -- read "the runtime" narrowly and the sentence
might hold -- and it fails harder than I argued: wz-ap-demo builds ONE
Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>> (runner.rs:777) and hands the SAME observer
to TokioSession::new, so the registry the demo arms ungated IS the runtime's own,
the one Session::sweep_expired_queries sweeps. No reading survives.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, #1 -- THE VERDICT. "The fixture surface is CLEAN of the
R264 shape. Do not re-run this sweep." UNEARNED, on four counts. (a) The blocker
I invoked to defer the strongest candidate is FALSE IN BOTH CONJUNCTS:
`/home/coin/zenoh-ref/plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager` and
`zenoh-backend-traits` EXIST, at tag 1.5.0 = the exact pin -- y302 cloned them --
and they were never needed anyway, because the zombie is a question about wz's
OWN types. My own memory FILE said "NOW PROVISIONED ... GRADABLE"; its INDEX line
still said "ABSENT -> UNGRADABLE", and I quoted the index. A blocker note is a
claim; I did not run it. (b) "Clean" cannot coexist with "the strongest
candidate was not graded" -- and "do not re-run" would have made the deferral
permanent, which is R264's own mechanism reproduced at the audit layer. (c) The
a-m argument proves 28 files and concludes over 32; the two excluded ap_demo_*
are LIVE FOREIGN-PEER e2e -- R264's own category -- and their headers use `//`
not `//!`, so a header sweep silently skips them. (d) The partition left ~75+
test files unswept, including crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/ = 58 files, larger
than the whole a-m range I gave a dedicated agent, and dense with this family.

GRADED, now that the blocker is gone: the zombie IS a borrowed precondition.
zenoh's StorageRuntimeInner holds ONE long-lived `session: Arc<Session>` -- the
Runtime's (zenoh-ref plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/lib.rs:99). zenoh
has no transient-client-session storage hosting at all, so there survival is by
construction. wz binds a StorageService to a TRANSIENT client Session's actions,
and its own production code papers over the result: "any zombie StorageService
the manager kept holds an Arc clone of this session's actions ... abort it
explicitly to avoid one lingering task per client" (wz-ap-demo runner, the
writer_handle.abort() site). The fixture's step-3 `Started` assert passes only
because of that. A lesser instance than R264 -- the header NAMES the zombie and
fences its claim rather than laundering it -- but a test pins the divergence in
place.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, #2 -- AND THIS IS THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING. I refuted
"respond_to_interest_borrowed drops its Final under a full staging buffer" by
sizing a PER-FRAME buffer against a PER-CHAIN worst case. An IterationEvent is a
FRAME, not an Interest: local_token.rs's dispatch_messages threads ONE `&mut
pending` across every Interest in `messages`, and the drain runs after the whole
frame. caps.rs SAYS SO, in the doc on the very constant I cited: "the buffer
accumulates across the Interests in a single poll batch, so the bound is sized
generously". 32 is 3.5 chains. Eight held tokens and four match-all CURRENT
Interests in one frame: chains 1-3 stage 27, chain 4 fills to 32, its token loop
breaks, and `let _ = pending.push(Final)` swallows the Err. That peer's CURRENT
query never resolves. I argued past my own SSOT.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, #3 -- MY OWN TEST CHANGE, REVERTED. The assert I added to
query_with_timeout_ms_is_silent_noop_* CANNOT FAIL. effective_timeout_ms()'s OFF
arm is a CONSTANT `{ 0 }` that never reads self.timeout_ms, and query_metadata()
threads that same accessor -- so under this cfg `opts.timeout_ms` is
unobservable by any assertion in the test. A leaked setter yields exactly the
state the pub-field twin already constructs, and that twin passes. Worse, the
twins' asymmetry was CORRECT and I broke it: under a wire-only-gate regression
the twin's raw field write arms a deadline and catches it, while the setter test
zeroes the field before the deadline path sees it. The twin NEEDS its deadline
assert; this one cannot use one. I mirrored the twin's text and not its reach --
and I retracted a conclusion that was true. y339's diagnosis of a "sibling
asymmetry" here was wrong in the direction that matters: the asymmetry was the
design.

Round 311y341.decision_summary:
R311y341 -- y340 called the dropped DeclFinal "THE REAL DEFECT, OWED A ROUND".
It is not a defect. It is unreachable, and I found that out the only way that
would have worked: by trying to REPRODUCE it instead of arguing about it.

THE ROUND'S SHAPE. y339 refuted the dropped Final with bad reasoning. A reviewer
broke the reasoning and asserted the defect was real, with closed-form arithmetic
over quoted code (8 tokens x 4 Interests in one frame = 36 items > 32 slots) and
an explicit note that no repro was executed. y340 accepted it. y341 wrote the
repro FIRST, per the rule y340 itself had just banked -- and the test PASSED.
That is what exposed the truth. The arithmetic was right; the profile was wrong.

WHY IT CANNOT HAPPEN. `BoundedVec<T, N>` has two backings, and its own
`capacity()` doc says so: "Advisory on the `alloc` backing (AP may exceed it);
the hard limit `push` enforces on the no-alloc backing."

Round 311y342.decision_summary:
R311y342 -- the user asked why I keep trying to prove things by READING code, and
why a test cannot confirm it outright. The question was right, and this round is
the answer: a real wire defect, found by reading, PROVEN by a failing test, and
fixed. First production behaviour change in four rounds.

THE DEFECT, and the test that proved it. wz emitted a keyexpr alias id that
NEITHER upstream can hold. zenoh types `DeclareKeyExpr.id` as `ExprId`, and
`pub type ExprId = u16` (zenoh-protocol core/wire_expr.rs); zenoh-pico's
`_z_decl_kexpr_t` holds `uint16_t _id`. wz's `send_declare_keyexpr` takes a u64
and validated only `== 0`. The codec carries the id as VLE u64 deliberately (the
shared wireexpr shape, per decl_kexpr.scxml), so an out-of-range id encodes
cleanly HERE and is structurally unreadable THERE.

Not argued -- measured. The new guard failed first, and its failure is the
evidence: `an alias id neither upstream can hold must not reach the wire: ()` --
`expect_err` panicking on `Ok(())` means `send_declare_keyexpr(65_536, ..)`
SUCCEEDED and put the frame on the wire. Then the gate, then green.

THE TELL WAS SIBLING ASYMMETRY. The id space has two ends. The lower one
(`== 0`) has had a gate AND a test since R300. The upper one had neither. And
after gating the declare half I swept the sibling again and found the SAME defect
unfixed in the retraction half: `send_undeclare_kexpr` emits without consulting
the mapping table (its own doc's "removing an absent id is a no-op" idempotence),
so gating declare never bounded it. It has no error channel, so its drop is
silent -- consistent with the contract that already drops its emit on a dead
link. Four tests: reject-too-wide + admit-u16::MAX, on both halves, so no
off-by-one hides in either.

FOUR OFF ARMS THAT ONLY PROSE DEFENDED. `decl_listener.rs` holds two listeners
whose feature-OFF arms are character-for-character identical
(`let _ = callback; Err(DeclListenerError::FeatureDisabled)`) and only the
subscriber one was ever pinned -- one file, two twins, one guarded. And
`announce_subscriber` / `announce_queryable` return the SAME `Ok(None)` a
legitimate session-local declare gets, so a regression that turned the announce
into a silent no-op ON a declare-* build would look identical from the caller's
side; `announce_subscriber`'s doc asserts "the local subscriber stays valid for
loopback ... only the router announce is elided" with nothing testing it. All
four now have guards that RUN on real C1j rows (handshake-only / pubsub-only /
queryable-only), asserted after Drop too, so the whole handle lifecycle is
wire-silent rather than just its construction.

ONE TAG EARNED, BY EXECUTION. `declare-undeclare` -> COMPLETE (COMPLETE 46 -> 47,
UNAUDITED 63 -> 62). Its 4x3 table -- four declare kinds x {encode, decode+apply,
test} -- is filled with no MISSING, and I RAN all four proofs rather than reading
them: 1 passed each. The keyexpr one needed the pubsub test module's own feature
union to compile at all; on a default `--lib` run it reports "0 passed; N
filtered out", a silent no-op that reads exactly like a green refutation. That
trap fired twice this round and was caught both times only by checking that the
COUNT MOVED.

WHAT I DID NOT TAG, deliberately. The other six declare atoms keep their
residuals: declare-final's sole gated fn `send_declare_final()` has zero callers
and emits `interest_id: None`, which pico HARD-ERRORS on (rx.c's
`_Z_ERR_MESSAGE_ZENOH_DECLARATION_UNKNOWN`) and which zenoh never emits -- every
working DeclFinal in this repo is liveliness-token's or codec-declare's.
declare-interest's Nonlocal (M=0) arm is parked while the DECLARE plane it points
at HAS its companions. declare-subscriber / -queryable still have unguarded
replay and matching-status OFF arms. This round shrank their residuals; it did
not close them, and COMPLETE would be a lie.

THE METHOD, restated because it cost this session to learn: READING FINDS, TESTS
PROVE. The u16 hole was FOUND by a code read -- but reading only ever reached
"PARTIAL, named residual". A test settled it in seconds and made the fix
checkable. Every failure earlier today (y339 reasoned, y340 direct-read-confirmed
a reviewer's arithmetic and was still wrong) came from stopping at the read. A3's
own docstring says tags are earned by CODE READ; that is the defect one level up.
A4 -- the axis that DERIVES which tests can witness a foreign impl and whether the
atom is even in the binary's feature closure -- is the shape A3 should borrow.

why a test cannot confirm it outright. The question was right, and this round is
the answer: a real wire defect, found by reading, PROVEN by a failing test, and
fixed. First production behaviour change in four rounds.

THE DEFECT, and the test that proved it. wz emitted a keyexpr alias id that
NEITHER upstream can hold. zenoh types `DeclareKeyExpr.id` as `ExprId`, and
`pub type ExprId = u16` (zenoh-protocol core/wire_expr.rs); zenoh-pico's
`_z_decl_kexpr_t` holds `uint16_t _id`. wz's `send_declare_keyexpr` takes a u64
and validated only `== 0`. The codec carries the id as VLE u64 deliberately (the
shared wireexpr shape, per decl_kexpr.scxml), so an out-of-range id encodes
cleanly HERE and is structurally unreadable THERE.

Not argued -- measured. The new guard failed first, and its failure is the
evidence: `an alias id neither upstream can hold must not reach the wire: ()` --
`expect_err` panicking on `Ok(())` means `send_declare_keyexpr(65_536, ..)`
SUCCEEDED and put the frame on the wire. Then the gate, then green.

THE TELL WAS SIBLING ASYMMETRY. The id space has two ends. The lower one
(`== 0`) has had a gate AND a test since R300. The upper one had neither. And
after gating the declare half I swept the sibling again and found the SAME defect
unfixed in the retraction half: `send_undeclare_kexpr` emits without consulting
the mapping table (its own doc's "removing an absent id is a no-op" idempotence),
so gating declare never bounded it. It has no error channel, so its drop is
silent -- consistent with the contract that already drops its emit on a dead
link. Four tests: reject-too-wide + admit-u16::MAX, on both halves, so no
off-by-one hides in either.

FOUR OFF ARMS THAT ONLY PROSE DEFENDED. `decl_listener.rs` holds two listeners
whose feature-OFF arms are character-for-character identical

legitimate session-local declare gets, so a regression that turned the announce
into a silent no-op ON a declare-* build would look identical from the caller's
side; `announce_subscriber`'s doc asserts "the local subscriber stays valid for
loopback ... only the router announce is elided" with nothing testing it. All
four now have guards that RUN on real C1j rows (handshake-only / pubsub-only /
queryable-only), asserted after Drop too, so the whole handle lifecycle is
wire-silent rather than just its construction.

R311y343 -- A3's own docstring said the implementation tag is earned by a CODE
READ. That is the defect one level up, and this round closes it: COMPLETE now
REQUIRES a test that names the atom's OWN cfg-necessary code, and the join is
DERIVED, never authored.

WHY NOW. R311y339-y341 spent three rounds naming residuals in prose and two of
them were WRONG. R311y342 then found a live wire defect -- a keyexpr alias id
wider than both upstreams' u16 -- that every read had only ever LABELLED
"PARTIAL, named residual"; a failing test settled it in seconds and the fix
followed in minutes. READING FINDS, TESTS PROVE. A3 was still grading by the
method that had just failed three times.

THE MACHINE (scripts/lib/atom_test_graph.py, invariant #6). graph() returns
atom -> (owned, test_named): the cfg-necessary symbols an atom owns, and which
of them any test context names. A4 already derives which tests witness a foreign
impl; this is A4's shape ported to A3. Nothing about the join is authored -- the
only thing a human writes is the atom's cfg, which already exists.

TWO DESIGNS DIED TO MEASUREMENT, and neither should be re-proposed. (1) A
cfg-to-cfg join CANNOT work: a sibling crate's integration test carries the
feature in its dependency MANIFEST and has no cfg to match. The live proof is
crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_fragment.rs:27 -- `use
wz_codecs::fragment::Fragment;` with ZERO `cfg(feature` in the whole file, the
feature arriving via wz-codecs' default set (Cargo.toml:53) and gating exactly
that module (wz-codecs/src/lib.rs:225). The join must go through the SYMBOL. The
script's own comment records the measured cost of the wrong design: it rejected
9 of 46 COMPLETE atoms, all false. (2) Necessity-by-EVALUATION is wrong under
any not() arm -- the second commit's whole subject. Evaluating a cfg with "X off,
everything else on" reads FALSE for EVERY feature of
`all(not(transport-multilink), any(.., declare-final, ..))`, so every feature
reads as necessary; measured, it credited declare-final with owning
`session_send_available`, which it merely OR-contributes to. NECESSITY IS
SATISFIABILITY: is there any build where this compiles WITHOUT X? Naming a
feature in a cfg is not owning the item.

IT BITES, and that was checked rather than assumed -- a gate that only ever
passes is decoration. Calibrated at 47 of 47 COMPLETE atoms passing (the audit
exits 0 with COMPLETE=47, and the gate's loop appends every COMPLETE atom whose
test-named set is empty, so exit 0 IS the 47/47). It fires on declare-final,
re-derived this round rather than quoted: owned = {send_declare_final},
test_named = {} -- an atom whose sole gated symbol no test can even name.
declare-final is tagged PARTIAL today, so the gate does not currently reject; the
point is that COMPLETE is now unreachable for it without a test.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. A NECESSARY condition, not a sufficient one. It proves the
atom's own gated code is reachable by some test; it does not prove the test
asserts the right thing. It cannot replace the read -- it bounds what a read is
allowed to conclude.

Round 311y344.decision_summary:
R311y344 -- the round set out to RATIFY a grammar widening and instead found the
machine underneath it broken. Three adversarial reviews killed the exemplar; then
measuring the machine's own output killed the machine. SIX distinct defects in
R311y343's atom<->test derivation, all live, all invisible, all one round old.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, and this is the whole lesson: R311y343 shipped
atom_test_graph.py CALIBRATED -- "47 of 47 COMPLETE atoms pass" -- and that
calibration was TRUE the entire time the derivation was wrong. A gate that only
ever passes cannot tell a correct derivation from a broken one. Every one of the
six was found by measuring the OUTPUT against the source; not one was findable by
re-reading the code, which is exactly the claim R311y343 itself was built to
make about atoms, applied one level up to the gate that makes it.

THE SIX, each proven by a fixture that is RED on 940b710 and green now:
  1. A cfg on an enum VARIANT is not a cfg inside a body. The walk-back looked
     only for an enclosing `fn`, sailed past the `enum` that actually encloses
     the variant, and landed on the last fn before the type. Measured on the real
     tree: `transport-link-vsock` OWNED `with_quic` -- a fn gated by
     `#[cfg(feature = "transport-link-quic")]`, 95 lines earlier.
  2. Same for a struct-form variant (`Udp { socket: .. }`).
  3. A cfg'd `impl` block declares no name, so it is not an item either -- 42
     sites, the largest class. `#[cfg(feat)] impl UdpDriver` resolved to
     `send_declare_final`. `impl<T> Trait<T> for WsDriver<T>` resolved to `poll`,
     a method of the PREVIOUS impl block.
  4. `const` is both an item kind and an fn modifier. Read left-to-right,
     `pub const fn encode_keep_alive()` parsed as a const ITEM whose NAME is the
     keyword `fn` -- an owned "symbol" no test can ever name.
  5. A test module is not the TAIL of its file. The src arm took the FIRST
     `#[cfg(test)]` and harvested every identifier to EOF. 161 src files carry
     top-level PRODUCTION items after their first test module; wz-runtime-tokio/
     src/lib.rs donated 58 of them (including `pub mod vsock_pipeline`) and one
     file donated 171. Production code was reading as test evidence.
  6. A TEST THAT NEVER RUNS IS NOT A TEST. The reference arm never looked at
     `#[ignore]`. 78 of this tree's 332 test regions execute NOTHING and every
     one of them was supplying evidence. This repo has named that disease twice
     ("a proof that never runs is not a proof"; "a skip is green") and it was
     installed in the gate built to enforce it.

THE EXEMPLAR DIED FIRST, and it died the right way. The design retagged
`transport-link-vsock` UNVERIFIED on the strength of its reason -- "the backend
is genuinely built ... but the round-trip is #[ignore]d" -- reading that as a
pure LANE gap. A reviewer refuted it and direct read confirmed: `bind_locator`
returns `io::Result<TcpListener>` by signature and wires only `Proto::Tcp`
(session_open.rs:780/:789); the vsock arm returns `unsupported` (:826-829) in the
SAME words the design quoted to disqualify quic. vsock shares the accept-seam
residual, so "no code is missing" is false. The reason had not rotted in its
cites -- every line number was exact -- it rotted by OMISSION: R311y305 audited
vsock, quic and quic-datagram in one round, named the accept gap for two, and
left it out of the third. Only the SIBLING sweep catches that, and I did not do
one. The right discriminator was there all along and I reached past it: quic's
e2e RUNS (quic_e2e.rs:17 "Fully runnable (NO #[ignore])", C1ac at run-ci.sh:1127
passes no --ignored), which is why quic is not UNVERIFIED.

rather than believed; the walk now shares `_attr_end`'s paren balancing with

Round 311y345.decision_summary:
R311y345 -- the user asked whether the test cases for zenoh+pico FULL were all
in place. They were not, and the honest answer to why is that R311y339-y344 spent
SIX rounds on the audit machinery and none on the thing it audits. This round
stops describing the gap and starts closing it: two atoms move from "no foreign
witness at all" to proven, each by a test whose RED was demonstrated first.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ACTUALLY SAID. `preset-ap-full` is 136 atoms, read from the
Cargo preset -- the SSOT -- rather than the store section, which says of itself
that it was "transcribed from Cargo preset-ap-full". FORTY of the 136 had zero
cross-impl proof: not scattered, but whole planes at once (all 8 locators, all 5
scouting atoms, 4 session extensions, the 3 access-* interceptors). Catalog-wide
the axis read proven=58 partial=31 unproven=71 against a denominator of 160, and
the corpus behind it was 78 files / 157 tests, of which only SIX witness zenohd.

TRANSPORT-KEEPALIVE -- the sibling-asymmetry tell, again. It had a dozen
host-side tests and zero foreign proof, while its codec twin `codec-keep-alive`
was proven against pico by layer3_keep_alive.rs's byte-parity. The BYTES were
checked against pico and the BEHAVIOUR never was -- and a KeepAlive that is
byte-perfect but emitted too late keeps nothing alive. The new test makes pico's
own lease timer the judge: the demo holds its burst 14s past Established, wider
than the 10s adopted lease, and a Put that still lands proves the KeepAlive held
the line open. Nothing in wz asserts it.

RED, and it was exact: with the emit suppressed, the demo's own log reads
`publisher_task holding the burst` at :21 and `session ended: Terminated` at :31
-- EXACTLY the 10s lease -- with `ActionTrace { .. send_keep_alive: 0 .. }`
naming the cause. Ten seconds of silence, and pico expired wz.

TRANSPORT-BATCHING -- COMPLETE on A3, and never once witnessed. Its A3 tag says
"a REAL measured TX buffer ... No residual"; its A4 line said unproven. That
combination is exactly what the north star turns on: the code is built, and
nobody had checked that the frame it emits is one a foreign peer can read. Not a
hypothetical -- wz's batcher is deliberately STRICTER than the pico primary it
mirrors (its own reason: pico "blind-appends mixed reliability" where wz enforces
zenoh's CurrentFrame/NewFrame homogeneity), so the two ends do NOT agree by
construction, which is the case only a real peer settles.

RED, and it VALIDATED THE ASSERTION'S SHAPE, which is the round's sharpest
result: dropping ONE byte from the flushed chain makes z_sub surface 4 of 5 --
not 0. pico walks the chain, decodes four, and stops at the truncated fifth. So
`wait_for_substring("Received")` -- "at least one arrived", the shape every
sibling test in this family uses -- PASSES that corrupted frame. Only a COUNT
catches it. Measured, not reasoned, and it is the difference between a test and
a decoration.

TWO DEMO KNOBS, and why they had to exist. Layer E's witness is `wz-ap-demo`, and
its publisher was a fixed script: wait for Established, then burst 5 Pushes at
200ms. No knob could produce an idle window (the default fires at once;
`--reconnect`'s long-lived mode publishes on a cadence), and none could produce a
batched frame -- the demo never called `batch_start`, so `batch.active` was
always false and the demo had NEVER batched. `--publish-after-ms` and `--batch`
are the two orderings, both in the family of the existing `--connect-after` /
`--unsubscribe-after-data`. `--publish-after-ms` is deliberately NOT cfg-gated on
transport-keepalive: it is a pure delay, and it MUST stay inert with the feature
off, because the keepalive-OFF build is exactly the anti-vacuity arm the proof
rests on.

BOTH TESTS OWN THEIR PRECONDITION (R311y338's fixture rule). A 14s wait that
succeeds would ALSO pass if the burst fired at t=0, and 5 receipts are
indistinguishable batched or not -- so each test asserts the demo's own bracket
lines FIRST, in order, and refuses to conclude anything until the window it needs
is confirmed open.

WHAT I FOUND OUT ABOUT THE REST, and it is not encouraging. Of the 38 ap-full
atoms still unproven, only TEN are in `preset-ap-client`, the preset the demo
builds; the other 28 need a different binary or preset. Within the ten,
liveliness-get/-history need an ordering the demo cannot produce, session-reconnect
needs a listening peer (pico CLIs are all clients, so it means zenohd -- absent
here, and hosted CI never runs Layer Z), and locator-tcp/-udp raise a question
this round did not answer: a locator string is LOCAL configuration a foreign peer
never sees, so whether those 8 belong in A4's denominator at all is a design
question, not a missing test.

200ms. No knob could produce an idle window (the default fires at once;
`--reconnect`'s long-lived mode publishes on a cadence), and none could produce a
batched frame -- the demo never called `batch_start`, so `batch.active` was
always false and the demo had NEVER batched. `--publish-after-ms` and `--batch`
are the two orderings, both in the family of the existing `--connect-after` /
`--unsubscribe-after-data`. `--publish-after-ms` is deliberately NOT cfg-gated on
transport-keepalive: it is a pure delay, and it MUST stay inert with the feature
off, because the keepalive-OFF build is exactly the anti-vacuity arm the proof
rests on.

succeeds would ALSO pass if the burst fired at t=0, and 5 receipts are
indistinguishable batched or not -- so each test asserts the demo's own bracket
lines FIRST, in order, and refuses to conclude anything until the window it needs
is confirmed open.

Round 311y347.decision_summary:
R311y347 -- the user's correction was the round's premise: ap AND pico must ALL be
full, so BUILD, do not grade. R311y339-y346 were seven rounds on the audit
machinery and none on the coverage it audits. This round closes `session-matching`
against a real zenoh-pico peer, from ZERO.

WHY THIS ATOM, DERIVED RATHER THAN PICKED: of `preset-ap-full`'s 38 atoms with no
foreign witness, only NINE are in `preset-ap-client` -- what wz-ap-demo actually
builds. Three of those nine are genuinely blocked (liveliness-get/-history need an
ordering the demo cannot make; session-reconnect needs a LISTENING peer, i.e.
zenohd). Two more sit behind R311y345's unanswered locator-8 denominator fork. That
leaves four, and `session-matching` is the one whose witness is strongest.

WHAT MAKES THIS ATOM UNUSUAL, AND WHY IT IS THE BEST WITNESS IN THE FOUR: wz does
not have to SEND anything for the proof to bind. A matching listener fires on every
status TRANSITION caused by an INBOUND remote Declare/UndeclSubscriber. So pico is
not a receiver being checked against wz's bytes -- pico is the CAUSE and wz is the
thing under test. That inverts the corpus's usual shape, and it is exactly the
axis rule "pico does not implement X" != "pico cannot witness X".

BOTH EDGES ARE PICO'S, and the second one is free: z_sub.c's loop breaks once its
-n count is met and then runs z_drop(z_move(sub)) (:91), which retracts the
declaration. So `z_sub -n 1` gives a declare AND an undeclare with no demo-side
choreography at all. wz has no local subscriber in this fixture, so nothing else
could have raised the status.

THE RED, and it is the sharp half: suppressing ONLY the undeclare arm's
matching_watches.reevaluate (declare/subscriber.rs) left matching=true firing
normally and matching=false never arriving. So the second edge is load-bearing --
a listener that fired once and latched would pass a one-edge test -- and the twin
arm surviving is what proves the assertion NARROWS rather than disables. Measured
on the real binary, not argued.

THE CFG SPLIT IS THE DESIGN FINDING, and it decides what the test may touch.
`Publisher::declare_matching_listener` is
`#[cfg(all(feature = "session-matching", feature = "declare-subscriber"))]`, but its
sibling `Publisher::get_matching_status` is gated on `declare-subscriber` ALONE and
conservatively returns false when that registry is elided. So the POLL is not this
atom's code: a proof that polled would have bound the claim to the wrong atom and
looked entirely reasonable doing it. The knob installs the CALLBACK for that reason
and no other.

MY OWN TEST CAUGHT MY OWN DESIGN BUG, which is the case for anti-vacuity arms.
The first run FAILED at the "listener installed" assertion, not at an edge -- the
demo installs its handles at run_demo scope, which it reaches only AFTER a peer
connects, so waiting for that line BEFORE spawning z_sub deadlocked the test
against the demo. Without that arm the failure would have been a timeout on
matching=true and I would have gone looking at pico. The ordering that replaced it
is safe STRUCTURALLY rather than luckily: an inbound Declare is dispatched by the
drive loop, and the drive loop starts after install_session_handles returns.

AND A LEDGER COUNT THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. R311y345's verification says this
lane's "passed total moved 39 -> 41". Measured this round with two independent
instruments and a SET diff: the baseline is 40 and adding this test makes 41, with
the set difference being exactly this test and nothing else. R311y345's commits

correction lands here, as a new entry, not as an edit to y345.

WHAT MAKES THIS ATOM UNUSUAL, AND WHY IT IS THE BEST WITNESS IN THE FOUR: wz does
not have to SEND anything for the proof to bind. A matching listener fires on every
status TRANSITION caused by an INBOUND remote Declare/UndeclSubscriber. So pico is
not a receiver being checked against wz's bytes -- pico is the CAUSE and wz is the

R311y348 -- the user stopped me mid-round: "why do you keep READING? didn't we agree
to build the test and let it decide?" They were right, and the cost of my being
wrong was about to be a headline number. I had spent the round reading, had built an
argument to EXCLUDE the 8 locator-* atoms from A4's denominator (160 -> 152), and had
just handed it to two reviewers to ARGUE about. One 12-second run settled it instead,
and settled it against me.

THE FORK IS ANSWERED: THE 8 STAY. R311y345 raised it on the premise that "a locator
string is LOCAL configuration a foreign peer never sees". THE PREMISE IS FALSE. Run
wz-ap-demo --peer + a real pico z_get at `@/**` and pico prints:
`@/<zid>/peer: {"locators":["tcp/127.0.0.1:58501"], ...}`. wz PUTS its locators on
the wire and a foreign implementation reads them. The exclusion would have been
wrong, and every step of the argument for it was individually defensible.

AND THE ARTIFACT IS THE ATOM'S, measured both ways before a line of test was
written: handed the BARE `127.0.0.1:P` (no scheme), pico reads back
`tcp/127.0.0.1:P`; handed `tcp/127.0.0.1:P`, pico reads back the same canonical
form. So wz's locator layer PARSED the bare form, canonicalised it, and rendered it
into a payload that crossed the wire. The `tcp/` cannot be an argv echo. That round
trip is `locator-tcp`, and pico decoding it is the foreign half.

WHAT MY ARGUMENT WAS, AND WHY IT LOOKED SOUND -- this is the part worth keeping. The
8 reasons all say "the parse is always-on; the cfg toggle is forward target
transport-link-X; cfg=0". Their cargo keys are `locator-tcp = ["transport-link-tcp"]`
-- byte-for-byte the shape of `link-batching = ["transport-batching"]`, which IS
excluded as a category-(2) alias. And crossimpl_audit.py's own comment (:420) says of
the alias-shaped FOUNDATIONALs -- a list that NAMES the 8 -- "which is why an alias
belongs in that set". Reasons, cargo shape, and the file's own sentence all agreed.
They were all agreeing about the wrong thing.

THE REVIEWER LANDED THREE KILLS I DID NOT HAVE, and the first is aimed at me. (1)
ALL EIGHT CITATIONS IN THOSE REASONS HAVE ROTTED: locator-tcp cites "locator.rs:144
Proto::Tcp"; :144 is inside a doc comment, the arm is :183. Same for all eight, dial
side included. I quoted eight reasons VERBATIM as my evidence and opened NOT ONE of
them -- the exact defect this repo has named repeatedly, committed by me in the round
where I was reasoning about whether prose can be trusted. (2) The premise is false on
THREE surfaces, not the one I found: the scouting HELLO carries a locator list behind
_Z_FLAG_T_HELLO_L (wz-codecs/src/lib.rs:677, scouting_glue.rs:453-457), linkstate
advertises per-node locators, and the adminspace renders them. My test found the
third. (3) locator-tcp is PROVEN-BUT-UNTAGGED today: pubkey_zenohd_interop.rs:164
calls parse_any_locator("tcp/127.0.0.1:{port}") in-process and dials a real zenohd,
claiming only the extauth atoms. Confirmed by direct read.

MY NARROWING WAS CHERRY-PICKING, and the reviewer's discriminator is better than
mine. I derived 18 sibling-aliases from cargo, found 3 in the exclusion set, and
narrowed to the 8 on the judgement that "io_uring is a different capability that
merely REQUIRES tokio". That judgement is right and it is NOT derived -- and applied
to locator-tcp it gives the OPPOSITE answer: the parse grammar is a different
capability that merely accompanies the dial backend. The discriminator that actually
works is "does the atom name an artifact of its OWN?" -- link-batching names none
(the code is transport-batching's; one thing, two names), locator-tcp names a real
always-compiled parse arm. Two artifacts with one gated is a MISLABELLED atom, not
an alias. And A4 counts LAYERS anyway: wz_e2e_queryable_to_zget.rs claims eleven
atoms on one path, a codec atom beside its transport atom on the same bytes.

R311y349 -- R311y348's ANSWER survives and its HEADLINE ARGUMENT does not. A review
that landed after that entry was frozen found the reasoning is a category error, and
direct read confirms it. The correction lands here because the ledger is frozen.

THE ERROR. y348 killed the locator-8 exclusion by running a fixture and showing that
wz PUTS its locators on the wire (`@/<zid>/peer` renders `{"locators":["tcp/..."]}`;
a real pico z_get decodes it). That refutes "a foreign peer never sees it" -- which
is the CATEGORY (1) predicate. But the exclusion I was proposing was CATEGORY (2),
and crossimpl_audit.py:45-49 defines category (2) as OBSERVABLE by construction:
"aliases / re-views -- observable, but the observable BELONGS TO a counted vehicle
atom ... Exclusion here is DE-DUPLICATION, not non-observability." So "pico decoded
the string" does not settle the de-dup question at all. I refuted a premise I was not
relying on, declared victory, and wrote it up as the headline.

WHAT ACTUALLY SETTLES IT was in the test's own docstring, one paragraph down, doing
the work while the headline took the credit: the test "proves the RENDER half of the
atom and not the DIAL half; the dial half belongs to transport-link-tcp". That is
SEPARABILITY, and separability is the whole question.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, now stated properly (the reviewer's, and it is better than mine):
DOES THE VEHICLE'S OWN FOREIGN PROOF NECESSARILY WITNESS X'S OBSERVABLE?
  YES -> X is a re-view; its witness IS V's witness; category (2); exclude.
  NO  -> X names a SEPARABLE observable that merely happens to be co-resident in V's
         compile unit. A distinct capability REQUIRING V. Keep it; it owes a witness.
Operational, and falsifiable: CAN YOU WRITE A TEST THAT WITNESSES X AND FAILS WHILE
V'S OWN PROOF STILL PASSES? For locator-tcp the answer is yes and y348 WROTE it --
transport-link-tcp's dial proofs pass regardless of whether the canonical string ever
renders. The test was the right answer to a question its own ledger asked wrong.
The trap this kills: "compiled together" != "same artifact". Cargo shape cannot
discriminate -- if X = [V] and X has 0 cfg sites, `--features X` and `--features V`
are byte-identical builds, and that is equally true of link-batching (a real re-view)
and scouting-gossip (not one). Which is exactly why reading the cargo keys produced a
confident wrong answer twice.

AND MY EVIDENCE 3 WAS NOT MERELY OVER-GENERALISED -- IT IS FALSE. y348 cited
crossimpl_audit.py:420-421 ("...which is why an alias belongs in that set") as the
file arguing my conclusion. Read prescriptively it turns the gate RED on SIX
COMMITTED CLAIMS: keyexpr-canon carries six `wz-proves` lines in
layer3_keyexpr_canon.rs, and the reviewer falsified this in a scratch harness rather
than arguing it. Read descriptively it is still false: the "only because" is
circular -- the A4-5 containment guard keys on `status == "active"`, and every one of
the 57 FOUNDATIONAL atoms is `reserved`, so containment never fires on them whether
or not FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE exists. FNO does none of the work that sentence
credits it with. The defect is confined to the comment; the code is right.
And the mechanism is this repo's own rule: R311y314 corrected that paragraph's LIST
and left the CONCLUSION the list existed to support untouched -- a retraction landing
where someone looked, inside the sentence that cites the lesson.

FOUR OF THE FIFTEEN WERE NEVER LIVE. y348 derived 18 sibling-aliases, found 3 in FNO,
and worried about 15. Four of those -- access-extauth-jwt and routing-static-routes
(deprecated/PHANTOM), routing-failover (BEYOND-PICO), runtime-tokio-uring (UNBUILT) --
are not in `built` at all, so adding them to FNO is a no-op on the denominator and
would only make the printed exclusion count overstate itself. Only 11 were ever live.

SEPARABILITY VERDICTS the review produced, worth keeping because each is an atom's

Round 311y350.decision_summary:
R311y350 -- the pre-push gate caught three breaks my own gates could not. LEDGER ENTRY
WRITTEN RETROACTIVELY, following R311y297's precedent: the fix shipped and pushed as
dde45d5 without an entry because the CI fire drill that became y351 ended the session
before the ledger step. The commit is unchanged and stays the record of what landed;
this entry is the audit trail it never got.

THE THREE BREAKS, in the order they surfaced, each one from fixing the last:

(1) DELETING A STUB LEFT ITS FEATURE GATING A DEAD IMPORT. session_actions.rs gated
`use crate::declare_build::*;` on a 5-feature any(...) list including `declare-final`.
Once `send_declare_final` was deleted, nothing reachable under `declare-final` ALONE
touched declare_build -- so the import is dead in exactly the subset the file's own
comment two lines up predicts: C4c's `liveliness-sub-only` = codec-declare +
declare-interest + liveliness-subscriber, which pulls declare-final and reaches no
builder. Under deny(warnings) that is a build break.

(2) LAYER E SWEPT THE LOCATOR TEST ONTO A DEMO THAT CANNOT SERVE IT. The cross-impl
witness committed at 7999af2 needs wz-ap-demo built with routing-peer +
adminspace-introspection-handlers. Layer E is a CATCH-ALL that runs `--ignored`
directly (run-ci.sh:4107) against a DEFAULT-feature demo which rejects `--peer`, so
`#[ignore]` is no shield -- only the test's NAME is, via `--skip wz_peer`. The name
was load-bearing and I did not know it.

(3) MY OWN FIX-COMMENT FOR (2) STRANDED THE ATTRIBUTE IT EXPLAINED. I put the
explanatory block BETWEEN `#[test]` and `#[ignore]`; Layer C0 requires adjacency. An
insertion that reads harmlessly is exactly how an attribute gets stranded -- and (3)
exists ONLY because I was fixing (2).

WHY MY GATES SAW NONE OF IT. y346 DID check (1): its ledger records "wz-session-core
--features declare-final rc=0 with no unused warning". That is a SOLO build, which
pulls consumers that DO reach declare_build. The break lives only where declare-final
arrives TRANSITIVELY and no builder is reached. The check passed because it was aimed
at the wrong UNIT, not because the code was sound. Worse, diagnosing it, my hand-run
of "C4c's exact command" returned rc=0 THREE TIMES while `run-ci.sh --layer C4c`
reproduced instantly. A HAND-COPIED LANE COMMAND IS A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE LANE.

AND (2) IS THE THIRD OF ITS EXACT KIND. run-ci.sh:4098-4106 records the other two in
its own comments: R311qg ("the lane-wiring gap a full run-ci surfaced") and R311y277
(wz_storage_host -- "E6h ran the right binary, but this catch-all also ran it against
the default one", surfaced by the y277 push's pre-push full run-ci). Three times, a
new binary-dep test met the catch-all sweep; three times the pre-push hook was the
thing that found it. The trap is structural, not carelessness, and nothing warns at
authoring time.

-subscriber / -queryable / -token. The list names the features under which the glob IS

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_locator_render_to_pico_zget.rs RENAMED to

WRITTEN RETROACTIVELY, following R311y297's precedent: the fix shipped and pushed as
dde45d5 without an entry because the CI fire drill that became y351 ended the session
before the ledger step. The commit is unchanged and stays the record of what landed;
this entry is the audit trail it never got.

THE THREE BREAKS, in the order they surfaced, each one from fixing the last:

(1) DELETING A STUB LEFT ITS FEATURE GATING A DEAD IMPORT. session_actions.rs gated
`use crate::declare_build::*;` on a 5-feature any(...) list including `declare-final`.
Once `send_declare_final` was deleted, nothing reachable under `declare-final` ALONE
touched declare_build -- so the import is dead in exactly the subset the file's own
comment two lines up predicts: C4c's `liveliness-sub-only` = codec-declare +
declare-interest + liveliness-subscriber, which pulls declare-final and reaches no
builder. Under deny(warnings) that is a build break.

(2) LAYER E SWEPT THE LOCATOR TEST ONTO A DEMO THAT CANNOT SERVE IT. The cross-impl
witness committed at 7999af2 needs wz-ap-demo built with routing-peer +
adminspace-introspection-handlers. Layer E is a CATCH-ALL that runs `--ignored`
directly (run-ci.sh:4107) against a DEFAULT-feature demo which rejects `--peer`, so
`#[ignore]` is no shield -- only the test's NAME is, via `--skip wz_peer`. The name
was load-bearing and I did not know it.

(3) MY OWN FIX-COMMENT FOR (2) STRANDED THE ATTRIBUTE IT EXPLAINED. I put the
explanatory block BETWEEN `#[test]` and `#[ignore]`; Layer C0 requires adjacency. An
insertion that reads harmlessly is exactly how an attribute gets stranded -- and (3)
exists ONLY because I was fixing (2).

WHY MY GATES SAW NONE OF IT. y346 DID check (1): its ledger records "wz-session-core
--features declare-final rc=0 with no unused warning". That is a SOLO build, which
pulls consumers that DO reach declare_build. The break lives only where declare-final
arrives TRANSITIVELY and no builder is reached. The check passed because it was aimed
at the wrong UNIT, not because the code was sound. Worse, diagnosing it, my hand-run
of "C4c's exact command" returned rc=0 THREE TIMES while `run-ci.sh --layer C4c`
reproduced instantly. A HAND-COPIED LANE COMMAND IS A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE LANE.

AND (2) IS THE THIRD OF ITS EXACT KIND. run-ci.sh:4098-4106 records the other two in
its own comments: R311qg ("the lane-wiring gap a full run-ci surfaced") and R311y277
(wz_storage_host -- "E6h ran the right binary, but this catch-all also ran it against
the default one", surfaced by the y277 push's pre-push full run-ci). Three times, a
new binary-dep test met the catch-all sweep; three times the pre-push hook was the
thing that found it. The trap is structural, not carelessness, and nothing warns at
authoring time.

Round 311y351.decision_summary:
R311y351 -- Layer F leaves the job it was pushing past 30 minutes. LEDGER ENTRY WRITTEN
RETROACTIVELY alongside y350's, following R311y297's precedent: the fix shipped and
pushed as d934c18 and the session ended on the green run it produced, before the ledger
step. The commit is unchanged; this entry is the audit trail it never got.

WHAT HAPPENED. Layer F had run as the `ci` job's last step since R311pt. Run
29571213015 (dde45d5) died at 30m03s INSIDE Layer F. Every gate through E5 passed and
no wz gate failed -- the same shape as the y296 disk overflow, on the other ceiling.

THE MEASUREMENT MOVED IT, NOT THE TIMEOUT. Layer F is ~12.9min of a ~28.5min job --
45% of it -- and it is stable at that. The `ci` job was therefore carrying ~28.5min
against a 30min cap: about 5% headroom, with nothing reporting the margin.

THE OVERRUN IS NOT CODE GROWTH. That was the first diagnosis and it was wrong. Against
the last green run the +2.18min is spread evenly across EVERY step, including steps
whose input is PINNED and did not change -- `Build sce-codegen` +17% on a pinned
vendor/sce, cache restore 16s -> 44s. That is runner variance, and at 5% headroom
variance ALONE decides the run. The job did not break on y350: it had been a coin flip
for some rounds and y350 is when the coin landed.

WHY SPLIT RATHER THAN RAISE `timeout-minutes`. A bigger number buys one atom's worth of
time and re-arms the identical failure, because the cost grows monotonically in atom
count -- each new atom is another exclusion lane in F and another subset lane in `ci`.
Splitting changes the SLOPE: F's growth is charged to its own budget instead of to the
gate every other layer shares.

AND y297 CALLED THIS, TO THE MECHANISM, AND IT WAS LEFT STANDING. ci.yml:84-86, written
at y297 and untouched since: "The prior green run (y291) had already taken 25m31s
against `timeout-minutes: 30`, so both ceilings were being approached at once and
nothing reported either." Its carry closed with "the next squeeze arrives on schedule."
Two ceilings were named; the disk one got a fix and the time one got a sentence. 54
rounds later the sentence fired. A NAMED RISK WITH NO GATE IS A PREDICTION, NOT A
CONTROL -- and this round's own fix repeats the shape, because it buys headroom without
buying visibility.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml ONLY -- 1 file changed, +104/-3. No script, no wz code, no
Cargo: Layer F's behaviour cannot have moved with it.
New `footprint` job ("codec-footprint catalog truthfulness (Layer F)"), ubuntu-22.04,
`timeout-minutes: 30`, whose only lane is `bash scripts/run-ci.sh --layer F`. The step
LEAVES the `ci` job, so `--layer F` now appears exactly once in the file (ci.yml:538) --
the split is a move, not a copy.
The job's prep is a deliberate MIRROR of `ci`'s rather than a trimmed one: checkout with
`submodules: recursive` (wz-ap-demo resolves through vendor/sce path deps, so it does
not build without them), the same apt list (cmake, libclang-dev, clang, perl), `rustup
show` for the rust-toolchain.toml pin, and Swatinem/rust-cache under a distinct
`key: footprint`. An over-provisioned job costs ~2min in parallel; an under-provisioned
one costs a fix-and-repush series.
It drops only what F provably cannot use: no `fetch-depth: 0` (F reads no history, only
`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), no python3-yaml (Layer D's dep), no protoc, no
mnemosyne-cli, no sce-codegen build, no zenoh-pico CLI.
The cache step is NAMED for what it does not buy: `workspaces: crates -> target` covers
crates/target, while every F lane builds into target/measure-codec-footprint/<lane>. The
registry half is the whole benefit; this job's ~13min is a COLD number and stays one.
The split, not a cache, is what bought the headroom.
verification_bullets: ALL 8 JOBS GREEN on run 29579390840 (d934c18), and the split is confirmed BY
MEASUREMENT rather than by the absence of a failure: `ci` 14m3s and `footprint` 14m7s,
each ~47% of its 30min budget. The work did not shrink -- 14m3s + 14m7s is about the
28m10s the single job was doing -- it was charged to two budgets.
THE CEILING, PINNED AS A SET rather than a remembered average: the three green runs
before the split took 28m28s (29557435656), 27m33s (29551467701) and 28m29s
(29507608581) against `timeout-minutes: 30`; run 29571213015 (dde45d5) then failed at
30m3s. Three runs at ~95% of budget is what "5% headroom" means.
LAYER F ACTUALLY RAN AND IS NOT A SKIP DRESSED AS A PASS -- the hosted log for job
87881198415 reads "Layer F pass (767s)". 767s = 12.78min, which is the ~12.9min the
split was sized on, now measured on the far side of it. Prep was therefore ~1m20s
against the ~2min the new comment budgeted for it.
THE MINIMAL DEP SET IS PROVEN BY THE GREEN ITSELF, which is stronger evidence than the
shim the commit message cites: the job ran F to completion with no protoc, no
mnemosyne-cli, no sce-codegen build, no python3-yaml and no pico CLI installed.
F's MEASUREMENT IS UNCHANGED BY THE MOVE -- a construction argument, not a comparison:
d934c18 touches only ci.yml, so measure-codec-footprint.sh is byte-identical across the
split and cannot have measured differently. The comparison is NOT available and is not
being implied: the pre-split job's log is past retention (`gh run view --job
87812564230 --log` returns 0 lines).
THE SPLIT IS THE THIRD OF ITS KIND IN THIS FILE, not a novel move: `interop` (which the
new comment cites) and `feature-gates`, whose own comment at ci.yml:987-996 names the
`ci` job's "26m22s against timeout-minutes: 30" as the reason it was given its own
runner. The `ci` job sheds a layer each time it reaches 30 minutes.
NOT VERIFIED, so the next reader does not infer it: no disk measurement was taken on
either job, so the y296-ceiling relief this move implies is unquantified.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y351 = Layer F moved out of the `ci` job into its own `footprint` job. ci
~28.5min -> 14m3s, footprint 14m7s, both ~47% of a 30min budget; all 8 jobs green on
run 29579390840. CI-infrastructure only: 1 file (ci.yml), no script, no wz code, no
inventory, no behaviour change.
STILL NOTHING REPORTS THE TIME MARGIN -- y297's named gap survives y351 intact. y297
wrote "nothing reports or gates the time margin either" and closed with "the next
squeeze arrives on schedule"; y350's dead push IS that squeeze, 54 rounds later. This
round bought headroom without buying visibility, which is the same trade y297 made. The
cheap control is a step that prints each job's elapsed against its cap; the honest one
gates on it. Until then the next squeeze is invisible until it is fatal.
THE SLOPE IS UNTOUCHED, exactly as after y297. Each new atom is another exclusion lane
in F and another subset lane in `ci`, so both budgets grow monotonically in atom count:
the split RESET the clock, it did not stop it. Both jobs now sit at ~47%, so the next

target` does not cover, so none of it is cached and all of it is disk. That load has now
left the job that overflowed on y296. Nobody measured the delta on either side, so the
size of the gift is unknown -- y297's `df -h` bracket still wraps only the `ci` job's
prune step, which is y297's own still-open carry.
OBSERVED WHILE VERIFYING, PRE-EXISTING, NOT INVESTIGATED: Layer F SKIPs GREEN when
python3 is absent (run-ci.sh:4216-4219), and NEITHER job apt-installs python3 -- both
ride the ubuntu-22.04 preinstall. Identical on both sides of the split, so y351 did not
introduce it; but "a SKIP is green" is this repo's named trap and a runner-image change
would turn this gate silently empty. Separately, F's own report prints `minus-all-codecs
delta: SKIP` and `handshake-only delta: SKIP` INSIDE a passing gate
(measure-codec-footprint.sh:132 = lane does not compile under the exclusion). Whether
either is legitimate is unexamined here.

Round 311y353.decision_summary:
R311y353 -- `liveliness-get` is PROVEN, and the note that said why it could not be
was wrong in both of its halves. This round's finding is not the atom; it is that a
carried blocker survived unexamined because nobody ran the thing it forbade.

THE CHEAP TIER IS EXHAUSTED, RE-DERIVED FROM CARGO rather than from the triage table:
`preset-ap-full` has 137 atom members, 35 with zero cross-impl proof, and only SIX of
those are inside `preset-ap-client` -- what wz-ap-demo actually builds. All six carried
a blocker. So progress now means REMOVING a blocker, not finding an easy atom.

THE NOTE SAID: "`liveliness-get` -- an ordering the demo can't make -> needs a knob".
I built the knob (`--liveliness-get-after-ms`, y345's `--publish-after-ms` shape), and
measurement killed the note twice:

NOT SUFFICIENT. With the hold in place and a pico peer dialled DIRECTLY, the get still
returns nothing, and pico's own source says why -- `interest.c:533-535`: "Check
transport type / if (zn->_tp._type == _Z_TRANSPORT_UNICAST_TYPE) { return _Z_RES_OK; //
Nothing to do on unicast }". ZENOH-PICO NEVER ANSWERS AN INTEREST ON UNICAST. The whole
responder, `_z_interest_send_decl_token` included, is multicast-only. Not a build gap:
the CLI build's generated config.h carries `Z_FEATURE_LIVELINESS 1` and
`Z_FEATURE_INTEREST 1`, and pico's token declaration itself arrives fine (wz logs
REMOTE TOKEN DECLARED). A wz<->pico unicast witness for this atom is not late, it is
IMPOSSIBLE, and no knob was ever going to produce it.

NOT NECESSARY EITHER. The ordering needs no knob at all: start the token holder first
and gate on its declaration banner. The new test passes with the hold removed entirely
-- measured, not reasoned. The knob survives on a NARROWER claim it earned honestly (a
one-shot get has no retry to cover the pico->zenohd propagation window, unlike the
burst-driven siblings whose 5x200ms burst is what "covers the window"), and its doc now
says that instead of the refuted story.

THE TOPOLOGY THAT WITNESSES IT: pico(token) -> zenohd(responder) <- wz(get). zenohd is
the full Rust router and DOES answer a CURRENT liveliness Interest over unicast -- the
exact thing pico declines. All three are load-bearing: drop pico and the reply is
zenohd echoing an empty world; drop zenohd and there is no responder at all.

AND THE SECOND FALSE BLOCKER, found on the way: the ap-full gap note says "hosted CI
never runs Layer Z". It is FALSE -- ci.yml:733 runs `--layer Z`, in the `interop` job
that BUILDS zenohd and its storage-manager plugin, and the audit's own execution line
has said "hosted CI runs Z" the whole time. That note is load-bearing for
`session-reconnect`'s blocker too, which now needs re-deriving rather than quoting.

wz->zenohd`). Three processes: zenohd via the existing `spawn_zenohd` helper, a pico
`z_liveliness -k demo/token/pico -e tcp/... -m client` token holder, and wz-ap-demo
`--connect <zenohd> --liveliness-get 'demo/**'`. Asserts the FULL reply line
(`filter='demo/**' keyexpr='demo/token/pico'`) plus the terminating FINAL.

which is a fact about the reply's CONTENT, not about wz's counterparty. The file's
`pico,zenohd` corpus category (3 -> 4) reports the pico leg on its own.

("Press CTRL-C to undeclare liveliness token"), not on a sleep. Without that gate an
empty snapshot and a slow token are indistinguishable from the reply side.

burst-driven siblings whose 5x200ms burst is what "covers the window"), and its doc now
says that instead of the refuted story.

exact thing pico declines. All three are load-bearing: drop pico and the reply is
zenohd echoing an empty world; drop zenohd and there is no responder at all.

Round 311y354.decision_summary:
R311y354 -- `liveliness-history` is PROVEN, as a PAIR, and the pair is the point.

THE ATOM. `history = true` on a liveliness subscriber puts the CURRENT bit on the
outbound Interest (wire mode CurrentFuture), so the subscriber is replayed the tokens
that ALREADY EXIST rather than only those declared from now on. runner.rs says the same
from the demo side: history "makes the subscriber order-independent of token declare
time". So the atom's observable is a token declared STRICTLY BEFORE the subscriber
existed -- which is why this fixture's ordering is deliberately the reverse of the
usual: pico declares first, wz subscribes late.

THIS ROUND WAS CHEAP BECAUSE y353 PAID FOR IT. The route was known before a line was
written: a history replay IS an Interest answer, and R311y353 measured that zenoh-pico
NEVER answers an Interest on a unicast transport (interest.c:533-535, "Nothing to do on
unicast"). So the topology is the same one y353 built -- pico(token) -> zenohd(responder)
<- wz(subscriber) -- and no round was spent re-discovering that pico cannot serve it.
That is what a carry is for. The contrast with the blocker note y353 refuted is the
lesson: a reason that is MEASURED transfers, a reason that is ASSERTED costs the next
round.

A SINGLE POSITIVE TEST HERE WOULD HAVE BEEN NEARLY WORTHLESS, and this is the round's
transferable finding. `LIVELINESS SAMPLE PUT` is what `liveliness-subscriber` logs for
ANY token, future ones included. A green positive arm therefore does not distinguish
"the pre-existing token was REPLAYED" (the atom) from "a token arrived somehow" (its
vehicle). The claim only becomes this atom's when the twin exists:

  history ON  -> the sample arrives, carrying pico's exact token.
  history OFF -> identical fixture, one CLI flag removed: the session Establishes and
                 the sample never comes.

Both arms were MEASURED by hand before the file was written (ON -> 1 sample, OFF -> 0),
so the pair was known to discriminate before it was encoded. The two differ in exactly
one flag, so together they say the replay is CAUSED by `history` -- neither says it
alone. This is the y352 twin rule applied to a claim rather than to a fixture's
precondition: there, the twin pinned that a dead port was dead; here, it pins that the
atom's own flag is what produces the observable.

Round 311y355.decision_summary:
R311y355 -- `session-reconnect` is PROVEN cross-impl, and the round's real content is a
methodology failure that a BISECT caught before it shipped.

THE ATOM. session-reconnect is the long-lived supervisor (open_session_with_reconnect)
that re-dials on link loss and REPLAYS the declaration cache (replay_declarations) so
the surviving session resumes. The existing wz-only e2e proves the replay against a wz
acceptor; this proves it against a real zenohd RESTARTED underneath a live wz session --
the cross-impl half no wz<->wz test can reach, because the wz-only one re-handshakes
against wz.

THE OBSERVABLE IS ENGINEERED SO ONLY REPLAY PRODUCES IT: wz subscribes to demo/**;
pico puts demo/pre through zenohd#1 (baseline routes); zenohd#1 is KILLED; a FRESH
zenohd#2 respawns on the same port; pico puts demo/post. zenohd#2 has no memory of wz's
subscription, so a `SUBSCRIBER FIRED keyexpr='demo/post'` line can ONLY mean the
supervisor re-dialled and replayed demo/** to it. Distinct keyexprs (pre/post) make the
witness unambiguous -- no reliance on payload length or ordering.

THE TWIN IS THE POINT, AND IT NEARLY DIED TO A HARNESS BUG. The pair: --reconnect
resumes and delivers demo/post; no --reconnect exits on link loss and never does. The
first hand-verification of the twin RECEIVED demo/post in BOTH arms -- which reads
exactly like a vacuous twin and would have condemned a correct design, or worse, made me
ship a positive-only test believing the twin was impossible. THE CAUSE: I killed zenohd
via `kill $!` where `$!` was a SHELL SUBPROCESS wrapping `timeout zenohd`, not zenohd.
zenohd#1 never died, kept the port, zenohd#2's bind failed, and the still-alive zenohd#1
routed demo/post to a wz that had never reconnected (record_established_at stayed 1). A
BISECT -- kill the REAL pid, assert it is dead, assert zenohd#2 bound -- flipped both
arms to correct: --reconnect -> demo/post + reconnects=1 + record_established_at=2; no
--reconnect -> wz exits, demo/post count 0. "Structurally cannot" is a claim, and so is
"my kill killed the thing"; the harness is part of the experiment and can lie.

WHY THE ASSERTION IS ON DATA, NOT ON THE COUNTER. The demo logs `reconnects=N` only at
graceful shutdown, and an early run showed reconnects=0 while data had already resumed
(the counter commit lagged the teardown). So the PRIMARY assertion is the replayed data
(demo/post, retry-gated, deterministic); reconnects=1 is a corroborating check read
AFTER demo/post is confirmed, when the reconnect has provably happened.

WHY IT IS NOT FLAKY, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED. zenohd restart on the same port is the
proven-reliable pattern the wz-only respawn test already uses (port reservation held
across the sever); the Rust fixture spawns zenohd as a direct Command child so
ChildGuard's kill hits the process, not a shell. Run 3x back to back: 28.2 / 27.2 /
28.0s, all green. The post-put is retried until the witness lands, so the reconnect
window is covered by a bounded loop, not a sleep.

Round 311y356.decision_summary: R311y356 -- CI hotfix (059c387) closing the ledger debt on the y354/y355 Layer-Z interop tests, plus the y356-investigation of the three remaining preset-ap-client atoms (inventory/ledger scoping, NO atom mutation). THE HOTFIX: Layer E's catch-all sweep (run-ci.sh:4107-4109, `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests -- --ignored --skip wz_e2e_ --skip multicast --skip zenohd --skip wz_router --skip wz_peer --skip wz_storage_host`) filters #[ignore] tests by a test-NAME substring (comment at run-ci.sh:4065), NOT by file name. Three zenohd-dependent fns landed with names lacking the `zenohd` token -- the y354 liveliness-history PAIR and the y355 reconnect TWIN -- so the `ci` job's Layer E (which does not build zenohd) swept them in and they panicked at zenohd_binary() (crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs:362). Round 311y357.decision_summary: R311y357 -- time-system-clock is PROVEN cross-impl (partial) via a new pico->wz storage-capture leg, and the round's real content is resolving the y356 OPEN QUESTION: the foreign-OBSERVED wall-clock readback is DEAD, so the witness is IN-PROCESS (foreign pico DRIVE + in-process StorageState READ), Layer E -- NOT the gap-doc's assumed Layer Z. THE ATOM: time-system-clock (FOUNDATIONAL, reserved) is the wall-clock NTP64 source (wall_clock_ntp64, (unix_seconds<<32)|frac), the PHYSICAL layer the time-hlc HLC WRAPS. SEPARABLE from time-hlc by the y349 discriminator: time-hlc's foreign proof is monotonicity (strictly-increasing stamps), which a FAKE counter satisfies WITHOUT reading the wall clock; time-system-clock's own observable is the stamp's wall-clock VALUE = current unix time. THE WITNESS: a stock zenoh-pico z_put sends an UN-TIMESTAMPED sample over a live unicast TCP link into an in-process wz StorageService on demo/**; apply_sample stamps the un-timestamped capture via FallbackStamp -> wall_clock_ntp64 (the ONLY auto-stamp site in wz); the test reads StoredData.timestamp in-process and asserts (1) its zid is the STORAGE stamper zid vec![0x01] (proving it is wz's fallback stamp, not a value pico carried) and (2) its seconds (time>>32) fall within the test's own SystemTime window [start,end] (the stamp is produced between the two reads, so the bound cannot flake; a stub source of any magnitude lands outside). Observed 1784335794 = 2026-07-18. WHY IN-PROCESS (resolved by direct read): the fallback stamp is applied ONLY on storage capture -- NOT re-emitted to a foreign reader (a subscriber sees the sample wz FORWARDS carrying the publisher's original, here absent, timestamp -- wz does not stamp the forward path; a z_get reply carries the payload but NOT the stored version's timestamp, a documented StorageState NON-goal). So the gap-doc's z_sub_attachment/z_get reader route is DEAD, and mirroring wz_storage_wildcard_update_pico_interop.rs (foreign drive + in-process read) is the achievable witness. Inventory UNCHANGED (a cross-impl proof moves the audit marker corpus, not an inventory flag; a 'proven' reason would be the metadata-vs-code lie A3 forbids). Layer E green; a broken-assert Layer E run went RED, proving the catch-all sweep executes it. validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

Round 311y370.decision_summary: R311y370 -- storage-mgr-complete-flag PROVEN cross-impl (wz->pico), a genuine UNPROVEN->proven count-mover (audit all-lanes proven 72->73, unproven 53->52; hosted-CI 69->70). A wz StorageService declared with StorageConfig.complete = true/false emits a DeclareQueryable whose QueryableInfo complete bit is decoded by the REAL zenoh-pico C _z_declaration_decode, which AGREES with the configured value in BOTH directions -- a foreign C decoder reading the wire bit is the cross-impl witness. Binds to the atom OWN code (the config->wire gate storage_queryable_complete at storage_service.rs:108-116, fed to QueryableOptions::with_complete at :211 via declare_with_backend), NOT to the shared QueryableInfo codec: a pure DeclareQueryable codec-parity test is insensitive to the gate, so the round DRIVES the StorageService declare and reads BOTH config directions off the wire. The complete bit has no single-hop serve-observable effect (an incomplete queryable still answers a directly-connected z_get; completeness only gates BestMatching routing), so a deterministic wire-decode is the honest witness, not a behavioral one. RED-verified BOTH ways: neutering storage_queryable_complete so it ignores config.complete (always true) fails the complete=false case (pico decodes true) while complete=true passes; always-false fails the true case -- the proof binds to the config->wire threading, not a flag. Deterministic (GREEN 3/3, reviewer 5/5). 3-agent worktree-ISOLATED adversarial review all SOUND (binding, non-vacuity, regression). 4 files: a new in-process codec-class test (runs Layer C1 every push) plus zenoh-pico-sys allowlist/wrapper expansion for the DECLARE decode path plus a storage-mgr-complete-flag dev-dep pin (A4-5 containment plus the gate honors config). inventory UNCHANGED.
