Round 311y372.decision_summary: R311y372 -- transport-lowlatency PROVEN cross-impl wz->zenohd (audit unproven 51->50, proven 73->74). The cross-impl test SURFACED a real fidelity bug the inventory R311y305 "No residual" missed: wz streamed-link framing (stream_link.rs) always emitted the universal 2-byte u16 length prefix, but zenoh lowlatency unicast transport frames post-Established data with a 4-byte LE u32 prefix (io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/lowlatency/link.rs), so a real zenohd negotiated lowlatency then REJECTED wz lean Put (Batch len 8192020 > 49152) and closed the link; wz<->wz lowlatency_e2e missed it (both sides shared u16). FIXED: StreamWriteDriver::send_blocking frames u16 XOR u32 per a shared is_lowlatency Arc<AtomicBool> flipped at Established by the lowlatency open helpers -- framing at ENQUEUE (synchronous with the FSM emit) so a handshake frame enqueued pre-flip stays u16 even if drained post-flip (first attempt framed at dequeue in writer_task, OpenAck raced the flip -> Established->Terminal); poll_framed reads the width-matched prefix (width fixed at frame start) and bounds the untrusted u32 at u16::MAX before allocating (zenoh read_with_link parity). Handshake stays u16, universal + non-TCP stream links keep u16. wz-ap-demo gained --lowlatency (initiate_and_open_session_with_lowlatency + logs negotiated is_lowlatency). New Layer Z test wz_lowlatency_zenohd_interop.rs asserts (1) negotiation true (zenohd mirrored the 0x05 ext) AND (2) the lean Put routes wz->lowlatency-zenohd->pico z_sub; zenoh-pico has NO lowlatency transport so zenohd is the only foreign witness (codec-parity impossible). RED-verified: force-u16 fails delivery while negotiation stays true; a wrong ext id fails negotiation; the universal wz_publish_routes leg stays green under both. 3-agent worktree-isolated review SOUND (obs#1 rx-bound folded into c3c27dc). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/stream_link.rs: StreamWriteDriver gains an is_lowlatency Arc<AtomicBool>; send_blocking now FRAMES each payload (u16 StreamEnvelope XOR a 4-byte LE u32 length prefix per the flag) and enqueues the framed wire -- framing moved here from writer_task so it is decided at ENQUEUE time (synchronous with the FSM emit). writer_task is now a raw byte writer (drains pre-framed wires). StreamReadDriver gains the flag; poll_event passes it to poll_framed.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: poll_framed(read_state, src, lowlatency) reads a width-matched prefix (4-byte u32 under lowlatency, else 2-byte u16), the width fixed at frame start (Idle->Length) so a mid-stream flag flip never splits a prefix; ReadState::{Length,Payload} carry the width/prefix_width. TcpDriver::poll_event passes false (the lowlatency helpers wire via StreamReadDriver, not TcpDriver). The 4-byte path BOUNDS the untrusted u32 length at u16::MAX before allocating (zenoh read_with_link parity: reject an over-max batch), with a new lowlatency_rx_rejects_oversize_u32_prefix unit test -- the review obs#1 hardening folded into the commit.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_pipeline.rs: new wire_tcp_stream_with_lowlatency threads the flag to the read + write drivers; wire_tcp_stream delegates with a fresh always-false flag.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: new wire_dialed_link_with_lowlatency threads the flag to the TCP arm (wire_dialed_link delegates false); initiate_/accept_and_open_session_with_lowlatency create the flag, wire it, and store(true) at Established iff opened.actions.is_lowlatency() -- the handshake stays u16, post-Established data/keepalive go u32.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/{tls,quic,vsock,unixpipe,unixsock}_pipeline.rs: StreamReadDriver::new + StreamWriteDriver::new pass a fresh always-false flag (lowlatency is a TCP-path negotiation; these links keep the u16 prefix).

verification_bullets: Root-cause direct-read (the arbiter): zenoh io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/lowlatency/link.rs read_with_link reads a 4-byte [0u8;4] u32::from_le_bytes prefix + send_with_link writes len = buffer.len()-4 as a 4-byte LE prefix; the zenohd RUST_LOG=debug run logged "Will use LowLatency transport! ... lowlatency: true" then "Rx task finished with Err(Batch len is invalid. Round 311y374.decision_summary: R311y374 -- the wz WebSocket ACCEPTOR wired + the accept side refactored SYMMETRIC to the dial side. The wz accept path was tcp-only (bind_locator returned a bare TcpListener, Unsupported for every non-tcp scheme), so no foreign peer could dial a wz ws acceptor -- transport-link-ws was proven only wz->zenohd (dialer). DESIGN (user: cost-ignored, most long-term-correct): the first ws cut was a point-fix (a locator_is_ws special-case in accept_locator) that would not scale; the real defect was ASYMMETRY with the dial side. FIX: a BoundListener enum = the accept-side mirror of DialedLink. bind_locator -> BoundListener (scheme-keyed), accept_bound dispatches per variant + runs the scheme handshake (the ws RFC6455 server upgrade), yielding the SAME DialedLink the dial side does (shared wire_* downstream). Adding a transport is now ONE arm in BoundListener + bind_locator + accept_bound. The ws point-fix is absorbed into the uniform BoundListener::Ws arm. PROVEN cross-impl transport-link-ws zenohd->wz + session-unicast-open zenohd->wz (the ACCEPTOR direction): zenoh-pico has no ws client so zenohd is the only foreign ws dialer -- pico z_put --tcp--> zenohd --ws--> wz --listen ws/... acceptor -> wz sub fires (wz was the acceptor per the InitAck/OpenAck action trace). RED: a demo built WITHOUT ws rejects a ws/ listen (Unsupported) -> the test fails at bind. The multi-peer/router accept_loop stays tcp-only (bind_endpoint projects BoundListener via into_tcp) pending its generalization. 3-agent worktree-isolated review found + FIXED 2 defects: (1) a feature-combo build error (the uniform local_addr()->SocketAddr accessor depended on the transport-link-udp-gated SocketAddr import; replaced by a per-variant log_listening() that formats to String, which also resolves the IP-address assumption the unix family could not satisfy -- the dial mirror DialedLink likewise exposes no uniform local_addr); (2) a stale negative unit test (non_tcp_listen_accept_is_unsupported_without_io) that asserted ws/ accept is Unsupported-before-bind and would HANG under --features transport-link-ws now that ws binds+accepts -- made feature-aware (ws only in the unwired list when the backend is off). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: new BoundListener enum -- the ACCEPT-side mirror of DialedLink. Round 311y375.decision_summary: R311y375 -- the wz TLS ACCEPTOR added as a UNIFORM BoundListener arm, the payoff of the R311y374 accept-side symmetric refactor. Where wiring the ws acceptor took a whole refactor (point-fix -> BoundListener), tls was ONE arm each: a BoundListener::Tls(TcpListener, Arc<ServerConfig>) variant + bind_locator's Proto::Tls arm (binds tcp + carries cfg.tls, else Unsupported) + accept_bound's Tls arm (accept_tls after accept_tcp) + AcceptConfig/TlsAcceptConfig (the DialConfig/TlsDialConfig mirror, carrying the server cert) + the demo --tls-cert/--tls-key. It worked cross-impl on the FIRST run -- the symmetry hypothesis validated. bind_locator/accept_locator/accept_endpoint thread a &AcceptConfig; bind_endpoint passes AcceptConfig::default() (the tcp-only router path is cert-free). PROVEN transport-link-tls zenohd->wz + session-unicast-open zenohd->wz (the ACCEPTOR direction; the existing wz_to_zenohd over_tls legs prove only wz->zenohd/dialer): zenoh-pico's CLI has no tls, so zenohd is the foreign tls dialer -- pico z_put --tcp--> zenohd --tls--> wz --listen tls/... acceptor -> wz sub fires; zenohd trusts wz's self-signed cert via root_ca_certificate (CA-trust LOAD-BEARING per a review falsification -- a wrong CA fails the handshake) + verify_name_on_connect:false (SAN-only relax). RED: a demo without tls rejects a tls/ listen -> the test fails at bind. The STREAM FAMILY (tcp/ws/tls, all TcpListener-based uniform arms) is now COMPLETE on the accept side. 3-agent worktree-isolated review all SOUND; 3 observations FOLDED IN (handshake log moved AFTER the handshake succeeds; docstrings corrected re SAN-disable vs decouple; temp cert files wrapped in a Drop guard). A pre-existing Layer E6 load-flake surfaced by the first full run-ci (a wz --peer not binding within 5s under load; 5/5 in isolation, unrelated to the accept-side change) was root-caused by widening spawn_on_ephemeral_port's bind wait 5s -> 10s (matching the 8s pico siblings; zero cost on green runs). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

Round 311y376.decision_summary: R311y376 -- accept-symmetry Stage 3: the multi-peer accept loop (--router / peer_loop) generalized to accept every BoundListener variant, not just tcp. FaceSources.listener changed TcpListener to BoundListener; the loop select arm accepts one raw connection per iteration via BoundListener::accept_raw (a fast, non-blocking accept), and the ws/tls SERVER handshake is DEFERRED into the spawned per-face open future (AcceptedLink::handshake in open_face/open_face_multilink) so a slow handshake never blocks accepting the next peer (the loop one-peer-never-blocks-another invariant -- the reason the handshake is NOT run in the select arm). bind_endpoint now returns BoundListener (was projected to a raw TcpListener via into_tcp); accept_bound (the one-shot --listen acceptor) delegates to accept_raw + handshake, its exact log strings preserved (the ws/tls completion note logged after the handshake succeeds, y375 obs1). New OpenError::AcceptHandshake surfaces a failed ws/tls SERVER handshake as an isolated FaceFailed. PROVEN cross-impl: a real zenohd ws-dials wz --router --listen ws/... and the accept loop accepts, Establishes and holds the foreign ws face (face 0 UP); the R311y374 ws-acceptor leg proved only the one-shot --listen acceptor, this is the multi-peer LOOP. RED: without Stage 3 a ws --router listen fails at bind (into_tcp Unsupported) so the test fails at spawn before zenohd starts. 3-agent worktree-isolated review: A (correctness+feature-gate) and B (test-discriminator, RED reproduced) SOUND; C (regression) found a CONFIRMED compile break in run_peer/run_router_hat (a blanket local_addr to local_addr_display swap left them on a String where they need .port()/.ip(); the default preset-ap-client build masked it) -- FIXED before finalizing by adding BoundListener::local_addr returning SocketAddr and re-verifying the exact Layer Z build EXIT 0. The routing-router marker advances the A4 cross-impl-proof audit: routing-router unproven to proven (audit proven 74 to 75, unproven 49 to 48). Structure-only, no wire/behavior change on the tcp path; inventory UNCHANGED (no new feature/cfg site, A3 consistent). The full run-ci runs at the .githooks/pre-push hook as the push gate, not pre-asserted here.

New BoundListener::accept_raw(&self) -> (AcceptedLink, std::net::SocketAddr): a fast NON-BLOCKING raw accept (accept_tcp_on per stream-family variant) that DEFERS the handshake; SocketAddr fully-qualified in the signature because its import is transport-link-udp-gated (this ungated accessor must compile no-udp). New BoundListener::local_addr_display(&self) -> io::Result<String> (per-variant address string, no SocketAddr in signature, y374-faithful) for the Display-only callers (run_router, run_storage_host, log_listening); log_listening refactored to compose it. New BoundListener::local_addr(&self) -> io::Result<std::net::SocketAddr> (stream-family, fully-qualified SocketAddr for the udp-gate) for the callers that need the STRUCTURED address -- run_peer/run_router_hat derive the node zid from .port() and gate self-locator advertisement on .ip().is_unspecified() (a 3-agent-review CONFIRMED compile break: the blanket local_addr()->local_addr_display() swap left those two on a String; the default-feature build masked it because preset-ap-client cfg-outs run_peer/run_router_hat -- fixed by this accessor). accept_bound (one-shot --listen acceptor) refactored to DELEGATE to accept_raw + handshake, preserving its exact log strings (the completion note logged AFTER handshake succeeds, y375 obs#1). bind_endpoint now returns BoundListener (was into_tcp() to a raw TcpListener). New OpenError::AcceptHandshake(io::Error) (the accept-side twin of Dial). Removed the now-unused accept_tcp (consuming) import.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: new ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET (30s) + wait_for_tcp_accept_alive(child, port, budget) -> Result<(),String>. Polls TCP connect but FAST-FAILS the instant child.try_wait() reports the process exited (Err "process exited ... (status)"), else Errs at budget ("did not start accepting ... within {budget}"); the Err self-labels which case fired. Liveness-aware, so the generous 30s budget never spins on a corpse -- the structural successor to the blind wait_for_tcp_accept (no liveness check, zenohd stderr null, fixed 10s).

The 6 zenohd spawn helpers (spawn_zenohd_listeners, ws_dialer, tls_dialer, lowlatency, tcp_tls, tcp_quic) + 4 direct test-file callers (pubkey/usrpwd/peer/storage *_zenohd_interop) move off the blind poll onto wait_for_tcp_accept_alive with ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET (let guard -> let mut guard for child_mut). The blind wait_for_tcp_accept stays for the 4 multicast wz-ap-demo callers (lighter process, 5s) -- a documented boundary, not a silent omission.

3 new unit tests + a budget-floor guard: wait_alive fast-fail (< budget on a dead child, RED-verified), timeout (>= budget on a live non-listener), success (Ok on a bound listener), and zenohd_accept_budget_keeps_headroom_over_the_observed_flake (ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET >= 20s so a revert toward the old 10s is RED -- guards the curative half a liveness-only test would miss).

Round 311y377.publishable_decision_summary: R311y377 -- kill the R311y376 Layer Z flake at its root: the blind fixed-10s TCP-accept poll for every zenohd spawn becomes wait_for_tcp_accept_alive, a liveness-aware self-diagnosing wait (child.try_wait fast-fail + generous 30s ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET + exit-vs-timeout labelling); 6 lib helpers + 4 direct test callers migrate; and scripts/run-ci.sh emits a ::error annotation so a failed lane is never opaque even when gh run view --log-failed returns empty. 3-agent worktree review SOUND (budget-floor + shell/doc fold-ins amended); Layer Z GREEN end-to-end with real zenohd.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: new ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET (30s) + wait_for_tcp_accept_alive(child, port, budget) -> Result<(),String>. Polls TCP connect but FAST-FAILS the instant child.try_wait() reports the process exited (Err "process exited ... (status)"), else Errs at budget ("did not start accepting ... within {budget}"); the Err self-labels which case fired. Liveness-aware, so the generous 30s budget never spins on a corpse -- the structural successor to the blind wait_for_tcp_accept (no liveness check, zenohd stderr null, fixed 10s).

3 new unit tests + a budget-floor guard: wait_alive fast-fail (< budget on a dead child, RED-verified), timeout (>= budget on a live non-listener), success (Ok on a bound listener), and zenohd_accept_budget_keeps_headroom_over_the_observed_flake (ZENOHD_TCP_ACCEPT_BUDGET >= 20s so a revert toward the old 10s is RED -- guards the curative half a liveness-only test would miss).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `bind_locator` `AnyLocator::Unixsock` arm -- cfg-on binds `bind_unixsock(&ep.path)` -> `BoundListener::Unixsock`; `#[cfg(not(...))]` returns a typed `Unsupported` (the always-present-variant cfg-on/off pair, mirroring dial_locator's `AnyLocator::Unixsock` arm; was a single ungated `Unsupported`). crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/accept_loop.rs: `Step::Accepted` peer type `SocketAddr` -> `AcceptedPeer`; the handler converts `AcceptedPeer::Ip(addr)` -> the unchanged mesh SocketAddr face path, and `AcceptedPeer::NonIp(name)` -> `on_event(AcceptError(Unsupported))` + `drop(accepted)` + `continue` (mesh stays IP-only; `next_id` / `summary.accepted` NOT bumped for the rejected peer -- keyed faces need a routable IP locator).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/unixsock_e2e.rs: new `wz_accepts_a_session_over_unixsock_via_the_bind_endpoint_seam` -- drives the SCHEME-KEYED seam `bind_endpoint("unixsock-stream/..") -> BoundListener::accept_raw -> AcceptedLink::handshake -> accept_and_open_session` (the chain the one-shot `accept_bound` composes), the acceptor twin of `dial_endpoint("unixsock-stream/..")`. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `BoundListener::accept_raw(&self)` -> `accept_raw(&mut self)` -- `tokio_vsock::VsockListener::accept` is `&mut self` (tcp/unixsock accept are `&`), so a Mutex-free vsock arm needs `&mut self`. The tcp/ws/tls/unixsock arms are unaffected (their `&`-taking accept_tcp_on/accept_unixsock_on reborrow-coerce from `&mut`); the vsock arm calls `accept_vsock_on(l)` where `l: &mut VsockListener` directly.

Round 311y38.decision_summary: R311y38 -- adminspace §5.23 self-sufficiency round (the carry's #2 self-sufficiency track): made adminspace-core honestly buildable + functional under --no-default-features by fixing two latent defects the default-set-only C1am lane masked, declaring two genuine-but-undeclared deps, and adding the standalone CI lane C1an that locks them. (1) session/mod.rs carried a `use ResponseSink as _` that went UNUSED under --all-targets deny-warnings dev-dep feature-unification (the trait send_response_final is a pure forward to the always-present inherent SessionLinkActions::send_response_final, so on the concrete Arc<SessionLinkActions> the import only re-routed resolution to the same fn) -- removed it, behavior identical. (2) The lib #[cfg(test)] helpers make_request_query/query_frame_outcome were gated query-queryable but their only 3 consumers are all(query-queryable,codec-response-final) -- dead-code under a query-queryable-without-codec-response-final build; re-gated the helpers to match. (3) adminspace-core declared NEITHER of its two real deps: keyexpr-wildcard-double (the @/<zid>/<whatami>/** queryable's wire-path match via keyexpr_intersects_target->intersect_chunks; without it `**` degrades to a literal chunk and a remote admin GET never matches) and pubsub-encoding (the reply EncodingHint application/json|text/plain via gated_reply_encoding; without it the reply loses its content-type) -- both now pulled by wz-session-core adminspace-core, transitively by the runtime facade. Diagnose-first: the runtime root e2e FAILS on the dropped encoding without pubsub-encoding, and a new wz-session-core unit FAILS without keyexpr-wildcard-double (drop-and-rerun proof). The local-loopback GET does NOT exercise `**`, so the matcher unit -- not the e2e -- locks keyexpr-wildcard-double. New CI Layer C1an runs the matcher lock + 3 runtime e2e combos + clippy --all-targets -D warnings, all under --no-default-features. No inventory change. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

A comment records why the inherent call is the honest one on a concrete handle.

Round 311y380.decision_summary: R311y380 -- accept-symmetry Stage 4 THIRD arm: wire unixpipe into the scheme-keyed accept seam. BoundListener/AcceptedLink gain a Unixpipe arm mirroring the dial side, and bind_locator gets the cfg-on/off pair (bind_unixpipe is SYNC like vsock bind_vsock, no await). unixpipe is STRUCTURALLY unlike the unixsock (y378) / vsock (y379) arms: BoundListener::Unixpipe holds UnixpipePaths rather than a listener object, because bind mkfifos the uplink+downlink pair and those paths ARE the rendezvous. It is also the FIRST NON-BLOCKING accept -- accept_unixpipe_on is a sync fn opening the FIFO ends O_NONBLOCK / O_RDWR, returning at once whether or not a peer dialed, unlike the tcp/unixsock/vsock async accepts that block for a peer. Because this round OPENS mesh reachability for a --listen unixpipe/.. string (bind_endpoint returned Unsupported before, and both runner.rs and the pico session feed bind_endpoint straight into accept_loop), the mesh NonIp-reject path would HOT-SPIN; the same commit therefore adds the throttle the Step::Accepted(Err) EMFILE arm already uses (identical ACCEPT_ERROR_THROTTLE_MS = 100). Both claims are proven BY TEST rather than by reading: the seam discriminator is RED-isolated independently at bind, accept and handshake, and the throttle discriminator MEASURES 4351 rejects per 300ms without the guard versus about 3 with it. Reviewer C further showed the hazard is runtime-only (removing the throttle still passes clippy -D warnings), so a runtime test is the only possible gate. 3-agent worktree-isolated review ALL SOUND; the CI gap agent A found (accept_loop is routing-accept-gated, so a unixpipe-only clippy lints nothing) is closed by a routing-accept+unixpipe clippy step in Layer C1al. No wire or behavior change to existing transports; inventory unchanged.

STRUCTURALLY unlike unixsock/vsock: the bound value is NOT a listener object -- bind_unixpipe mkfifo's the uplink+downlink pair and those PATHS are the rendezvous. accept_raw's Unixpipe arm calls the SYNC accept_unixpipe_on (no .await; the &mut UnixpipePaths auto-reborrows to &) and yields AcceptedPeer::NonIp("unixpipe"); handshake wraps directly into DialedLink::Unixpipe, the mirror of dial_locator. Dial side unchanged. Both discriminators plus a stray-new-src regression RED-witnessed; 3-agent worktree-isolated review ALL sound after the fix. carry_forward_bullets: R311y382 = the udp accept demux: BoundListener::Udp's R311y381 single-shot Option<UdpSocket> is superseded by a src-keyed multi-peer demux. A pump task (udp_demux_task) is the sole recv_from owner of the listen socket and routes each datagram to its SOURCE's per-face bounded channel; accept_raw awaits each new src. This retires reviewer-C's two R311y381 mesh gaps: F1 CROSS-TALK (each face now reads only its own src's channel, not a shared recv_from) and F2 PERPETUAL-THROTTLE (a second src is a real second face; no-new-src PENDS instead of the single-shot Err the mesh throttled on). KEY LESSON (pump lifetime): the recv pump must OUTLIVE the BoundListener, because the one-shot accept_bound path drops the listener before the accepted session is driven (the mesh accept_loop instead holds it for life). A plain TokioJoinHandle does NOT abort on drop, and a .closed()-on-listener-drop pump would STARVE the one-shot face -- so the pump is kept alive by an Arc<UdpDemuxPump> (abort-on-drop guard) SHARED by the listener and every accepted face, aborting only when the last holder drops. This was the design-review BLOCKER, caught before code by the 2-agent design review.

FOLLOW-UP (deferred, honestly documented in the BoundListener::Udp doc): (a) the faces HashMap grows one entry per distinct src until a later datagram reaps it -- UDP src is spoofable without a round-trip, so this is a cheaper face-creation surface than TCP; bounded per-face by the cap-256 channels + reap-on-send-error, the map itself uncapped, at PARITY with the uncapped TCP accept_loop (zenoh caps at the transport-manager accept layer, not the link demux). (b) src-only keying vs zenoh's (src,dst)+IP_PKTINFO: equivalent for a concrete-IP --listen udp/HOST:P, weaker for a wildcard 0.0.0.0 bind (wz cannot reply from the exact local dst the peer targeted). Both re-openable if a hardened multi-peer udp router needs them.

KEY LESSON (pump lifetime): the recv pump must OUTLIVE the BoundListener, because the one-shot accept_bound path drops the listener before the accepted session is driven (the mesh accept_loop instead holds it for life). A plain TokioJoinHandle does NOT abort on drop, and a .closed()-on-listener-drop pump would STARVE the one-shot face -- so the pump is kept alive by an Arc<UdpDemuxPump> (abort-on-drop guard) SHARED by the listener and every accepted face, aborting only when the last holder drops. This was the design-review BLOCKER, caught before code by the 2-agent design review.

FOLLOW-UP (deferred, honestly documented in the BoundListener::Udp doc): (a) the faces HashMap grows one entry per distinct src until a later datagram reaps it -- UDP src is spoofable without a round-trip, so this is a cheaper face-creation surface than TCP; bounded per-face by the cap-256 channels + reap-on-send-error, the map itself uncapped, at PARITY with the uncapped TCP accept_loop (zenoh caps at the transport-manager accept layer, not the link demux). (b) src-only keying vs zenoh's (src,dst)+IP_PKTINFO: equivalent for a concrete-IP --listen udp/HOST:P, weaker for a wildcard 0.0.0.0 bind (wz cannot reply from the exact local dst the peer targeted). Both re-openable if a hardened multi-peer udp router needs them.

Round 311y383.decision_summary: R311y383 -- fix the closed_port() TOCTOU flake in wz-integration-tests that failed hosted CI Layer C1 (wait_alive_fails_fast_when_child_exits_before_accepting). Root cause: closed_port bound an ephemeral port, recorded it, then DROPPED the listener, leaking the port to the OS; under a loaded CI run a parallel process rebinds the closed port into a live listener, so wait_for_tcp_accept_alive (which polls TcpStream::connect before child.try_wait) connects and returns Ok before observing the exited child. Fixed by binding the port with socket2 WITHOUT listen and holding the Socket guard for the test -- the port stays reserved (no rebind) and connect-refused (RST), finally wiring the socket2 dep R311if added for exactly this but never applied to closed_port. NOT a regression of R311y382 (different crate; the udp round run-ci merely surfaced the latent flake). Discriminator test closed_port_reserves + RED-witness; 1 focused worktree-isolated review ALL SOUND (incl the deliberate non-extension to ReservedPort::pick, whose port the child binds). Combined run-ci green through Layer C1 with R311y382 before stop; pushed --no-verify per explicit user consent, hosted CI at the pin gating post-push; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: closed_port() rewritten from bind-then-drop (TcpListener::bind 127.0.0.1:0 -> record the OS-assigned port -> drop the listener -> return the bare u16) to a socket2 bind-WITHOUT-listen reservation returning (Socket, u16). std's TcpListener always listen()s, so a bound std listener ACCEPTS a connect against the kernel backlog; socket2 binds a Type::STREAM socket WITHOUT listen, so a connect gets RST (ECONNREFUSED) AND the port is RESERVED for the guard's lifetime (no third party can rebind it). The two callers -- wait_alive_fails_fast_when_child_exits_before_accepting and wait_alive_times_out_for_a_live_nonlistening_child -- now bind the guard as `_closed_guard` (an underscore-PREFIXED named binding lives to end-of-scope; a `let _ =` / `(_, port)` would drop it at once and reopen the race). Mirrors the refused_locator helper in wz-runtime-tokio/tests/static_scout_open.rs.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: added the `use socket2::{Domain, Socket, Type};` + SocketAddr import. The socket2 dep was DECLARED in Cargo.toml (with a comment justifying it for exactly this TOCTOU fix) since R311if but never wired -- src usage was 0 until now.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: new discriminator test closed_port_reserves_the_port_and_refuses_connect asserting, while the guard is held, that (a) a concurrent TcpListener::bind to the reserved port FAILS and (b) a TcpStream::connect is refused.
verification_bullets: The 3 wait_alive* tests (wait_alive_returns_ok_once_the_port_accepts, wait_alive_fails_fast_when_child_exits_before_accepting, wait_alive_times_out_for_a_live_nonlistening_child) + the new closed_port_reserves_the_port_and_refuses_connect discriminator all pass.

RED-witness (calibration-is-not-evidence): reverting closed_port to release the reservation (drop the bound socket -- the old bind-then-drop leak) makes closed_port_reserves' concurrent-bind assertion FAIL ("guard must reserve the port against a concurrent bind" -- the freed port is rebindable); GREEN with the guard held.

stress-loop: wait_alive_fails_fast_when_child_exits_before_accepting x15 = 0 fails. The cross-PROCESS rebind race cannot be reproduced locally (it needs a parallel binder under load), so the reservation discriminator -- not a loop -- is the direct proof that the flake's root cause (a rebindable leaked port) is eliminated.
clippy -p wz-integration-tests --all-targets -D warnings clean (socket2 now USED, no unused-import); cargo fmt -p wz-integration-tests --check clean.

Round 311y384.decision_summary: R311y384 -- ledger the c0c93f2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CI experiment after A/B validation. VERDICT: KEEP, harmless + marginally positive (cargo-compile steps -22s), NOT the top-line speedup the raw job delta suggested. It does NOT move the 14m49s critical path -- the real Tier-1 lever remains the structural job split designed this round (peel the tooling-heavy A+B layers, which do not compile crates/target, into a parallel validate+codegen job). sccache stays REFUTED (prior PoC). ci.yml env-only; no code/Cargo/Section change. A single A/B pair is noisy, so -22s (~4% of cargo time) is NOT claimed as a strong speedup; the honest verdict is harmless + marginally positive -> KEEP.

No second confirmation run spent: the step decomposition already isolates the confound cleanly (cargo -22s vs infra +165s), so the non-regression conclusion needs no tighter -22s estimate; a re-run would cost a full CI cycle for zero verdict change.

OPEN before implementing the split: VERIFY that Layer A3/A4 (and B/B2) do NOT require a full crates/target compile -- if they are cargo-metadata-level, the peel loses zero warm-target reuse; if any compiles the workspace, reconsider the cut. It now runs only (1) mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace (SSOT integrity, seconds) and (2) cargo test -p <crate> for ONLY the crates the push diff changes (default features; crate dir -> package name via its Cargo.toml). The FULL validation surface -- the feature-subset matrix, C2 clippy, Layers B/B2 codegen, F/G/Q/Z footprint / cross-compile / interop, every non-default combo -- is now the HOSTED CI job ONLY (it runs on every push to main and is the single full gate). Kept the R224a empty-ref short-circuit; dropped the R224b flock + R250 HEAD-re-source (they existed for the multi-lane run-ci race a single cargo test -p avoids). run-ci.sh itself is UNCHANGED (still the on-demand full sweep + what hosted CI runs); only the hook stopped auto-invoking it. CLAUDE.md Local CI gates rewritten to the new policy. Pairs with R311y385: hosted CI is now the single full gate AND ~40 percent faster. bash -n clean; dry-run proved the diff->crate->package pipeline (a91916a -> wz-runtime-tokio). NOT pushed without consent.

F was ONE job of 16 release+LTO lanes (~13min, high-variance 6.5-13.5min). measure-codec-footprint.sh gains a round-robin shard filter (WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS=n + WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=i, idx % n == i); each shard builds baseline + its codec subset, shard 0 adds the two whole-catalog lanes (minus-all-codecs + handshake-only). The per-lane build command + isolated target-dir are byte-identical to before, so the byte gate is unchanged; only the SET of lanes per runner shrinks. Caching F stays deferred (byte-gate risk). Pushed --no-verify per consent.
changes_bullets: scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: added an optional round-robin shard filter. WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS=n + WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=i restrict THIS run to the codec lanes where idx % n == i; baseline builds on EVERY shard (every codec delta is computed against it); minus-all-codecs + handshake-only (whole-catalog lanes, whose excludes are computed over the FULL codec set, kept in FULL_CODEC_FEATURES) run ONLY on shard 0. Unset / SHARDS<=1 => all 16 lanes (default local behavior unchanged). The per-lane `cargo build --release ... --features ... --target-dir <lane>` command + isolated target dir are byte-identical to before -- only the SET of lanes per invocation shrinks, so the byte gate itself is unchanged. A range assert (SHARD in [0,SHARDS)) + a coverage log line per shard.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: footprint job -> matrix (strategy.matrix.shard [0,1,2,3], fail-fast:false) with job env WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS="4" + WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=matrix.shard; per-shard rust-cache key (footprint-shard-<i>) so the parallel matrix jobs do not race one cache save. A loud co-located DROP-PROOF comment: the matrix `shard` list MUST equal [0..WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS-1] and match WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS, else a codec silently stops being byte-gated.
No run-ci.sh change: layer_f_codec_footprint still calls measure-codec-footprint.sh and the env flows through; local `run-ci.sh --layer F` stays unsharded (16 lanes).

Round 311y390.decision_summary: R311y390 -- the CALLER fail-fast slice (the y389-deferred immediate follow-up, run_router half): the demo mesh router now REJECTS a non-mesh-capable --listen at bind instead of silently reject-throttling every accept and holding 0 faces. New pub BoundListener::supports_mesh_multi_peer() is the wildcard-free BIND-time twin of the accept loop's AcceptedLink backstop (every variant true except Unixpipe=false; the two twins agree per-transport). run_router is split into a thin wrapper (passes shutdown_signal()) + a testable inner run_router_until(listen, shutdown: impl Future); the inner adds, right after bind_endpoint, an if !listener.supports_mesh_multi_peer() -> Err(Unsupported) guard. A wz-ap-demo off-default transport-link-unixpipe passthrough makes the guard REACHABLE -- without it the unixpipe/ scheme still parses but bind_locator returns a feature-gated Unsupported at bind (the accept backend is not compiled), so bind_endpoint errors before the guard (dead code). Discriminator run_router_rejects_a_unixpipe_listen_at_bind drives run_router_until with an injected std::future::ready(()) shutdown and asserts Err(Unsupported); RED reproduced by neutralizing ONLY the guard (returns Ok(()) in 0.00s -- a clean fast fail, not a SIGTERM hang). Predicate pins boundlistener_tcp_is_mesh_capable / boundlistener_unixpipe_is_not_mesh_capable (both polarities). run-ci Layer C1bl gains a count-guarded test + feature clippy (the sole lane compiling the caller_failfast_tests module + reaching a real BoundListener::Unixpipe). 3-agent worktree-isolated review: correctness/RED CONFIRMED-SOUND (twins agree for all 7 transports, RED reproduced by reverting only the guard), CI-gating CONFIRMED-SOUND after fixing a duplicate C1bg label (relabeled C1bl -- the pre-existing storage lane already held C1bg, C1ba..C1bk all taken) + scoping a sole-lane overclaim (E3/Z also compile the body, only C1bl compiles the discriminator + reaches a real Unixpipe), design/faithfulness CONFIRMED-SOUND after correcting 2 comments that called the without-feature failure an unsupported-SCHEME error (it is a feature-gated accept-BACKEND Unsupported at bind). Known minor artifact (not fixed, pre-existing): a production --router unixpipe/x reject leaves the mkfifo'd FIFO pair on disk (UnixpipePaths has no Drop -- all bind sites unlink manually, a Drop would prematurely unlink the SUCCESS path; self-heals on re-bind). pico drive_listen fail-fast DEFERRED (pico does not compile unixpipe today, so its guard would be unreachable dead code). Inventory UNCHANGED (no new cfg atom; the passthrough forwards an existing wz/transport-link-unixpipe). Code = 066c248, LOCAL only, NOT pushed.

The doc claim "the one-shot accept_bound path serves such a listener" CONFIRMED (accept_raw + handshake have Unixpipe arms). No present-tense overclaim of the deferred pico caller.

Self-heals on re-bind (make_fifo unlinks stale nodes). A demo-side cleanup would leak the library FIFO path-naming; deferred as cosmetic.

FOLLOW-UPS beyond the pico caller (remaining AP-full roadmap): the multi-client unixpipe acceptor (zenoh UnicastPipeListener -- invitation handshake + per-connection dedicated sub-pipe); when it lands, BOTH supports_mesh_multi_peer twins flip unixpipe->true and unixpipe joins the mesh through the generalized accept loop. Round 311y392.decision_summary: R311y392 -- the multi-client unixpipe acceptor slice: wz named-FIFO transport became MULTI-CLIENT + zenoh-wire-compatible (a shared request channel carries per-client 8-byte invitations, each keyed to a dedicated sub-pipe pair; flock is the load-bearing rendezvous/reservation/single-listener primitive on all three reader ends), so supports_mesh_multi_peer flipped false->true on both twins and unixpipe joins the generalized accept_loop mesh; wz<->zenohd cross-impl over unixpipe was proven in BOTH directions (manual smoke + a formal Layer Z test); the y390/y391 reject discriminators were retired/flipped to admit; a HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT bounds a stalled peer, a superset over zenoh unbounded serial wedge (reviewer-A fix).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/unixpipe_pipeline.rs: full multi-client rewrite (70%) of the named-FIFO transport, zenoh-wire-compatible with UnicastPipeListener/UnicastPipeClient. A shared base request channel (P_uplink) carries 8-byte invitations (magic 0xDEADBEEF ++ suffix.to_ne_bytes, native-endian, matching zenoh unicast.rs:55-67); each accepted client gets a DEDICATED pipe pair keyed by a random u32 suffix formatted DECIMAL (P_uplink{suffix}/P_downlink{suffix}, matching zenoh get_dedicated_pipe_names). flock (raw libc::flock, == zenoh's advisory_lock crate) is load-bearing on ALL THREE reader ends (listener base + listener dedicated_uplink + client dedicated_downlink) for zenoh's PipeW::new bail-if-lock-free probe, plus suffix-collision detection (retry <=100) + single-listener enforcement. create_fifo_tolerant is no-unlink EEXIST-tolerant (flock is the reservation, not mkfifo). FifoReadEnd unlinks its read node on Drop + releases flock via fd close (zenoh PipeR::Drop parity). UnixpipeAcceptor + UnixpipeAcceptorPump (abort-on-drop). The acceptor task reads invitations serially and bounds each handshake with a HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (10s, zenoh accept_timeout parity) wrapper -- a SUPERSET over zenoh's serial-UNBOUNDED loop: a stalled/hostile peer is bounded to the timeout (then the acceptor drops the half-open handshake + recovers) instead of wedging the acceptor forever as zenoh's UnicastPipeListener does (review fix for reviewer A's MAJOR; a per-invitation-concurrent variant was tried and reverted -- it hung the 2-dialer test).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: BoundListener::Unixpipe now holds a UnixpipeAcceptor (was UnixpipePaths); accept_raw awaits acc.recv_new_link() (cancel-safe mpsc recv, closed->pending, byte-for-byte the udp demux arm); dial_locator/bind_locator arms are async; local_addr_display renders the base path. BOTH supports_mesh_multi_peer twins (BoundListener + AcceptedLink) flip Unixpipe false->true. AcceptedPeer / variant / predicate docs rewritten (unixpipe is now mesh-capable). boundlistener_unixpipe_is_not_mesh_capable retired -> boundlistener_unixpipe_is_mesh_capable (asserts true, async bind).

publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/unixpipe_pipeline.rs: full multi-client rewrite (70%) of the named-FIFO transport, zenoh-wire-compatible with UnicastPipeListener/UnicastPipeClient. A shared base request channel (P_uplink) carries 8-byte invitations (magic 0xDEADBEEF ++ suffix.to_ne_bytes, native-endian, matching zenoh unicast.rs:55-67); each accepted client gets a DEDICATED pipe pair keyed by a random u32 suffix formatted DECIMAL (P_uplink{suffix}/P_downlink{suffix}, matching zenoh get_dedicated_pipe_names). flock (raw libc::flock, == zenoh's advisory_lock crate) is load-bearing on ALL THREE reader ends (listener base + listener dedicated_uplink + client dedicated_downlink) for zenoh's PipeW::new bail-if-lock-free probe, plus suffix-collision detection (retry <=100) + single-listener enforcement. create_fifo_tolerant is no-unlink EEXIST-tolerant (flock is the reservation, not mkfifo). FifoReadEnd unlinks its read node on Drop + releases flock via fd close (zenoh PipeR::Drop parity). UnixpipeAcceptor + UnixpipeAcceptorPump (abort-on-drop). The acceptor task reads invitations serially and bounds each handshake with a HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (10s, zenoh accept_timeout parity) wrapper -- a SUPERSET over zenoh's serial-UNBOUNDED loop: a stalled/hostile peer is bounded to the timeout (then the acceptor drops the half-open handshake + recovers) instead of wedging the acceptor forever as zenoh's UnicastPipeListener does (review fix for reviewer A's MAJOR; a per-invitation-concurrent variant was tried and reverted -- it hung the 2-dialer test).

Round 311y396.decision_summary: R311y396 -- wz --router-hat (a TRUE wire WhatAmI::Router) binds a unixpipe listener and routes a Put between two clients, PRODUCT CODE (the counterpart of R311y395 which closed the star --router test-only). run_router_hat derived its node zid from the listen .port() and its admin locator from the listen .ip(), so a non-IP unixpipe listen was rejected at bind (no IP SocketAddr). This is the ap/pico SUPERSET -- zenoh-pico cannot be a router at all. New e2e (two distinct-zid --connect unixpipe clients routed through the router-hat) + a fail-fast unit; run-ci Layer E7u. changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs (run_router_hat, PRODUCT CODE): replaced `let local = listener.local_addr()?` (IP-only, errored for a non-IP listen) with `local_display = listener.local_addr_display()` + `local_ip = listener.local_addr().ok()`. The node zid is computed BEFORE the listening-on log: an explicit --zid override wins for ANY transport; else an IP listener port-derives (same ROUTER_HAT_ZID_PREFIX bytes, TCP byte-identical); else (non-IP, no --zid) a fail-fast Err naming --zid. The admin local_data locator (adminspace-router-linkstate) renders the scheme from transport_name() in BOTH arms -- an IP listen is tcp/ws/tls/udp by its ACTUAL transport (correcting a pre-existing tcp-hardcode), a non-IP listen is scheme/path e.g. unixpipe/<base>.

TEST + CI + a demo vsock feature + a ZENOHD_VSOCK=1 variant-oracle recipe (the bind_vsock to BoundListener::Vsock accept arm is pre-existing R311xj, proven wz<->wz by vsock_e2e; this adds the INDEPENDENT-impl witness). A VSOCK-enabled zenohd (target/zenohd-vsock/, built --features zenoh/transport_vsock since zenoh default omits it) DIALS the wz --listen vsock/VMADDR_CID_LOCAL:VMADDR_PORT_ANY acceptor over AF_VSOCK loopback, and a pico z_pub routes tcp->zenohd->vsock->wz into the acceptor subscriber; wz binds ONLY vsock (no TCP listener). HOST-ONLY unlike ws/tls/unixsock/udp: AF_VSOCK loopback needs the vsock_loopback kernel module, ABSENT on the hosted CI runner, so the Layer Z leg SKIPs when the vsock oracle is absent even under WZ_Z_REQUIRE (the same kernel-gated host-only treatment as vsock_e2e / the C1ab lane; the demo still COMPILES with vsock every CI run). New e2e wz_vsock_acceptor_zenohd_interop.rs + spawn_zenohd_vsock_dialer / zenohd_vsock_binary + build-zenohd.sh generalized to a shared VARIANT_FEATURE/VARIANT_NAME (unixpipe + vsock) + a run-ci Layer Z leg (no ci.yml change). RED x2: feature-gate (a demo without --features vsock rejects the vsock listen and never binds; a SINGLE demo-feature drop elides it since preset-ap-client carries tcp+udp not vsock, unlike udp two-feature trap) + delivery (keyexpr mismatch). 3-agent worktree review of 7661382 all SOUND-WITH-NITS, 0 blockers: R1 correctness/RED, R2 CI/no-flaky (build-zenohd VARIANT refactor PRESERVED for unixpipe; 39/39), R3 design/doc (all load-bearing claims TRUE, no y399-class over-claim). Amend 9dc36de folded the NITs: explicit (vsock)+accepted-peer witnesses + softened a TCP-only shorthand. GREEN 10/10 + amend 5/5 + RED x2. Code local 9dc36de, NOT pushed. Unlike the udp/unixsock/vsock acceptor slices (test+CI only, accept arm pre-existed), the QUIC accept SEAM was MISSING: the quic pipeline primitives (bind_quic/accept_quic_on/quic_server_endpoint) + a wz<->wz quic_e2e existed, but session_open had no BoundListener::Quic. Round 311y411.decision_summary: R311y411 = cross-impl MESH quic-DATAGRAM proof (the y407 mesh-quic leg's UNRELIABLE twin) that EXPOSED and fixed a real routing-identity defect: wz's Zid was not canonical, so a node whose zid ended in a zero byte could not recognise ITSELF in a neighbour's link-state flood. Seven legs: --router-hat routers_net convergence plus a real LinkStateList decode; --peer mutual linkstate edge; a gossip ROUTING neuter; real pub/sub data crossing the accepted datagram mesh link BOTH directions; a TRANSPORT neuter (the SAME listen/endpoint/cert dialed WITHOUT `?rel=0` never brings a face up and must fail as `Terminal`, so a cert regression cannot satisfy it) that pins legs 1-5 to the DATAGRAM data plane since the mesh listen line carries no transport tag; and a REGRESSION leg for the zid defect below. THE DEFECT (product code, not test): zenoh's identity for a zid is the VALUE -- `uhlc::ID::size()` counts significant LE bytes (`MAX_SIZE - leading_zeros(u128::from_le_bytes(..))/8`, uhlc-0.8.1 src/id.rs:67, which `ZenohIdProto` wraps) -- so `[70,72,83,00]` and `[70,72,83]` are ONE zid. wz's `Zid::from_slice` kept the caller's slice length verbatim, making them two. `wz-ap-demo` derives its mesh zid from its listen PORT, so an ephemeral port with a `0x00` low byte (1 in 256) produced a self zid ending in zero; the peer announced it, zenohd canonicalised it on the wire, and the LinkStateList flood came back TRIMMED and no longer compared equal to self. The node then entered its OWN topology graph as a phantom peer with no edges and the spanning-tree next-hop computation silently stopped forwarding -- a `--publish` peer's data never left the box. The wz type doc had already named this corner and dismissed it as "unreachable today"; that assumption is what this round falsifies by measurement. FIXED at the root: `from_slice` now trims trailing zero bytes, so identity is the value and the ordering equivalence the cross-impl edge-jitter tie-break rests on holds unconditionally rather than only for canonical inputs. HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the process correction: a 30-run campaign showed 29/30 and a 100-run campaign 99/100. Re-running is how you MEASURE a rate, not how you find a cause; the investigation only moved when the harness was made observable (the spawn helper hardcoded `RUST_LOG=info`, which reports topology as COUNTS while node identity and advertised locators are `debug`). With that unpinned, 250 instrumented runs produced 6 failures and named the phantom in every one: `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<own listen port>"]`, always a zero-low-byte port. 5 failures were the data-out leg; the 6th was the router tier counting 3 and skipping the exact `(2 node(s))` witness -- one cause, two faces. A SECOND flake, root-caused earlier the same way: zenohd exit 255 "process exited before accepting", because every acceptor-direction test derives its zenohd tcp port as `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` on a namespace argument that only excludes wz's OWN socket; reproduced deterministically, with TIME_WAIT (zenohd sets no SO_REUSEADDR) as the amplifier. Fixed by removing the guess: zenohd binds `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and the test reads the kernel-assigned port back from its own announcement. RED+TWIN on every claim: demo without `quic-datagram` -> 7/7 red while the y407 reliable-quic legs stay 5/5 green on the SAME binary; neuter dialing datagram -> leg 6 red; wrong trust anchor -> leg 6 red on the cause assertion; router-hat witness suppressed -> leg 1 red; canonicalisation reverted -> leg 7 red and the pico receives NOTHING; liveness check removed -> the corpse unit test red at 30.05s instead of 0.40s; terminator requirement removed -> the parser unit test red. Two pre-existing Zid tests turned red and were UPDATED, not silenced: they pinned the non-canonical contract (a zero-extended prefix as a distinct, adjacent identity) via a `Vec<u8>` ordering proxy; the load-bearing property their own comment names is agreement with ZENOH, so they now pin that directly. NO atom-count change: A4 measured 78/37/45 at HEAD and after (the ledger's carried 77/37/46 does not reproduce at that commit and is retired here). Full `run-ci.sh` sweep exit 0 (108 lanes) after the core-type change. 3 worktree-isolated adversarial reviewers of sha b75a00a: 0 blockers, 5 should-fix folded.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-routing-graph/src/lib.rs: `Zid::from_slice` now CANONICALISES -- trailing zero bytes do not count toward the length, so `[0x70,0x72,0x83,0x00]` and `[0x70,0x72,0x83]` are the same zid, matching `uhlc::ID::size()` (the significance rule zenoh's `ZenohIdProto` wraps). This is the ROOT FIX for a node failing to recognise its own zid when a neighbour's LinkStateList returns it wire-trimmed. The type doc, which previously called this corner "unreachable today", now records the measured failure it caused. 2 new unit tests (canonicalisation incl. equality/hash/interior-zero/all-zero; self-zid-arriving-trimmed is not a second node) and 2 pre-existing tests UPDATED from the non-canonical contract: the Ord test now pins agreement with ZENOH's 16-byte LE ordering (its own comment's stated invariant) instead of a `Vec<u8>` proxy that diverged only on zero-extended prefixes, and the Display test pins that a TRAILING zero is not part of the identity while an INTERIOR zero is.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_mesh_quic_datagram_acceptor_zenohd_interop.rs (NEW, 7 #[ignore] legs): a real zenohd DIALS a wz `--peer` / `--router-hat quic-datagram/...` MESH listen over RFC9221 datagram frames. (1) --router-hat routers_net converges + wz decodes the LinkStateList OAM, settling on the NEW in-run ingest witness rather than the handshake-satisfiable convergence line; (2) --peer forms a MUTUAL linkstate edge; (3) a gossip ROUTING neuter; (4) a pico z_pub's Put crosses INTO wz; (5) wz's Put crosses OUT to a pico z_sub; (6) a TRANSPORT neuter -- the SAME listen/endpoint/cert dialed WITHOUT `?rel=0` never brings a face up (served 0 peer(s), ingested 0 link-state(s), 0 graph edge(s)) and must fail as `Terminal`; (7) a REGRESSION leg pinning `--zid 70728300` (trailing zero byte): the peer must still route data OUT and must see exactly `peak 2 node(s)`, the deterministic form of the 1-in-256 port lottery.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: new shared `spawn_zenohd_dialer_on_ephemeral_tcp` -- zenohd binds `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and the helper reads the KERNEL-assigned port back from zenohd's own announcement, replacing the `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` GUESS (measured flake: `Address already in use` -> zenohd exit 255, amplified by TIME_WAIT since zenohd sets no SO_REUSEADDR). Supported by `wait_for_capture_alive` (LIVENESS-aware capture wait: a corpse reports its real ExitStatus in ms instead of burning the 30s budget) and `parse_announced_tcp_port` (pure; REFUSES an unterminated digit run so a torn read cannot yield a truncated port). The spawn pins `RUST_LOG=z=info` -- it is the first helper whose correctness depends on zenohd's LOG rather than its socket. 3 new unit tests, all RED-verified.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: `demo_log_filter()` -- the `wz-ap-demo` children's `RUST_LOG` is now overridable via `WZ_TEST_DEMO_LOG` instead of hardcoded `info`. The hardcoding is what blocked this round's investigation: topology witnesses are COUNTS at info, while node identity and advertised locators are debug. Unpinning it is what turned "peak 3 node(s), cause unknown" into `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<own port>"]`.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the router-hat loop grows the in-run INGEST witness its peer-loop sibling already had. `routers-net converged` rises on add_link from the INIT-derived zid+whatami -- handshake-satisfiable -- while the shutdown summary's `learned mesh topology` is gated on a real LinkStateList decode, so a topology e2e that settled on convergence and terminated could race a witness it had already earned.

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer Z: new invocation of the test with `--ignored --test-threads=1`, count-guarded `^test result: ok\. 7 passed` -- ANCHORED, unlike the sibling `grep -q 'N passed'` guards: a reviewer reproduced a false GREEN through the verbatim pipeline (`FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed` matches the unanchored form, as does `16 passed`). NO build-line change.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/{wz_mesh_quic,wz_quic,wz_quic_datagram,wz_tls,wz_ws,wz_router_ws}_acceptor_zenohd_interop.rs: comment-only correction at the 10 surviving `wrapping_add(1)` sites, whose quic-family comments asserted "different protocol namespace, so it cannot collide" -- now known FALSE. Each site records the real failure mode, the measured rate and the race-free replacement. Migrating the callers is carried work.
verification_bullets: ROOT-CAUSE evidence for the Zid defect, from instrumented reproduction (not from re-running): 250 runs with the demo's log filter raised produced 6 failures, and every one named the phantom -- `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<the peer's OWN listen port>"]`. The ports were 33536/49664/39424/54016/56832, i.e. 0x8300/0xC200/0x9A00/0xD300/0xDE00: EVERY failure had a zero LOW BYTE, and the phantom zid was the port-derived self zid with its trailing zero trimmed. 5 failures were the data-OUT leg (pico received nothing); the 6th was the router tier, where the phantom made routers-net count 3 so the exact `(2 node(s))` witness was never logged -- one cause, two faces. Reference rule verified by DIRECT READ, not memory: `uhlc::ID::size()` = `MAX_SIZE - leading_zeros(u128::from_le_bytes(bytes))/8` (uhlc-0.8.1 src/id.rs:67) and `ZenohIdProto` is a transparent wrapper (zenoh 1.5.0 commons/zenoh-protocol/src/core/mod.rs:63-72).

DETERMINISTIC RED/GREEN for the fix, single variable = `Zid::from_slice` canonicalisation, same `--zid 70728300`: PRE-FIX = phantom self-node 1, `peak 3 node(s)`, pico received 0. POST-FIX = phantom 0, `peak 2 node(s)`, pico received 1. CONTROL (post-fix, `--zid 70728301`, no trailing zero) = phantom 0, peak 2, received 1. The 1-in-256 lottery is now a 100% reproduction.

RED+TWIN on the shipped artifact, seven falsifications: (a) demo rebuilt WITHOUT `quic-datagram` -> all 7 legs FAIL (typed Unsupported at bind_locator) while the y407 reliable-quic mesh legs stay 5 passed on the SAME binary = isolation; (b) neuter's locator suffix flipped to `?rel=0` -> leg 6 FAILS; (c) neuter given an UNRELATED trust anchor -> leg 6 FAILS on the new `Terminal` cause assertion (this scenario PASSED before the fix -- a reviewer-found hole); (d) router-hat witness text suppressed in runner.rs -> leg 1 FAILS on its new ingest barrier at 15.40s; (e) `Zid::from_slice` canonicalisation reverted -> leg 7 FAILS with the pico receiving nothing; (f) liveness check removed from wait_for_capture_alive -> the corpse unit test FAILS and the lib suite goes 0.40s -> 30.05s; (g) terminator requirement removed from parse_announced_tcp_port -> the torn-line unit test FAILS.

PORT-COLLISION flake (the round's first, separately root-caused): binding the derived port before the spawn makes zenohd log `Address already in use (os error 98)` and exit 255 -- byte-identical to the campaign failure. A reviewer independently confirmed the mechanism, showed exit 255 is not bind-specific (a malformed --config aborts with SIGABRT) but that every other 255 path in this lane is config-DETERMINISTIC and so cannot produce 1-in-30, refuted the competing dial-failure hypothesis, refuted an adjacency-bias hypothesis (0 collisions in 400 trials), and identified TIME_WAIT as the amplifier.

Seven legs: --router-hat routers_net convergence plus a real LinkStateList decode; --peer mutual linkstate edge; a gossip ROUTING neuter; real pub/sub data crossing the accepted datagram mesh link BOTH directions; a TRANSPORT neuter (the SAME listen/endpoint/cert dialed WITHOUT `?rel=0` never brings a face up and must fail as `Terminal`, so a cert regression cannot satisfy it) that pins legs 1-5 to the DATAGRAM data plane since the mesh listen line carries no transport tag; and a REGRESSION leg for the zid defect below. THE DEFECT (product code, not test): zenoh's identity for a zid is the VALUE -- `uhlc::ID::size()` counts significant LE bytes (`MAX_SIZE - leading_zeros(u128::from_le_bytes(..))/8`, uhlc-0.8.1 src/id.rs:67, which `ZenohIdProto` wraps) -- so `[70,72,83,00]` and `[70,72,83]` are ONE zid. wz's `Zid::from_slice` kept the caller's slice length verbatim, making them two. `wz-ap-demo` derives its mesh zid from its listen PORT, so an ephemeral port with a `0x00` low byte (1 in 256) produced a self zid ending in zero; the peer announced it, zenohd canonicalised it on the wire, and the LinkStateList flood came back TRIMMED and no longer compared equal to self. The node then entered its OWN topology graph as a phantom peer with no edges and the spanning-tree next-hop computation silently stopped forwarding -- a `--publish` peer's data never left the box. The wz type doc had already named this corner and dismissed it as "unreachable today"; that assumption is what this round falsifies by measurement. FIXED at the root: `from_slice` now trims trailing zero bytes, so identity is the value and the ordering equivalence the cross-impl edge-jitter tie-break rests on holds unconditionally rather than only for canonical inputs. HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the process correction: a 30-run campaign showed 29/30 and a 100-run campaign 99/100. Re-running is how you MEASURE a rate, not how you find a cause; the investigation only moved when the harness was made observable (the spawn helper hardcoded `RUST_LOG=info`, which reports topology as COUNTS while node identity and advertised locators are `debug`). With that unpinned, 250 instrumented runs produced 6 failures and named the phantom in every one: `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<own listen port>"]`, always a zero-low-byte port. 5 failures were the data-out leg; the 6th was the router tier counting 3 and skipping the exact `(2 node(s))` witness -- one cause, two faces. A SECOND flake, root-caused earlier the same way: zenohd exit 255 "process exited before accepting", because every acceptor-direction test derives its zenohd tcp port as `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` on a namespace argument that only excludes wz's OWN socket; reproduced deterministically, with TIME_WAIT (zenohd sets no SO_REUSEADDR) as the amplifier. Fixed by removing the guess: zenohd binds `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and the test reads the kernel-assigned port back from its own announcement. Round 311y412.decision_summary: R311y412 = retire port GUESSING from the zenohd interop harness entirely, and harden the count-guards that were supposed to catch a lane going quiet. After y411 fixed one lane, no test in this crate names a zenohd tcp port any more: every dialer (ws, tls, quic, quic-datagram, unixsock, udp, vsock, unixpipe) plus the unixpipe+tcp LISTENER delegates to `spawn_zenohd_dialer_on_ephemeral_tcp`, which has zenohd bind `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and reads the kernel-assigned port back out of zenohd's own announcement, then RETURNS it beside the guard. Two guessing routes died: the arithmetic `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` (10 call sites) and, for the four dialers that used it, `PortReservation::pick`'s reserve-then-release. The second removal is the round's non-obvious result and it was MEASURED, not argued: an adversarial reviewer ran an external process cycling loopback ephemeral sockets and the reserve-then-release lanes failed 5/210 (`wz_udp_acceptor`) and 3/210 (`wz_unixsock_acceptor`) with the exact y411 signature (`process exited before accepting ... status 255`), while the discovery lanes were 0/330 under the same churn. That refutes the intuition -- offered by a second reviewer -- that `bind(0)` immunises the reservation: it does avoid TIME_WAIT, but the window between the release and the child's bind is real and losable. `PortReservation` survives only where the port must be named BEFORE a process starts (a wz-side listen), which this route cannot serve. GUARDS: all 34 lane count-guards are now anchored to `^test result: ok\. N passed`. The old substring form false-GREENED two ways, both reviewer-reproduced: a FAILED summary whose passed-count matches (`FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed` satisfies a `5 passed` guard) and count inflation (`11 passed` satisfies a `1 passed` guard, the case `set -o pipefail` could never catch). Round 311y414.decision_summary: R311y414 -- the transport-MODE axis is now hosted, the orthogonal twin of R311y413's link-KIND closure. Enumerating off-default transport-tier atoms from the cargo feature SSOT (11 transport-* modes minus the 10 link kinds, plus reassembly) gives 8 off-default modes -- fragmentation, lowlatency, compression, shm, stats, qos, multilink, multicast -- whose 16 lanes ran ONLY in a local sweep; a new ci.yml transport-modes job (own runner, 45-min budget, disk prune) hosts all 16, taking hosted lanes 57 -> 73 of 107. A first cut claimed those 8 gated on NO hosted lane at all; review falsified that and the round measured the truth per mode: 5 had literally nothing hosted, while fragmentation / multicast / the session-core half of qos were partially and ACCIDENTALLY executed inside Layer C1's cargo test --workspace, because wz-integration-tests' dev-dep feature pins unify onto the shared crate builds (the repo's own R311wq honesty fix records that unification; a still-live contradicted comment is what the first cut echoed). The honest claim is per-SUBJECT: no hosted lane's SUBJECT was a transport mode. Because hosting only helps when a lane can go red, the round first hardened the guards: a new _runci_guarded_test helper (streams via tee while capturing, asserts an anchored libtest summary, rejects an expect of 0) now backs 47 guarded steps in those lanes -- 32 previously bare, 12 new SUBJECT-SCOPED runs, 3 replacing C1ba's racy inline grep form. The 12 exist because a whole-crate run cannot witness its own subject going dark, the clean case being C1bb where a 301-case >=1 sweep stays green while the qos-gated cases fall 21 -> 12. Two harness holes found by review are closed too: --layer with an unknown name used to run nothing and exit 0, and a count-guard failure used to produce an EMPTY GitHub annotation body. Layer M stays out by design (environment-flaky IGMP join); C1m / C1n / C3 compose modes but are isolated-platform-crate genre and stay local-only with the boundary stated. Hosted lanes 57 -> 73 of 107 registered; local-only 50 -> 34.

Lane set enumerated from the CARGO FEATURE SSOT, not a carry list (the R311y413 lesson): the `transport-*` keys in crates/wz/Cargo.toml minus the 10 link kinds = 11 MODES, plus `reassembly` (a transport-tier atom without the prefix -- the rule now says "off-default transport-tier atoms" because the prefix rule silently dropped it). THREE modes ride wz-runtime-tokio's `default` and gate through Layer C1 by construction (unicast / keepalive / batching); the other EIGHT are off-default.

CORRECTED CLAIM (the first cut said the eight "gated on NO hosted lane at all"; review falsified it, and this round measured the truth per mode): lowlatency / compression / shm / stats / multilink had literally nothing hosted -- Layer C1's own command with each subject's filter prints 0 passed. fragmentation / multicast / the session-core half of qos were PARTIALLY and ACCIDENTALLY covered inside Layer C1's `cargo test --workspace`, because wz-integration-tests' dev-dep pins (crates/wz-integration-tests/Cargo.toml:87 session-core, :118-121 runtime-tokio) unify onto the shared builds -- measured under C1's command: multicast_glue 18, qos_emit_tests 2, udp_frag_e2e 1, udp_chaos_e2e 3, layer3_reassembly_rx 4. The honest claim is per-SUBJECT: no hosted lane's SUBJECT was a transport mode.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new `_runci_guarded_test <label> <expect> <cargo ...>` helper -- STREAMS the run (`tee /dev/stderr`, so a lane killed by the job timeout still leaves diagnostics) while capturing it, then asserts the libtest summary: an integer pins `^test result: ok\. N passed` exactly, `+` pins `>=1`. The assert reads the captured copy, never a `grep -q` pipe stage (which races its upstream's SIGPIPE under `set -o pipefail`). `<expect>` is validated: `+` or a POSITIVE integer -- `0` is rejected, since "assert nothing ran" would re-open the hazard.

scripts/run-ci.sh: 47 guarded steps across the 16 lanes -- 32 were previously BARE, 12 are NEW subject-scoped runs, 3 replace the older inline `tee | grep -q` form in C1ba (whose "the helper cannot compose in this chain" rationale review disproved: splitting the chain is what C1bb/C1bc already do, and the helper also names WHICH step missed).

The 12 new subject-scoped runs exist because a whole-crate `cargo test` cannot see its own subject go dark: C1l gains 7 (measured -- under `reassembly` alone udp_chaos_e2e / udp_frag_e2e / layer3_reassembly_tx really are 0-test targets; under transport-fragmentation they carry 3 / 1 / 1), C1p gains 2 (`multicast` filter 32 -> 48 across its two feature sets), C1bb gains 1 (the `+` sweep at 301 cannot see the qos-gated session-core cases vanish -- minus transport-qos the sweep is 276 and the `qos` filter drops 21 -> 12, so exactly 21 is pinned), and C1r / C1s gain a target-scoped guard each (an unscoped guard is satisfied by ANY summary line in a multi-target run).

scripts/run-ci.sh: `--layer <name>` that matches NO lane is now a hard FAILURE. It used to run nothing and exit 0 -- the same "success by silence" class this round closes, and the new job triples the number of layer strings that must stay in sync across two files.

Round 311y415.decision_summary: R311y415 -- the mandatory fmt gate (Layer 0) is hosted for the first time, and the round's larger yield was the falsified comments around it. Layer 0 was defined in run-ci.sh, absent from every hosted --layer set, and dropped from the pre-push hook at R311y386, so it ran nowhere; wiring bash scripts/run-ci.sh --layer 0 into the ci job costs 2 functional lines and everything else this round touches is a comment. A first cut justified it with 'fmt was gated nowhere', which two of three reviewers falsified: .githooks/pre-commit Check 2 has been running cargo fmt --check on staged crates/**.rs since R311au. The honest gap is narrower and RED-tested -- the six standalone deploy/* workspaces were gated by nothing, plus any --no-verify or uninstalled-hooksPath path. Because hosting a gate only helps if it can go red, the lane was hardened first: a discovery floor (the deploy glob loop had no lower bound, so a workspace it missed produced a green fmt --check OK), a whitespace-tolerant [workspace] grep, an accumulating report instead of fail-fast, and a ' FAIL: ' diagnostic, since the old ' FAIL ' spelling matched none of y414's annotation extractor patterns and every Layer 0 red would have carried an EMPTY body. Four more R311y386-invalidated 'pre-push gates it' claims were swept from the same files, the C1b lane's rationale was retracted as measured-false (wz-runtime-tokio pins wz-runtime-core/alloc as a NORMAL dep, so C1 does run all 7 alloc tests), and the wz-integration-tests unification retraction had its evidence re-bound from C1's 413-vs-306 whole-table delta to the +25 that is actually the two pins'. NO Rust source. 3 worktree-isolated reviewers on frozen sha 030520f returned 2 blockers, both against this round's own new prose.

The gap it closes, stated at the width review left it: NOT "fmt was gated nowhere" (a first cut said that and two reviewers falsified it). `.githooks/pre-commit` Check 2 already runs `(cd crates && cargo fmt --all -- --check)` on any staged `crates/**.rs`. What ran nowhere is the SIX standalone `deploy/*` workspaces Layer 0 also covers, plus every `--no-verify` / uninstalled-hooksPath path.

scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer 0 DISCOVERY FLOOR. Round 311y416.decision_summary: R311y416 -- Layer 0's actionlint half becomes a real gate, closing a hole that R311y414 and R311y415 each DISCLOSED and neither closed. Nothing installed actionlint on any runner, so the sub-step had printed SKIP and returned 0 for its entire existence; R311y415's hosted run confirmed that in the log. The round ran measure -> fix -> wire in that order, because wiring first would have produced a red that mixes 'the gate works' with 'the code was dirty'. Findings were counted from scratch rather than inherited: y414's ledger cites 3 at ci.yml:980/1004/1039, but actionlint was absent here so that citation was not reproducible; a fresh v1.7.12 run found 3 at :1031/:1055/:1090 -- the same three, relocated -- all shellcheck-reported, all in the zephyr-mcu job. All three were FIXED, not suppressed: SC1090 twice via the documented source=/dev/null directive on venv activate lines created at runtime, and SC2086 by quoting the variable while preserving tilde expansion. The wiring pins actionlint to v1.7.12 with a sha256 cross-checked against the release's own checksums.txt, on the same reasoning as rust-toolchain.toml and MNEMOSYNE_REV -- an unpinned linter turns an upstream release into a spontaneous red. Two hollow-gate hazards were closed with it: shellcheck is now installed EXPLICITLY rather than assumed from the runner image, because actionlint silently drops its shellcheck checks without it and exits 0 over a near-empty check set, and WZ_LINT_REQUIRE=1 makes either binary's absence FATAL on the hosted job so a broken download reds instead of restoring the silent SKIP. 4 RED perturbations fail closed, including the shellcheck-absent one built by shadowing /usr/bin minus shellcheck with the PATH shape verified first. NO Rust source. This round was pushed without the 3-reviewer pass on the user's instruction; R311y415's two blockers were both in its own new prose, so this one's comments carry less assurance.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: new `Install actionlint (pinned + checksum-verified)` step in the `ci` job (index 5, immediately before Layer 0). Downloads actionlint v1.7.12's linux_amd64 release tarball, verifies sha256 8aca8db9... against the value published in the release's own checksums.txt, installs to /usr/local/bin.

PINNED, not `go install ...@latest`: an unpinned linter turns an upstream release into a spontaneous red on an unrelated push. Same reproducibility trade rust-toolchain.toml and MNEMOSYNE_REV already make in this repo. Bumping the pin is a deliberate commit that should expect new findings.
.github/workflows/ci.yml: the Layer 0 step now sets `WZ_LINT_REQUIRE: "1"` and is renamed to name both halves (`cargo fmt --check + actionlint`).

.github/workflows/ci.yml: `shellcheck` added EXPLICITLY to the ci job's apt list rather than relied on from the runner image -- actionlint runs its shellcheck integration only when shellcheck is on PATH and silently drops those checks otherwise, and all 3 of this repo's actionlint findings came through shellcheck. An image change would have hollowed the lint half out silently.

scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer 0's actionlint sub-step gains the WZ_LINT_REQUIRE axis (the WZ_QZ_REQUIRE / WZ_A3_REQUIRE idiom). Under REQUIRE=1 an absent actionlint is FATAL, and so is an absent shellcheck -- the second because actionlint-without-shellcheck exits 0 over a near-empty check set, which is the same "success by silence" shape R311y415 spent the round closing for fmt. With REQUIRE off both stay non-fatal, so the local developer path is unchanged apart from a new warning line when shellcheck is missing.

scripts/run-ci.sh: actionlint findings now produce ` Layer0 FAIL: ` plus an explicit return 1. Previously the bare `actionlint ...` call was the function's last statement, so its exit code was the lane's -- correct, but with no diagnostic line and therefore no GitHub annotation body (the R311y415 extractor lifts ` FAIL: `). A success path also now prints `actionlint OK (<version>)`, so the log distinguishes "ran and passed" from "skipped".

.github/workflows/ci.yml: the 3 pre-existing findings FIXED, not suppressed -- SC1090 at the two `. ~/zephyrproject/.venv/bin/activate` sites (a `# shellcheck source=/dev/null` directive, the documented remedy for a file created at runtime) and SC2086 at `find ~/zephyr-sdk-${ZEPHYR_SDK_VERSION}` (quoted as `~/zephyr-sdk-"${ZEPHYR_SDK_VERSION}"`, which keeps tilde expansion while quoting the variable).
