Round 311y418.decision_summary: R311y418 -- build the guard R311y417's carry commissioned: a local gate that refuses a store whose schema_version has outrun the pinned CI mnemosyne-cli, so the class that has now fired FOUR times (y15, y401, y406, y416, every one discovered on hosted CI) reds locally instead. MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA lands beside MNEMOSYNE_REV, verified at the pin rather than inherited from prose, and the comparison logic moves into scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh so pre-commit and pre-push share one implementation. Three worktree-isolated reviewers on the frozen first cut found THREE blockers, all reproduced independently before folding: git commit was the only guarded route, so cherry-pick, rebase, merge and --no-verify carried a migrated store straight to the push boundary; the store was graded from the WORKING TREE while hosted CI grades the COMMITTED tree, which both let an index-only staging escape and falsely blocked unrelated commits over an uncommitted migration; and the ceiling was self-asserted, so raising it one character silenced the gate while CI still installed the old reader. The fold grades the INDEX for both halves, adds the same gate to pre-push against every pushed commit, requires the ceiling and the rev to move together, and closes a fail-open where a leading-zero ceiling made bash arithmetic error out inside an if and fall through to green. The round also shipped and fixed its own defect mid-session: the first cut read the pin by SOURCING the index blob, which executed an installer from inside a commit hook. Reading a shell file must not mean running it. Also removed: pre-push's mnemosyne-cli SKIP, unreachable in the flow it was written for and reachable only where the gate matters most. NO Rust source; store schema_version unchanged at 43.
changes_bullets: scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh: NEW MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA="43", the pinned rev's ceiling. Verified at the pin, not inherited: crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:1678 at d7f048b5 defines CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 43 and :1924 rejects on_disk_version > CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION outright. The rationale block also corrects its own count -- see the decision summary.

scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh: NEW shared library, pure function definitions, no top-level statements. wz_schema_pin_gate <spec-prefix> grades the store at any git tree against the pin read from the same tree; wz_schema_pin_cochange_gate refuses an index that moves the ceiling while MNEMOSYNE_REV stands still. Both hooks source it; sourcing is side-effect free by construction, which is the invariant the first cut violated.
.githooks/pre-commit: NEW Check 3 (SSOT gate renumbered to 4), grading the INDEX for BOTH halves. The header comment for the hook now enumerates four checks.

.githooks/pre-push: NEW gate 1, the same check against EVERY pushed commit rather than only the last ref; validate-workspace renumbered to gate 2, changed-crate tests to gate 3. git commit is not the only route to origin.

.githooks/pre-push: the mnemosyne-cli SKIP in gate 2 is REMOVED -- an absent tool is now a hard fail. The lenient branch was unreachable in the flow it was written for, since pre-commit hard-fails on the same condition, and reachable only in the flows where the SSOT gate matters most.

Extraction hardening: the ceiling pattern is line-anchored, bounded to 6 digits, and rejects a leading zero. bash reads 043 as octal 35 (a false red) and ERRORS on 08/09 -- and an erroring (( )) inside an if is false, so the comparison was skipped and the commit passed.

CLAUDE.md + README.md + README.ko.md: the hook descriptions now enumerate every check, and record python3 as a hard requirement of both hooks. The READMEs are the clone-setup docs and had never learned of it.
NO Rust source. NO store mutation beyond this entry; schema_version stays 43.
verification_bullets: HARNESS, rewritten after review: 35/35 cases, each driving a REAL git commit or git push to a local bare remote. The first harness's 22 cases all invoked ./.githooks/pre-commit by hand, which put git's choice of WHETHER to run the hook and WHICH index to hand it out of scope by construction -- reviewer 1 named that, and it is why the three blockers below were invisible to it.

DISCRIMINATOR on the real repo: dropping the ceiling to 42 against the real schema-43 store reproduces the y416 hosted error text, "schema version mismatch: store=43 expected <= 42". Tree restored byte-exact afterwards.

BLOCKER 1, reproduced by me before folding: cherry-pick / rebase / merge / --no-verify never run pre-commit. A store migrated on a side branch landed on main via cherry-pick with rc=0 and HEAD carrying schema 44. Harness C1/C1b now pin the bypass and C1c pins pre-push catching it.

BLOCKER 2, reproduced: grading the WORKING TREE was wrong in both directions. Staging a migrated store then git restore --worktree inverted index 44 vs worktree 43 and the hook went green (harness B1). Conversely a dirty UNCOMMITTED migration blocked commits carrying no store at all, while origin stayed green (B2). Index grading removes both.

BLOCKER 3, reproduced: raising MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA by one character satisfied the gate while MNEMOSYNE_REV still pinned the old reader -- the gate silenced, CI red exactly as before. Harness A3 blocks it, A4 confirms moving both together still lands.

FAIL-OPEN, reproduced: MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA="08" made (( )) error out; because that sits in an if condition, set -e does not fire and control fell through to a green commit with store 43 over a ceiling of 8. Harness D1/D1b/D2/D3/D4.

A DEFECT THIS ROUND SHIPPED AND FIXED MID-SESSION: the first cut read the pin by SOURCING the index blob. The index still held the pre-round script, so the hook EXECUTED an installer and cargo install ran from inside a commit hook (rc=101). Local CLI verified intact afterwards -- d7f048b5, validate clean, entries 1424. Harness F1/F2 pin that reading a shell file is not running it.
DEPENDENCY ABSENCE: python3 absent blocks the commit (G1) with a negative control proving the same minimal PATH plus python3 lands (G1b); mnemosyne-cli absent now blocks the push (G2).
STATIC: bash -n clean on all four shell files. shellcheck introduces ZERO new findings against the 40298d7 baseline -- the two SC2001 notes in pre-commit are pre-existing and untouched.

COST, re-measured interleaved 10 pairs after review found the first number cherry-picked: pre-commit median 0.21s -> 0.36s, delta median 0.15s (min 0.13, max 0.16). Of that, git show of the 16 MB store blob is 0.09s. The 24d46d3 commit message says "+0.06s", which was the low end of a 3-run sample; it is RETRACTED here and cannot be corrected in place.
REVIEW: 3 worktree-isolated reviewers on frozen sha 24d46d3 (falsification / hollow-gate / claim-audit). Every finding I folded was first reproduced by me independently.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y418 built the guard R311y417's carry commissioned, and the review turned it from a one-hook check into a two-hook one. The wiring shipped in the first cut was defeated three ways; none of them were visible to a harness that called the hook directly instead of driving git.

THE COUNT WAS WRONG AND I INHERITED IT. y417's carry said this class "has now fired twice (y406, y416)". Enumerating the ledger gives FOUR: y15 (store=23 expected <= 9), y401 (41 vs 39, repaired at y403), y406 (42 vs 41), y416 (43 vs 42). Every one surfaced on hosted CI. This is the same lesson y417 recorded as costing that session three times -- and it recurred here in the one place a round is most likely to trust prose: a number carried forward from the previous entry rather than counted.

STILL NOT GATED, and it is the honest next step: nothing verifies that MNEMOSYNE_REV's actual CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION equals MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA. The co-change gate proves only that the two moved together. Verifying the value needs the pinned source, so it belongs in ci.yml beside the cargo install --rev, where the source is already fetched.

DISCLOSED, not fixed: (a) pre-commit Checks 1 and 2 end their greps in "|| true", which cannot distinguish "no match" from "grep failed" -- a reviewer reproduced a lock-desync sailing through on a non-ASCII staged path, mitigated only by the English-only policy; (b) nothing lints scripts/*.sh or .githooks/* at all, so the ~150 new shell lines and the shellcheck directives in them are ungated, checked only by hand this round; (c) mapfile is avoided in the new library but pre-push still uses it, so bash 3.2 (stock macOS) remains unsupported, consistent with the existing macOS port debt; (d) shellcheck still floats on the runs-on image while actionlint is pinned.

A HARNESS THAT CANNOT REACH THE FAILURE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ITS ABSENCE. 22/22 was true and meant less than it looked: the cases were well chosen but the DRIVER was wrong, so an entire class -- everything git does around the hook -- was silently out of scope. When a gate's subject is a git workflow, the harness has to run git.

publishable_verification_bullets: HARNESS, rewritten after review: 35/35 cases, each driving a REAL git commit or git push to a local bare remote. The first harness's 22 cases all invoked ./.githooks/pre-commit by hand, which put git's choice of WHETHER to run the hook and WHICH index to hand it out of scope by construction -- reviewer 1 named that, and it is why the three blockers below were invisible to it.

DISCRIMINATOR on the real repo: dropping the ceiling to 42 against the real schema-43 store reproduces the y416 hosted error text, "schema version mismatch: store=43 expected <= 42". Tree restored byte-exact afterwards.

BLOCKER 1, reproduced by me before folding: cherry-pick / rebase / merge / --no-verify never run pre-commit. A store migrated on a side branch landed on main via cherry-pick with rc=0 and HEAD carrying schema 44. Harness C1/C1b now pin the bypass and C1c pins pre-push catching it.

BLOCKER 2, reproduced: grading the WORKING TREE was wrong in both directions. Staging a migrated store then git restore --worktree inverted index 44 vs worktree 43 and the hook went green (harness B1). Conversely a dirty UNCOMMITTED migration blocked commits carrying no store at all, while origin stayed green (B2). Index grading removes both.

BLOCKER 3, reproduced: raising MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA by one character satisfied the gate while MNEMOSYNE_REV still pinned the old reader -- the gate silenced, CI red exactly as before. Harness A3 blocks it, A4 confirms moving both together still lands.

FAIL-OPEN, reproduced: MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA="08" made (( )) error out; because that sits in an if condition, set -e does not fire and control fell through to a green commit with store 43 over a ceiling of 8. Harness D1/D1b/D2/D3/D4.

A DEFECT THIS ROUND SHIPPED AND FIXED MID-SESSION: the first cut read the pin by SOURCING the index blob. The index still held the pre-round script, so the hook EXECUTED an installer and cargo install ran from inside a commit hook (rc=101). Local CLI verified intact afterwards -- d7f048b5, validate clean, entries 1424. Harness F1/F2 pin that reading a shell file is not running it.
DEPENDENCY ABSENCE: python3 absent blocks the commit (G1) with a negative control proving the same minimal PATH plus python3 lands (G1b); mnemosyne-cli absent now blocks the push (G2).
STATIC: bash -n clean on all four shell files. shellcheck introduces ZERO new findings against the 40298d7 baseline -- the two SC2001 notes in pre-commit are pre-existing and untouched.

COST, re-measured interleaved 10 pairs after review found the first number cherry-picked: pre-commit median 0.21s -> 0.36s, delta median 0.15s (min 0.13, max 0.16). Of that, git show of the 16 MB store blob is 0.09s. The 24d46d3 commit message says "+0.06s", which was the low end of a 3-run sample; it is RETRACTED here and cannot be corrected in place.
REVIEW: 3 worktree-isolated reviewers on frozen sha 24d46d3 (falsification / hollow-gate / claim-audit). Every finding I folded was first reproduced by me independently.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311y418 built the guard R311y417's carry commissioned, and the review turned it from a one-hook check into a two-hook one. The wiring shipped in the first cut was defeated three ways; none of them were visible to a harness that called the hook directly instead of driving git.

THE COUNT WAS WRONG AND I INHERITED IT. y417's carry said this class "has now fired twice (y406, y416)". Enumerating the ledger gives FOUR: y15 (store=23 expected <= 9), y401 (41 vs 39, repaired at y403), y406 (42 vs 41), y416 (43 vs 42). Every one surfaced on hosted CI. This is the same lesson y417 recorded as costing that session three times -- and it recurred here in the one place a round is most likely to trust prose: a number carried forward from the previous entry rather than counted.

STILL NOT GATED, and it is the honest next step: nothing verifies that MNEMOSYNE_REV's actual CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION equals MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA. The co-change gate proves only that the two moved together. Verifying the value needs the pinned source, so it belongs in ci.yml beside the cargo install --rev, where the source is already fetched.

DISCLOSED, not fixed: (a) pre-commit Checks 1 and 2 end their greps in "|| true", which cannot distinguish "no match" from "grep failed" -- a reviewer reproduced a lock-desync sailing through on a non-ASCII staged path, mitigated only by the English-only policy; (b) nothing lints scripts/*.sh or .githooks/* at all, so the ~150 new shell lines and the shellcheck directives in them are ungated, checked only by hand this round; (c) mapfile is avoided in the new library but pre-push still uses it, so bash 3.2 (stock macOS) remains unsupported, consistent with the existing macOS port debt; (d) shellcheck still floats on the runs-on image while actionlint is pinned.

A HARNESS THAT CANNOT REACH THE FAILURE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ITS ABSENCE. 22/22 was true and meant less than it looked: the cases were well chosen but the DRIVER was wrong, so an entire class -- everything git does around the hook -- was silently out of scope. Round 311y419.decision_summary: R311y419 -- three CI-gate closures, taken in the order R311y418's carry and disclosures named them, with no wire / atom / inventory change: the schema pin now verifies itself against the pinned BINARY, the repo's own shell is linted for the first time, and the three isolated-crate lanes gate hosted. (1) THE PIN CEILING IS NO LONGER SELF-ASSERTED. R311y418 shipped a store-vs-ceiling gate and named its own residual in its carry: nothing proved MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA was MNEMOSYNE_REV's real CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, since both numbers are hand-set from a hand-read of upstream source, and the co-change gate proves only that they moved together. scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh closes it by asking the INSTALLED binary: mnemosyne-cli describe-schema --json -> .schema_version, which mnemosyne-ops::describe_schema() populates from mnemosyne_atomic::CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION. Its purity was established by construction rather than from its doc comment -- it reports 43 with no workspace present at all, and 43 unchanged against a store hand-set to schema_version 999 -- so it is a property of the binary and never of the tree it runs in. Grading the binary rather than crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs out of the cargo checkout is deliberate: the source file need not be what cargo install actually built. It grades command -v mnemosyne-cli, i.e. what later CI steps run, so a shadowing earlier-PATH binary is caught rather than bypassed. It is called from the TAIL of scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh rather than wired as a ci.yml step, because that script exists so ci.yml and release.yml cannot drift and a gate bolted onto one workflow reintroduces exactly that drift; every install route now runs it, and the SC2034 disable the constant used to carry is gone because it is live code. DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, recorded so a later round does not "strengthen" it into a brittle check: that the binary was built from MNEMOSYNE_REV. mnemosyne-cli --version embeds git describe --always --dirty=-dirty --abbrev=8, so its output is a bare short hash only while NO tag is reachable upstream and degrades to the literal unknown without .git -- a gate whose truth would depend on another project's tagging policy. Git hooks still never install, so a wrong ceiling stays locally invisible until somebody reinstalls the pinned CLI. (2) THE REPO'S OWN SHELL IS LINTED. Layer 0 gains sub-lane 0.2: shellcheck over 18 tracked files (scripts/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh, .githooks/*), a surface disjoint from the workflow run: blocks actionlint covers and, verified by enumerating every gate first, previously linted by nothing. Its first run found a real defect: two prose comments in run-ci.sh began with the word shellcheck, which the tool reads as a malformed DIRECTIVE (SC1073/SC1072) and then abandons the enclosing brace group over (SC1009) -- so all ~13k lines of that file, including the function that runs the linters, had been analysed by nothing. 11 findings were visible at HEAD; 2 of them were that parse-error pair, and clearing them exposed 4 more, for 13 ordinary findings resolved. The gate then went RED ON ITS OWN AUTHOR when a third such comment was written while documenting the trap. One structural fix was load-bearing: shellcheck-presence resolution was hoisted ABOVE the actionlint block, whose early return 0 had been swallowing the new lane whenever actionlint was merely absent -- two independent tools must not share one another's absence. (3) C1m / C1n / C3 GATE HOSTED, on a NEW isolated-crates job. A third genre job rather than a step on an existing one: the transport-modes job states its lane-selection rule and names these three as OUT of it, and both sibling jobs declare disk rather than time as the binding constraint (a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR carrying just these three reaches 1.7G). The genre rule is the complement -- the crate CANNOT participate in --workspace feature unification (C1m/C1n force wz-session-core/no_std, which sce-rust-runtime's compile_error! makes exclusive with the http-send std runtime wz-runtime-tokio pulls, so Layers C1/C2 exclude them by construction), or the matrix exists because unification MASKS what isolation surfaces (C3). Hardened FIRST per R311y414's rule that hosting only helps if the lane can go red: 15 _runci_guarded_test steps at measured counts. The hazard was demonstrated, not assumed -- cargo test -p wz-mcu-session-acceptor --test host_acceptor_reassembly_e2e WITHOUT --features reassembly exits 0 reporting 0 passed. Hosted lanes 73 -> 76 of 107; C4c / C4d (the R311y332 gap) and C1bf are the same genre and remain LOCAL-ONLY, stated because R311y413 recorded "class closed" being overclaimed twice. Three commits, no code/Cargo/atom/inventory change: 2bd59d8, 11a3fb3, dfa38d7.

scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh (2bd59d8): the DISCLOSED LIMIT note on wz_schema_pin_cochange_gate no longer says the check "is not built here" -- it points at the new script and states the surviving half honestly (hooks never install, so a wrong ceiling is locally invisible until a reinstall).

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer 0 (11a3fb3): NEW sub-lane 0.2 shellchecks 18 tracked shell files at shellcheck's DEFAULT severity, with a discovery floor (sc_files_min=18) mirroring fmt_dirs_min so a pathspec that stops matching reds instead of printing OK over a shorter list. .githooks/* entries are admitted by SHEBANG, not by name, since they are extensionless. scripts/run-ci.sh + .githooks/pre-commit + scripts/check-footprint.sh + scripts/verify-codegen.sh (11a3fb3): the 13 findings the new lane surfaced. Two prose comments in run-ci.sh reworded off the word `shellcheck` (they were parsing as malformed directives and suppressing analysis of the whole file); `cd "$repo_root" || exit 2`; two expansions quoted inside a `date -d @$...`; two dead locals removed; one useless `cat | tail` collapsed. Six SC2034 on check-footprint.sh's BASELINE_* arrays are FALSE POSITIVES -- the arrays are resolved through `declare -n` namerefs shellcheck cannot follow -- so they carry a reasoned disable, not a deletion. Two SC2001 in pre-commit likewise: a per-LINE prefix over a multi-line variable is not expressible as ${var//a/b}.

C1m's nine runs are guarded at exact counts that DIFFER per combo (1/1/3/4/5/4/7/3/5), so each pins the arms its own features add; the crate has no tests/ dir, so each run emits exactly two summaries and an exact count is meaningful. C1n keeps its three whole-crate runs BARE (six summaries, four reading `1 passed` under reassembly, so neither an exact count nor >=1 asserts which binary ran) and adds six TARGET-SCOPED guarded runs where the count is unambiguous.

The transport-modes job's "and stay local-only" clause about these three is retracted in place, since it went false the moment this job landed.

.github/workflows/ci.yml Layer 0 step (11a3fb3): records that WZ_LINT_REQUIRE now arms a third lane, and the finding count that a first look does not give (11 visible, 2 of them parse errors hiding 4 more, 13 resolved).
verification_bullets: Pin gate, 22/22 RED/GREEN against the REAL script and the REAL installer: match green; ceiling above AND below the real value both red; the red names the actual value; no-args / two-args / leading zero / non-numeric / empty / 7 digits / negative all rejected; absent mnemosyne-cli and absent python3 both FAIL rather than skip; describe-schema removed, non-JSON, key renamed, value as string, value as bool all red with a re-point-do-not-delete message; a shadowing earlier-PATH cli is the one graded; the installer tail runs the gate and reds through it. The first harness run reported 7 false FAILs from a minimal PATH lacking `bash` itself -- a harness bug, bisected before touching the gate.

Pin gate end-to-end with the REAL `cargo install --git --rev`, not a stub: `bash scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh` rc=0 in 1m6s, ending `verify-mnemosyne-pin: OK -- /home/coin/.cargo/bin/mnemosyne-cli reads schema 43, matching MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA`. Gate cost alone 0.01s over five runs.

Layer 0 sub-lane 0.2, 7/7: baseline green over 18 files; an injected SC2086 in a tracked file reds the lane and the victim is restored byte-identical; a narrowed pathspec trips the discovery floor (found 1, expected >= 18) instead of printing OK; shellcheck absent under WZ_LINT_REQUIRE=1 is FATAL for both lints; shellcheck absent without REQUIRE skips 0.2 and stays green with a message naming BOTH consequences; and 0.2 RUNS even when actionlint is absent -- the swallow this round fixed. Cases needing an unstageable precondition drive a one-line-patched COPY of run-ci.sh, which is disclosed in the harness itself.

C1m / C1n guards, 9/9 falsified through the REAL helper: three baselines green; a count perturbed 3 -> 4 reds; the transport-multicast feature dropped so the run selects 1 instead of 3 reds; the maximal combo reduced 7 -> 4 reds; the reassembly feature dropped so a target selects ZERO tests reds; a renamed target reds rather than skipping; and an expect of 0 is rejected by the helper outright.

The C1n hazard measured directly rather than argued: `cargo test -p wz-mcu-session-acceptor --test host_acceptor_reassembly_e2e` without `--features reassembly` exits rc=0 with `test result: ok. 0 passed`. A bare run would have been green.

Cost measured two independent ways that converge. Local medians over this repo's ~560 archived run-ci logs (n=64 for C3, 66 for C1m, 66 for C1n): 15s / 19s / 5s = 39s, p90 21/31/10 = 62s; at the transport-modes job's measured hosted/local-median ratio of ~3.3x that projects ~2.1 min typical, ~3.4 min p90. An independent cold run (fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR, the three sequential) totals 129s and 1.7G, landing on the same number from the other side. Layer 0's new sub-lane adds ~1s; the lane is 27-30s locally with all three linters.

Full Layer 0 green in the hosted-equivalent configuration, with the ci.yml-pinned actionlint 1.7.12 installed locally so 0.3 was actually exercised after the restructure rather than assumed: `fmt --check OK (7 workspaces)` / `shellcheck OK (18 files)` / `actionlint OK (1.7.12; shellcheck 0.8.0)`, rc=0 with and without WZ_LINT_REQUIRE=1. C3 / C1m / C1n each rc=0 on the edited tree. shellcheck clean over all 18 files; actionlint clean over the edited ci.yml.

validate-workspace unchanged across all three commits: T1 orphan total=13, new=+0, resolved=-0; T3 warn=4 / T4 info=4; sections 266. Store schema 43 == MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA 43 == the pinned CLI's describe-schema 43, re-checked immediately before this append per the R311y416 lesson that a session-start reading has no shelf life.

Hosted lane count verified by parsing rather than grepping, because the naive grep is wrong twice: `grep -oE "run-ci.sh --layer [A-Za-z0-9]+"` returns 77 (it counts the `--layer X` doc placeholder at ci.yml:195), and anchoring on `^        run: bash` returns 75 (Qz lives inside a `run: |` block). The real figure is 76, up from 73.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y419 closed the three items R311y418 left named: its carry's one explicit "honest next step" (the pin ceiling was self-asserted), its disclosure (b) (nothing lints the repo's own shell), and its NEXT line (C1m / C1n / C3 hosted). All three were gate work; no wire, atom, inventory or Cargo change.

THE SHELL LINT GATE PAID FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN, and what it found is the sharpest instance yet of this repo's recurring class. Two prose comments in run-ci.sh started with the word `shellcheck`, so the tool parsed them as malformed DIRECTIVES and abandoned the file -- all ~13k lines, including the very function that runs the linters, had been analysed by nothing, with four real findings sitting behind that silence. R311y418 had hand-checked ~150 new shell lines instead of gating them; hand-checking is exactly what missed this. Then the new gate went red on ITS OWN AUTHOR, on a third such comment written while documenting the trap. The match is a PREFIX, not a whole word -- `shellcheck-backed` triggers it too -- so the first detector regex, which required whitespace after the word, missed the second instance. Never start a comment line with it.

A GATE CAN BE SWALLOWED BY AN UNRELATED TOOL'S ABSENCE. The new sub-lane sat after the actionlint block's early `return 0`, so a developer without actionlint silently skipped the shell lint too, with shellcheck installed and working. Two independent tools sharing one another's absence is the same success-by-silence shape as a SKIP that reports green; resolve shared prerequisites ABOVE the first consumer, not inside the first one that happens to need them.

STILL NOT GATED, carried forward from R311y418 and not narrowed by this round: (a) pre-commit Checks 1 and 2 end their greps in `|| true`, which cannot distinguish "no match" from "grep failed"; (c) pre-push still uses mapfile, so bash 3.2 (stock macOS) remains unsupported -- the new lane deliberately avoids it; (d) shellcheck floats on the `runs-on` image while actionlint is pinned, so a runner-OS bump is a silent linter bump and should expect new findings in BOTH lanes now, not just actionlint's. NEW this round: the pin gate still cannot fire in a git hook, because hooks never install -- a wrong ceiling stays locally invisible until somebody reinstalls the pinned CLI.

NOT GENRE CLOSURE for the isolated-crate job, stated because R311y413 recorded "class closed" being overclaimed twice: C4c and C4d (the wz-runtime-tokio arbitrary-subset BUILD and CLIPPY matrices, the R311y332 gap) and C1bf are the same genre and remain LOCAL-ONLY. Hosted lanes are 76 of 107. Count them by parsing `run:` lines, not by grepping `--layer`: the naive grep counts the `--layer X` doc placeholder, and a strict `^        run: bash` anchor misses Qz inside a `run: |` block.

OPERATIONAL, local-only and not a repo change: the mnemosyne MCP server was dead at session start with nothing but `Connection closed` to show for it. Running the binary by hand is what diagnosed it -- `mnemosyne-mcp` was still at 3bf4c8da (schema <= 39) while the store and the pinned CLI were both at 43, because scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh installs `--bin mnemosyne-cli` ONLY. The local schema-pin gate cannot catch that shape: it grades the store against the ceiling, and both were correct. Reinstalling mnemosyne-mcp at MNEMOSYNE_REV fixes it, but not for the session that discovered it, since the stdio server is spawned once at startup. When bumping the pin, reinstall BOTH binaries.

THE SHELL LINT GATE PAID FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN, and what it found is the sharpest instance yet of this repo's recurring class. Two prose comments in run-ci.sh started with the word `shellcheck`, so the tool parsed them as malformed DIRECTIVES and abandoned the file -- all ~13k lines, including the very function that runs the linters, had been analysed by nothing, with four real findings sitting behind that silence. R311y418 had hand-checked ~150 new shell lines instead of gating them; hand-checking is exactly what missed this. Then the new gate went red on ITS OWN AUTHOR, on a third such comment written while documenting the trap. The match is a PREFIX, not a whole word -- `shellcheck-backed` triggers it too -- so the first detector regex, which required whitespace after the word, missed the second instance. Never start a comment line with it.

A GATE CAN BE SWALLOWED BY AN UNRELATED TOOL'S ABSENCE. The new sub-lane sat after the actionlint block's early `return 0`, so a developer without actionlint silently skipped the shell lint too, with shellcheck installed and working. Two independent tools sharing one another's absence is the same success-by-silence shape as a SKIP that reports green; resolve shared prerequisites ABOVE the first consumer, not inside the first one that happens to need them.

OPERATIONAL, local-only and not a repo change: the mnemosyne MCP server was dead at session start with nothing but `Connection closed` to show for it. Running the binary by hand is what diagnosed it -- `mnemosyne-mcp` was still at 3bf4c8da (schema <= 39) while the store and the pinned CLI were both at 43, because scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh installs `--bin mnemosyne-cli` ONLY. Reinstalling mnemosyne-mcp at MNEMOSYNE_REV fixes it, but not for the session that discovered it, since the stdio server is spawned once at startup. When bumping the pin, reinstall BOTH binaries.

Round 311y420.decision_summary: R311y420 -- the five items R311y419 carried forward as unresolved, all closed, with one of them REFUTED on re-measurement rather than fixed as described. No wire, atom, inventory or Cargo change. (1) THE DISCLOSED grep HAZARD DID NOT REPRODUCE, and the mechanism that does is different and worse. R311y418 recorded a reviewer reproducing a lock-desync sailing through pre-commit on a non-ASCII staged path, mitigated only by the English-only policy. Re-measured: git escapes non-ASCII under the default core.quotePath, so grep never sees the bytes; and forcing core.quotePath=false with genuinely invalid UTF-8, GNU grep 3.7 still returns the match. What DOES reproduce is that `grep` on the author's box is an EXPORTED SHELL FUNCTION (a ugrep wrapper), which on the same input suppressed a valid match and returned 1 -- and git hooks inherit exported functions, so which grep graded a commit was environment-dependent. The first attempt to reproduce the disclosed claim was itself contaminated by that wrapper, which is how the distinction surfaced. Both staged-path filters now route through one `_staged_matching` helper using `command grep` (bypasses functions and aliases), `-a` (no implementation's binary-detection can suppress a match), and a hard block on rc>=2 (grep FAILING, which `|| true` had collapsed into "nothing staged", i.e. into a pass). A negative control proves the case discriminates: with a bare `grep` the hijack succeeds, with `command grep` it does not. (2) THE LAST mapfile IS OUT OF .githooks. mapfile is a bash 4.0 builtin and stock macOS ships 3.2, so pre-push could not run there at all; it is now a while-read loop, matching what scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh already did. This is NOT a claim of repo-wide bash 3.2 support -- scripts/verify-codegen.sh still uses six, including `mapfile -d ''` forms that are awkward to express portably, and rewriting a working script for a platform nobody has asked for is the wrong trade. The hooks are the part a macOS clone must pass before it can commit at all. A scan for bash-4-only constructs caught this round introducing `${push_shas[-1]}` (negative subscripts are 4.3+) in the same commit that was removing the 4.0 dependency; it is index arithmetic now. (3) shellcheck IS PINNED, at 0.11.0 with a published sha256, out of the apt list and into its own step beside actionlint's. R311y417 assessed this exposure as "latent, not live" on the measurement that 0.8.0 / 0.9.0 / 0.10.0 agreed on this tree -- true when Layer 0 linted only the `run:` blocks inside .github/workflows/, and no longer true once R311y419 put scripts/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh and .githooks/* in scope. On THAT surface the versions disagree: 0.11.0 finds 5 SC2086 (unquoted `return $fail`) that 0.8.0 misses, all fixed here, plus SC2329, a check 0.8.0 does not have. 0.11.0 rather than the image's 0.8.0-2 because pinning to the floating value would freeze a 2021 release to avoid triaging its successors. SC2329 fires on 119 functions in run-ci.sh because every lane is reached through `run_layer <name> <fn>` invoking `"$@"`, which no static analysis can follow; that is the design, so it carries a FILE-scoped disable and stays live for the other 17 files. (4) THE PIN GATE NOW FIRES IN THE HOOKS, and earlier than the two that preceded it. R311y419 built scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh but ran it from the installer's tail, and hooks never install -- so it could not fire locally. It does not need to install: the hooks already require mnemosyne-cli on PATH and `describe-schema` is a pure report of the binary's own constant. wz_local_cli_pin_gate asks it directly, from pre-commit against the index ceiling and from pre-push against the pushed tip's. What it catches that the other two cannot is the ORDERING: wz_schema_pin_gate compares the STORE to the ceiling and so fires only once a migration has happened, and the co-change gate only proves two constants moved together; this one fires on the condition that CAUSES the migration, before the next mutate. That is exactly why R311y401, y406 and y416 were each discovered on hosted CI after the store had already been committed and pushed. Both directions block: ahead of the pin migrates the store past the reader CI installs, behind it cannot open a store the pin permits. (5) C4c / C4d / C1bf GATE HOSTED, closing the R311y332 gap R311y419 named and left open; hosted lanes 76 -> 79 of 107. Hardened first, and the hardening found a real hole: all three matrices read the subset SSOT through a PROCESS SUBSTITUTION, whose exit status the reading `while` loop cannot see, so an empty producer would have run zero iterations and returned 0 -- a matrix gate reporting success over an empty matrix. Round 311y421.decision_summary: R311y421 -- the three atoms Layer A4 reported in the headline `proven` with NO hosted-CI witness of any kind, split by DIAGNOSIS rather than treated as one problem, and two of them closed. The A4 roll-up names them together, but mapping each atom's witnesses to the lanes that carry them shows two different failures. router-multicast-faces (5 witnesses) and transport-multicast (7) have EVERY witness in Layer M, which was opt-in and therefore ran on NO default path at all -- not hosted, not even the pre-push sweep. transport-link-vsock has ONE witness, and its lane (Z) IS hosted; the test echo-skips because the runner lacks the vsock_loopback kernel module and a vsock-enabled zenohd. codec-join, separately flagged as "promoted by a test hosted CI never runs", had all its `full` claims in Layer M too. LAYER M IS NOW HOSTED, on the interop job, with WZ_M_REQUIRE=1. That job already builds the zenoh-pico CLI these witnesses need, so a separate runner would pay that build again to gain nothing. WZ_M_REQUIRE makes every SKIP path fatal -- the opt-in guard itself and the pico-CLI prereq -- on the same rule as WZ_Z_REQUIRE: the job guarantees the CLI, so a SKIP would be a provisioning regression wearing a green badge and would silently restore the exact state this round closes. THE OPT-IN RATIONALE WAS RE-READ, NOT INHERITED. run-ci.sh kept the lane opt-in because multicast is "environment-dependent: a CI CONTAINER without a multicast route on the default interface drops the IGMP join". That is a claim about containers; GitHub's hosted runners are full VMs with a default route. The tests also use 224.0.0.224 -- the link-local control block -- joined with INADDR_ANY and set_multicast_loop_v4(true), so both ends are the same host and the datagram never leaves it. Measured locally: 5/5 green, 0 skips, 15-26s. None of that PROVES the runner can join, so the lane now prints a multicast preflight (routes, links, a real IGMP join attempt) before its first test; a failure is therefore readable as environment-versus-code in ONE run instead of an unexplained red. VSOCK GETS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A GUESSED GATE. Its two blockers differ in kind: the zenohd-vsock oracle is a known cached recipe (ZENOHD_VSOCK=1, exactly like the unixpipe variant already provisioned), but whether this runner image can load vsock_loopback is an unknown no local measurement can settle. Two halves. (A) THE VSOCK MEASUREMENT REFUTED THE CLAIM THAT JUSTIFIED THE EXEMPTION. HOST_GATED_CI_TARGETS excluded wz_vsock_acceptor_zenohd_interop because "AF_VSOCK loopback needs the vsock_loopback kernel module + a vsock-enabled zenohd oracle; the hosted runner has neither and ci.yml provisions neither". R311y421 shipped a probe rather than guess, and run 30251723895 answered it: kernel 6.8.0-1062-azure, `sudo modprobe vsock_loopback` succeeds, /dev/vsock appears, and a bind+listen on VMADDR_CID_LOCAL returns (1, 3517351901). The oracle half was true and is a known cached recipe; the KERNEL half was never measured and is false. So the probe became real provisioning -- modprobe as a hard step that reds with a named cause if the module will not load, plus a cached ZENOHD_VSOCK build and a presence assertion, mirroring the unixpipe oracle beside it -- the Layer Z vsock leg lost its WZ_Z_REQUIRE exemption, and HOST_GATED_CI_TARGETS is now EMPTY. The mechanism is deliberately kept: a genuinely host-gated target still belongs there with its reason, and assert_host_gated_ci_targets() still falsifies such a declaration in both directions. (B) SIX LOCATOR ATOMS WIRED TO WITNESSES THAT ALREADY EXISTED, ONE REFUTED, ONE BLOCKED. All 8 unproven locator-* atoms had ZERO `wz-proves` lines while every kind already had a hosted cross-impl acceptor test, so this was a claim-wiring problem rather than a test-writing one -- but the honesty burden falls entirely on manual verification, because A4-5 containment is EXEMPT for FOUNDATIONAL atoms (they name no cfg site, so containment over their name is vacuous) and 7 of the 8 are FOUNDATIONAL. Round 311y423.decision_summary: R311y423 -- the four unproven scouting-* atoms, worked in order and reported by what each actually needs rather than as one task. ONE CLOSED, ONE'S WITNESS BUILT AND PROVEN, TWO BLOCKED BEHIND PRODUCT CODE -- and the blockers were established by running the real binaries, not inferred. (1) scouting-gossip CLOSED, by binding it to a witness that already existed and was already asserted. wz_router_hat_zenohd_interop's leg 1 asserts that wz DECODED at least one of zenohd's LinkStateList OAM floods -- `forwarder.ingested() > 0`, surfaced as the `learned mesh topology` shutdown line -- and that decode IS the atom (wz-routing-graph + linkstate_forward.rs, FOUNDATIONAL/always-on). The test's own comment already separates that assertion from the convergence tick it calls handshake-satisfiable, which is the R311y140 distinction; the claim binds to the decode, not to the link-up. zenohd->wz only: wz's own flood reaching zenohd is not asserted there, so no reverse claim was made. A4: proven 84 -> 85, unproven 39 -> 38, both populations still identical. (2) scouting-autoconnect's WITNESS did not exist and now does. The demo has driven `--autoconnect` since it was added, but the only log on that path says "gossip-autoconnect enabled" -- which proves the FLAG was parsed, not that anything was dialed -- and `summary.dialed` counts the static `--connect` seed and reconcile adds too, so asserting on either would credit the atom to a node autoconnect never moved. That is the hollow-witness shape R311y140 recorded. So `AcceptLoopSummary` gains `gossip_dialed`, incremented in exactly one place -- the `Step::Dial` arm, reachable only through a DialIntent the forwarder emits after the autoconnect policy admits a peer discovered in a link-state flood -- and the demo latches a shutdown line when it is > 0. The counter's DISCRIMINATION is proven rather than asserted: the existing autoconnect unit test now requires gossip_dialed == 1 and the existing static-dial test requires gossip_dialed == 0, and mirroring the increment at the static site makes that second assertion fail, verified. (3) scouting-autoconnect's cross-impl PROOF is blocked on a topology fact, measured twice with real binaries. A wz peer attached to a zenohd router learns `peak 2 node(s)` -- itself and that router -- with one zenohd and also with two linked zenohds. zenoh's link-state flood is ROUTER-TIER, so a peer-tier attachment never receives a dialable third party; and a wz node attached as `--router-hat` WOULD receive it, but linkstate_forward.rs:233 states the autoconnect matcher for a ROUTER admits nobody, mirroring zenoh. So the precondition the proof needs does not exist in the demo's current mode set. (4) scouting-active and scouting-multicast are blocked earlier still: the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting at all (args.rs:157 mentions it only in prose). zenohd answers scouts on 224.0.0.224:7446 by default and R311y421 both hosted Layer M and MEASURED the runner's IGMP join, so the execution environment is ready -- what is missing is one product-code entrypoint, after which a single test witnesses both (scouting-multicast is FOUNDATIONAL, "always-on under scouting-active"). NOT WIRED, deliberately: layer3_scout.rs and layer3_hello.rs prove SCOUT/HELLO codec parity against pico's C source, and scouting-active's F names that codec pair -- but a codec-parity test proves the BYTES match, not that wz actively scouts, and the atom's own note calls it a MODE ("indep of passive/static modes"). Claiming it there would be the same over-claim R311y422 caught with locator-iface, and containment would not have refuted it. Two commits: 843c0a8, 223c128.

A CLAIM-WIRING ROUND AND A PRODUCT-CODE ROUND LOOK IDENTICAL FROM THE UNPROVEN LIST. R311y422's locator block was 6 atoms of pure wiring: every witness already existed and only the `wz-proves` line was missing. The scouting block has the same shape in A4's output and almost none of it is wiring -- one atom was wireable, one needed a new counter and log, and two need a CLI entrypoint that does not exist. Before estimating a block, trace one atom end to end: witness -> test -> lane -> hosted. The list tells you what is unproven, never what it costs.

A FLAG IS NOT A WITNESS. `--autoconnect` had been drivable for many rounds and logged "gossip-autoconnect enabled" -- a line that proves argument parsing. `summary.dialed` was equally useless because the static seed and reconcile bump it too. The fix was a counter with exactly one increment site plus a PAIRED assertion (1 on the gossip path, 0 on the static path), and the pair is the whole point: mirroring the increment makes the second assertion fail, which is what "discriminator" has to mean.

THE BLOCKER IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A MISSING TEST, and it is worth recording so the next attempt does not re-run these spikes: zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a wz PEER attached to zenohd sees `peak 2 node(s)` and never a dialable third party; a wz `--router-hat` node does receive the flood but its autoconnect matcher admits nobody by design (linkstate_forward.rs:232-233, mirroring zenoh). Either the demo needs a peer-tier gossip path that carries locators, or the proof needs a topology where the foreign side advertises a router the wz peer may dial.

(2) scouting-autoconnect's precondition, which is a design question before it is a test. (3) The axis then has 36 unproven left, plus 37 `partial` to upgrade.

A CLAIM-WIRING ROUND AND A PRODUCT-CODE ROUND LOOK IDENTICAL FROM THE UNPROVEN LIST. R311y422's locator block was 6 atoms of pure wiring: every witness already existed and only the `wz-proves` line was missing. The scouting block has the same shape in A4's output and almost none of it is wiring -- one atom was wireable, one needed a new counter and log, and two need a CLI entrypoint that does not exist. Before estimating a block, trace one atom end to end: witness -> test -> lane -> hosted. The list tells you what is unproven, never what it costs.

A FLAG IS NOT A WITNESS. `--autoconnect` had been drivable for many rounds and logged "gossip-autoconnect enabled" -- a line that proves argument parsing. `summary.dialed` was equally useless because the static seed and reconcile bump it too. The fix was a counter with exactly one increment site plus a PAIRED assertion (1 on the gossip path, 0 on the static path), and the pair is the whole point: mirroring the increment makes the second assertion fail, which is what "discriminator" has to mean.

THE BLOCKER IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A MISSING TEST, and it is worth recording so the next attempt does not re-run these spikes: zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a wz PEER attached to zenohd sees `peak 2 node(s)` and never a dialable third party; a wz `--router-hat` node does receive the flood but its autoconnect matcher admits nobody by design (linkstate_forward.rs:232-233, mirroring zenoh). Either the demo needs a peer-tier gossip path that carries locators, or the proof needs a topology where the foreign side advertises a router the wz peer may dial.

NEXT, in cost order: (1) a demo entrypoint for ACTIVE multicast scouting -- one product-code slice that opens BOTH scouting-active and scouting-multicast, since the latter is FOUNDATIONAL and always-on under the former; zenohd answers on 224.0.0.224:7446 by default, Layer M is hosted, and the runner's IGMP join is measured, so only the entrypoint is missing. (2) scouting-autoconnect's precondition, which is a design question before it is a test. (3) The axis then has 36 unproven left, plus 37 `partial` to upgrade.

DO NOT wire layer3_scout / layer3_hello to scouting-active. They prove SCOUT/HELLO codec parity against pico's C source; the atom is the MODE ("indep of passive/static modes"). Containment would not refute it -- scouting-active is active, so containment applies, but it checks feature closure, not whether the test drives the mode. Same trap as locator-iface at R311y422.

Round 311y424.decision_summary: R311y424 -- a defect R311y423 shipped, found by asking of its own green run the question this repo exists to ask: WHICH LANE COMPILES THIS. R311y423 added a paired assertion (gossip_dialed == 1 on the autoconnect path, == 0 on the static path) that makes `AcceptLoopSummary::gossip_dialed` a discriminator rather than a mirror of `dialed`, reported it as "11/11 with a falsification", and pushed into a 14/14-green hosted run. The assertions are inside `#[cfg(feature = "routing-peer")]`, `routing-peer` is NOT in wz-runtime-tokio's default set, and nothing unifies it in -- measured, not reasoned: `cargo test --workspace --lib accept_loop -- --list` selects NEITHER test. So Layer C1 compiles them out, the only lane that runs them is `layer_c1y_cargo_test_routing_peer`, and C1y appeared in NO ci.yml `--layer` step. The hosted green said nothing about the new assertions because it never built them. This is the class the whole session has been closing -- a proof that never runs -- authored fresh inside a round whose own subject was that class, and R311y414 had already been blocked by the same wrong assumption about `--workspace` feature unification. THE FIX, in the order R311y419 established. First HARDEN: C1y's nine FILTERED / TARGET-SCOPED runs were all bare, and `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 when the filter selects nothing, so each was one rename or cfg-slip away from passing over an empty selection. They are now `_runci_guarded_test` at counts measured on this tree -- accept_loop 11, linkstate 199, interceptor 10, linkstate+access 210, extauth 10, auth_dispatch 4, usrpwd e2e 3, extauth_pubkey 7, pubkey e2e 1 -- while the unfiltered whole-crate `-p wz-routing-graph` run stays BARE, per the convention that an unfiltered run has no meaningful count to pin. Falsified TWO ways, the second being the exact shape of this incident: perturbing a count reds the lane, and dropping `--features routing-peer` makes the run select ZERO tests and the guard reds where a bare `cargo test` would have exited 0. Then HOST: C1y goes on the feature-gates job, whose genre line -- "subsets no other job composes" -- describes it verbatim. Hosted lanes 79 -> 81 (the other addition since R311y420 being Layer M at R311y421). Cost is measured, not guessed: local median 45s / p90 99s over 66 archived run-ci logs, ~194s / ~426s at this repo's own measured 4.3x hosted-to-local-median ratio, inside the job's 30-minute budget. AND ONE MEASUREMENT THE JOB ASKED FOR ITSELF: the feature-gates header declares "THIS JOB HAS NO OTHER DISK HEADROOM" while recording in the same paragraph that end-of-job free space is UNKNOWN rather than known-tight, and that "a post-lane `df -h` would settle it". Adding a lane is the moment to stop deferring that, so the job now reports free space after its lanes -- a report, never a gate, and the number is what should decide whether the next lane belongs here or on a new runner. One commit: d59986c.

Round 311y425.decision_summary: R311y425 -- the GENERAL FORM of the R311y423/y424 defect, enumerated instead of waited for, and its first and largest batch closed. R311y424 fixed one lane (C1y) after tracing one test, and named the sweep it had not done: nothing had ever asked, across ALL local-only lanes, which of them is the SOLE runner of some test. That sweep now exists and its answer was not one more C1y: of 107 run-ci lanes, 27 were local-only, 21 of those were the sole runner of at least one test selector, and 44 selectors -- `--lib` filters and `--test` integration targets alike -- were named by NO hosted lane. Every one of them is a test that cannot fail the merge gate, which is the same success-by-silence this repo has spent the round series closing, at 44x the scale of the incident that revealed it. THE PLACEMENT DECISION WAS DECIDED BY A MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE INHERITED RATIONALE. Grouped by genre the 21 lanes cost ~29 min hosted at the median and ~82 min at p90, so they do not fit one job, and the obvious move was a fourth runner -- the feature-gates header has declared "THIS JOB HAS NO OTHER DISK HEADROOM" since R311y318, and that declaration is precisely what sent feature-gates, transport-modes and isolated-crates onto separate machines. R311y424 added the post-lane `df -h` that same header had asked for since R311y415, and its first run reported 146G total / 78G used / 68G AVAIL after the lanes. The disk argument is measured false; the real constraint is TIME. So this batch lands on the existing feature-gates job with its budget raised 30 -> 45, and no fourth runner is created. That is the fourth inherited claim this session has overturned by measuring it. WHAT LANDED: the ext-pubsub §5.25 and singleton groups -- C1ap C1aq C1ar C1at C1au C1av C1aw C1ah C1ai C1k C1o -- eleven lanes carrying 13 of the 44 orphan selectors at a 64s local median. Hardened first, per the R311y419 rule that hosting only helps if the lane can go red: all 15 of their filtered runs were BARE, and `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 when the filter selects nothing, so each was one rename or cfg-slip from passing over an empty selection. They are now `_runci_guarded_test` at counts measured on this tree, and the counts are real discriminators rather than decoration -- the same `--lib advanced_subscriber` filter yields 3, 14 and 24 under C1ar's, C1at's and C1av's feature sets respectively, so each guard pins the arms its own features add. Falsified three ways: a perturbed count reds, a dropped `--features` (the run then selects ZERO tests and a bare invocation would exit 0) reds, and a narrowed feature set that changes the count reds. Round 311y426.decision_summary: R311y426 -- the STORAGE group, second of the three R311y425 left named, and the worst single instance of the class this arc has been closing. C1z carried SIXTEEN filtered `cargo test` invocations and every one was bare; since `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 when the filter selects nothing, each was one rename or cfg-slip from passing over an empty selection, and the lane ran on no hosted job at all. All sixteen are now `_runci_guarded_test` at counts measured on this tree, and the counts are discriminators rather than decoration: the SAME `--lib storage` filter returns 27, 35, 39, 40, 46, 50, 53 and 127 under eight different storage feature sets, so each guard pins the arms its own features add. C1bg needed a different fix: it was already guarded, but with an inline `grep -qE '^test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'` -- a `>= 1` form that catches an EMPTY selection and not a set that silently shrinks. Both of its runs move to `_runci_guarded_test` at exact counts (14, 2), the same substitution R311y414 made for three other inline forms. Falsified two ways against the real lane: perturbing the 127 count reds, and dropping `--features storage-aligner` from the `--test storage_aligner_convergence_e2e` run -- which makes it select ZERO tests and exit 0 bare -- reds. PLACEMENT, and why the remaining two groups are NOT here. Both lanes go on feature-gates, whose ceiling R311y425 raised to 45 after R311y424's `df -h` disproved the disk rationale. The arithmetic that admits storage also excludes routing: the job measured 14m37s with C1y, R311y425's eleven add ~4.6 min median / ~16.6 p90, and these two add ~5.6 / ~8.7 -- landing near 25 min typical and ~40 at p90, inside 45. Routing (C1x, C1ax, C1ay, E7b) would add ~17.5 min at p90 and put the job over its own ceiling, and adminspace (C1am, C1an, C1ao, E7c) is worse at ~39 min p90. RESULT: local-only lanes 16 -> 14, sole-runner lanes 10 -> 8, orphan selectors 31 -> 22, hosted lanes 92 -> 93. C1am's own orphan count fell 7 -> 6 as a side effect, because C1z now runs `--lib storage_manager_service` hosted. One commit: d3ecf0a.

Round 311y427.decision_summary: R311y427 -- the routing and adminspace groups hosted, which effectively closes the sole-runner class: 2 lanes and 2 selectors remain, from 21 and 44 when R311y425 first swept. AND IT CORRECTS R311y426, whose placement conclusion the very next measurement falsified. That round wrote that routing and adminspace "need their own runner", projecting them at the 4.3x hosted-to-local-median ratio R311y419 measured, which put feature-gates over its 45-minute ceiling. Hosted run 30267052174 then timed the eleven lanes R311y425 had added: 138s hosted against a 64s local median -- 2.2x, not 4.3x -- and the job as a whole moved only 14m37s -> 16m43s. The explanation is structural rather than noise: a lane APPENDED to a job that has already built the workspace reuses those artefacts, while the lanes the 4.3x came from did not. Recomputed at 2.2x these eight cost about 5.8 min (routing) and 4.0 (adminspace), landing the job near 26 min inside its existing ceiling. So no new runner, no budget change, and R311y426's "they need their own runner" is retracted here rather than inherited. That is the THIRD firing of the borrowed-ratio lesson in this arc and the first in the OVER-estimating direction; the durable form is that a borrowed ratio sizes a timeout and does not decide a placement. HARDENED FIRST, per the rule this arc has followed since R311y419: 42 filtered runs across the six pure-cargo lanes were all bare, and `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 on an empty selection, so each was one rename or cfg-slip from passing over nothing. All are now `_runci_guarded_test` at counts measured on this tree. Two things surfaced that guessing would have gotten wrong. C1ax ran four namespace e2e targets in ONE invocation, which prints four summaries of which two read `1 passed` -- an exact count would have matched the wrong line -- and measuring the targets individually showed the combined run's summary ORDER is not the target order (namespace_e2e is 4, namespace_query_e2e is 1, not the reverse the combined output suggests). And a falsification came back GREEN: dropping `--features adminspace-core` from C1am's `--lib zid_hex` run left all 3 tests running, because that feature is not load-bearing for that filter. The guard was fine; the PERTURBATION was invalid, and the round re-falsified against `compiled_plugins`, where the feature genuinely gates, plus a count perturbation. RESULT: hosted lanes 93 -> 99, local-only 14 -> 8, sole-runner lanes 8 -> 2, orphan selectors 22 -> 2. Round 311y428.decision_summary: R311y428 -- the product-code slice R311y423 named as next, and it opened BOTH atoms it was supposed to: scouting-active and scouting-multicast now have a cross-impl proof against zenohd, executed by hosted CI. THE MISSING PIECE WAS NOT THE FLAG. R311y423 recorded the blocker as "the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting", which reads as one CLI flag; the flag was the smallest of three gaps. The wz facade's scouting-active was a declaration-only "= []" key, so a consumer enabling it got the marker and NONE of the scouting code -- the multicast FSM was unreachable through the facade entirely, and the only way in was a direct wz-runtime-tokio dep that no facade consumer has. Second, ScoutParams was a PRIVATE use in scouting_glue, so the module's own public constructor ScoutingActions::new could not be CALLED through the facade -- its parameter type was unnameable there; the in-tree tests never hit it because they carry a wz-session-core dev-dep the facade's consumers lack. Both are now forwarded (AP-only, mirroring session-extauth: wz-runtime-coop has no scouting-active key, and inventing one would claim an MCU active-scouting path that does not exist). THE ENTRYPOINT IS A LOCATOR SOURCE, NOT A NODE KIND. --scout resolves the Initiator's connect locator by active multicast scouting before the role exists -- the active-mode twin of the static synth_static_locators bypass (docs/scouting-fsm.md 2.4.3) -- so everything downstream of the resolved string is the ordinary one-shot Initiator and needed no change; --router / --peer / --router-hat / --storage-host are separate node KINDS and this is deliberately not one. It repeats the scout cycle within a budget because drive_scouting_until_resolved is one cycle by construction (zenoh-pico's __z_scout_loop shape, scout.c:57) and a single datagram races a responder still joining the group; repetition is zenoh's own shape (Runtime::scout loops the send while receiving, orchestrator.rs:848-877), while its exponential backoff is deliberately NOT mirrored -- that loop is an unbounded background task, this is a bounded startup budget. MEASURED BEFORE BUILT: a hand-built wz-shaped SCOUT to 224.0.0.224:7446 returned a real zenohd HELLO (hdr 0x22, one locator "tcp/127.0.0.1:17447") that was DIALABLE, which is why the slice composes scout -> session-open instead of stopping at discovery. RUNNING IT FOUND THE DEFECT THAT MATTERED: with env_logger::init still downstream of the resolution, a real --scout run discovered and dialed the right locator while printing NO scouting line at all -- a test written against that binary would have asserted on a line it could never print, and every other assertion would still have passed. The init and banner moved up. THE ASSERTION IS SOMETHING THE DEMO WAS NEVER TOLD: zenohd binds tcp/127.0.0.1:0, the kernel picks the port, the demo's argv carries no address, so a log line naming that exact port can only have come from decoding zenohd's Hello. Three REDs prove the leg discriminates -- a zenohd with --no-multicast-scouting fails the readiness gate; a dial not derived from the scout fails the Established assertion; a witness locator not derived from the decode fails the port equality -- and a no-responder negative control emits 3 Scouts, records 0 Hellos, prints no witness and exits 1. Hosted on Layer M, placed above the pico-CLI guard since it needs only zenohd, with a zenohd prereq that SKIPs locally and is FATAL under WZ_M_REQUIRE. A4: proven 85 -> 87, unproven 38 -> 36, both populations identical. scouting-autoconnect stays unproven -- R311y423's topology blocker is a design question this round did not touch. DISCLOSED, because it changed this round's NUMBER: the session opened on a view of the repo four commits stale -- its kickoff git log and the harness snapshot both reported HEAD at c468712 (R311y423), and the first validate-workspace printed 1430 ledger entries, exactly the store's state at that commit, while HEAD had been 9586f3f (R311y427) since 22:10, before the session began. Nothing was raced (the reflog dates all four intervening commits before the session) and the working TREE was never stale. The stale view was caught by the frozen-ledger gate rejecting an append to an existing Round 311y424; renumbered to y428, with all 20 in-code citations across 9 files renumbered with it.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: scout_for_peer_locator -- join 224.0.0.224:7446, emit a Scout, return the first locator a peer's Hello advertises, with the constants it needs (SCOUT_GROUP / SCOUT_PORT / SCOUT_WHAT=0x03 ROUTER|PEER / SCOUT_CYCLE_MS / SCOUT_TICK_MS). It REPEATS the cycle within the budget because drive_scouting_until_resolved is one cycle by construction (pico's __z_scout_loop shape, vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/scout.c:57) and a single Scout races a responder still joining the group. Repetition is zenoh's own shape (Runtime::scout loops the send with a growing delay while receiving, zenoh net/runtime/orchestrator.rs:848-877); the exponential backoff deliberately is NOT mirrored, since that loop is an unbounded background task and this is a bounded startup budget.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the witness log -- "scouted peer locator <loc> (scout_emit=N, record_hello=N)". The locator has exactly one producer, ScoutOutcome::Discovered, reachable only through record_hello_and_emit decoding a peer Hello; the FSM's own dispatch counters ride the same line so the claim binds to scouting.scxml's actions.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: --scout / --scout-timeout-ms parse feature-uniformly and resolve into the Initiator's connect locator BEFORE the role match -- scouting is pre-session locator resolution (the active twin of the static synth_static_locators bypass), so everything downstream of the resolved string is the ordinary one-shot Initiator and needed no change. THE BLOCKER WAS BIGGER THAN THE CARRY SAID, and the carry was not wrong so much as looking at the wrong layer. RUNNING THE BINARY IS WHAT FOUND THE REAL DEFECT. The lesson is narrow and repeatable: when a round's whole value is a witness LINE, run the binary and read the line before writing the assertion.

ASSERT ON SOMETHING THE SUBJECT WAS NEVER TOLD. THE SESSION OPENED ON A FOUR-COMMIT-STALE VIEW, AND THE FROZEN-LEDGER GATE IS WHAT CAUGHT IT -- disclosed because it changed this round's NUMBER. The kickoff `git log` and the harness's own git snapshot both reported HEAD at c468712 (Round 311y423), and the session's first validate-workspace printed "atomic ledger: entries=1430" -- which is exactly the store's state AT c468712 (R311y423's own verification bullet records 1429 before its append). HEAD was in fact 9586f3f (Round 311y427) and had been since 22:10, before this session began: git reflog dates the four intervening commits at 20:51-22:10, so nothing was committed concurrently and no work was raced. The stale view survived every later read silently -- validate-workspace printed 1434 from then on -- until "append-changelog-entry --entry-id Round 311y424" was REJECTED with "frozen ledger: entry_id Round 311y424 already exists". That rejection is the gate doing precisely its job: the round is renumbered y428, and all 20 in-code R311y424 citations across 9 files were renumbered with it. Verified after the fact: refs/remotes/origin/main = HEAD = 9586f3f with nothing unpushed, the worktree store is byte-identical to HEAD, and HEAD's blob parses to 1434 changelog_entries / 266 sections / schema 43 containing y424-y427. Every delta in this entry is stated against the verified 1434, and the A4 / Layer M / clippy / fmt measurements above all ran on the real tree (they postdate the discovery of nothing -- the working tree was never stale, only the reported HEAD and that first count).

The guard's WIRING falsified, not just the helper trusted: running the same _runci_guarded_test call with expect=2 instead of 1 returns rc=1, so the exact-count assertion is live rather than decorative. publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311y428 built the entrypoint R311y423 named as the cheapest next item and closed BOTH atoms it was supposed to open: scouting-active and scouting-multicast are proven cross-impl against zenohd, A4 unproven 38 -> 36, and the leg runs on hosted CI (Layer M) rather than only locally.

THE BLOCKER WAS BIGGER THAN THE CARRY SAID, and the carry was not wrong so much as looking at the wrong layer. R311y423 recorded "the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting" -- true, and it read as "add a flag". The flag was the smallest part: wz/scouting-active was a declaration-only "= []" key, so NO facade consumer could reach the scouting FSM at all, and ScoutParams was unnameable through the facade, so the glue's own public constructor could not be CALLED from a facade consumer even with the feature on. Neither gap was visible from the demo's argv, and neither would have been found by grepping for the flag. When a carry says "only X is missing", check that X's dependencies are actually reachable from where X has to live.

RUNNING THE BINARY IS WHAT FOUND THE REAL DEFECT. The scouting witness lines went to a logger that was not yet initialised: the demo discovered the right locator, dialed it, and Established, while printing NOTHING about scouting. A test written against that binary would have asserted on a line it could never print, and it would have been a hollow proof of exactly the R311y140 shape -- except invisible, because every OTHER assertion would have passed. The lesson is narrow and repeatable: when a round's whole value is a witness LINE, run the binary and read the line before writing the assertion.

ASSERT ON SOMETHING THE SUBJECT WAS NEVER TOLD. This leg's discriminator is that zenohd binds tcp/127.0.0.1:0, the KERNEL picks the port, and the demo's argv carries no address at all -- so a log line naming that exact port can only have come from decoding zenohd's Hello. That is stronger than any assertion over values both sides knew in advance, and it is available whenever a test can let the foreign side CHOOSE something.

NEXT, in cost order. Either the demo needs a peer-tier gossip path carrying locators, or the proof needs a topology where the foreign side advertises a router the wz peer may dial. Nothing in this round touched that. (2) The axis has 36 unproven left plus 37 partial to upgrade.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, so a later round does not read these as oversights. --scout composes with --reconnect (the discovered locator becomes the reconnect target, since --scout only fills in what --connect would have named) but that combination has NO test; it is reachable and plausible, not proven. And the group address stays a constant rather than a CLI knob: an address the peers do not share discovers nothing, and zenoh exposes the override in its config file, not its scouting API.

Round 311y429.decision_summary: R311y429 -- adopt mnemosyne's Round-783 citation-gate coverage check and move the pin, in ONE commit because measurement shows they cannot be split. THE TRIGGER, and it is the inverse of every prior pin round: nothing was red on hosted CI. The author's PATH mnemosyne-cli carried a validator this repo's pin did not, so validate-workspace FAILED in the pre-commit hook ("1883 Rust source(s) neither scanned by [plugins.set_equality_validator].paths nor declared in scan_exclusions") while hosted CI, which installs the pinned rev, stayed green through R311y428. The four prior firings of the pin class all ran the other way (store ahead of the pinned READER, discovered only on hosted CI), so this one is worth naming as its own shape: any upstream change to validate-workspace can red the local hook, and the diagnosis is which BINARY produced the failure, not what the round changed. WHY ONE COMMIT, measured rather than argued: SetEqualityValidatorConfig is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], and the OLD pin (d7f048b5) rejects the new table outright -- "unknown field `scan_exclusions`, expected one of `paths`, `severity_missing`, ..." -- so config-without-rev reds hosted Layer A, and rev-without-config reds it on the coverage check instead. NOT A SCHEMA BUMP, the first here that is not: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is 43 at both d7f048b5 and b867bfe2 (read at the new rev, mnemosyne crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:1678, not inherited from prose) and the store is 43, so MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA does not move; the co-change gate permits that direction and refuses only a ceiling moving alone. WHAT THE GATE IS: `paths` declares what the citation validator scans, `scan_exclusions` declares what this workspace knowingly does not, and any .rs in NEITHER fails -- so a tree that merely appears is loud rather than silently uncovered. Declaring nothing is not a passing state, which is why adoption was forced rather than optional. THE COVERAGE DECLARED, chosen by measuring rather than by taste: scan the author-written Rust (`crates`, `deploy`, `xtask` -- 790 files, ZERO citation violations, so the gate cost nothing to turn on and now holds every `Round NNN` / §N reference in wz's own code against the store), exclude `vendor` (four third-party submodules; only vendor/sce carries .rs, 1021 files, read-only from this repo) and `out` (sce-codegen emits, whose header policy is SCE's). `deploy` is scanned WHOLESALE rather than by src/ subdir for a reason that only measurement exposes: a local gitignored `deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e/target-loopback/` build tree holds 287 dependency-generated .rs that the validator's built-in `target/` skip does not match, and it cannot be excluded either -- it is UNTRACKED, so on a CI checkout that exclusion would match no file, and a stale exclusion is FATAL ("delete them", verified by planting one). Scanning the parent is the only stable answer. DISCLOSED as a new local requirement: because a stale exclusion is fatal, the `vendor` row needs vendor/sce actually checked out -- all 10 ci.yml checkouts and release.yml use `submodules: recursive`, so hosted CI is safe, but a local clone with uninitialised submodules now fails the pre-commit hook until `git submodule update --init --recursive`. The pin bump also REPAIRS the doctrine deviation disclosed at R311y417: b867bfe2 is simultaneously mnemosyne origin/main and the exact rev the local PATH binary reports, so pin, local reader and CI reader are one rev again for the first time since that round.
changes_bullets: mnemosyne.toml: new [plugins.set_equality_validator] with paths = ["crates", "deploy", "xtask"] and scan_exclusions = ["vendor", "out"] -- the Round-783 coverage declaration this workspace had never made (no [plugins] table existed at all, so the gate saw 0 scanned / 1883 unscanned and refused every commit). The comment records what each list means, why each entry is on the side it is on, why `deploy` is wholesale rather than by subdir (the untracked target-loopback tree cannot be excluded without going stale on CI), and the new submodule requirement the `vendor` row creates for local runs.

Round 311y43.decision_summary: R311y43 -- §5.23 combined-node FOUNDATION (trait seam + retained config), the root fix for the y42 "uncomposed config" HIGH finding. The y42 review (registered §5.23 caveat) found the "reads AND drives LIVE config" capability uncomposed: run_peer built a TRANSIENT WzConfig (build->log->install->DROP) while the test-only declare_adminspace serialized a FRESH from_init_params -- two unrelated instances, "single SSOT" false at runtime; green per-round CI missed it (isolation tests do not catch "never run together"). User chose Foundation-first over the full combined node (the wire-queryable adminspace in a routing peer needs a NEW forwarder self-query dispatch bridge -- bigger than the carry implied: direct read showed the forwarder EXCLUDES self from query routing [linkstate_forward.rs:1282-1302] and reply-production is Session-level only). This round delivers the foundation by-construction: (1) an InterceptorSink trait seam decoupling the typed WzConfig from the concrete LinkstateForwarder (install/reconfigure take &dyn InterceptorSink; LinkstateForwarder impls it via UFCS delegation; call sites coerce, no edits); (2) run_peer RETAINS one OWNED WzConfig for the node lifetime (read at startup install+log AND a shutdown echo) instead of dropping it -- held owned not Rc/Arc since nothing shares it yet (the sharing primitive is deferred to the Phase-2 adminspace second holder, not speculative now); (3) a single-instance composition test proving ONE WzConfig both DRIVES the live forwarder (deny verdict flips) and serves to_admin_json -- the structural refutation of the two-instance gap. NO inventory flip (refactor of the existing active §5.23 config atom; A3 active=101 unchanged). The wire-queryable adminspace GET + PUT remain DEFERRED to Phase 2/3 (the self-query dispatch bridge first). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
