Round 311y430.decision_summary: R311y430 -- scouting-autoconnect, the last unproven scouting atom, is CLOSED cross-impl, and it needed NO product code: the blocker seven rounds of carries repeated was a mis-diagnosis of its own measurement. R311y423 measured a wz peer beside a zenohd seeing only "peak 2 node(s)" -- correct -- and then attached a causal story that was never checked: "zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a wz PEER attachment never receives a dialable third party". That is a claim about zenoh, and it is false. zenoh routing.peer.mode is SUBSYSTEM-WIDE, not per-node: hat/mod.rs:275-281 selects linkstate_peer::HatCode for "linkstate" and p2p_peer::HatCode otherwise, and DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:240-241 states the option "needs to be set to the same value in all peers and routers of the subsystem". wz LinkstateNetwork ingest mirrors the FULL-linkstate path, so wz IS a linkstate-mode peer; y423 spike left its zenohd at the "peer_to_peer" default, which zenoh own rule forbids mixing. "peak 2 node(s)" was the documented consequence of a NON-UNIFORM subsystem, not a wall in the demo mode set -- so the FIXTURE was what had to change. THE PROOF is a three-node topology: a zenohd ROUTER, a THIRD-PARTY zenohd PEER listening beside it, and a wz --peer --autoconnect whose argv names ONLY the router; wz learns the third party listen port from the router LinkStateList and DIALS it, giving dialed 2 / accepted 0 and one gossip dial, with peak 3 node(s) where y423 saw 2. THE ASSERTION IS A PORT THE DEMO WAS NEVER TOLD, and it discriminates the DIRECTION of the dial rather than the existence of a mesh: with --autoconnect removed the mesh still forms, because the foreign peer own autoconnect dials wz instead, but the face then sits on a kernel-chosen SOURCE port and the leg REDS. Both REDs were planted and run, not argued -- restoring the "peer_to_peer" fixture also REDS the positive leg, at the 20s deadline. Join order is NOT a precondition, measured both ways (network.rs:860-864: the whatami==Router narrowing on the add_link delta applies only when NOT full_linkstate), so the test carries no inter-node gate. A4: proven 87 -> 88, unproven 36 -> 35, both populations identical; Layer Z, already hosted under WZ_Z_REQUIRE, runs the three legs. TWO THINGS NAMED AND NOT FIXED: wz implements only ONE of zenoh two peer routing modes (p2p_peer, zenoh DEFAULT, ingests via process_linkstates_peer_to_peer with no edge rebuild and no prune -- wz always runs the full path), and the demo hardcodes AutoConnectStrategy::GreaterZid where zenoh defaults to always, which is why this fixture must pin three zids.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs: NEW, three legs on a THREE-node topology no existing file hosts — a zenohd ROUTER (zid ff), a THIRD-PARTY zenohd PEER listening beside it (zid 01, seeded to the router with `-e`), and `wz-ap-demo --peer --autoconnect --zid 02` whose argv names ONLY the router's port. All three run `--cfg routing/peer/mode:"linkstate"`, which is what the earlier spike lacked. Leg 1 (positive) asserts wz's face to the third party landed on that peer's LISTEN port plus `autoconnected to gossip-discovered peer(s) (1 dial(s))` and `dialed 2, accepted 0`; leg 2 is the option-atom PAIR with `--autoconnect` removed and the fixture otherwise byte-identical; leg 3 is a no-third-party control with the flag ON.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs: the zids are PINNED (`P=01 < W=02 < R=ff`) and the module doc says why — the demo builds its policy with `AutoConnectStrategy::GreaterZid`, not zenoh's `always` default, so the tie-break is what makes the candidate set exactly {P} and the dial COUNT deterministic. Random ids would make `1 dial(s)` a coin flip. `--id` takes `1` and not `01` because zenohd rejects a leading zero (`Invalid id: 01 - Leading 0s are not valid`, measured); the byte on the wire is the same, so the face-UP needle still matches wz's zero-padded `zid 01`.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the Layer Z lane gains the new `--test` invocation directly after `wz_peer_zenohd_interop`, under the same `--test-threads=1` (this file spawns TWO zenohd per leg). The comment records why the round is a fixture change rather than a product change, so a later reader does not re-derive it.

NOT CHANGED, each for a checked reason. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: Layer Z is already hosted with `WZ_Z_REQUIRE: "1"` (ci.yml:1015-1016), so the proof executes on hosted CI with no edit. The Layer Z demo build: `router-hat-router` implies `routing-router-hat` which implies `routing-peer` (wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml:377,387), so the binary already carries `--peer` / `--autoconnect` / `--zid`. The `scouting-autoconnect` inventory row: its `reason` describes the CODE (FOUNDATIONAL, always-on, cfg=0) and that is still exactly true — the proof axis is computed from `wz-proves` annotations, not from inventory status, so editing it would have been an invented change.
verification_bullets:
THE POSITIVE LEG, run against real binaries (zenohd v1.5.0, two instances): `wz-ap-demo peer: face 1 UP (peer 127.0.0.1:

, zid 01)` then `shutdown; dialed 2, accepted 0, served 2 peer(s), ..., ingested 4 link-state(s), peak 3 node(s) in topology graph, 3 graph edge(s)` and `autoconnected to gossip-discovered peer(s) (1 dial(s))`. `peak 3 node(s)` is the direct refutation of R311y423's `peak 2 node(s)` under the same node count — the difference is the subsystem's peer mode, nothing else.

RED 1 — THE FIXTURE IS LOAD-BEARING, proven by planting the old condition rather than by argument: flipping the helper's one cfg to `routing/peer/mode:"peer_to_peer"` (zenoh's default, i.e. exactly R311y423's non-uniform subsystem) makes the positive leg FAIL, `wz peer never brought up a face to the third-party zenohd peer ... within 20s`, `finished in 20.26s`. Reverted.

RED 2 — THE ASSERTION DISCRIMINATES THE DIAL DIRECTION, not the existence of a mesh. Removing `--autoconnect` from the POSITIVE leg only (fixture untouched) still produces `face 1 UP (peer 127.0.0.1:58452, zid 01)` and `reciprocal mesh link confirmed (2 edge(s))` — the mesh forms anyway, because the foreign peer's own zenoh autoconnect dials wz — yet the leg FAILS, because 58452 is a kernel-chosen SOURCE port and the needle names the peer's LISTEN port. A liveness-shaped assertion would have passed here. Reverted.

JOIN ORDER IS NOT A PRECONDITION, measured both ways rather than assumed, which is why the test carries no inter-node readiness gate: wz-last gives `dialed 2, accepted 0` + `1 dial(s)`, and wz-FIRST (wz already attached when the third party joins) gives the same `dialed 2, accepted 0` + `1 dial(s)` with `ingested 6` instead of 4. This matches zenoh net/protocol/network.rs:860-864, where the `whatami == Router` narrowing on the add_link delta applies only when NOT full_linkstate.

THE NEUTER LEG'S OWN LEDGER: `dialed 1, accepted 1` plus `learned mesh topology` and NO `autoconnected` line. Both halves are asserted — discovery unchanged, dial gone — so the pair establishes that the flag moved the dial and not the discovery.

THE LANE ACTUALLY RUNS IT: `WZ_Z_REQUIRE=1 bash scripts/run-ci.sh --layer Z` exits 0, `Layer Z pass (117s)`, and the log shows `Running tests/wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs` -> `running 3 tests` -> `3 passed`. Not a SKIP: WZ_Z_REQUIRE turns a missing prerequisite into a FAIL.

A4 AFTER THE LEG: `bash scripts/audit-crossimpl-proof.sh` reports CROSS-IMPL PROOF [all lanes] proven=88 partial=37 unproven=35 and [executed by hosted CI] the SAME 88/37/35 — both populations identical, so nothing is credited to a lane hosted CI does not run. Baseline before was 87/37/36. `scouting-autoconnect` is gone from the printed unproven list; no malformed `wz-proves` line and the feature-closure check passed.

WORKSPACE GATES: `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` clean — T1 orphan total=13 (ledger=13, new=+0), T3 warn=4 / T4 info=4 unchanged, and the R311y429 citation gate now reports `1884 rust source(s), 791 scanned, 0 unscanned, 0 stale exclusion(s)` (the new test file is the 791st and carries zero citation violations). `cargo fmt -p wz-integration-tests --check` clean; `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` clean on run-ci.sh.

DISCLOSED, observed and NOT diagnosed: in the three-node linkstate spike the ROUTER zenohd logs one `ERROR ... [Peers Network] Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` — zenoh net/protocol/network.rs:527-539, where a link psid in wz's advertisement had no zid mapping yet on that link, so zenohd dropped THAT EDGE and continued. It is not fatal here (the mesh still converged to 3 edges and every leg's assertion holds) and it is on the wz->zenohd flood, not the discovery direction this round claims. The cause is not established, so nothing is asserted about it beyond the observation.
carry_forward_bullets: SCOUTING IS CLOSED. All four `scouting-*` atoms are now proven cross-impl: gossip (R311y423), active + multicast (R311y428), autoconnect (this round). A4 stands at proven=88 partial=37 unproven=35 with the all-lanes and hosted-CI populations identical.

THE LESSON THIS ROUND COST THE MOST TO LEARN, and it is not about scouting: a MEASUREMENT and its EXPLANATION are two claims, and only the first was verified. R311y423 measured `peak 2 node(s)` correctly and then attached a causal story about zenoh ("floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a peer never receives a dialable third party") that was never checked against zenoh's source. The story was wrong, it was carried verbatim through y424, y428 and y429, and it shut the atom for seven rounds. When a carry says "blocked by <fact about a foreign system>", the fact is the thing to re-read first — the blocker, not the workaround.

WHAT THE FACT ACTUALLY IS, worth keeping because it governs every future wz-peer fixture: zenoh's `routing.peer.mode` is SUBSYSTEM-WIDE. `hat/mod.rs:275-281` picks `linkstate_peer::HatCode` for "linkstate" and `p2p_peer::HatCode` otherwise, and `DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:240-241` says the option "needs to be set to the same value in all peers and routers of the subsystem". wz's ingest mirrors the FULL-linkstate path, so a wz peer belongs in a `linkstate` subsystem and EVERY zenohd in a wz peer fixture needs `--cfg routing/peer/mode:"linkstate"` — the router too, not just the peer. A default zenohd in that fixture is a misconfigured subsystem by zenoh's own rule, and its symptoms will look like wz bugs.

A NAMED, NOT-INVENTED GAP: wz implements only ONE of zenoh's two peer routing modes. `p2p_peer` (zenoh's DEFAULT `routing.peer.mode = "peer_to_peer"`) ingests via `process_linkstates_peer_to_peer` (network.rs:559-614) — no edge rebuild, no reachability prune — while wz's `LinkstateNetwork` always runs the full-linkstate path. So wz cannot join a DEFAULT-configured zenoh peer subsystem as a peer. This is a real capability gap, distinct from `scouting-autoconnect` (which is the POLICY, and is now proven), and it is nobody's atom yet. Naming it is the point; sizing it is a later round.

A DIVERGENCE LEFT IN PLACE DELIBERATELY: the demo hardcodes `AutoConnectStrategy::GreaterZid` (wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs) while zenoh's default is `always` (DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5 `autoconnect_strategy`, `defaults.rs` `Unique(Always)`), and there is no flag to reach the default. wz's own `autoconnect.rs` doc already records Always as zenoh's default, so this is a demo-surface expressiveness gap, not a policy bug — but it is why this round's test has to pin three zids, and any future autoconnect fixture will pay the same tax until a `--autoconnect-strategy` flag exists.

THE ZENOHD-SIDE ERROR is unexplained and should not be forgotten: `[Peers Network] Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` fires once on the router when wz floods, meaning one psid in wz's advertised links had no zid mapping on that link yet and zenohd dropped that edge (network.rs:527-539). Non-fatal today. It is a wz->zenohd flood-hygiene question, and the honest next step is to reproduce it minimally before theorising.
NEXT on the proof axis: 35 unproven plus 37 `partial` to upgrade. Nothing in this round touched them.

WHAT THE FACT ACTUALLY IS, worth keeping because it governs every future wz-peer fixture: zenoh's `routing.peer.mode` is SUBSYSTEM-WIDE. `hat/mod.rs:275-281` picks `linkstate_peer::HatCode` for "linkstate" and `p2p_peer::HatCode` otherwise, and `DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:240-241` says the option "needs to be set to the same value in all peers and routers of the subsystem". wz's ingest mirrors the FULL-linkstate path, so a wz peer belongs in a `linkstate` subsystem and EVERY zenohd in a wz peer fixture needs `--cfg routing/peer/mode:"linkstate"` — the router too, not just the peer. Round 311y431.decision_summary: R311y431 -- the three items R311y430 left open, all closed, and not one of them was what its carry said. (1) THE UNEXPLAINED ROUTER ERROR was a real wz divergence with a one-line cause. zenoh propagate_link_states withholds only the UPDATED half from the source link (network.rs:661); NEW nodes ride back out on it. wz dropped the whole source face, on a written rationale -- "every node it would echo back was advertised BY that source, so the echo is redundant" -- that is false, because PSID SPACE IS PER-SENDER: the source knows that node under ITS numbering and nothing about ours, so our next self-entry naming that psid in links is unresolvable and zenohd rejects the edge. Read off the wire with zenohd tracing, and established as OURS rather than upstream by a pure-zenoh three-node control that logs the error ZERO times. (2) THE STRATEGY DIVERGENCE was a missing flag: --autoconnect-strategy now exists and DEFAULTS to always, which is zenoh default and was previously unreachable since the demo hardcoded GreaterZid; the opt-in carries the strategy inside an Option so "off, but with a strategy" is unrepresentable. (3) THE PEER-MODE GAP is closed at the DISCOVERY plane. LinkstateNetwork gains zenoh full_linkstate flag plus process_linkstates_peer_to_peer -- no edge rebuild, no reachability prune -- because running a gossip flood through the linkstate ingest makes every links-less entry unreachable and the trailing GC deletes the node the flood just introduced. That is literally observable as "pruning detached node" in the wrong mode. A second, INDEPENDENT fix was needed and only running found it: in gossip mode the add_link 2-entry delta must be unconditional (zenoh own condition), since the gossip re-flood relays direct neighbours only and would otherwise never introduce the freshly-dialed peer. wz now gossip-autoconnects inside a STOCK zenoh subsystem -- no routing/peer/mode on either zenohd -- with the router logging no error. NOT CLAIMED, and named rather than blurred: the p2p_peer DATA plane. wz routes along the linkstate spanning tree and a gossip mesh has no edges to build one from, so --peer-mode peer-to-peer switches discovery only; the default stays linkstate because that is the mode wz whole stack implements. The interop file goes 3 legs to 7 (two new PAIRS plus the router-log regressions), and a REAL FLAKE was root-caused rather than retried: a leg that asserted a link the foreign peer opens after its 0-100ms backoff was settling on the flood instead, green in isolation and red under sibling load. verification_bullets: THE DEFECT WAS READ OFF THE WIRE, not inferred. With zenohd tracing `zenoh::net::protocol::network`, the router logged wz sending `[LinkState { psid: 0, sn: 3, zid: None, links: [1, 2] }]` — a links-only self entry naming psid 2 — while the mappings it had ever received from wz were psid 0 and psid 1 only. Hence `ERROR ... Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` (zenoh `network.rs:527-539`).

IT IS wz's BUG AND NOT UPSTREAM BEHAVIOUR, established by a PURE-ZENOH control rather than by reading: the identical three-node linkstate topology with a zenohd peer in wz's place logs `unknown link mapping` ZERO times across all three processes. Its trace shows why — the zenoh peer sends `[psid 2, sn 2, zid Some(1), links [1]]` (the new node, WITH its zid) before the links-only self entry that references psid 2.

AFTER the `propagate` fix, wz's wire matches that shape: the router now receives `[LinkState { psid: 2, sn: 2, zid: Some(1), whatami: Peer, links: [1] }]` first and the links-only self entry second, and logs no error.

UNIT RED for the propagate fix: the new `propagate_sends_new_nodes_back_to_the_source_face` fails with the old whole-source-face exclusion (`assertion left == right failed: the NEW node must ride back out on the source face`) and passes with it. The same test also pins the per-node exclusion (the other face gets the updated half only, links-only) so the fix cannot be over-applied.

CROSS-IMPL RED for the propagate fix: restoring the old exclusion makes leg 1 fail on the router-log assertion ALONE (`wz-integration-tests/.../wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs:352`) — every other assertion in that leg still passes, so the assertion is bound to this fix and nothing else.

THE GOSSIP-MODE HALF NEEDED A SECOND FIX, found by running rather than by reasoning: with `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` the router STILL logged one `unknown link mapping`, because the gossip re-flood relays direct neighbours only, so the newly-dialed peer was never introduced by that path either. Making `flood_link_added`'s 2-entry delta unconditional in gossip mode (zenoh's own condition) drops it to zero, verified against a stock zenohd.

THE MODE SWITCH, proven as a PAIR against a STOCK zenoh subsystem (no `routing/peer/mode` on either zenohd, so both run zenoh's `peer_to_peer` default). `--peer-mode peer-to-peer`: `discovered peer 01 reachable at ["tcp/127.0.0.1:17902"]`, `face 1 UP (peer 127.0.0.1:17902, zid 01)`, `dialed 2, accepted 0`, `autoconnected to gossip-discovered peer(s) (1 dial(s))`, `peak 3 node(s)`. `--peer-mode linkstate`, same fixture: `pruning detached node Zid(01)`, `peak 2 node(s)`, `dialed 1`, no gossip line — the reachability GC deleting the announcement, observed directly.

UNIT TWIN for the mode switch: `gossip_ingest_keeps_a_links_less_node_the_linkstate_ingest_prunes` feeds ONE builder-produced gossip announcement to two receivers differing only in the flag; RED-checked by neutering `set_full_linkstate` to ignore its argument, which fails it. A second test pins `gossip_reflood_admits` (direct neighbours only until multihop).

THE STRATEGY PAIR, on a fixture where wz's zid is the LOWER so the two values must disagree: `always` reports `1 dial(s)` and `dialed 2, accepted 0`; `greater-zid` reports no gossip line and `dialed 1, accepted 0`. Same topology, same discovered peer, one flag apart.

A REAL FLAKE WAS FOUND AND ROOT-CAUSED RATHER THAN RETRIED. The neuter leg passed in isolation and FAILED once six sibling legs shared the CPU: it settled on the flood but asserted `accepted 1`, which lands after the foreign peer's 0-100ms backoff. Every leg that asserts a link now settles on that link (`settle_needle`); 7 legs x 3 consecutive runs green, plus the full Layer Z lane.

WHO MAY DIAL IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not a race won: legs asserting `accepted 0` run the foreign peer with `scouting/gossip/autoconnect:{router:[],peer:[]}` (verified accepted by zenohd — its `Initial conf` echo shows `autoconnect: {peer: [], router: []}`), so the foreign side CANNOT initiate.

carry_forward_bullets: ALL THREE ITEMS R311y430 LEFT OPEN ARE CLOSED, and none of them turned out to be what its carry said. The "unexplained" router error was a real wz divergence with a one-line cause; the strategy divergence was a missing flag; and the "wz implements only one of zenoh's two peer modes" gap was closable at the DISCOVERY plane without touching the data plane.

A DIVERGENCE WITH A WRITTEN RATIONALE IS STILL A CLAIM. `propagate`'s source-face exclusion carried a confident paragraph explaining why the echo was redundant. It was wrong, it had been wrong since the function was written, and no test covered it — the only thing that ever objected was a foreign implementation's ERROR log. When a comment says "a DELIBERATE divergence", treat the paragraph as the least-tested thing in the file. Same disease as R311y430's blocker prose, one layer down.

PSID SPACE IS PER-SENDER. This is the invariant behind both halves of the fix and it is easy to lose: a link-state's `links` array carries the SENDER's psids, so advertising a node to a peer is not the same as that peer being able to resolve it. Any change that omits a node from a flood must ask "does the receiver still have a mapping for every psid I am about to reference".

WHAT `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM. It switches the DISCOVERY plane — ingest, re-flood shape, and the add_link introduction — so a wz peer joins a stock zenoh subsystem, learns third parties and gossip-autoconnects there. It does NOT claim the DATA plane: wz routes along the linkstate spanning tree, and a gossip mesh has no edges to build one from (`peak 3 node(s)`, `0 graph edge(s)` in the proving run). zenoh's `p2p_peer` hat routes pubsub/queries by direct faces instead, and wz has no equivalent. That hat is the remaining half and is nobody's atom yet — name it before building it.

THE DEFAULT STAYS `linkstate` even though zenoh's is `peer_to_peer`, deliberately: wz's data plane implements linkstate, so defaulting to the other mode would ship a node whose discovery and routing disagree. Revisit only when the p2p data plane exists.

FLAKE-HUNTING RULE THIS ROUND PAID FOR: settle on the event you ASSERT, not on the event that motivates it. The neuter leg asserted `accepted 1` (a link the foreign peer opens after a 0-100ms backoff) while waiting on the flood, and passed three times in isolation before failing under sibling load. Isolation-green is not green.
STILL UNTOUCHED: the A4 axis's remaining 35 unproven plus 37 `partial`. `scouting-autoconnect` gained a stock-subsystem leg this round, so its claim is now mode-independent on the discovery plane.

publishable_verification_bullets: THE DEFECT WAS READ OFF THE WIRE, not inferred. With zenohd tracing `zenoh::net::protocol::network`, the router logged wz sending `[LinkState { psid: 0, sn: 3, zid: None, links: [1, 2] }]` — a links-only self entry naming psid 2 — while the mappings it had ever received from wz were psid 0 and psid 1 only. Hence `ERROR ... Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` (zenoh `network.rs:527-539`).

IT IS wz's BUG AND NOT UPSTREAM BEHAVIOUR, established by a PURE-ZENOH control rather than by reading: the identical three-node linkstate topology with a zenohd peer in wz's place logs `unknown link mapping` ZERO times across all three processes. Its trace shows why — the zenoh peer sends `[psid 2, sn 2, zid Some(1), links [1]]` (the new node, WITH its zid) before the links-only self entry that references psid 2.

AFTER the `propagate` fix, wz's wire matches that shape: the router now receives `[LinkState { psid: 2, sn: 2, zid: Some(1), whatami: Peer, links: [1] }]` first and the links-only self entry second, and logs no error.

UNIT RED for the propagate fix: the new `propagate_sends_new_nodes_back_to_the_source_face` fails with the old whole-source-face exclusion (`assertion left == right failed: the NEW node must ride back out on the source face`) and passes with it. The same test also pins the per-node exclusion (the other face gets the updated half only, links-only) so the fix cannot be over-applied.

CROSS-IMPL RED for the propagate fix: restoring the old exclusion makes leg 1 fail on the router-log assertion ALONE (`wz-integration-tests/.../wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs:352`) — every other assertion in that leg still passes, so the assertion is bound to this fix and nothing else.

THE GOSSIP-MODE HALF NEEDED A SECOND FIX, found by running rather than by reasoning: with `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` the router STILL logged one `unknown link mapping`, because the gossip re-flood relays direct neighbours only, so the newly-dialed peer was never introduced by that path either. Making `flood_link_added`'s 2-entry delta unconditional in gossip mode (zenoh's own condition) drops it to zero, verified against a stock zenohd.

THE MODE SWITCH, proven as a PAIR against a STOCK zenoh subsystem (no `routing/peer/mode` on either zenohd, so both run zenoh's `peer_to_peer` default). `--peer-mode peer-to-peer`: `discovered peer 01 reachable at ["tcp/127.0.0.1:17902"]`, `face 1 UP (peer 127.0.0.1:17902, zid 01)`, `dialed 2, accepted 0`, `autoconnected to gossip-discovered peer(s) (1 dial(s))`, `peak 3 node(s)`. `--peer-mode linkstate`, same fixture: `pruning detached node Zid(01)`, `peak 2 node(s)`, `dialed 1`, no gossip line — the reachability GC deleting the announcement, observed directly.

UNIT TWIN for the mode switch: `gossip_ingest_keeps_a_links_less_node_the_linkstate_ingest_prunes` feeds ONE builder-produced gossip announcement to two receivers differing only in the flag; RED-checked by neutering `set_full_linkstate` to ignore its argument, which fails it. A second test pins `gossip_reflood_admits` (direct neighbours only until multihop).

THE STRATEGY PAIR, on a fixture where wz's zid is the LOWER so the two values must disagree: `always` reports `1 dial(s)` and `dialed 2, accepted 0`; `greater-zid` reports no gossip line and `dialed 1, accepted 0`. Same topology, same discovered peer, one flag apart.

A REAL FLAKE WAS FOUND AND ROOT-CAUSED RATHER THAN RETRIED. The neuter leg passed in isolation and FAILED once six sibling legs shared the CPU: it settled on the flood but asserted `accepted 1`, which lands after the foreign peer's 0-100ms backoff. Every leg that asserts a link now settles on that link (`settle_needle`); 7 legs x 3 consecutive runs green, plus the full Layer Z lane.

WHO MAY DIAL IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not a race won: legs asserting `accepted 0` run the foreign peer with `scouting/gossip/autoconnect:{router:[],peer:[]}` (verified accepted by zenohd — its `Initial conf` echo shows `autoconnect: {peer: [], router: []}`), so the foreign side CANNOT initiate.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: ALL THREE ITEMS R311y430 LEFT OPEN ARE CLOSED, and none of them turned out to be what its carry said. The "unexplained" router error was a real wz divergence with a one-line cause; the strategy divergence was a missing flag; and the "wz implements only one of zenoh's two peer modes" gap was closable at the DISCOVERY plane without touching the data plane.

A DIVERGENCE WITH A WRITTEN RATIONALE IS STILL A CLAIM. `propagate`'s source-face exclusion carried a confident paragraph explaining why the echo was redundant. It was wrong, it had been wrong since the function was written, and no test covered it — the only thing that ever objected was a foreign implementation's ERROR log. When a comment says "a DELIBERATE divergence", treat the paragraph as the least-tested thing in the file. Same disease as R311y430's blocker prose, one layer down.

PSID SPACE IS PER-SENDER. This is the invariant behind both halves of the fix and it is easy to lose: a link-state's `links` array carries the SENDER's psids, so advertising a node to a peer is not the same as that peer being able to resolve it. Any change that omits a node from a flood must ask "does the receiver still have a mapping for every psid I am about to reference".

WHAT `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM. It switches the DISCOVERY plane — ingest, re-flood shape, and the add_link introduction — so a wz peer joins a stock zenoh subsystem, learns third parties and gossip-autoconnects there. It does NOT claim the DATA plane: wz routes along the linkstate spanning tree, and a gossip mesh has no edges to build one from (`peak 3 node(s)`, `0 graph edge(s)` in the proving run). zenoh's `p2p_peer` hat routes pubsub/queries by direct faces instead, and wz has no equivalent. That hat is the remaining half and is nobody's atom yet — name it before building it.

THE DEFAULT STAYS `linkstate` even though zenoh's is `peer_to_peer`, deliberately: wz's data plane implements linkstate, so defaulting to the other mode would ship a node whose discovery and routing disagree. Revisit only when the p2p data plane exists.

FLAKE-HUNTING RULE THIS ROUND PAID FOR: settle on the event you ASSERT, not on the event that motivates it. The neuter leg asserted `accepted 1` (a link the foreign peer opens after a 0-100ms backoff) while waiting on the flood, and passed three times in isolation before failing under sibling load. Isolation-green is not green.

(1) Layer C2 clippy: `//!   4/5.` in the scouting-autoconnect interop file is not an ordered-list marker, so `clippy::doc_lazy_continuation` read it as a lazy continuation of item 3 and `-D warnings` refused the crate. y431 ran clippy on wz-routing-graph, wz-runtime-tokio and wz-ap-demo -- and named that as the FULL Layer Z feature set -- but never on wz-integration-tests, the crate whose file it had just written. (2) Layer C1y: `run-ci.sh` pins `C1y linkstate` at exactly 199 and y431 added a linkstate unit test, so the run printed 200 and the guard fired. A COUNT IS A CITATION: adding a test invalidates it, and the invalidation is not local to the one line CI happened to reach. THE SAME SHAPE WAS THEN FOUND IN THE TOOLCHAIN while repairing it, and it is the more expensive one. `mnemosyne-mcp` had been stale since R311y429: that round moved MNEMOSYNE_REV d7f048b5 -> b867bfe2 to adopt `scan_exclusions`, the CLI followed because scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh installs it, and the MCP binary did not because NOTHING installs it -- the installer passes `--bin mnemosyne-cli` alone. The old server died at startup on `unknown field scan_exclusions`, and the only thing the client surfaces is `Connection closed`, which is indistinguishable from a server that was never configured. So two rounds of sessions ran with the Mnemosyne concept resources unreachable and no session diagnosed it; this one did only because the kickoff reported the absence instead of routing around it. Closed by scripts/install-mnemosyne-mcp.sh, which READS the rev through scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh rather than carrying a second copy of the hash, and proves the install with a real `initialize` handshake against this workspace. Deliberately NOT a version-string match: scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh:46-55 already reasons that out for the CLI -- `--version` embeds `git describe`, so it is a bare short hash only while no tag is reachable upstream and degrades to the literal `unknown` when .git is absent -- and the reasoning transfers verbatim. So the CLI moved with the pin and the MCP binary had no install path at all.

THE EXIT-CODE CLAIM IS MEASURED, and the first reading of it was wrong. An initial probe appeared to show the failing server exiting 0; that 0 was `head`'s, from the pipeline. Run without a pipe against a workspace whose mnemosyne.toml holds an unknown field, the server exits 1 with an empty stdout and the diagnostic on stderr.
SHELL GATES on the new script: `bash -n` clean and `shellcheck -S warning` clean.

NOT CLAIMED: that hosted CI is green again. Layer Z, the lane that actually runs the seven interop legs, was NOT re-run this round -- the edit to that file is comment-only and Layer C2 compiled it, which is the evidence available without a zenohd sweep. The verdict on 30324520884's remaining twelve green jobs is inherited, not re-measured.
carry_forward_bullets: A GATE LIST RECITED IS NOT A GATE SET ENUMERATED. R311y431's verification named clippy on three crates as "the FULL Layer Z feature set" and it was not the full CRATE set -- the one crate it had just written a file into was missing. The rule that survives: after editing a file, the crate that OWNS that file is in the gate set, and no amount of feature-set thoroughness elsewhere substitutes. Same disease as the negative-claim lesson, applied to gates instead of claims.

A COUNT PIN INVALIDATES IN CLUSTERS, and the guard's early return hides the rest. `_runci_guarded_test` returns on the first mismatch, so hosted CI reported ONE stale count out of two that the same new test had broken. When a pinned count moves, re-measure every OTHER pin that shares the filter before assuming CI showed you the whole blast radius.

A DRIFT THAT REPORTS AS AN ABSENCE GETS DIAGNOSED AS ONE. The stale MCP server surfaced to the client as `Connection closed`, which reads identically to "no server configured", so two rounds of sessions treated a broken pin as a missing feature. When a capability is reported unavailable, drive the underlying tool by hand ONCE before accepting the absence -- the real diagnostic was one pipe away the whole time.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT CAUSED IT IS STILL THERE, deliberately. `mnemosyne-mcp` remains outside the CI installer because CI never speaks MCP, so nothing in a hosted run will ever notice the two binaries diverging again. The mitigation is entirely documentary -- CLAUDE.md step 1 plus the new script -- and that is weaker than a gate. If this recurs, the honest next step is a local hook check that the PATH server answers `initialize`, not more prose.

DO NOT STRENGTHEN THE NEW SCRIPT INTO A VERSION-STRING MATCH. It is the obvious "improvement" and scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh:46-55 already argues it out for the CLI: `--version` embeds `git describe`, so it is a bare short hash only while no tag is reachable upstream and becomes `unknown` with no .git. The handshake grades the property actually wanted -- can this server serve THIS workspace -- and does not depend on another project's tagging policy.

THE HOSTED VERDICT IS STILL OPEN. This round fixed the two lanes that failed and re-ran exactly those two locally; it did not re-run Layer Z, and it cannot pronounce on the run as a whole until a push produces one. Treat `main` as red until a hosted run says otherwise.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: A GATE LIST RECITED IS NOT A GATE SET ENUMERATED. R311y431's verification named clippy on three crates as "the FULL Layer Z feature set" and it was not the full CRATE set -- the one crate it had just written a file into was missing. The rule that survives: after editing a file, the crate that OWNS that file is in the gate set, and no amount of feature-set thoroughness elsewhere substitutes. Same disease as the negative-claim lesson, applied to gates instead of claims.

A COUNT PIN INVALIDATES IN CLUSTERS, and the guard's early return hides the rest. `_runci_guarded_test` returns on the first mismatch, so hosted CI reported ONE stale count out of two that the same new test had broken. When a pinned count moves, re-measure every OTHER pin that shares the filter before assuming CI showed you the whole blast radius.

A DRIFT THAT REPORTS AS AN ABSENCE GETS DIAGNOSED AS ONE. The stale MCP server surfaced to the client as `Connection closed`, which reads identically to "no server configured", so two rounds of sessions treated a broken pin as a missing feature. When a capability is reported unavailable, drive the underlying tool by hand ONCE before accepting the absence -- the real diagnostic was one pipe away the whole time.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT CAUSED IT IS STILL THERE, deliberately. `mnemosyne-mcp` remains outside the CI installer because CI never speaks MCP, so nothing in a hosted run will ever notice the two binaries diverging again. The mitigation is entirely documentary -- CLAUDE.md step 1 plus the new script -- and that is weaker than a gate. If this recurs, the honest next step is a local hook check that the PATH server answers `initialize`, not more prose.

DO NOT STRENGTHEN THE NEW SCRIPT INTO A VERSION-STRING MATCH. It is the obvious "improvement" and scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh:46-55 already argues it out for the CLI: `--version` embeds `git describe`, so it is a bare short hash only while no tag is reachable upstream and becomes `unknown` with no .git. The handshake grades the property actually wanted -- can this server serve THIS workspace -- and does not depend on another project's tagging policy.

THE FIRST GREEN WAS NOT A COMPRESSION PROOF, and the payload size is why. A 20-byte value routes through a compression-enabled zenohd, but keep-only-if-smaller ships it with the COMPRESSION bit CLEAR, so that run witnessed the 1-byte header framing and nothing about lz4. The CONTROL falsified it: the same value, same zenohd, WITHOUT --compression also fails to arrive. So the ceiling is independent of compression and is not this slice's subject. Measured routable sizes at 100 / 400 / 1000 bytes: all delivered.

THE ZENOH SIDE WAS READ, NOT RECALLED. init::ext::Compression = zextunit!(0x6,false) (zenoh-protocol-1.5.0 transport/init.rs:168); the `&=` merge on both FSM sides (zenoh-transport-1.5.0 unicast/establishment/ext/compression.rs:79,165); BatchHeader is 1 byte with COMPRESSION = 1<<0 and exists ONLY on a negotiated link (common/batch.rs:107-146); compress keeps the smaller form (:346-352) and decompress is lz4_flex::block (:489-500); the handshake is uncompressed and the OpenAck is explicitly shipped raw by a named workaround (unicast/link.rs:288-296).

carry_forward_bullets: A GREEN CROSS-IMPL LEG CAN WITNESS THE WRONG LAYER. The first hand-driven run of this slice passed with a 20-byte payload and proved nothing about lz4: keep-only-if-smaller had cleared the COMPRESSION bit, so the batch went out RAW and zenohd routed it exactly as an un-negotiated one. The negotiation flag was true the whole time, which is what made it convincing. For any atom whose wire form is CONDITIONAL on the data (compression, batching, fragmentation), the fixture has to be sized so the condition provably holds, and the sizing belongs in the test's prose where the next reader will see it.

A FAILURE THAT LOOKS LIKE YOUR SUBJECT NEEDS A CONTROL BEFORE IT NEEDS A DIAGNOSIS. The 4121-byte payload not arriving read as "compression breaks on large batches" and would have become a carried blocker. One run without --compression killed that reading in seconds. Same shape as R311y430's mis-diagnosis and R311y423's blocker: the measurement was right, the explanation was an unchecked claim.

THE DEFAULT-FEATURES WORKSPACE CLIPPY IS BLIND TO EVERY MODE ATOM'S DEMO ARM, and this round proved it rather than inferring it (C2 exit=0 with a planted useless_format in both witness blocks). transport-lowlatency had carried that hole since R311y372. If a future mode adds a `--flag` to wz-ap-demo, its own lane needs the `cargo clippy -p wz-ap-demo --features <atom>` step; Layer Z's `cargo build` catches a compile error and no lint.

STILL OPEN ON COMPRESSION, and deliberately not claimed: the zenohd->wz direction. Both legs dial out and assert on wz's TX wrap plus zenohd's decompress; wz's own RX un-wrap (drive.rs:86-107, incl. the decompression-bomb bound) has no cross-impl witness. The cheapest vehicle is probably a zenohd-side publisher on the same negotiated link rather than a new fixture.

THE LARGE-PAYLOAD CEILING IN THE wz -> zenohd -> pico CHAIN IS UNEXPLAINED, and it is a real gap even though it is not compression's. A 4121-byte Put does not reach the pico z_sub with or without compression, while 1000 bytes does. transport-fragmentation IS in preset-ap-client, so "the demo cannot split it" is NOT the answer. Whoever picks this up should establish where the sample dies (wz tx, zenohd route, pico rx buffer) before assuming a wz defect.

LOWLATENCY AND COMPRESSION DIVERGE FROM ZENOH WHEN COMPOSED, disclosed here and NOT fixed. wz wraps compression OUTSIDE the lean encode (session_actions.rs:1417-1435), so a wz peer offering both compresses the lean wire; zenoh's lowlatency transport serializes `[len:4][msg]` straight to the link and never consults the batch compression path at all (zenoh-transport-1.5.0 unicast/lowlatency/link.rs:33-73 -- no WBatch, no BatchHeader). zenoh's config makes lowlatency exclusive with QOS, not with compression, so both CAN be enabled upstream and compression is simply inert there. wz's C1ag composition lane locks in the divergent behaviour wz<->wz. This round only stops the demo from producing such a session (the main.rs guard); deciding whether wz should suppress the wrap under lowlatency is a product question this slice did not take.

STILL UNTOUCHED: the A4 axis's remaining 33 unproven plus 37 partial. The 33 are dominated by two clusters -- ext-pubsub-advanced-* (8) and the router-* / routing-*-route-compute family (8) -- with session-extshm and transport-shm NOT in reach for the same reason this round WAS: extshm.rs:101-126 negotiates SHM with a UNIT offer instead of zenoh's ZBuf-on-Init challenge-response, so it is not wire-compatible with zenohd and proving it needs product code, not a fixture.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: A GREEN CROSS-IMPL LEG CAN WITNESS THE WRONG LAYER. The first hand-driven run of this slice passed with a 20-byte payload and proved nothing about lz4: keep-only-if-smaller had cleared the COMPRESSION bit, so the batch went out RAW and zenohd routed it exactly as an un-negotiated one. The negotiation flag was true the whole time, which is what made it convincing. For any atom whose wire form is CONDITIONAL on the data (compression, batching, fragmentation), the fixture has to be sized so the condition provably holds, and the sizing belongs in the test's prose where the next reader will see it.

A FAILURE THAT LOOKS LIKE YOUR SUBJECT NEEDS A CONTROL BEFORE IT NEEDS A DIAGNOSIS. The 4121-byte payload not arriving read as "compression breaks on large batches" and would have become a carried blocker. One run without --compression killed that reading in seconds. Same shape as R311y430's mis-diagnosis and R311y423's blocker: the measurement was right, the explanation was an unchecked claim.

THE DEFAULT-FEATURES WORKSPACE CLIPPY IS BLIND TO EVERY MODE ATOM'S DEMO ARM, and this round proved it rather than inferring it (C2 exit=0 with a planted useless_format in both witness blocks). transport-lowlatency had carried that hole since R311y372. Both legs dial out and assert on wz's TX wrap plus zenohd's decompress; wz's own RX un-wrap (drive.rs:86-107, incl. the decompression-bomb bound) has no cross-impl witness. The cheapest vehicle is probably a zenohd-side publisher on the same negotiated link rather than a new fixture.

THE LARGE-PAYLOAD CEILING IN THE wz -> zenohd -> pico CHAIN IS UNEXPLAINED, and it is a real gap even though it is not compression's. A 4121-byte Put does not reach the pico z_sub with or without compression, while 1000 bytes does. transport-fragmentation IS in preset-ap-client, so "the demo cannot split it" is NOT the answer. Whoever picks this up should establish where the sample dies (wz tx, zenohd route, pico rx buffer) before assuming a wz defect.

LOWLATENCY AND COMPRESSION DIVERGE FROM ZENOH WHEN COMPOSED, disclosed here and NOT fixed. wz wraps compression OUTSIDE the lean encode (session_actions.rs:1417-1435), so a wz peer offering both compresses the lean wire; zenoh's lowlatency transport serializes `[len:4][msg]` straight to the link and never consults the batch compression path at all (zenoh-transport-1.5.0 unicast/lowlatency/link.rs:33-73 -- no WBatch, no BatchHeader). zenoh's config makes lowlatency exclusive with QOS, not with compression, so both CAN be enabled upstream and compression is simply inert there. wz's C1ag composition lane locks in the divergent behaviour wz<->wz. This round only stops the demo from producing such a session (the main.rs guard); deciding whether wz should suppress the wrap under lowlatency is a product question this slice did not take.

STILL UNTOUCHED: the A4 axis's remaining 33 unproven plus 37 partial. The 33 are dominated by two clusters -- ext-pubsub-advanced-* (8) and the router-* / routing-*-route-compute family (8) -- with session-extshm and transport-shm NOT in reach for the same reason this round WAS: extshm.rs:101-126 negotiates SHM with a UNIT offer instead of zenoh's ZBuf-on-Init challenge-response, so it is not wire-compatible with zenohd and proving it needs product code, not a fixture.

Round 311y434.decision_summary: R311y434 -- wz composed two transport modes in an order zenoh does not, and a test was holding the divergence in place. R311y433 disclosed it as a carry: wz wraps lz4 compression OUTSIDE the lowlatency lean encode, so a session that negotiated both emitted a compressed lean wire. zenoh never produces that. Its establishment sets is_lowlatency on the transport config and is_compression on the link BatchConfig independently, so both flags CAN be true -- upstream config makes lowlatency exclusive with qos, not with compression -- but the lean transport serializes straight to the link behind a 4-byte length prefix and never touches WBatch or BatchHeader, and its lean rx never decompresses. Upstream the negotiated wrap is simply INERT on a lean link. So this was not a superset: superset means wz can do MORE, and a wire no zenoh peer can read is less. THE FIX IS A DATA-PATH CORRECTION, NOT A HANDSHAKE ONE, which is the whole design question this round had to settle. wz keeps offering and merging the 0x6 ext exactly as zenoh does, so Init/Open stays byte-identical for the same config; only the wrap is suppressed. That split now has a name in the code: is_compression reports the NEGOTIATED capability, compresses_batches reports whether the wrap is ACTIVE, and the bug was reachable precisely because one flag was answering both questions. Both the TX wrap and the RX un-wrap consult the single predicate, because a hand-maintained pair of conditions is exactly how a build ends up wrapping what it will not un-wrap, and that failure is silent on the wire. THE TEST THAT HAD TO BE REWRITTEN IS THE LESSON. transport_compose_e2e was written to answer a review saying the three modes were designed to compose and verified by a clippy pass; it did capture a real three-layer wire and assert it. It was still wrong, because the composition was never read against the reference impl -- each single-mode leg matched zenoh, the composed one matched only wz. It is now an option-atom PAIR: with lowlatency the wire leads with the bare lean Push and compresses_batches is false while is_compression stays true; dropping ONLY the lowlatency offer brings the BatchHeader back, which is the leg that catches an over-broad suppression. Both REDs were measured separately, and the byte assertion had to be provoked on its own because the invariant assertion panics first and would have left the bytes unexercised. WHAT THIS ROUND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: a cross-impl witness for the composed session. No leg dials zenohd with both modes, because the demo cannot stage both offers -- session_open has one entrypoint per MODE. R311y433 guarded that combination for a reason that this fix makes false, so the guard survives with its justification replaced by the real one, a local API limit, and widening session_open to an offer SET is named as the next slice rather than smuggled into a bug fix.

carry_forward_bullets: A COMPOSITION TEST CAN CERTIFY A DIVERGENCE. transport_compose_e2e was written to answer a review that said the three modes were "designed to compose, verified by a clippy pass" -- and it did assert a real, captured, three-layer wire. It was still wrong, because nobody checked the composition against the reference impl; the single-mode legs each matched zenoh, and the composed one matched only wz. When a test's subject is two atoms INTERACTING, the upstream behaviour of the interaction is a separate read from the upstream behaviour of each atom.

NEGOTIATED IS NOT APPLIED, and the codebase now has a name for the difference (`is_compression` vs `compresses_batches`). The bug was reachable precisely because one flag was serving both questions. Any future capability whose wire effect is conditional on ANOTHER capability wants the same split rather than a longer boolean expression at each use site.

THE COMPOSED SESSION HAS NO CROSS-IMPL WITNESS, and this is the round's largest deliberate gap. wz<->wz pins that the composed wire is the lean wire; R311y372 pins that the lean wire interops with zenohd; the composition of those two is an argument. Closing it needs a demo that can stage BOTH offers, which needs a session_open entrypoint taking an offer SET rather than one wrapper per mode -- four modes would otherwise be sixteen wrappers. That refactor is the natural next slice and it also deletes the demo's `--lowlatency --compression` rejection.

THE DEMO REJECTION IS NOW A LOCAL API LIMIT, not a protocol fact, and its comment says so. If someone widens session_open, delete the guard in the same change; leaving it would re-create exactly the stale-justification problem this round had to correct one day after writing it.

CHECK WHETHER ANY OTHER MODE PAIR DIVERGES THE SAME WAY. This round establishes that wz composed two transport modes in an order zenoh does not. The other pairs -- shm x lowlatency, shm x compression, qos x compression, batching x lowlatency -- were never read against zenoh's composed data path either. C1ag covers three of them in ONE test whose assertions are now known to have been wz-only for two rounds. That audit is bounded (the pairs are enumerable) and it is the same defect class, not a new one.

NOT CLAIMED: a cross-impl witness for the COMPOSED session. No leg dials zenohd with both modes, because the demo cannot stage both offers. What is proven is narrower and stated as such: the composed session now emits exactly the lean wire (this round, wz<->wz byte assertion) and the lean wire interoperates with zenohd (R311y372's leg). The composition of those two is an argument, not a measurement.

NOT CLAIMED: that hosted CI is green for this commit. The R311y433 run 30328539022 was still in_progress at authoring time with 12/14 green and no red, including the cross-impl and transport-MODE jobs this round also touches.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: A COMPOSITION TEST CAN CERTIFY A DIVERGENCE. transport_compose_e2e was written to answer a review that said the three modes were "designed to compose, verified by a clippy pass" -- and it did assert a real, captured, three-layer wire. It was still wrong, because nobody checked the composition against the reference impl; the single-mode legs each matched zenoh, and the composed one matched only wz. When a test's subject is two atoms INTERACTING, the upstream behaviour of the interaction is a separate read from the upstream behaviour of each atom.

NEGOTIATED IS NOT APPLIED, and the codebase now has a name for the difference (`is_compression` vs `compresses_batches`). The bug was reachable precisely because one flag was serving both questions. Any future capability whose wire effect is conditional on ANOTHER capability wants the same split rather than a longer boolean expression at each use site.

THE COMPOSED SESSION HAS NO CROSS-IMPL WITNESS, and this is the round's largest deliberate gap. wz<->wz pins that the composed wire is the lean wire; R311y372 pins that the lean wire interops with zenohd; the composition of those two is an argument. Closing it needs a demo that can stage BOTH offers, which needs a session_open entrypoint taking an offer SET rather than one wrapper per mode -- four modes would otherwise be sixteen wrappers. That refactor is the natural next slice and it also deletes the demo's `--lowlatency --compression` rejection.

THE DEMO REJECTION IS NOW A LOCAL API LIMIT, not a protocol fact, and its comment says so. If someone widens session_open, delete the guard in the same change; leaving it would re-create exactly the stale-justification problem this round had to correct one day after writing it.

STILL OPEN FROM R311y433, unchanged: the compression zenohd->wz direction (wz's RX un-wrap has no foreign witness; both legs dial out), and the unexplained large-payload ceiling in the wz -> zenohd -> pico chain (a 4121-byte Put does not arrive with OR without compression, while 1000 bytes does; transport-fragmentation IS in preset-ap-client, so "the demo cannot split it" is not the answer).

CHECK WHETHER ANY OTHER MODE PAIR DIVERGES THE SAME WAY. This round establishes that wz composed two transport modes in an order zenoh does not. The other pairs -- shm x lowlatency, shm x compression, qos x compression, batching x lowlatency -- were never read against zenoh's composed data path either. C1ag covers three of them in ONE test whose assertions are now known to have been wz-only for two rounds. That audit is bounded (the pairs are enumerable) and it is the same defect class, not a new one.

STILL UNTOUCHED: the A4 axis's 33 unproven plus 37 partial, flat this round by design. The classification sweep that turns "33" into a schedule -- fixture-only vs product-code vs not-foreign-observable vs out-of-scope -- has not been done, and R311y433's shm finding (extshm.rs:101-126 negotiates with a UNIT offer instead of zenoh's ZBuf challenge-response) is so far the only bucket assignment backed by a read.

Round 311y435.decision_summary: R311y435 -- Layer F was reporting green on the very defect it exists to catch. Its minus-codec-push and minus-codec-frame lanes printed SKIP (binary does not compile under this exclusion; consumer features still referenced) and the layer passed. Rebuilding that exact feature set by hand showed the failure was not in the binary at all: wz-session-core (lib) did not compile, because pubsub.rs:131 imports wz_codecs::push under alloc AND (pubsub-put OR pubsub-delete) with no codec-push conjunct, while wz_codecs::push is itself codec-push-gated and Cargo.toml declared pubsub-put = []. The dependency was real and merely unwritten, so that profile was BROKEN rather than unmeasurable -- and a SKIP is green, so the catalog defect read as a measurement limitation for as long as the lane existed. A second defect of the same shape sat behind minus-codec-declare: prune_declaration was gated on session-reconnect alone while every caller is a declare-path, so excluding codec-declare removed all callers and turned the method into never used, which -D warnings makes a build failure. Both are now written down: pubsub-put / pubsub-delete SELECT codec-push, and prune_declaration is gated on the union of its call sites. Adding the codec-push conjunct to the cfg in pubsub.rs was rejected as the alternative, because it would make pubsub-put silently stop emitting Puts -- a degradation, not a gate. minus-codec-push consequently went from SKIP to a measured 10072-byte delta, roughly ten times the threshold: one of the largest codecs in the catalog had been contributing no evidence at all. THE GATE ITSELF IS HARDENED so this cannot hide again. measure-codec-footprint.sh now separates the two failure modes it used to merge: a LIBRARY crate failing to compile is a CATALOG DEFECT and FAILS the layer, while only the measurement binary (wz-ap-demo, which references consumer features unconditionally) failing remains an honest SKIP. The culprit crate is extracted from cargos own could not compile line, so the message names it instead of blaming the binary for both. That hardening was RED-measured: reverting only the pubsub-put edge makes the codec-push shard print CATALOG DEFECT -- library crate wz-session-core and exit 1. WHAT THIS ROUND DOES NOT CLOSE, stated rather than implied: minus-codec-frame, minus-codec-declare, minus-all-codecs and handshake-only are still SKIP. After the library fixes their failure is genuinely in wz-ap-demo, which is the honest form of the old message; closing them needs the smaller cfg-gated measurement binary the script has recommended in a comment since R311n.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/Cargo.toml: `pubsub-put` / `pubsub-delete` now SELECT `codec-push`. They were declared standalone (`= []`) on the stated reasoning that "the gating is at the wz-session-core dispatch level, not the codec level" -- but `pubsub.rs:131` imports `wz_codecs::push::{PushOwned, PushOwnedVariant}` under `alloc AND (pubsub-put OR pubsub-delete)` with NO codec-push conjunct, and `wz_codecs::push` is itself codec-push-gated. The dependency was real and merely unwritten: `pubsub-put` without `codec-push` does not compile. The alternative fix -- adding `codec-push` to the cfg in pubsub.rs -- was rejected because it would make `pubsub-put` silently stop emitting Puts, which is a degradation rather than a gate.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: `prune_declaration`'s gate widened from `session-reconnect` alone to the UNION OF ITS CALL SITES -- `session-reconnect AND declare-undeclare AND any(declare-keyexpr, declare-subscriber, declare-queryable, declare-token)`. Every caller is an undeclare path gated on `declare-undeclare` plus its own `declare-*`; with `codec-declare` excluded those pullers go too, every caller compiles out, and the method became `never used`, which `-D warnings` turns into a build failure rather than a warning.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the compile-failure path now SEPARATES two failure modes that were one SKIP. A LIBRARY crate failing to compile under an exclusion set means a feature is used without being selected -- the catalog-truthfulness defect this gate exists to catch -- and is now reported as `CATALOG DEFECT` and FAILS. Only the measurement BINARY (wz-ap-demo, which references consumer features unconditionally) failing remains an honest SKIP. The culprit crate is extracted from cargo's `could not compile` line, so the message names it instead of asserting "binary does not compile" as the old text did for both cases.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the threshold stage judges `DEFECT` before the delta comparison (there is no binary to measure, so it is not a threshold question), and the SKIP comment now names the four lanes that remain unmeasurable for this binary plus the smaller cfg-gated test binary that would close them.
verification_bullets: THE DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY REPRODUCING A LANE THAT REPORTED GREEN. Layer F's minus-codec-push lane printed `SKIP (binary does not compile under this exclusion; consumer features still referenced)` and the layer passed. Rebuilding that exact feature set by hand showed the failure was NOT in the binary: `error[E0432]: unresolved import wz_codecs::push --> wz-session-core/src/pubsub.rs:135` and `error[E0599]: no variant ... Push found for enum NetworkMessage --> pubsub.rs:591`, i.e. `could not compile wz-session-core (lib)`. The lane's own diagnostic named the wrong crate, and because a SKIP is green nothing ever contradicted it.

MINUS-CODEC-PUSH IS NOW MEASURED, NOT SKIPPED: baseline 2486528, minus-codec-push 2476456, delta 10072 bytes -- roughly TEN TIMES the 1024-byte threshold. One of the largest codecs in the catalog had been contributing no evidence at all for as long as the lane existed.

THE GATE HARDENING WAS RED-MEASURED, not asserted. Reverting only the `pubsub-put` / `pubsub-delete` edge and running the codec-push shard (`WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS=13 WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=6`) produces `minus-codec-push: CATALOG DEFECT -- library crate wz-session-core does not compile under this exclusion`, then `CATALOG DEFECT codec-push (library does not compile; see above)`, and `Layer F FAIL (rc=1)`. So the same defect that hid as a green SKIP for the lane's whole life now fails the layer. Probe reverted; `grep RED-PROBE` = 0.

BASELINE IS UNCHANGED AT 2486528 BYTES, which is the check that the two Cargo/cfg corrections are catalog-only: writing a feature edge that was already implied by the code, and matching a gate to its callers, must not move the DEFAULT build. It did not.
LAYER F PASSES END TO END after the fixes (exit 0, 194s), with minus-codec-push measured and the four SOFT-SKIP small-codec lanes unchanged (fragment 0, keep-alive 208, scout -144, hello -144).

WHAT IS STILL SKIPPED AND WHY, stated rather than left implicit: minus-codec-frame, minus-codec-declare, minus-all-codecs and handshake-only. Reproducing minus-codec-declare by hand after the `prune_declaration` fix moves the failure into `wz-ap-demo` itself (`no field liveliness_gets / remote_subscribers / remote_queryables on ApplicationLayerObserver`, 9 errors), which is the honest form of the old message: this measurement binary references consumer features unconditionally and cannot express the profile. Those four need a smaller cfg-gated probe binary and are NOT closed by this round.

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IS CLAIMED. Neither correction alters a compiled artifact on any profile that already built: the Cargo edge only adds a selection that the code already required, and the widened cfg only removes a method from builds that had no caller for it. `cargo check` on wz-session-core / wz-runtime-tokio / wz-ap-demo is clean, and full run-ci judges the rest.
carry_forward_bullets: A SKIP IS GREEN, SO A GATE THAT SKIPS ITS OWN SUBJECT MATTER REPORTS SUCCESS FOREVER. Layer F exists to catch "a feature is declared optional but does not actually gate code". When the profile it built failed to compile because a feature was used without being selected -- exactly that defect -- it printed SKIP and passed. The two defects this round fixes were sitting in that blind spot, and the lane's diagnostic actively pointed away from them by blaming the binary. Any gate with a skip path should be audited for whether the skip can absorb the thing it is gating.

REPRODUCE A GREEN SKIP BEFORE TRUSTING IT. Nothing in the log distinguished "unmeasurable" from "broken"; the difference only appeared by rebuilding the lane's exact feature set by hand and reading which crate cargo named. That took one command. The lane had been printing its misleading line since R311n.

FOUR LAYER F LANES REMAIN UNMEASURABLE AND THE REASON IS NOW EXACT: minus-codec-frame, minus-codec-declare, minus-all-codecs, handshake-only. After this round's library fixes the failure is genuinely in `wz-ap-demo` (it references `ApplicationLayerObserver` fields unconditionally), so the remaining work is a smaller measurement binary whose source is cfg-gated against the consumer features -- the one the script has recommended in a comment since R311n. That would also re-open the whole-catalog lanes, which have never produced a number.

THE FOUR SOFT-SKIP SMALL-CODEC LANES DESERVE THE SAME AUDIT. codec-fragment (0 bytes), codec-keep-alive (208), codec-scout (-144) and codec-hello (-144) are carried as "honest near-zero delta, wz-codecs level only". That was asserted, not measured, and the negative deltas say the measurement noise floor is above the signal. With a smaller probe binary the same codecs might produce real numbers, which would let the soft-skip list shrink rather than grow.

THE THRESHOLD IS AN ABSOLUTE BYTE COUNT ON A 2.4MB BINARY, and that is fragile in a direction worth recording: consolidating code paths REDUCES what a codec exclusion can remove, so a refactor that improves the library can push a delta under the threshold without any catalog regression. This was observed on a working branch (codec-close 1944 -> 600 bytes when eight open-path wrappers were consolidated behind one entrypoint) and is the strongest argument for the smaller probe binary, where the ratio would be large enough that consolidation cannot cross the bar.

Round 311y436.decision_summary: R311y436 -- Layer F graded thirteen codecs with one number, and that number was wrong in both directions at once. The 1024-byte global threshold was TOO LOW to catch a regression in a large codec (codec-response elides 74472 bytes; it could have lost 98.6 percent of that and still cleared the bar) and TOO HIGH for the small ones, which is what produced the hand-maintained SOFT-SKIP list: codec-scout, codec-hello, codec-join, codec-fragment and codec-keep-alive were exempt, judging nothing, and the list only ever grew. Five of thirteen lanes graded nothing. R311y435 established where that ends -- a gate whose exemptions absorb its own subject matter reports green forever -- and this round applies the same lesson one level up. THE GLOBAL THRESHOLD IS DELETED, replaced by CODEC_DELTA_FLOOR: a pinned minimum elision delta per codec, measured at 49f2ea9 and carried with a margin far above the observed run-to-run noise of plus-or-minus 32 bytes. Every lane is judged now, and the exemption MECHANISM is gone rather than curated: a near-zero codec is pinned AT near-zero, which is strictly more informative than exempting it because a jump upward becomes visible too. Two branches make the table honest. An unpinned codec FAILS (FLOOR MISSING) instead of passing silently -- codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so without that branch the table would quietly fall behind the catalog exactly as the SOFT-SKIP list did. And a floor that the build cannot meet FAILS with both legitimate causes named: a consumer re-pulling the codec, which is the catalog-truthfulness defect this gate exists to catch, or a refactor consolidating the paths the codec used to own, which is legitimate but must be re-pinned deliberately with before/after numbers in the ledger -- never by lowering the constant alone, the same rule MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA carries and for the same reason. THIS ROUND DOES NOT CLOSE the four lanes wz-ap-demo cannot express (codec-frame, codec-declare, minus-all-codecs, handshake-only); their floors are placeholders and the whole-catalog lanes have still never produced a number. It also does not touch product code.
changes_bullets: scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the single global `THRESHOLD_BYTES=1024` is DELETED and replaced by `CODEC_DELTA_FLOOR`, a pinned minimum elision delta per codec. Every one of the thirteen lanes is now judged against its own measured floor instead of one number that could not be right for deltas spanning 0 to 74472 bytes.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the hand-maintained SOFT-SKIP list (codec-scout / codec-hello / codec-join / codec-fragment / codec-keep-alive) is DELETED outright. Those codecs are now pinned AT their near-zero measurements (-256 / -256 / 128 / -256) rather than exempted, which is strictly more informative: an exempt lane judges nothing in either direction, while a pinned one still catches a drop and makes an unexpected RISE visible.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: an unpinned codec is now a FAILURE (`FLOOR MISSING`), not a silent pass. Codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so a newly added one would otherwise be measured and then ignored -- the same "absence reads as success" shape R311y435 found behind SKIP.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the `FLOOR FAIL` message names both legitimate causes (a consumer re-pulling the codec, or a refactor consolidating the paths it owned) and states that the second must be re-pinned deliberately with before/after numbers in the ledger -- never by lowering the constant alone. That is the same rule MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA carries, and for the same reason: a floor lowered on its own silences the gate it belongs to.
verification_bullets: THE FLOORS ARE MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. Layer F at 49f2ea9 (baseline 2486528) gives: response 74472, request 66456, init-body 14608, open-body 10192, push 10072, response-final 9712, close 1944, keep-alive 208, fragment 0, scout -144, hello -144; frame and declare SKIP on this binary. Each floor is that number carried down by a margin far above the observed run-to-run noise (+-32B: keep-alive read 208 and 224 across runs, scout/hello -144 and -128).
GREEN AT HEAD: `run-ci.sh --layer F` exits 0 with all thirteen lanes judged and no FLOOR MISSING / FLOOR FAIL (210s).

RED 1 -- A FLOOR THE BUILD CANNOT MEET FAILS. Raising only `[codec-close]` from 1500 to 3000 and running the codec-close shard (WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS=13 WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=5) prints `FLOOR FAIL codec-close (1944B < pinned 3000B)` and `Layer F FAIL (rc=1)`.

RED 2 -- AN UNPINNED CODEC FAILS, which is the half that a table-driven gate usually gets wrong. Deleting the `[codec-close]` row entirely prints `FLOOR MISSING codec-close (measured 1944B, no pinned floor)` and `Layer F FAIL (rc=1)`. Without this the table would silently stop judging any codec added later.
BOTH PROBES REVERTED and the file restored from a pre-probe copy; `grep -c 'codec-close]=1500'` = 1.

THE GATE IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES, and the arithmetic says so rather than the prose: codec-response elides 74472B and the old global threshold passed it at anything above 1024, i.e. it could have lost 98.6% of its elision without a single lane going red. Its floor is now 60000. In the other direction five of thirteen lanes were exempt under SOFT-SKIP and judged nothing at all; that number is now zero.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: minus-codec-frame, minus-codec-declare, minus-all-codecs and handshake-only still SKIP because wz-ap-demo cannot express those exclusion sets. Their floors are placeholders (0) and are unused while the lane skips. Closing them still needs the smaller cfg-gated measurement binary R311y435 named.
NO PRODUCT CODE IS TOUCHED. The round edits one script; `cargo fmt --check` is clean and full run-ci judges the rest.
carry_forward_bullets: ONE THRESHOLD ACROSS THIRTEEN SUBJECTS IS TWO BUGS, NOT A COMPROMISE. The global 1024B was simultaneously too low to catch a regression in a 74KB codec and too high for a near-zero one, and the second half is what produced the SOFT-SKIP list: five of thirteen lanes exempted, judging nothing, and the list only ever grew. A per-subject pin fixes both at once and deletes the exemption mechanism rather than curating it. Look for the same shape wherever one constant grades a population whose real values span orders of magnitude.

A PINNED NEAR-ZERO BEATS AN EXEMPTION. codec-fragment measures 0 and codec-scout/hello measure -144; exempting them said "we do not judge this", while pinning them at -256 says "this is what it is, tell me when it changes". The pinned form also catches a RISE, which the exemption could not -- if a near-zero codec suddenly elides 8KB, something was re-pulled that was not before, and that is worth seeing.

THE FLOOR-MISSING BRANCH IS THE ONE TO KEEP HONEST. Codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so the table can silently fall behind the catalog. Making an unpinned codec FAIL is what stops the table from decaying into a partial gate the way the SOFT-SKIP list did. If a future round finds this branch annoying, that is the branch working.

THE R311y435 REFACTOR IS STILL BLOCKED BY codec-close AND THAT IS NOW A PINNED, VISIBLE FACT. The stashed offer-SET work (`initiate_and_open_session_with_offer` and its accept/connect twins) consolidates eight per-capability wrappers into one entrypoint, which drops codec-close's elision from 1944B to 600B -- measured twice, and bisected to the demo's call site (routing the demo back to the bare entrypoint restores 1944 exactly). That is a legitimate consolidation, not a re-pull: 600B is still real elision, well clear of the near-zero band. When that refactor lands it must re-pin `[codec-close]` with both numbers in its ledger entry, which is precisely the deliberate re-pin this gate is designed to force.

STILL OPEN, UNCHANGED BY THIS ROUND: the four lanes wz-ap-demo cannot express (codec-frame, codec-declare, minus-all-codecs, handshake-only). They need a small measurement binary whose source is cfg-gated against the consumer features -- the one the script has recommended in a comment since R311n and that R311y435 re-derived independently. Until then their floors are placeholders and the whole-catalog lanes have never produced a number.
Round 311y436.publishable_decision_summary: R311y436 -- Layer F graded thirteen codecs with one number, and that number was wrong in both directions at once. The 1024-byte global threshold was TOO LOW to catch a regression in a large codec (codec-response elides 74472 bytes; it could have lost 98.6 percent of that and still cleared the bar) and TOO HIGH for the small ones, which is what produced the hand-maintained SOFT-SKIP list: codec-scout, codec-hello, codec-join, codec-fragment and codec-keep-alive were exempt, judging nothing, and the list only ever grew. Five of thirteen lanes graded nothing. R311y435 established where that ends -- a gate whose exemptions absorb its own subject matter reports green forever -- and this round applies the same lesson one level up. THE GLOBAL THRESHOLD IS DELETED, replaced by CODEC_DELTA_FLOOR: a pinned minimum elision delta per codec, measured at 49f2ea9 and carried with a margin far above the observed run-to-run noise of plus-or-minus 32 bytes. Every lane is judged now, and the exemption MECHANISM is gone rather than curated: a near-zero codec is pinned AT near-zero, which is strictly more informative than exempting it because a jump upward becomes visible too. Two branches make the table honest. An unpinned codec FAILS (FLOOR MISSING) instead of passing silently -- codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so without that branch the table would quietly fall behind the catalog exactly as the SOFT-SKIP list did. And a floor that the build cannot meet FAILS with both legitimate causes named: a consumer re-pulling the codec, which is the catalog-truthfulness defect this gate exists to catch, or a refactor consolidating the paths the codec used to own, which is legitimate but must be re-pinned deliberately with before/after numbers in the ledger -- never by lowering the constant alone, the same rule MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA carries and for the same reason. THIS ROUND DOES NOT CLOSE the four lanes wz-ap-demo cannot express (codec-frame, codec-declare, minus-all-codecs, handshake-only); their floors are placeholders and the whole-catalog lanes have still never produced a number. It also does not touch product code.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the hand-maintained SOFT-SKIP list (codec-scout / codec-hello / codec-join / codec-fragment / codec-keep-alive) is DELETED outright. scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: an unpinned codec is now a FAILURE (`FLOOR MISSING`), not a silent pass. Codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so a newly added one would otherwise be measured and then ignored -- the same "absence reads as success" shape R311y435 found behind SKIP.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh: the `FLOOR FAIL` message names both legitimate causes (a consumer re-pulling the codec, or a refactor consolidating the paths it owned) and states that the second must be re-pinned deliberately with before/after numbers in the ledger -- never by lowering the constant alone. That is the same rule MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA carries, and for the same reason: a floor lowered on its own silences the gate it belongs to.
publishable_verification_bullets: THE FLOORS ARE MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. Layer F at 49f2ea9 (baseline 2486528) gives: response 74472, request 66456, init-body 14608, open-body 10192, push 10072, response-final 9712, close 1944, keep-alive 208, fragment 0, scout -144, hello -144; frame and declare SKIP on this binary. Each floor is that number carried down by a margin far above the observed run-to-run noise (+-32B: keep-alive read 208 and 224 across runs, scout/hello -144 and -128).
GREEN AT HEAD: `run-ci.sh --layer F` exits 0 with all thirteen lanes judged and no FLOOR MISSING / FLOOR FAIL (210s).

RED 1 -- A FLOOR THE BUILD CANNOT MEET FAILS. Raising only `[codec-close]` from 1500 to 3000 and running the codec-close shard (WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARDS=13 WZ_FOOTPRINT_SHARD=5) prints `FLOOR FAIL codec-close (1944B < pinned 3000B)` and `Layer F FAIL (rc=1)`.

RED 2 -- AN UNPINNED CODEC FAILS, which is the half that a table-driven gate usually gets wrong. Deleting the `[codec-close]` row entirely prints `FLOOR MISSING codec-close (measured 1944B, no pinned floor)` and `Layer F FAIL (rc=1)`. Without this the table would silently stop judging any codec added later.
BOTH PROBES REVERTED and the file restored from a pre-probe copy; `grep -c 'codec-close]=1500'` = 1.

THE GATE IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES, and the arithmetic says so rather than the prose: codec-response elides 74472B and the old global threshold passed it at anything above 1024, i.e. it could have lost 98.6% of its elision without a single lane going red.
