publishable_verification_bullets: THE HEADLINE NUMBER WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED: with the parser counting only inbound queries, the armed arm measures 14 recovery GETs over the 8 s window, not 15. R311y447 reported 15, which was 14 GETs plus 1 reply line, and that figure reached the const doc AND the commit subject of 580eab5 ("15 GETs armed"). Commits are immutable, so the correction lives here. Confirmed by direct read of zenoh-ref advanced_cache.rs: the reply at :292-294 interpolates query.selector() verbatim, exactly like the query line at :244.

THE UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE WAS REFUTED BY ENUMERATION, in five places. "Sample-driven fires ONLY from handle_live's gap branch" is false in BOTH implementations: wz issues the request at advanced_subscriber.rs:605, OUTSIDE the match, gated on !state.pending_samples.is_empty(); upstream is the same shape and gate at zenoh-ext advanced_subscriber.rs:704-709. pending_samples has a SECOND writer, the history buffering at :574, and finish_history (:672) skips the flush for a source with a GET in flight -- so a periodic tick landing during the startup history GET can strand buffered samples and let a later live sample fire sample-driven with no gap present. Verified by my own read of all four sites after the reviewer raised it. The round's CONCLUSION survives -- the gate-inversion damage takes leg 11 to 0 GETs, so every GET in that run traces back to the periodic tick -- but the structural reason given for it did not.

TWO REVIEWERS CONVERGED INDEPENDENTLY on the in-flight-gate divergence, from different lenses. Confirmed by read: wz periodic_requests gates on pending_queries == 0 (:691); upstream PeriodicQuery::run increments unconditionally (:592) while gating its other two triggers. Observable consequence: when a GET round trip exceeds the period, upstream overlaps GETs and wz issues at most one. NOT WITNESSED -- a reviewer damage that removes wz's gate (adopting upstream's shape) reds no leg in the file, so nothing pins the behaviour either way.

THE COUNT FLOOR DID NOT DISCRIMINATE, measured. A reviewer damage combining repeated wire loss with the periodic trigger UNARMED produced 9 GETs, clearing the floor of 8 on a stream with zero periodic activity; only the distinct-bound check fired, and at 3 against a constant floor of 4 -- a margin of ONE that shrinks as the window grows, because a longer run lets a multi-loss stream reach more distinct bounds while a constant does not. The floor is now delivered.len() - 2, so both sides scale together. Re-verified with my own multi-loss damage: 3 GETs, 3 distinct, 7 delivered -> floor 5 -> BOTH legs red.

MY OWN FIX TO LEG 12 WAS FALSIFIED BY RUNNING IT, which is the second time this round a new assertion failed its own damage test. I first asserted the oracle trace must contain an inbound-query line, reasoning that the startup history GET every advanced subscriber issues would produce one. Measured: the control arm's trace carries ZERO AdvancedCache Handle query lines -- wz's history GET does not reach this oracle's cache in this fixture at all -- so the assertion was permanently red on a wrong premise. Replaced with the cache-CREATION marker, which the trace does carry ("Create AdvancedCache{key_expr: demo/example/adv, max_samples: ...}"), keeping the claim to what it is: an answerer existed and wz asked it for nothing.

COUNTS THAT DID MOVE, disclosed here because R311y447 bundled them under a "no count movement" sentence: the corpus went 247 -> 249 tests and witnesses-no-atom 24 -> 25. DEFECT 5 -- MY LEG-12 FIX WAS ITSELF WRONG, caught by running it: the startup history GET never reaches this oracle's cache in this fixture, so the inbound-query marker I invented was permanently red. A new assertion is a claim; run it before believing it. This is the SECOND new assertion this round that failed its own damage test.
DEFECT 6 -- an asymmetric guard: I rejected a 0 ms period because it misrepresents the armed state, and left u64::MAX accepted, which misrepresents it identically from the other side. Ceiling added.

Round 311y448.decision_summary: R311y448 -- the INERT-reporting gate for the advanced / group demo flags, track (3) of the three tracks. wz-ap-demo keeps that CLI feature-uniform: the flags parse in every build, and a build without the atom behind them drops the capability and says so naming the missing feature. Nothing exercised those arms until now, and the reason was structural rather than incidental: every advanced/group leg builds the feature ON and asserts the NEGATIVE, while the one sweep that could run a default binary inherits whichever variant a prior lane last built, so it can assert nothing about the variant. The cfg(not(feature)) arms therefore compiled everywhere and ran nowhere, while three fixtures' failure messages depended on their exact wording. New Layer E4i is E4's OPPOSITE contract on the same DEFAULT binary -- E4 asserts --router and --peer are rejected with exit 2, E4i asserts the advanced/group flags are accepted, dropped and reported -- and it owns its build, which is the only place such a contract can live. Three legs, self-contained wz<->wz with a second wz-ap-demo as the peer, so no external binary and no SKIP path; pinned at 3 by the guarded-test helper; every fn name carries an  token for the catch-all skip, verified to match exactly those 3 of 215 ignored tests. Damage matrix, each damage compiled first: a feature-ON build reds all three (which is what makes the skip token necessary rather than decorative), a field-label rename reds the subscribe leg alone, and dropping the feature name from a message reds the group leg alone. A FOURTH damage would not compile, and that is itself the finding: under the feature-OFF cfg the INERT line is the only consumer of its bindings, so the compiler already gates a field's PRESENCE, and what the leg adds is its spelling at runtime -- the realistic failure mode here is degradation, not deletion. Stated honestly in the code: the capability-was-not-activated negative is defence in depth, never yet the sole failure, since the is-INERT assertion fires first. Layer E4i pass 3/3 in 0.31s; C0 pass; A4 UNCHANGED at 97/38/25 with corpus 249 (the file spawns only wz's own binary, so it is not cross-impl corpus and needs no wz-proves annotation, matching wz_peer_reject_without_feature); fmt, clippy, shellcheck and actionlint clean; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

Self-contained wz<->wz: the peer is a second wz-ap-demo --listen, so there is no external binary and the lane cannot SKIP.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the Layer E catch-all gains --skip inert, with the reason recorded next to the existing zenoh_ext / wz_storage_host / wz_peer entries: on a binary this sweep inherited with --features advanced all three legs fail, which is a correct diagnosis in the wrong lane.

verification_bullets: THE GAP WAS REAL AND STRUCTURAL, not hypothetical. Every advanced/group leg builds the feature ON and asserts the NEGATIVE !contains("is INERT"); the Layer E catch-all skips that entire family by fn-name substring; so the #[cfg(not(feature = ...))] arms in runner.rs compiled everywhere and RAN nowhere, while three fixtures' failure messages ("If this says INERT, the demo was built without --features advanced") depended on their wording. R311y447-review named it after R311y447 widened the surface by a field.

DAMAGE MATRIX, each damage compiled before being believed. (1) Build the demo with --features advanced,group instead of default: ALL THREE legs red -- which is also the measurement that makes the `inert` skip token necessary rather than decorative. (2) Rename the field label recovery_periodic_ms= to periodic= on the INERT line: the advanced-subscribe leg reds ALONE. (3) Replace "built without the `group` feature" with wording that does not name the feature: the group leg reds ALONE.

A DAMAGE THAT WOULD NOT COMPILE IS ITSELF A FINDING. Deleting recovery_periodic_ms from the INERT line fails to build: under #[cfg(not(feature = "advanced"))] that line is the ONLY consumer of the binding, so the compiler already gates the field's PRESENCE. What the new leg adds is its SPELLING and its presence at runtime in the right build -- a rename compiles cleanly and the leg catches it. The realistic failure mode for this contract is degradation, not deletion, and the leg is aimed at that.
THE SKIP TOKEN WAS CHECKED FOR COLLISIONS rather than assumed safe: `inert` matches exactly the 3 new legs out of 215 ignored tests in the crate, so --skip inert drops nothing that used to run.

HONEST LIMIT, stated in the code as well: the "capability was not activated" negative is DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not a proven-necessary guard. Its three markers are real and do appear on a feature-ON build (DECLARED ADVANCED SUBSCRIBER in runner.rs, DECLARED ADVANCED PUBLISHER and JOINED GROUP in tasks.rs), but the `is INERT` assertion fires first, so it has never been the sole failure.

Gates: Layer E4i pass 3/3 in 0.31s (lane 3s); Layer C0 pass (the new file is in the spawn predicate, and every #[test] carries an adjacent #[ignore]); Layer A4 pass UNCHANGED at proven=97 partial=38 unproven=25, corpus 249 -- the file spawns only wz's own binary, so it is not in the cross-impl corpus and needs no wz-proves annotation, matching wz_peer_reject_without_feature; cargo fmt --all --check clean; clippy -D warnings clean on wz-integration-tests; bash -n and shellcheck clean on run-ci.sh; actionlint clean on ci.yml.
LANE ORDERING is safe: E4i leaves the DEFAULT binary at the shared path, which is what E4 already left, and E5 rebuilds with --features routing-routes before asserting anything.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y448 = the INERT-reporting gate, track (3) of the three the user asked for in order. Layer E4i is E4's OPPOSITE contract on the same DEFAULT binary: E4 asserts --router / --peer are REJECTED with exit 2 when their feature is absent; E4i asserts --advanced-* / --group-join are ACCEPTED, dropped, and reported naming the missing feature. Both contracts are deliberate -- the reject arm guards a run MODE, the inert arm keeps an additive role's CLI feature-uniform.

WHAT MADE IT UNGATEABLE UNTIL NOW was not difficulty but SHAPE: the existing legs all assert the negative !contains("is INERT") on a feature-ON build, and the one sweep that runs a default-ish binary inherits whatever a prior lane built, so it can assert nothing about the variant. A dedicated lane that OWNS its build is the only place this contract can live -- the same reason E4, E6 and E6h each own theirs.

A COMPILER CAN BE PART OF THE GATE, and noticing that changed what the leg aims at. Removing a field from the INERT line does not build, because under the feature-OFF cfg that line is the binding's only consumer. So deletion was already caught; what was not caught is RENAMING or rewording, and that is what the leg pins.

CARRIED: the "capability was not activated" negative has never been the sole failure in any damage, because the is-INERT assertion fires first. Documented in the code as defence in depth rather than left to read as proven.

STILL OPEN in this family: track (2), the consolidation residual -- a foreign advanced subscriber _sn-range-GETting a wz @adv cache; legs 7/8 already build most of that fixture. Also unchanged from y447-review: the wz-vs-upstream periodic in-flight-gate divergence is unwitnessed, and arming heartbeat + periodic together is reachable from the CLI but exercised by nothing.

Round 311y449.decision_summary: R311y449 -- the review remediation for R311y448. A 3-agent adversarial panel against the frozen tree at f44aa39, arbitrated by direct source read, returned ZERO BLOCKERs, ZERO fabricated findings and ZERO functional defects in y448 code: the E4i lane is a real hard gate, the assertions are non-tautological, and coverage is unchanged. It returned two MAJOR honesty defects, and they are ONE CLASS -- a real measurement restated as the reason for a decision it does not support. MAJOR 1: y448 claimed that under the advanced-OFF cfg the INERT line is the only consumer of its bindings, so the compiler already gates a field PRESENCE and the test only adds SPELLING. True for two of the five subscribe fields. runner.rs carried allow(unused_variables) on three of them, so deleting those from the INERT line BUILT CLEANLY and only the test caught it; y448 measured one unattributed field and generalized to five. Fixed by REMOVING the three attributes rather than softening the sentence: both feature variants still build clean, and the damage that used to compile now fails with unused variable and cargo exit 101, so the gate covers five fields where it covered two. MAJOR 2: y448 recorded the --skip inert token as NECESSARY because the Layer E catch-all runs whichever binary a prior lane last built. That premise is false and has been since R311y265 -- layer_e_ap_demo_round_trip builds the DEFAULT demo itself at :4985 before its own sweep at :5098, both inside :4973-5101 -- so those three legs would have PASSED there. The skip stays on honest grounds (no duplicate run, three process-spawning legs out of a ~49-test parallel sweep) and the stale SOURCE parenthetical y448 copied from was corrected too, so the next round cannot inherit it. Also corrected by enumeration: four fixtures depend on the INERT wording, not three, and the fourth is the group one inside this round own scope; 14 of 15 advanced/group legs assert the negative, not every leg; the INERT warnings have two emitters, not one; the activation-marker negative is DECORATIVE for two verified reasons, structural cfg complementarity and task timing, replacing a weaker mis-attributed claim; and the header SC2329 count 119 was actually 124. Gates after the fix: E4i 3/3, C0, A4 UNCHANGED at 97/38/25 corpus 249, fmt, clippy on both variants, shellcheck, validate_workspace orphan new=+0. Left open and SAID SO: the count pin still cannot catch a test-fn rename that drops the skip token, and Layer E has no count guard at all; both are documented at the lane rather than silently carried.

They suppressed nothing (the advanced-OFF INERT report consumes all five bindings under that cfg) while disarming the compiler gate R311y448's rationale leaned on. The fix STRENGTHENS the claim instead of weakening it: deleting any of the five fields from the INERT line is now a hard unused_variables error under workspace warnings = "deny", which is what y448 asserted and only two fifths of its subject actually had.

"three fixtures" is FOUR, and the fourth is the group one, inside this round's own advanced/group scope. And the record of WHY --skip inert exists is replaced with the honest reason.

(2) TIMING for 2 of 3: DECLARED ADVANCED PUBLISHER and JOINED GROUP are logged from spawned tokio tasks, unordered against the barrier this fixture reads at. The assertion that actually trips first on a feature-ON build is the {flag}= one, not is INERT.

The exclusions above it remain correct for the reason that actually holds (routing-router / routing-routes are absent from a default build), not because the variant is unknown.

Round 311y45.decision_summary: R311y45 -- §5.23 Phase 2b: a routing peer hosts its adminspace on the forwarder and answers its OWN config GET over the wire, reading its forwarder-bound WzConfig -- the runtime composition the R311y42 review found missing, now STRUCTURALLY closed (ONE Rc<RefCell<WzConfig>> both drives the forwarder AND answers the GET). Built on the y44 self-dispatch bridge. Changes: (1) EXTRACTED the Session admin handler's match+reply logic into a Session-INDEPENDENT SSOT wz_session_core::adminspace::answer_admin_query(view, out, ctx, sessions, config_json) + AdminAnswerCtx (root local_data / metrics / config + the read gate, now carried in ctx.read so it is feature-toggle-independent); (2) REFACTORED Session::declare_adminspace to call it (6 existing adminspace tests pass UNCHANGED -- parity); (3) run_peer promotes wz_config to a SHARED Rc<RefCell<WzConfig>> (the Phase-1 deferred sharing primitive, with the admin handler as its 2nd holder) and, under the new --config-queryable flag, register_local_queryable's the admin handler reading the shared config via answer_admin_query; (4) wz-runtime-tokio re-exports adminspace (cfg adminspace-core) + zid_hex; the demo's routing-peer feature pulls wz/adminspace-core; (5) a WIRE e2e (wz_peer_adminspace_config.rs, Layer E6): peer A --config-queryable hosts the admin, client B --connect A --query @/<A_zid>/peer/config gets A's config JSON over TCP (asserted: keyexpr + body=Put + the typed read-at-open fields). User chose the wire e2e as the proof. SCOPE/HONESTY (2-agent adversarial review, NO correctness/soundness/build/parity/flakiness defect found): the e2e proves config-GET-over-the-wire WORKS + the single shared instance serves both surfaces BY CONSTRUCTION; the served JSON is the READ-AT-OPEN mirror (handshake-fixed), so it cannot OBSERVE a runtime change -- live-reconfigure-over-wire visibility (interceptor config in the JSON) is a deferred §5.23 layer, and sessions[] for the forwarder host is empty (live-faces enumeration deferred). Both honesty findings remediated (the "LIVE" framing qualified to read-at-open / structural composition; the session/mod.rs sessions[] comment corrected to empty/deferred). A3 active=101 unchanged (no new library atom; the demo feature change + re-exports add no atom). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

fmt + clippy clean (warnings=deny) across wz-session-core / wz-runtime-tokio / wz-ap-demo / wz-integration-tests; the 2 peer entry points carry #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] (8 args, codebase-accepted).

Round 311y450.decision_summary: R311y450 -- the first of the AP+pico CORE 11: the node-scoped Hybrid Logical Clock, and the cross-impl proof of the forward-path stamp. It closes a LIVE DEFECT whose own module note called it hypothetical. R311xw wrote that the per-storage HLC should be promoted to a single node-scoped Option<Arc<HLC>> WHEN a second auto-stamp consumer landed; that consumer landed at R311y69, ~380 rounds ago, so a build with time-hlc,ext-pubsub-advanced-publisher really did hold TWO independent uhlc::HLCs deriving the SAME uhlc::ID from one node zid with SEPARATE last_time, which is exactly the premise uhlc uniqueness rests on. The fix is zenoh shape: NodeHlc, one clock per node, role-gated on zenoh shipped timestamping.enabled map { router: true, peer: false, client: false }, borrowed by every consumer instead of derived at each call site. The role gate is not a wz invention and its None arm is not a downgrade -- zenoh Session::new_timestamp resolves a missing clock to a plain wall clock and its storage plugin stamps through exactly that, so a peer-hosted storage taking the wall clock is parity. On top of that the round implements the FORWARD-PATH stamp, zenoh treat_timestamp macro, once at the head of route_push and forward_push before any fan-out -- not inside compute_push_forward, which is called per tier-net and would give one Put a different timestamp per mesh leg. The router role stamps, the linkstate peer does not, and that split is upstream default rather than a gap. PROVEN, not asserted: a real zenoh-pico z_sub_attachment decodes a timestamp the wz router-hat added to a Put its publisher sent bare, and an attribution twin on a demo built without the clock routes the same Put with NO timestamp line while the positive leg FAILS against that binary. A4 unproven 25 -> 24 on BOTH the all-lanes and the HOSTED populations, because E8t went into ci.yml in this same commit. The round methodology lesson is the inverse of y449: y449 caught a real measurement restated as a reason it did not support, whereas here the measurement itself was blind -- the sharing test PASSED over the real wall clock against two forked clocks, because the confound ceiling (physical advance) sits above the signal (a shared logical counter). Frozen, it reds with the literal repeated (time, zid) pair. Three of five new assertions needed damage-testing to earn their place and one was an outright tautology until rewritten. The round also corrected its OWN plan: the recorded A4 prerequisite named the wrong crate, and the gate actually derives the demo feature closure from run-ci.sh build lines, so the real prerequisite is a lane that owns the build -- a better coupling, since deleting the lane now reds A4. Left open and said so: the ABSORB branch has no cross-impl witness and cannot get one from this harness, and a node hosting both a Session and a forwarder would hold two clocks -- unreachable today, recorded rather than deferred on a trigger nobody re-checks.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/node_clock.rs: NEW module, UNCONDITIONAL. `NodeHlc` = wz's mirror of zenoh's `Option<Arc<HLC>>` on the Runtime (`zenoh/src/net/runtime/mod.rs:147`, `Runtime::hlc()` at `:336`), plus `TimestampingEnabled`, the per-role gate carrying zenoh's shipped `{ router: true, peer: false, client: false }` verbatim (`DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:206`). `NodeHlc` is ZERO-SIZED without `time-hlc`, so every holder carries it with no cfg and no constructor signature changes across the toggle. `treat_timestamp` is the zenoh `treat_timestamp!` macro mirror (`dispatcher/pubsub.rs:176-210`): no clock -> untouched; Put with no timestamp -> mint; Put WITH one -> absorb via `update_with_timestamp`, and on its error return REPLACE, which is zenoh's shipped `drop_future_timestamp: false` default. `build_clock` takes the physical clock as a parameter for a testing reason stated at the fn: only a FROZEN clock can tell one shared clock from two clocks sharing an id.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/timestamp_source.rs: `FallbackStamp` no longer OWNS a `uhlc::HLC` -- it BORROWS `NodeHlc`, and `new` takes it as a parameter. The R311xw per-storage-scope disclosure in the module doc is rewritten as CLOSED, and records that the second consumer it deferred on had already landed in R311y69.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: `Session` gains a `node_hlc` field, built ONCE in `Session::new` from `actions.params.zid` + `.whatami` against the default map -- the same inputs zenoh uses, and derived rather than passed so the 113 existing `Session::new` call sites are untouched. `Clone` shares it (an Arc bump, not a fork). `new_multicast` gets the non-stamping handle: a handshake-free session has neither a zid nor a role, and no auto-stamp consumer takes a multicast session. New `Session::node_hlc()` accessor = zenoh's `Runtime::hlc()`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_service.rs + advanced_publisher.rs: both auto-stamp consumers now borrow `session.node_hlc()`. THIS IS THE LIVE DEFECT FIX. Both called `FallbackStamp::new(local_zid)` with the same node zid, so a `time-hlc,ext-pubsub-advanced-publisher` build held two independent HLCs deriving the same `uhlc::ID` with separate `last_time`. Reachable since R311y69; the module note called it hypothetical.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs + linkstate_forward.rs: the §5.18 forward-path stamp, applied ONCE at the head of `route_push` and `forward_push`, before any fan-out -- zenoh stamps at one point (`pubsub.rs:328`) and fans the SAME msg to every leg. Deliberately NOT inside `compute_push_forward`, which `forward_push_tier` calls PER TIER-NET; a stamp there gives one Put a different timestamp per mesh leg. Each forwarder derives its clock from the identity and role its nets are already seeded with, so the gate cannot disagree with the role. The router is `WhatAmI::Router` and therefore STAMPS; the linkstate peer is `WhatAmI::Peer` and holds no clock, leaving its wire byte-identical.

crates/wz-session-core/src/push_build.rs: three no_std-safe codec primitives -- `push_is_put`, `read_push_timestamp`, `set_push_timestamp`. The clock cannot enter this crate (`uhlc` carries an unconditional `extern crate alloc` and a non-optional `rand`/`getrandom`), so the split is codec-edit here, policy in wz-runtime-tokio. `set_push_timestamp` keeps the `_Z_FLAG_Z_P_T` (0x20) header bit in sync with the field, the same contract `set_push_keyexpr_literal` carries for `N`, and routes through `gated_timestamp_field` so a `pubsub-timestamp`-off build cannot grow a forward stamp its own builders would refuse to emit.

The sharing test was first written over the REAL wall clock and it PASSED against two independently built clocks -- the physical clock advances between reads and masks the fork, so a wall-clock version of the test would have gone green on the broken code. Rewritten over a FROZEN clock it reds with the literal collision this atom's own module note called hypothetical: "interleaved stamps from two handles must share one counter: 20014547599360 !> 20014547599360" -- the same (time, zid) pair emitted twice. EVERY NEW ASSERTION WAS DAMAGE-TESTED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS A TAUTOLOGY UNTIL IT WAS FIXED. (1) Removing `put.header |= 0x20` from `set_push_timestamp` reds the header-bit leg ("_Z_FLAG_Z_P_T must be set"). (2) Deleting the absorb-Ok early return reds the absorb leg ("an absorbed timestamp must survive the relay untouched"). (3) The Del leg as first written passed WITH THE GUARD DELETED, because `set_push_timestamp`'s own variant match also refuses a non-Put -- so it tested nothing about the guard. Rewritten to assert the frozen-clock counter delta across the treat, it reds at "left: 2, right: 1" when the guard is stubbed out, which is what makes the guard load-bearing rather than decorative.

THE FORWARD SEAM IS COMPILED, PROVEN BY DAMAGE, NOT BY A GREEN LANE. Renaming the call to a nonexistent method reds BOTH forwarders in BOTH cfgs (with and without `time-hlc`) -- 4 diagnostics each for the linkstate seam, an E0599 for the router seam -- so no cfg hides either seam and the routing clippy leg really compiles what it claims to. The bare clippy exit 0 was NOT taken as evidence: it returned in 0.09s off cache.

CROSS-IMPL PROOF, EXECUTED. A real zenoh-pico `z_sub_attachment` printed, for a Put whose publisher log shows no timestamp anywhere: ">> [Subscriber] Received ('demo/hlc': 'bare-put-stamped-by-wz-router')" then "with timestamp: 7668076673402197184". The wz router added it. THE ATTRIBUTION WAS ESTABLISHED BOTH WAYS: the same topology on a demo built WITHOUT `time-hlc` routes the Put and prints NO timestamp line, and the positive leg FAILS against that binary with "relayed the sample WITHOUT adding a node-HLC timestamp". A pair of greens would not have shown this; the RED is what pins the timestamp to the clock.

A4 MOVED, ON BOTH POPULATIONS. proven=97 partial=38 unproven=25 -> proven=97 partial=39 unproven=24, corpus 117 files/249 tests -> 118/251, and `time-hlc` is gone from the UNPROVEN list. A4 ALSO CORRECTED THIS ROUND'S OWN PLAN. The prerequisite for the claim was recorded as "add time-hlc to wz-integration-tests' dev-dep features". That is the WRONG CRATE: A4-5 reported "not in wz-ap-demo's enabled-feature closure", and `feature_closure.py::ap_demo_lane_features` derives that closure by unioning every `cargo build -p wz-ap-demo --features` line in run-ci.sh. FAITHFULNESS ESTABLISHED BY DIRECT READ, NOT FROM MEMORY. zenoh's role gate at `net/runtime/mod.rs:147-148`; the shipped map at `DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:206`; `drop_future_timestamp: false` as the shipped default at `:207-209`; the macro at `dispatcher/pubsub.rs:176-210` and its single call site at `:328`; `Session::new_timestamp()`'s wall-clock None arm at `api/session.rs:833-843`; the storage plugin reaching the clock through it at `plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/service.rs:182`; the publish auto-stamp at `api/session.rs:2129` and `Runtime::new_timestamp()` returning None without a clock at `:296`. ONE DIVERGENCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. zenoh stamps INSIDE `if !route.is_empty()`, after computing the route; wz stamps at the head, before the four independently-routed blocks of `route_push`. So a Put with no interested route still advances this node's logical counter. That is HLC-internal and not wire-visible, and hoisting the stamp is what buys the single-timestamp-across-all-legs guarantee the per-tier-net alternative cannot give.

NOT PROVEN, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN LEFT TO READ AS DONE. THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE INVERSE OF R311y449's: y449 named "a real measurement restated as the reason for a decision it does not support". Here the measurement itself was the trap. The sharing test PASSED over the real wall clock against two forked clocks, because the confound (physical clock advance) has a higher ceiling than the signal (a shared logical counter). A test can be true, run, and green, and still be blind to the exact defect it was written for. The counter is to calibrate against the CONFOUND's ceiling -- freeze it -- and then damage-test. Three of five new assertions needed that treatment and one was an outright tautology until rewritten.

A DEFERRAL RATIONALE ROTS EXACTLY LIKE A STALE PREMISE. R311xw wrote "promote WHEN the second consumer lands". The second consumer landed at R311y69, ~380 rounds ago, and the note kept reading as a live deferral because nobody re-evaluated its trigger. The class is the same as y449's ~180-round-stale parenthetical: a conditional recorded in prose has no gate to re-check it. Prefer a trigger something can MEASURE.

If a leg ever builds both, thread ONE NodeHlc rather than letting each derive its own. Recorded now precisely because a deferral whose trigger nobody re-checks is what this round just spent itself on.

THE LESSON: A DROP-PROOF IS THE EASIEST PROOF TO FAKE, AND THE CALIBRATION IS WHAT MAKES IT REAL. "The message did not arrive" is satisfiable by a dead session, a wrong port, or a foreign binary built without the feature, so the leg carries an admit control through the SAME topology. But that alone still would not have discriminated: an over-sized payload is dropped by the OLD code too. The budget had to be set to exactly the payload so that payload-only accounting ADMITS and payload+attachment DROPS. Generalise: for a filter atom, pick the input the old code and the new code disagree on, and derive the threshold from the oracle rather than hardcoding it.

THE SECOND LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT TEST VEHICLES: a production feature gate can silently empty a test fixture. The wire-chain test went through build_push_literal_with_meta and measured zero attachment bytes, because that builder's attachment arm needs pubsub-attachment, which low-pass deliberately does not require -- it must SIZE an attachment it cannot EMIT. The test failed rather than passing over nothing only because it asserted the measured size against the known input. A fixture built through a gated builder needs its precondition asserted, not assumed.

Round 311y453.decision_summary: R311y453 -- the 5.16 SUBJECT-SCOPING SEAM, built once and serving all three interceptors, and the round where A3 finally moves: REMAINING WORK 89 -> 87 EXACT, the first movement in three rounds, as access-quota and access-downsampling both go PARTIAL -> COMPLETE on their last residual. A rule now narrows to the NIC names and the link protocol of the face a message arrived on, resolved once at LINK OPEN by the driver that owns the socket and read per message as a field, never a syscall. The seam is DELIBERATELY STRICTER THAN UPSTREAM on three counts, each a defect in zenoh 1.5.0 established by direct read rather than inferred: zenoh caches the host interface table in a process-lifetime lazy_static so a NIC appearing later is invisible for the life of the process, while wz resolves live; zenoh maps a FAILED interface lookup to the same empty vector it uses for a link genuinely on no NIC, while wz keeps could-not-determine distinct from resolved-to-nothing and only the second is a definite non-match; and zenoh's two subject axes disagree with EACH OTHER, interfaces requiring every link to match and skipping the check on error while link_protocols requires any and installs nothing on error, whereas wz applies ONE policy to both -- ANY, fail-CLOSED on an indeterminate subject, which is the conservative direction because all three interceptors are restrictive when they apply. It costs no new workspace dependency: zenoh reaches this data through pnet_datalink, wz through the libc already in-tree for unixpipe's mkfifo. PROVEN, not asserted, and as an A/B on the axis itself rather than with a control -- the sibling leg already proves the rate limit fires, so what needed showing is that the subject decides whether a rule governs a face AT ALL. The same real zenoh-pico z_pub burst meets two peers differing in exactly one thing: a rule narrowed to the protocol pico dials throttles it to one of three, the identical rule narrowed to vsock is inert at three of three; a rule narrowed to lo throttles the accepted loopback link, one narrowed to an absent NIC is inert. That interface arm is also the live-getifaddrs witness, since it can only throttle if the peer really resolved 127.0.0.1 to lo at open. With both matchers made inert the demo rebuilt and both negative arms throttled, failing both tests. Three findings about METHOD, each measured: the damage harness lied twice before any result was trustworthy, once because --quiet hides libtest's per-test FAILED lines and once because a deleted filter left an unused variable and reported a compile error instead of a red test; and one damage redded NOTHING, correctly, because no test constructed a subject that had resolved its NICs but not its protocol -- the fail-closed arm was unreachable from the suite, and only the damage run could have found that. Also closed as a side effect: all EIGHT access feature subsets now pass clippy --all-targets, the defect R311y452 recorded as pre-existing, fixed by adding the four missing admin-JSON shape assertions the dead-code warning was pointing at rather than by silencing it.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/link.rs: NEW InterceptorLink (zenoh's 9 link kinds, zenoh-config/src/lib.rs:314-327, plus the wz-only QuicDatagram) with as_str / from_config_str in upstream's kebab-case spelling, and NEW LinkSubject { protocol, interfaces } carrying the two axes plus the four matchers. Proto was tried first and REJECTED: it is the SocketAddr-based IP scheme set, so serial / unixsock / unixpipe / vsock are unrepresentable in it. BoxedLinkDriver gains link_subject() -> Option<&LinkSubject>, defaulted to None so the six test doubles need no change.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_interfaces.rs: NEW. Live getifaddrs / freeifaddrs resolution of the NIC names a local address sits on, every unsafe block carrying a SAFETY note and the sockaddr read done with read_unaligned. ip_link_subject / addressless_link_subject are the two constructors the pipelines call. No new workspace dependency: libc was already in-tree for unixpipe's mkfifo and only moved from the target_os = "linux" table to cfg(unix), since getifaddrs is POSIX.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio: ten production drivers resolve their subject AT LINK OPEN and store it. StreamWriteDriver serves six pipelines and is transport-neutral, so its subject is a CONSTRUCTOR parameter -- a new stream pipeline cannot compile without stating it. Round 311y454.decision_summary: R311y454 -- the locator-iface atom CLOSES, and both grading axes move in one round for the first time in five: A3 REMAINING WORK 87 to 86 EXACT and A4 unproven 22 to 21. All three named residuals fall. The QUIC and quic-datagram LISTEN halves now honour the iface tail through one shared seam that pre-binds the UDP socket, applies SO_BINDTODEVICE and hands it to quinn Endpoint::new rather than the convenience constructor that owns its own socket -- the identical route zenoh takes, and the exact mirror of wz s own dial arm. The UDP multicast semantic, previously absent entirely, pins BOTH directions: imr_interface on the join and IP_MULTICAST_IF on egress, the pair zenoh splits across two sockets and wz already split at a higher level without pinning either. The honor is reachable as a LOCATOR, not as a bespoke flag, because this atom is about honouring a locator tail and a knob would have left its semantic unclosed. THREE THINGS THIS ROUND GOT WRONG AND CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING, each by measurement rather than argument. First, the planned deliberate divergence was not one: zenoh is ALSO hard-error for a not-found, down or carrier-less interface, and its silent fallback fires in exactly one narrower case, so the broad claim would have been a false ledger statement. Second, my own four-case multicast measurement said a pico-driven A/B would discriminate; it will not, because my probe had one joining socket while the real interop topology requires both stacks to co-bind, and IP_MULTICAST_ALL then makes the per-socket pin invisible -- reproduced independently before accepting the refutation, so the multicast half is recorded as not foreign-observable on a single host and the A4 witness is the QUIC A/B alone. Third, the resulting multicast test was FLAKY, passing alone and failing in its file s concurrent run, and the cause was the same mechanism at a different scale: the leaking membership is per group and device, not per port, so a unique port was never enough and a dedicated group was. Fixed, re-damaged to confirm it still discriminates, run clean three times. The proof is an A/B on ONE real zenohd dial differing in a single token, with both arms asserting the listen tag so the negative is a DELIVERY failure and not a bind failure, plus a delivery-based wz-internal twin that exists specifically to catch an implementation that device-binds a socket and then drops it -- a bug that would pass both an it-works-on-lo test and an absent-device-gives-ENODEV test. Two syscall facts were measured because the documentation answers neither: SO_BINDTODEVICE works unprivileged, which means the pre-existing dial-side honor has always actually worked and nobody had checked, and an absent device returns ENODEV. A FOURTH upstream honor site was found and deliberately NOT claimed: iface also filters which addresses a wildcard listener advertises, and wz has no wildcard expansion at all, so that residual belongs to the absent locator-advertisement capability and COMPLETE is scoped in writing to the socket-bind semantic. Closed as a side effect: Layer C1bd, the atom s own lane since R311y236, both ran nowhere hosted and only clippy-compiled the honor path -- it is now registered in ci.yml and executes it.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_interfaces.rs: NEW unicast_addresses_of_interface -- the inverse getifaddrs walk (name to addresses), returning Result with a typed IfaceResolveError rather than the Option its y453 sibling returns. Three outcomes are needed, not two, because upstream treats them differently: NotFound / NotUp / NotRunning are hard errors, while a resolvable interface carrying no address of the group family is what zenoh silently falls back on. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: bind_multicast_v4 gains iface and pins BOTH directions on its one socket -- imr_interface on the join and IP_MULTICAST_IF on egress -- because that one socket does both. crates/wz-ap-demo: NEW --multicast-locator udp/GROUP:PORT#iface=NAME, parsed by the SHARED wz_session_core::locator parser (already re-exported at wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:183, so no new facade surface). EVERY NEW ASSERTION WAS DAMAGE-TESTED, FIVE FOR FIVE, EACH REDDING ONLY ITS OWN TEST AND EACH PROVING ITS REBUILD: building the device-bound socket and then DROPPING it (quinn's convenience constructor still called -- the bind-then-drop bug) reds only the quic listen A/B while its sibling e2e passes; the join falling back to INADDR_ANY reds only the multicast A/B while the four other multicast tests pass; the egress IP_MULTICAST_IF pin going no-op likewise; the IFF_RUNNING rejection never firing reds only the sysfs carrier cross-check; an absent interface reporting Undetermined instead of NotFound reds only the policy-boundary test. None escaped into a compile error: each damage kept its variable used deliberately.

THE CROSS-IMPL DAMAGE NEEDED AN EXPLICIT DEMO REBUILD, AND SAYING SO MATTERS. The fixture launches the wz-ap-demo BINARY, a separate artifact from the crate cargo test rebuilds, so damaging the library and re-running the test would have exercised a stale binary and read exactly like damage-not-caught. With cargo build -p wz-ap-demo forced, arm B reported STILL completed the handshake and redded.

THE MULTICAST A/B WAS FLAKY AND WAS ROOT-CAUSED, NOT REVERTED. It passed alone and FAILED inside its file's concurrent run. Cause, measured: IP_MULTICAST_ALL defaults to 1 and the leaking membership is per (group, device) -- the PORT only decides which socket receives what the membership already admitted. A sibling test joining 224.0.0.224 with INADDR_ANY installs a host membership on the default-route device, and arm B, whose egress is pinned to that device, then receives its own datagram on a port nothing else binds. Fixed with a DEDICATED 239.0.0.0/8 group, then re-damaged to confirm the fixed test still discriminates, then run three times clean. My own earlier reasoning that a unique PORT sufficed was wrong.

THE PRE-CODE DESIGN PANEL REFUTED MY OWN MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE ROUND'S SHARPEST FINDING. I had measured a four-case multicast matrix and concluded a pico-driven join/egress A/B would work. It does not: my probe had exactly ONE joining socket, while the real pico interop topology requires BOTH stacks to wildcard-bind with SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT to co-exist on one host, and that co-bind is precisely what makes the pin invisible. Reproduced independently before accepting it: with a peer co-joined on a real NIC, a lo-joined socket still receives that NIC's traffic. So the multicast half is recorded as NOT foreign-observable on a single host, and the A4 witness is the QUIC listen A/B alone.

THE PANEL ALSO REFUTED THE ROUND'S PLANNED DIVERGENCE. I had intended to record a deliberate hard-error divergence against zenoh's silent fallback. zenoh is ALSO hard-error for not-found / not-up / not-running: get_unicast_addresses_of_interface bails on all three (zenoh-util/src/net/mod.rs:233-247) and zenoh-link-udp propagates with ? (multicast.rs:229). The fallback fires in ONE case only -- an interface up and running but carrying no address of the group's family. Verified by direct read before narrowing the claim; recording the broad version would have been a false statement in the ledger.

TWO SYSCALL FACTS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, BECAUSE THE DOCUMENTATION DOES NOT ANSWER EITHER. SO_BINDTODEVICE succeeds UNPRIVILEGED (euid 1000, on lo and on a real NIC) -- which also means the pre-existing dial-side honor has always actually worked, something the project had never checked. An absent device name returns ENODEV(19); man 7 socket documents the delivery semantic but not that errno, so the negative arm could not have been designed on the page alone.

A FOURTH UPSTREAM HONOR SITE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. get_locators() reads BIND_INTERFACE to filter which local addresses a WILDCARD-bound listener ADVERTISES (zenoh-link-commons/src/listener.rs:115-144). wz has no counterpart because wz has no wildcard-to-concrete locator expansion at all -- one is_unspecified use in the entire runtime, and get_locators appears only in comments citing zenoh. The residual therefore belongs to the absent locator-advertisement capability, not to this atom, and COMPLETE is scoped to the socket-bind semantic in the inventory reason.

NO no_std CRATE WAS TOUCHED, so the MCU hand-check that R311y453 needed does not apply here: every change is in wz-runtime-tokio, wz-ap-demo, wz-integration-tests, two Cargo.toml files, run-ci.sh and ci.yml.
carry_forward_bullets: UNASSERTED ARM, NAMED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the one real resolution-policy divergence -- an interface that is up and running but carries no address of the group's family, where zenoh substitutes another non-loopback multicast interface and wz refuses -- has NO test. It needs a real NIC that is up with no IPv4, which cannot be constructed without CAP_NET_ADMIN. Everything else in multicast_iface_selector_v4 is covered.

THE MULTICAST HALF OF locator-iface IS NOT FOREIGN-OBSERVABLE ON A SINGLE HOST, and this is a MECHANISM to reuse, not a one-off excuse. IP_MULTICAST_ALL defaults to 1 and the leaking membership is per (group, device); a foreign peer must share the group to interoperate, and sharing it installs the membership that hides any per-socket interface pin. Any future round tempted to prove a multicast per-socket property cross-impl on one host should read this first. Observing it needs two link domains: two hosts, or netns with CAP_NET_ADMIN.

A LANE CAN BE WEAKER THAN ITS OWN NAME FOR MANY ROUNDS. Layer C1bd has existed as the locator-iface lane since R311y236, and it (a) was absent from ci.yml so it ran only in a manual local full sweep, and (b) only clippy-COMPILED the honor path, executing none of it -- so even that sweep proved nothing about behaviour. Both are now fixed. Generalise: when a round claims an atom's lane covers it, check that the lane RUNS HOSTED and that it EXECUTES rather than compiles. Neither is implied by the lane existing.

REVERT A DAMAGE BY INVERSE REPLACEMENT, NEVER BY git checkout -- ON A FILE THE ROUND IS EDITING. Doing the latter wiped this round's legitimate quic_pipeline.rs work along with the damage and cost a full re-apply; the next compile caught it, but a damage protocol that destroys the work under test is a hazard worth stating once.

A NAME-FILTERED TEST LEG NEEDS A COUNT GUARD. A leg that selects a whole binary reddens when the binary goes quiet, but one carrying a filter selects zero on a rename and exits green. The new Layer M leg is guarded at 1 passed for that reason; the sibling legs above it select whole binaries and do not need it.

STILL OPEN on the accept/locator family, unchanged by this round: wz has no wildcard-to-concrete listener locator advertisement at all, which is why upstream's fourth BIND_INTERFACE honor site has no counterpart. That is a locator-advertisement / adminspace-introspection concern and it now has a written home.

Fixed with a DEDICATED 239.0.0.0/8 group, then re-damaged to confirm the fixed test still discriminates, then run three times clean. My own earlier reasoning that a unique PORT sufficed was wrong.

THE PRE-CODE DESIGN PANEL REFUTED MY OWN MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE ROUND'S SHARPEST FINDING. I had measured a four-case multicast matrix and concluded a pico-driven join/egress A/B would work. It does not: my probe had exactly ONE joining socket, while the real pico interop topology requires BOTH stacks to wildcard-bind with SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT to co-exist on one host, and that co-bind is precisely what makes the pin invisible. Reproduced independently before accepting it: with a peer co-joined on a real NIC, a lo-joined socket still receives that NIC's traffic. So the multicast half is recorded as NOT foreign-observable on a single host, and the A4 witness is the QUIC listen A/B alone.

THE PANEL ALSO REFUTED THE ROUND'S PLANNED DIVERGENCE. I had intended to record a deliberate hard-error divergence against zenoh's silent fallback. zenoh is ALSO hard-error for not-found / not-up / not-running: get_unicast_addresses_of_interface bails on all three (zenoh-util/src/net/mod.rs:233-247) and zenoh-link-udp propagates with ? (multicast.rs:229). The fallback fires in ONE case only -- an interface up and running but carrying no address of the group's family. Verified by direct read before narrowing the claim; recording the broad version would have been a false statement in the ledger.

TWO SYSCALL FACTS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, BECAUSE THE DOCUMENTATION DOES NOT ANSWER EITHER. SO_BINDTODEVICE succeeds UNPRIVILEGED (euid 1000, on lo and on a real NIC) -- which also means the pre-existing dial-side honor has always actually worked, something the project had never checked. An absent device name returns ENODEV(19); man 7 socket documents the delivery semantic but not that errno, so the negative arm could not have been designed on the page alone.

A FOURTH UPSTREAM HONOR SITE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. get_locators() reads BIND_INTERFACE to filter which local addresses a WILDCARD-bound listener ADVERTISES (zenoh-link-commons/src/listener.rs:115-144). wz has no counterpart because wz has no wildcard-to-concrete locator expansion at all -- one is_unspecified use in the entire runtime, and get_locators appears only in comments citing zenoh. The residual therefore belongs to the absent locator-advertisement capability, not to this atom, and COMPLETE is scoped to the socket-bind semantic in the inventory reason.

Both are now fixed. Generalise: when a round claims an atom's lane covers it, check that the lane RUNS HOSTED and that it EXECUTES rather than compiles. Neither is implied by the lane existing.

A NAME-FILTERED TEST LEG NEEDS A COUNT GUARD. A leg that selects a whole binary reddens when the binary goes quiet, but one carrying a filter selects zero on a rename and exits green. Round 311y455.decision_summary: R311y455 -- a HOSTED RED inherited from R311y453 is diagnosed and fixed, and the hazard that caused it is finally gated. R311y453 added a subject-scoping cross-impl fixture whose FILE name carried the wz_peer family token but whose two test FUNCTIONS did not. libtest --skip matches the TEST name, which for an integration test is the function name, so Layer E s default sweep did not exclude them: it ran both against the DEFAULT demo binary, the demo refused --peer for want of the routing-peer feature, and the hosted run for 2ab214a4 went red at Layer E. The fixture itself is sound -- Layer E6, which owns the routing-peer build, runs it two passed -- so what failed was routing, not the proof. Both functions now carry the token, and Layer E selects zero of them while E6 still selects both, each measured rather than assumed. THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS THE GATE. run-ci.sh had ALREADY written this hazard down, at the E4i lane in R311y449, in as many words: the token is a naming obligation that no gate enforces. Six rounds later R311y453 walked into it. A documented-but-ungated hazard is one that recurs, so Layer C0 now enforces the obligation: any fixture under wz-integration-tests whose basename declares an excluded family must have every test function carry at least one skip token. The gate was falsified before being trusted, in both directions and including its own self-check, and it was CALIBRATED after a first draft flagged twenty-nine sites of which twenty-eight were not hazards -- it had demanded every token the filename carries, where any one token suffices, and it had scanned crates Layer E never runs. That miscalibration is recorded rather than quietly corrected, because a gate that fails the build on non-hazards is worse than no gate at all. A second lesson lands beside it: R311y453 was pushed and recorded as shipped with its hosted verdict unread, and the red sat there until R311y454s push happened to list the prior run next to it. The carried note said to read the verdict; it was still not read.

Round 311y456.decision_summary: R311y456 -- R311y454 broke two hosted lanes and this fixes them, with the honest cause named: one error in two places, error E0061, six arguments where seven are needed, in the wz-ap-demo bin TEST target. R311y454 threaded a multicast_locator parameter through four functions and verified each with a feature-narrow cargo check that carried no --all-targets, so the crate own test targets -- which call two of those functions -- were never compiled at all. Layer C1bf hit the compile error directly; Layer C1bl hit it through the very test whose call site was missed, so its count guard found no passing test and the lane redded. Confirmed as one cause by reading what C1bl actually runs, not by observing that the fix worked. The sweep that would have caught it is now run across all three touched crates and is clean. Two things the R311y454 run itself said, read from the run rather than assumed. First, Layers A3, A4, C0, M and Z were all SUCCESS on hosted, so that round grading movement and both of its new proof legs do rest on hosted evidence. Second, and this qualifies a claim R311y454 made: Layer C1bd was SKIPPED, not run. It sits after Layer C1bf in a job with fail-fast step semantics, so C1bf failing skipped ten subsequent lanes including it. Registered in ci.yml is not the same as executed, and a skipped step reads exactly like a green one to anyone reading only the lane list. C1bd has still never executed on hosted CI; the next green run is its first.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the two IN-CRATE test call sites of run_router_hat_until / run_router_hat pass the R311y454 multicast_locator argument. R311y454 threaded that parameter through the production path and missed both test callers, because it verified with `cargo check -p wz-ap-demo --features router-hat-router,locator-iface` -- no --all-targets, so the crate's own test targets were never compiled.
verification_bullets: THE TWO LANES R311y454 BROKE ARE GREEN, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE ERROR IN TWO PLACES: error[E0061] "this function takes 7 arguments but 6 arguments were supplied" in the wz-ap-demo bin TEST target. Layer C1bf (--all-features clippy) hit it directly; Layer C1bl hit it through `cargo test -p wz-ap-demo --features router-hat-router,quic run_router_hat_admits_a_quic_listen_with_cert_at_bind`, which is EXACTLY one of the two call sites -- the test could not compile, so its `1 passed` count guard found nothing. Same root cause, verified by reading what C1bl runs rather than by inferring from the fix working.
BOTH LANES RUN CLEAN LOCALLY NOW: Layer C1bf pass 19s, Layer C1bl pass 26s.

THE SWEEP THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT IS NOW RUN: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings across wz-ap-demo, wz-runtime-tokio and wz-integration-tests, all three clean. R311y454's own verification used narrow feature sets and no --all-targets, which is precisely the gap a signature change needs covered.

WHAT ELSE THE R311y454 RUN SAID, read from the run rather than assumed: Layers A3, A4, C0, M and Z all SUCCESS on hosted, so the round's grading moves and both its new proof legs stand on hosted evidence. Layer E failed for the inherited R311y453 reason R311y455 fixes.

LAYER C1bd WAS SKIPPED, NOT RUN, AND SKIPPED READS AS GREEN. It sits in the "feature-gate NEG lanes" job AFTER Layer C1bf; that job has fail-fast step semantics, so C1bf's failure skipped ten subsequent lanes including C1bd. So R311y454's claim that C1bd "now runs hosted" is precise only as REGISTERED: it runs when the lanes ahead of it in its job pass, and its first real hosted execution has not happened yet.
carry_forward_bullets: A SIGNATURE CHANGE NEEDS --all-targets, NOT A FEATURE-NARROW cargo check. R311y454 threaded one parameter through four functions and verified each with a narrow `cargo check`; the crate's OWN test targets call two of those functions and were never compiled. The cheap habit that prevents it: after any signature change, `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on every touched crate before the round claims to be done.

A LANE REGISTERED IN A FAIL-FAST JOB IS NOT YET A LANE THAT RAN. Steps in the feature-gate NEG lanes job stop at the first failure, so ten lanes after C1bf were skipped. When a round adds a hosted lane, the verdict to read is that STEP's conclusion -- success / failure / SKIPPED -- and not merely that the lane appears in ci.yml.
STILL OPEN: R311y454's Layer C1bd has never actually executed on hosted CI. The next green run is its first, and that step's conclusion is what settles it.

NEXT: access-acl, and the design read is already done. Its fail-OPEN arm at interceptor/access_control.rs:102-106 is NOT a data-plane bypass -- both the forward path (linkstate_forward.rs:1547-1549) and the local-delivery path (:2656-2659) drop an unresolvable keyexpr anyway, so the comment claiming routing handles it is TRUE for those paths. But the naive fix is a REGRESSION: acl_action governs NetworkMessage::Response(_) wholesale and the keyexpr-None arm is what admits ResponseFinal, so flipping admit to deny would deny every query end-marker. zenoh does not rely on that path at all -- it puts ResponseFinal in an explicitly unfiltered arm beside Interest and OAM (net/routing/interceptor/access_control.rs:614-617 and :921-924). So the fix is TWO parts in order: make ResponseFinal an unfiltered kind in acl_action, THEN deny on an unresolvable keyexpr, matching the 22 of 22 zenoh arms that all `return false`. Also established: zenoh DOES govern UndeclareSubscriber (:468-484, with a deliberate ingress asymmetry keyed on ext_wire_expr) and DOES govern token-carrying Interest (:557-591), so those inventory residuals are real -- the `Interest(_)` unfiltered arm is a catch-all that sits AFTER the guarded ones.

Round 311y458.decision_summary: R311y458 -- the access-acl governed SET now equals zenoh's: the three undeclare kinds, the liveliness token declare/undeclare, and a token-carrying Interest are all governed, which closes the undeclare, Interest and liveliness-action residuals in one round. AclMessage carries zenoh's same nine actions in the same order, each declare/undeclare pair sharing ONE action as upstream does, and the Interest arms split on MODE rather than on the token flag because that is how zenoh splits them -- CURRENT-only is the one-shot GET, anything with FUTURE registers for the stream. The load-bearing subtlety is an asymmetry that had to be reproduced rather than simplified away: zenoh routes only its three INGRESS undeclare arms through a helper whose absent-keyexpr answer is Allow, while the egress twins deny, so R311y457's blanket deny-on-unresolvable needed one flow-keyed exception and not a general softening. An undeclare's keyexpr is not inline -- it rides the optional ext_wire_expr -- so the resolver reads it through the extension SSOT the forwarders already use. Four separate damage passes each falsify a different leg, including one that isolates the ingress-only condition to a single test. Also corrected: a comment claiming the Request write arms mirror a zenoh dispatch that does not exist, since zenoh's RequestBody has only a Query variant. That is the third stale prose claim in two rounds, all three settled by opening the upstream type.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-access-control/src/lib.rs: AclMessage gains LivelinessToken, DeclareLivelinessSubscriber and LivelinessQuery, so wz carries the SAME NINE actions in the SAME order as zenoh (zenoh-config/src/lib.rs:354-364), with as_str emitting zenoh's snake_case names. The enum doc no longer says the liveliness actions are pending, and SubjectSelector's doc no longer says the link-protocol and interface subjects are deferred -- R311y453 put those on AclRule, and the axes actually absent are cert_common_name and username.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/interceptor/access_control.rs: acl_action returns a GovernedAction, not a bare AclMessage. The struct carries the action plus ONE bit -- whether the kind is an undeclare -- because that is the only thing the unresolvable-keyexpr branch needs to reproduce zenoh's asymmetry, and the flow it needs is already on the enforcer.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/interceptor/access_control.rs: the Declare arm governs all SIX declaration bodies, each (un)declare pair under ONE action exactly as zenoh pairs them -- Declare/UndeclareSubscriber under DeclareSubscriber, Declare/UndeclareQueryable under DeclareQueryable, Declare/UndeclareToken under LivelinessToken.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/interceptor/access_control.rs: a token-carrying Interest is governed, split on MODE and not on the flag, which is how zenoh splits it (:557-591): CURRENT-only is the one-shot GET (LivelinessQuery), anything with FUTURE registers for the stream (DeclareLivelinessSubscriber). Mode comes from the outer header's C / F bits (zenoh-codec network/interest.rs:53-58), the token flag from the body's `to` bit. A Final Interest has no body at all, so it takes the no-token exit and is admitted -- zenoh's unfiltered arm.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/interceptor/access_control.rs: intercept's unresolvable-keyexpr branch admits when the kind is an undeclare AND the flow is Ingress, and denies otherwise. That is zenoh's asymmetry verbatim, not a softening of R311y457: only the three ingress undeclare arms go through cached_result_or_action_undecl, whose None arm answers Allow (:159-166), and the egress twins take the ordinary deny (:762-776).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: resolve_governed_keyexpr resolves the new kinds. The Declare half moved into declare_governed_keyexpr, because the six governed bodies carry their keyexpr in TWO places -- inline for the three declares, and in the optional ext_wire_expr for the three undeclares, read through the existing declare_ext_keyexpr SSOT that the forwarders' undeclare ingest already uses. An Interest resolves through its (mode != Final) body. declare_token_wireexpr lost its routing-token-tables gate: this resolver calls it on every routing-peer build, so it is no longer dead code without that feature.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: --acl-deny also denies the three liveliness actions, so `--acl-deny K` means what its own comment says and the new governance is reachable from the only CLI that installs a policy.

(B) dropping the `&& self.flow == AclFlow::Ingress` condition -- leaving the undeclare admit unconditional -- reds exactly ONE, the egress test, which is the whole point of the pair. (C) swapping the two Interest mode arms reds exactly ONE, the mode test. (D) ignoring the body's TOKENS bit and governing every bodied Interest reds exactly that same one, via its untokened leg. THE UNTOKENED LEG EXISTS BECAUSE THE TEST NAME PROMISED IT. All three wz Interest builders are liveliness builders, so there is no ungoverned-but-bodied Interest to build; the leg takes the FUTURE subscription and clears the body's `to` bit -- the same message, one bit different -- and asserts `!body.to()` before making the claim. Without it, damage (D) would have passed and the name would have been covering nothing.

Round 311y459.decision_summary: R311y459 -- the foreign witness R311y458 was missing: real zenoh-pico CLIs now drive a DeclareToken, its UndeclareToken and a token-carrying CURRENT Interest at a wz peer running --acl-deny, and all three are denied on the denied keyexpr while all three are admitted on the allowed one. y458 shipped five new governed arms with nothing but wz's own fixtures behind them; this closes that. The count is the discriminator and so the emitter was read first: pico carries the keyexpr on BOTH halves of a token's life, the undeclare putting it in the optional ext_wire_expr, so a denied token costs TWO drops -- and one drop rather than two would have meant the ingress asymmetry admitted the undeclare instead of judging it. That the second drop really is the undeclare was settled by moving the CLI hold from one second to three and watching the gap follow, not by assuming. The liveliness get sends exactly one message, so its drop is attributable to the Interest arm alone. Every allowed message runs FIRST and must leave the drop counter at zero, which rules out the ACL dropping the whole liveliness plane -- something a per-message positive control cannot distinguish. The A4 headline does not move and that is worth stating plainly: access-acl was already proven by the data-plane leg, so the gate is structurally unable to show that the CONTENT of the proof grew.

verification_bullets: RED PROVED AGAINST THE y458 CODE, WITH THE REBUILD VISIBLE. Removing the DeclareToken and UndeclareToken arms and making the Interest arm ungoverned -- i.e. restoring the pre-y458 state -- makes the leg FAIL at its first liveliness barrier: "wz peer never reached 'interceptor dropped (2 message(s))' for the DENIED secret/alive token within 15s". The wz-ap-demo rebuild is in the same output, so this is a behaviour change and not a stale binary. Restored and re-verified: 1 passed, 4.32s.

WHAT EACH pico CLI EMITS WAS READ BEFORE THE COUNTS WERE TRUSTED, not inferred from them. z_liveliness declares a token and, after -t seconds, undeclares it, and BOTH messages carry the keyexpr -- _z_liveliness_send_declare_token builds a DeclToken with an inline wireexpr, _z_liveliness_send_undeclare_token builds an UndeclToken via _z_make_undecl_token(id, &wireexpr), i.e. the OPTIONAL ext (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/liveliness.c:32-50). z_get_liveliness sends EXACTLY ONE message, an Interest with KEYEXPRS|TOKENS|RESTRICTED|CURRENT and no subscriber declaration (:314-362).

THE "SECOND DROP IS THE UNDECLARE" CLAIM WAS SETTLED BY MOVING IT, NOT BY ASSUMING IT. With -t 1 the two drops are one second apart; re-running with -t 3 moved the gap to three seconds. So the second drop tracks the undeclare's timing and is not a retry or a teardown artefact. The test then uses -t 1 so the pair lands inside its barrier.

THE FOREIGN ENCODER EXERCISES THE ext_wire_expr PATH, WHICH NO wz FIXTURE PROVED. pico's UndeclareToken carries its keyexpr as the optional extension, so the drop of the DENIED undeclare goes through R311y458's resolve path for undeclares -- the branch that reads declare_ext_keyexpr rather than an inline wireexpr. Had pico omitted the extension, the ingress asymmetry would have ADMITTED it and the count would have been 1, not 2; the count is what distinguishes the two.

Frozen ledger keeps both entries as written; this is the correcting record. Nothing else remains open from the three rounds.

Round 311y461.decision_summary: R311y461 -- the round set out to write the missing foreign witness for liveliness-historical-samples and instead falsified the classification that made it look writable. Round 311y462.decision_summary: R311y462 -- adopt upstream mnemosyne [tool] pin, and correct the notice that asked for it. mnemosyne sent an unsolicited notice (its R868/R871) reporting that this tree gate RESULT changed twice in one day with nothing changed here, because a repo that declares no pin is interpreted by whatever binary the machine installed LAST. Every claim was reproduced before acting, and two facts the notice did not have came out of that. FIRST, its section 4 is incomplete for this machine: mnemosyne-mcp is a SEPARATE binary that also parses mnemosyne.toml, it was installed at 25d30d16 -- the very rev this repo declared -- and on an isolated copy it dies on the new key with a TOML parse error at [tool], while 0c82ad73 and be4c1647 both know the key and merely enforce it. Since ci.yml:594 installs that same constant and then validates with it, declaring the key alone would have red-ed every hosted job AND killed the agent-session MCP server. So the key and the rev moved in ONE commit, with both binaries installed and verified first, and upstream own escape hatch does not cover it because MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP is read only after the config parses. SECOND, its section 2 is wrong about this tree: it says we were lucky and skipped the R840 red window, but Round 311y453 records that gate firing here on a drifted 27396a99 and blocking every commit. Its section 5 question is answered NO by VCS -- vendor/ holds four entries, all mode 160000, and zero wz-authored files -- and its section 6 verdict that nothing is wrong with our configuration is confirmed. The real drift was never a missing pin: it was that the declared pin and the PATH binary had diverged, silently.
changes_bullets: mnemosyne.toml: a new [tool] pin = "a886cd0f25682056b4f0fb1d88be89356180f32a" declares WHICH Mnemosyne build may interpret this workspace, placed beside [plugins.set_equality_validator] with the ordering rule written in-file. scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh stays the pin's SSOT -- it is what ci.yml:594 and release.yml:94 install and what install-mnemosyne-mcp.sh parses out of HEAD -- and this key states the same fact where EVERY binary reads it, including mnemosyne-mcp, which the installer's schema gate never sees.

scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh: MNEMOSYNE_REV 25d30d161c2c54c3bbcfde9f2a0156724b5f6471 -> a886cd0f25682056b4f0fb1d88be89356180f32a. This bump is NOT schema-forced (the first in this file's history that is not): it exists because declaring the key without moving the rev would have red-ed every hosted job. MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA stays 44, RE-READ at the new rev rather than carried -- git show a886cd0f:crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:1688 defines CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 44 and :1972 still rejects on_disk_version above it.

Binaries (machine state, not repo state): mnemosyne-cli be4c1647 -> a886cd0f and mnemosyne-mcp 25d30d16 -> a886cd0f, both installed BEFORE the key was declared, per the notice's own ordering rule and this file's.

NOTHING was written to the mnemosyne repo and nothing of theirs was copied here. The isolated parse experiment ran on a COPY of the store in the scratch dir, never on docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json.
verification_bullets: THE PARSE HAZARD WAS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, AND ON AN ISOLATED COPY. A scratch workspace with a COPY of the store (never docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json itself) was given the same mnemosyne.toml plus a [tool] pin, and three builds were run against it. 0c82ad73 (R858) KNOWS the key and refuses with "pins Mnemosyne <rev>, and this build is 0c82ad73"; be4c1647 (R869) refuses identically; 25d30d16 -- the rev this repo declared, and the rev mnemosyne-mcp was actually installed at -- FAILS EARLIER AND DIFFERENTLY: "mnemosyne.toml parse failed: TOML parse error at line 560, column 2 | [tool]". That third result is the whole reason the rev moved in the same commit.

THE HARNESS WAS BISECTED BEFORE ITS FIRST RESULT WAS BELIEVED. The scratch run initially exited 1 for an unrelated reason -- "configured scan paths resolve to nothing ... a validator with no file to read reports the same clean as a clean tree" -- because the scratch dir has no crates/, deploy/ or xtask/. Round 311y463.decision_summary: R311y463 -- liveliness-historical-samples is PROVEN, and R311y461 is corrected: its central claim that the atom needs CODE rather than a witness is FALSE. The atom needed the right NODE KIND. R311y461 read the client-token plane in router_forward.rs, pointed real zenoh-pico CLIs at a --peer node, measured zero deliveries on both the CURRENT dump and the FUTURE push, and concluded the behaviour was absent. But --peer constructs a LinkstateForwarder (runner.rs:2465) which has no client-token plane at all; the plane belongs to RouterForwarder, which ONLY run_router_hat_until constructs (runner.rs:3602). Against a --router-hat node the same fixture is a clean discriminator: pico A declares a token, gated on its own banner so it provably pre-exists, then pico B subscribes with -h and is replayed a token it never saw declared -- history ON 1 1 1 1 1, history OFF 0 0 0 0 0 over five runs per arm, and the sample carries A exact literal while B asked with a wildcard. EXACTLY ONE sample, never two, is itself the evidence the precondition is owned, because a token pre-dating the subscriber session is neither proactively pushed to it nor sitting in pico own cache -- the two confounds that made y461 acceptor topology flaky and overlapping. RED binds to the atom own code: damaging ONLY the client_tokens fold makes the history arm fail while the twin still passes, with the rebuild visible. Two hypotheses y461 left open are each refuted by their own measurement rather than by the fix working -- the face tier IS Client (the new whatami log says so) and the keyexpr resolution was never involved (the pre-existing unit fixture uses the same inline form pico emits). The unit layer was intact throughout, which is what pointed the bisect outward at the vehicle instead of inward at the logic; two arms it never covered -- CURRENT+FUTURE and a wildcard target, the two dimensions the real pico case uses -- are now covered and passed first try. A4 moves proven 99 -> 100, unproven 21 -> 20, and the AP+pico core remainder drops 7 -> 6.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/{session_open.rs,accept_loop.rs} + crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the face-lifecycle observability gap that made this defect undiagnosable is closed. A new `SessionOpened::peer_whatami()` returns Option<WhatAmI> through the WhatAmI::from_wire SSOT; `Face` gains `peer_whatami` beside `peer_zid` (the two inputs the routing boundary classifies a face by); the demo's face-UP line prints it. `None` is kept DISTINCT from Some(Peer) on purpose -- the routing boundary defaults an unclassifiable face to Peer, but for an observer "the role never arrived" and "the peer said peer" are different facts, and conflating them is what makes a face that silently routes nothing look like one that correctly routes nothing.

THE SAMPLE CARRIES pico A's EXACT LITERAL, not an echo of the request: ">> [LivelinessSubscriber] New alive token ('group1/pico-token')" while B asked with the WILDCARD 'group1/**'. A wildcard request cannot produce that string except by a real intersect against a real declaration.

RED PROVED AGAINST THE ATOM'S OWN CODE, WITH THE REBUILD VISIBLE. THE ROOT CAUSE OF R311y461's WRONG CONCLUSION, ESTABLISHED BY READ THEN CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT. `--peer` constructs a LinkstateForwarder (wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs:2465) which has NO client-token plane -- its only two mentions of one are COMMENTS pointing at the router's. The whole plane belongs to RouterForwarder, which ONLY run_router_hat_until constructs (runner.rs:3602), and whose banner says so out loud: "dual-tier RouterForwarder". So R311y461's 0-of-5 was correct behaviour for the node it pointed pico at.

TWO HYPOTHESES R311y461 LEFT OPEN ARE BOTH REFUTED, each by its own measurement rather than by the fix working. (a) FACE TIER: the new whatami log reads `whatami Some(Client)` for BOTH pico faces, and register() inserts a Client-tier face into `faces` with no plane (:5297), so is_client_face is TRUE -- tier was never the problem. What was wrong was not the measurement but the VEHICLE: I read a plane in router_forward.rs and then measured a node whose run-mode constructs a different forwarder entirely. Frozen ledger keeps y461 as written; this is the correcting record.

THE HABIT THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: a capability plane belongs to a TYPE, and the run-mode picks which type is constructed. Before grading a plane's behaviour end-to-end, read which forwarder/engine the mode under test instantiates -- `grep "XForwarder::new"` against the run-mode fn -- not merely whether the FEATURE is compiled in. y461 checked the feature (and even rebuilt to prove the feature added code, 29.7 -> 31.3MB) and still tested the wrong object. A feature being present does not mean the code path is reachable in that mode.

THE OBSERVABILITY GAP THAT MADE IT EXPENSIVE IS CLOSED, and the shape is worth keeping: `Face` carried peer_zid but not the peer's ROLE, and the role is what decides the tier that gates the CLIENT-only token/subscriber dump and future-push. So a face that routes nothing was indistinguishable from one that routes correctly, and RUST_LOG=trace printed nothing about it (180 lines, no token or interest entry). When a diagnosis stalls because a decision input is not observable, add the input to the event -- that is not scaffolding, it is the missing half of an existing log line.

STILL OPEN ON THIS ATOM, and NOT witnessed by this round: the `--peer` / LinkstateForwarder node has no client-token plane at all. Whether that is correct (a linkstate peer converges tokens by flood, not by client replay) or a real gap is UNDECIDED here -- I did not read zenoh's p2p_peer hat to settle it, and the honest state is that only the router-hat node is witnessed. If a wz `--peer` is ever expected to serve a foreign liveliness history subscriber, that is a separate question with a separate answer.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: THE CORRECTION R311y461 NEEDS, STATED PLAINLY: its central claim -- that liveliness-historical-samples "needs CODE, not a witness" -- is FALSE. The atom is now PROVEN by a foreign witness with no production change to the plane at all. What was wrong was not the measurement but the VEHICLE: I read a plane in router_forward.rs and then measured a node whose run-mode constructs a different forwarder entirely. Frozen ledger keeps y461 as written; this is the correcting record.

THE HABIT THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: a capability plane belongs to a TYPE, and the run-mode picks which type is constructed. Before grading a plane's behaviour end-to-end, read which forwarder/engine the mode under test instantiates -- `grep "XForwarder::new"` against the run-mode fn -- not merely whether the FEATURE is compiled in. y461 checked the feature (and even rebuilt to prove the feature added code, 29.7 -> 31.3MB) and still tested the wrong object. A feature being present does not mean the code path is reachable in that mode.

THE OBSERVABILITY GAP THAT MADE IT EXPENSIVE IS CLOSED, and the shape is worth keeping: `Face` carried peer_zid but not the peer's ROLE, and the role is what decides the tier that gates the CLIENT-only token/subscriber dump and future-push. So a face that routes nothing was indistinguishable from one that routes correctly, and RUST_LOG=trace printed nothing about it (180 lines, no token or interest entry). When a diagnosis stalls because a decision input is not observable, add the input to the event -- that is not scaffolding, it is the missing half of an existing log line.

STILL OPEN ON THIS ATOM, and NOT witnessed by this round: the `--peer` / LinkstateForwarder node has no client-token plane at all. Whether that is correct (a linkstate peer converges tokens by flood, not by client replay) or a real gap is UNDECIDED here -- I did not read zenoh's p2p_peer hat to settle it, and the honest state is that only the router-hat node is witnessed. If a wz `--peer` is ever expected to serve a foreign liveliness history subscriber, that is a separate question with a separate answer.
