THE AP+pico CORE REMAINDER IS 6, not 7: locator-serial, session-extqos, session-extshm, storage-history, transport-multilink, transport-shm. `locator-serial` is the last one still carrying an untested FOUNDATIONAL/witness-only label, and this round is a direct warning about trusting that label -- the sibling atom carrying it turned out to be witnessable once the right node kind was used.

Round 311y464.decision_summary: R311y464 -- the hosted verdict for bf240427 is FAILURE, and both reds are R311y463 regressions of mine rather than anything the four rounds claimed. 12 of 14 jobs are green, and the three things at risk were each confirmed from their OWN log line: R311y462 pin is hosted-verified (the validate+codegen job ran install-mnemosyne-cli.sh and validated with no pins-Mnemosyne refusal, so CI installed a886cd0f and parsed the new key), R311y461 preset is confirmed (C4 wz preset-ap-full OK), and R311y463 witness RAN rather than SKIP-greened past its two foreign-binary guards (the Running tests/... compile line plus Layer E7 pass in 21s). The first red is a COUNT GUARD: C1ay pins six separate counts on router_forward and y463 added two cfg(routing-token-tables) unit tests, so exactly the one arm whose feature set includes them moved, 171 to 173. y463 ran the lane that OWNS its new e2e leg and never ran the lane that COUNTS the module it added to. The second red is a NEEDLE CONTRACT: y463 appended whatami after the zid in the face-UP log, stranding all FOUR wz_peer tests in wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs, whose two barriers constrain that group from both sides -- one wants the closing paren as the zid right delimiter, the other wants peer and zid adjacent -- so no position inside the parens satisfies both. Measured in two steps: the obvious middle position fixed three of four and still stranded the fourth; appending OUTSIDE the group strands none. My first fix loosened the needle instead and was reverted once its purpose was read: that paren is what stops zid ff matching zid ffab, so loosening would have traded a visible break for a permanently weaker test. The diagnosis came from a panic that contradicted its own captured log -- the barrier said no link-state arrived while the stderr in the same message showed it arriving -- which is the signature of a stranded needle rather than a behaviour change. Both previously-red lanes now pass locally, C1ay in 87s and Z in 312s with zenohd present.

verification_bullets: THE HOSTED VERDICT FOR bf240427, READ LANE BY LANE: run 30549632737 = FAILURE, but 12 of 14 jobs SUCCESS and both failures are R311y463 regressions of mine -- a count guard I did not move and a log-string contract I broke. (2) R311y461's preset addition is confirmed: `C4 wz preset-ap-full OK`. (3) R311y463's witness RAN and was not a SKIP despite its two foreign-binary guards: "Running tests/wz_router_hat_liveliness_history_pico_interop.rs (target/debug/deps/...)" followed by "Layer E7 pass (21s)".

FAILURE 1, C1ay, diagnosed from the gate's own message: "expected exactly 171 passed from cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --features routing-router-hat,routing-token-tables --lib router_forward -- no libtest summary matched". The run printed 173. Fixed and re-measured with the guard's EXACT command: "173 passed". Full lane: Layer C1ay pass (87s), all six guards green.

FAILURE 2, Layer Z, was ALL FOUR wz_peer_* tests in wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs, not the one my first truncated grep showed -- the full failing-test list was enumerated before diagnosing. Reproduced locally against the Z-lane binary: 3 failed on the first attempt, 7 pass now.

THE DIAGNOSIS WAS DRIVEN BY A LOG THAT CONTRADICTED ITS OWN BARRIER: the panic said "wz peer never ingested a link-state within 20s" while the captured stderr in the SAME message contained "ingested neighbour link-state (4 so far)". An event that demonstrably happened and a barrier that did not fire is a stranded needle, not a behaviour change -- that is what pointed at the log line instead of at the gossip policy.

THE INSERTION POINT WAS FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, IN TWO STEPS, and the intermediate result is the interesting one: moving whatami BETWEEN peer and zid fixed THREE of the four and still stranded the fourth, because face_needle needs those two adjacent while settle_needle only needs the closing paren. Appending after the group strands none: 7 passed, 2.55s.

THE CONSUMER SET WAS ENUMERATED, not assumed. Exactly two needles anchor on that group, both in the gossip file (:310 and :357). wz_peer_mesh.rs's needles are the PREFIX "peer: face 0 UP" / "face 1 UP" and stop before the parenthesis, so they were never at risk -- confirmed by running Layer E6 (pass) rather than by reading them alone.

EVERY LANE THAT CONSUMES THE CHANGED LINE OR THE CHANGED COUNT PASSES LOCALLY: C1ay pass (87s), E7 pass, E6 pass, and the previously-red Z pass (312s) with zenohd present. bash -n scripts/run-ci.sh clean; cargo fmt --check clean.
carry_forward_bullets: RUNNING THE LANE THAT OWNS YOUR NEW TEST IS NOT ENOUGH -- ALSO RUN THE LANES THAT COUNT WHAT YOU TOUCHED. R311y463 added two unit tests to router_forward and ran Layer E7, the lane that owns the new e2e leg. It never ran C1ay, which pins SIX separate guarded counts on that same module. The rule that would have caught it: after adding a test, grep run-ci.sh for the module/file name and run every lane that names it, not just the lane the round is about. `grep -n "_runci_guarded_test" scripts/run-ci.sh | grep <module>` is the whole check.

A LOG LINE CAN BE A NEEDLE CONTRACT CONSTRAINED FROM BOTH SIDES, and appending to it is not the safe default it looks like. Here `(peer

, zid )` was pinned by two barriers with DIFFERENT shapes -- one needing the closing paren as the zid's right delimiter, one needing peer and zid adjacent -- so every position inside the parens stranded at least one. Before inserting a field into a logged line, enumerate its needles (`grep` the surrounding literal, not just the field name) and prefer appending OUTSIDE the anchored group. The two-step measurement here is the proof that reasoning about it is not enough: the "obviously safe" middle position still broke one of four.

A BRITTLE-LOOKING ASSERTION MAY BE LOAD-BEARING; READ ITS PURPOSE BEFORE LOOSENING IT. My first fix dropped face_needle's trailing paren to make it tolerate new fields. That paren is the zid's RIGHT DELIMITER -- without it `zid ff` matches `zid ffab...` too -- so loosening would have quietly traded a compile-time-visible break for a permanently weaker test. The file's own comment said so and I had to go read it. Reverted; the fix moved to the log site.

I SAW THE BROKEN CONSUMER AND WALKED PAST IT. While placing the y463 log change I grepped "UP (peer" and the output included wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs:357 -- the exact needle I was about to strand -- and I read it as a hit about the demo rather than a consumer of the line I was editing. A grep result is not read until its RELATION to the edit is stated. This cost a hosted red.

STILL OPEN, unchanged by this hotfix: the `--peer` / LinkstateForwarder node has no client-token plane (UNDECIDED whether that is correct); the FUTURE push path is unwitnessed foreign-side; and the mnemosyne follow-up notice (R872) reports that the pin has nothing to DELEGATE to on this machine -- `~/.local/mn/` lacks a886cd0f because install-mnemosyne-cli.sh installs only to the shared ~/.cargo/bin slot. That gap fails LOUD with an exact recovery command, so it is safe, and closing it means ADDING a per-rev root install (never replacing --force with --root: three sites resolve mnemosyne-cli through `command -v` and two of them hard-FAIL on absence).

On this machine the shared slot moved twice in one day, so that is a routine case. THE SHARED SLOT IS UNTOUCHED, which is the half that could have broken everything: `verify-mnemosyne-pin: OK -- /home/coin/.cargo/bin/mnemosyne-cli reads schema 44, matching MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA`, i.e. the gate still grades the `command -v` binary and still finds it. A REAL BUG IN MY OWN SELF-CHECK WAS FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE SHIPPING, and it is worth recording because it is the hollow-gate shape: the prefix test is a `case` pattern built from the stamp, and an EMPTY stamp collapses `"$_mn_stamp"*` to `*`, which matches anything -- so an unreadable `--version` would have printed "pin root ready" and passed. Round 311y466.decision_summary: R311y466 -- locator-serial is PROVEN cross-impl (A4 100->101), and the thing that had kept it unproven was a paragraph, not a gap. tests/layer3_serial_framing.rs asserted that zenoh-pico has no unix serial LINK backend and that a live pico serial process is therefore impossible; that was true when written and is false at this pin -- upstream MOVED the backend out of src/system/plat/ into src/link/transport/serial/tty_posix.c, so the directory the paragraph tells you to check keeps coming back empty and keeps confirming itself. Turning the feature on then exposed a second, sharper trap: -DZ_FEATURE_LINK_SERIAL=ON compiles tty_posix.c into the build AND removes the entire serial link from the binary, because the cache string is substituted verbatim into config.h while every consumer guards on == 1, and ON is 0 in preprocessor arithmetic. The build log shows the file compiling either way. Measured, not reasoned: with ON, strace shows pico never opens the device; with =1 it writes the INIT frame. Roles were then forced by pico rather than chosen -- pico implements only the CONNECT half of the serial-link handshake and never emits ACK, so pico is Initiator and wz Responder, and a first draft that spawned pico after accept_serial deadlocked because accept_serial already drives that handshake. The witness binds the atom OWN code: wz opens its tty from the parse, and with the split damaged AND the parse assertions bypassed the run still reds at accept_serial, so the grammar is load-bearing for the LINK. That same damage reds locator.rs::parses_serial_device, which already pinned the split, so the discriminator drafted here was redundant and was deleted instead of kept. That Layer E runs the test was established by falsification -- quiet prints no name on pass, so the assertion was damaged until the lane went red naming it.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_serial_link_to_wz_acceptor.rs (NEW): a real zenoh-pico z_pub client opens a SERIAL link against a wz acceptor over a PTY and delivers a Put. Both stacks are handed a `serial/<device>#baudrate=115200` string; wz's side is opened FROM the parse (`parse_any_locator` -> `AnyLocator::Serial` -> `accept_serial`), so the grammar is load-bearing for the link rather than merely asserted next to it.

scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh: `-DZ_FEATURE_LINK_SERIAL=1`. THE VALUE IS THE FINDING. The cache entry is a CMake STRING substituted VERBATIM into the generated `zenoh-pico/config.h`, while every consumer guards on `#if Z_FEATURE_LINK_SERIAL == 1`. `ON` is an undefined identifier in preprocessor arithmetic, so it is 0 and the serial link vanishes from the binary WHILE THE BUILD LOG STILL SHOWS tty_posix.c compiling -- the file is in the source list, its contents are inside the guard. The sibling `Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API=ON` is safe only because its consumers use `#ifdef`.

crates/wz-integration-tests/Cargo.toml: the wz-runtime-tokio `transport-link-serial` dev-dep pin is back, for a DIFFERENT reason than the R311nx pin R311ny correctly removed -- that one was a cross-crate gate-skew workaround; this is a BACKEND requirement (`accept_serial` exists only under the feature). Plus `tokio-serial` for the pty fixture.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_serial_framing.rs: a CORRECTION block above the paragraph asserting "zenoh-pico has NO unix serial LINK backend ... a live external pico unix process cannot open a serial link". False at this pin, and load-bearing wrong: it is why the live shape went unattempted. The paragraph is left intact beneath it (its NEXT sentence, that the codec functions are platform-independent, is still true and is still why that test needs no link).
NOT CHANGED: the `locator-serial` inventory entry. A4's own design puts the proof claim in the test, not in `reason` -- so a proof round moves the A4 count and touches no inventory row.
verification_bullets: A4 MOVED: proven 100 -> 101, unproven 20 -> 19, `locator-serial` gone from the actionable list; `cross-impl proof audit OK`. A3 unchanged at 86 EXACT / UNAUDITED 0, as a proof round should leave it.

THE PROOF IS A REAL LINK, NOT A PARSE ASSERTION. Measured at the wire before wz was involved: with the feature at `ON`, strace shows pico never `openat`s the device at all and prints "Unable to open session!"; with `=1` it writes `020101010101010100`, which COBS-decodes to `01 0000 00000000` -- header `_Z_FLAG_SERIAL_INIT`, len 0, crc32 0. A python stand-in that answered a hand-built INIT|ACK then received pico's InitSyn confirmed the two-pty bridge before any Rust was written.

DAMAGE-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (1) With `parse_serial_locator` changed to leave the `#` tail on the address, the e2e reds. (2) With that damage AND this file's parse assertions BYPASSED, it still reds -- at `accept_serial`, on `Device("/dev/pts/N#baudrate=115200")`. So the split is load-bearing for the LINK, not just for an adjacent assert. (3) The same damage reds `wz-session-core/src/locator.rs::parses_serial_device`, which already pinned the split -- so the discriminator drafted here was redundant and was REMOVED rather than kept as duplicate coverage.

THE LANE REALLY RUNS IT, established by falsification rather than inference. Layer E's filter list contains the fn (50 tests, mine among them), but `--quiet` prints no name on PASS, so a green lane is not evidence. Damaged the assertion to an impossible value: `Layer E FAIL (rc=101)` naming `pico_serial_client_establishes_and_publishes_to_wz_acceptor`. Restored: `Layer E pass (57s)`.

ROLES WERE FORCED, NOT CHOSEN, and reading pico settled it before a line was written: `_z_connect_serial` sends INIT and loops for INIT|ACK, while `_z_serial_protocol_listen` opens the tty and returns -- nothing in pico ever EMITS `_Z_FLAG_SERIAL_ACK`. So pico must be link-Initiator and wz link-Responder. A first draft that spawned pico AFTER `accept_serial` deadlocked, because `accept_serial` already drives the Responder handshake internally.

LANES: C0 pass (it caught the non-ignored `#[test]` in a binary-dep file -- the gate did its job on this change), C1 pass 93s (the dev-dep feature DOES unify onto the shared wz-runtime-tokio build under --workspace; nothing regressed), C2 pass 33s, Layer 0 pass (`shellcheck OK (20 files)`, `fmt --check OK`), E pass 57s, E2 pass. Three standalone runs of the new test: 3/3 green, 11.11s each -- deterministic.

A CMAKE `ON` IS NOT A `1`, AND THE BUILD LOG WILL NOT TELL YOU. Round 311y469.decision_summary: R311y469 -- wz now implements zenoh full locator canon proto/address[?metadata][#config] on EVERY leaf, closing the residual R311y467 named. Before this round the leaves split only the # config separator -- and the unixsock and unixpipe leaves split nothing at all -- so a canon locator carrying metadata pushed it into the ADDRESS: R311y467 measured pico opening the device from serial/<dev>?meta=x#baudrate=115200 while wz built the device path <dev>?meta=x and failed the open NotFound. One shared split_locator_parts seam, mirroring zenoh address/metadata/config accessors (zenoh-protocol/src/core/endpoint.rs:32-54), now serves all six parse sites: the numeric IP leaf, the DNS-name classifier, serial, unixsock, unixpipe and vsock. Reading the reference to build it forced a second, unplanned correction: accepting-then-ignoring metadata would have INTRODUCED a defect, because zenoh gives the QUIC stream and QUIC datagram links the SAME quic scheme string and separates them by the rel metadata key alone (zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:165-171), so quic/...?rel=0 would have dialed a stream where zenoh dials a datagram. rel is therefore honoured on the quic scheme and ONLY there; prio, and rel on the other schemes, are parsed and explicitly not claimed. A4 moves proven 100 -> 101 and partial 41 -> 40 -- locator-serial is proven -- on the strength of the e2e now driving BOTH shapes against a real zenoh-pico process rather than hardening one, which is precisely the stopping lesson R311y467 recorded.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: new `split_locator_parts` — the ONE seam every leaf now goes through — returns the address / metadata / config spans of a locator body, mirroring zenoh's three accessors (`zenoh-protocol/src/core/endpoint.rs:32-54`, canon `<proto>/<address>[?<metadata>][#<config>]` at :460) and pico's `_z_locator_address_from_string` (`src/link/endpoint.c:110-137`). The address ends at whichever of `?` / `#` comes first; metadata is the span between them; config is everything after the first `#`. It replaces `split_config_tail`, which split only `#`.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: all SIX parse sites moved onto that seam — `parse_locator` (numeric IP), `classify_named_ip` (DNS name), `parse_serial_locator`, `parse_unixsock_locator`, `parse_unixpipe_locator`, `parse_vsock_locator`. The unixsock and unixpipe leaves are the widest fix: they took the whole remainder VERBATIM, so they carried BOTH a `?metadata` and a `#config` tail into the socket / FIFO path — a `#config` hole that predates the metadata one and had not been recorded.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: new `reliability_adjusted_proto` maps the `quic` scheme + `rel=0` onto `Proto::QuicDatagram`. NOT a feature, a defect this round would otherwise have INTRODUCED: zenoh gives both QUIC links the same `"quic"` scheme string (`zenoh-link-quic/src/lib.rs:42` and `zenoh-link-quic_datagram/src/lib.rs:35`) and separates them by `rel` alone (`zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:165-171` via `QuicLocatorInspector::is_reliable`, `quic/src/lib.rs:59-70`), so accepting-then-ignoring metadata would have dialed a STREAM where zenoh dials a DATAGRAM. wz's own distinct `quic-datagram` scheme stays and does not consult `rel`.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: `parse_iface` now reads the CONFIG span only, via a shared `lookup_param` — metadata and config share one `key=value` grammar in zenoh (one `parameters` module serves both, `parameters.rs:32-33`) but are DISTINCT namespaces, so `?iface=eth0` is not a NIC bind.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs tests: +17 — 12 pinning the address/metadata/config cut on every leaf and through `parse_any_locator`, 5 pinning the `rel` mapping. Four are DISCRIMINATORS against a naive fix that cuts on `[?#]` and feeds the whole tail to one parser: `iface` and `baudrate` must NOT be read out of metadata, `rel` must NOT be read out of config, and `rel=0` must not touch a non-quic scheme.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_serial_link_to_wz_acceptor.rs: the e2e is parameterised on the `?metadata` span and now runs TWO arms against a real zenoh-pico process — `pico_serial_client_establishes_and_publishes_to_wz_acceptor` (no metadata) and `pico_serial_client_establishes_over_a_metadata_bearing_locator` (the shape R311y467 measured as divergent). The `#baudrate=` config span is built identically from BAUDRATE in both, so the metadata span is the ONLY variable. The `locator-serial pico->wz` claim drops `partial` on both; `transport-link-serial pico->wz partial` is untouched, its partiality being a separate matter that R311y467 did not touch either.

Before this round the leaves split only the # config separator -- and the unixsock and unixpipe leaves split nothing at all -- so a canon locator carrying metadata pushed it into the ADDRESS: R311y467 measured pico opening the device from serial/<dev>?meta=x#baudrate=115200 while wz built the device path <dev>?meta=x and failed the open NotFound. One shared split_locator_parts seam, mirroring zenoh address/metadata/config accessors (zenoh-protocol/src/core/endpoint.rs:32-54), now serves all six parse sites: the numeric IP leaf, the DNS-name classifier, serial, unixsock, unixpipe and vsock. Reading the reference to build it forced a second, unplanned correction: accepting-then-ignoring metadata would have INTRODUCED a defect, because zenoh gives the QUIC stream and QUIC datagram links the SAME quic scheme string and separates them by the rel metadata key alone (zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:165-171), so quic/...?rel=0 would have dialed a stream where zenoh dials a datagram. rel is therefore honoured on the quic scheme and ONLY there; prio, and rel on the other schemes, are parsed and explicitly not claimed. A4 moves proven 100 -> 101 and partial 41 -> 40 -- locator-serial is proven -- on the strength of the e2e now driving BOTH shapes against a real zenoh-pico process rather than hardening one, which is precisely the stopping lesson R311y467 recorded.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: new `split_locator_parts` — the ONE seam every leaf now goes through — returns the address / metadata / config spans of a locator body, mirroring zenoh's three accessors (`zenoh-protocol/src/core/endpoint.rs:32-54`, canon `<proto>/<address>[?<metadata>][#<config>]` at :460) and pico's `_z_locator_address_from_string` (`src/link/endpoint.c:110-137`). The address ends at whichever of `?` / `#` comes first; metadata is the span between them; config is everything after the first `#`. It replaces `split_config_tail`, which split only `#`.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: all SIX parse sites moved onto that seam — `parse_locator` (numeric IP), `classify_named_ip` (DNS name), `parse_serial_locator`, `parse_unixsock_locator`, `parse_unixpipe_locator`, `parse_vsock_locator`. The unixsock and unixpipe leaves are the widest fix: they took the whole remainder VERBATIM, so they carried BOTH a `?metadata` and a `#config` tail into the socket / FIFO path — a `#config` hole that predates the metadata one and had not been recorded.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: new `reliability_adjusted_proto` maps the `quic` scheme + `rel=0` onto `Proto::QuicDatagram`. NOT a feature, a defect this round would otherwise have INTRODUCED: zenoh gives both QUIC links the same `"quic"` scheme string (`zenoh-link-quic/src/lib.rs:42` and `zenoh-link-quic_datagram/src/lib.rs:35`) and separates them by `rel` alone (`zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:165-171` via `QuicLocatorInspector::is_reliable`, `quic/src/lib.rs:59-70`), so accepting-then-ignoring metadata would have dialed a STREAM where zenoh dials a DATAGRAM. wz's own distinct `quic-datagram` scheme stays and does not consult `rel`.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: `parse_iface` now reads the CONFIG span only, via a shared `lookup_param` — metadata and config share one `key=value` grammar in zenoh (one `parameters` module serves both, `parameters.rs:32-33`) but are DISTINCT namespaces, so `?iface=eth0` is not a NIC bind.

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs tests: +17 — 12 pinning the address/metadata/config cut on every leaf and through `parse_any_locator`, 5 pinning the `rel` mapping. Four are DISCRIMINATORS against a naive fix that cuts on `[?#]` and feeds the whole tail to one parser: `iface` and `baudrate` must NOT be read out of metadata, `rel` must NOT be read out of config, and `rel=0` must not touch a non-quic scheme.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_serial_link_to_wz_acceptor.rs: the e2e is parameterised on the `?metadata` span and now runs TWO arms against a real zenoh-pico process — `pico_serial_client_establishes_and_publishes_to_wz_acceptor` (no metadata) and `pico_serial_client_establishes_over_a_metadata_bearing_locator` (the shape R311y467 measured as divergent). The `#baudrate=` config span is built identically from BAUDRATE in both, so the metadata span is the ONLY variable. The `locator-serial pico->wz` claim drops `partial` on both; `transport-link-serial pico->wz partial` is untouched, its partiality being a separate matter that R311y467 did not touch either.

The 12th (`serial_leaf_does_not_read_baudrate_out_of_metadata`) passed BEFORE and after by design: it is a discriminator, green for the wrong reason pre-fix and for the right one after. 65 locator tests pass after; the full crate is 251 pass / 0 fail.

THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING was not the one it set out to fix. Reading the reference to implement the split surfaced that accepting-then-ignoring metadata would have INTRODUCED a defect: zenoh gives the QUIC stream and datagram links the same `"quic"` scheme and separates them by `rel` alone, so `quic/...?rel=0` would have dialed a stream. The general lesson: "parse it and ignore it" is a CLAIM about every key in the vocabulary, and it has to be checked key by key against what the reference DOES with them, not assumed from the fact that the key is unfamiliar.

STILL NOT HONOURED, deliberately and named so no future round mistakes silence for support: `prio` (priority-range link selection, `endpoint.rs:464-470`) belongs to `transport-multilink`, which is UNPROVEN; `rel` on the non-quic schemes belongs to the reliability axis. Both are parsed into the metadata span and dropped. Neither is claimed anywhere in code, tests or inventory.

DELIBERATE LENIENCY, recorded rather than hidden: on the NON-canon order (`#` before `?`) zenoh's own `metadata()` would panic on a reversed slice and its `EndPoint::try_from` rejects the string outright (`endpoint.rs:626-630`); wz returns an empty metadata span instead. `address` and `config` still equal zenoh's accessors byte-for-byte on every string zenoh accepts. Making wz REJECT that order would need a new variant on five public error enums, which buys no interop and was not taken.

NEXT, unchanged by this round: the 19 unproven, of which the AP+pico core-11 still holds 5 — `session-extqos`, `session-extshm`, `storage-history`, `transport-multilink`, `transport-shm`. The FOUNDATIONAL / witness-only label list is exhausted, so each of those needs CODE. `session-extshm` remains wire-incompatible with zenoh, i.e. a design decision to reopen rather than a build.

Round 311y471.decision_summary: R311y471 -- the foreign witness R311y470 was carrying as a named gap. y470 fixed WHAT wz advertises; nothing proved a foreign stack could dial it, and the existing unixsock leg could not, because it writes unixsock-stream/<path> into BOTH wz --listen and zenohd -e, so the two sides agree by construction and pass identically before and after the fix. The new leg reads the locator wz LOGGED for itself and hands that string verbatim to a real zenohd. That required making the advertise path observable at all: run_peer and run_router_hat now log ADVERTISED SELF LOCATOR, a new needle, and the absence of any such line is exactly why y470 two undialable schemes survived unnoticed. Damage confirms the leg is load-bearing and harder than expected -- with the pre-y470 rendering restored, zenohd does not merely fail to connect, it EXITS 255 on the unknown scheme before accepting. Registered in Layer Z beside the acceptor leg, with routing-peer added to that lane demo build since run_peer is the only advertise seam and it is gated. Two of my own harness errors were caught by measuring: wait_for_substring returns the buffer from the needle onward rather than one line, and --peer is a MESH mode that logs face N UP, never session Established -- the run had been failing for 15s against a link that was in fact up. A4 counts do NOT move (proven=101 partial=40 unproven=19) and that is correct: locator-unixsock was already proven by the acceptor leg, so this adds a distinct guard to a green atom rather than a grade. The quic-datagram arm of y470 stays unwitnessed and is carried as such.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: `run_peer` and `run_router_hat` now log `wz-ap-demo: ADVERTISED SELF LOCATOR <locator>` for each advertised dial locator. A NEW needle, so no pinned consumer moves. This is the enabling change, not a cosmetic one: until now the advertised string was reachable only through an adminspace query, which is precisely why R311y470's two undialable schemes survived — no e2e could see what wz actually put on the wire.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_advertised_locator_zenohd_dial.rs (NEW): a real zenohd dials the locator wz CHOSE, not one the test composed. wz runs `--peer unixsock-stream/<path>` (the mode that takes the advertise path), the test reads the needle above, and hands that string VERBATIM to zenohd's `-e`. Claims `locator-unixsock zenohd->wz` — direction by the corpus convention of who DIALS, matching the `*_acceptor_zenohd_interop` legs.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the new leg is registered in Layer Z immediately after `wz_unixsock_acceptor_zenohd_interop`, with a comment recording why it is NOT a duplicate of it. `routing-peer` is added to Layer Z's `wz-ap-demo` build (kept on ONE line — `feature_closure.py`'s scraper cannot cross a newline): `run_peer` is this crate's only advertise seam and it is `routing-peer`-gated. Additive, since no other Z leg passes `--peer`.
NO change to the fix itself. R311y470's `advertised_locator` is untouched; this round only makes its output observable and puts a foreign stack on the other end of it.
verification_bullets: THE WITNESS IS LOAD-BEARING, MEASURED BY DAMAGE: with `advertised_locator` reverted to the pre-R311y470 body and wz-ap-demo REBUILT, the leg reds — and harder than expected. zenohd does not merely fail to connect: handed `unixsock//tmp/<...>.sock` it EXITS 255 before accepting ("process exited before accepting on 127.0.0.1:42443"), which is zenoh's unknown-scheme `bail!` (`io/zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:183`). Damage reverted; tree re-verified clean of scaffolds.

THE LEG RUNS IN ITS LANE, read off the run rather than inferred: full Layer Z pass (306s) and its log shows `Running tests/wz_advertised_locator_zenohd_dial.rs` -> `running 1 test` -> `1 passed`. Registered-but-skipped was the specific failure mode checked for.

TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS WERE CAUGHT BY MEASURING RATHER THAN ASSUMING, and both would have produced a false verdict. (1) `wait_for_substring` returns the captured buffer from the needle ONWARD, not one line, so the first extraction carried three later log lines into the "locator"; the assertion caught it and the fix cuts at the first newline. (2) The readiness needle was `session Established`, which `--peer` never logs — it is a MESH mode and logs `face N UP`. The run had been failing for 15s on a link that was in fact UP; a manual reproduction showed `face 0 UP (peer <anonymous unixsock peer>, zid 8ccd…) whatami Some(Router)` plus `ingested neighbour link-state`, i.e. real traffic over the link. The assertion now also requires the face line to name the unixsock peer, so a face from another transport cannot pass.

A ~0.10s GREEN WAS NOT ACCEPTED ON ITS FACE. It looked impossible for spawn + bind + dial, so it was chased: process polling during the run confirmed both a `wz-ap-demo --peer` and an extra `zenohd` really start, and the 9-second gap seen in the manual reproduction turned out to be the latency between two hand-issued commands, not the software. Everything here is loopback AF_UNIX against a release zenohd, so ~100ms is real.

A4 accepts the claim: corpus 125 -> 126 files, 260 -> 262 tests, zenohd class 8 -> 9, `cross-impl proof audit OK`. The COUNTS DO NOT MOVE (proven=101 partial=40 unproven=19) and that is the honest outcome: `locator-unixsock` was already proven by the existing acceptor leg, so this round adds a distinct GUARD to an atom that was already green, not a new atom grade.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_advertised_locator_zenohd_dial.rs (NEW): a real zenohd dials the locator wz CHOSE, not one the test composed. wz runs `--peer unixsock-stream/<path>` (the mode that takes the advertise path), the test reads the needle above, and hands that string VERBATIM to zenohd's `-e`. Claims `locator-unixsock zenohd->wz` — direction by the corpus convention of who DIALS, matching the `*_acceptor_zenohd_interop` legs.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the new leg is registered in Layer Z immediately after `wz_unixsock_acceptor_zenohd_interop`, with a comment recording why it is NOT a duplicate of it. `routing-peer` is added to Layer Z's `wz-ap-demo` build (kept on ONE line — `feature_closure.py`'s scraper cannot cross a newline): `run_peer` is this crate's only advertise seam and it is `routing-peer`-gated. Additive, since no other Z leg passes `--peer`.
NO change to the fix itself. R311y470's `advertised_locator` is untouched; this round only makes its output observable and puts a foreign stack on the other end of it.
publishable_verification_bullets: THE WITNESS IS LOAD-BEARING, MEASURED BY DAMAGE: with `advertised_locator` reverted to the pre-R311y470 body and wz-ap-demo REBUILT, the leg reds — and harder than expected. zenohd does not merely fail to connect: handed `unixsock//tmp/<...>.sock` it EXITS 255 before accepting ("process exited before accepting on 127.0.0.1:42443"), which is zenoh's unknown-scheme `bail!` (`io/zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:183`). Damage reverted; tree re-verified clean of scaffolds.

THE LEG RUNS IN ITS LANE, read off the run rather than inferred: full Layer Z pass (306s) and its log shows `Running tests/wz_advertised_locator_zenohd_dial.rs` -> `running 1 test` -> `1 passed`. Registered-but-skipped was the specific failure mode checked for.

TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS WERE CAUGHT BY MEASURING RATHER THAN ASSUMING, and both would have produced a false verdict. (1) `wait_for_substring` returns the captured buffer from the needle ONWARD, not one line, so the first extraction carried three later log lines into the "locator"; the assertion caught it and the fix cuts at the first newline. (2) The readiness needle was `session Established`, which `--peer` never logs — it is a MESH mode and logs `face N UP`. The run had been failing for 15s on a link that was in fact UP; a manual reproduction showed `face 0 UP (peer <anonymous unixsock peer>, zid 8ccd…) whatami Some(Router)` plus `ingested neighbour link-state`, i.e. real traffic over the link. The assertion now also requires the face line to name the unixsock peer, so a face from another transport cannot pass.

A ~0.10s GREEN WAS NOT ACCEPTED ON ITS FACE. It looked impossible for spawn + bind + dial, so it was chased: process polling during the run confirmed both a `wz-ap-demo --peer` and an extra `zenohd` really start, and the 9-second gap seen in the manual reproduction turned out to be the latency between two hand-issued commands, not the software. Everything here is loopback AF_UNIX against a release zenohd, so ~100ms is real.

A4 accepts the claim: corpus 125 -> 126 files, 260 -> 262 tests, zenohd class 8 -> 9, `cross-impl proof audit OK`. The COUNTS DO NOT MOVE (proven=101 partial=40 unproven=19) and that is the honest outcome: `locator-unixsock` was already proven by the existing acceptor leg, so this round adds a distinct GUARD to an atom that was already green, not a new atom grade.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, Layer C0 pass, Layer C2 pass, Layer Z pass (306s). A3 unchanged (atoms=213 active=130, REMAINING WORK 86 EXACT). validate_workspace T1 orphan 14 new=+0, entries=1482; citation-gate coverage 1904 -> 1905 sources scanned, 0 unscanned (the new test file).

Layer C2 FAILED once on the new test (`unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` on a `bool::then` closure) and was fixed by simplifying the expression to `advertised.as_deref().filter(|_| bound)`, not by an allow. A stale line in the new file's module doc — the diagram still said `session Established` after the needle changed — was corrected in the same pass.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311y469 -> y470 -> y471 is one arc and it is now closed on the unixsock arm: READ the canon (y469), WRITE it (y470), and have a FOREIGN stack dial what we wrote (y471). The advertise path is observable for the first time (`ADVERTISED SELF LOCATOR` in run_peer / run_router_hat), which is what made the witness possible at all.

STILL UNWITNESSED, and named precisely so it is not read as done: the `quic-datagram` arm of R311y470. Its correction is pinned by a unit test (string + wz-side round-trip) but no foreign stack dials it, because that needs cert threading on both ends AND a zenohd variant build. The cheap unixsock arm was taken first on purpose.

THE STRUCTURAL LESSON, which generalises past locators: an interop test that composes the same string for BOTH sides proves the LINK and says nothing about either side's CHOICE. `wz_unixsock_acceptor_zenohd_interop` passes identically before and after R311y470 for exactly that reason. When the thing under test is a value one side DERIVES, the test must read it from that side, not restate it.

ALSO STILL OPEN on the advertise path, pre-existing and untouched: an unspecified IP bind (0.0.0.0 / [::]) advertises NOTHING where zenoh expands it to the host's concrete interface addresses (`io/zenoh-link-commons/src/listener.rs:115-145`). The warn log says so. Separate gap from the scheme one.

Round 311y472.decision_summary: R311y472 -- transport-multilink is A4-PROVEN, and the atom's own reason had named the gap: S4, only wz<->wz aggregation e2e exist, no wz<->zenohd byte interop. The whole C1ba behavioural lane is wz<->wz, so nothing had ever put a foreign stack on the other end of the 0x4 MultiLink establishment envelope. A --max-links 2 wz linkstate peer now dials ONE zenohd twice and the verdict is read off ZENOH'S OWN adminspace: a second wz process GETs @/*/router and the leg asserts that the session object whose peer is wz's pinned zid carries TWO links. wz's own 'link AGGREGATED' log is explicitly NOT the proof -- it is wz arithmetic over wz's session table and would print identically over a garbage wire the router tolerated. The sharpest finding is about assertion ORDER, not about multilink: the first draft asserted the wz-side JOIN line BEFORE zenoh's count, and under the ext-id damage wz CORRECTLY declines to claim aggregation, so the local check fired and the foreign one was never evaluated -- the verdict assertion was unreachable under the entire damage space while reading as the careful one. Ordering the foreign assertion first is what made the damage land on it. Layer C0 rejected the shape twice and was right both times: a binary-dep tests/ file must have every test fn ignored, which would have left the adminspace parser's calibration never running, so the parser moved into the crate lib where its units run in Layer C1; and the module doc explaining that move QUOTED the test attribute, which C0's scanner arms on before binding to the next fn, so my own prose made a helper look like an un-skippable test. A4 moves proven 101 -> 102 and unproven 19 -> 18; the AP+pico core-unproven block is now 4. A3 is UNCHANGED at 86 EXACT and transport-multilink is still in it, correctly: S5 adminspace is untouched, so wz's own adminspace still cannot answer the question this round asked zenoh's.

Claims transport-multilink wz->zenohd -- direction by the corpus convention of who DIALS.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_multilink_aggregation_zenohd_interop.rs: the foreign assertion runs BEFORE the wz-side one, which is a correctness property and not a style choice -- see the verification bullet on the unreachable verdict. The wz JOIN line rides in the failure message instead, and its own assertion follows the verdict to catch the reverse disagreement (zenoh aggregated, wz did not notice).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_multilink_aggregation_zenohd_interop.rs: ships its calibration TWIN in the same file. The SAME argv against a STOCK zenohd (whose transport/unicast/max_links defaults to 1) must see ONE link and NO wz-side JOIN, so the count the leg reads tracks the ROUTER's budget rather than restating wz's. Declared wz-proves: none -- an aggregation that correctly does not happen witnesses no atom.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: parse_zenoh_admin_sessions + ZenohSession -- a STRUCTURAL parse of zenoh's @/<zid>/router body (depth- and string-literal-aware bracket scan), not a substring count. A document-wide count of "dst" reads 2 for TWO SEPARATE single-link sessions, which is exactly the state a refusing router produces and exactly the confusion this leg exists to rule out. It lives in the LIB, not beside its caller, because Layer C0 requires every test fn in a spawning tests/ file to be ignored and an instrument whose calibration never runs is not calibrated; here its units run in the ordinary Layer C1 workspace lane.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: line_with -- select the capture line CARRYING a needle. wait_for_substring returns the WHOLE buffer, so the obvious lines().next() yields the child's startup banner; this is lifted into the lib with its own unit so the next caller does not rediscover it.

crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: spawn_zenohd_multilink_on_ephemeral_tcp(max_links, ..) -- a zenohd whose unicast transport aggregates up to max_links links per peer. No variant build: transport_multilink rides zenoh's DEFAULT feature set, so the STOCK oracle speaks it once configured, like the compression oracle and unlike the unixpipe / vsock ones. Its documented TWIN is the existing spawn_zenohd_on_ephemeral_tcp.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the leg is registered in Layer Z immediately after wz_advertised_locator_zenohd_dial, with the same --test-threads=1 per-zenohd isolation as every other zenohd leg. transport-multilink is added to Layer Z's wz-ap-demo build (kept on ONE line -- feature_closure.py's scraper cannot cross a newline): --max-links is parsed only under that feature, AND A4-5 containment requires a claimed atom to sit inside the closure of the binary the proof drives. Additive: the knob defaults to 1, so every other Z leg dials through an unchanged binary.

Original text preserved verbatim ahead of it.

verification_bullets: THE WITNESS IS ZENOH'S, NOT WZ'S, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. Read off a live zenohd's adminspace during authoring: with transport/unicast/max_links:2 it answers @/*/router with ONE session object for wz's zid carrying TWO links (dst tcp/127.0.0.1:49538 and :49548); with the knob left at its default it answers ONE link for the SAME wz argv, and wz's second dial is refused outright (face N FAILED, retried on backoff). Same wz binary, same flags, different router config -- so the number the leg asserts on tracks zenoh's budget and cannot be a wz-side fiction.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED, AND THE DAMAGE LANDS ON THE VERDICT. With MULTILINK_EXT_ID moved 0x04 -> 0x0A and wz-ap-demo REBUILT, leg 1 reds with zenoh reporting 1 link where 2 was required, while the twin stays green. Damage reverted and both legs re-run green 3/3.

THE FIRST DRAFT'S VERDICT ASSERTION WAS UNREACHABLE, and only measuring found it. It asserted wz's own JOIN log BEFORE zenoh's link count; under the ext-id damage wz correctly DECLINES to claim aggregation, so the wz-side check fired and the zenoh-side one was never evaluated -- i.e. the foreign assertion was decorative under every wire damage available to it. Reordering the foreign assertion FIRST is what made the damage land on it; wz's own claim now rides in the failure message, and a follow-up assertion catches the reverse disagreement (zenoh aggregated, wz did not notice).

TWO OF MY OWN HARNESS DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT BY MEASURING RATHER THAN ASSUMING, and each alone would have produced a false verdict. (1) wait_for_substring returns the WHOLE captured buffer, so lines().next() yielded the peer's startup banner, which was then asserted against as the aggregation line; the extraction now selects the line CARRYING the needle, lifted into the lib as line_with with its own unit. (2) The two dials RACE and the surviving face index is not stable -- the twin came up on face 1 with face 0 FAILED, which a face 0 UP needle reads as a dead node; the needle now names the peer ADDRESS, which also stops a face to some other peer from passing as readiness.

A 0.26s GREEN WAS NOT ACCEPTED ON ITS FACE. It looked impossible for a zenohd spawn plus four wz processes, so it was chased: an attempted process-table sample turned out to be counting its own pgrep command line and was discarded as an instrument, and the leg's dependence on a live router was measured directly instead -- pointed at a stand-in binary it reds in 0.05s with the actionable diagnosis "process exited before announcing its bound tcp listener". Everything here is loopback TCP against a release zenohd with warm page cache, so ~0.3s is real.

LAYER C0 REJECTED THE FIRST SHAPE TWICE, and both rejections were correct. First: a binary-dep tests/ file must have every test fn ignored, which would have left the adminspace parser's calibration never running -- so the parser and its units moved into the crate's lib, where they run in the ordinary Layer C1 workspace lane (cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --lib: 15 passed). Second: the module doc explaining that move QUOTED the test attribute, and C0's scanner arms on any line matching it and binds to the next fn -- so my prose made the helper below it look like an un-skippable test fn. Reworded; C0 pass.

That is code, not a test.

THE REMAINING 4 ARE NOT ALIKE. session-extshm is WIRE-INCOMPATIBLE by design (wz offers a UNIT ext at establishment id 0x2 where zenoh declares ZBuf-on-Init / z64-on-Open) and is a decision to reopen, not a test to write. transport-shm carries the same challenge-response residual. storage-history needs the versioned-tombstone semantics AND a zenohd with the storage-manager plugin. session-extqos needs the z64 QoSLink priority-range wire plus a config path that flips is_qos true at all.

A PROOF ROUND SHOULD SAY WHICH ASSERTION THE DAMAGE HITS. The first draft here asserted wz's own JOIN log before zenoh's count, and under the 0x4-ext-id damage wz correctly DECLINED to claim aggregation — so the wz-side check fired and the zenoh-side verdict was never reached. The verdict assertion was unreachable under every wire damage available to it, i.e. it was decorative. Ordering the foreign-side assertion FIRST is what made the damage land on it. Check assertion ORDER, not just presence, when a leg has a precondition.

TWO HARNESS DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY MEASURING, NOT BY READING. (1) wait_for_substring returns the WHOLE captured buffer, so lines().next() yields the process banner, not the needle's line — R311y471's note that it returns "from the needle onward" describes that test's own split_once, not this helper. (2) The two dials RACE, so the surviving face index is not stable: a "face 0 UP" needle read a healthy node as dead when face 1 won. The needle now names the peer ADDRESS, which is also stricter.

Round 311y473.decision_summary: R311y473 -- transport-multilink's LAST named residual, S5, is closed, and the atom moves PARTIAL -> COMPLETE: A3 REMAINING WORK 86 -> 85 EXACT. R311y472 had to read a multilink session's link count off ZENOH'S adminspace because wz's own reported nothing -- the sessions[] array was a hard-coded empty vector at BOTH admin hosts, and to_admin_json rendered neither max_links nor the aggregated link set. Its carry named the fix as code, not a test, and this is that code plus the foreign-calibrated witness for it. Config half: to_admin_json renders max_links (and the transport-qos offer, whose field doc carried the identical not-rendered caveat). Runtime half: local_data sessions[].links, from a new SessionLinkActions::admin_links that enumerates the aggregation set -- or this binding's single link when the set is empty, so a non-multilink session reports its link too -- and reads each link's {src,dst} off a new BoxedLinkDriver::link_endpoints resolved once at link open by the constructing pipeline, exactly as R311y453's LinkSubject is. The locator strings come from ONE table: InterceptorLink::locator_for, which BoundListener::advertised_locator (the R311y470 site) now delegates to instead of carrying a second copy, so a new emitter cannot repeat y470's log-word-as-scheme defect -- and y470's own three tests, run under the gated transports where two of them live, are what proved the delegation preserved every value. Proven by wz_own_adminspace_reports_aggregated_links (Layer Z, hosted): a --max-links 2 --config-queryable wz peer dials ONE zenohd twice and WZ's adminspace answers ONE router session carrying TWO links plus max_links:2, with a STOCK-zenohd twin reporting ONE so the count tracks a FOREIGN budget; damage-verified on the ext id (proof reds on the verdict, twin green) and on admin_links itself (both red). Two findings the measurement produced rather than the reading: a joined_faces de-dup filter was DEAD CODE and was removed after damaging it changed nothing, and the demo's tick-only sessions[] refresh was genuinely FLAKY and was root-caused into a refresh-before-log happens-before edge. A4 corpus 127 -> 128 files / 264 -> 266 tests, zenohd class 10 -> 11; proven/partial/unproven UNCHANGED at 102/40/18, correctly -- transport-multilink was already proven by y472 and adminspace-core was never in the unproven set.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/link.rs: new LinkEndpoints {src,dst} + BoxedLinkDriver::link_endpoints() (default None) -- the wz counterpart of the {src,dst} object zenoh's link_to_json emits per link (net/runtime/adminspace.rs:608-613). Resolved ONCE at link open and stored, for the same reason link_subject is: an admin GET must not become a syscall per reply, and the constructing pipeline is the only object that knows both its scheme and its socket.

crates/wz-session-core/src/link.rs: new InterceptorLink::locator_for(address) -- the DIALABLE locator table, deliberately NOT as_str(), which is a CONFIG spelling whose quic-datagram is a wz-only word zenoh cannot dial. This is the ONE table now; crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs::BoundListener::advertised_locator (the R311y470 site) delegates to it via a new BoundListener::interceptor_link() rather than carrying a second copy, so the scheme for a new transport is stated once and every emitter inherits it. Both matches stay wildcard-free.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_interfaces.rs: ip_link_endpoints (both ends required -- a half-known pair rendered as a locator is a string an admin client cannot dial and cannot tell apart from one it can) + addressless_link_endpoints for path / cid:port addressed links. Siblings of the R311y453 subject helpers, in the same module.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio: endpoints threaded through the write drivers exactly as R311y453 threaded the subject -- StreamWriteDriver::new gains the parameter (so all six stream pipelines must state it to compile) and WsWriteDriver with it. Resolved in link_pipeline (tcp), tls_pipeline, ws_pipeline, quic_pipeline (endpoint.local_addr + Connection::remote_address), unixsock_pipeline (as_pathname; an unnamed end yields None rather than an invented path) and vsock_pipeline (wz's own vsock/<CID>:<PORT> form). unixpipe passes None with its reason stated: a FIFO pair cannot name the acceptor's rendezvous base.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: new SessionLinkActions::admin_links() (adminspace-core) -- one AdminLink per PHYSICAL link, from the aggregation set when populated and from this binding's own link when it is empty, so the multilink and single-link cases are one method rather than a caller-side branch a caller can forget. A link whose driver cannot name its endpoints still gets an entry with blank ends: the COUNT is the load-bearing fact, so dropping the link to tidy a string would corrupt the answer.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: declare_adminspace_with_permissions now fills sessions[].links from actions.admin_links(); it was a hard-coded Vec::new().

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: new LinkstateForwarder::admin_sessions() -- the forwarder-hosted enumeration that was a documented deferral (the host passed an empty slice, so a wz peer's admin GET reported no sessions whatever it was connected to). One entry per face with NO aggregation de-dup, and that is measured: an aggregated link is recorded via register_joined and never enters the faces map (accept_loop.rs:1594 vs :1696), so a first-draft joined_faces filter here could never fire and was removed rather than kept as a guard whose prose claimed work it did not do.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/config.rs: to_admin_json renders max_links (transport-multilink) and qos (transport-qos), both mid-object in the R311y50 sorted-pairs assembly. The two field docs that said it did not render them are corrected in place.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/config.rs tests: the seven exact-string access-axis pins gain not(transport-multilink)/not(transport-qos) so the orthogonal transport keys do not multiply seven assertions by four; +to_admin_json_ap_full_shape_alphabetical, the exact pin for the preset-ap-full shape, which had NONE before; +to_admin_json_max_links_tracks_the_builder and +to_admin_json_qos_tracks_the_builder, which assert the rendered value follows with_max_links / with_qos rather than merely being present (presence alone passes against a hard-coded default).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the --config-queryable host now answers from a live admin_sessions buffer instead of an empty slice. The buffer follows the introspection precedent (the handler lives INSIDE the forwarder so it cannot also hold &forwarder), but is refreshed on every FACE EVENT before that event is logged -- not only on the app tick, which left a real window in which faces were up and the admin view was empty.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_own_adminspace_reports_aggregated_links.rs (NEW, 2 legs) + scripts/run-ci.sh Layer Z registration after the y472 leg, same --test-threads=1 per-zenohd isolation. No feature was added to Layer Z's wz-ap-demo build: adminspace-core is absent from preset-ap-client, but routing-peer (added by y471) pulls wz/adminspace-core, so the FULL build line already carried it -- resolved from the demo's own feature table rather than read off one preset.
verification_bullets: THE COUNT WZ RENDERS TRACKS A FOREIGN PROCESS'S BUDGET, WHICH IS WHAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING WZ AGREEING WITH ITSELF. Leg 1: a max_links:2 zenohd, dialed twice by a --max-links 2 --config-queryable wz peer -> wz's own @/<zid>/peer reports ONE whatami=router session carrying TWO links, and its config body reports max_links:2. Leg 2 (twin): the SAME wz argv against a STOCK zenohd, whose max_links defaults to 1 -> wz reports ONE link and logs no JOIN. Same wz binary, same flags, different ROUTER config.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED TWICE, AND THE DAMAGE LANDS ON THE VERDICT. (a) MULTILINK_EXT_ID 0x04 -> 0x0A with wz-ap-demo REBUILT: the proof leg reds with wz reporting 1 link where 2 was required, the twin stays GREEN -- so the verdict assertion is reachable under the damage, which is R311y472's ordering lesson applied rather than restated. (b) admin_links() returning an empty vector: BOTH legs red at 0 links, so the assertion depends on this round's code and not on something already present. Both damages reverted; the leg re-run 5/5 green plus once more after the revert.

THE INSTRUMENT IS ZENOH'S OWN. wz's sessions[] is parsed by parse_zenoh_admin_sessions, the structural parser R311y472 wrote against zenohd's @/<zid>/router body -- so reading wz's @/<zid>/peer body with it unchanged asserts that wz's local_data is the shape a zenoh admin client expects, not merely one wz can read back. That parser's calibration units run in the ordinary Layer C1 lane (cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --lib: 15 passed).

A FIRST-DRAFT GUARD WAS DEAD CODE, AND ONLY DAMAGING IT SHOWED THAT. admin_sessions shipped with a !joined_faces.contains_key(id) filter and a comment calling it load-bearing. Damaging the filter changed NO test outcome, which sent the question to the registration sites: a joined link goes through register_joined (accept_loop.rs:1594), which writes only the id mapping, while faces is written by register (:1696) on the primary alone. The filter could never fire. It was removed and the prose corrected to what is actually true, rather than kept as an unwitnessed guard.

THE LEG WAS GENUINELY FLAKY AND WAS ROOT-CAUSED, NOT PAPERED OVER. After the damage runs the proof leg failed with sessions: [] while its twin passed -- because the demo's sessions[] buffer refreshed only on the app tick, and the twin only ever passed by spending 10s in a needle timeout that let a tick land. Fixed at the source: the buffer is refreshed on every face event BEFORE the event is logged, so the log line an observer keys on is a real happens-before edge. 5/5 green after, and damage (a) re-run afterwards still discriminates -- the fix did not mask the measurement.

TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND BY MEASURING. (1) Both admin queriers on the demo's stock zid 01020304: the wz peer's face table is zid-keyed, so the second querier's transport was torn down before it could emit (observed as TransportUnavailable from its query task). Run by hand seconds apart both succeed, which is exactly the race a fast test finds and a manual check does not; the queriers now carry distinct pinned zids. (2) The admin key is SCRAPED from the peer's own log line rather than derived, so the leg never reproduces wz's zid-hex rendering by hand.

ADMINSPACE-CORE IS THE ATOM THIS ROUND MOST OBVIOUSLY ADVANCED AND IT IS STILL PARTIAL, deliberately. sessions[] is now live at both hosts, but its own residuals are untouched: the unixpipe pipeline reports no endpoints (a FIFO pair cannot name the acceptor's rendezvous base) so those links render with blank {src,dst}; and the pure-Session admin host still does not enumerate declarations (its sink fires while the observer is locked mid-iter_mut). Read the atom's reason before assuming which of §5.23's seven atoms this helped.

THE NEXT ADMINSPACE RESIDUAL IS ENDPOINT COVERAGE, NOT PLUMBING. link_endpoints is a trait method with a None default, so quic-datagram, udp and serial silently report blank ends today -- the count stays right, the strings do not. Each is a small edit at its pipeline's driver constructor; the pattern is established six times over. unixpipe is the only one that needs a widened type (UnixpipeLink would have to carry the base path).

A DEAD GUARD READS EXACTLY LIKE A LOAD-BEARING ONE UNTIL YOU DAMAGE IT. The joined_faces de-dup filter removed here had a confident comment explaining why it was necessary, and the reasoning was sound in the abstract -- a multilink peer DOES hold a face per link. It was wrong about this codebase, and no amount of re-reading the filter would have said so; damaging it and seeing nothing change is what sent the question to register_joined vs register. Damage the guard, not just the feature.

A TWIN THAT PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON HIDES A FLAKE IN ITS SIBLING. The stock-zenohd twin here passed reliably while the proof leg raced, because the twin spends 10s in a needle timeout that no aggregation will ever satisfy -- and that timeout was incidentally acting as a sleep. When one leg of a matched pair is flaky and the other is not, check whether the stable one is stable for a reason the pair does not share.

A DEAD GUARD READS EXACTLY LIKE A LOAD-BEARING ONE UNTIL YOU DAMAGE IT. Damage the guard, not just the feature.

A TWIN THAT PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON HIDES A FLAKE IN ITS SIBLING. The stock-zenohd twin here passed reliably while the proof leg raced, because the twin spends 10s in a needle timeout that no aggregation will ever satisfy -- and that timeout was incidentally acting as a sleep. When one leg of a matched pair is flaky and the other is not, check whether the stable one is stable for a reason the pair does not share.

Round 311y474.decision_summary: R311y474 -- adminspace-core's link-endpoint residual, the one R311y473's carry named, is closed on the FULL variant set rather than a sample: udp, quic-datagram, serial and unixpipe now fill BoxedLinkDriver::link_endpoints, so every production write driver reports its {src,dst} (all 13 impls enumerated; the exceptions are the lwIP MCU driver and the test doubles, both named by the trait doc). changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs: dial_udp now CONNECTs the dial socket to its peer after the bind, as zenoh does (zenoh-link-udp/src/unicast.rs:311, immediately after its identical UNSPECIFIED:0 bind at :285-289). This is the root-cause fix for the wildcard src the measurement found, not a rendering workaround: the kernel resolves the route, so local_addr reports the concrete egress address instead of 0.0.0.0:<port>, which is what upstream's src_addr is (:317). It also filters inbound datagrams to the one peer, upstream's behaviour. Scoped to the DIAL path: the acceptor's socket is shared across demux faces and stays unconnected, and UdpDriver::connect (lib.rs:1660) / the multicast + scouting binds have their own binds and never route through here. The fn doc and the module bullet both say bind AND connect now, and both name the UdpDriver::connect divergence, so neither drifts.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs: udp_writer_task picks send vs send_to from the socket's OWN connectedness (peer_addr().is_ok()) rather than a caller flag, so the two wire paths cannot disagree with the socket they were handed. Not stylistic: sendto(2) on a connected socket is permitted on Linux but returns EISCONN on macOS/BSD, so an unconditional send_to would break every udp dial on a platform 5.20 carries as an atom.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs: UdpWriteDriver gains endpoints + link_endpoints(), filled at BOTH wire sites -- wire_udp_socket (dial: own socket vs the dialled peer) and wire_udp_demuxed (accept: the SHARED listener socket vs this face's demultiplexed peer). Those two are the whole udp surface; they are the only UdpWriteDriver constructors.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/quic_datagram_pipeline.rs: QuicDatagramWriteDriver gains endpoints + link_endpoints(). The src prefers Connection::local_ip() over the endpoint's bound address, keeping the endpoint's port -- a deliberate SUPERSET over upstream, which publishes quic_endpoint.local_addr() unconditionally (zenoh-link-quic_datagram/src/unicast.rs:292) and therefore reports quic/0.0.0.0:<port>?rel=0 for a WILDCARD-LISTENING router, the ordinary deploy. quinn answers None on the initiating side, so a client's own src stays the wildcard bind, which is upstream's shape verbatim.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/serial_pipeline.rs: wire_serial_stream takes the dialled SerialEndpoint (a tty's address is not readable off SerialStream) and SerialWriteDriver gains endpoints + link_endpoints(). Both ends render the SAME tty locator, which is upstream's DIAL side verbatim (zenoh-link-serial/src/unicast.rs:310-315 passes its one path as both src_path and dst_path). Upstream's LISTENER side puts a random UUIDv4 in dst (:329-333); that is deliberately NOT reproduced -- it is not a locator anything can dial, and wz has no wired serial acceptor to apply it to (session_open.rs:2048).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: DialedLink::Serial becomes a struct variant carrying the SerialEndpoint alongside the stream, filled at the one construction site (the AnyLocator::Serial dial arm, which already had the parsed endpoint in hand).

crates/wz-session-core/src/locator.rs: new SerialEndpoint::locator_address_with_config() -- the address span PLUS the required #baudrate= tail, the argument InterceptorLink::locator_for prefixes with the scheme. It sits beside parse_serial_locator on purpose and writes NO scheme of its own, so the R311y473 one-table collapse still holds. A round-trip unit test pins renderer against parser for both address forms.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/unixpipe_pipeline.rs: UnixpipeLink gains write_node (the FIFO the Sender writes; the read half's node is already inside FifoReadEnd, which unlinks it on drop, so it is not stored twice) and wire_unixpipe_stream renders src = the FIFO this end reads, dst = the one it writes. This CORRECTS R311y473's stated blocker rather than working around it: that note said a FIFO pair cannot name the acceptor's rendezvous base, but upstream does not use the base either -- it renders the DEDICATED per-link pair on both sides (zenoh-link-unixpipe/src/unix/unicast.rs:264-274 client, :417-427 listener). No type had to be widened beyond the write node.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/link_endpoints_pairing.rs (NEW, 5 legs): the witness. Every leg drives the REAL seam for its transport and reads BOTH ends.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the new proof is registered in the FOUR lanes that own the transports rather than one place -- C1t (serial, 2), the quic-datagram lane C1aj (3), the unixpipe lane C1al (2), and C1l (udp, 1, via the existing _runci_guarded_test helper). Each count is the number that lane's own feature set selects; the file is cfg-gated so a set arming none of the four link features compiles to nothing rather than to unused helpers.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/config.rs: to_admin_json seeds its pair vector with the THREE unconditional fields (batch_size, lease_ms, whatami) instead of pushing them after the cfg-gated ones. Identical output -- the explicit alphabetical sort still follows -- but it retires a REAL, PRE-EXISTING clippy::vec_init_then_push failure that run-ci Layer C1bb was already red on before this round: with Vec::new() first, a combo in which several gated pushes expand back-to-back (transport-multilink + transport-qos alone was enough, and C1bb arms both) leaves clippy looking at a plain push chain it wants folded into vec![..] -- a suggestion this code CANNOT take, since under another combo those pushes are absent. Found by running clippy on an ap-full-ish combo for THIS round's work; introduced by R311y473, which added the qos push beside max_links.
verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT FOUND TWO DEFECTS THE READING DID NOT. The first draft of this round only threaded endpoints through four pipelines; the test then failed on udp AND quic-datagram with a wildcard src, which sent the question to the zenoh source. udp: upstream CONNECTs and wz did not, so wz was genuinely diverged and the fix is the connect, not the string. quic-datagram: upstream reports the wildcard too, so the mirror assertion was over-strong and was replaced by the half that does mirror plus a port-level cross-check -- and the residual value of Connection::local_ip got its own leg. Neither conclusion was available from reading the wz diff.

EVERY LEG IS BOUND TO SOMETHING THE EMITTER DOES NOT CONTROL. (a) MIRROR (udp, unixpipe): both ends of one real link are wired and neither is ever told the other's src -- the dialer learns only the address it dials, the acceptor only the peer its kernel or the FIFO handshake reports -- so dialer.src == acceptor.dst and dialer.dst == acceptor.src compares two independently resolved answers. (b) PARSE-BACK (all five legs): every emitted string round-trips through parse_any_locator, wz's own dial-side parser in a different crate, which is the R311y470 contract. (c) THE FILESYSTEM (unixpipe): both parsed paths must be live FIFO nodes on disk, a source that is not wz code. (d) BOTH ADDRESS FORMS (serial): the two ends get DIFFERENT endpoints, one Device and one Pins, and each must report its own parsed back to the exact SerialEndpoint -- an emitter hard-coding either spelling fails on the other.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED FIVE TIMES, EACH WITH THE REBUILD OBSERVED IN THE CARGO OUTPUT. (1) dial_udp connect removed -> udp leg reds on the wildcard, other four green. (2) udp src/dst swapped -> udp leg reds, other four green. (3) quic Connection::local_ip preference replaced by the bound address -> ONLY the wildcard-bind leg reds while its concrete-bind twin stays green, so the branch is load-bearing and not defensive. (4) serial #baudrate= tail dropped -> serial leg reds with Serial(MissingBaudrate), i.e. wz's own parser refusing wz's own string. (5) unixpipe rendering the rendezvous base -> unixpipe leg reds on the distinctness rule. All five reverted; 5/5 green after.

THE LANE PINS WERE PROVEN TO BIND, WHICH THE LOG CANNOT SHOW. Every lane runs cargo test --quiet, which suppresses the Running tests/<file> line, so grepping the run-ci log for the new file name returns NOTHING in all four lanes -- the log cannot distinguish "my step ran" from "my step was never invoked". Instead a 6th always-passing test was appended to the file, shifting every lane's count by one: C1t, C1aj, C1al and C1l ALL failed. Removed again, all four pass. That is what establishes the steps run and the exact counts are pinned.

THE NEGATIVE CLAIM IS ENUMERATED, NOT SAMPLED. All 13 BoxedLinkDriver impls in the workspace were listed and checked for a link_endpoints override: the 5 production write drivers (StreamWriteDriver serving tcp/tls/quic/unixsock/vsock/unixpipe, WsWriteDriver, UdpWriteDriver, SerialWriteDriver, QuicDatagramWriteDriver) all report; the exceptions are wz-session-lwip's LwipUdpDriver and 7 test doubles, both classes named by the trait doc. So "every production write driver reports its endpoints" is a checked statement about a closed set.

THE UDP CONNECT IS A TRANSPORT BEHAVIOUR CHANGE AND ITS EXISTING PROOF SURFACE WAS RE-RUN, NOT ASSUMED: udp_seam_e2e 4 passed, udp_frag_e2e 1 passed, udp_chaos_e2e 3 passed. Its blast radius was also bounded by enumeration -- dial_udp has exactly two callers (the AnyLocator::Serial-sibling udp dial arm at session_open.rs:1559 and one unit test), and UdpDriver::connect plus the multicast and scouting paths each carry their own bind.

GATES, all re-run on the FINAL tree after the last doc edit: A3 REMAINING WORK 85 EXACT and A4 corpus 128 files / 266 tests with proven/partial/unproven 102/40/18 -- BOTH UNCHANGED, and both correctly so. A3 scores an ATOM's implementation axis and adminspace-core keeps its other residuals (metadata null, weight null, multicast peers, the config/** subscriber, declaration enumeration), so it stays PARTIAL. A4 scores FOREIGN-witnessed proof and this round's witness is wz-to-wz. A round can close a real residual and move no gate number.
validate_workspace: T1 orphan 14 new=+0, T3 warn 4 / T4 info 4 unchanged, citation-gate 1907 -> 1908 rust sources with 0 unscanned, 0 stale exclusions.

A PRE-EXISTING HOSTED-GATE RED WAS FOUND AND FIXED, AND IT WAS PROVEN PRE-EXISTING RATHER THAN ASSUMED: with this round's changes git-stashed, clippy on the same combo still failed at config.rs:241 on the ORIGIN tree, so R311y473 shipped it. Layer C1bb (which arms transport-qos AND transport-multilink for a --all-targets -D warnings clippy) FAILED before the fix and PASSES after; Layer C1ba passes too. The minimal trigger was bisected by feature: adminspace-core alone clean, +transport-multilink clean, +transport-qos clean, multilink+qos RED. Under the default set the lint never fires, which is why local pre-push (default features only) never caught it and why it sat on main.

THE OUTPUT-IDENTITY CLAIM FOR THAT REFACTOR IS PINNED BY THE EXACT-STRING TESTS, NOT BY INSPECTION: all 10 admin/config tests pass on the ap-full-ish combo -- including to_admin_json_ap_full_shape_alphabetical, to_admin_json_max_links_tracks_the_builder and to_admin_json_qos_tracks_the_builder -- and the not(multilink)/not(qos)-gated access-axis pins (to_admin_json_full_access_alphabetical + the acl / downsampling rule dumps) pass under a combo that arms the access set WITHOUT multilink or qos, which is the arm where those exact strings differ.

UNIT SUITES on the final tree: wz-session-core 271 (transport-link-serial) and 252 (default), wz-runtime-tokio 318 (default) and 607 (the ap-full-ish combo), all 0 failed; the new file 5/5 under all four link features and 1/2/2/3 under the four individual lane sets. cargo fmt --all --check clean. clippy -D warnings clean on wz-session-core (serial) and on wz-runtime-tokio across the four single-transport sets plus the ap-full-ish combo, --all-targets.

run-ci Layer Z pass (313s, 0 FAILED across 33 test-result lines), which is the lane that owns the adminspace interop and therefore the one config.rs sits in. R311y473's own leg was read off the log by name rather than inferred from the lane verdict: Running tests/wz_own_adminspace_reports_aggregated_links.rs -> running 2 tests -> ok, 2 passed, 10.69s. So the to_admin_json refactor did not disturb the foreign-read admin body. Layer C1t / C1aj / C1al / C1l all pass with the new counts, and Layer C1ba / C1bb pass after the config fix.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y474 CLOSED adminspace-core's link-endpoint residual and MOVED NO GATE, and both halves of that are correct. A3 REMAINING WORK stays 85 EXACT because A3 scores an ATOM's implementation axis and adminspace-core keeps its other residuals (metadata hardcoded null, sessions[].weight null, no multicast peers / group field, the config/** subscriber declare_adminspace omits, the pure-Session host's missing declaration enumeration). A4 stays 102/40/18 with corpus 128/266 because A4 scores FOREIGN-witnessed proof and this round's witness is wz-to-wz. Do not read "closed a residual" as "moved a number", in either direction.

THE FOREIGN WITNESS IS THE NEXT STEP AND IT IS ALREADY PROVISIONED. target/zenohd-unixpipe/zenohd exists on this machine, and unixpipe is the one transport of the four that is WIRE-COMPATIBLE with zenohd (native-endian invitation + decimal dedicated-suffix node names, unixpipe_pipeline module doc). A Layer Z leg in which zenohd dials wz over unixpipe and the TWO adminspaces are read against each other would cross-check the dedicated FIFO node pair across implementations -- the strongest available form, since each side names the two nodes independently -- and it is the shape that can move A4 for transport-link-unixpipe. udp / serial / quic-datagram have no comparable cheap foreign path: zenohd would need a udp-listen deploy, a real tty pair, and a quic-datagram variant build with certs at both ends respectively.

THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE READING, FOUND BOTH DEFECTS THIS ROUND -- AND THEY WERE OPPOSITE IN KIND. The udp wildcard src was a genuine wz divergence (upstream connects, wz did not) and the fix was the connect. The quic-datagram wildcard src was upstream's own behaviour and the fix was to the TEST, plus a superset for the wildcard-LISTEN case quinn can answer. Same failing symptom, opposite verdicts, and only the zenoh source could tell them apart. When a mirror assertion fails, ask which side is wrong before assuming it is yours.

A STATED BLOCKER IN A CARRY IS A CLAIM, AND THIS ONE WAS FALSE. R311y473 recorded that a unixpipe link "cannot name its endpoints" because the rendezvous base belongs to the acceptor. Checking upstream instead of trusting it showed zenoh never uses the base -- it renders the DEDICATED per-link pair on both sides -- so the residual closed with no type widened beyond the write node. The blocker had a confident mechanism attached, which is exactly what made it look settled.

A LANE THAT RUNS cargo test --quiet CANNOT BE AUDITED FROM ITS LOG. --quiet suppresses the "Running tests/<file>" line, so grepping a run-ci log for a newly registered test file returns nothing even when the step ran -- indistinguishable from never being invoked. The way to establish it is to break the count (a 6th always-passing test shifted all four lanes red, then removed) rather than to read the log. Any future round registering a --quiet step should expect to prove it this way.

THE DEFAULT FEATURE SET IS NOT A CLIPPY GATE. The config.rs lint that had Layer C1bb red never fires under default features, so local pre-push (default-only by design since R311y386) was structurally blind to it and it reached main. When a round touches a cfg-assembled builder, clippy the COMBOS, not the default.

THE FIRST DESIGN WAS MEASURED WRONG, AND THAT MEASUREMENT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. The obvious witness -- seed N versions of one key, count N replies at a foreign querier -- was built, run, and produced ONE reply. The cause is not in wz: pico's z_get passes empty selector parameters (examples/unix/c11/z_get.c), so Z_CONSOLIDATION_MODE_AUTO resolves to LATEST rather than NONE (src/net/primitives.c:567-571 -- the branch turns on a _time parameter being present), and pico then drops every non-newest same-key reply INSIDE THE QUERIER before the application callback (src/session/query.c:133-150). A reply count for one key is therefore not observable through that CLI at all. z_querier does accept a ?params selector but returned no replies in this harness; that is recorded as an open question rather than pursued.

SO THE OBSERVABLE BECAME THE GATE SKIP, WHICH IS THE SAME CAPABILITY THROUGH A SINGLE REPLY. zenoh implements History::All as the ABSENCE of the newer-wins guard (plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/service.rs:319 runs it only for History::Latest; zenoh-backend-traits/src/lib.rs:161-165 defines the two modes), and wz mirrors that in StorageState::latest_mode / process_put. A put replayed after a NEWER delete is the one mutation whose outcome differs: accepted under All, Outdated under Latest. One reply either way, so the difference survives pico's consolidation.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH NEITHER LEG COULD DO ALONE. Forcing latest_mode TRUE (the gate always runs) reds the All leg and leaves the Latest twin green; forcing it FALSE (the gate never runs) reds the Latest twin and leaves the All leg green. The pair therefore brackets the mechanism from both sides -- a build that ignored history() in either direction is caught. A third damage emptied the WIRE reply set (matching_versions returns nothing): the All leg reds, and the Latest twin PASSES, which is the honest limit of an absence assertion and exactly why the round does not rest on the twin.

THAT THIRD DAMAGE ALSO EXPOSED A REAL RACE IN THE HARNESS, WHICH WAS ROOT-CAUSED RATHER THAN RETIMED. The select! treated the drive future completing as a failure, but pico is a one-shot querier, so the session ending is the ORDINARY consequence of it exiting -- and on a leg whose answer is empty pico exits almost immediately, so the drive branch could win with the terminator ALREADY in the capture. The verdict now comes from pico's own terminator in the final capture and neither select! branch decides it. 5/5 green after the fix.

THE A4 LEVERS THAT REMAIN, CHECKED RATHER THAN GUESSED. A FOREIGN CLI'S CONSOLIDATION CAN MAKE A PROPERTY UNOBSERVABLE, AND IT LOOKS LIKE A wz DEFECT UNTIL YOU READ THE CLI. pico's z_get collapses same-key replies in the QUERIER (AUTO -> LATEST because it sends empty selector parameters), so "N versions" arrives as one line however many wz sent. Before designing a witness around a reply COUNT, check what the foreign client does to reply sets. The general move when it collapses: find a mutation whose outcome differs in a SINGLE reply -- here the newer-wins gate skip.

AN ABSENCE-ASSERTING TWIN CANNOT DETECT A DEAD REPLY PATH. Measured: emptying matching_versions reds the History::All leg and leaves the Latest twin GREEN, because "pico received nothing" is exactly what a broken serve path also produces. The twin is still what makes the positive leg mean something -- it just must never be the only leg.

A `--quiet` LANE STILL CANNOT BE AUDITED FROM ITS LOG, and this is the second round running to hit it. Layer E named neither new test in run-ci's log.
