The obvious witness -- seed N versions of one key, count N replies at a foreign querier -- was built, run, and produced ONE reply. The cause is not in wz: pico's z_get passes empty selector parameters (examples/unix/c11/z_get.c), so Z_CONSOLIDATION_MODE_AUTO resolves to LATEST rather than NONE (src/net/primitives.c:567-571 -- the branch turns on a _time parameter being present), and pico then drops every non-newest same-key reply INSIDE THE QUERIER before the application callback (src/session/query.c:133-150). A reply count for one key is therefore not observable through that CLI at all. z_querier does accept a ?params selector but returned no replies in this harness; that is recorded as an open question rather than pursued.

SO THE OBSERVABLE BECAME THE GATE SKIP, WHICH IS THE SAME CAPABILITY THROUGH A SINGLE REPLY. zenoh implements History::All as the ABSENCE of the newer-wins guard (plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/service.rs:319 runs it only for History::Latest; zenoh-backend-traits/src/lib.rs:161-165 defines the two modes), and wz mirrors that in StorageState::latest_mode / process_put. A put replayed after a NEWER delete is the one mutation whose outcome differs: accepted under All, Outdated under Latest. One reply either way, so the difference survives pico's consolidation.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH NEITHER LEG COULD DO ALONE. Forcing latest_mode TRUE (the gate always runs) reds the All leg and leaves the Latest twin green; forcing it FALSE (the gate never runs) reds the Latest twin and leaves the All leg green. The pair therefore brackets the mechanism from both sides -- a build that ignored history() in either direction is caught. A third damage emptied the WIRE reply set (matching_versions returns nothing): the All leg reds, and the Latest twin PASSES, which is the honest limit of an absence assertion and exactly why the round does not rest on the twin.

THAT THIRD DAMAGE ALSO EXPOSED A REAL RACE IN THE HARNESS, WHICH WAS ROOT-CAUSED RATHER THAN RETIMED. The select! treated the drive future completing as a failure, but pico is a one-shot querier, so the session ending is the ORDINARY consequence of it exiting -- and on a leg whose answer is empty pico exits almost immediately, so the drive branch could win with the terminator ALREADY in the capture. The verdict now comes from pico's own terminator in the final capture and neither select! branch decides it. 5/5 green after the fix.

Round 311y476.decision_summary: R311y476 -- api-compat-pico gains a FOREIGN witness and leaves Layer A4's unproven list: unproven 17 -> 16, partial 40 -> 41, on both the all-lanes and the executed-by-hosted-CI counts. The atom's headline claim is that a zenoh-pico C program can link the wz cdylib as a BINARY DROP-IN, and until now nothing checked it: every gate was a Rust test calling the exported extern C symbols from inside the workspace, and the inventory said so plainly -- no C compiler consumes it, there is no cc dependency and no C lane. This round hands the checking to artifacts wz does not own. Two UNMODIFIED upstream examples are compiled against zenoh-pico's OWN headers, including the CMake-generated config.h that fixes the feature set the pico oracles were built with, linked against libwz_capi_pico.so, and run against a real zenoh-pico CLI: z_sub.c on wz receives from a real z_put, and z_queryable.c on wz answers a real z_get with the FOREIGN querier reporting the verdict. Coverage was MEASURED across all 31 upstream examples rather than sampled, and the first measurement was wrong in a way worth keeping: six appeared to link, but three of those compile to a stub main because a Z_FEATURE the generated config disagrees with #if-s the body out, so exactly ONE example genuinely linked before this round. Damage-verified three ways: restoring the null reds only the queryable leg, nulling z_sample_payload reds only the subscriber leg, and removing the export reds the queryable leg at LINK time. A3 REMAINING WORK stays 85 EXACT, correctly -- api-compat-pico keeps a now-precise implementation residual, the keyexpr-declaration family that upstream's z_put.c is still waiting on.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS, AND THE FIRST TWO BRACKET THE PAIR FROM OPPOSITE SIDES. (1) Restoring the conditional null in z_query_payload reds leg 2 on its foreign assertion and leaves leg 1 green. (2) Nulling z_sample_payload reds leg 1 on its payload assertion and leaves leg 2 green. (3) Removing no_mangle from z_bytes_from_static_str makes the symbol vanish from nm -D and reds leg 2 at LINK time with the undefined-reference diagnostic, leg 1 still green. Each damage was rebuilt and the rebuild confirmed (Compiling line plus a fresh .so), so none of the three is a stale-binary reading.

Its NAMED RESIDUAL is now precise and actionable rather than a bulk count: upstream's z_put.c needs exactly FOUR more exports -- z_declare_keyexpr, z_undeclare_keyexpr, z_keyexpr_loan, z_keyexpr_move -- and they are not four stubs. A faithful build needs per-face mapping ids (the id space is per-peer, as faces.rs already documents for observers), a declare fan-out that REPLAYS onto faces that appear later exactly as declare_subscriber does, and Session::publish_aliased on the put path. z_owned_keyexpr_t is 48 B, measured with a real C compiler against pico's headers.

UPSTREAM'S OWN EXAMPLES ARE A BETTER ABI ORACLE THAN ANY TEST wz CAN WRITE, AND THIS ROUND IS THE EVIDENCE. A wz-authored C program is written against the exports wz happens to have, which is the bias that let this atom sit at BUILT for many rounds with its headline claim unwitnessed. Upstream's programs were written with no knowledge of wz, so the first one that ran past the linker immediately exposed a getter whose null-contract wz had never been forced to get right. The remaining 29 examples are a queue of the same kind of pressure, and the link-failure output names exactly which exports each one is waiting on.

A COMPILE+LINK SWEEP OVER FOREIGN EXAMPLES NEEDS A REAL-BODY CHECK OR IT COUNTS STUBS. Six examples appeared to link; three of them compile to a stub main because a Z_FEATURE the generated config disagrees with #if-s the body out. Checking nm -u for a z_open reference is what separates the two, and it is cheap. Before reporting "N of the examples work", verify the bodies exist.

FIXING ONE GETTER MEANS AUDITING ITS SIBLINGS AGAINST THE FOREIGN SOURCE, NOT AGAINST EACH OTHER. z_query_payload and z_query_attachment shared the fatal shape and were fixed together. z_reply_ok / z_reply_err have the same conditional-null shape and are CORRECT to keep it, because pico supplies z_reply_is_ok as a guard and the C side is expected to call it first. The discriminator is whether pico's API gives the caller any way to avoid the unconditional call; where it does not, a conditional null is a memory-safety bug rather than a defensive nicety.

A cdylib IS NOT A DEV-DEPENDENCY, AND THE REASON IS A SYMBOL COLLISION. wz-integration-tests links the REAL zenoh-pico through zenoh-pico-sys for the layer3 codec-parity tests. Adding wz-capi-pico as a dev-dep would put a second definition of z_open / z_put / z_bytes_loan into the same test binary. The drop-in therefore stays at the OS linker boundary, which is also the only shape that witnesses the real deployment: a C program picks ONE library at link time. That is why Layer E builds the crate explicitly instead of cargo doing it as a side effect.

NEXT A4 LEVERS, UNCHANGED FROM R311y475 EXCEPT THAT api-compat-pico IS OFF THE LIST. Of the 16 unproven, nine are reserved/FOUNDATIONAL and are not levers at all. The actionable seven are config-mutate-runtime, rest-http-bridge, rest-sse-subscribe, router-connect-reconcile, session-extshm, storage-mgr-garbage-collection, transport-shm. rest-http-bridge + rest-sse-subscribe remain the only pair that could move A4 by TWO in one round, and their oracle ships inside the stock zenohd binary. Consult python3 scripts/lib/crossimpl_corpus.py --list-claims BEFORE proposing a lever.

A COMPILE+LINK SWEEP OVER FOREIGN EXAMPLES NEEDS A REAL-BODY CHECK OR IT COUNTS STUBS. FIXING ONE GETTER MEANS AUDITING ITS SIBLINGS AGAINST THE FOREIGN SOURCE, NOT AGAINST EACH OTHER. z_query_payload and z_query_attachment shared the fatal shape and were fixed together. z_reply_ok / z_reply_err have the same conditional-null shape and are CORRECT to keep it, because pico supplies z_reply_is_ok as a guard and the C side is expected to call it first. The discriminator is whether pico's API gives the caller any way to avoid the unconditional call; where it does not, a conditional null is a memory-safety bug rather than a defensive nicety.

A cdylib IS NOT A DEV-DEPENDENCY, AND THE REASON IS A SYMBOL COLLISION. wz-integration-tests links the REAL zenoh-pico through zenoh-pico-sys for the layer3 codec-parity tests. Adding wz-capi-pico as a dev-dep would put a second definition of z_open / z_put / z_bytes_loan into the same test binary. The drop-in therefore stays at the OS linker boundary, which is also the only shape that witnesses the real deployment: a C program picks ONE library at link time. That is why Layer E builds the crate explicitly instead of cargo doing it as a side effect.

Round 311y477.decision_summary: R311y477 -- the keyexpr-declaration family lands and upstream's z_put.c joins the drop-in witness, closing the named residual R311y476 recorded. The four missing symbols were never four stubs: z_declare_keyexpr needs a real declare plane, and this round builds it. SharedSession gains a THIRD SSOT next to subscriptions and queryables, with a session-global alias id (pico's own model -- safe because a keyexpr mapping table is directional, so one id may go to every peer), a per-face send_declare_keyexpr fan-out, replay onto faces that connect later ordered BEFORE the subscriber and queryable replays so a peer can never see an alias it has not registered, retraction via send_undeclare_kexpr, and z_put routing through publish_aliased_auto when the keyexpr carries a declaration. Ids are refused above u16::MAX rather than wrapped, because the wire's ExprId is u16 in both zenoh and pico and a reused id would silently re-point a peer's live alias. The ABI keeps the literal at slots 0/1 for BOTH the view and the declared arm so the reader stays branchless, with the handle and the mapping id additive and mapping 0 -- reserved on the wire -- as the not-declared discriminant. Leg 3 of the drop-in witness is upstream's own z_put.c, which declares its keyexpr and reaches a real zenoh-pico z_sub. Its outcome CANNOT distinguish an aliased publish from a literal one, so the property rests on a damage: suppressing only the DeclareKeyExpr emit makes the peer drop a Push for an id it never registered and reds leg 3 alone, while a literal-publishing build would be untouched. That damage first produced a FALSE GREEN -- its initial cut left a field unread, failed to compile under deny-warnings, and the suite ran against the previous good binary reporting three passes -- which is why the rebuild is now confirmed before the verdict is read. Two counts from R311y476 are corrected here rather than rewritten: there are 32 upstream examples, not 31, and SIX of them link while calling nothing at all because the generated feature set compiles their bodies out to a stub main. Real-body linkers went 1 to 3. A3 stays 85 EXACT and A4 stays 103/41/16, both correctly -- the atom was already PARTIAL on one axis and already partial-proven on the other.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/keyexpr.rs: the keyexpr-DECLARATION family, 9 exports -- z_declare_keyexpr, z_undeclare_keyexpr, z_keyexpr_loan/_loan_mut/_move/_take/_drop, z_internal_keyexpr_null/_check. z_declare_keyexpr allocates a wire alias id, announces it, and returns an owned keyexpr that OWNS its literal (upstream's z_put.c keeps the declared value past the argv-backed string it built it from, so a borrow would dangle). z_keyexpr_drop frees the local value ONLY and does not retract, which is pico's own split -- drop takes no session, and a drop that silently retracted would lose a live alias when a value went out of scope.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/abi.rs: z_owned_keyexpr_t / z_moved_keyexpr_t added at pico's measured 48 B, and z_loaned_keyexpr_t widened to {start, len, handle, mapping}. Both the view arm and the declared arm keep the LITERAL at slots 0/1, so keyexpr_str stays a single branchless read and the declaration is additive; the alternative (a handle at slot 0 for the owned form) would make slot 0 ambiguous and force every reader to carry a tag. _mapping == 0 is the not-declared discriminant, sound because 0 is RESERVED on the wire. A `borrowed()` constructor replaces six struct literals so the two new slots cannot be left un-zeroed at an inbound site -- a forgotten zero would be read as a live alias id.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/faces.rs: KexprEntry, the THIRD SSOT next to subscriptions and queryables. declare_keyexpr allocates a session-global id (pico's `_z_get_resource_id` model; safe because a mapping table is DIRECTIONAL, so one id may go to every peer), fans send_declare_keyexpr over live faces, and records the entry so face_up REPLAYS it -- ordered BEFORE the sub/qbl replays, because a peer must never see a declaration or Push referencing an alias it has not registered. undeclare_keyexpr drops the entry and emits send_undeclare_kexpr per face. publish_aliased_all fans publish_aliased_auto, treating UnknownMapping as the per-face transient publish_all treats TransportUnavailable (a face whose declare failed mid-teardown has no table entry, and the healthy peers should still get the sample). Id allocation REFUSES above u16::MAX instead of wrapping: the wire's ExprId is u16 in both zenoh and pico, and a reused id would silently re-point a peer's live alias at a different keyexpr.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: z_put reads the declaration off the loaned keyexpr and publishes ALIASED when present, literal otherwise -- the same discriminant pico's _z_write reads off its _z_declared_keyexpr_t.
crates/wz-capi-pico/include/wz_capi_pico.h: the 9 new prototypes plus the z_owned_keyexpr_t / z_moved_keyexpr_t typedefs and the widened z_loaned_keyexpr_t, with the slot table recorded next to them.

Round 311y478.decision_summary: R311y478 -- the platform surface lands and the drop-in gains a full ROUND-TRIP witness: real-body upstream linkers go 3 to 7 and exports 159 to 172 of 726. The target was picked by measurement rather than guess: every real-body example still short of exports was compiled, its undefined-reference set collected, and symbols ranked by how many examples each blocks, then candidate bundles scored by how many they fully CLOSE. That ranking is what identified pico's PLATFORM surface -- z_malloc and z_free block nine examples each and z_sleep_s seven, more than any protocol-level export -- and it also showed why the block alone is not enough: platform plus helpers closes exactly one example, and it took z_declare_background_subscriber, one further export, to take it to four. z_malloc and z_free forward to libc because pico defines them as exactly malloc and free and a C program may mix them with plain free on one pointer; z_clock_now is clock_gettime on the monotonic clock through libc so the constant stays correct per platform; and z_clock_elapsed reproduces pico's signed difference with its clamp to zero rather than a Duration subtraction, which would panic exactly where pico returns zero. The new leg is upstream's own z_ping.c completing five round trips against a real zenoh-pico z_pong, and it is the widest witness in the file because every printed line needs a publish, a foreign process receiving and republishing, wz's background subscriber delivering the echo, and the platform clock, all correct at once. Round 311y480.decision_summary: R311y480 -- preset-ap-full gets an EXECUTABLE and its first foreign witness. The gap was established by the toolchain rather than by reading: cargo build -p wz --no-default-features --features preset-ap-full exits 0, which is all Layer C4 ever proved, while the same invocation against wz-ap-demo answered that the package does not contain this feature. So the 137-feature kitchen sink had no binary, had never been run, and no foreign peer had ever spoken to it, while every pico proof in the tree drives a NARROW single-purpose build instead -- routing-peer for E6, router-hat-router plus time-hlc for E8t, storage-backend for E6e -- leaving COMPOSITION the one axis none of them reaches. A demo-side preset-ap-full key now exists, forwarding the facade preset plus switchboard plus only those demo passthroughs whose atom the preset already carries, and new Layer E9 drives that binary against real zenoh-pico on two planes: a --listen acceptor round-tripping a real z_put, and two real pico clients exchanging through a --peer node. The composition claim is narrow on purpose and the file says so: leg 1 does NOT pin the build (it passes on the default binary) while leg 2 does, since --peer is cfg routing-peer and a wrong build exits 2 at spawn. What the pair genuinely adds is that session-extqos, session-extshm (recorded WIRE-INCOMPATIBLE) and transport-shm are now OBSERVED to leave the pico handshake intact -- something no narrow lane could see. Damage refuted this round's first wording: inverting the tree-forward predicate left leg 2 green, because two co-attached clients never traverse the mesh spanning tree, so the prose was corrected to the co-attached client egress and the routing-routes claim was dropped rather than left bound to code the leg never executes. A3 stays 85 EXACT and A4 stays 103/41/16, both correctly, with only the corpus moving.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: NEW preset-ap-full key. It forwards wz/preset-ap-full plus switchboard (mirroring the preset-ap-client key) plus every demo-side passthrough whose ATOM the preset already carries: tls, quic, quic-datagram, ws, unixsock, vsock, transport-link-unixpipe, locator-iface, scouting-active, transport-lowlatency, session-extcompression, time-hlc, storage-backend, routing-router, routing-routes, routing-peer, routing-token-tables. The passthroughs gate the CLI surface rather than the library feature, so omitting them would compile the transports in and leave argv unable to reach them. Deliberately EXCLUDED: namespace, advanced, group, transport-multilink, transport-qos, storage-backend-filesystem and the adminspace-* family, whose atoms the preset does not list -- including them would make the key a superset of the contract it is named after.

Round 311y481.decision_summary: R311y481 -- the preset-ap-full QUERY PLANE gets its first live foreign witnesses, closing the bundle R311y480 named. Three atoms in the preset carried a codec-parity claim and NOTHING else: query-selector-parameters, query-attachment, query-reply-err. A codec-parity claim compares wz's encoder against pico's own _z_request_encode / _z_response_encode over the same buffer via the live FFI, which pins the BYTES and nothing more -- it cannot see whether they reach a socket, whether a real process decodes them, or whether the emit path stages the record at all. All three are also preset-ap-full-ONLY, so the witness had to drive the composed binary, and y480's carry had established why none existed: wz-ap-demo had no argv that reached them. This round adds that surface (--query-params, --query-attachment as ze_serializer kv pairs, --reply-err, and --query-after-ms for the one-shot ordering) and three Layer E9 legs against real pico: stock z_queryable printing the concatenated selector, the newly-built z_queryable_attachment deserializing both kv pairs, and z_get printing the ERR payload. A4 moves 103/41/16 to 106/38/16; A3 stays 85 EXACT, correctly, since a witness round moves no atom status. Two findings cost real time and are recorded rather than smoothed. The reply-err leg first read as a wz defect -- pico received only the FINAL -- and a hex-dumping TCP relay settled it: 6 bytes where the right binary sends 41, because a later cargo build with default features had written over the same target path and the atom is absent from preset-ap-client. And a wz-runtime-tokio Cargo row claimed attachment-bytes was "selected transitively" by pubsub-attachment / query-attachment, which cargo cannot do; the first attachment-bytes cfg site in that crate exposed it. The edges are fixed, and the comment now also records the damage result that refuted my own first claim about them: reverting them left the ap-full build green, because access-quota already reaches the key, so they are a correctness fix for narrow subsets rather than a dependency of this round.

verification_bullets: EVERY LEG WAS HAND-MEASURED AGAINST REAL PICO BEFORE BEING ASSERTED, and the printed lines are quoted from those runs: z_queryable printed ">> [Queryable handler] Received Query 'demo/key?p=42&kind=hand'"; z_queryable_attachment printed "with attachment:" then "0: wz-k1, wz-v1" and "1: wz-k2, wz-v2"; z_get printed ">> Received an error: wz-reply-err-payload". THE MEASUREMENT THAT LOOKED LIKE A wz DEFECT WAS MY OWN BUILD ORDER, and the wire settled it. The reply-err leg first ran against a target/debug/wz-ap-demo that a later "cargo build -p wz-ap-demo" (default features) had written over, and pico received only the FINAL. A hex-dumping TCP relay showed 6 bytes (ResponseFinal alone) where the correct binary sends 41 (Response(Err) + ResponseFinal). The atom is absent from preset-ap-client, so that build was behaving correctly. Diagnosed by capturing the wire, not by reading the emit path -- three candidate causes (into_response returning Err, dispatch_response dropping, pico consolidation hiding it) were all wrong.

DAMAGE 1 (query-selector-parameters): neutered the meta.parameters threading in request_build.rs, which is the atom's OWN cfg site. Rebuild confirmed by a Compiling wz-ap-demo line BEFORE reading any verdict. The params leg FAILED; the other two stayed ok.
DAMAGE 2 (query-attachment): same treatment of the meta.attachment threading. Rebuild confirmed; the attachment leg FAILED, the other two ok.

DAMAGE 3 (query-reply-err): gated out the send_err call in query.rs's ReplyOut impl. Rebuild confirmed; the reply-err leg FAILED, the other two ok. So all three legs are attributable INDIVIDUALLY -- no damage reds a sibling.

DAMAGE 4 (the ABSENCE assertion is not a tautology): made the ERR arm also send an OK reply. The leg failed with its own intended message, "pico decoded an ERR reply AND an OK sample for the same query", so the !contains("Received PUT") guard is reachable and load-bearing rather than vacuous.

DAMAGE 5 (the ordering precondition is load-bearing): renamed the "hold elapsed" bracket line. BOTH querier legs failed on the hold assertion while the reply-err leg stayed ok -- which is correct, since only the querier legs arrange an ordering.

THE FEATURE-GRAPH FIX WAS DAMAGE-TESTED AND THE RESULT REFUTED MY FIRST CLAIM. Reverting the query-attachment -> attachment-bytes edge left the ap-full demo building GREEN: preset-ap-full carries access-quota, which already reaches that key. So the edges are a correctness fix for NARROW subsets, not a dependency of this round, and the Cargo comment now says so. The asymmetry itself is real and was measured separately: with the forward temporarily UNGATED and ONLY query-attachment enabled, wz_session_core::attachment resolves -- the child had compiled the module while this crate's key was OFF.

THE SKIP IS LOAD-BEARING, BROKEN BOTH WAYS. Layer E's selector with --skip apfull lists 59 tests and 0 matching apfull; WITHOUT the skip it lists 64 and names exactly the five (2 preset legs + 3 query-plane legs). The count is unchanged from the pre-round baseline, so the new tests are filtered rather than counted.

Round 311y482.decision_summary: R311y482 -- the harness was DISCARDING THE EVIDENCE, and that is the defect this entry records; the flake it hid is still open. R311y481 reported a Layer E failure in pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin and said the failing test's NAME was unrecoverable because the lane runs --quiet. That was false: run-ci writes a full log and names it in its own final line, and lines 192-208 of that file carry the test name, the file:line and the panic text. Opening it produced the real finding. Every witness in that file is a C program's printf captured to a file, where libc is block-buffered and only flushes at exit -- and each leg is driven by a self-terminating `-n N` invocation. So on the PASS path exit-flush works, and on the FAIL path the process has by definition not reached its exit count, nothing flushes, and the capture handed to the panic is ZERO BYTES. Measured: an `-n 2` subscriber that has seen one event holds 0 bytes while running and 0 after a kill, against 148 bytes with `stdbuf -oL`. Every failure mode therefore produced a byte-identical empty capture, and the leg-5 panic message asserted one specific mode -- "produces the ALIVE line and nothing else" -- that the harness could not distinguish from any other. R311y480 had already scanned for this and cleared the file as a "deliberate exit-flush design"; that exemption is retracted, since it describes only the path where the output is not needed. A derived scan (C-program binding AND captured stdout) found seven such sites and now finds zero. The leg-5 token holder was worse than unbuffered -- its stdout went to Stdio::null(), throwing away upstream's "Undeclaring liveliness token..." line, which is the one observable that separates "wz never reached the retraction" from "wz retracted and the frame did not arrive". Both sides now capture and the panic reports both, enumerating the three legs they distinguish instead of asserting one. The fix is verified by the failure it produces: with the capi staticlib damaged the leg now prints alive=true and the captured ALIVE line. The flake itself is measured (7/1 file-parallel, 0/10 serial, 0/6 under CPU load) and NOT root-caused; the one hypothesis I formed by reading -- close() latching stop while the drive future sits in a tokio::select! with no outbound drain -- was refuted by a 200 ms pre-latch probe that changed the rate not at all.

The file header's exit-flush paragraph is CORRECTED in place: it is true of the PASS path and was wrong as an exemption, because a failing leg has by definition not reached its `-n` exit count, so libc never flushes and the panic's capture is 0 bytes.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs: the leg-5 TOKEN HOLDER's stdout was `Stdio::null()` -- the same defect on the other side of the same test. It now captures, because upstream's z_liveliness.c prints "Undeclaring liveliness token..." immediately before `z_drop(z_move(token))`, and that line is what separates "wz never reached the retraction" from "wz retracted and the frame did not arrive".

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs: the leg-5 panic message now REPORTS both observables (subscriber saw ALIVE / holder reached undeclare) and enumerates the three legs they distinguish, instead of asserting one mode. Its previous wording claimed a failure "produces the ALIVE line and nothing else" -- a claim about a state the harness could not observe.
crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_advanced_pubsub_zenoh_ext_interop.rs: the "pico z_get (no _anyke)" spawn wrapped in stdbuf, the seventh and last site.
verification_bullets: RETRACTION 1 -- R311y481's verification said "WHICH test failed is unknown because the lane runs --quiet, which prints no test names". FALSE, and the file was there the whole time. `crates/target/run-ci-logs/run-ci-20260731-184619-2689945.log` lines 192-208 carry the FAILED line, the `failures:` block, the test name, the file:line and the panic text. I had grepped only the background-task capture, not the log run-ci names in its own final line. The claim was retracted by opening the file.

RETRACTION 2 -- R311y480's verification said a scan for pico CLIs spawned without stdbuf "flagged two files; both are deliberate exit-flush designs". That exemption was WRONG, and it is why this stood. Exit-flush is a property of the PASS path: a failing leg has not reached its `-n` exit count, so nothing flushes. MEASURED: an `-n 2` z_sub_liveliness that has seen ONE event holds 0 bytes on its capture file while running, and 0 bytes after a kill (the buffer is lost outright). With `stdbuf -oL` the same state shows 148 bytes including the ALIVE line. The two files named in that bullet are exactly the two fixed here.

THE ENUMERATION IS DERIVED, NOT SAMPLED. A scan over every `Command::new` in the corpus that binds a C program (`zenoh_pico_cli_binary` / `dropin_binary`, plus the helper params that are C by contract) AND captures stdout via `Stdio::from` found SEVEN sites; the same scan now reports ZERO. The 134 raw `Command::new` hits are NOT all affected: wz and zenohd are Rust processes writing through unbuffered stderr, which is why the class is C-stdout specifically.

THE FIX IS VERIFIED BY THE FAILURE IT PRODUCES, not by a green run. With the capi staticlib damaged (TokenState::drop no longer retracting) the leg fails and now prints "subscriber saw the ALIVE line: true" plus the captured ALIVE line -- the exact discrimination the old empty capture could not make. NOTE the second trap this exposed: `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests` does NOT rebuild `libwz_capi_pico.so` (wz-capi-pico is not a dependency of that crate), so the first damage read GREEN until `cargo build -p wz-capi-pico` ran.

THE UNDERLYING FLAKE IS MEASURED BUT NOT ROOT-CAUSED, AND IS REPORTED THAT WAY. Rate: file-PARALLEL 7 pass / 1 fail; serial single-test 10 pass / 0 fail; CPU-loaded serial 6 / 0. So it is parallel-specific, not load-specific. The failing run's evidence says the subscriber saw ALIVE and never saw the retraction.

THE ONE HYPOTHESIS I FORMED BY READING WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. `SessionState::close` sets the stop latch and the drive future is a `tokio::select!` arm, so a cancel with no outbound drain looked like the loss. A 200 ms probe inserted BEFORE the latch left the rate unchanged (7 / 1), so the enqueued-frame-loses-a-scheduling-race story is WRONG and is not carried forward as a cause.

GATES on the final tree: Layer E pass (78s, 59 passed) -- unchanged count, so the stdbuf wrappers cost the sweep nothing; the drop-in file 12/12 parallel runs green after the change (NOT a fix claim: the pre-change rate was ~1/8, which 12 passes do not contradict); cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo clippy -p wz-integration-tests --all-targets -D warnings clean. wz_advanced_pubsub_zenoh_ext_interop reports 1 passed / 11 failed BOTH with and without this round's edit (verified by git stash), so those are pre-existing oracle-environment failures on a file Layer E deliberately skips, not a regression.
carry_forward_bullets: A HARNESS THAT READS A FOREIGN PROCESS'S STDOUT MUST LINE-BUFFER IT. "It flushes on exit" is a statement about the path where you do not need the output. Every failure mode of an `-n N` C program collapses to an identical EMPTY capture, so the panic message can only restate the observation. This class is now zero in the corpus by a derived scan; keep it there.

DISCARDING THE EVIDENCE IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE SYMPTOM. Two ledger entries had already looked at this and cleared it -- y480 by exempting "deliberate exit-flush designs", y481 by blaming --quiet for a name the log actually contained. Both times the artifact was reachable and I reasoned about it instead of opening it.

STILL OPEN: the leg-5 parallel flake itself. Rate ~1/8 file-parallel, 0/10 serial. Evidence now says the subscriber sees ALIVE and never the retraction. The select!-cancel-without-drain hypothesis is REFUTED (a 200 ms pre-latch probe changed nothing) -- do not re-litigate it without new evidence. Next step is the WIRE on a failing run (a hand relay, as this round used for the reply-err diagnosis), not more reading.

`cargo test -p wz-integration-tests` DOES NOT REBUILD `libwz_capi_pico.so`, because wz-capi-pico is not a dependency of that crate -- the drop-in links whatever artifact is already in target/debug. Same class as the wz-ap-demo target-path trap. Any damage test on the capi must `cargo build -p wz-capi-pico` first, and Layer E's ability to validate a stale .so is worth a look.

Round 311y483.decision_summary: R311y483 -- one shared artifact path was behind every misdiagnosis this session, and the fix is to make the binary name itself. Three failures were each first read as a wz defect and all three were the same cause: every feature-set-specific lane writes `crates/target/debug/wz-ap-demo`, so whichever cargo build ran last wins and a fixture silently drives the wrong binary. The reply-err leg against an ap-client build (R311y482), a capi damage test that read GREEN because `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests` does not rebuild `libwz_capi_pico.so`, and `wz_advanced_pubsub_zenoh_ext_interop`'s 11 failures -- which R311y482 recorded as pre-existing environment failures and which are NOT: they were the file's own INERT diagnostic against the preset-ap-full binary, which deliberately excludes `advanced`, and the file is 12/12 on its lane's `--features advanced` build. So three fixes land. wz-ap-demo now prints `BUILD FEATURES = [...]` on stderr at the top of main, ahead of the --help return and every mode branch, listing its OWN cargo keys so the line reports what argv can reach. `wz_capi_pico_cdylib` refuses a cdylib older than the wz-capi-pico sources, naming the build command -- verified by touching a source and watching it fail in 0.02s. And the last four DISCARDED C stdouts in the drop-in file now capture and feed the panics that need them, which paid off inside this round: a parallel failure printed that wz DECLARED and PUBLISHED while the peer received nothing, moving the flake from "pico received nothing" to a loss downstream of wz's enqueue at process teardown. That flake is deliberately NOT fixed here. Its fix is named -- wz-capi-pico's teardown drops the per-session runtime without the drain discipline the library already ships as `OpenedSession::drain_to_close` / `WRITER_DRAIN_MS`, which wz-ap-demo's own teardown uses -- but the rate is load-dependent (16/16 green idle against 7/1 under load), so no A/B could be run to a conclusion today, and an unverifiable teardown change in a shared path is worse than none.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/usage.rs + main.rs: NEW `BUILD FEATURES = [...]` line on stderr, emitted at the TOP of main -- ahead of the --help return and ahead of every mode branch, so no invocation can omit it. Each entry is the demo's OWN cargo key, so it reports what argv can REACH. `eprintln!` not `log::info!`: the --router / --peer / --router-hat / --storage-host modes each own their env_logger init further down, so a logged line would be dropped by whichever path had not initialised.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs: the four remaining DISCARDED C stdouts now capture -- the wz-side z_put driver (the most-failing leg), the foreign z_put, the z_pong echo, and the foreign z_liveliness holder -- and each feeds the panic that needs it. Every panic now reports BOTH sides and enumerates the legs they distinguish.

Round 311y484.decision_summary: R311y484 -- the teardown drain was attempted, could not be guarded, and was REVERTED; what the attempt produced instead is a deterministic defect worth more than the flake. Five fixtures were built to make the wz-capi-pico teardown race observable and none of them measured it: load could not summon it (16/16 green idle against 7/1 loaded), a 64 KB pico put was refuted by the pico CLI's own Z_FRAG_MAX_SIZE of 4096, a 3900-byte one passed 4/4 for want of writes to lose, a bare stalling TCP peer could not answer the session handshake at all, and a recording relay between a capi dialer and a capi acceptor needed two corrections before it even ran -- the acceptor had declared no subscriber, so wz correctly emitted nothing, and the stall was longer than the 50 ms drain window, which demands what no bounded best-effort drain can deliver. The corrected fifth fixture is what settled the matter: with the payload at the largest size that reaches the wire at all, it passes 3/3 WITHOUT the fix, so it does not discriminate. The reason it cannot is the finding: wz-capi-pico composes no `transport-fragmentation`, so a z_put above the negotiated 65535-byte batch is dropped SILENTLY while z_put still returns Z_OK -- measured 65000 on the wire against zero wire bytes at 131072 and 262144, three runs each. Filling a loopback socket buffer therefore needs more bytes than the capi will emit, which removes the only lever for leaving a frame provably pending at close. So the drain stays unshipped rather than unverified, the fragmentation gap is now the blocking item ahead of it, and the five refuted fixtures are recorded so a sixth does not repeat them.
changes_bullets: NO CODE CHANGE. The teardown drain was written, measured, and REVERTED; the guard that would have justified it was written, measured, and DELETED. This entry is the record of what was established, so the next attempt does not repeat five fixtures.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: the drain (drop driver/engine/actions, then a bounded await on writer_handle, mirroring the library's OpenedSession::drain_to_close / WRITER_DRAIN_MS) was applied and then reverted. It is still believed correct -- `drop(writer_handle)` only DETACHES, and the per-session runtime drop that follows kills the task -- but no measurement showed it changing any observable, and shipping an unverifiable teardown change into a shared path is worse than not shipping it.
verification_bullets: A NEW DETERMINISTIC DEFECT WAS FOUND ON THE WAY, and it is the durable result of this round. `wz-capi-pico` does NOT compose `transport-fragmentation` (`cargo tree -p wz-capi-pico -e features` reports 0 occurrences), so a `z_put` larger than the negotiated 65535-byte batch has no fragmentation path -- and it is dropped SILENTLY while `z_put` still returns Z_OK. Measured through a recording TCP relay between a capi dialer and a capi acceptor: 200 B and 65000 B reach the wire; 131072 B and 262144 B produce ZERO wire bytes beyond the 48-byte handshake, 3 runs each. A C caller cannot distinguish a delivered put from a discarded one.

FIVE FIXTURES WERE BUILT FOR THE TEARDOWN DRAIN AND NONE MEASURED IT. Recorded individually because each looked like a reproduction: (1) LOAD -- an idle host ran 16/16 green after 7/1 under load, so the flake could not be summoned; (2) a 64 KB pico put -- refuted by the pico CLI fixture's own Z_FRAG_MAX_SIZE of 4096 (the documented reassembly ceiling, not a wz defect); (3) a 3900-byte pico put just under that ceiling -- 4/4 green, too few writes to lose; (4) a bare TCP peer that stalls -- z_open returned -128, since a dumb listener cannot answer the session handshake; (5) a RELAY between a capi dialer and a capi acceptor that stops reading to back the writer up -- which failed for two further reasons before it ran at all (no subscriber declared on the acceptor, so wz correctly emitted nothing; and a stall of 400 ms, longer than the 50 ms drain window, which demands what no bounded best-effort drain can deliver).

THE FIFTH FIXTURE IS THE ONE THAT SETTLED IT, BY FAILING TO DISCRIMINATE. With the payload at 65000 (the largest that reaches the wire at all) and the stall inside the drain window, the test passes 3/3 WITHOUT the fix. So the lever it depends on -- leaving a frame provably pending at close -- is unavailable on this path: filling loopback socket buffers needs more bytes than the capi will emit before it silently drops them. The drain cannot be guarded until the fragmentation gap above is closed.

THE ONE HYPOTHESIS FORMED BY READING REMAINS REFUTED. `SessionState::close` latches stop while the drive future sits in a `tokio::select!`, which looked like the loss; a 200 ms probe inserted BEFORE the latch left the file-parallel rate unchanged at 7/1. Do not re-litigate it without new evidence.

GATES: the tree is byte-identical to the pushed ee2fc6a8 apart from this entry -- `git status` clean after the revert, and `drop(writer_handle)` is back at session.rs:331. No gate moved because no code moved.
carry_forward_bullets: DO THIS FIRST NEXT TIME: `wz-capi-pico` silently drops a `z_put` above the negotiated 65535-byte batch and returns Z_OK. It composes no `transport-fragmentation`. Measured 65000 OK / 131072 and 262144 zero wire bytes, 3 runs each, via a recording relay. That is a deterministic, reproducible defect on a shipped path and it is worth more than the flake that uncovered it -- a C caller has no way to tell a delivered put from a discarded one.

AND IT BLOCKS THE FLAKE'S GUARD. The teardown-drain fix cannot be verified until fragmentation exists, because the only lever for leaving a frame pending at close is a payload big enough to fill the socket buffers, which is above the size the capi will emit. Close the fragmentation gap, THEN guard the drain.

STILL OPEN, unchanged and unshipped: the teardown drain itself (`drive_dial` ends with `drop(writer_handle)`, which only detaches before the per-session runtime is dropped). The fix is written down in this entry's changes and in R311y483's carry; the primitive to copy is `OpenedSession::drain_to_close` / `WRITER_DRAIN_MS`.

FIVE FIXTURES ARE ENUMERATED IN THIS ENTRY'S VERIFICATION. Read them before writing a sixth; three of the five were refuted by a FIXTURE defect rather than by wz, which is the cheaper mistake to avoid twice.

Round 311y485.decision_summary: R311y485 -- oversize puts now fragment, reassemble, and fail loudly when they cannot. R311y484 named one cause (wz-capi-pico composes no transport-fragmentation) and composing it did NOT restore delivery, which is this round's first finding: the AP reassembly slot cap was 65536 while the negotiated TCP unicast batch is 65535, and a chain only forms ABOVE the batch, so the reassembly window was ONE BYTE wide and every fragmented chain was staged past the cap and dropped. That is an AP-PROFILE defect, not a capi one -- TX fragmented correctly and RX could never absorb, which is also why the existing pico frag legs never caught it (pico negotiates batch 2048 with Z_FRAG_MAX_SIZE 4096, so no chain from or to pico ever approached 65536). Fixed by raising sce:slot-size to 1 MiB in the SCXML SSOT plus the missing capi feature; the AP dispatcher is heap-backed so the value is a CAP and not an allocation, and the SCE-emitted array struct is never instantiated in crates/, so the raise adds no static footprint. Second half: above the cap z_put still returned Z_OK and dropped silently, which was R311y484's actual complaint (a C caller cannot tell delivered from discarded) merely relocated. The sender now refuses LOCALLY -- SessionCore carries a max_reassembly_bytes the host declares from the SAME constant TokioReassembly enforces at RX, and emit_frame_or_fragments rejects with SendWireError::ExceedsReassemblyCap at the one point that knows the exact staged length, before any wire byte and before the follow-on SN reserve. Default is usize::MAX (no cap), so every profile that declares none is byte-identical to before, and the field plus gate are compiled out without transport-fragmentation. The refusal is LOCAL by construction and claims only that: a peer's cap is not observable, so it does not promise delivery to a smaller-cap peer -- it removes exactly the case the sender could have known about and reported.

Both halves are needed because wz-capi-pico is BOTH peers in the pico topology.

Regenerated via scripts/regen-codegen.sh; the shared source-hash header moved in 6 sibling emits whose bodies are unchanged.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: new `SessionCore::max_reassembly_bytes` (R::Mutex<usize>, default usize::MAX = no cap, `transport-fragmentation`-gated) with `set_max_reassembly_bytes` / `max_reassembly_bytes` on SessionLinkActions next to `negotiated_batch_mtu`; `dispatch_network_message` resolves it BEFORE the tx_mutex hold (same disjoint-mutex discipline as mtu / sn_mask) and its closure now returns Result; `emit_frame_or_fragments` takes the new `FrameEmit` context struct (grouping ext_qos / sn / reliable / mtu / sn_mask / max_reassembly_bytes rather than tripping clippy::too_many_arguments with an allow) and rejects when the reassembled body would exceed the cap.

DELIVERY GATE: tests/fragmentation_roundtrip.rs publishes 200 / 65000 / 131072 / 262144 / 1044480 bytes and asserts each arrives at the subscriber closure byte-identical (position-dependent filler, so a truncated delivery cannot masquerade as a whole one).

THE BOUNDARY CASE IS A UNIT CHECK, NOT A SIZE CHECK. 1044480 (4 KiB under the cap) must arrive: if the sender's bound and the receiver's bound measured different things -- framed bytes on one side, caller payload on the other -- there would be a band just under the cap that the sender accepts and the receiver still drops. LOUD-FAILURE GATE + DAMAGE TEST: a 4 MiB z_put must not return Z_OK-with-no-delivery. Damaged by removing the one host wiring line in new_session_actions -> the test FAILS with the recorded `z_put returned Z_OK (0)` for 4194304 bytes; restored -> passes. So the assertion binds to the guard and is not a tautology, and the sibling delivery test stayed green under the damage.

THE SN GAP IS DISCLOSED AND GUARDED. A refused send has already minted one Frame SN (the encode is what reveals the size), so it leaves a 1-SN gap in that conduit's ring -- the same gap the pre-R311y206 fragment path put on the wire routinely. The loud-failure test publishes an ORDINARY put AFTER the refusal and requires it to arrive, so the gap is asserted tolerable rather than assumed.

Round 311y486.decision_summary: R311y486 -- the wz-capi-pico teardown drain, the item R311y484 left open as unguardable, is shipped and guarded. y484 built five fixtures and none discriminated because the capi could not emit past one 65535-byte batch and one batch always cleared the writer before teardown; R311y485 lifted that ceiling. This round found the other missing half: volume alone is still not the lever, because the outbound channel is unbounded and the producer is slower than the writer, so the queue is empty at close unless the PEER stops reading -- 768 KiB, and then 6 MiB in eight puts, both passed WITHOUT the fix. The lever is a subscriber closure that sleeps: it runs on the acceptor own drive task, the task that polls the read half, so it stops that peer reading, the receive buffer fills, the dialer send buffer fills behind it, and the writer task blocks with encoded frames still queued. That fixture failed 3/3 before the fix, losing the same 5 of 8 payloads each time, every one after z_put had returned Z_OK. The fix is one call: drive_dial ended with drop(writer_handle), which only detaches, while open_blocking driver thread drops the per-session runtime on the very next line and aborts the task where it stands. The dial role now runs the library own OpenedSession::drain_to_close -- the same primitive accept_loop drains every accepted face through, which is why the LISTEN role never had this defect. Two claims were corrected by measurement instead of shipped. The comment saying face_down must precede the drain or nothing flushes: damaging that order delivered every byte anyway and cost the full WRITER_DRAIN_MS on every z_close instead, 51.5 ms against 0.1-0.5 ms, so the invariant is about LATENCY and now has its own test. And the justification that pico z_close flushes its transport: _z_session_close moves no outbound byte, and pico needs no flush because its z_put writes on the calling thread the whole way down. The honest statement is that our async writer is a queue pico does not have, hence a teardown obligation pico does not have.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: drive_dial's terminal drop(writer_handle) -> reconstruct the OpenedSession and await OpenedSession::drain_to_close. drop() only DETACHES the writer task, and open_blocking's driver thread drops its per-session runtime on the very next line, aborting that task wherever it stands -- which, with an unbounded outbound channel and a peer that has stopped reading, routinely means blocked mid-write with encoded frames still queued. The struct is reconstructed rather than the sequence hand-inlined so the drop order (engine before actions before the bounded await) stays in ONE place: the same library primitive accept_loop drains every accepted face through, which is why the LISTEN role never had this defect.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs: the face_down comment now states what damaging it established, not what reading it suggested -- the ordering is a LATENCY invariant, not a delivery one, and it names the test that holds it.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs + tests/teardown_drain.rs: the pico-contract justification corrected against the vendored source. _z_session_close (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/utils.c:167) moves no outbound byte; pico needs no flush because its z_put writes on the CALLING thread all the way down (_z_write -> _z_send_n_msg -> _z_transport_tx_send_n_msg, src/net/primitives.c:170, src/transport/common/tx.c:487). The accurate claim is that this crate's async writer task is a queue pico does not have, hence a teardown obligation pico does not have.

crates/wz-capi-pico/tests/teardown_drain.rs: NEW, two tests. a_put_immediately_before_z_close_is_drained_not_discarded is the delivery gate; an_idle_z_close_does_not_burn_the_whole_drain_window is the latency gate the green damage forced into existence.
verification_bullets: THE SIXTH FIXTURE IS THE FIRST TO DISCRIMINATE, and the lever is named so a seventh does not re-derive it. A subscriber closure runs on the acceptor's OWN drive task -- the task that polls the link's read half -- so a closure that sleeps stops that peer reading, its receive buffer fills, the dialer's send buffer fills behind it, and the writer task blocks with frames still in its unbounded channel. R311y484's five fixtures all lacked this because the capi could not emit past one 65535-byte batch; R311y485 lifted that ceiling and this round spends it.

BEFORE THE FIX: 3/3 runs FAILED, each losing the SAME 5 of 8 payloads (789504 790528 791552 792576 793600 arrived never; 786432 787456 788480 arrived, absorbed by the socket buffers). Every one had returned Z_OK from z_put. AFTER: 8/8 green, then 5/5 more after the doc corrections.

THE FIRST FIXTURE SHAPE DID NOT DISCRIMINATE AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REBUILT. 768 KiB published and closed on the next line passed 5/5 WITHOUT the fix, and so did 8 such puts back to back (6 MiB): the outbound channel is unbounded, so z_put never blocks, and the producer is slower than the writer -- the queue is empty at close unless the PEER stops reading. Volume alone is not the lever; back pressure is.

DAMAGE A (drain -> the old drop(writer_handle)): the delivery test FAILS with the same 5 payloads, and the latency test stays GREEN. DAMAGE B (face_down moved below the drain): the latency test FAILS at 51.228 ms against its 40 ms budget, and the delivery test stays GREEN. Each assertion binds to a different line, and neither is a tautology.

A GREEN DAMAGE CORRECTED A CLAIM RATHER THAN PASSING ONE. The comment asserted face_down must precede the drain or nothing flushes; damaging it delivered every byte anyway (the writer drains the channel during the window either way -- only the task's EXIT is missed) while costing the full WRITER_DRAIN_MS on every close: 51.5 ms against 0.1-0.5 ms, five rounds each. The invariant is real but it is about latency, so it got its own test and the comment was rewritten.

THE LATENCY BOUND IS THE MINIMUM OVER 5 CLOSES, not one: a loaded host can stretch a single teardown, but the ordering defect stretches EVERY one to the full window, so the minimum separates them without depending on a quiet host.

Round 311y487.decision_summary: R311y487 -- the R311y486 close-frame carry measured on the wire, and RETRACTED by the measurement. That carry recorded that wz-capi-pico z_close emits no Close frame "where pico sends a session Close", and it named the second half as newly cheap to fix. A new Layer E10 counts Close-opening batches through the harness own counting relay for three closers against one wz-ap-demo acceptor: the demo on SIGTERM as a positive control, a real zenoh-pico z_put, and the C ABI z_close. What ships is the calibration as a hard gate (a zero is unreadable until the control reaches one), a delivery precondition on both zero legs so silence cannot be an unopened session, and a single stable assertion that the capi emits none -- pinning current behaviour rather than blessing it. THE CARRY IS RETRACTED BY IT. R311y486 recorded that the capi sends a bare FIN 'where pico sends a session Close'. The first half is confirmed; the second is false. A bare FIN at z_close is INSIDE real pico's own envelope, so the capi's silence is fidelity, not a gap, and no fix is warranted.

THE INSTRUMENT IS CALIBRATED AND THE CALIBRATION IS A HARD GATE. Leg 1 must count at least one Close or the test aborts before publishing any zero -- without it a broken relay, a wrong mid and a genuinely silent client are the same output.
BOTH ZERO LEGS PROVE THEY MEASURED A LIVE SESSION. require_delivery blocks on the acceptor logging SUBSCRIBER FIRED for that leg's own put, so 'sends no Close' cannot be a session that never opened.

A DIVERGENCE DAMAGE WAS RUN AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS INVALID. Swapping leg 3's client for a Close-emitting demo made the count read 1 (the assertion's input moves as intended). Round 311y488.decision_summary: R311y488 -- AP-full now carries the ADVANCED PUB/SUB plane, and a real zenoh-pico witnesses it in both directions. The round started from a measurement of how full "full" is: preset-ap-full is 137 of wz s 246 feature keys and omits 100, among them all 10 ext-pubsub-* atoms. Making it literally full is not a coherent target (a union of every non-platform non-runtime key does not build; no_std and http-send are mutually exclusive through sce-rust-runtime), so the target became the one whole PLANE the kitchen sink dropped, which builds clean on top of the preset. Two blockers stood in the way and both were BUILD facts that had been restated as implementation facts. On the pico side, Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION and _SUBSCRIPTION default to 0, so every advanced example in the vendored tree compiled to its own #else stub main -- and "zenoh-pico has no advanced-pubsub plane whatsoever" had entered a test module doc and the corpus KIND_CLASS note as if it described zenoh-pico. On the wz side, wz-ap-demo deliberately mirrors the library preset, so with the family omitted the AP-full binary logged INERT for --advanced-publish and declared no cache. Both are fixed and both fixes are asserted rather than assumed: the pico build script reads back the GENERATED config.h, and every leg checks the demo s own BUILD FEATURES line before any wire wait. What ships is Layer E11, hosted in the same commit, with two legs through an AP-full peer hub -- wz s cache answering a real z_advanced_sub s history GET, and wz s AdvancedSubscriber recovering a real z_advanced_pub s cache. Three things the round found by measuring rather than reading are recorded as prominently as the result. The first draft of leg 1 PASSED while proving nothing, because the demo s burst is triggered by session-Established and so every sample postdated pico; the fixture asserting its own precondition is what caught it. A publisher-detection leg was written, observed working, and REMOVED, because its ordering is a race the fixture cannot own. And session-extqos is closed as pico-unobservable: a real pico InitSyn carries one extension and no QoS one, and pico has no QoS knob to turn on.
changes_bullets: crates/wz/Cargo.toml: preset-ap-full += the whole ext-pubsub-* family (10 atoms). The "kitchen-sink" preset omitted an entire PLANE and the omission was recorded nowhere -- not in the preset's own comment, not in the ledger, not in any member atom's inventory reason. Same incoherent-artifact shape R311y461 fixed for routing-token-tables, one plane wider. The whole family, not a subset: a publisher without its cache answers a history GET from nothing, and a subscriber without recovery cannot notice the gap it exists to close.

crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: preset-ap-full += advanced + group, and those two LEAVE the R311y480 held-back list by that note's own rule -- it holds back demo keys whose ATOMS the library preset omits, and it no longer omits theirs. Without them the AP-full binary compiled the advanced plane in and could not reach it from argv: --advanced-publish logged INERT and declared no cache.

scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh: -DZ_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION=1 -DZ_FEATURE_ADVANCED_SUBSCRIPTION=1, z_advanced_sub + z_advanced_pub added to TARGETS, and a READBACK of the GENERATED config.h that fails the build when a requested STRING flag did not land. Three mechanisms turn a requested pico feature into a compiled-out one and all are quiet: ON evaluating to 0 in #if (the serial-flag lesson this script already documents), the CMakeLists prerequisite guards that FORCE a flag back to 0 with a mere warning (:386), and the vendor default itself. The generated header is the only place the truth is written down.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/apfull_advanced_pubsub_pico_interop.rs: NEW, two legs, both through an AP-full --peer hub between two of its clients. wz's cache answers a real z_advanced_sub's @adv history GET; wz's AdvancedSubscriber recovers a real z_advanced_pub's cache. Both assert the demo's own BUILD FEATURES line carries `advanced` BEFORE any wire wait.

Round 311y488.publishable_decision_summary: R311y488 -- AP-full now carries the ADVANCED PUB/SUB plane, and a real zenoh-pico witnesses it in both directions. The round started from a measurement of how full "full" is: preset-ap-full is 137 of wz s 246 feature keys and omits 100, among them all 10 ext-pubsub-* atoms. Making it literally full is not a coherent target (a union of every non-platform non-runtime key does not build; no_std and http-send are mutually exclusive through sce-rust-runtime), so the target became the one whole PLANE the kitchen sink dropped, which builds clean on top of the preset. Two blockers stood in the way and both were BUILD facts that had been restated as implementation facts. On the pico side, Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION and _SUBSCRIPTION default to 0, so every advanced example in the vendored tree compiled to its own #else stub main -- and "zenoh-pico has no advanced-pubsub plane whatsoever" had entered a test module doc and the corpus KIND_CLASS note as if it described zenoh-pico. On the wz side, wz-ap-demo deliberately mirrors the library preset, so with the family omitted the AP-full binary logged INERT for --advanced-publish and declared no cache. Both are fixed and both fixes are asserted rather than assumed: the pico build script reads back the GENERATED config.h, and every leg checks the demo s own BUILD FEATURES line before any wire wait. What ships is Layer E11, hosted in the same commit, with two legs through an AP-full peer hub -- wz s cache answering a real z_advanced_sub s history GET, and wz s AdvancedSubscriber recovering a real z_advanced_pub s cache. Three things the round found by measuring rather than reading are recorded as prominently as the result. The first draft of leg 1 PASSED while proving nothing, because the demo s burst is triggered by session-Established and so every sample postdated pico; the fixture asserting its own precondition is what caught it. A publisher-detection leg was written, observed working, and REMOVED, because its ordering is a race the fixture cannot own. And session-extqos is closed as pico-unobservable: a real pico InitSyn carries one extension and no QoS one, and pico has no QoS knob to turn on.

Round 311y489.decision_summary: R311y489 -- preset-ap-full now carries the ADMINSPACE plane, a real zenoh-pico witnesses it COMPOSED in both directions (Layer E12, hosted), and the demo's BUILD FEATURES self-report is made drift-proof by generation. The plane was the third instance of the shape R311y461 and R311y488 each fixed one family wider: a kitchen-sink preset dropping a whole family with the drop recorded nowhere. Here it was sharper, because it was HALF present -- routing-peer has hard-pulled adminspace-core since the preset existed, so an AP-full node already answered @/<zid>/peer with its node record while every leg that makes that record worth querying (per-entity introspection, metrics, plugins, both permission gates, hot-reload, router linkstate) was compiled out. A node that answers its own identity and nothing else is not an admin space. What no lane could previously ask is COMPOSITION: every one of the eight atoms already had a pico witness (y270 core+introspection, y237 plugins, y275 metrics, y276 read gate, y51 write gate), but each builds its own narrow feature set into the ONE shared wz-ap-demo path and they actively assert the others are OFF -- y270's test ends by requiring /metrics ABSENT, which is what makes its own cfg-gate argument work and what makes it structurally unable to be the metrics witness. Six proofs of six parts and none of the whole. Layer E12 runs the whole plane on the AP-full binary in four legs: one z_get reads node record + introspection + metrics + plugins at once; --no-admin-read suppresses every one of them from the SAME build; a real z_put reconfigures the node and reads its own write back through a second z_get; and the same topology without --config-write-permit has pico observe ON THE WIRE that its un-permitted write did not land. The round also found and corrected two of its own errors rather than shipping them: the BUILD FEATURES line under-reported four declared features including adminspace-read, and the first draft of the plugins claim was graded full when it witnesses only one of that atom's three surfaces -- an over-claim that would have moved the A4 count on nothing.
changes_bullets: crates/wz/Cargo.toml: preset-ap-full += the whole adminspace-* family (8 atoms: core / read / write / metrics / introspection-handlers / plugins-handlers / config-hotreload / router-linkstate). The whole family, by the rule R311y488's note states one plane down: the read gate with nothing to read, or the write gate with no hot-reload behind it, are each the half of a pair whose other half is what makes it observable.

crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: the seven adminspace demo keys LEAVE the R311y480 held-back list by that note's own rule -- it holds back demo keys whose ATOMS the library preset omits, and it no longer omits theirs. storage-backend-filesystem deliberately STAYS held back, and that is the rule working rather than an oversight: storage-backend is a preset member, the filesystem VOLUME is not, so including its demo key would make the preset a superset of the contract it is named after.

crates/wz-ap-demo/build.rs: NEW. The BUILD FEATURES self-report is now GENERATED -- the key set from this crate's own [features] table, the on/off answer from cargo's CARGO_FEATURE_<KEY> env vars. It was a hand-maintained push_if! list and it had drifted: adminspace-read, routing-router-hat, storage-backend-filesystem and the preset-* keys were declared features the report never mentioned. Given usage.rs's own promise that 'a key absent from the list is a flag that will be rejected or run INERT', an omission does not read as silence -- it asserts the opposite of the truth to the one reader (a failing fixture) with no other way to check. The generator FAILS THE BUILD on any CARGO_FEATURE_* its manifest scan cannot account for, so the scan cannot be wrong and quiet at the same time.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/apfull_adminspace_pico_interop.rs: NEW, four legs, all on the AP-full binary against real zenoh-pico z_get / z_put. Each asserts the demo's own BUILD FEATURES line BEFORE any wire wait, and the ordering is load-bearing rather than tidy (see verification).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs: leg 3's compiled drop-in no longer has its stderr sent to Stdio::null. Its assertion names three functions any of which could have returned the -1, and with stderr discarded it could never say which -- upstream prints the distinguishing line there. The panic now carries the drop-in's stdout+stderr and the subscriber capture. Evidence only; the underlying intermittency is NOT diagnosed and is carried, not claimed fixed.

verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT THAT SET THE TARGET, taken before any change: preset-ap-full's literal member list was 137 of wz's 246 feature keys, and of the 96 real atoms it omitted, the adminspace family was the one whole plane with an existing pico oracle. It builds clean on top of the preset (measured first, 5.5s), which is what made it the coherent next plane rather than an aspiration.

FOUR LEGS, ALL MEASURED AGAINST A REAL PICO. Leg 1: one z_get returns the node record (live zid + the port THIS test reserved + a sessions entry naming pico's own client session), the per-entity subscriber leg with the zenoh Sources body, the OpenMetrics zenoh_build gauge, and the plugins/storage_manager record at state=Loaded -- four legs, one process, the assertion y270 cannot make. Leg 2: --no-admin-read on the SAME build, pico receives ONLY the terminating Final and every one of those four is required absent. Leg 3: pico GETs acl_deny:[], PUTs acl-deny=mesh/data, GETs again and reads back acl_deny:["mesh/data"] plus the expanded ingress/egress rule pair. Leg 4: same topology without --config-write-permit, and pico's own follow-up GET still reads acl_deny:[] -- the refusal observed on the wire by the implementation that attempted the write, which is stricter than y51's witness reading wz's rejection out of wz's log.

WHICH CODE THE LEGS BIND TO, by damage, each rebuilt before it was read. adminspace.rs metrics key +'X' -> leg 1 ONLY reds, naming the missing leg. admin_read_permit forced true -> leg 2 ONLY reds. admin_write_permit forced true -> leg 4 ONLY reds while leg 3 stays green, which is exactly what the PAIR needs (alone, 'the write did not land' is equally consistent with the write path being broken). The build.rs drift guard was damaged too: making the manifest scan skip one key FAILS the build naming CARGO_FEATURE_ADMINSPACE_READ.

A DAMAGE THAT DID NOT COMPILE PASSED FIRST, and only the exit-code discipline caught it. The metrics damage used format! in a no_std crate; `cargo build ... | tail -3 && cargo test` took tail's status, so the test ran against the STALE binary and reported 4 passed. Re-run with pipefail after fixing the damage to String::push: 3 passed, 1 failed. The green was the old artifact, not the new code.

THE BUILD-CHECK ORDERING IS MEASURED, not asserted. The first draft asserted BUILD FEATURES only in the registration wait's Err arm: running the four legs against an ap-client binary reported the right cause and took 60.15s to do it. Moving the check ahead of the wire wait -- which the demo's own banner makes possible, since it precedes every mode branch -- gives 0.20s for the same diagnosis.

AN OVER-CLAIM WAS CAUGHT BY MEASURING, NOT BY REVIEW. The first draft graded adminspace-plugins-handlers full and A4 moved 106/38/16 -> 107/37/16. Read back with scripts/lib/crossimpl_corpus.py: that atom's only prior claim is R311y237's, graded partial because the atom has THREE surfaces (plugins/**, status/plugins/**, and local_data.plugins) and that test witnesses one. This leg witnesses the same one -- re-measured here: storage_manager is Loaded but nothing STARTS it, so the status legs reply nothing and the node record carries "plugins":{}. Re-graded partial; A4 is back to 106/38/16, and THIS ROUND MOVES NO A4 COUNT. That is the correct outcome, not a shortfall: A4 scores an ATOM, and a second witness of the same surface adds no surface.

Round 311y489.publishable_decision_summary: R311y489 -- preset-ap-full now carries the ADMINSPACE plane, a real zenoh-pico witnesses it COMPOSED in both directions (Layer E12, hosted), and the demo's BUILD FEATURES self-report is made drift-proof by generation. The plane was the third instance of the shape R311y461 and R311y488 each fixed one family wider: a kitchen-sink preset dropping a whole family with the drop recorded nowhere. Here it was sharper, because it was HALF present -- routing-peer has hard-pulled adminspace-core since the preset existed, so an AP-full node already answered @/<zid>/peer with its node record while every leg that makes that record worth querying (per-entity introspection, metrics, plugins, both permission gates, hot-reload, router linkstate) was compiled out. A node that answers its own identity and nothing else is not an admin space. What no lane could previously ask is COMPOSITION: every one of the eight atoms already had a pico witness (y270 core+introspection, y237 plugins, y275 metrics, y276 read gate, y51 write gate), but each builds its own narrow feature set into the ONE shared wz-ap-demo path and they actively assert the others are OFF -- y270's test ends by requiring /metrics ABSENT, which is what makes its own cfg-gate argument work and what makes it structurally unable to be the metrics witness. Six proofs of six parts and none of the whole. Layer E12 runs the whole plane on the AP-full binary in four legs: one z_get reads node record + introspection + metrics + plugins at once; --no-admin-read suppresses every one of them from the SAME build; a real z_put reconfigures the node and reads its own write back through a second z_get; and the same topology without --config-write-permit has pico observe ON THE WIRE that its un-permitted write did not land. The round also found and corrected two of its own errors rather than shipping them: the BUILD FEATURES line under-reported four declared features including adminspace-read, and the first draft of the plugins claim was graded full when it witnesses only one of that atom's three surfaces -- an over-claim that would have moved the A4 count on nothing.

The whole family, by the rule R311y488's note states one plane down: the read gate with nothing to read, or the write gate with no hot-reload behind it, are each the half of a pair whose other half is what makes it observable.

crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: the seven adminspace demo keys LEAVE the R311y480 held-back list by that note's own rule -- it holds back demo keys whose ATOMS the library preset omits, and it no longer omits theirs. storage-backend-filesystem deliberately STAYS held back, and that is the rule working rather than an oversight: storage-backend is a preset member, the filesystem VOLUME is not, so including its demo key would make the preset a superset of the contract it is named after.

crates/wz-ap-demo/build.rs: NEW. The BUILD FEATURES self-report is now GENERATED -- the key set from this crate's own [features] table, the on/off answer from cargo's CARGO_FEATURE_<KEY> env vars. It was a hand-maintained push_if! list and it had drifted: adminspace-read, routing-router-hat, storage-backend-filesystem and the preset-* keys were declared features the report never mentioned. Given usage.rs's own promise that 'a key absent from the list is a flag that will be rejected or run INERT', an omission does not read as silence -- it asserts the opposite of the truth to the one reader (a failing fixture) with no other way to check. The generator FAILS THE BUILD on any CARGO_FEATURE_* its manifest scan cannot account for, so the scan cannot be wrong and quiet at the same time.

Round 311y490.decision_summary: R311y490 -- both R311y489 carries closed, each by measuring the thing rather than mitigating around it. The Layer E flake: PortReservation's exclusion was a `static` mutex, which is PROCESS-global, while cargo runs a crate's test BINARIES concurrently -- 17 were MEASURED alive at once in Layer E's --ignored sweep. So the mutex covered one seventeenth of the contention and the other sixteen ran the bind(0) -> close -> child-bind window against each other, unguarded and continuously. That is exactly the window the type's own doc dismissed as an EXTERNAL process, "sub-millisecond ... not observed in this workspace's CI history", deferring the fix "until the in-process race is confirmed insufficient" -- and the doc's named fix, FD inheritance, is unavailable here anyway because the listener in the leg that surfaced it is zenoh-pico's own z_sub, a foreign C binary with no --listen-fd. The fix widens the exclusion to the scope the design always intended: an flock held for the same window as the mutex, chosen over a sentinel file because the kernel releases it on fd close including SIGKILL. Layer E wall time is unchanged (53/54/66s against a 58/68s baseline), so the serialisation costs nothing measurable. Independently, all six of that suite's readiness barriers move from wait_for_tcp_accept to the liveness-aware wait_for_tcp_accept_alive: a bare TCP connect proves only that SOMETHING accepts, so a child that lost the port race and died left the barrier PASSING against whatever won, and the failure resurfaced downstream as a foreign process exiting -1 with no diagnosis -- which is the exact shape observed. Damage-verified: an unbindable listen locator now fails in 0.11s naming "process exited before accepting ... (status: exit status: 255)" instead of spending the 10s budget to say "never accepted". The second carry -- deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e/Cargo.lock committed stale -- is refreshed, and because NOTHING in this repo checked any of its EIGHT workspaces' locks, new Layer L checks all of them, hosted in the same commit. Full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

Non-unix returns None and degrades to the mutex, which is what every platform had before.

verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT THAT IDENTIFIED THE COMPETITOR: sampling live `target/debug/deps/` processes during Layer E's own `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests -- --ignored` invocation gives a peak of 17. PortReservation's mutex is a `static`, hence one per process, so sixteen siblings were never serialised against each other at all. This is what turns the doc's 'external process' framing from a remote hazard into the lane's own design.

THE RACE REPRODUCED: 17 concurrent processes running bind(0) -> close -> bind(port) lose the port 1 time in 6800 with a MINIMAL window (runs of 0, 1, 1 across 3x6800). With the fix's mechanism (an flock over the same window) the same reproducer loses 0, 0, 0.

A PREDICTION OF MINE WAS REFUTED MID-ROUND AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. I expected a wider window (a 2 ms sleep standing in for fork+exec) to RAISE the loss rate; measured, it fell to 0/2040. The dominant term is the FREQUENCY of reserve calls, not the width of the window -- a tight loop keeps the processes phase-locked on the kernel's ephemeral cursor in a way a real lane does not. So the reproducers bracket the real-world rate, they do not measure it; what is established is the mechanism and that the fix removes it.

THE COST IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: Layer E wall time with the cross-process lock is 53s, 54s and 66s, against a 58s / 68s pre-change baseline. Reservations are held only from pick() to just past the readiness barrier, so serialising them across processes is not observable at lane scale.

THE BARRIER FIX IS DAMAGE-VERIFIED. Pointing leg 3's pico listener at an unbindable locator (tcp/203.0.113.9:1) now fails in 0.11s with 'the real zenoh-pico z_sub never accepted on tcp/127.0.0.1:44425 -- process exited before accepting on 127.0.0.1:44425 (status: exit status: 255)'. Before the change that same condition spent the full 10s LISTEN_TIMEOUT and reported only 'never accepted' -- and, when a rival process held the port, would not have failed there at all.

LAYER L IS DAMAGE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: with the stale lock restored it FAILs naming the file and the exact refresh command; with the refresh applied all EIGHT workspaces report OK (crates, xtask, and six under deploy). Its cache-miss branch is not hypothetical either -- it is what made crates/Cargo.lock look stale on this Linux box during the enumeration, before the io-kit-sys download warmed the cache.

ENUMERATED RATHER THAN SAMPLED, twice, and once it changed the answer: all EIGHT committed locks were checked (not just the one that surfaced), and all SIX readiness barriers in the drop-in suite were converted (not just leg 3's). The lock sweep produced one FALSE POSITIVE -- crates/Cargo.lock under --offline -- which is why Layer L distinguishes the two messages instead of treating any non-zero exit as staleness.

GATES: full local run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 -- the first clean exit-0 sweep of this session, 115 lanes, judged by exit code. Layer L pass (5s), Layer E pass (66s), Layer E12 pass, Layer C2 pass. A4 unchanged at proven=106 partial=38 unproven=16, corpus 135 files / 286 tests; A3 atoms=213 active=130. This round adds no claim and moves no proof count -- it is a harness correctness round.

The Layer E intermittency had a real, measured cause: PortReservation's `static` mutex is process-global while cargo runs 17 test BINARIES concurrently, so the bind->spawn->bind window was unguarded between siblings. Fixed with an flock held for the same window. Do NOT re-add a retry or a longer sleep on top of this; if the leg ever flakes again the remaining candidate is a genuinely unrelated machine process, and the barriers now name a lost bind at the point it happens.
