Round 311y491.decision_summary: R311y491 -- R311y489's "Named bound" closed by DRIVING THE RUN-MODES, and the incoherence that closing it exposed fixed too. y489 shipped E12 with adminspace-config-hotreload and adminspace-router-linkstate listed as compiled-into-the-AP-full-binary but unclaimed, because both live in run-modes the four --peer legs never enter: hot-reload's host is --storage-host, and the linkstate render is inside run_router_hat. That bound was accurate and it was a poor stopping point -- the gap was a run-mode not being driven, so what closes it is driving the run-mode, not asserting harder. Both are now E12 legs on the SAME binary with no second build. Writing the router-hat leg surfaced a preset defect of exactly the shape y489 had just fixed one plane over: preset-ap-full carried the router-hat FOUNDATION (routing-router-hat, via routing-token-tables since y461), the token tables themselves, and -- since y489 -- adminspace-router-linkstate, whose render lives INSIDE run_router_hat, while omitting router-hat-router, the run-mode's own atom. So the library contract carried the plumbing for a mode it did not claim, and wz-ap-demo reached the mode anyway through its own routing-token-tables chain, making the demo a superset of the contract it is named after -- which that manifest's own held-back rule forbids in as many words. The whole router-hat TIER (7 atoms, all measured to build on the preset) is now a member and three demo keys leave the held-back list. Two damages bind the new legs, and the storage-host one is the round's sharpest: suppressing ONLY the real add_storage call while leaving its "storage_manager Started" log firing still reds the leg, because the assertion is on what PICO reads back, not on wz's log. A third correction is the round's own: the first draft of the linkstate assertion was line-scoped against a MULTI-LINE DOT body and failed on a correct render, so a `reply_body` extractor now scopes both it and the metrics assertion to the leg's own body.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/apfull_adminspace_pico_interop.rs: TWO new legs closing y489's Named bound. `apfull_router_hat_linkstate_decoded_by_a_real_pico_z_get` runs TWO AP-full --router-hat nodes -- two, because one renders a single-node graph and an empty successor table, which any build produces -- and pico decodes the routers-net render naming both LIVE zids plus a successor entry keyed on R2 as destination. `apfull_storage_host_hotreload_state_flip_seen_by_a_real_pico` has pico read storage_manager `Loaded`, PUT a storage-add, read `Started`, PUT a storage-del, and read `Loaded` again: a single reading could be a constant, a round trip in both directions cannot.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/apfull_adminspace_pico_interop.rs: new `reply_body` extractor, and it is a CORRECTION not a convenience. pico prints one reply as `>> Received PUT ('<key>': '<body>')`, and two bodies this file reads are MULTI-LINE (the OpenMetrics text and the linkstate DOT), so a `lines().find(..)` sees only `graph {`. The first draft of the linkstate assertion was scoped that way and failed against a perfectly correct render. Both that assertion and leg 1's metrics one are now scoped to the leg's OWN body rather than to the transcript.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/apfull_adminspace_pico_interop.rs: the spawn is factored into `spawn_apfull`, so both new legs inherit the build-check-before-wire-wait ordering R311y490 measured at 0.20s versus 60.15s; the required-feature list gains adminspace-config-hotreload + adminspace-router-linkstate, asserted by EVERY leg because the file's claim is that the preset carries the whole plane.

crates/wz/Cargo.toml: preset-ap-full += the ROUTER-HAT TIER (router-hat-router, -hat-multihat, -multicast-faces, -connect-reconcile, -face-management, -master-election, -orchestration). The whole tier rather than the run-mode atom alone, by the rule R311y488 states: a partial membership is what produced the y461 defect. All seven measured to build clean on top of the preset.

crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: router-hat-router / router-multicast-faces / router-connect-reconcile leave the held-back list now that the library preset claims their atoms. router-hat-router was ALREADY reachable here through the demo's routing-token-tables -- that side effect is the incoherence this round found, and naming the key explicitly makes the membership a decision instead.

scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer E12's --exact loop grows the two new leg names. One invocation per leg, unchanged in shape: a rename or a silently-dropped test then fails the lane instead of shrinking it quietly.

verification_bullets: BOTH RUN-MODES MEASURED REACHABLE ON THE AP-FULL BINARY BEFORE ANY TEST WAS WRITTEN: `--router-hat` logs `router-hat: listening on 127.0.0.1:39979` and `adminspace router legs hosted at @/2b9c6872/router/**`; `--storage-host` logs `config WRITE at @/4030201/peer/config/` and its admin GET. Neither needed a second build -- routing-token-tables already pulls the run-mode into the demo.

THE STORAGE-HOST DAMAGE IS THE SHARPEST OF THE ROUND. Suppressing ONLY the real `manager.add_storage(..)` call while LEAVING its `spawned live storage 'demo' — storage_manager Started` log firing: the host's own log lies, the test's barrier passes on it, and the leg STILL reds with left=`Loaded` right=`Started`. The leg therefore binds to the state a foreign client reads back, not to a wz log line -- the distinction R311y487 had to learn the hard way.

THE LINKSTATE DAMAGE: `linkstate/routers` -> `linkstate/routersX` in adminspace.rs reds that leg ONLY (`pico decoded no reply at @/ad806872/router/linkstate/routers`), with the other five green. Rebuilt before reading, and the build's exit code checked under `set -o pipefail` -- the R311y489 trap where a non-compiling damage let a STALE binary report 4 passed.

A DRAFT ASSERTION OF MINE WAS WRONG AND THE TEST CAUGHT IT, which is worth more than if it had passed. The linkstate leg failed on first run with `got: >> Received PUT ('@/9fa96872/router/linkstate/routers': 'graph {` -- the DOT body is multi-line and my `lines().find(..)` saw only its first line, so the assertion would have failed on a CORRECT implementation. It was never vacuous; it was mis-scoped. Fixed with `reply_body`, and leg 1's metrics assertion re-scoped the same way (it had been matching the whole transcript, where another leg could in principle have satisfied it).

THE PRESET INCOHERENCE, established by reading both manifests rather than inferred: wz's `routing-token-tables = ["routing-router-hat", ..]` pulls the FOUNDATION, while the demo's `routing-token-tables = ["router-hat-router", "wz/routing-token-tables"]` pulls the RUN-MODE. So preset-ap-full claimed the plumbing and the demo entered the mode. Adding the tier makes the contract match what the binary can do; the demo's own held-back rule is what named this a defect.

Round 311y492.decision_summary: R311y492 -- §5.22 plugin-dynamic-loading BUILT, and the four atoms R311y256 deprecated return with it exactly as that round said they would. My previous answer called this family "a design boundary, not an unexercised run-mode"; the inventory says otherwise in as many words, and the user was right to push. R311y256's own reason for plugin-dynamic-loading records the out-of-scope label as REMOVED by user decision 2026-07-13, the atom as "genuinely unbuilt and genuinely buildable ON THE AP PROFILE", and the deferral as a scoping choice "which under NO-DEFERRAL belongs on the schedule". Its deprecation of the other four was CONDITIONAL in its own text: they "exist only to SERVE dynamic loading, so if this is ever built they return with it". So four of five were not a boundary at all, and the fifth was scheduled backlog. What ships is a real vertical: wz-plugin-abi, a no_std zero-dependency repr(C) contract that the host and every plugin cdylib link INDEPENDENTLY (its own crate precisely so a third-party author needs no session implementation behind it); wz-plugin-example, a real loadable cdylib whose ONLY dependency is that ABI crate, which is what demonstrates the ABI suffices; and wz-runtime-tokio::plugin, a dlopen loader with the compatibility gate, the Declared->Loaded->Started FSM and the id-keyed registry. The discriminator was already in the tree and needed nothing invented: AdminPlugin::path carries WZ_STATIC_PLUGIN_PATH "__static__" for a compiled-in subsystem, so a dlopen'd plugin reports the FILE IT WAS LOADED FROM, and pico has decoded that field since R311y237. Layer C1bp witnesses it: one real z_get, two records, one "__static__" and one carrying a path the test computed at runtime. The round's own mistake is recorded as prominently: the two new tests were swept into Layer E's catch-all against the DEFAULT demo binary and failed there, which is the R311y481 shared-artifact trap in a new mask -- caught in 0.10s by the build discriminator, and fixed by the naming convention (wz_plugin_*) that makes a test excludable by its own name.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-plugin-abi (NEW): the host<->plugin C ABI. `no_std`, zero dependencies, all `repr(C)` — the two sides are separate compilation units that need not share a rustc version, so a Rust-ABI type crossing this boundary is UB waiting for a toolchain bump. ENTRY_SYMBOL returns a descriptor and runs NO initialisation, so a host can interrogate compatibility without letting the plugin execute anything. `PluginEntry::compatibility` is the plugin-abi-compat atom: abi_major equality, abi_minor <= host (asymmetric on purpose — a host may know fields a plugin never fills, but a plugin expecting a newer host may reach for one that is not there), and vtable size+align, the check that catches a stale rebuild at an UNCHANGED declared ABI. Its bound is stated rather than implied: it cannot check that the function pointers do what they say, and nothing at a dlopen boundary can.

crates/wz-plugin-example (NEW): a real loadable plugin, `cdylib` ONLY so nothing can link it directly and skip the boundary the proof is about. Its whole dependency list is wz-plugin-abi. `start` records that it ran in a counter exposed through a SEPARATE exported symbol — read through the vtable it would be the mechanism vouching for itself — and honours a `"refuse": true` config, because a plugin that cannot refuse leaves the host's start-failure path unexercised.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/plugin.rs (NEW): the host. `DynamicPlugin::load` is a real dlopen+dlsym; the ABI gate runs BEFORE the vtable pointer is ever followed; `PluginRegistry` is BTreeMap-ordered so the admin reply sequence is deterministic rather than per-process. A library is never dlclosed: `dlclose` while any pointer into it is reachable is a use-after-free the borrow checker cannot see, and zenoh's dynamic_plugin.rs takes the same position. Every plugin string is COPIED at load rather than borrowed out of the mapping.

crates/wz-ap-demo: `--plugin <path>` (repeatable — `parse_repeated`, because a plugin HOST loads a set and `parse_pair` silently keeps only the first) on the `--storage-host` run-mode, which already owns the plugins reply slice and already has a foreign witness reading it. A load or start failure is REPORTED and the node stays up; exiting would let one bad plugin take the node down, which is the opposite of what a plugin host is for.

crates/wz/Cargo.toml + crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: the five §5.22 features stop being `= []` no-op facades and forward to the ONE wz-runtime-tokio key that carries them; `preset-ap-full` gains `plugin-dynamic-loading` (a runtime loader is AP/unix/std-only, which is exactly this preset's profile) and the demo key leaves the held-back list behind it.

docs/.atomic (inventory): plugin-dynamic-loading reserved -> ACTIVE, tagged COMPLETE. The other four deprecated -> RESERVED, tagged FOUNDATIONAL — reserved and not active because A3's invariant is active <=> at least one cfg site and they have none of their own; they ride the single cargo key and are not independently selectable.

scripts/run-ci.sh + .github/workflows/ci.yml: new Layer C1bp, hosted in the same commit. It BUILDS the cdylib first and that is not optional — nothing depends on wz-plugin-example, so without that step the host unit tests skip and the e2e fails on a missing file. Layer E's catch-all sweep gains `--skip wz_plugin`.
verification_bullets: THE INVENTORY, NOT MY JUDGEMENT, SETTLED THE SCOPE. Read before writing any code: plugin-dynamic-loading is `reserved` with 'the out-of-scope label is REMOVED by user decision 2026-07-13 ... genuinely unbuilt and genuinely buildable ON THE AP PROFILE ... under NO-DEFERRAL belongs on the schedule'. plugin-abi-compat is `deprecated` with 'inseparable from plugin-dynamic-loading and obviated with it; if that atom is ever built (it is now real backlog, AP-only), this one returns with it'. My prior 'design boundary' framing was wrong on four of the five atoms and wrong about the fifth being unscheduled.

THE FOREIGN WITNESS, MEASURED BY HAND BEFORE IT WAS A TEST: one real pico z_get over `<root>/plugins/**` returns BOTH `{"name":"wz_example",...,"path":"/home/.../libwz_plugin_example.so","state":"Started"}` AND `{"name":"storage_manager",...,"path":"__static__","state":"Loaded"}`. The path field is the discriminator and it is not invented for this round — `WZ_STATIC_PLUGIN_PATH`'s own doc says wz subsystems 'are STATICALLY linked ... so there is no dylib path', and pico has decoded that field since R311y237. A `.so` path cannot be produced without a dlopen having happened.

DAMAGE: suppressing ONLY the merge of the registry's records into the admin reply slice (`if false { plugins.extend(..) }`) reds leg 1 with 'pico decoded no record for the dlopen'd plugin', while leg 2 stays green. Rebuilt under `set -o pipefail` with the build exit code checked, per the R311y489 stale-artifact trap.

THE ABI GATE IS BOUND BY FIVE UNIT TESTS, and they are unit tests deliberately: the check is a pure function over a descriptor, so every arm is reachable — matching, major bumped in BOTH directions, minor older accepted / newer refused, and layout mismatched at an unchanged ABI in size and in alignment. An e2e cannot reach those without a second plugin built against a different contract, which is why the atom is NOT claimed on the pico transcript.

THE HOST TESTS REALLY DLOPEN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: with the `.so` present, 0 of the 6 legs print a skip; with it removed, 4 do. The skip is LOUD in all four because three of them return early and a silent early return is a green test that proved nothing — this project's own anti-masked-skip rule. Layer C1bp builds the `.so` so the absence cannot arise there.

MY OWN LANE-WIRING DEFECT, caught and fixed rather than diagnosed as a flake. Layer E runs a CATCH-ALL `--ignored` sweep against the DEFAULT demo, and `--skip` matches the TEST FUNCTION name; my two tests were not named to be excludable, so they were swept in and failed against a `preset-ap-client` binary. The build discriminator reported it in 0.10s with `BUILD FEATURES = [default preset-ap-client switchboard]` — which is the only reason it read as a wiring defect and not a loader one. Fixed by the `wz_plugin_*` naming the `wz_storage_host_*` / `apfull_*` convention already uses, plus `--skip wz_plugin`.

TWO MORE GATE FINDINGS, both correct and both mine: A4 containment refused the claim because `plugin-dynamic-loading` was not in wz-ap-demo's feature closure (fixed by adding the atom to the LIBRARY preset first, then the demo key — the held-back rule's own order); and A3 refused the inventory reasons for lacking an implementation-tag prefix, which is the A3 grading protocol working.

Bump `ABI_MAJOR` when a vtable field changes MEANING, `ABI_MINOR` when one is APPENDED, and never edit `PluginVTable` without one of the two — the layout check will catch a stale plugin, but only if the numbers are honest. `PluginEntry::new` fills size/align from the caller's own compilation unit for exactly that reason; a hand-written constant would keep matching after the struct changed.

NOT BUILT, and named so it is not mistaken for done: the loader takes NO plugin config from the admin space (the demo passes `None` to `start`), plugins cannot be loaded or unloaded at RUNTIME (the set is fixed at startup, so there is no dlclose question yet), and there is no zenoh-plugin-rest / -storage-manager `.so` compatibility — a wz plugin implements the wz vtable, not zenoh's. `plugin-static-registration` stays reserved/FOUNDATIONAL: cargo [features] + cfg ARE wz's static registration.

A NEW BINARY-DEP TEST IS AUTO-INCLUDED IN LAYER E'S CATCH-ALL. If it needs a non-default demo binary it MUST be excludable by its TEST FUNCTION name (`--skip` matches the fn, not the file), which is why the convention is `wz_storage_host_*` / `apfull_*` / now `wz_plugin_*`. Getting this wrong looks exactly like a defect in the feature under test until the BUILD FEATURES line is read.

Round 311y494.decision_summary: R311y494 -- Layer L's PREMISE was wrong and hosted CI refuted it on the lane's first hosted run, which is the whole reason the lane was wired hosted in the same commit that added it. R311y490 ran `cargo metadata --locked --offline` per workspace and split the failure messages TWO ways: the `--locked` refusal meant STALE (fail), and the `--offline was specified` message meant a benign cache miss (skip). Hosted produced a THIRD message the split did not cover -- `no matching package named cortex-m found` for all five MCU deploy workspaces, whose dependencies that job never builds and therefore never caches -- and the catch-all refused to guess, so the gap surfaced as a red rather than as a silent pass. Adding the third string would have been the wrong fix. The real defect is that OFFLINE MODE CANNOT CLASSIFY AT ALL: a lock that is stale BECAUSE it lacks a newly-added dependency produces the not-cached message, not the `--locked` one, so the R311y490 design would have SKIPPED precisely the drift the lane exists to catch, and cargo says as much in its own note about surprising offline resolution failures. The fix keeps `--offline` as a fast path and RETRIES ONLINE on any failure that is not the unambiguous `--locked` refusal; with the index available a resolution failure means the lock is genuinely stale and nothing else. A network outage on a cold cache now reports as an unrecognised failure and FAILS, which is the honest outcome for a gate that could not read its input. Verified by reproducing the hosted condition locally with an empty CARGO_HOME rather than by reasoning about it, including the case that mattered most: a stale lock on a COLD cache, which the old design would have skipped, is now reported STALE.
changes_bullets: scripts/run-ci.sh, layer_l_lockfile_freshness: `--offline` stays the FAST path and is conclusive only two ways -- success, or the `because --locked was passed` refusal. Every other offline failure is now treated as INCONCLUSIVE and retried WITHOUT `--offline`. The online attempt is what produces the verdict: with the index reachable, a `--locked` refusal means stale and anything else means the lane could not determine the answer, which FAILS.

The lane's comment block records the refuted premise in place rather than quietly describing the new behaviour, because the next reader's question is why it does two passes: R311y490's two-way split is stated, the third hosted message is named, and the deeper reason the split could not have worked is spelled out.

Per-workspace output now says which path produced the verdict — `OK (offline)` or `OK (online; not in the local cache)` — so a hosted log shows at a glance whether the runner's cache covered a workspace, instead of leaving 'why did this take network' to be inferred.
verification_bullets: THE HOSTED FAILURE REPRODUCED LOCALLY, not reasoned about: `CARGO_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo metadata --locked --offline` in deploy/mcu-freertos-demo prints exactly the hosted string, `error: no matching package named `cortex-m` found / location searched: crates.io index`. The same command without `--offline` against the SAME cold cache returns 0 after fetching the index.
THE WHOLE LANE UNDER A COLD CACHE: 8 of 8 workspaces pass, 7 of them via the online retry (`OK (online; not in the local cache)`) and one still offline. That is the hosted condition, green.

THE VERIFICATION THAT MATTERS MOST, because it is the case the old design would have got WRONG: restoring the pre-R311y490 stale `deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e/Cargo.lock` and running the lane with a COLD CARGO_HOME reports `L FAIL: ... is STALE` and exits 1. Under the R311y490 split that same combination -- stale lock, uncached dependency -- would have printed the not-cached message and SKIPPED green.
Layer 0 pass (shellcheck + actionlint over the edited run-ci.sh), Layer L pass on the warm local cache. The lock file damaged for the stale test was restored and `git status deploy/` is clean.

THE LANE DID ITS JOB EVEN WHILE BEING WRONG. Its catch-all branch existed because R311y490 could not enumerate every cargo failure string, and it FAILED loudly on the one it had not seen instead of assuming benignity. A lane that had defaulted the unknown case to SKIP would have reported green on five workspaces it never checked.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y494 = Layer L retries ONLINE when offline is inconclusive. `--offline` alone cannot tell a stale lock from an uncached dependency, because a lock that is stale for having a NEW dependency fails with the not-cached message. Do not 'fix' a future Layer L red by adding another string to the offline classifier -- that is the mistake this round corrected.

WIRING A NEW LANE HOSTED IN THE SAME COMMIT IS WHY THIS WAS CAUGHT IN ONE ROUND. Layer L was green locally on every run (the dev box caches every dependency) and could only fail where the cache does not -- hosted CI. The project's rule of wiring a lane hosted with its own commit turned a latent, permanently-green-locally gate into a red within hours.

AND THE GENERAL FORM: a gate whose verdict depends on a CACHE is a gate whose verdict depends on the machine. If a lane can only be wrong on a cold cache, verify it on one -- `CARGO_HOME=$(mktemp -d)` reproduces the hosted runner exactly and costs seconds.

PENDING VERDICT: hosted run 30692391077 on 3e2659cb is RED solely on this Layer L defect (job `validate + verify + test`, the only failing job). Every other lane in that run passed, including the other two lanes new this session, C1bp and E12. The next push should re-read the hosted verdict rather than assuming this fix cleared it.

Round 311y495.decision_summary: R311y495 -- Layer C1bp was wired into the wrong hosted job and SKIP-PASSED on its first hosted run, which the run's own conclusion could not show. R311y492 put the step in `validate + verify + test`, a job that does not provision the zenoh-pico CLI. The lane therefore built the plugin cdylib, ran the ABI unit tests, the host dlopen/lifecycle/registry tests and clippy -- 86 seconds of real work -- and then hit its pico guard and printed `Layer C1bp SKIP (zenoh-pico CLI not built)` before reporting pass. The one leg that makes it a CROSS-IMPL proof, a real z_get reading the dlopen'd plugin's path beside the static subsystem's marker, never ran hosted at all. This is the R311y265 masked-skip burn exactly: a SKIP is green, and Layer A4 additionally reads "this lane is in ci.yml" as evidence its proofs executed, so the lie compounds. It was found only by reading the lane's hosted LOG rather than the job's verdict, which is the project's own stated rule for what a hosted verdict is. The fix is to move the step into the cross-impl proof job, which provisions the pico CLI AND already sets WZ_PICO_REQUIRE=1 for precisely this reason -- its env comment calls a SKIP on a binary that job provisions "a provisioning regression wearing a green badge". So the move does two things at once: the guard can no longer be reached, and if provisioning ever regresses the lane FAILS instead of skipping. That job's name, which enumerates its lanes, was two behind (it listed neither E12 nor C1bp) and is corrected with it.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: the `Layer C1bp` step MOVES from the `validate + verify + test` job to the `cross-impl proof lanes` job, beside the E12 step. The step's comment records why in place -- the SKIP-pass, the 86s of work that did happen, and the leg that did not -- so the next reader does not have to reconstruct it from a ledger entry.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: that job's `name:` enumerates its lanes and was stale by two. R311y491 added E12 to the job without touching the name and R311y492 repeated it for C1bp; both are now listed. The name is what a reader scans in the Actions UI, so a stale one hides which proofs a job carries.
No change to scripts/run-ci.sh, to the lane itself, or to any code. The lane was correct; where it ran was not.
verification_bullets: THE SKIP IS QUOTED FROM THE HOSTED LOG, not inferred: run 30692391077, job `validate + verify + test`, `Layer C1bp SKIP (zenoh-pico CLI not built; run: bash scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh)` immediately followed by `INFO Layer C1bp pass (86s)`. The 86s is what makes this worth recording -- the lane did real work and then reported pass on a proof it had not run.

E12, BY CONTRAST, RAN FOR REAL: same run, job `cross-impl proof lanes`, `INFO Layer E12 pass (13s)` with no SKIP line. The difference between the two is entirely which job each was wired into, which is the whole finding.

THE GUARD IS ARMED WHERE THE LANE NOW LIVES, verified by executing it rather than by reading the env block: removing `target/zenoh-pico-cli/z_get` and running the lane with WZ_PICO_REQUIRE=1 gives `Layer C1bp FAIL -- required (WZ_PICO_REQUIRE set) but the zenoh-pico CLI is not built`, rc=1. Without the variable the same condition is a green SKIP, which is what hosted did.

Round 311y496.decision_summary: R311y496 -- preset-ap-full is made literally full, the omission class that produced it is gated, and the fifth missing family turned out to be hiding a functional defect rather than only a manifest gap. MEASUREMENT FIRST: of 213 inventory atoms, 164 were members and 49 were not; building the preset plus all 36 plausible candidates was clean under warnings = "deny", so "every atom this preset can carry" is a measured set, not a judged one. All 36 join (membership 200/213), and the 13 that stay out do so through a reasoned exclusion table whose categories are re-validated against the live inventory on every run. THE HEADLINE FAMILY IS STORAGE, and it is the sharpest instance yet of why membership is not bookkeeping. The preset's own header comment has claimed "all storage" since it was written while carrying four of seventeen atoms: the whole storage MANAGER (storage-mgr-*, seven atoms) and every backend implementation (filesystem / memory-volume / volume-trait / capability) were compiled out, while `--storage-host` remained reachable. So an AP-full node could report a live storage in its admin plane that its storage plane could not serve one foreign read from -- and that is exactly what a real zenoh-pico measured: a z_get on a mount a z_put had just written received only the terminating Final. THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH was a lifetime conflation the run-mode's own doc had NAMED as a "zombie storage" bound and accepted: a storage was created by add_storage(&session, ..) on whichever transient one-shot client carried the storage-add, so its capture subscriber and answering queryable died with that client. R311y496 splits the two lifetimes explicitly -- a storage's DATA is its StorageState over the volume-created backend, its two declaration handles are a BINDING TO ONE SESSION -- via StorageService::rebind and RuntimeStorageManager::rebind_all, which run_storage_host calls on every accepted client. Data outliving the PROCESS stays the volume's job, which is what --storage-host-dir asks for. FIFTH ROUND OF ONE SHAPE IS A MISSING GATE, not five mistakes (y461 routing-token-tables, y488 ext-pubsub-*, y489 adminspace-*, y491 the router-hat tier, y496 storage), so the round builds Layer A5: membership is DERIVED from cargo metadata + the Mnemosyne inventory, every omission must be on the exclusion table, and every exclusion must satisfy its category's predicate against the inventory -- out-of-scope requires an OUT-OF-SCOPE reason, unbuilt requires UNBUILT -- so the table cannot become the silencing mechanism it replaces. A5 also mechanises the wz-ap-demo manifest's own "held back" rule, which was prose; that list is now EMPTY, and storage-backend-filesystem leaving it is what makes --storage-host-dir more than an accepted flag. Layer E13 witnesses the plane on ONE AP-full binary with four legs driven entirely by foreign one-shots, including a durability PAIR (restart on the same dir must return the value; the same script without the flag must not). TWO SELF-CAUGHT ERRORS, both by gates rather than by review: the first version of E13 was FLAKY (leg 2, 3 failures in 8) because a log barrier that is not unique to its event matches the previous occurrence -- read_captured re-reads from offset 0, so wait_for_substring means "has this EVER appeared" -- root-caused to a counted barrier, then measured 12/12; and Layer A4 REFUSED two of this file's first-draft claims (storage-mgr-config, storage-backend-volume-trait) as foreign-NON-observable, which is correct and the claims are withdrawn rather than the exclusions widened. MEMBERSHIP IS A BUILD CLAIM: adding 36 atoms moves neither A3 nor A4 by itself.

Also CONFIG (4), REST (2), the remaining ROUTING (8), the remaining PLUGIN (5), and seven singletons (query-value, transport-multilink, transport-qos, transport-link-serial, locator-serial, api-compat-pico, switchboard). The set was established by BUILDING it, not by judging atoms one at a time: cargo build -p wz --features preset-ap-full plus all 36 is clean under warnings = "deny". crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: the held-back key list is now EMPTY, by the rule that filled it rather than by dropping the rule. namespace / storage-backend-filesystem / transport-multilink / transport-qos were held back because the preset omitted their atoms; the preset now carries them. storage-backend-filesystem is the one whose absence was load-bearing: without it --storage-host-dir was an accepted flag that logged a warning and changed nothing.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: run_storage_host calls manager.rebind_all on every accepted client session. Its "zombie storage" NAMED bound is replaced by the split that removes it: a storage's DATA belongs to the storage, its two declaration handles are a binding to one session. A rebind failure is logged and the session is still served, so the admin surface stays reachable for diagnosis.

A LOG BARRIER THAT IS NOT UNIQUE TO ITS EVENT MATCHES THE PREVIOUS ONE. read_captured re-reads the capture from offset 0 every poll -- it must, or the parent's seek rewinds the child's shared write offset -- so wait_for_substring answers "has this EVER appeared", never "again". Round 311y497.decision_summary: R311y497 -- storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading is BUILT, which discharges R311y256's own conditional deprecation, and preset-ap-full goes 200 -> 201 of 213 with api-compat-c left as the sole OPEN item Layer A5 prints. Three parts, because any one alone is inert: a repr(C) host<->volume ABI crate (wz-volume-abi) that is deliberately NOT merged into wz-plugin-abi and that gates TWO layout fingerprints rather than one, since unlike the plugin ABI it passes a struct BY POINTER; a dlopen host (dynamic_volume) that presents a loaded shared object as an ORDINARY Volume, so register_volume takes it unchanged and every storage-mgr-* feature composes over it for free, with one Arc<Library> shared with each store so the mapping outlives its last user by construction rather than by the leak-and-argue the plugin host needs; and a WIRE widening, storage-add becoming name-at-volume-colon-keyexpr with AddStorage.volume_id an Option, without which no foreign client can reach any volume but the host's own. R311y496 deferred that widening as needing a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body, and it dissolves once the split is applied to the leading NAME field instead of the whole payload: a storage name is not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr grammar is never involved. THE HONEST BOUND, which the witness is designed around rather than despite: the host keeps an in-memory read mirror over every backend because StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value, so within one process a read cannot separate the volume working from the host answering itself -- only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, reaching a fresh host solely through store_entries, which is why leg 2 is a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. Three damages bind three different claims: reverting the wire honouring reds all four legs, skipping register_volume reds legs 1-2 while the negative legs stay green by construction, and skipping the mirror rebuild reds EXACTLY leg 2. SIX SELF-CAUGHT ERRORS, none by review: three unit legs stomping a process-global root (the volume's own put counter read 5 where 2 puts were made), an inventory reason starting with a word outside A3's closed tag set, a comment claiming a log that no caller emitted, an unsafe impl Send with no consumer and an untrue justification, and -- only on the FULL sweep -- a BUILD ERROR in a feature combination the round never considered plus two consumers pinning a log line THROUGH the tail the round inserted into. A green subset is not a green gate. RUNCI_EXIT=0 on the final tree, 120 lanes.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-volume-abi: NEW. The host<->volume C ABI contract, no_std, zero deps, everything repr(C) — linked INDEPENDENTLY by the loader and by every volume cdylib. It is NOT merged into wz-plugin-abi despite the shape similarity: a plugin is started and stopped while a volume creates stores that are put to, deleted from and enumerated, so one crate would make every plugin author link a storage vtable they never fill AND would tie the two ABI version numbers together, so a storage-side field append would invalidate every existing plugin .so for no reason. Two decisions differ deliberately from the plugin ABI. (1) TWO layout fingerprints, not one: this ABI passes a struct BY POINTER (StoredEntry), so that struct's layout is part of the contract and a volume rebuilt against a stale header would agree on the vtable and disagree on the record it is handed — the failure the version numbers cannot see. VolumeEntry::compatibility checks vtable size/align AND entry size/align, with a distinct verdict for each. (2) Enumeration is a host CALLBACK (EntrySink), not a returned array: an array would have to be allocated by one side and freed by the other, which is the classic C-ABI ownership bug this shape simply does not have. The entry symbol is wz_volume_entry, deliberately distinct from wz_plugin_entry, because one shared object may legitimately be both and a shared name would let the wrong loader resolve the wrong vtable while passing its own gate.

crates/wz-volume-example: NEW, cdylib-only so nothing can link it directly and skip the boundary; depends on wz-volume-abi and nothing else, which is itself the demonstration that the ABI crate suffices to author a volume. It is DURABLE (one file per key, hex-encoded because a key legally contains /, with a distinct r stem for the mount-root slot because that slot is the ABSENCE of a key rather than the empty key) and that is load-bearing rather than gratuitous: the host keeps a read mirror over every backend, so a volatile volume's proof could not separate "the host called through the vtable" from "the host answered itself". It exports two out-of-band counters that are deliberately NOT in the vtable, so a test can establish the calls landed without asking the mechanism under test to vouch for itself. A refused configure FAILS CLOSED (clears any root it held): a volume still writing to a root the operator has since replaced, because the replacement was rejected, persists data somewhere nobody named any more.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs: NEW. DynamicVolume::load does the dlopen + dlsym + ABI gate + metadata copy, and configure is a SEPARATE call so a host can interrogate what a .so claims to be before letting it act. DynamicVolume implements the ordinary wz-session-core Volume trait, so RuntimeStorageManager::register_volume takes it unchanged and every storage-mgr-* feature above it composes over a loaded volume for free — a dynamic volume with its own registry would have made all of that conditional. DynamicStore implements StorageBackend with an in-memory read mirror rebuilt from the volume's store_entries at create time, exactly as FilesystemStorage does and for the same reason (StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value). LIFETIME: one Arc<Library> is shared by the volume and every store it creates, so the mapping outlives its last user by CONSTRUCTION — unlike crate::plugin, which leaks its registry because a plugin's effects can outlive every handle the host holds. Both Send impls are justified against the ABI's written threading contract rather than asserted.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs, three things a self-review of the finished module changed rather than documented. (1) load_mirror now CLEARS before rebuilding: its name and doc said replace and the body merged. Today that is a no-op — the only caller runs on a fresh empty store — so it is a latent trap removed, not a live bug fixed, and no test can reach it; stated that way rather than claimed as a fix. (2) put and delete now treat anything that is not one of the DOCUMENTED success codes as a failure, where they had only checked the ERR sentinel: an out-of-contract volume returning an unrecognised code was read as a successful write, which is how a value that was never written comes to be believed persisted. (3) a key or encoding schema carrying an interior NUL is now LOGGED at error before being dropped. The comment claimed "the caller logs it" and no caller did, so a key would have been silently written to the mount-root slot — the prose was wrong, and the behaviour was the thing worth fixing.

crates/wz-session-core/src/adminspace.rs: the storage-add wire payload becomes <name>[@<volume_id>]:<keyexpr> and AdminConfigWrite::AddStorage.volume_id becomes Option<String>. The Option is the load-bearing part: before it the wire always encoded mem and the host overrode it unconditionally, so no client could select a volume AND no host could tell "the client wants mem" from "the client did not say". R311y496 deferred this and recorded why — "it needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body". The delimiter is keyexpr-safe by CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: it is applied only to the leading NAME field, which is a manager-unique identifier and not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar freedom (which @ is part of — every adminspace key begins @/) is untouched. Split on the LAST @ so a name containing one stays addressable; an empty volume is Malformed rather than a storage on a volume called "". to_storage_config resolves None to the new DEFAULT_STORAGE_VOLUME_ID, so a legacy payload produces the identical config it always did.

crates/wz-ap-demo: --storage-volume <path.so> + --storage-volume-config <text> on the --storage-host run-mode, loaded and configured BEFORE the listener binds so a client cannot race startup. The volume is registered under the id the .so ITSELF declares, never an operator-chosen name, or two libraries could be registered as one volume and a storage naming it would land on whichever loaded last. The pair is ONE struct argument (args::DynamicVolumeArgs) rather than two adjacent Option<String> parameters, which is the shape a caller transposes — and a transposed pair here would dlopen the config text and hand the volume its own path as a directory. run_storage_host now applies its own volume choice ONLY when the client named none; a client that NAMES a volume gets that volume or a VolumeNotFound it can see, never a silent substitution. The spawn log gains "on volume '<id>'" AFTER the existing barrier substring, so a witness can assert which volume the storage landed on without moving any existing wait.

Three parts, because one alone is inert: a repr(C) ABI crate (wz-volume-abi), a dlopen host that presents a loaded .so as an ORDINARY Volume so every storage-mgr-* feature composes over it for free (dynamic_volume), and a WIRE widening so a foreign client can name a volume at all — storage-add is now <name>[@<volume_id>]:<keyexpr>. preset-ap-full membership 200 -> 201 of 213; api-compat-c is now the ONLY item A5 prints as OPEN.

A GATE THAT PRINTS AN OPEN ITEM EVERY RUN IS WHY THIS ROUND HAPPENED. R311y256 deprecated this atom on a condition, the condition fired at y492, and nothing would have noticed — the same shape that kept the atom mislabelled for months — except that y496 refused to let the exclusion be silent. The lesson to keep is the mechanism, not the atom: when a status word carries a CONDITION, the condition needs a gate, because the word will outlive it.

WHAT MADE THE WIRE CHANGE POSSIBLE WAS ASKING WHICH FIELD THE DELIMITER LANDS ON. R311y496 deferred volume selection because it "needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body", and read that way it is a hard problem — every plausible delimiter is a legal keyexpr byte. It dissolves once the split is applied to the leading NAME field instead of to the payload as a whole: a storage name is a manager-unique identifier, not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar is simply not involved. The json5 body was never needed for this.

THE READ-MIRROR BOUND IS THE HONEST LIMIT ON EVERY CLAIM HERE, and it is shared with storage-backend-filesystem rather than specific to this atom: the in-tree StorageBackend::get returns a BORROWED value, so any backend whose real store is external must keep an in-memory mirror, and inside one process a read is therefore answered by the mirror. A read cannot distinguish a working volume from a broken one — only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, and it reaches a fresh host solely through store_entries. That is why the witness discriminates on a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. A seam whose get returned owned data would remove the bound for both backends; that is a kernel-seam question, not a follow-up to this round.

RESIDUAL, and it is why the A3 tag is PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE: the operator seam loads ONE volume per host, where zenoh's config declares N volume plugins each with its own config object. N needs a pairing syntax, not a second Vec — pairing an i-th --storage-volume-config to an i-th --storage-volume by argv order is an interface that misfires silently, which is exactly the hazard the singular flag avoids. Per-storage volume config beyond the single configure() string is likewise not client-drivable.

THE DEFERRED §5.23 parse_storage_add_payload FOLLOW-UP NARROWS BUT DOES NOT CLOSE: volume selection is now on the wire, so what remains of it is strip_prefix and the complete flag, which stay host-side choices and are still not foreign-drivable.

NEXT, if the goal is A5 reporting zero OPEN items: api-compat-c, and it is not a membership line either. It is the zenoh-c C ABI drop-in — a sibling surface to api-compat-pico (proven at R311y479) but a different upstream ABI, so it is a build of comparable size to that one, not a flag. Nothing in this round moved it.

A LOG LINE IS AN INTERFACE, AND WHERE YOU ADD TO IT DECIDES WHO BREAKS. Appending a field to the host's storage spawn line looked safe and a comment said so: "the barrier substring is unchanged". It was unchanged relative to the storage NAME and inserted before the "— storage_manager Started" tail, which two older integration tests pin THROUGH. Moving the field to the END of the line makes every existing barrier a prefix by construction, which is strictly better than editing the two consumers — that would have fixed this instance and left the next inserter the same trap. The general rule: extend a log line at the END, and enumerate the pinners before believing any claim about which substring survived.

A GREEN SUBSET IS NOT A GREEN GATE, and this round is the demonstration. Every lane it touched deliberately was green, an interim read of the sweep said "21 lanes passed, 0 ERROR", and FOUR failures were still ahead of that point — including a BUILD ERROR in a feature combination the round never thought about (adminspace-config-hotreload WITHOUT the volume feature, where the new args struct's fields were dead). The verdict is the full run's exit code and nothing earlier.

LANE PLACEMENT IS A DESIGN DECISION AND WAS TREATED AS ONE: the atom's proof is split C1bv (no foreign binary, cannot SKIP anywhere) / E14 (pico job), instead of bundled the way C1bp is. C1bp did 86s of real work and then SKIP-passed the one leg that made it a cross-impl proof because it was wired into a job that provisions no pico CLI (R311y495 found that two rounds late). Applying that lesson costs one extra lane and removes the whole failure mode.

THE HONEST BOUND, which the witness is designed around rather than despite: the host keeps an in-memory read mirror over every backend because StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value, so within one process a read cannot separate the volume working from the host answering itself -- only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, reaching a fresh host solely through store_entries, which is why leg 2 is a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. Three damages bind three different claims: reverting the wire honouring reds all four legs, skipping register_volume reds legs 1-2 while the negative legs stay green by construction, and skipping the mirror rebuild reds EXACTLY leg 2. SIX SELF-CAUGHT ERRORS, none by review: three unit legs stomping a process-global root (the volume's own put counter read 5 where 2 puts were made), an inventory reason starting with a word outside A3's closed tag set, a comment claiming a log that no caller emitted, an unsafe impl Send with no consumer and an untrue justification, and -- only on the FULL sweep -- a BUILD ERROR in a feature combination the round never considered plus two consumers pinning a log line THROUGH the tail the round inserted into. A green subset is not a green gate. RUNCI_EXIT=0 on the final tree, 120 lanes.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-volume-abi: NEW. The host<->volume C ABI contract, no_std, zero deps, everything repr(C) — linked INDEPENDENTLY by the loader and by every volume cdylib. It is NOT merged into wz-plugin-abi despite the shape similarity: a plugin is started and stopped while a volume creates stores that are put to, deleted from and enumerated, so one crate would make every plugin author link a storage vtable they never fill AND would tie the two ABI version numbers together, so a storage-side field append would invalidate every existing plugin .so for no reason. Two decisions differ deliberately from the plugin ABI. (1) TWO layout fingerprints, not one: this ABI passes a struct BY POINTER (StoredEntry), so that struct's layout is part of the contract and a volume rebuilt against a stale header would agree on the vtable and disagree on the record it is handed — the failure the version numbers cannot see. VolumeEntry::compatibility checks vtable size/align AND entry size/align, with a distinct verdict for each. (2) Enumeration is a host CALLBACK (EntrySink), not a returned array: an array would have to be allocated by one side and freed by the other, which is the classic C-ABI ownership bug this shape simply does not have. The entry symbol is wz_volume_entry, deliberately distinct from wz_plugin_entry, because one shared object may legitimately be both and a shared name would let the wrong loader resolve the wrong vtable while passing its own gate.

crates/wz-volume-example: NEW, cdylib-only so nothing can link it directly and skip the boundary; depends on wz-volume-abi and nothing else, which is itself the demonstration that the ABI crate suffices to author a volume. It is DURABLE (one file per key, hex-encoded because a key legally contains /, with a distinct r stem for the mount-root slot because that slot is the ABSENCE of a key rather than the empty key) and that is load-bearing rather than gratuitous: the host keeps a read mirror over every backend, so a volatile volume's proof could not separate "the host called through the vtable" from "the host answered itself". It exports two out-of-band counters that are deliberately NOT in the vtable, so a test can establish the calls landed without asking the mechanism under test to vouch for itself. A refused configure FAILS CLOSED (clears any root it held): a volume still writing to a root the operator has since replaced, because the replacement was rejected, persists data somewhere nobody named any more.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs: NEW. DynamicVolume::load does the dlopen + dlsym + ABI gate + metadata copy, and configure is a SEPARATE call so a host can interrogate what a .so claims to be before letting it act. DynamicVolume implements the ordinary wz-session-core Volume trait, so RuntimeStorageManager::register_volume takes it unchanged and every storage-mgr-* feature above it composes over a loaded volume for free — a dynamic volume with its own registry would have made all of that conditional. DynamicStore implements StorageBackend with an in-memory read mirror rebuilt from the volume's store_entries at create time, exactly as FilesystemStorage does and for the same reason (StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value). LIFETIME: one Arc<Library> is shared by the volume and every store it creates, so the mapping outlives its last user by CONSTRUCTION — unlike crate::plugin, which leaks its registry because a plugin's effects can outlive every handle the host holds. Both Send impls are justified against the ABI's written threading contract rather than asserted.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs, three things a self-review of the finished module changed rather than documented. (1) load_mirror now CLEARS before rebuilding: its name and doc said replace and the body merged. Today that is a no-op — the only caller runs on a fresh empty store — so it is a latent trap removed, not a live bug fixed, and no test can reach it; stated that way rather than claimed as a fix. (2) put and delete now treat anything that is not one of the DOCUMENTED success codes as a failure, where they had only checked the ERR sentinel: an out-of-contract volume returning an unrecognised code was read as a successful write, which is how a value that was never written comes to be believed persisted. (3) a key or encoding schema carrying an interior NUL is now LOGGED at error before being dropped. The comment claimed "the caller logs it" and no caller did, so a key would have been silently written to the mount-root slot — the prose was wrong, and the behaviour was the thing worth fixing.

crates/wz-session-core/src/adminspace.rs: the storage-add wire payload becomes <name>[@<volume_id>]:<keyexpr> and AdminConfigWrite::AddStorage.volume_id becomes Option<String>. The Option is the load-bearing part: before it the wire always encoded mem and the host overrode it unconditionally, so no client could select a volume AND no host could tell "the client wants mem" from "the client did not say". R311y496 deferred this and recorded why — "it needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body". The delimiter is keyexpr-safe by CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: it is applied only to the leading NAME field, which is a manager-unique identifier and not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar freedom (which @ is part of — every adminspace key begins @/) is untouched. Split on the LAST @ so a name containing one stays addressable; an empty volume is Malformed rather than a storage on a volume called "". to_storage_config resolves None to the new DEFAULT_STORAGE_VOLUME_ID, so a legacy payload produces the identical config it always did.

crates/wz-ap-demo: --storage-volume <path.so> + --storage-volume-config <text> on the --storage-host run-mode, loaded and configured BEFORE the listener binds so a client cannot race startup. The volume is registered under the id the .so ITSELF declares, never an operator-chosen name, or two libraries could be registered as one volume and a storage naming it would land on whichever loaded last. The pair is ONE struct argument (args::DynamicVolumeArgs) rather than two adjacent Option<String> parameters, which is the shape a caller transposes — and a transposed pair here would dlopen the config text and hand the volume its own path as a directory. run_storage_host now applies its own volume choice ONLY when the client named none; a client that NAMES a volume gets that volume or a VolumeNotFound it can see, never a silent substitution. The spawn log gains "on volume '<id>'" AFTER the existing barrier substring, so a witness can assert which volume the storage landed on without moving any existing wait.

A GATE THAT PRINTS AN OPEN ITEM EVERY RUN IS WHY THIS ROUND HAPPENED. R311y256 deprecated this atom on a condition, the condition fired at y492, and nothing would have noticed — the same shape that kept the atom mislabelled for months — except that y496 refused to let the exclusion be silent. The lesson to keep is the mechanism, not the atom: when a status word carries a CONDITION, the condition needs a gate, because the word will outlive it.

WHAT MADE THE WIRE CHANGE POSSIBLE WAS ASKING WHICH FIELD THE DELIMITER LANDS ON. R311y496 deferred volume selection because it "needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body", and read that way it is a hard problem — every plausible delimiter is a legal keyexpr byte. It dissolves once the split is applied to the leading NAME field instead of to the payload as a whole: a storage name is a manager-unique identifier, not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar is simply not involved. The json5 body was never needed for this.

THE READ-MIRROR BOUND IS THE HONEST LIMIT ON EVERY CLAIM HERE, and it is shared with storage-backend-filesystem rather than specific to this atom: the in-tree StorageBackend::get returns a BORROWED value, so any backend whose real store is external must keep an in-memory mirror, and inside one process a read is therefore answered by the mirror. A read cannot distinguish a working volume from a broken one — only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, and it reaches a fresh host solely through store_entries. That is why the witness discriminates on a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. A seam whose get returned owned data would remove the bound for both backends; that is a kernel-seam question, not a follow-up to this round.

RESIDUAL, and it is why the A3 tag is PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE: the operator seam loads ONE volume per host, where zenoh's config declares N volume plugins each with its own config object. N needs a pairing syntax, not a second Vec — pairing an i-th --storage-volume-config to an i-th --storage-volume by argv order is an interface that misfires silently, which is exactly the hazard the singular flag avoids. Per-storage volume config beyond the single configure() string is likewise not client-drivable.

THE DEFERRED §5.23 parse_storage_add_payload FOLLOW-UP NARROWS BUT DOES NOT CLOSE: volume selection is now on the wire, so what remains of it is strip_prefix and the complete flag, which stay host-side choices and are still not foreign-drivable.

Round 311y498.decision_summary: R311y498 -- the zenoh-c C ABI arrives, and the session model stops living inside one of the two ABIs that use it. Three parts, sequenced so each had an independent verdict before the next began: a DEPENDENCY INVERSION (the face registry stored one ABI's C closure types and called its make_*_callback constructors, pointing the dependency upward; it now takes callback FACTORIES and never learns what they close over, with the C drop(context) semantics unmoved because the factory owns the Arc), the EXTRACTION of that model into wz-capi-core (1435 lines, judged by the SIBLING's own drop-in gate compiling upstream zenoh-pico examples against wz's cdylib -- a foreign compiler's verdict on foreign source, not a reading of the diff), and wz-capi-c slice 1, where upstream's OWN examples/z_put.c links against wz's cdylib and a real wz subscriber receives what it publishes, with the real libzenohc.so as a REFERENCE arm. Duplicating the model was the alternative and would have copied exactly what a second copy gets wrong invisibly: the race-free close and the drop-outside-the-lock discipline. THE SCOPE IS AN UPSTREAM PROGRAM, NOT A SYMBOL LIST, and that paid immediately -- a hand-picked 12-symbol list drafted before measuring named four symbols zenoh-c never calls and missed three it does, so a hand-written corpus would have reported 12 of 12 while building a different ABI. TWO ARMS because they answer different questions: upstream's examples give representativeness, the real library gives equivalence. Layer A5 now reports NO OPEN ITEMS for the first time since it was built. FOUR THINGS WENT WRONG AND EVERY ONE WAS A REAL DEFECT FOUND BY A GATE. The sharpest: with api-compat-c added to preset-ap-full, EIGHT lanes reddened on rust-lld duplicate symbols -- zenoh-pico and zenoh-c SHARE the z_* namespace, so the two ABIs are mutually exclusive in one binary; it is now a compile_error on the feature pair rather than a comment, and A5 gained an alt-abi category with a predicate. The subtlest: provisioning upstream's published archive beside this machine's install showed they are DIFFERENT ABIs (z_owned_bytes_t 40 vs 32) because the archive defines Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API, so wz had one of the two hardcoded -- silently -- and 'wz is a zenoh-c drop-in' is not a complete sentence until the build is named. Layer A4 refused this round's proof claims three times and was right every time, so the round claims NOTHING on the cross-impl axis. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0, 121 lanes.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-core: NEW, and it is a MOVE rather than a design. The ABI-neutral session model -- the face registry, the declaration SSOT replayed onto each face as it comes up, and the one-OS-thread-per-session drive loop -- left wz-capi-pico so a second C ABI could sit on it. Duplicating it was the alternative, and it would have copied precisely the two things a second copy gets wrong invisibly: the race-free close (the stop latch is set BEFORE the notify, because a Notify permit is single-use and notify_waiters would drop the wakeup) and the drop-outside-the-lock discipline (releasing the last closure reference runs a C drop(context), which is allowed to re-enter the session). 1435 lines, verified by the SIBLING's own gates rather than by review.

crates/wz-capi-pico (the DEPENDENCY INVERSION that made the move possible): the registry stored the C closure TYPES and called make_*_callback to turn them into wz callbacks, which pointed the dependency upward -- an ABI-neutral model reaching into one specific ABI's closure shape. It is inverted through three FACTORY aliases (SubscriberSink / LivelinessSink / QueryableSink): the shim hands in something that MINTS a callback and the registry never learns what it closes over. A factory rather than a ready-made callback because a callback is needed once per FACE -- every declaration is replayed onto each new face. The C drop semantics are unchanged: the factory owns the Arc<CClosure>, so the last one released still runs drop(context).

crates/wz-capi-core, the three edges the compiler and clippy found while moving: session_state(*const z_loaned_session_t) had drifted into the neutral range and went back to the shim (it takes an ABI type); open_blocking returned pico's Z_ERR_GENERIC and became a neutral OpenError, because BOTH C ABIs typedef z_result_t to int8_t and then disagree about the values, so shared code returning one ABI's constant is silently wrong in the other; and a blanket pub(crate)->pub widening made two Result<_, ()> functions public API, which became FanoutError (named to avoid wz-runtime-tokio's own PublishError, already imported in that file).

crates/wz-capi-c: NEW -- the zenoh-c ABI. It ships NO header, unlike its sibling's R1: zenoh-c's header is cbindgen OUTPUT so it IS the ABI, and a wz-authored header would make the drop-in claim untestable by construction. Twelve symbols, and the SCOPE IS AN UPSTREAM PROGRAM rather than a symbol list -- z_put.c links and runs. That distinction paid immediately: a hand-picked list drafted before measuring named four symbols zenoh-c never calls and missed three it does, including zc_init_log_from_env_or, which nothing about implementing a put would suggest.

crates/wz-capi-c/src/abi.rs: the opaque owned/loaned/moved families with const-asserted footprints, plus a `wz_capi_c_layout` export so a gate can READ the numbers out of the shipped cdylib instead of re-transcribing them into a test. THE FOOTPRINTS ARE FEATURE-DEPENDENT and that was measured, not read: upstream's published standalone archive is built WITH Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and a build without it is a different ABI (z_owned_bytes_t 40 vs 32, z_put_options_t 56 vs 48), so "wz is a zenoh-c drop-in" is incomplete until the build is named. publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-core: NEW, and it is a MOVE rather than a design. The ABI-neutral session model -- the face registry, the declaration SSOT replayed onto each face as it comes up, and the one-OS-thread-per-session drive loop -- left wz-capi-pico so a second C ABI could sit on it. Duplicating it was the alternative, and it would have copied precisely the two things a second copy gets wrong invisibly: the race-free close (the stop latch is set BEFORE the notify, because a Notify permit is single-use and notify_waiters would drop the wakeup) and the drop-outside-the-lock discipline (releasing the last closure reference runs a C drop(context), which is allowed to re-enter the session). 1435 lines, verified by the SIBLING's own gates rather than by review.

crates/wz-capi-pico (the DEPENDENCY INVERSION that made the move possible): the registry stored the C closure TYPES and called make_*_callback to turn them into wz callbacks, which pointed the dependency upward -- an ABI-neutral model reaching into one specific ABI's closure shape. It is inverted through three FACTORY aliases (SubscriberSink / LivelinessSink / QueryableSink): the shim hands in something that MINTS a callback and the registry never learns what it closes over. A factory rather than a ready-made callback because a callback is needed once per FACE -- every declaration is replayed onto each new face. The C drop semantics are unchanged: the factory owns the Arc<CClosure>, so the last one released still runs drop(context).

The fix is a cargo feature (`zenoh-c-no-unstable-api`, default = the published archive), a lane that reads the installed header and selects the matching arm, clippy on BOTH arms, and a layout-gate message that names the feature to flip. Had the archive not been provisioned locally, this would have first appeared as a red hosted lane whose cause was my own premise.

THE LANE ITSELF FAILED TWICE FIRST, both real. Then the lane reddened with every assertion passing: a `| grep -q` in the pipe races its upstream's SIGPIPE under this script's `set -o pipefail`, a hazard this tree had already documented AND provided `_runci_guarded_test` to close. The lane now uses the helper.

THE FULL SWEEP CAUGHT A LINK ERROR THAT NO TARGETED LANE DID, and it invalidated a design decision rather than a line of code. With api-compat-c added to preset-ap-full, EIGHT lanes reddened (C1bp, E5, E6, E6b, E6c, E9, E11, E12) on `rust-lld: error: duplicate symbol: z_session_loan_mut` and its siblings: wz-capi-pico and wz-capi-c both export the `z_*` C symbols, because zenoh-pico and zenoh-c share that namespace with different type layouts behind it. The two ABIs are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE in one binary. Every lane the round had run deliberately was green; only building the kitchen-sink preset surfaced it.

The fix is three things, and the first is the one that matters: a `compile_error!` in the wz facade for the feature PAIR, so the conflict is unrepresentable at the layer that understands it rather than discovered from a linker message that names a symbol and no reason. Then preset-ap-full keeps its pico ABI and says in its own comment why the other is absent. Then Layer A5 gains an `alt-abi` category whose predicate is the alt-platform / alt-runtime shape -- an `api-compat-*` other than the one the preset names -- so the exclusion cannot cover an atom that is not an alternative ABI. A5 back to 201 of 213 with 12 exclusions and still no OPEN items.

"WZ IS A ZENOH-C DROP-IN" IS NOT A COMPLETE SENTENCE. zenoh-c's own Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API changes TYPE SIZES, not just option fields -- z_owned_bytes_t is 40 with it and 32 without -- so a drop-in is a drop-in FOR A BUILD. This was found by provisioning upstream's published archive beside the machine's pre-existing install and measuring both; reading would not have found it, and the round had already hardcoded one of the two numbers. Any future claim of ABI compatibility with anything must name the configuration it holds for.

THE CORPUS DECISION PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY, and the number is the argument. A 12-symbol list picked by hand before measuring named FOUR symbols zenoh-c never calls and missed THREE it does. Had the corpus been hand-written, the round would have reported "12 of 12 implemented" while building a different ABI. api-compat-pico's own test file states the principle; this round is its second, quantified instance.

THE EXTRACTION WAS SEQUENCED, NOT BUNDLED, and that is reusable: invert first and let the PROVEN crate's existing gate judge it, then move, then add the new consumer. A refactor of a proven crate mixed into the same commit as a new feature makes a red lane ambiguous; this way each step had an independent verdict before the next began.

TWO C ABIs CANNOT SHARE A BINARY, and nothing short of building them together says so. zenoh-pico and zenoh-c both own the `z_*` symbol namespace, so adding api-compat-c to preset-ap-full turned eight lanes red with duplicate-symbol errors while every lane the round had run deliberately stayed green. The general form: a new `#[no_mangle]` surface is not additive, and the gate that finds it is the one that links everything at once. It is now unrepresentable -- a compile_error on the feature pair -- rather than a comment, and Layer A5 gained an `alt-abi` category so the preset's omission is a recorded decision with a predicate behind it.

RESIDUAL, measured and printed every run: 1 of 22 upstream examples link. The next two are cheap and named -- z_delete needs ONE symbol, z_liveliness two -- and the expensive families are the closure/channel ones (z_sub, z_get, z_queryable), which need the callback plumbing the inversion just made reusable. That ordering is a fact from the coverage report, not a plan.

[honesty] to_admin_json now emits acl_default ("allow"/"deny" base verdict) alongside acl_deny -> a default-deny policy is no longer mis-read as "open" (a bare acl_deny:[] inverts the truth). Rides the existing E6 registration (same test file).

Round 311y500.decision_summary: R311y500 -- api-compat-c slice 2 (the zenoh-c SUBSCRIBER family plus z_delete, 15 symbols measured with nm -u) and the atom's FIRST cross-impl proof. y498 built slice 1 and Layer A4 twice REFUSED a proof annotation on its fixture, correctly: the C program links wz and the observer is a wz node, so no foreign implementation is on the wire. The fix was the COUNTERPARTY, not more ABI -- A4 scores a foreign IMPLEMENTATION opposite wz, not a specific one, and a real zenoh-pico CLI shares no code with either end. Four legs now do that: upstream z_sub.c on wz receives from a real pico z_put; upstream z_put.c on wz reaches a real pico z_sub with the FOREIGN process reporting; upstream z_delete.c has its Del body decoded by that subscriber; and upstream z_sub.c renders an attachment a real pico encoded and a real zenohd routed. A4 unproven 19 -> 18, partial 38 -> 39; upstream-example coverage 1 of 22 -> 4 of 22; exported z_ surface 19 -> 40. The round's real lesson was a RETRACTED inference: pico's attachment publisher delivered nothing, pico-to-pico failed identically, and that was read as 'not a wz defect' -- which is invalid, because matching the reference shows non-divergence and not correctness, wz is a superset rather than a mirror, and a shared cause was never measured. Putting a real zenohd in the path settled it (pico z_pub delivers 3 of 3 through zenohd AND through wz's own --router-hat): the failures were the ABSENT ROUTER, and the witness written off as impossible exists. Also closed a lane hazard y498 left: Layer C4 rebuilds libwz_capi_c.so with DEFAULT features between C1cc and Layer E, so Layer E's catch-all would link upstream examples against a mismatched ABI arm -- both fixtures renamed to carry a capi_c token, --skip capi_c added, and the token registered with Layer C0's naming gate. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0, 122 lanes.

DISCRIMINATOR MATRIX -- every damage rebuilt and the artifact's mtime checked before the result was read. sample_kind_of mapping Put -> DELETE: leg1 FAIL (naming z_sample_kind, capture showing "Received DELETE"), legs 2-3 pass. z_bytes_to_string dropping 3 bytes: leg1 FAIL, others pass. z_declare_subscriber registering keyexpr + "/wrong": leg1 FAIL, others pass. z_put truncating the wire payload by 4: leg2 FAIL with the REAL pico subscriber printing the short payload, others pass. z_delete addressing a different key: leg3 FAIL, others pass. z_owned_subscriber_t 48 -> 40: the layout gate FAILs naming both numbers, so it binds the slice-2 types and not only the y498 ones. bind() dropping the attachment view: the new unit test FAILs.

CALIBRATION, not only refutation. A damage making z_delete publish an empty PUT instead of a Del PASSES leg 3 -- which is why leg 3's doc claims the Del BODY survives a foreign decoder and explicitly does NOT claim the kind. An earlier damage (z_sample_kind returning a constant) did NOT COMPILE, the kind field went dead, and the first run of it read the OLD artifact as green; it was re-cut as a mapping flip that compiles.

RETRACTED MID-ROUND, and the retraction is the honest part. The attachment arm was first reported as having no possible foreign witness, on the reasoning that pico's z_pub_attachment delivers nothing and a real pico z_sub fares no better. That inference was refuted: 'the reference fails identically' shows non-divergence, not correctness, and does not establish a shared cause. Re-measured with a real zenohd in the path -- pico z_pub -> zenohd -> pico z_sub 3 of 3; pico z_pub -> wz --router-hat -> pico z_sub 3 of 3; pico z_pub_attachment -> zenohd -> wz-ap-demo 3 of 3; and pico z_pub_attachment -> zenohd -> upstream z_sub.c on wz's cdylib rendering the attachment. The earlier failures were the ABSENT ROUTER. Leg 4 and Layer C1cd now carry the witness, and damaging z_sample_attachment to report absent reddens leg 4 alone.

Layer C1cd pass under WZ_C1CD_REQUIRE=1, wired onto the interop job because ci.yml builds zenohd there and only there; Layer A4's derived disclosure now lists C1cd under both the pico and zenohd execution sets, so the leg has a hosted witness rather than a local-only one. The fixture's corpus class moved pico -> pico,zenohd accordingly.

THE GAP WAS THE COUNTERPARTY, NOT THE CODE. y498's fixture already compiled upstream's z_put.c against upstream's header and linked wz's cdylib, with the real libzenohc.so as a reference arm -- a strong differential that Layer A4 twice refused a claim on, correctly: the C program links wz and the observer is a wz node, so no foreign implementation is on the wire. That file named the missing leg as "upstream z_sub.c on the REAL libzenohc.so" and deferred it for needing the closure and channel families. That framing looked past a foreign counterparty this tree already provisions: A4 scores a foreign IMPLEMENTATION opposite wz, not a specific one, and a real zenoh-pico CLI shares no code with either end -- so agreement is agreement on the WIRE rather than on a library. Putting pico opposite needed slice 2 built, but not the closure/channel families the deferral assumed.

FOR THE NEXT SLICE: the same coverage report names the cheapest remaining examples -- z_liveliness needs ONE symbol (z_liveliness_declare_token), z_sub_liveliness two, z_pull five. z_get / z_queryable need the channel + closure families (fifo/ring handlers), which is the real next lump.

A FOREIGN CLI CAN HIDE THE PROPERTY, and it did here. Leg 3 was written to assert that a real pico prints DELETE where z_put prints PUT; it was run and refuted -- the vendored pico z_sub prints only key and payload, and a scan of EVERY subscriber example in vendor/zenoh-pico (unix, zephyr, windows, freertos, threadx) found none that renders the kind. So an empty-payload PUT and a DEL are the same two lines at that observer. The leg was rewritten to claim only what the foreign decoder establishes (the Del BODY parses and is delivered) and the limit was CALIBRATED rather than asserted: a damage making z_delete emit an empty PUT PASSES leg 3, and a damage addressing a different key FAILS it. The kind mapping is covered instead by leg 1, whose observer is upstream's own kind_to_str.

DISCRIMINATOR MATRIX (measured, each damage rebuilt before it was read): sample_kind_of Put->DELETE -> leg1 FAIL / legs 2-3 pass; z_bytes_to_string truncating -> leg1 FAIL / others pass; z_declare_subscriber registering a different keyexpr -> leg1 FAIL / others pass; z_put truncating the wire payload -> leg2 FAIL / others pass; z_delete addressing a different key -> leg3 FAIL / others pass; z_owned_subscriber_t 48 -> 40 -> the layout gate FAILs naming both numbers. One damage (z_sample_kind returning a constant) did NOT compile -- the kind field went dead -- and the first run of it read the OLD artifact as green, which is the damage-must-build-first rule firing again.

THE LESSON OF THE ROUND, and it was the user's catch, not mine. z_sample_attachment's PRESENT arm needs pico's z_pub_attachment, which publishes through a DECLARED PUBLISHER, and that delivered NOTHING in the client-to-listening-peer topology the first three legs use. I read that as a wz ingress defect, then calibrated foreign-to-foreign, saw pico z_pub fail into a real pico z_sub too, and concluded 'a pico topology property, not a wz defect'. THAT INFERENCE IS INVALID and the user said so: (1) matching the reference proves wz is not DIVERGENT, never that the behaviour is CORRECT -- wz's north star is a SUPERSET, so if full zenoh delivers where pico does not, wz still owes delivery; (2) I never measured that the two failures share a CAUSE, and a twin can be stable for an unshared reason; (3) the calibration arm itself was suspect, because a pico peer is not a router and z_declare_publisher may simply require one -- in which case the experiment says my topology was invalid, not that the path is unsupported. What I had actually established was only that the topology was not a valid vehicle. Putting a REAL zenohd in the middle decided it: pico z_pub -> zenohd -> pico z_sub delivers 3 of 3, pico z_pub -> wz --router-hat -> pico z_sub delivers 3 of 3, and pico z_pub_attachment -> zenohd -> upstream z_sub.c ON WZ renders the attachment (its serializer field names source/index appear in upstream's own printf). So there is no wz defect AND the witness I had written off as impossible exists -- leg 4 and Layer C1cd are that witness. The generalisable rule: 'the reference fails too' is not a defence; measure the shared CAUSE, or find the topology the feature is DEFINED in.

LANE HAZARD CLOSED IN PASSING: Layer C4's preset matrix rebuilds libwz_capi_c.so with DEFAULT features between C1cc and Layer E, so Layer E's catch-all would have compiled upstream's examples against a header whose z_owned_bytes_t is 32 and linked them to a cdylib built for 40. y498's two legs had the same exposure and nothing named it. Both fixtures and one test fn were renamed so every fn in the family carries capi_c, --skip capi_c added to Layer E, and the token registered with Layer C0's naming gate so a future leg that omits it fails there.

Note that zenohd accepts --rest-http-port with or without the cdylib and then dies in plugin load, so the flag in --help is not evidence the oracle exists -- the leg asserts the .so. Measuring the live plugin BEFORE writing code showed wz's value rendering was UTF-8-driven where zenoh's is ENCODING-driven, and it diverged on five of eight measured rows: JSON payloads were stringified rather than embedded, any non-text encoding rendered its bytes as a bare string rather than base64, a schema-bearing encoding took the wrong arm, timestamp was always null, and an absent encoding hint rendered the empty string where zenoh renders zenoh/bytes. The proof is a DIFFERENTIAL: both bridges subscribe to one zenohd, one foreign PUT fans out to both, and the two JSONSample objects must be equal field for field across the bare-string, embedded-JSON and base64 classes -- expectations produced by the reference in the same run, so the leg cannot rot into agreeing with a transcription, and the timestamp rendering gets a witness no wz-side test could give it. Round 311y502.decision_summary: R311y502 -- a correction to R311y501, filed as a new entry rather than an edit because the y501 entry is frozen. y501's leg 2 differential was UNSOUND, and its own verification bullet (2 passed against a live zenohd) was true but did not mean what it claimed. The leg re-published each class key on a poll cadence until both SSE streams showed it -- but every PUT mints a NEW sample with a NEW timestamp, so when one subscriber's Declare propagated a round later than the other's, each side's first event for that key was a DIFFERENT publish and the differential compared two unrelated renderings. It passed repeatedly, including through a damage probe, and surfaced only on re-running the exact Layer Z leg command: identical key, value and encoding, timestamps one publish apart, same zid. The retry was not the safeguard, it was the defect -- a retry is not a synchronisation primitive, and when the compared thing has IDENTITY, retrying to absorb propagation delay silently changes WHICH thing is compared. The fix separates the two concerns: a WARMUP key is re-published until BOTH streams show it, which is a real barrier on both subscriptions being live, and only then is each class published EXACTLY ONCE. Sample identity is now structural rather than hoped for, and an assertion that each side saw exactly one event for the key converts any recurrence into a loud failure instead of a wrong comparison. 20 consecutive runs pass, but that is corroboration and not the argument -- the old code also passed consecutive runs.
