Round 311y503.decision_summary: R311y503 -- A4 cross-impl unproven 16 -> 5 (proven 113 -> 123, partial 38 -> 39), and ONE of those moves is a real implementation gap closed rather than a claim added. The round's method is uniform: every atom claimed was first BOUND to its own code by a damage probe against a live foreign counterparty (a real zenohd + real zenoh-pico CLIs), never by reading. Six §5.21/§5.19 router/routing FOUNDATIONAL atoms ride the existing wz_router_hat_zenohd_interop corpus, each attributed to the ONE leg its own damage reds: router-orchestration (clearing the router-scoped `dials` after the parse loop reds only the topology leg), routing-data-route-compute (an early return in deliver_to_client_subscribers, compute_data_route block 3, reds only the pico-data-across-the-backbone leg), routing-interest-broker (an early return in respond_to_interest reds the reverse leg, where a real pico publisher's WRITE FILTER is the assertion), router-face-management (voiding absorb_keyexpr_declaration for CLIENT-tier faces only -- so zenohd's router-tier aliases keep resolving -- still reds 7 legs, which is what fixes the direction as pico->wz), routing-query-route-compute (an early return in route_request reds the 3 query legs while every pubsub leg stays green), and router-master-election, which is claimed PARTIAL on MEASUREMENT: forcing is_master=false reds 5 legs (the gate is live) but inverting elect_router's HRW comparison from MAX to MIN leaves all 10 GREEN, because shared_nodes is {self} here -- zenoh only recomputes shared_nodes under router_full_linkstate && peer_full_linkstate (hat/router/mod.rs:384) and a stock zenohd runs peers in gossip, so no foreign router joins wz's linkstatepeers_net. Remaining unproven 5, each measured not assumed: routing-interceptor-hotreload and routing-interest-pending-gc are, on direct read of zenoh, a per-face keyexpr CACHE plus an ArcSwap version (tables.rs:84, face.rs:151) and a CLIENT/p2p_peer-hat mechanism the router hat never populates (hat/router/interests.rs has no pending_current_interests) -- neither has a wire artifact a foreign peer could distinguish, which is the same ground routing-route-cache is already excluded on; session-extqos and session-extshm/transport-shm are the two design decisions a prior round deferred BY USER CHOICE (per-priority SN split; the wire-incompatible SHM ext). Round 311y505.decision_summary: R311y505 -- a real cross-impl DEFECT found and fixed on the wire, and the residual it was hiding behind was recorded backwards. The user picked the SHM establishment ext as the highest-value long-term item on the grounds that it is the only remaining unproven atom that could be silently WRONG rather than merely absent. Establishing that took two things nothing had built: `wz-ap-demo --shm` (the library's `SessionOffer::with_shm` / `connect_and_open_session_with_shm` have existed since R3b and NO spawnable binary ever set them, so wz's one occupant of zenoh's establishment ext space had never faced a foreign decoder) and a `shared-memory` zenohd oracle (`ZENOHD_SHM=1 scripts/build-zenohd.sh`, the third feature-variant oracle after unixpipe and vsock -- zenoh's `default` set omits `shared-memory` and zenohd's default is `zenoh/default`, so the STOCK oracle has no `init::ext::Shm` compiled in at all and can neither send the challenge nor react to an offer; reading its `shm negotiated = false` as an answer would have been the foreign-CLI-hides-the-property trap). With both in place the measurement inverted the inventory on both counts. REFUTED: the recorded WIRE-INCOMPATIBLE residual claimed zenoh's ZExtZBuf reader dispatches on the ID alone and would desync an SHM-enabled peer's ext chain on wz's UNIT@0x2. It does not -- `zenoh-codec/src/common/extension.rs:224` is `if iext::eid(self.header) != ID { return Err(DidntRead) }`, an identity check with the ENCODING BITS INCLUDED, and an SHM-enabled zenohd receiving wz's offer completes the handshake with zero errors. wz's UNIT@0x2 (header 0x02) and zenoh's `Shm` ZBuf@0x2 (header 0x42) are DIFFERENT extensions in one 4-bit id space, exactly as zenoh relies on itself (`QoS = zextunit!(0x1)` beside `QoSLink = zextz64!(0x1)`, `transport/init.rs:147-148`). FOUND: the defect was on the WZ side and in the opposite direction. `unit_ext::chain_has_ext_id` matched capability offers on the 4-bit id field alone, so when the SHM zenohd DIALLED wz, wz read zenoh's `Shm` ZBuf as its own UNIT offer and negotiated `shm negotiated = true` -- wz would then have put SHM DESCRIPTORS on a link whose peer had issued a challenge wz cannot answer and expects payload bytes, i.e. silent corruption at the application layer rather than a clean refusal. Fixed at the MECHANISM rather than the SHM site: `chain_has_ext_eid` matches on `iext::eid`. The same loose match sat under `peer_offered_qos`, where stock zenohd enables QoS by DEFAULT -- but there the acceptance of BOTH forms is FAITHFUL (zenoh's QoS is a genuine dual ext), so that site now names its two forms explicitly instead of inheriting them from a loose match, which is a narrower and checkable claim. Only ONE arm could catch this: zenoh sends `Shm` on the InitSyn unconditionally but on the InitAck only in reply to an offer it understood (`ext/shm.rs:455`), so a wz that merely dials never receives one -- hence `--shm` on the ACCEPT role, and hence leg 2. A4 unproven 5 -> 4 (session-extshm proven).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/ext_header.rs: new `ext_eid(header) = header & !EXT_FLAG_Z` -- zenoh `iext::eid`, the extension IDENTITY, with the encoding and mandatory bits part of it. The pre-existing `ext_id` (`header & 0x0F`) is zenoh's `mid`, the 4-bit id FIELD; conflating the two is what this round measured as a defect, and both are now documented against each other.

crates/wz-session-core/src/unit_ext.rs: `chain_has_ext_id(exts, id)` -> `chain_has_ext_eid(exts, expected_header)`, matching on identity. Callers pass the header they ENCODE, so a capability offer (header == id) and an M-flagged body marker (header == id|M) each match only their own form. New regression test drives both real zenoh shapes (`Shm` ZBuf@0x2 header 0x42, `QoSLink` z64@0x1 header 0x21) plus the M-bit and chain-flag cases.

crates/wz-session-core/src/extqos.rs: `peer_offered_qos` now names BOTH zenoh QoS forms explicitly (`zextunit!(0x1)` OR `zextz64!(0x1)`) instead of accepting anything at id 0x1 in any encoding. Behaviour-preserving -- the existing `peer_offer_detected_for_the_z64_qoslink_form` test stays green -- but the claim is now bounded and cited. extshm / extcompression / extlowlatency switched to the identity match; the SHM BODY marker passes `SHM_BODY_EXT_ID | EXT_FLAG_M`, which is byte-identical to zenoh's `put::ext::Shm = zextunit!(0x2, true)`.

crates/wz-ap-demo: new `--shm` on BOTH roles (`args::Role::{Initiator,Acceptor}`), staged through `initiator_offer` / the new `acceptor_offer`, with a `shm negotiated = <bool>` witness logged by both. The accept path moved from `accept_and_open_session` to `accept_and_open_session_with_offer` (its own thin wrapper), so a build without the flag is byte-identical. New `session-extshm` feature on the demo manifest, NOT in `default`.

Round 311y506.decision_summary: R311y506 -- session-extqos BUILT and PROVEN cross-impl; A4 unproven 4 -> 3 (proven 124 -> 125, partial 39 unchanged), A3 active 133 -> 134. The atom sat `reserved` with 0 cfg sites behind a `= []` facade, its residual named by R311y215: "the z64 QoSLink priority-range wire semantics (S4 wz<->zenohd interop) + the AP WzConfig->set_qos_offer negotiation-from-config (until it lands is_qos never flips true so the wire stays DEFAULT-inert)". Both halves are built. zenoh's QoS establishment ext is DUAL at id 0x1 -- `QoS = zextunit!(0x1)` (presence) XOR `QoSLink = zextz64!(0x1)` (a packed priority range + reliability class), never both -- and wz had only the unit form plus a decoder that read either as "peer does QoS". Now: `State::to_u64` / `try_from_u64` mirrored byte-for-byte (3 tag bits, priority bytes at shifts 3 and 11, reliability bit at 19, INCLUDING upstream's reserved-tag reject arm); the emit choice in ONE function so the unit-XOR-z64 exclusivity is structural rather than a rule two call sites remember; and both DIRECTIONAL merges -- the acceptor demands the initiator's band be a SUBSET of its own and adopts theirs, the initiator demands the acceptor's be a SUPERSET and keeps its own, a declared reliability must MATCH, and every violation ABORTS the handshake as it does upstream (`DriverLoopOutcome::QosLinkRejected` -> `OpenError::QosLinkRejected`, the InitAckCapsRejected teardown pattern). The config path is real, not a test hook: `WzConfig::with_qos_link` -> `FaceSources::qos_link` -> the `_with_offer` open entrypoints on BOTH roles, driven by wz-ap-demo `--qos-band START-END` / `--qos-rel 0|1` in zenoh's own endpoint-metadata spelling. One deliberate strictness deviation: an out-of-range priority BYTE is REFUSED, not clamped -- `Priority::from_wire`'s permissive clamp is correct on the 3-bit Frame field where it is unreachable, but the QoSLink field is a full byte and zenoh errors on it, so reusing the clamp would negotiate a band the peer never offered. THE ORACLE'S OWN SHAPE DECIDED THE FIXTURE, and only measurement found it: the obvious test (zenohd LISTENING on a `?prio=` endpoint, wz dialling a deliberately non-subset band) was run FIRST and the session came UP, because `accept.rs:672` seeds the acceptor state from `link.get_src().to_endpoint()` and zenoh-link-tcp hard-codes an accepted link's src-locator metadata to the empty string (`unicast.rs:103`) -- a listening zenohd has no band at all over TCP. Three of the four legs therefore have zenohd DIAL wz; the limit is upstream's and is recorded in the test's module doc rather than worked around. Layer C4 then caught a SILENT DOWNGRADE the reading had missed: a `schedule_redial` call site without the band would have re-established a flapped peer on the presence-only UNIT ext, keeping none of the configured containment and reporting nothing. The MULTILINK open path has the same hazard and is NOT fixed (its entrypoints take `(qos, band)` and stage no SessionOffer), so that combination now EXITS with a named error -- a per-link band on the aggregation path is a design step, since zenoh's PriorityRange genuinely IS per link. `session-extqos` also LEAVES the `pubsub-priority` alias, where it rode as what the prior comment itself called a pre-y307 asymmetry: harmless while the key was a no-op, but as a real forward it pulls transport-qos -> alloc into `preset-cortex-m4-default`, a no-alloc MCU preset. changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/extqos.rs: +the z64 `init::ext::QoSLink` half. `QosLinkState` (the priority band + reliability class a link declares), `qos_state_to_u64` / `qos_state_try_from_u64` (byte-for-byte zenoh `State::to_u64` / `try_from_u64`: 3 tag bits, priority bytes at shifts 3 and 11, reliability bit at shift 19, and upstream's reject arm for a reserved tag), `encode_qos_link_ext` (header 0x21 = id 0x1 | ENC_Z64), `encode_qos_ext_for` (the ONE place the unit-XOR-z64 choice is made, so the exclusivity is structural), `peer_qos_ext_state` (zenoh `try_from_exts`, both-forms-at-once is the hard error), and the two DIRECTIONAL merges `merge_qos_link_init_syn` (acceptor: subset, adopt theirs) / `merge_qos_link_init_ack` (initiator: superset, keep mine). verification_bullets: CROSS-IMPL, against a live zenohd 1.5.0 built by scripts/build-zenohd.sh (4/4 pass, `wz_qos_link_zenohd_interop.rs`): (1) wz declares NOTHING (`--qos` alone, log says `declared = none`) and reports `negotiated = prio=2-5;rel=1` -- values that exist in no wz configuration on that run and can only have been decoded out of zenohd's z64 body, reliability bit at shift 19 included; (2) wz declaring `prio=3-4` REFUSES a zenohd dialling `?prio=0-7` with `QosLinkRejected(PriorityRangeNotSubset)` and no face reaches the negotiated witness; (3) wz declaring `prio=0-7` ADOPTS the dialer's narrower `prio=2-5` and establishes -- the calibration that rules out "wz refuses every QoSLink"; (4) wz DIALS declaring `prio=1-4;rel=1` and a stock zenohd parses, adopts and echoes it, which wz's superset merge then accepts -- a full encode -> foreign parse -> foreign emit -> decode round trip.

DAMAGE-BOUND, and the two damages SEPARATE the legs rather than bundling them. DECODER (read the range's END byte at shift 12 instead of 11): legs 1, 3 and 4 all red -- `QosLinkRejected(InvalidValue)` on 1 and 4, `Terminal` on 3 -- confirming the decoder is on every leg including the one where wz reads zenohd's InitAck echo. ENCODER (write the reliability bit at shift 18 instead of 19): legs 1 and 4 red (Terminal) while leg 3 stays GREEN, because leg 3 declares no reliability and the damaged bit is never written. Both damages compiled and were driven against the real oracle; all four legs re-measured GREEN after restore, and again after `cargo fmt`.

MEASURED FIRST, and it changed the design: the obvious fixture -- zenohd LISTENING on `tcp/..?prio=2-5`, wz dialling a deliberately non-subset `prio=0-7` -- was run and the session came UP. Round 311y507.decision_summary: R311y507 -- transport-shm + session-extshm CROSS-IMPL PROVEN against a real `zenohd --features shared-memory`; A4 unproven 3 -> 2 (proven 125 -> 126, partial 39 unchanged). wz negotiated shared memory in BOTH directions, where R311y505 measured `false` on both and was right to: wz then put a UNIT ext at establishment id 0x2 while zenoh declares `Shm = zextzbuf!(0x2)`, so `false` was the only correct outcome of a capability marker no zenoh peer recognises. This round built the real thing. zenoh's SHM establishment is a four-message CHALLENGE-RESPONSE over real POSIX segments (`establishment/ext/shm.rs`): InitSyn carries the initiator's AUTH SEGMENT id; the acceptor MAPS that segment, reads the random challenge stored inside, and returns it on InitAck beside its own segment id; the initiator validates the echo against its own challenge, maps the acceptor's segment, and answers with ITS challenge on OpenSyn; the acceptor validates that second echo and confirms with the literal 1 on OpenAck. Each side therefore PROVES map-ability to the other, which is the point -- a token exchange would pass between two hosts that share nothing at all. The segment is a genuine POSIX object at `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` (the NAME is wire format: a foreign peer opens exactly that string through `shm_open`) holding the u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`, with the challenge stored BITWISE-INVERTED exactly as upstream stores it -- load-bearing interop, not obfuscation, and the damage below is what shows it. wz mirrors zenoh's failure ASYMMETRY rather than smoothing it: a version mismatch, an unmappable segment and a wrong echo all degrade to "no shared memory" with the session intact, while only a MALFORMED InitSyn body aborts the handshake (zenoh's single `bail!`, against its tolerant `recv_init_ack` -- a malformed challenge aimed at an acceptor is an attack surface, a malformed answer is just a peer that will not get SHM). The change is OPT-IN and cannot half-mix: the dispatch is EMPTY until an authenticator is installed and an empty one emits nothing, so a deploy that installs none keeps the pre-R311y507 UNIT wire byte-identical; the challenge REPLACES the UNIT ext at the stage seam (they share id 0x2 and must never ride one chain); and the "did the peer offer SHM" predicate follows whichever mechanism is running, which is the correction that made the exchange work at all -- keeping the UNIT predicate for both cleared the capability the moment a peer spoke the real protocol, and it presented as "the challenge-response never completes". Two wz<->wz half-mix legs pin that a ONE-SIDED authenticator leaves BOTH sides without SHM, which is the arm that matters for safety: a session ending with one side believing SHM was on would put descriptors on a wire the peer reads as payload bytes. THE EVIDENCE SPLITS HONESTLY, and the round records how: deleting the challenge CHECK reds the forged-echo unit test but leaves the wz<->wz e2e GREEN, because two cooperating wz peers genuinely map each other. So the e2e proves the exchange COMPLETES and only the forged-echo test proves the check is ENFORCED -- an end-to-end test between two instances of the same implementation can rarely show enforcement, which needs a peer that lies. What keeps transport-shm PARTIAL is now the DATA path rather than establishment: the receiver still copies once off the shared page into wz's owned Sample, there is no segment pool / watchdog / generation, and zenoh's payload descriptor (`ShmBufInfo` with its metadata-segment `MetadataDescriptor{id,index}`) is collapsed to a single segment_id, so PAYLOAD interop is explicitly NOT claimed. Two Layer C1af count pins moved (5 -> 16, 2 -> 5), both measured; the guards firing is them working. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 (122 layers, 0 errors); validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/extshm.rs: +zenoh's SHM establishment CHALLENGE-RESPONSE. The wire shapes -- `SHM_INIT_EXT_HEADER` (0x42, `zextzbuf!(0x2)`) and `SHM_OPEN_EXT_HEADER` (0x22, `zextz64!(0x2)`), the InitSyn body (one VLE segment id), the InitAck body (`challenge` THEN `segment`, zenoh's field order), and the Open-phase bare z64 -- plus `ShmAuthDispatch`, the four-step FSM as a plain object so it can be driven and tested without a socket. `ShmAuthenticator` is the no_std/std seam (`local_segment_id` / `local_challenge` / `open_peer_challenge`). `ShmAuthError::MalformedInitSyn` is the ONE hard error, mirroring zenoh's single `bail!` and its asymmetry with the tolerant `recv_init_ack`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_auth_segment.rs (new): the POSIX AUTH SEGMENT. `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` -- the NAME is wire format, since a foreign peer opens exactly that string via `shm_open` -- holding the u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`. The challenge is stored BITWISE-INVERTED as upstream stores it. 0600 mode and a SHARED advisory `flock` mirroring zenoh; wz deliberately never takes the EXCLUSIVE lock upstream uses to invalidate a recycled segment, because wz has no pool for it to guard and a lock it never meaningfully releases would make its segments look invalid to a peer. `PosixShmAuthenticator` draws its challenge from `getrandom`, not a counter: a guessable one would make the whole exchange decorative.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: the per-session `shm_auth` dispatch + `install_shm_auth` / `shm_auth_installed` and the six FSM seams. `shm_peer_offered` decides what counts as "the peer offered SHM" BY MECHANISM -- the ZBuf challenge when an authenticator is installed, the UNIT marker otherwise; keeping the UNIT predicate for both cleared the capability the moment a peer spoke the real protocol, which presented as "the challenge-response never completes". `stage_shm_challenge` stages only the challenge form and self-clears on id 0x2, so the two forms can never ride one chain; the legacy UNIT branch stays visible at the two Init call sites. `stage_capability` gained the cfg under which it actually HAS a caller (a capability feature AND the enclosing Init block's own `codec-init-body` + unicast role), so it is absent rather than dead in builds without them.

crates/wz-session-core/src/{drive,driver_loop}.rs: the Init-phase demux (acceptor maps on InitSyn, initiator validates the echo on InitAck) and the Open-phase demux, where BOTH roles finally decide `is_shm` -- the acceptor on the initiator's echo, the initiator on the literal 1. A malformed InitSyn body injects FramingError and surfaces `DriverLoopOutcome::ShmChallengeRejected`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `install_shm_authenticator` creates and installs the segment on every `_with_offer` path whose offer asks for SHM (zenoh builds one per MANAGER; wz per SESSION, the same superset direction `set_qos_offer` already takes). A creation failure is `OpenError::ShmAuthSegment`, a hard error rather than a silent downgrade.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/shm_e2e.rs: +3 legs -- the challenge-response over a real driven wz<->wz handshake, and the two half-mix arms proving a one-sided authenticator leaves BOTH sides without SHM.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_shm_establishment_zenohd_interop.rs: both legs' expectations FLIPPED from `shm negotiated = false` to `true`, and the fns renamed to what they now assert. R311y505's `false` was correct for the UNIT mechanism it measured; `true` is what the challenge-response completing looks like. Both claims lose their `partial` grade and each also claims `transport-shm`.

docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json: session-extshm reason -> COMPLETE (the residual R311y505 named is closed); transport-shm reason rewritten -- what keeps it PARTIAL is now the DATA path (the receiver's bounded copy, no segment pool, and zenoh's `ShmBufInfo` payload descriptor), NOT establishment.

scripts/run-ci.sh: the two Layer C1af count pins moved (5 -> 16 for `--lib shm`, 2 -> 5 for `--test shm_e2e`), both MEASURED rather than inferred. The guards firing is them working: this round adds the challenge-response wire tests, the four-step FSM driven both ways, and the wz<->wz half-mix arms, and an unmoved pin would have let a later cfg-out of any of them pass silently.
verification_bullets: CROSS-IMPL, against a real `zenohd --features shared-memory` (`ZENOHD_SHM=1 ZENOHD_SRC=<checkout> scripts/build-zenohd.sh`): BOTH directions report `shm negotiated = true` with the session Established -- wz DIALLING zenohd, and zenohd DIALLING wz. R311y505 measured `false` on both and was right for the UNIT mechanism it had; `true` is what the four-message exchange completing looks like, and it means a real zenoh peer mapped wz's auth segment and echoed the challenge from inside it, and wz did the same to zenohd's.

DAMAGE-BOUND at the wire layer: storing the auth challenge UN-INVERTED on the page (`write_u64(.., CHALLENGE_INDEX, challenge)` instead of `!challenge`) flips both cross-impl legs to `shm negotiated = false` while the session still reaches Established. That binds the green to the exact page layout a foreign zenohd reads -- the inversion is upstream interop, not obfuscation -- and the surviving session is the correct degradation, not a broken link.

A SECOND DAMAGE SPLITS THE EVIDENCE HONESTLY. Removing the challenge CHECK itself (`if alice_challenge != a.local_challenge()`) reds the forged-echo unit test and leaves the wz<->wz e2e GREEN -- because two cooperating wz peers genuinely map each other, so deleting the check does not change their outcome. The e2e therefore proves the exchange COMPLETES; only the forged-echo test proves the check is ENFORCED. Recorded rather than glossed: a suite where every test stays green under a damage is not evidence about that damage.
A THIRD DAMAGE binds the e2e to something: corrupting the acceptor's echo (`alice_challenge ^ 1`) reds both wz<->wz challenge legs while the legacy-UNIT legs stay green.

wz<->wz, 5 legs in `shm_e2e` (all pass): the challenge-response over a real driven handshake; the pre-R311y507 UNIT negotiation still intact; and two half-mix arms showing that a ONE-SIDED authenticator leaves BOTH sides without SHM -- the arm that matters for safety, since a session ending with one side believing SHM was on would put descriptors on a wire the peer reads as payload bytes.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y507 = transport-shm / session-extshm CROSS-IMPL PROVEN; A4 unproven 3 -> 2 (proven 125 -> 126). wz negotiates shared memory with a real `zenohd --features shared-memory` in BOTH directions, using zenoh's actual ZBuf-on-Init / z64-on-Open CHALLENGE-RESPONSE over a real POSIX auth segment rather than the scoped UNIT capability offer/reflect/`&=` that R311y505 recorded as the substitute. The exchange is symmetric proof of MAP-ABILITY: each side publishes a segment holding a random challenge, and only a peer that mapped it can echo what is inside. R311y505's cross-impl assertion of `shm negotiated = false` was correct for the mechanism it measured and is now correctly `true`.

THE REMAINING A4 UNPROVEN IS TWO, AND NEITHER IS A BUILD. `routing-interceptor-hotreload` and `routing-interest-pending-gc` are the `FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE` ratify candidates y503 measured by direct read (a per-face keyexpr cache + ArcSwap version; a mechanism only the client and p2p_peer hats populate, absent from `hat/router`). Shrinking the denominator is still not a proof, so that is a decision round with a ledger entry, not an end-of-session edit.

WHAT KEEPS transport-shm PARTIAL IS NOW THE DATA PATH, not establishment. The receiver still copies once off the shared page into wz's owned Sample, there is no segment pool / watchdog / generation, and zenoh's payload descriptor (`ShmBufInfo` with its metadata-segment `MetadataDescriptor{id,index}`) is collapsed to a single segment_id -- so a negotiated wz<->zenohd session agrees on SHM at establishment while PAYLOAD interop is NOT claimed. That is the next slice if the atom is pushed further.

A SUITE WHERE EVERY TEST STAYS GREEN UNDER A DAMAGE IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THAT DAMAGE. Deleting the challenge check left the wz<->wz e2e green, because two cooperating peers genuinely map each other; only the forged-echo unit test moved. Generalise: an end-to-end test between two instances of the SAME implementation can show a protocol COMPLETES and almost never that a check is ENFORCED -- enforcement needs a peer that lies, which means a hand-built message, not a second honest process.

`ZENOHD_SRC=<checkout>` IS WHAT MAKES `build-zenohd.sh` TAKE SOURCE A on a machine with no cargo git checkout of zenoh (this one). Without it the script falls to crates.io and can build NEITHER the plugin cdylibs NOR any feature variant, so the shared-memory oracle looks unobtainable when it is one env var away. That is also how R311y506's REST-plugin install fix got exercised.

Round 311y508.decision_summary: R311y508 -- routing-interceptor-hotreload BUILT and PROVEN BY TEST, after this round first proposed excluding it from the A4 denominator on a reading alone. A4 proven 126 -> 127, unproven 2 -> 1. wz now mirrors zenohs version-keyed interceptor cache: InterceptorChain carries a version, every set_interceptors installs both flow chains at a fresh one, and a per-(face, keyexpr) verdict table computed against an older chain is recomputed instead of served. The ACL precomputes all nine governed actions for a keyexpr; an interceptor whose verdict does not factor through the keyexpr caches nothing and keeps the direct path; a face with no resolved subject caches nothing, since the subject can resolve later and a cached admit would outlive its reason. The version is the load-bearing part: without the bump a live reconfigure installs a new chain while every face already seen keeps answering out of the OLD policy, which is a reconfigure that silently does nothing for exactly the traffic that is flowing. THE ROUND REVERSED ITS OWN FIRST ANSWER and that is the finding. It opened by proposing routing-interceptor-hotreload and routing-interest-pending-gc as FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE exclusions, argued from direct reads of zenoh 49c8a53 and wz. The exclusion was reverted and the atom built, because a read establishes what a mechanism IS while only a damage probe establishes whether a claim about it is load-bearing -- and the first cross-impl claim written here was VACUOUS. Deleting the version bump left the pico E2E green: the host started with no ACL, admit_inbound short-circuits an EMPTY chain before the cache is consulted, so nothing was cached for the config write to invalidate. The leg now starts its host with a deny on an UNRELATED keyexpr, which changes nothing it asserts and makes the foreign publishers admitted traffic leave a verdict table behind. So a claims FIXTURE PRECONDITION is part of the claim: when an optimisation sits behind a fast-path guard, the proof must first show the guard was passed, and the guard is invisible in the assertion. Damage-bound at three levels, each run: the bump deletion reds the new invalidation unit test on its recompute witness, reds the pre-existing config-write merge test on the verdict itself, and reds the pico cross-impl leg 2 of 2 runs at its 30s barrier while the undamaged build passes 7 of 7 in about 2.4s. Two intermediate failures were diagnosed rather than waved off: cargo test does not rebuild wz-ap-demo, so the binary on disk was still the previous probes DAMAGED build -- neither flakiness nor a bug, and diagnosable only because the demo logs its BUILD FEATURES. Residual, named: the cache serves the INGRESS flow of the linkstate peer only; the egress chain and the RouterForwarder path still recompute per message, correct but uncached, so PARTIAL is the honest tag. Unit 593 pass with the feature ON and 592 with it OFF; fmt and clippy clean; A3 pass with active 134 -> 135; validate_workspace orphan new=+0. Full run-ci is owed before any push and is not part of this commit.

The `Interceptor` trait gains `compute_keyexpr_cache(ctx, keyexpr)` and `intercept_cached(ctx, msg, cache)`, both defaulted, so an interceptor whose verdict does not factor through the keyexpr -- a rate limiter, a size cap -- caches nothing and keeps the direct path. `build_chain_versioned` stamps both flow chains of one install with the same version. A4 proven 126 -> 127, unproven 2 -> 1. wz now mirrors zenohs version-keyed interceptor cache: InterceptorChain carries a version, every set_interceptors installs both flow chains at a fresh one, and a per-(face, keyexpr) verdict table computed against an older chain is recomputed instead of served. The ACL precomputes all nine governed actions for a keyexpr; an interceptor whose verdict does not factor through the keyexpr caches nothing and keeps the direct path; a face with no resolved subject caches nothing, since the subject can resolve later and a cached admit would outlive its reason. The version is the load-bearing part: without the bump a live reconfigure installs a new chain while every face already seen keeps answering out of the OLD policy, which is a reconfigure that silently does nothing for exactly the traffic that is flowing. THE ROUND REVERSED ITS OWN FIRST ANSWER and that is the finding. Round 311y509.decision_summary: R311y509 -- the wz linkstate PEER gains a liveliness-TOKEN plane, in both tiers, closing a functional hole rather than a grading one. It had none: the inbound Declare dispatch carried no token arm, so a client DeclToken fell through to the subscriber CATCH-ALL and ingest_client_subscription rejected it on its body match and returned, silently discarding the token; and respond_to_interest answered only the su() and qu() planes. A foreign liveliness GET through a wz peer therefore ALWAYS read empty, where zenohs linkstate_peer hat answers it (hat/linkstate_peer/token.rs:659 declare_token_interest, folding linkstatepeer_tokens at :672 beside the client leaves) and wzs own RouterForwarder already did. Built: client_tokens, the leaf store keyed by declaration id because a clients undeclare is id-only; tokens, the mesh tier keyed by graph zid; a client token advertised into the mesh under SELFs zid and flooded on the 0-to-1 transition only; mesh-sourced Declare and Undeclare routed through the SAME forward_interest_declaration and forward_interest_withdrawal seams the subscriber and queryable planes use; withdraw-if-unbacked so SELFs advertisement is retracted only when no co-attached client still holds the keyexpr; and the token table joined to the face-down purge, because a detached peers tokens must leave with it -- a liveliness tokens ABSENCE is the information, so replaying one for an unreachable node is worse than reporting nothing. THE HOLE WAS FOUND BY A TEST AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST WAS VACUOUS. It asserted only that the querying face received something, which a terminating DeclareFinal always satisfies, and it PASSED against a peer with no token plane at all. Decoding the reply bodies is what turned it red: one Final, zero DeclToken, with a token declared on the other face. That is the second vacuous proof caught in two rounds, the same shape as R311y508s empty-chain fixture, and both were caught by damage rather than by re-reading. The fixture also had a precondition worth recording: the test stayed red after the implementation until both faces were CLIENT leaves, because zenoh gates the token replay on face.whatami == Client (token.rs:668) and wz mirrors it -- which could have been misread as an implementation bug, and the damage probes are what separate a wrong fixture from wrong code. DAMAGE-BOUND, AND THE DAMAGES SEPARATE THE TIERS: disabling the CURRENT dump arm or the client ingest reds the client-leaf test alone; disabling the mesh ingest reds ONLY the mesh-sourced test. THIS CLOSES A routing-token-tables RESIDUAL, NOT THE LAST A4 ATOM -- A4 still reports unproven 1 (routing-interest-pending-gc), and the peer tier has NO foreign witness yet, so no A4 claim is made for it and the atom stays PARTIAL. 595 lib tests pass, fmt and clippy clean, C1y linkstate pin 211 to 213 measured. A full run-ci in flight reported Layer C1ah FAIL while this file was mid-edit; all four of its clippy combinations were re-run on the settled tree and pass, and that run was stopped rather than reported -- editing the tree under a sweep invalidates it.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +client_tokens (per-client-face decl_id -> keyexpr, the leaf store) and +tokens (LinkstatepeerInterest<()>, the MESH tier keyed by graph zid). The peer had neither; the router's twins are behind cfg(routing-token-tables) because that feature also carries router-hat tiers a peer does not have, so the peer's are UNGATED like client_subs beside them.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +explicit DeclToken / UndeclToken arms in the inbound Declare dispatch, forking client vs mesh exactly as the subscriber arms do. Before this the arms did not exist: a DeclToken fell through to the subscriber CATCH-ALL, and ingest_client_subscription's body match rejects a non-subscriber and returns, so the token was silently discarded.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +ingest_client_token / withdraw_client_token. A client's token is stored by declaration id (its undeclare is id-only, carrying no ext_wire_expr) AND advertised into the mesh under SELF's zid, flooded to the tree children on the 0->1 transition only, so a duplicate holder does not re-flood. id-reuse displacement is handled the same way the subscriber twin handles it.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +withdraw_mesh_token_if_unbacked -- SELF's advertisement is retracted and the retraction flooded only when NO co-attached client still holds the keyexpr, the token twin of withdraw_mesh_sub_if_unbacked.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +forward_token / +forward_token_undeclare -- mesh-sourced Declare/Undeclare routed through the SAME forward_interest_declaration / forward_interest_withdrawal seams the subscriber and queryable planes use; only the body extractor (declare_token_wireexpr, which already existed), the table and the carrier builder differ.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: +dump_interest_tokens -- the CURRENT-dump token leg, folding the MESH tier (every OTHER zid, the requester's own excluded as zenoh excludes tables.zid) with the CLIENT leaves (the requesting face's own excluded -- never replay a face its own token), emitted through the shared emit_current_interest_replies so the aggregate-vs-explicit reply shape is the one every other plane uses. Wired into respond_to_interest's CURRENT half under body.to(), client-face gated as zenoh gates the token replay on face.whatami == Client.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: the mesh token table joins purge_detached_interest. A detached peer's tokens leave with it; no affected-keyexpr list is collected because there is no token equivalent of the undeclare-push.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs tests: +a_peer_answers_a_client_liveliness_token_interest (the client-leaf tier) and +a_peer_answers_with_a_mesh_sourced_token (the mesh tier). Both DECODE the replies rather than counting them -- a terminating DeclareFinal alone makes any count assertion pass while proving nothing about the token plane, which is how the first draft of the first test passed against a peer that had no token plane at all.

changes_bullets: vendor/sce pin a51b5e7e1 -> 43695e572 (145 commits). SCE b054af933 makes
{Codec}Owned generic over CodecStorage with DefaultStorage as the default
profile; SCE 1eb145107 moves the Rust crate roots under backends/rust/.
Path deps rewritten on 18 lines across 11 manifests: 16 in crates/ member
manifests (NOT crates/Cargo.toml, which holds none) plus 2 in
deploy/mcu-noheap-probe/Cargo.toml, which the SCE notice omitted by
scoping its scan to crates/. out/** regenerated via the xtask codegen
SSOT: 66 files, +3651/-1951; all 41 owned mirrors are now storage-generic.
Five literals needed S pinned: handshake_encode.rs:95 (InitBodyOwned) and
:169 (OpenBodyOwned) take a binding annotation; layer3_hello.rs:118,
scouting_glue.rs:457 and scouting_multicast_loopback.rs:47 are method
chains whose binding is Vec<u8>, so each needed a new intermediate owned
binding instead. codec_owned.rs:8 re-cited: SceString now lives in
backends/rust/forge-runtime/src/storage.rs, SceBytes in
backends/rust/portable-bytes/src/lib.rs.
verification_bullets: Layer B2 pass (committed out/** == regenerated, 7s) after the commit;
Layer C1 workspace tests. Per-crate cargo check swept all 44 buildable
members with each member's full non-no_std feature set: 40 pass. The four
reds resolved to two annotation crates (fixed, now 0) plus two artefacts
of the synthetic all-features combination, both pre-existing and not
bump-caused: the sce-rust-runtime no_std x http-send compile_error, whose
guard is present at BOTH pins (a51b5e7e1 and 43695e572, lib.rs:81 each),
and wz-runtime-coop/src/reassembly_rx.rs:104 naming Fragment.zid, a field
renamed to peer_key at R311kp in wz's own reassembly_dispatch.rs:175. Both
crates pass at default features. The wide-feature green was damage-bound:
corrupting the type name at linkstate_oam.rs:106 reds the lane (E0422),
reverting re-greens it, so the lane genuinely compiles the sites the SCE
notice predicted would break.
carry_forward_bullets: The SCE notice's impact table is wrong and the correction is reportable
upstream. It predicted 37 annotation sites; the measured count is 5. Its
classifier read only the binding statement's syntax, but rustc also infers
a let binding's type from its LATER uses: declare_ext_keyexpr.rs:190 needs
nothing because read_ext_keyexpr(:121) takes Option<&Vec<ExtEntryOwned>>
and pins S there. Breakage needs BOTH a projection field (zid: S::Bytes<16>)
and no later use that pins S (as_borrowed holds for every S). The notice
also predicted the wrong shape: 3 of the 5 are method chains where the
documented binding-annotation fix does not apply. And its section 2 claim
that N inference stays intact is false — 3 of the 5 root errors were E0284
on owned_bytes' const N, which only resolves once S is pinned; the section
3 claim that one outermost annotation suffices is correct and was measured.
Not yet run locally: the feature-subset matrix, C2 clippy, and the
F/G/Q/Z footprint / cross-compile / interop lanes, which are the hosted
gate's job per CLAUDE.md:194-201.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-coop/src/reassembly_rx.rs:104 built a Fragment with a
field named zid, renamed to peer_key at R311kp, and omitted the priority

the latter because this round edits run-ci.sh itself. The new lane is
damage-bound in both directions: reverting ONLY the fixture repair and
re-running --layer C1l reds it (E0560, rc=101, 28s), restoring the repair
re-greens it, so the added line is what closes the hole rather than
decorating it. The restored tests are not vacuous either: multiplying the
sourced REASSEMBLY_TIMEOUT_MS by 1000 fails 2 of the 3
(mcu_dims_come_from_the_buffer_pool_ssot and

Round 311y512.decision_summary: R311y512 -- the LAST A4 unproven atom closed by a BUILD, not an exclusion. routing-interest-pending-gc goes reserved -> active/PARTIAL and Layer A4 reads proven=128 / partial=39 / unproven=0. R311y508 had ratified this atom as a FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE denominator exclusion from a correct direct read, and the user rejected shrinking the denominator; that ratify carried its own explicit re-open trigger -- wz implements no p2p_peer-shaped broker, and if one is ever built the exclusion is wrong and must come out -- so this round built the broker and retracted the exclusion exactly as prescribed. What landed: LinkstateForwarder now PROPAGATES a CLIENT face's CURRENT token interest to every upstream (non-client) face with a freshly minted id, holds one PendingCurrentInterests entry per propagated copy, and WITHHOLDS the client's terminating DeclareFinal until the last upstream answers; an inbound Declare on an upstream face stamped with a minted id is intercepted ahead of every mesh-ingest arm and either relayed down with the interest_id rewritten to the client's own or, for a DeclFinal, retires the entry; and three paths retire an entry -- the upstream's final, the upstream face dying, and the tick-driven timeout sweep the atom is named for. wz uses an EXPLICIT refcount where zenoh uses Arc strong counts, because the forwarder is a single-threaded RefCell actor with no shared ownership; only the 1->0 edge yields a final, so a client fanned to N upstreams sees exactly one. Proven against a real zenoh-pico z_get_liveliness, whose CURRENT interest carries NO timeout of its own (net/liveliness.c:348 discards the parameter), which makes PROCESS EXIT the wire observable rather than a proxy for it: with the upstream SIGSTOPped -- link open, answering nothing -- pico still returns at the 2.5s GC deadline and the broker reports 1 reaped; with the upstream live it returns in 0.15s with 0 reaped; with no upstream at all the final is emitted inline. Round 311y513.decision_summary: R311y513 -- a bare routing-peer build could not send a single Declare, and the tree had been saying so for months into a lane nobody ran. ROOT CAUSE: the send seam's Declare arm (send_network_message_qos) and dispatch_declare were gated on the declare-* APP-SURFACE origination union, while routing-peer pulls codec-declare -- its own manifest calls the Declare wire surface part of a routing peer's contract -- and none of that union. So every Declare a linkstate forwarder ORIGINATED fell to the no-emit catch arm and returned FeatureDisabled; fan_out_qos counts only successful sends, so the flood reported 0 faces reached. On such a build declare_subscription and declare_queryable flood nothing, forward_subscription and forward_queryable re-flood nothing, the tree-change re-advertise reaches no late joiner, and respond_to_interest emits neither the dump NOR the terminating DeclareFinal -- so a foreign client soliciting that peer is wedged, which is the exact hang R311y512 had just built a GC for. FIX: mirror the OAM arm's ALREADY-PRESENT routing marker onto the Declare arm and, for the same reason, onto the Interest arm -- codec-linkstate plus codec-push is what a routing peer IS inside wz-session-core, and the OAM arm two arms below carries that condition and documents it. The alternative -- adding the declare-* keys to routing-peer's closure -- looks free because each is literally a codec-declare alias, and was REJECTED on measurement: they also switch on the observer.rs session-declaration surface a mesh node never uses. The Interest half is not theoretical: the R311y512 broker propagates a client's CURRENT interest through that seam, so on a bare build every propagated copy returned FeatureDisabled and the broker degraded silently into the inline answer it exists to replace. WHY IT HID: every Layer C1y arm passes --features routing-peer WITHOUT --no-default-features, so what those pins measured was default plus routing-peer, and the default set carries the missing origination features. A lane named for a feature must compile that feature ALONE at least once, or it is measuring the default set and reporting the feature's name; C1y now carries a bare pin (200) that reds at 150 on the exact pre-fix tree. Also fixed while in there: propagate_current_interest recorded its pending entry BEFORE sending, and send_one_to_face discards the fan-out count, so a copy that never left still created an entry and would withhold the client's final for a whole GC window -- it now sends through the counted fan_out seam and records only what left. 50 failing tests -> 0; no inventory or atom-status change (this is a defect fix, not a capability).

The condition is not invented: it MIRRORS the OAM arm two arms below, which carries the same all(codec-linkstate, codec-push) for the same reason and says so ("the routing-peer feature PULLS codec-push, so a routing peer always compiles this arm").

Round 311y513.publishable_decision_summary: R311y513 -- a bare routing-peer build could not send a single Declare, and the tree had been saying so for months into a lane nobody ran. ROOT CAUSE: the send seam's Declare arm (send_network_message_qos) and dispatch_declare were gated on the declare-* APP-SURFACE origination union, while routing-peer pulls codec-declare -- its own manifest calls the Declare wire surface part of a routing peer's contract -- and none of that union. So every Declare a linkstate forwarder ORIGINATED fell to the no-emit catch arm and returned FeatureDisabled; fan_out_qos counts only successful sends, so the flood reported 0 faces reached. On such a build declare_subscription and declare_queryable flood nothing, forward_subscription and forward_queryable re-flood nothing, the tree-change re-advertise reaches no late joiner, and respond_to_interest emits neither the dump NOR the terminating DeclareFinal -- so a foreign client soliciting that peer is wedged, which is the exact hang R311y512 had just built a GC for. FIX: mirror the OAM arm's ALREADY-PRESENT routing marker onto the Declare arm and, for the same reason, onto the Interest arm -- codec-linkstate plus codec-push is what a routing peer IS inside wz-session-core, and the OAM arm two arms below carries that condition and documents it. The alternative -- adding the declare-* keys to routing-peer's closure -- looks free because each is literally a codec-declare alias, and was REJECTED on measurement: they also switch on the observer.rs session-declaration surface a mesh node never uses. The Interest half is not theoretical: the R311y512 broker propagates a client's CURRENT interest through that seam, so on a bare build every propagated copy returned FeatureDisabled and the broker degraded silently into the inline answer it exists to replace. WHY IT HID: every Layer C1y arm passes --features routing-peer WITHOUT --no-default-features, so what those pins measured was default plus routing-peer, and the default set carries the missing origination features. A lane named for a feature must compile that feature ALONE at least once, or it is measuring the default set and reporting the feature's name; C1y now carries a bare pin (200) that reds at 150 on the exact pre-fix tree. Also fixed while in there: propagate_current_interest recorded its pending entry BEFORE sending, and send_one_to_face discards the fan-out count, so a copy that never left still created an entry and would withhold the client's final for a whole GC window -- it now sends through the counted fan_out seam and records only what left. 50 failing tests -> 0; no inventory or atom-status change (this is a defect fix, not a capability).

Round 311y514.decision_summary: R311y514 -- wz negotiated a QoS priority band with full cross-impl fidelity and then routed traffic by the pre-handshake offer. THE GAP, measured at R311y512 by enumerating every caller of qos_link_metadata(): the merged QoSLink state was read at exactly three post-handshake sites -- two Init emit seams and one copy onto Face whose only consumer was a demo log line. Nothing in the data path consulted it, so a link that agreed prio=4-5 still attracted every band. THE UPSTREAM MECHANISM, read not remembered: zenoh rebuilds TransportLinkUnicastConfig from the negotiated ext_qos state on BOTH sides (establishment/open.rs:694-706, accept.rs:818-830) and calls link.reconfigure, and unicast/universal/tx.rs:81-90 shows that same link.config is the input to the egress select -- so upstream the handshake OUTCOME routes traffic, not the offer. FIX: a new apply_negotiated_qos_to_link, called from negotiate_qos_link_against_peer on both directions, writes the merged band into LinkState::priority_range and the merged reliability into LinkState::reliability_pref, the two inputs select_link reads. ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION, and transcribing upstream literally would have been the bug: zenoh writes None through, but upstream the offer and the selection input are ONE endpoint-metadata field, so a merged None means the config was ALREADY None and that arm is a no-op there. wz reaches the seam with a SECOND band source that never sees the wire -- the y217 deploy split -- so writing None through would have cleared a band no peer ever contradicted. Only a Some outcome is applied, and a negative-arm test pins it. PROVEN BY TEST FIRST: the band test failed at exactly the post-merge assertion (0 vs 1) with its calibration and merge legs green, then passed. Three sibling tests on one cfg key, each damage-bound to a different half; the lane itself reds 9/11 on the pre-fix tree. WHY IT HID: Layer C1bb-s multilink arm did not pass session-extqos, so all three tests were compiled out of the lane named for the feature -- the R311y513 shape, one feature key over. C1bb now carries the key and the pin moved 8 -> 11. Atom stays PARTIAL: the enforcement residual is retired and replaced by the FIELD-IDENTITY one -- wz has two band sources where zenoh has one, and the deploy split is still never advertised.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: negotiate_qos_link_against_peer now calls a new apply_negotiated_qos_to_link after set_qos_link_metadata. It writes the merged band into LinkState::priority_range and the merged reliability into LinkState::reliability_pref -- the two inputs select_link reads. Two cfg arms so the call site is unconditional: the transport-multilink arm does the work, the cfg(not) twin is a no-op because a session with no aggregation set never runs select_link (send_wire takes self.link directly), which is the same both-arms discipline the R311mx note imposes on the send seam in this file.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multilink.rs (test): three siblings on one cfg key, each damage-bound to a different half. the_negotiated_band_narrows_egress_selection -- the acceptor merge adopts a subset band and a priority the band gave up leaves the link. the_negotiated_reliability_reclasses_the_link -- an undeclared side inherits the peer's class and the reliable conduit moves to the link still in it. a_metadata_less_peer_does_not_clear_the_deploy_band -- the NEGATIVE arm: a bare-QoS peer must not clear a band it never mentioned.

verification_bullets: DEFECT PROVEN BY TEST BEFORE THE FIX, not by reading: the_negotiated_band_narrows_egress_selection failed at exactly the post-merge assertion (left: 0, right: 1) with its calibration leg and its merge assertion both GREEN -- so the band merged correctly and the egress selection ignored it. That is the defect stated as a measurement.

UPSTREAM ANCHOR, read not remembered: zenoh rebuilds the link config from the negotiated state on BOTH sides -- establishment/open.rs:694-706 and accept.rs:818-830, priorities: state.transport.ext_qos.priorities() / reliability: ... into link.reconfigure(o_config) -- and unicast/universal/tx.rs:81-90 shows that same link.config is the input to the egress select. So the write-back is upstream's own mechanism, not a wz invention.

WHY ONLY A Some OUTCOME IS APPLIED, measured not assumed: upstream the offer and the selection input are ONE endpoint-metadata field, so a merged None implies mine was None implies config.priorities was ALREADY None -- the None arm is a no-op in zenoh. wz reaches the seam with a second band source that never sees the wire, so a literal transcription would clear a deploy band no peer contradicted.

DAMAGE PROBES, three, each binding exactly ONE sibling on the same cfg key: (A) neuter the band write-back -> only the band test reds (10 passed / 1 failed); (B) neuter the reliability write-back -> only the reliability test reds; (C) write None through, the naive transcription -> only the negative-arm test reds. The first attempt at (A) removed the CALL and failed to compile under -D dead-code, so the damage was moved into the BODY -- a probe that does not build is not a probe.

A pre-existing dead-code failure at session-extqos,codec-init-body ALONE was checked against HEAD and reproduces there -- not introduced here, and not a lane.

LANES RUN LOCALLY: C0, C1, C1bb, C2, A3, A5, plus the Layer Z qos interop leg driven directly. A3 still prints REMAINING WORK = 85 EXACT and impl-axis UNAUDITED = 0 -- this round changed an atom's RESIDUAL, not its tag, so no count moves. NOT RUN: the rest of the feature-subset matrix and the F/G/Q/Z lanes; hosted CI is the single full gate.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y514 closed the enforcement half of session-extqos: the negotiated QoSLink band and reliability now drive select_link, mirroring zenoh's link.reconfigure at the end of establishment. Before this, wz negotiated a band with full fidelity -- 4 cross-impl legs against a real zenohd prove the containment -- and then routed traffic by the pre-handshake offer. Establishment fidelity had been proven; enforcement had never been built.

THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES: a negotiated value is not enforced until something in the DATA path reads it. The R311y512 residual was found by enumerating every caller of the reader (three sites, all establishment or logging) and that enumeration is the technique -- for any negotiated capability, list the readers of its post-handshake state and ask which one is on the send path. session-extshm, session-extcompression and session-extauth have not been put through it.

THE FAITHFULNESS TRAP THIS ROUND AVOIDED, and it is worth reusing: transcribing upstream literally would have been WRONG here. zenoh's link.reconfigure writes None through, and copying that would have cleared wz's deploy band, because upstream has ONE band field where wz has two. The rule that resolved it: reproduce the upstream OBSERVABLE, and where the two trees' field topology differs, work out which upstream states are reachable before copying the assignment.

NEW, NAMED RESIDUAL on session-extqos (the atom stays PARTIAL): the FIELD-IDENTITY gap. wz's deploy band -- accept_loop::multilink_priority_range's FaceId-parity split, installed by set_link_priority_range at bring-up -- is never ADVERTISED, so a wz multilink deploy negotiates a band it did not tell the peer about. zenoh's prio= endpoint metadata is simultaneously the offer and the selection input. Unifying them is wire-visible for existing deploys and needs its own cross-impl witness.

SECOND NAMED RESIDUAL: wz's LinkReliabilityPref::Any means NO PREFERENCE, where zenoh's undeclared case falls back to the link's INTRINSIC class (config.reliability.unwrap_or(Reliability::from(link.is_reliable()))). Pre-existing in select_link, independent of the handshake, deliberately not folded into the write-back.

STILL OPEN, unchanged from R311y513: the send_one_to_face sweep (28 of 29 call sites still swallow a failed send); A3's domain census carries 3 unaudited omissions; the SCE reply is written but NOT SENT; the dead-cfg(test)-behind-a-feature sweep beyond wz-runtime-coop; the lane-hygiene sweep for other --features X without --no-default-features. A3 REMAINING WORK is still 85 EXACT.

Round 311y516.decision_summary: R311y516 -- the RX SHM enforcement hole, closed. Running the R311y514 enumeration technique (list every reader of a negotiated capability's state, name which one is on the data path) against the three unswept establishment extensions produced three verdicts: session-extcompression is already ENFORCED both ways (is_compression -> compresses_batches() -> emit_on_link on TX, drive.rs on the RX un-wrap); session-extauth has no data-path consumer and upstream has none either, its enforcement being the handshake reject that drives FramingError + returns AuthRejected; and session-extshm was enforced on TX (publish_shm reads is_shm and swaps the descriptor for the bytes) but NOT on RX. The receive un-swap in pubsub.rs dispatch_push consulted ONLY the body's 0x2 marker, so a peer that had never negotiated SHM could name a /dev/shm segment and this node would map it and deliver its contents -- the negotiation was decorative on the receive side. Direct read of zenoh 49c8a53 is the arbiter: io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/universal/rx.rs:50-51 wraps map_zmsg_to_shmbuf in `if self.config.shm.is_some()`, literally the expression behind its is_shm() at unicast/universal/transport.rs:349-350, so upstream gates the WHOLE un-swap on the negotiated capability. wz now carries the counterpart: SubscriberRegistry gains a shm_negotiated gate (default false = fail-closed) plus a shm_unnegotiated_drops counter, RESTAMPED live every dispatch iteration from the unicast dispatch SSOT Session::dispatch_iteration_event_with (wz's counterpart of zenoh's trigger_callback) rather than snapshotted -- negotiate_shm_against_peer is a monotonic `&=`, so a reconnect can only drive the capability DOWN and a construction-time snapshot would go stale in the fail-OPEN direction. PROVEN by a new e2e whose two arms differ in EXACTLY ONE bit, with the same live segment, resolver and descriptor in both; DAMAGE-BOUND, since disabling the gate delivers the stranger's bytes. The round also repairs a REAL `-D warnings` build break at HEAD: `--no-default-features --features session-extqos,codec-init-body` reded on dead send_wire / emit_on_link, because the establishment codecs entered those cfg unions BARE while all four handshake senders additionally require a unicast ROLE key. They are now role-conjoined -- the R311y205 codec-close exclusion one level over -- and Layer C1h gains three arms so the combination is finally named by a lane. Layer C1af's shm_e2e pin 5 -> 6. Inventory reasons updated on transport-shm + session-extshm; no status flip, A3 unchanged at 85 EXACT.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/pubsub.rs: SubscriberRegistry gains the RX SHM ENFORCEMENT gate -- a `shm_negotiated` bool (default false = fail-closed), `set_shm_negotiated` / `shm_negotiated` accessors, and a `shm_unnegotiated_drops` counter distinct from the pre-existing `shm_unresolved_drops`. dispatch_push's `transport-shm` un-swap now refuses the 0x2-marked body when the session never negotiated SHM, dropping + counting instead of decoding the descriptor and mapping the segment. Drop rather than deliver-raw: handing the application the descriptor bytes in place of its data is worse than a counted refusal.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: Session::dispatch_iteration_event_with -- the unicast dispatch SSOT and wz's counterpart of zenoh's TransportUnicastUniversal::trigger_callback -- restamps the LIVE `actions().is_shm()` onto the subscriber registry before dispatch_event. RESTAMPED, not snapshotted: negotiate_shm_against_peer is a monotonic `&=`, so a reconnect can only drive the capability DOWN and a construction-time snapshot would go stale in the fail-OPEN direction. dispatch_multicast_iteration_event deliberately does not stamp (no multicast SHM negotiation), leaving that registry fail-closed at the default.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: `send_wire` / `emit_on_link` / the `Reliability` import ROLE-CONJOIN the establishment codecs -- `codec-init-body` / `codec-open-body` alone do not imply a caller, because all four handshake senders (send_init_syn / send_open_syn / send_init_ack_with_cookie / send_open_ack, :6364/:6441/:6482/:6578) additionally require session-unicast-open or session-unicast-accept. This is the R311y205 codec-close / transport-keepalive exclusion one level over, and it repairs a REAL `-D warnings` build break at HEAD (`--no-default-features --features session-extqos,codec-init-body` -> dead-code reject on both methods).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/shm_e2e.rs: new `an_unnegotiated_peer_cannot_make_this_node_map_its_segment` -- the two arms differ in EXACTLY ONE bit (`set_shm_negotiated`), with the same live /dev/shm segment, the same installed PosixShmResolver, the same valid descriptor and the same Push in both, so the refusing arm cannot pass for a boring reason. The existing zero-copy e2e's custom drive closure now stamps from the LIVE actions rather than a hard-coded true, keeping it a measurement of the negotiation rather than an assertion about itself.

The technique -- list every reader of a negotiated capability's state and ask which one is on the data path -- produced three verdicts: extcompression already enforced both directions, extauth enforced by handshake reject with no upstream data-path consumer either, and extshm enforced on TX but NOT on RX. wz honoured the 0x2 body marker alone, so a peer that never negotiated SHM could name a /dev/shm segment and have this node map it and deliver its contents. zenoh gates the whole un-swap on the negotiated capability (rx.rs:50-51). THE LESSON, and it generalises past SHM: a capability can be cross-impl PROVEN on its handshake and still govern nothing. session-extshm is A4-proven against a real zenohd in both directions and was tagged COMPLETE -- and its receive path ignored the result of that handshake. A4 grades the negotiation; nothing grades the consequence. The enumeration is cheap and it has now found a real defect on the first capability it was pointed at that had a data path.

Adding the gate silently broke the zero-copy e2e, because that test drives a raw ApplicationLayerObserver through `drive_session_until_terminal` instead of the production `Session::dispatch_iteration_event_with`. The test was RIGHT to fail -- a custom drive closure now owes the registry the same live stamp, the way one already owes it a `drain_deferred_fires` -- but the failure is the evidence that a `pub` drive API can bypass an enforcement point. Threading the flag through IterationEvent would make it unforgettable; it was rejected as out of scope at 139 FramePayload construction sites across 38 files, and that trade is the open residual.

(1) Layer C1's teardown drain was a data-loss defect: a 50 ms wall-clock budget cannot tell a WEDGED peer from a SLOW one, so on a loaded host it expired mid-progress and discarded frames the C ABI z_put had already answered Z_OK for. Reproduced byte-for-byte by setting the budget to 1 ms. The fix splits the two obligations the one number had collapsed: a SEAL on the outbound queue (finish the queue, then exit) for TERMINATION, which ends the writer regardless of how many sender clones the routing lifecycle still holds and so makes R311y518's leaked accept-path sender irrelevant instead of something to chase through multilink failover; and a per-write WRITER_STALL_MS for the WEDGED-PEER defence, armed even under a write already in flight. R311y518 tried the per-write bound alone and had to revert it because teardown then hung; two damage probes here show each half is separately necessary -- restoring the budget reds the delivery test with the identical hosted prefix, suppressing only the seal hangs the face-death test at 15.23 s. (2) Layer C1cd panicked before one attachment byte moved because spawn_zenohd gates readiness on a real wz-ap-demo open and the hosted interop job never builds that binary; the lane now provisions it, which was reproduced by DELETING the local binary and re-verified from that same state. (3) Layer Q was a footprint regression root-caused to a commit and to symbols rather than re-baselined: 18d2d870^ measures the standing baseline EXACTLY and 18d2d870 measures +412, so the whole growth is the R311y510 SCE pin bump -- the fourth signal from that one bump. The first local reading was wrong by 208 B until it used Layer Q's own --remap-path-prefix, which is why the baseline was not moved to it.

Round 311y519.publishable_decision_summary: R311y519 -- all three hosted-red lanes named by R311y517 closed at their root, each reproduced locally FIRST. (1) Layer C1's teardown drain was a data-loss defect: a 50 ms wall-clock budget cannot tell a WEDGED peer from a SLOW one, so on a loaded host it expired mid-progress and discarded frames the C ABI z_put had already answered Z_OK for. Reproduced byte-for-byte by setting the budget to 1 ms. The fix splits the two obligations the one number had collapsed: a SEAL on the outbound queue (finish the queue, then exit) for TERMINATION, which ends the writer regardless of how many sender clones the routing lifecycle still holds and so makes R311y518's leaked accept-path sender irrelevant instead of something to chase through multilink failover; and a per-write WRITER_STALL_MS for the WEDGED-PEER defence, armed even under a write already in flight. R311y518 tried the per-write bound alone and had to revert it because teardown then hung; two damage probes here show each half is separately necessary -- restoring the budget reds the delivery test with the identical hosted prefix, suppressing only the seal hangs the face-death test at 15.23 s. (2) Layer C1cd panicked before one attachment byte moved because spawn_zenohd gates readiness on a real wz-ap-demo open and the hosted interop job never builds that binary; the lane now provisions it, which was reproduced by DELETING the local binary and re-verified from that same state. (3) Layer Q was a footprint regression root-caused to a commit and to symbols rather than re-baselined: 18d2d870^ measures the standing baseline EXACTLY and 18d2d870 measures +412, so the whole growth is the R311y510 SCE pin bump -- the fourth signal from that one bump. The first local reading was wrong by 208 B until it used Layer Q's own --remap-path-prefix, which is why the baseline was not moved to it.
publishable_changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/writer_queue.rs (new): OutboundQueue + WriterHandle. A SEAL ("finish the queue, then exit") closes the receiving half so the queue is finite and the writer terminates regardless of how many Arc<SessionLinkActions> clones the routing lifecycle still holds. WriterHandle::spawn is the ONLY constructor, so a new pipeline cannot spawn a writer nobody can seal. WRITER_STALL_MS = 2000 bounds ONE write once sealed, armed even under a write already in flight, and expiry ends the writer rather than skipping a frame.

wz-runtime-tokio: WRITER_DRAIN_MS DELETED from session_open. drain_to_close now seals + awaits to completion. DAMAGE PROBE 1 -- the budget. Restoring the wall-clock form (timeout 50 ms over into_join) with everything else in place reds a_put_immediately_before_z_close_is_drained_not_discarded with that same delivered: prefix. So the seal, not the raised fixture stall, is what carries the test.

DAMAGE PROBE 2 -- the seal, separately. Suppressing ONLY the seal send (drain still awaits to completion) hangs c_get_completes_promptly_when_the_face_dies_mid_flight past its 15 s bound, failing at 15.23 s. That is exactly the state R311y518 built and reverted, and it establishes that the two halves are each necessary: await-to-completion alone hangs, budget alone loses data.

Paused time, so the 2 s bound costs nothing.

Round 311y520.decision_summary: R311y520 -- the first pico-parity round after R311y519 split the 85 into 71 zenoh / 5 pico / 9 neither. scouting-active had FOUR named residuals vs the vendored zenoh-pico; three of them were one defect wearing three faces, and this round closed all three in one edit. record_hello_and_emit decoded a Hello and projected it down to locators[0], throwing away version, whatami and zid, every locator after the first, and any Hello that advertised no locator at all -- the last of which made a peer that ANSWERED indistinguishable from a window that timed out. It now records the complete Hello into a ScoutedHello accumulator shaped like pico's _z_hello_t, including the locator-less case that pico keeps (src/session/scout.c:88-110). The cbyte layout was established by reading BOTH references rather than assumed. Proven three ways: a unit test per residual, a damage probe per residual, and a cross-impl witness against a REAL zenohd whose own role and 16-byte zid now reach the consumer. The fourth residual is NOT closed and is now precisely priced: wz exits on the first Hello because scouting.scxml:128 targets Idle on hello.received, so collecting the window is an SCXML change with codegen, not Rust work -- the accumulator is a Vec so that change stays additive. A3 stays at 85 because an atom leaves PARTIAL only when every residual closes.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/scouting_glue.rs: new public ScoutedHello (version / whatami / zid / ALL locators), mirroring pico's _z_hello_t field for field, plus a ScoutingActions::hellos accumulator and a scouted_hellos() read. record_hello_and_emit now records the whole decoded Hello instead of projecting it down to locators[0], and records a LOCATOR-LESS Hello as well -- pico's HELLO arm clears the locator vector and keeps the hello (src/session/scout.c:88-110), where wz previously made that peer indistinguishable from silence. discovered / discovered_locator keep their exact former meaning (the first locator, the dial-target read), so no existing caller changed.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/scouting_glue.rs tests: craft_hello_datagram generalised to craft_hello_with(whatami, zid, locators) accepting ZERO or more locators -- the locator-less wire shape (L flag clear) could not be crafted before, which is why that residual went unmeasured. Three new tests, one per closed residual, plus a negative arm (a timed-out window records nothing) so "one record" cannot be satisfied by an unconditional push.

wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the scouted-peer log line gains hellos=[...] carrying version / role / zid / locators. APPENDED at the END of the existing line so every current matcher (the zenohd interop asserts the locator and record_hello=1 substrings) keeps matching.

wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_scout_zenohd_interop.rs: assertion 2b -- the decoded line must carry zenohd's own role and a 32-hex-char (16-byte) zid. Neither value is chosen by the test; zenohd puts them on the wire.
verification_bullets: WIRE SEMANTICS VERIFIED BY DIRECT READ OF BOTH REFERENCES, not inferred. pico decodes the Hello cbyte as _whatami = _z_whatami_from_uint8(cbyte) with 1 shl (b and 0x03) (src/protocol/codec/message.c:675, src/protocol/codec/transport.c:35-37) and zidlen = ((cbyte and 0xF0) shr 4) + 1 (message.c:676). wz's WhatAmI::from_wire masks the same two bits with the same index semantics. That is why WhatAmI::from_wire(hello.cbyte) is the correct extraction rather than a guess.

UNIT: 3 new tests, one per closed residual -- every locator of a 3-locator Hello survives in wire order; version + role + zid reach the caller (role asserted as CLIENT, a value that is neither the fixture default nor the on-failure default, so a decode that quietly defaults fails); a locator-less Hello is recorded as a peer WITH no dial target. Plus a negative arm: a timed-out window records nothing.

DAMAGE PROBES, one per residual, each red on its own test. P1 restore the locators[0] projection -> only the multi-locator test fails (6 pass / 1 fail). P2 discard whatami -> the metadata test fails, AND SO DOES the locator-less test, because that one also asserts the role (5 pass / 2 fail) -- reported as measured, not as a clean 1:1. P3 drop a locator-less Hello -> only the locator-less test fails (6 pass / 1 fail).

CROSS-IMPL WITNESS, against a REAL zenohd, not a crafted fixture. Layer M pass (102s), and the evidence was READ rather than inferred from the verdict: wz-ap-demo logs "scouted peer locator tcp/127.0.0.1:37651 (scout_emit=1, record_hello=1) hellos=[v9 router zid=2cc9ff1ea7fc082c43be07f629181ed9 locators=[tcp/127.0.0.1:37651]]". The role and the 16-byte id are bytes zenohd chose and put in its Hello; before this round all three fields were decoded and thrown away.

A TRAP HIT AND NAMED. Running the interop test standalone FAILED with "the Scout got no Hello back" -- not a regression: cargo test does not rebuild wz-ap-demo, so it ran the DEFAULT-feature binary the C1cd lane had just left in target/debug, which has no scouting-active. Layer M builds the binary itself, which is why it passed there. Rebuilt with the feature, the standalone run passes and prints the line above.

LANES: C0 pass (3s), C1 pass (91s, cargo test --workspace), C2 pass (34s), M pass (102s). Lane hygiene checked: --no-default-features --features scouting-active compiles ALONE, and so does scouting-active,scouting-static.

A3 UNCHANGED AT 85, and that is correct rather than disappointing: the atom stays PARTIAL because residual 1 is open, and the counter only decrements when EVERY residual of an atom closes. Judge the round by which residuals closed.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y520 is the first round of the PICO-PARITY burn-down (bucket P, 5 atoms) that R311y519's classification separated out of the undifferentiated 85. It closed 3 of scouting-active's 4 residuals.

THE REMAINING ONE IS A STATECHART CHANGE, and knowing that is the round's other product. wz exits scouting on the FIRST Hello because sources/session/scouting.scxml:128 targets Idle on hello.received. pico's exit_on_first is a PARAMETER (src/session/scout.c), so collecting the window needs that transition to become a self-transition plus a timer-driven exit -- SCXML plus codegen plus out/** regen, i.e. Layers B/B2. The hellos accumulator built here is a Vec precisely so that change is additive rather than a rewrite.

THE SHAPE WORTH CARRYING: three of the four residuals were one defect wearing three faces -- the decoder projected a rich wire message down to a single string. Whenever an atom's residual list reads like several small omissions in one function, check whether they are one lossy projection before pricing them separately; these three closed together in one edit.

A FIXTURE THAT CANNOT CRAFT THE SHAPE CANNOT MEASURE IT. The locator-less residual survived because craft_hello_datagram took exactly one locator and could not emit the L-flag-clear wire shape at all. Generalising the builder was the whole cost of measuring it.

THE SHARED-ARTIFACT TRAP FIRED AGAIN, in a new place: cargo test does not rebuild wz-ap-demo, so the interop test ran the DEFAULT-feature binary the C1cd lane had left in target/debug and failed with a symptom (no Hello) that reads exactly like a real regression. Layer M builds it, which is why the lane was green while the standalone run was red. When a foreign-witness test fails, check WHICH binary it ran before believing the symptom.
