Round 311y521.decision_summary: R311y521 -- the second pico-parity round, and it produced a BUILD and a DECLINED build. BUILT: session-reconnect's remote-liveliness flush. On link loss wz kept every remote liveliness token it had learned, so a subscriber went on believing a dead peer's token was alive -- and since the link that would have carried the UndeclToken is precisely what died, no undeclare could ever arrive. The stale entry also survived reset_for_reopen, so a re-declared token fired a SECOND Put for something the application was never told had gone. wz now transcribes pico's _z_liveliness_subscription_undeclare_all, drained before the sinks run as pico's own NOTE prescribes, fired ahead of the reopen as pico fires it from transport failure, and CALLED by wz-ap-demo so it is not a primitive nothing ships. DECLINED: the intended target was scouting-static's multi-locator residual, and measurement stopped it -- open_session_static, the only multi-locator entry point, has no production caller at all (20 references, every one a test), and the demo's --connect is a single String, so building the behaviour there would have produced exactly the driver-with-no-caller shape R311y503 caught. The residual is real; its cost is a production caller, not the loop. A3 stays 85: session-reconnect keeps three named residuals.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core/src/declare/liveliness_subscriber.rs: new LivelinessSubscriberRegistry::flush_peer_tokens_on_link_loss() -- drains the peer_token_table and fans a Delete to each matching slot, returning the count. Direct transcription of pico's _z_liveliness_subscription_undeclare_all (src/session/liveliness.c:99-120). The drain happens BEFORE any sink runs, mirroring pico's own move-then-iterate, so a sink that re-declares during the fan-out lands in the fresh table.

wz-session-core/src/observer.rs: ApplicationLayerObserver::flush_liveliness_on_link_loss() passthrough, a no-op returning 0 when liveliness-subscriber is compiled out. Deliberately NOT part of the dispatch_iteration_event fan: no inbound message announces a dead link, so whoever observed the loss must say so.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/reconnect.rs: ReconnectingSession gains an optional observer handle plus set_liveliness_flush(), and the reopen loop flushes BEFORE reset_for_reopen -- pico's ordering, where the flush rides transport failure ahead of any reopen. A poisoned observer mutex recovers via into_inner rather than leaking the registry, matching the crate's other shutdown paths. A SETTER, not a consuming builder, because the observer is built after the supervisor.

wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the DriveSource::Reconnect arm calls set_liveliness_flush(observer.clone()) -- the PRODUCTION caller, without which this would be a library primitive no shipped binary reaches.
verification_bullets: PICO'S BEHAVIOUR ESTABLISHED BY DIRECT READ, both halves. _zp_unicast_failed_result calls _z_liveliness_subscription_undeclare_all under Z_FEATURE_LIVELINESS && Z_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION (src/transport/unicast/lease.c:74-78), and that function moves the whole _remote_tokens map out, fires _z_trigger_liveliness_subscriptions_undeclare per key, and clears it (src/session/liveliness.c:99-120). Its own NOTE is why the drain precedes the fan-out here.

UNIT: 3 tests. Link loss fires one Delete per remote token, asserted BY KEYEXPR NAME rather than by count (a flush firing the right number with a wrong keyexpr would tell a subscriber the wrong token died) and leaves the table empty. A flush with no remote tokens fires nothing -- the negative arm that stops "3 Deletes" being satisfiable by a per-SLOT fabrication. A token the subscriber's pattern does not match is flushed but not fired, keeping that asymmetry explicit against a future fan-to-every-slot shortcut.

DAMAGE PROBES, one per half of the fix. Clear the table WITHOUT notifying -> the main test reds (the Deletes never arrive), which is what a naive "just reset the registry" fix would have shipped. Notify WITHOUT clearing -> the main test AND the unmatched-token test red (the table stays populated). Neither half is redundant.

NO DRIVER WITHOUT A CALLER: wired to wz-ap-demo's reconnect arm, the shipped binary path. This was checked deliberately -- the same round found that open_session_static, the only multi-locator entry point, has NO production caller (20 references, all tests), and DECLINED to build the multi-locator residual onto it for exactly that reason.

LANES: C0 pass (2s), C1 pass (57s, cargo test --workspace), C2 pass (13s), session_reconnect_e2e 5/5. Lane hygiene: --no-default-features with session-reconnect ALONE, with liveliness-subscriber, and with transport-multilink all compile; the observer hook compiles with liveliness-subscriber both on and off.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y521 = the second pico-parity round. It closed session-reconnect's remote-liveliness-flush residual: a token used to outlive the link that announced it, so a subscriber believed a dead peer was alive, and the stale entry survived the reopen so a re-declare fired a SECOND Put for something the app was never told had gone.

THE ROUND'S OTHER PRODUCT IS A DECLINED BUILD, and it is worth as much. The intended target was scouting-static's "wz returns after the FIRST locator where pico adds every remaining locator as a peer". Measurement stopped it: open_session_static has NO production caller -- 20 references, every one a test or a doc-link -- and wz-ap-demo's --connect is a single String. Building the multi-locator behaviour there would have created a driver nothing ships, the exact R311y503 shape. The residual is real but its COST is a production caller, not the loop.

READ THE RESIDUAL, THEN CHECK THE CALLER. A residual describes a behavioural gap; it does not promise the gap is reachable. Before building one, grep for the entry point's callers -- if they are all tests, the atom's real work is upstream of the behaviour.

PICO'S ORDERING WAS COPIED DELIBERATELY: the flush rides TRANSPORT FAILURE, ahead of any reopen, not the re-dial. And the table is drained BEFORE the sinks run, which pico's own NOTE calls out; here that also happens to be what makes the borrow legal, so the two reasons agree rather than compete.

STILL OPEN in bucket P: scouting-static (needs a production multi-locator caller first), api-compat-pico, transport-link-udp, scouting-active's SCXML residual, and session-reconnect's own remaining three (multi-locator failover, exponential backoff, multicast reconnect). Re-measure from project_a3_remaining_split_by_reference before quoting.

Round 311y522.decision_summary: R311y522 -- the accept-side half of the liveliness link-loss flush, and a fix that had to be reverted once before it worked. A C program that declared z_liveliness_declare_subscriber was never told when the peer holding a token VANISHED: face_down dropped the FaceEntry and with it the whole per-face observer, in silence, and no UndeclToken can rescue that because the link that would carry one is what died. The obvious fix -- flush the per-face observer before dropping the entry -- was built, measured, and REVERTED at first, because it did not work and the reason was not guessable: wz's liveliness registry does not call the application callback at all. It stages each matched sample on a DEFERRED-FIRE queue (R311lg, session/mod.rs:3743-3752) so the callback may re-enter the session safely, and the DRIVE LOOP drains it -- but face_down runs after the drive loop has returned, so nothing ever did. Flushing therefore measured as one slot FIRED and reached the application as silence. The shipped fix flushes AND drains, and the flush-without-drain state is now pinned by its own damage probe. The gate also had to LEAK its token: a bound one emits an UndeclToken that R311y519's teardown drain now delivers, so a bound-token version passes through the ordinary undeclare path -- measured, with the fix removed.
changes_bullets: wz-capi-core/src/faces.rs: SharedSession::face_down flushes the dying face's remote liveliness tokens as Deletes to the C application, then DRAINS the session's deferred-fire queue so those Deletes actually run. Both steps happen before the FaceEntry is dropped, because the sinks that must receive them are owned by it.

wz-capi-pico/tests/liveliness_face_death.rs (new): the ABI-level gate. A C listener declares z_liveliness_declare_subscriber; a wz-native peer dials, declares a liveliness token, and VANISHES. The PUT is asserted first (so the Delete leg is not vacuous), then the DELETE. The peer LEAKS its token with std::mem::forget on purpose -- a bound token's RAII drop emits an UndeclToken that R311y519's teardown drain now delivers, which would satisfy the gate through the ordinary undeclare path.
verification_bullets: THE ROOT CAUSE WAS FOUND BY READING, after instrumentation had narrowed it to a contradiction. The measurement trail said: face_down runs, the observer holds slots=1 tokens=1, the flush drains 1 and fan_to_matching_slots reports 1 slot FIRED, on_sample calls the boxed closure with no gating -- and yet the C shim was entered only for the Put. The resolution is at session/mod.rs:3743-3752: declare_liveliness_subscriber registers a DEFERRED-FIRE staging sink (R311lg), so on_sample stages the sample on the session fire queue and the callback runs later, when the drive loop drains it. face_down runs AFTER the drive loop has returned, so nothing ever drained it. Adding drain_deferred_fires is the fix.

THREE DAMAGE PROBES, and the third is the one that matters most. (1) No flush at all -- the pre-R311y522 state -- FAILS (15.04 s, the Delete wait expiring). (2) Flush WITHOUT the drain FAILS: this pins the exact trap that caused the first attempt to be reverted, so it can never be reintroduced silently. (3) Fix removed AND the token merely BOUND rather than leaked PASSES -- which is the proof that std::mem::forget is load-bearing and that a bound-token version of this gate would be vacuous. That third probe is why the earlier attempt looked green at first.

A FLUSH THAT STAGES IS NOT A FLUSH THAT DELIVERS. wz's liveliness registry does not call the application callback: it stages the sample on a deferred-fire queue (R311lg) so the callback can re-enter the session without self-deadlocking, and the DRIVE LOOP drains it. Any teardown path that fires samples after the drive loop has returned owes an explicit drain_deferred_fires -- otherwise the fan-out reports "1 slot fired" and the application hears nothing. That is exactly the shape of an emitter that exists on a path that does not run.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS REVERTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED, and that was the right call: it flushed without draining, so the registry was cleaned and the C application still never learned. It is now pinned by its own damage probe, so the same half-fix cannot return quietly.

A LIVELINESS FACE-DEATH TEST MUST LEAK THE TOKEN. A merely BOUND token emits an UndeclToken from its RAII drop, and since R311y519's teardown drain that tail frame is actually DELIVERED -- so the gate passes through the ordinary undeclare path and proves nothing. Measured, not feared: with the token bound the test passed even with the fix removed. R311y519 made a previously-safe test idiom unsafe, which is worth remembering for any other teardown gate written before it.

INSTRUMENT TO A CONTRADICTION, THEN READ. Four probes narrowed this to "the registry fired into a slot whose sink is somehow not the C shim", which is impossible as stated -- and that impossibility is what made the deferred-fire seam findable by reading the declare path. Instrumentation bounded the search; it did not answer it.

Round 311y523.decision_summary: R311y523 -- R311y522's lesson applied backwards to R311y521's own fix, and it was needed. The dial-path liveliness flush shipped at R311y521 flushed the registry but never drained the deferred-fire queue, so it STAGED Deletes and depended on something else delivering them. wz-ap-demo happens to run a periodic sweep that calls drain_deferred_fires, so the demo delivered them late rather than never -- but that is an accidental dependency, and a consumer without such a sweeper delivered nothing. R311y521's own unit tests could not have caught it: they exercise LivelinessSubscriberRegistry directly with a plain sink and so never cross the deferred-fire seam that breaks. set_liveliness_flush now takes the SESSION rather than the observer, because drain_deferred_fires lives on the session and the observer alone cannot deliver anything. The meta-point is the durable one: when a round root-causes an omission, re-audit the earlier rounds that used the same mechanism instead of assuming the omission was local.

wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the production caller passes the session.

WHY THIS WAS FOUND: R311y522 root-caused the identical omission on the accept path and the generalisation was applied backwards to the round before it, rather than assumed to be a one-off.

Round 311y524.decision_summary: R311y524 -- transport-link-udp: one residual CLOSED, one RETRACTED as stale, and the retraction is the more useful half. CLOSED: a udp/<name>:<port> locator now resolves and dials. pico treats a named UDP endpoint as ordinary, resolving it through getaddrinfo with SOCK_DGRAM/IPPROTO_UDP (udp_posix.c:32-40), so wz's typed Unsupported was a parity gap rather than a deliberate narrowing; the new dial_udp_host walks resolved addresses in order like its tcp sibling and hands the concrete peer out because DialedLink::Udp cannot take a name. The gate asserts the RESOLVED peer rather than success, since a UDP dial is bind+connect and returns Ok against a bogus address. RETRACTED: the atom's other residual claimed bind_locator/accept_locator refuse udp regardless of feature, citing session_open.rs:763,790 -- both lines are gone and the behaviour changed at R311y382, where Proto::Udp binds a demux listener and accept_raw awaits each new source. That is the second stale residual found in three rounds, so the lesson is now general: a residual is a claim with a date on it, and its cited lines are the cheapest way to test whether it still holds.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs: new dial_udp_host(host, iface) -> (UdpSocket, SocketAddr). Walks the resolved addresses in order and keeps the first that dials, mirroring dial_tcp_host's walk and getaddrinfo's ordered list. Returns the resolved address because DialedLink::Udp needs a concrete peer, which a name cannot supply.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: the AnyLocator::Named dial arm gains Proto::Udp (feature-gated, with the cfg-off twin returning the same typed Unsupported the numeric arm uses). The catch-all message now says name dial is wired for tcp AND udp.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs tests: non_tcp_named_dial_is_unsupported_without_io became ws_and_tls_named_dial_is_unsupported_without_io -- it encoded the contract this round changed -- plus a positive arm for the udp name.
verification_bullets: PICO PARITY ESTABLISHED BY DIRECT READ, not preference. pico resolves a named UDP endpoint through getaddrinfo(s_address, s_port, &hints, ..) with hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_DGRAM and ai_protocol = IPPROTO_UDP (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/link/transport/udp/udp_posix.c:32-40). A named udp endpoint is ordinary there, so wz's typed Unsupported was a gap rather than a narrowing.

THE ASSERTION IS ON THE RESOLVED PEER, not on success. A UDP dial is a bind plus connect and returns Ok against a bogus address, so a test that only checked Ok would pass without any resolution happening. The test asserts peer.port() and peer.ip().is_loopback() for udp/localhost:17457 -- localhost rather than a public name, so the property measured is that the arm reaches the resolver at all rather than host connectivity.

DAMAGE PROBE, and it took three attempts to make it VALID. Deleting the arm did not compile (unused import), and a stubbed arm did not compile either (type mismatch) -- a damage that does not build proves nothing. The probe that worked resolves exactly as the fix does and then refuses, which reds a_named_udp_locator_resolves_and_dials alone.

A CARRIED RESIDUAL WAS RETRACTED AS STALE. The atom claimed bind_locator/accept_locator return Unsupported for udp regardless of feature at session_open.rs:763,790. Both cited lines are gone and the behaviour changed at R311y382: Proto::Udp binds a demux listener into BoundListener::Udp and accept_raw awaits each new source. This is the SECOND stale residual found in three rounds (query-get's C1j claim was the first).
LANES: C0 pass (3s), C1 pass (64s), C2 pass (17s). Lane hygiene: --no-default-features with transport-link-udp ALONE and with transport-link-tcp alone both compile.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y524 closed transport-link-udp's named-dial residual and RETRACTED its accept-side one as stale.

Round 311y525.decision_summary: R311y525 -- the dial-path delivery gate for the link-loss liveliness flush, and it failed on its first run. R311y521 built that flush, R311y523 corrected its missing drain, and neither shipped an end-to-end test: R311y521's unit tests drive the registry directly with a plain sink and so never cross the deferred-fire seam that was the whole defect. Writing the missing gate immediately exposed a THIRD problem in the same few lines -- the flush sat inside the reopen retry loop, BELOW the stop check, so a supervisor stopped during a link loss returned Stopped without ever telling the application. A vanishing peer does not coordinate with the caller's stop flag, and shutdown is precisely when a caller stops a supervisor, so this was not a test artifact. The flush now runs on TRANSPORT FAILURE, above both stop checks and once per loss rather than once per retry, which is also what pico does. Three damage probes pin it: no flush, flush without drain, and the flush moved back below the stop check -- each reds this test alone. The durable lesson is about evidence layers: one small fix was wrong three times in three ways, and each way was only visible to a test at a different layer.

It also runs once per loss rather than once per retry attempt, which the old placement inside the loop did not guarantee.
wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_reconnect_e2e.rs: a_dying_link_delivers_remote_liveliness_deletes_to_the_dialer -- the dial-path delivery gate R311y521/y523 shipped without.

THREE DAMAGE PROBES, each redding this test alone (5 pass / 1 fail): no flush; flush WITHOUT drain (the R311y523 shape); and the flush moved BACK below the stop check (the shape this round found). All three compile.
NON-VACUITY: the PUT is asserted first, from the same sink, so the Delete leg cannot pass on a run where the acceptor's token never reached the dialer.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: RecoveryConfig gains `periodic_queries: Option<Duration>` + a `with_periodic_queries` builder (the struct is already #[non_exhaustive] -> no API break). `State::periodic_requests` collects a `_sn=last+1..` RecoveryRequest for every retransmission source with no GET in flight, marking each pending (no-op when retransmission is off). `run_periodic_tick` collects the requests under the state lock then issues the GETs OUTSIDE it (the same re-entrancy discipline as the sample-driven path), reusing `issue_recovery_query` + `handle_recovered`/`finish_recovery`.

Round 311y89.decision_summary: R311y89 -- review C3 remediation: the advanced-subscriber recovery/history GETs now carry a query timeout so a no-answerer GET cannot wedge the subscriber forever. issue_recovery_query / issue_history_query were building QueryOptions with timeout_ms=0 (the never-expire sentinel: the pending reply entry registers with deadline_ms=None, which ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out skips on every pass) and swallowing the Session::query Result. With Locality::Any a no-cache history GET gets only the loopback Final (1 of 2 expected) and the peer Final never arrives, so finish_history never runs -> history_pending stays set -> EVERY live sample buffers undelivered (the subscriber delivers nothing). Fix: a RecoveryConfig::query_timeout field (default Duration::from_secs(10) = zenoh-ext RecoveryConfig::query_timeout default + zenoh-pico Z_GET_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT), converted by recovery_query_timeout_ms (clamped to [1,u32::MAX] so a 0/sub-ms Duration cannot re-open the never-expire sentinel) and threaded via with_timeout_ms onto every recovery + history GET; ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery now composes query-timeout (else with_timeout_ms no-ops). Plus an Err-rollback: a GET that fails to issue calls finish_recovery / finish_history directly so pending_queries / history_pending do not wedge. STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory unchanged (ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery/-history stay active).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: RecoveryConfig gained an always-present `query_timeout: Duration` field (default Duration::from_secs(10), zenoh's shared recovery/history GET timeout) + a with_query_timeout builder (signature-stable).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: new pure recovery_query_timeout_ms(Duration)->u32 clamps to [1,u32::MAX] -- the LOWER clamp is the correctness bite (a 0/sub-ms Duration is the timeout_ms==0 never-expire sentinel that registers the GET with deadline_ms=None, which ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out skips on every pass).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: issue_recovery_query + issue_history_query take a timeout_ms param set via QueryOptions::with_timeout_ms; run_periodic_tick threads it; declare_impl computes timeout_ms once and threads it to all 4 GET call sites (sample-driven / periodic / heartbeat / startup-history).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: issue_recovery_query / issue_history_query now inspect the Session::query Result and roll back on Err (finish_recovery / finish_history) -- a GET that never registered (Session::query rolled its pending entry back on a wire-emit error) can be released by neither its on_final nor the deadline sweep, so pending_queries / history_pending would wedge otherwise.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery now composes query-timeout (with_timeout_ms is a silent no-op without it, which would leave the wedge in place).

Round 311y90.decision_summary: R311y90 -- review C5 remediation: the advanced pub/sub background-task spawns now fail clear off-runtime instead of panicking. AdvancedPublisher::declare (heartbeat beacon) + AdvancedSubscriber::declare_with_recovery (periodic recovery task) call tokio::spawn, which PANICS without a tokio runtime; both are Result-returning fns whose Result swallowed that failure mode. Fix: a fail-fast Handle::try_current() guard before the side-effecting declares -> a dedicated NoRuntime Err variant. Publisher: AdvancedPublisherError gained #[non_exhaustive] + a NoRuntime variant (cfg-gated on ext-pubsub-sample-miss-detection). Subscriber: a NEW dedicated AdvancedSubscribeError {Subscribe(SubscribeError), NoRuntime} (advanced-recovery gated, #[non_exhaustive], From<SubscribeError>) returned by declare_with_recovery + declare_impl -- kept OUT of the base SubscribeError so toggling the additive ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery feature cannot change SubscribeError's shape and break a base declare_subscriber caller's exhaustive match (the H1 signature-stability class); the plain declare keeps SubscribeError. STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory unchanged.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_publisher.rs: AdvancedPublisherError gained #[non_exhaustive] + a NoRuntime variant (cfg-gated on ext-pubsub-sample-miss-detection); AdvancedPublisher::declare adds a fail-fast tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() guard (when sample_miss_detection.state_publisher is set + SequenceNumber) BEFORE declaring the cache/token, returning NoRuntime instead of the heartbeat-task tokio::spawn panic.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: new dedicated AdvancedSubscribeError {Subscribe(SubscribeError), NoRuntime} (#[cfg ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery], #[non_exhaustive], From<SubscribeError>); declare_with_recovery + declare_impl now return it (the plain declare keeps SubscribeError -- signature-stable). declare_impl adds a fail-fast Handle::try_current() guard when periodic_queries is set, BEFORE declaring the subscriber, returning NoRuntime instead of the periodic-task spawn panic.

Layering rationale: the NoRuntime spawn-failure mode lives in the ext modules' own error types (AdvancedPublisherError / the new AdvancedSubscribeError), NOT the base SubscribeError -- a cfg-gated variant on the shared SubscribeError would change its shape when an additive ext feature toggles, the H1 signature-stability violation. Mirrors the publisher's already-dedicated error type.

Round 311y92.decision_summary: R311y92 -- review S1 remediation: the @adv key-expr namespace SSOT. The advanced publisher CONSTRUCTS the @adv/pub/<zid>/<disc>/_ KE (cache queryable + liveliness token + heartbeat beacon) while the advanced subscriber MATCHES it (the recovery @adv/*/<zid>/<eid>/** + history @adv/** + heartbeat-sub @adv/pub/** GETs + the parse_heartbeat_source beacon parser). Previously the publisher held KE_ADV_PREFIX/KE_EMPTY consts (with pub still inline) while the subscriber hand-wrote @adv/pub inline x4, so the namespace had no single source of truth -- a drift on either side would silently break the recovery round-trip. Fix: a new pub(crate) advanced_ke module (the @adv/pub/_ consts + the publisher_adv_ke / recovery_get_ke / history_get_ke / heartbeat_sub_ke builders, each cfg-gated to its consumer feature so no combo dead-codes) that BOTH sides consume; the publisher construction + the subscriber's 4 inline sites now route through it. STRUCTURE-only, byte-identical KEs (the composed publisher->subscriber tests still pass); inventory unchanged.

Round 311y93.decision_summary: R311y93 -- review S3 + V1 remediation (V2 deferred). S3: AdvancedPublisherOptions gained #[non_exhaustive] (additive-field stability, consistent with the sibling AdvancedSubscriberOptions + AdvancedPublisherError). V1: the sporadic-heartbeat emit gate (!sporadic || sn > last_emitted), previously only compiled inside the spawned beacon loop, extracted to a pure deterministic should_emit_heartbeat(sporadic, sn, last_emitted) -> bool seam + a unit asserting non-sporadic-always-emit vs sporadic-skip-unless-advanced. V2 (the _max history cap composed test) DEFERRED: the cache _max filter is ALREADY unit-tested (advanced_cache answer_from_ring _max=1), but a composed loopback end-to-end test is BLOCKED by a core Session::query gap -- the loopback fan builds Query::default() with EMPTY parameters (R239 design point: loopback Query does not surface payload/params), so a SessionLocal history GET _max=N selector never reaches the cache answer_from_ring on loopback (the recovery _sn path only works on loopback because the subscriber reorder buffer masks the cache over-return; _max has no such mask). Fixing it is a core loopback-param-threading change with blast radius across ALL loopback queryables (storage/adminspace), surfaced for a separate decision. STRUCTURE/coverage-only; inventory unchanged.

advanced_cache.rs: parse_now_expr_ntp64 now resolves the now(±dur) offset in UNSIGNED NTP64 space (saturating_sub/add) instead of casting now_ntp64 through i64 — fixes a latent Y2038 wrong-drop (once unix secs reach 2^31 the NTP64 word is >= 2^63, so `as i64` wraps NEGATIVE; an UPPER now() bound then collapses to Included(0) and the filter drops every sample). Corrected the numerically-wrong justifying comment (~7.6e18 today, not ~1.8e18). NEW regression test parse_time_range_survives_post_2038_now_word (now=2^63: `[..now(-1h)]` keeps a large positive end; a 2h-old sample passes where the bug dropped it).
advanced_subscriber.rs: HistoryConfig::max_age gains a debug_assert!(seconds >= 0.0) + a doc note (a negative age would render the malformed now(--Ns) form the lower-bound emit negates).

SCE codegen template bug workaround in build.rs post-process: SCE emits `#![doc = "SCE-MAP: stem:line"]` as a file-leading inner attribute. SCE's own `cargo test -p sce-forge-runtime --features alloc` hits the same wall — verified R40. Workaround strips the redundant inner-attr line; the SCE-MAP info itself is also emitted on the very next line as a regular `// SCE-MAP: stem:line` comment, so zero info loss. Proper fix is an SCE upstream PR (R41 carry — see below).

TokioLinkDriverAdapter<D: LinkDriver> implements BoxedLinkDriver by holding a tokio::runtime::Handle and `block_on`-ing the async LinkDriver methods inside the sync NativeMethod closure shape (Lua's register_global_function takes a `Fn(&[ScriptValue]) -> ScriptValue + Send + Sync`).

wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_glue_dispatch.rs (~140 lines): single integration test walking the full happy-path + listener + close-reason script-action sequence through `dispatch_script`, asserting both the trace counters on SessionLinkActions and the RecordingDriver-side open/close/sends list. Single test on purpose — the Lua engine singleton + register_global_function are process-global, so cargo test's thread-parallel runner races concurrent installs.

Lua-engine process-globality is a production concern for multi-peer FSM instances on one process. Two FSM instances would race on `register_global_function` name space (link_driver_open() means whose LinkDriver). Either (a) push per-session bindings via `bind_native_object(session_id, ...)` and use session-scoped function tables, or (b) accept the single-FSM-per-process constraint and document it. Decide before multi-peer integration tests land.

R29 SCXML script-name single-source-of-truth audit. R54 wired 17 native fns by string name match; if `session_fsm_unicast.scxml` adds a new <script>foo()</script> without a matching install_session_actions registration, the Lua engine silently returns Nil + the SCE FSM continues. Consider a SCE codegen pass that emits the action-name set as a const `&[&str]` and a build-time check that `register_global_function` covers every name in that set.

changes_bullets: SessionInitParams::default removed. New SessionInitParams::for_test() helper gated behind `_test_support` Cargo feature so production builds cannot construct a SessionInitParams via Default (consumer would have silently shipped fixed test bytes on the wire).

changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_fsm_coverage.rs (~250 lines): single mega-test r61_full_coverage_sequential walks 11 scenarios covering every transition edge in session_fsm_unicast.scxml outside the R59 happy path — listener path (Init→AwaitingInitSyn→SentInitAck→SentOpenAck→Established), all 4 close-reason setters (Generic / Invalid / Expired / Unresponsive), all 5 close-from-state edges (LinkOpening / Opening.SentInitSyn / Opening / Established / Accepting), all 3 direct-to-Closed edges (link.lost from LinkOpening, peer.close from Established, link.lost from Accepting).

fresh_engine() helper isolates each scenario via rebind_session_actions_for_test (R60 feature-gated path); a fresh Driver + Actions triple resets every counter to zero between scenarios while INSTALLED OnceLock stays at its first-install pointer.

Sequential dispatch in one test fn is the only race-safe shape until R60 carry on session-scoped Lua binding lands. Initially split into 11 #[test] fns and observed 9/11 races; consolidated to one fn after diagnosis.

Each scenario asserts (a) Engine::get_current_state matches the SCXML target state, (b) trace.close_reason discriminator matches the set_close_reason_* action the transition runs, (c) send_close_frame_with_reason counter increments only on Closing-routed paths (not on direct-to-Closed via link.lost / peer.close).

changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: zeroize = '1' with zeroize_derive feature added. RustCrypto-ecosystem standard for cryptographic secret lifecycle.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: new SigningKey struct wrapping Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>; SigningKey::new(bytes) validates >= 32 bytes at construct (RFC §5.M) and returns Err(SigningKeyTooShort) instead of panicking at HMAC site. Drop wipes the heap allocation — cookie key bytes no longer linger in core dumps / heap-leak windows / panic backtraces.

2 new RFC 4231 test cases (TC1 + TC2) cross-check against the canonical HMAC-SHA256 vectors. If RustCrypto's hmac/sha2 ever regresses on us the assertion fires loud.
Removed signing_key_short_panics test; replaced with signing_key_short_returns_err matching the new typed-error path.

carry_forward_bullets: wz_codecs::request encode/decode roundtrip discrepancy — Request::default() with header=0x1C produces bytes where Request::decode consumes a different (smaller) byte count, leaving residual bytes that the R74 batch loop absorbs as Unknown. The contract should be 'encode then decode consumes exactly the encoded bytes' regardless of state. Likely root cause: Wireexpr default-state encode/decode mismatch OR RequestVariant Default-arm tag round-trip. A focused round on the wz-codecs codegen or Wireexpr default state would close this; without it, real production Request payloads (where header is set and inner body is meaningful) may roundtrip cleanly, but the codec contract is currently soft on default state.

PUSH is the highest-priority next target (pub/sub data path = put/del without request-reply correlation); RESPONSE follows for request-reply parity. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: IterationEvent<'a> enum (Poll(&'a DriverLoopOutcome) / Lease(LeaseCheckOutcome)) + manual Debug impl (DriverLoopOutcome has no derive Debug per R74; the manual impl prints Poll(o:?) / Lease(o:?) for test {ev:?} assertions). Variant choice mirrors the loop body's two work paths; the 'a borrow is the iteration's stack frame so observers retaining outcome data must clone owned fields (e.g. messages.clone() from FramePayload) into external storage.

LeaseCheckOutcome gains derive(Clone, Copy) — all three unit variants make Copy trivially correct, and the IterationEvent::Lease variant can take it by value without forcing observers to deal with move semantics.

drive_session_until_terminal signature: new generic param F: FnMut(IterationEvent<'_>) appended after max_iters; the 3 inner work paths (tokio::select Poll arm, tokio::select Lease arm, no-baseline await arm) each bind the outcome to a let-binding and call on_event(IterationEvent::...) before continuing. Previously the outcome bindings were `_ = ...` (silently discarded); after R83 every iteration surfaces exactly one event.

Rustdoc on the function extended with an R83 section explaining the bridge from producers (R74 FramePayload / R76 AdvancedFsm-LinkLost-ParseError / R77 LeaseCheckOutcome) to downstream consumers (pub/sub topic dispatcher / telemetry / logging). Synchronous-contract caveat documented: the closure runs inside the select arm so expensive consumers must buffer.

carry_forward_bullets: Multi-observer registry — R83 ships a single FnMut callback. Production deploys with multiple independent consumers (telemetry logger + pub/sub topic dispatcher + Lua bridge) need either a Vec<Box<dyn FnMut(IterationEvent)>> wrapper or an Observer trait with multiple registered impls. Defer until a real second-consumer use case lands so the registry shape is informed by an actual access pattern (mpsc broadcast vs cloned per-observer borrow vs shared-state lock).

FSM state snapshot in IterationEvent — the observer currently has no view of engine.get_current_state() at the iteration boundary because the loop holds &mut engine. Telemetry callers wanting `(state, outcome)` tuples must read engine state out-of-band before re-entering drive_session_until_terminal, which defeats the per-iteration observer pattern. Option: add a `state: SessionFsmUnicastState` field to each IterationEvent variant captured at iteration top before the select. Defer until a telemetry consumer requests it.

Async observer — R83's FnMut is synchronous; the closure body cannot .await. Consumers needing async work (HTTP POST telemetry, file IO) must buffer into a channel and process on a separate task. A future round could offer an async observer variant via a separate function (drive_session_with_async_observer) once a consumer pattern justifies the API split.

Per-iteration observer for outbound side — R83 covers inbound poll + lease only. Outbound TX path (send_init_syn / send_open_ack / etc.) goes through SCE dispatch and currently doesn't surface its own per-action events. A symmetric outbound observer is out of R83 scope but would close the telemetry surface.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: SessionLinkActions gains established_at: Mutex<Option<Instant>> slot, initialized None in SessionLinkActions::new; ActionTrace gains record_established_at: u32 counter for test-side observation; clone_via_copy() updated to forward the new field.

register_state_internal_fns adds bind_unit(lua, "record_established_at", ...) — sets trace.record_established_at += 1 AND populates *established_at.lock() = Some(Instant::now()). Two independent mutex locks (no deadlock risk); ordering trace-first matches handle_inbound's existing KeepAlive pattern.

REGISTERED_SCRIPT_NAMES (session_glue.rs:~1762) + EXPECTED_SCRIPT_NAMES (build.rs:~50) both gain "record_established_at" — the build.rs verifier cross-checks SCXML script-name references against the runtime registration set, so adding to one list without the other fails the build (drift hazard guarded by R60's consolidation).

sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml: Established.onentry gains <script>record_established_at()</script> as the second onentry action (after enable_rx_tx_regions, before start_lease_monitor / start_keepalive_worker). The script-call ordering matches the prose-level intent: regions enable first, the entry timestamp is recorded next so the lease monitor and keepalive worker start with the slot already populated.

check_lease_deadline baseline rewrite: prior R77 logic took stamp = last_inbound_keepalive_at, returning NoBaseline whenever that slot was None. handle_inbound: new match arm for InboundFrame::Init { is_ack: false, body, .. } that clones body.zid into the slot. Mirrors the existing InitAck (is_ack: true) inbound_cookie capture pattern at the same dispatch point. InitAck does NOT touch the slot (cross-role-confusion safety; r86_handle_inbound_init_ack_does_not_overwrite_peer_zid test pins this).

encode_init internal fn + encode_init_with_role public method gain cookie_override: Option<&[u8]> parameter (mirrors encode_open_with_role's existing override slot). encode_init uses cookie_override.unwrap_or(&params.cookie) for InitAck and ignores override entirely for InitSyn (wire-spec forbids cookie field there). The 4 external integration-test call sites in crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_ext_chain_outbound.rs updated to pass None — no compat shim per the project's no-shim rule (Round 60 textbook).

send_init_ack_with_cookie Lua binding: reads inbound_peer_zid slot, computes generate_cookie_hmac_sha256(&params.cookie_signing_key, peer_zid) when populated, passes the 16-byte result as cookie_override to encode_init_with_role. The prior R62 path used params.cookie verbatim — a deploy-static value that gave no per-peer replay defense. Production callers staging params.cookie as placeholder bytes (per R57's caller-owned interface) now get the spec-compliant HMAC value automatically once an InitSyn has arrived.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_fsm_accepting_path.rs: r86_send_init_ack_with_cookie_binds_to_inbound_peer_zid integration test added. carry_forward_bullets: Cookie verification on inbound OpenSyn — R86 closes the OUTBOUND cookie binding (Accepting side mints HMAC-bound cookie on InitAck). The INBOUND side (Accepting-side OpenSyn cookie verification) still trusts the peer's echoed cookie blindly (R57's guard_fns just returns true for cookie_valid). RFC §5.M requires the Accepting side to re-HMAC peer_zid with the same cookie_signing_key on OpenSyn arrival and compare against body.cookie. A follow-up round wires that verification through the cookie_valid guard.

inbound_peer_zid stale across handshake retries — R86's slot is populated once on InitSyn arrival but never cleared. A retry scenario where the FSM goes back to AwaitingInitSyn (currently NOT a wire-spec edge, but theoretically possible if a future round adds inbound.restart) would see stale peer_zid. Defensive: clear the slot on AwaitingInitSyn entry. Defer until the retry edge is on the roadmap.

Cookie ext-chain extension — R86 produces the 16-byte HMAC cookie in body.cookie. RFC §5.M also allows the cookie to carry additional MAC material via the ext chain (HMAC ext entry, deploy-specific anti-amplification token). The ext_chain_for(ExtChainRole::InitAck) slot is already wired (R68b); composing the HMAC into the ext chain is a separate extension point not covered by R86.

Initiator-side cookie verification — the Initiator (sending InitSyn) receives the Accepting side's InitAck cookie via inbound_cookie capture (R62). The Initiator echoes that cookie verbatim in OpenSyn (R57 caller-owned cookie field). Both sides should ideally re-derive the cookie locally and compare — but the Initiator doesn't know the cookie_signing_key (only the Accepting side does). So echo-only is the correct contract on the Initiator side; R86 only addresses the Accepting-side mint path.

changes_bullets: Root cause identified for the R82 codec discrepancy: `RequestVariant::default()` returns `CodecZenohMsgPut(MsgPut::default())` per sce-codegen's 'pick first variant' rule, but `MsgPut::default().header = 0` (low-5 MID = 0) causes Request::decode's inner-MID dispatch (line 102 of generated request.rs: `match (peek >> 0) & 0x1F { 1=>MsgPut, 2=>MsgDel, 3=>Query, other=>Default{tag:other, body:Query} }`) to route to the Default arm with Query::decode. End-to-end RFC §5.M cookie binding closure: (1) InitSyn arrives -> handle_inbound captures peer_zid (R86); (2) SentInitAck.onentry -> send_init_ack_with_cookie computes HMAC(key, peer_zid)[..16] and embeds in InitAck wire (R86); (3) Initiator echoes cookie back in OpenSyn (Initiator-side R62 chain); (4) OpenSyn arrives -> handle_inbound captures echoed cookie (R89); (5) cookie_valid() re-HMACs and compares (R89); (6) match -> FSM advances to SentOpenAck, mismatch -> stuck at SentInitAck.
carry_forward_bullets: Constant-time comparison — R89 uses standard byte-equality (==) for the HMAC compare. For a single-peer test fixture this is fine; production hardening against timing oracles would swap to subtle::ConstantTimeEq. Defer until a security review surfaces a timing-side-channel concern in the deploy.yaml scope (mostly an issue for multi-tenant routers, less so for embedded AP pairings).

Slot lifetime / replay defense — R89 captures the inbound_opensyn_cookie slot once on each OpenSyn arrival and overwrites on subsequent arrivals. A replay attack (peer re-sends a stale OpenSyn) is possible if the FSM ever revisits SentInitAck. Current session-fsm doesn't have a SentInitAck re-entry edge so this is theoretical; a defensive clear-on-exit hook (similar to R84's established_at carry #1) would close it preemptively.

Cookie ext-chain MAC material — RFC §5.M allows additional MAC carriers in the cookie ext-chain. R89 verifies the base 16-byte HMAC only. The ext-chain extension point lives in `ext_chain_for(ExtChainRole::InitAck)` (R68b slot) but isn't HMAC-composed yet. Out of R89 scope.

half_open_cap_available + accept_rate_token guards still R57 placeholders (bind_bool true). bind_guard infrastructure from R89 now exists, so retiring those placeholders is a 2-line change once cap-quota / token-bucket implementations land. Defer until DoS-mitigation rounds.

Initiator-side cookie verification absent — R89 is Accepting-side. The Initiator receives the Accepting side's cookie via InitAck and echoes it verbatim on OpenSyn. The Initiator cannot verify the cookie itself (only the Accepting side holds cookie_signing_key); echo-only is the correct contract per RFC §5.M. No carry needed — explicitly NOT a gap.

SLICE 1 = upstream's OWN examples/z_put.c links against crates/wz-capi-c's cdylib, compiled against UPSTREAM's unmodified header, and a real wz subscriber receives what it publishes. SLICE 2 (R311y500) = the SUBSCRIBER family plus z_delete, so upstream's own z_sub.c and z_delete.c link and run: 15 symbols measured with nm -u, spanning four new planes -- the sample closure (z_closure_sample, TRANSPARENT in upstream's header so it matches field for field, not merely in size), the subscriber declaration (z_declare_subscriber over the shared face registry, consume-on-all-paths for the moved closure), the sample accessors (z_sample_keyexpr / _payload / _kind / _attachment over a per-call SampleMarshal), and the string family (one StringRepr behind z_owned_string_t / z_view_string_t / z_loaned_string_t, because upstream's two loans are pointer casts). RESIDUAL, printed by Layer C1cc every run: 4 of 22 upstream examples link, up from 1 (7 more do not compile against this oracle build at all -- SHM and unstable-API -- and are out of the denominator, being a property of the oracle rather than of wz). The cheapest next ones are named by the same report: z_liveliness needs ONE symbol, z_sub_liveliness two. CROSS-IMPL PROOF (R311y500): the sibling fixture zenoh_c_examples_on_wz_capi_c_dropin.rs carries NO proof annotation and Layer A4 was right to refuse one -- the C program links wz and the observer is a wz node, so no foreign implementation is on the wire. zenoh_c_capi_c_pico_interop.rs puts a REAL zenoh-pico CLI opposite instead: upstream z_sub.c on wz receives from a real pico z_put (pico->wz), and upstream z_put.c on wz reaches a real pico z_sub, where the FOREIGN process reports the verdict (wz->pico). A third leg drives z_delete: it proves wz's Del BODY survives a foreign decoder, and it deliberately does NOT claim the KIND, because a scan of every subscriber example in vendor/zenoh-pico found none that renders it -- measured, and calibrated by a damage that makes z_delete emit an empty PUT and passes. All three partial, the residual being the ratio above. A FOURTH leg (Layer C1cd, on the job that has zenohd) witnesses z_sample_attachment's PRESENT arm with TWO foreign implementations on the path: a real pico z_pub_attachment encodes it, a real zenohd routes it, and only the rendering is wz's. It is a separate lane because it needs a router, and that requirement was ESTABLISHED rather than assumed. pico's attachment example publishes through a DECLARED PUBLISHER, which delivers nothing in the client-to-listening-peer topology the other three legs use -- not to wz, and not pico-to-pico. Two wrong readings preceded the right one: first that wz had an ingress defect, then that pico failing identically made it not wz's problem. The second is the more dangerous error, because matching pico is not the same as being correct (wz is a superset, not a mirror) and two implementations can miss one observable for unrelated reasons. What settled it was measuring all four arms with a real zenohd: pico z_pub reaches a pico subscriber through zenohd (3 of 3) and through wz's own --router-hat (3 of 3), so the declared-publisher path works and wz forwards it as the reference router does -- the earlier failures were the ABSENT ROUTER, a fact about the harness and about neither implementation. The NULL arm and the null-pointer guards are additionally unit-tested. THE SCOPE IS A PROGRAM, NOT A SYMBOL LIST, and that distinction earned its keep immediately: a hand-picked 12-symbol list drafted before measuring named four symbols zenoh-c never calls and missed three it does (z_bytes_from_static_str not z_bytes_copy_from_str; zc_config_from_file + zc_config_insert_json5 not zc_config_from_str; and zc_init_log_from_env_or, which nothing about implementing a put would suggest). SHIPS NO HEADER, unlike its sibling api-compat-pico's R1: zenoh-c's header is cbindgen OUTPUT so it IS the ABI, and a wz-authored header would make the claim untestable. TWO ARMS on the dropin fixture, which the sibling atom lacks: upstream's examples give REPRESENTATIVENESS (a wz-authored program calls only what wz exports -- the bias that let api-compat-pico sit at BUILT unwitnessed), and the real libzenohc.so as a REFERENCE arm gives EQUIVALENCE (linking alone cannot show wz's answers are the same answers). THE FOOTPRINTS ARE FEATURE-DEPENDENT, measured not assumed: upstream's published standalone archive is built WITH Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and a build without it is a different ABI -- z_owned_bytes_t is 40 vs 32, z_put_options_t 56 vs 48 -- so "wz is a zenoh-c drop-in" is incomplete until the build is named. wz expresses that as the zenoh-c-no-unstable-api cargo feature (default = the published archive), Layer C1cc reads the INSTALLED header and selects the matching arm, and both arms are clippy-gated. The layout gate covers the slice-2 types too (subscriber 48, string 32, closure 24) because z_sub.c STACK-ALLOCATES them, and a stack-allocated type whose size wz gets wrong corrupts the caller's frame rather than failing anything. Session machinery is NOT duplicated: wz-capi-core (extracted R311y498 from wz-capi-pico, with the C-closure dependency inverted into callback factories) is the one session model both ABIs run on. cfg sites: the wz facade's api-compat-c composition toggle. AP/std-only. NOT a member of preset-ap-full and cannot be: zenoh-pico and zenoh-c both own the z_* symbol namespace, so the facade compile_error!s on both and Layer A5 carries api-compat-c as an alt-abi exclusion. Source: zenoh-c 1.5.0 (tag 1.5.0, f5d5a90d).

Async-drive bridge (wz has no self-driving Session): per-session multi-thread tokio runtime on a dedicated thread block_on-ing the open handshake + drive_session_until_terminal loop; z_close signals shutdown via Notify. Byte-compat wz-own header (include/wz_capi_pico.h); ABI is not copyrightable expression, no zenoh-pico header vendored. A3 gate = `#[cfg(feature="api-compat-pico")] pub use wz_capi_pico as capi_pico` in crates/wz/src/lib.rs. KEYEXPR-DECLARATION FAMILY BUILT (R311y477): a real declare plane -- SharedSession gains a THIRD SSOT (KexprEntry) with a session-global mapping id (pico's `_z_get_resource_id` model; safe because a keyexpr mapping table is DIRECTIONAL), per-face send_declare_keyexpr fan-out, REPLAY onto later faces ordered BEFORE the sub/qbl replays, send_undeclare_kexpr on retract, and z_put routing through publish_aliased_auto when the keyexpr carries a declaration. Ids REFUSED above u16::MAX rather than wrapped. ABI: literal at slots 0/1 in BOTH the view and declared arms, _handle and _mapping additive, _mapping == 0 the not-declared discriminant (0 is wire-reserved). PLATFORM SURFACE BUILT (R311y478): z_malloc / z_free / z_sleep_{us,ms,s} / z_clock_now / z_clock_elapsed_{us,ms,s} (src/platform.rs) plus z_bytes_from_buf, z_bytes_from_static_buf, z_view_keyexpr_from_str_unchecked, z_declare_background_subscriber. Chosen by BUNDLE-CLOSURE ranking, not blocked-count: z_malloc/z_free blocked nine examples each but the platform bundle alone closes ONE; adding z_declare_background_subscriber took it to four. z_malloc/z_free forward to libc (pico defines them as exactly malloc/free and a C program may mix them with plain free() on one pointer); z_clock_now is clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) via libc so the constant stays right per platform; z_clock_elapsed_* reproduces pico's SIGNED difference with its clamp-to-zero (system.c:235-238) rather than a Duration subtraction, which would panic where pico returns 0. z_bytes_from_buf invokes the caller's deleter immediately after copying on every path -- pico's ownership transfer is unconditional, so dropping it would leak the caller's buffer. LIVELINESS PLANE BOUND (R311y479): z_liveliness_declare_token / z_liveliness_undeclare_token + the token ownership set, z_liveliness_declare_subscriber, and both options-default constructors (src/liveliness.rs). Binds wz's already-ACTIVE liveliness-token and liveliness-subscriber atoms; no new protocol. Adds the FOURTH and FIFTH SSOTs (TokenEntry, LiveSubEntry), both replayed in face_up -- a token declared before any peer connects is the ORDINARY case for upstream's z_liveliness.c, which declares and then sleeps. The liveliness subscriptions share SubId space with the ordinary ones because C gets back the same z_owned_subscriber_t either way, so undeclare_subscriber searches both maps. DROPPING A TOKEN RETRACTS IT: the retraction lives in TokenState::drop, so the explicit z_liveliness_undeclare_token and the implicit z_drop take the identical path and cannot drift. That is pico's contract -- z_liveliness_token_drop runs _z_liveliness_token_clear which calls _z_undeclare_liveliness_token (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/liveliness.c:35-43) -- and upstream's z_liveliness.c relies on it, never calling the explicit undeclare. A liveliness event reaches C as an ORDINARY sample closure: EMPTY payload, PUT for a token appearing and DELETE for one going away. FOREIGN WITNESS (R311y476, extended y477/y478/y479): crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs compiles UNMODIFIED upstream examples against zenoh-pico's OWN headers (vendored tree + the CMake-GENERATED config.h that pins the Z_FEATURE_* set the pico CLI oracles were built with), links them against libwz_capi_pico.so, and runs them against a real zenoh-pico CLI. SIX legs: z_sub.c receives from a real z_put; z_queryable.c answers a real z_get with the FOREIGN querier reporting the verdict; z_put.c DECLARES its keyexpr and the aliased publish reaches a real z_sub; z_ping.c completes 5 round trips against a real z_pong; z_liveliness.c is seen ALIVE then DROPPED by a real z_sub_liveliness; z_sub_liveliness.c sees a real pico token come and go. All claims `partial`. Lane = Layer E, which also builds the cdylib and guards on z_pong / z_liveliness / z_sub_liveliness. Layer A4 checks the claim against the closure of `wz --features api-compat-pico`. MEASURED COVERAGE ACROSS UPSTREAM'S EXAMPLES (R311y479, all 32 -- R311y476 said 31 and was WRONG): NINE now link with a real body (z_liveliness, z_ping, z_pong, z_put, z_queryable, z_queryable_lat, z_sub, z_sub_liveliness, z_sub_thr), up from 7 at y478, 3 at y477 and 1 before y476. SIX link while calling nothing at all (z_advanced_pub, z_advanced_sub, z_pub_st, z_pub_tls, z_sub_st, z_sub_tls compile to a `#else` stub main because the generated feature set disagrees with what they demand). A link is NOT a pass; `nm -u <obj> | grep z_open` is what separates them. 15 examples are still short of exports and 2 more are stubs AND short. Of the nine linkers, SIX are driven as legs, z_pong serves as the witness file's own counterparty, and z_queryable_lat / z_sub_thr link but are NOT yet driven -- recorded rather than rounded up. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BY THE FOREIGN WITNESS (R311y476): z_query_payload and z_query_attachment returned NULL for an absent payload/attachment. pico's own getters are unconditional address-of (api.c:476 and :472) while the neighbouring z_query_source_info (:478-481) DOES gate on a check -- pico is asymmetric on purpose and wz had copied the wrong sibling. Upstream's z_queryable.c calls z_bytes_to_string(z_query_payload(query), &s) UNCONDITIONALLY and only then tests the length, so the null left a stack-allocated owned string uninitialized and the next line loaned it: the example ABORTED on a garbage handle the moment a real z_get reached it. The distinction that makes this class of divergence fatal versus benign: pico supplies a guard function for the reply getters (z_reply_is_ok) and supplies NONE for the query payload/attachment. RESIDUALS vs the vendored zenoh-pico C API, MEASURED not estimated, re-measured R311y479: coverage is 184 of 726 declared functions (cpp -P over zenoh-pico.h at the generated config, against nm -D --defined-only on the built cdylib), so 542 are missing -- and all 184 wz names exist in pico's declared set, 0 invented. Entire families still absent: encoding, ze_serialize, handlers/channels, the _z_rc_* refcount primitives those handlers inline, scouting/hello, advanced pub/sub, matching listener, querier. Sample accessors cover only keyexpr/payload/kind, missing encoding/timestamp/attachment/priority. z_delete and z_publisher_delete are absent. z_put_options_default and the publisher/subscriber equivalents are NOT exported while the get/queryable ones are, so the idiomatic pico call form fails to link -- a sibling asymmetry. Options are ignored on the whole pubsub/session path, dropping congestion_control, priority, express, encoding, attachment and timestamp. zp_start/stop read and lease tasks are unconditional no-ops returning Z_OK. z_owned_publisher_t is 32 bytes against pico's 160 (z_owned_keyexpr_t is 48 B and z_owned_liveliness_token_t 24 B, both MATCHING). Z_ERR_INVALID = -1 is INVENTED: -1 is not a member of pico's _z_res_t. z_bytes_from_static_str / z_bytes_from_static_buf COPY where pico ALIASES -- a named cost divergence. z_declare_publisher does NOT alias even when handed a declared keyexpr; correct on the wire, just not bandwidth-optimised, and a named follow-up. Source: zenoh 1.5.0 49c8a53 / the vendored zenoh-pico 1.9.0, which is the graded upstream. R311y522 -- ACCEPT-PATH LIVELINESS FLUSH ADDED. A C program that declared z_liveliness_declare_subscriber was never told when the peer holding a token VANISHED: face_down dropped the FaceEntry and with it the whole per-face ApplicationLayerObserver, in silence, and no UndeclToken can arrive because the link that would carry one is what died. face_down now flushes that observer AND drains the deferred-fire queue. The drain is the load-bearing half and is why an earlier attempt was reverted: the registry slot holds a DEFERRED-FIRE staging sink (R311lg), so flushing alone stages Deletes that nothing delivers -- it measures as 1 slot FIRED and reaches the application as silence. Flushing the WHOLE observer is correct here only because face_up builds one per face; on a shared observer it would delete other faces tokens. Gated by wz-capi-pico/tests/liveliness_face_death.rs, which Layer C1 was CONFIRMED to run, with three probes: no flush -> red, flush without drain -> red, and fix-removed-plus-token-BOUND -> green, which is why the test must std::mem::forget the token (a bound token emits an UndeclToken that R311y519's drain now delivers, so the gate would pass through the ordinary undeclare path).

session-extshm.reason: COMPLETE (R311y507 closed the residual R311y505 named). F=the SHM establishment handshake; P=zenoh `init::ext::Shm` (`zextzbuf!(0x2)`) + `open::ext::Shm` (`zextz64!(0x2)`), FSM at `establishment/ext/shm.rs`; C=requires transport-shm. wz now runs zenoh's real CHALLENGE-RESPONSE, not the scoped UNIT capability offer/reflect/`&=` the prior reason recorded as the substitute. The exchange: InitSyn carries the initiator's AUTH SEGMENT id; the acceptor MAPS that segment, reads the random challenge inside it, and returns it on InitAck beside its own segment id; the initiator validates the echo against its own challenge, maps the acceptor's segment, and answers with ITS challenge on OpenSyn; the acceptor validates that second echo and confirms with the literal 1 on OpenAck. Each side therefore PROVES map-ability to the other -- a token exchange would pass between two hosts that share nothing. The segment is a real POSIX object (`wz-runtime-tokio::shm_auth_segment`, `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` -- the NAME is wire format, since a foreign peer opens exactly that string) holding a u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`; the challenge is stored BITWISE-INVERTED as upstream stores it, which is load-bearing interop rather than obfuscation. `SHM_VERSION` mismatch, an unmappable segment, and a wrong echo all degrade to "no shared memory" with the session intact; only a MALFORMED InitSyn body aborts, mirroring zenoh's one `bail!` and its asymmetry with the initiator's tolerant `recv_init_ack`. OPT-IN: the dispatch is EMPTY until an authenticator is installed, and an empty one emits nothing, so a deploy that installs none keeps the pre-R311y507 UNIT wire byte-identical; the two mechanisms never half-mix, because the challenge REPLACES the UNIT ext at the stage seam and the offer predicate follows whichever mechanism is running. CROSS-IMPL PROVEN (A4, `wz_shm_establishment_zenohd_interop`, run-ci Layer Z) against a real `zenohd --features shared-memory`: BOTH directions now report `shm negotiated = true` where R311y505 correctly asserted `false` for the UNIT mechanism. DAMAGE-BOUND: storing the challenge un-inverted flips both legs to `false` with the session still Established, so the green is bound to the exact page layout zenohd reads; a second damage (accepting any echo) reds the forged-challenge unit test while leaving the wz<->wz e2e green, which is the honest split -- two cooperating wz peers cannot show that the CHECK is enforced. Still scoped vs upstream: no segment pool / watchdog / generation, and wz never takes the EXCLUSIVE flock upstream uses to invalidate a recycled segment (wz has no pool for it to guard). R311y516 -- the R311y514 enumeration was run against this atom (list every reader of the negotiated state, name which is on the data path) and found the negotiation ENFORCED on TX but NOT on RX. The TX side was already there (Session::publish_shm reads is_shm() and swaps the descriptor for the bytes); the RX un-swap honoured the 0x2 body marker ALONE, so an un-negotiated peer could still make this node map a segment it named. The gate now lives on the data path where it belongs -- see the transport-shm atom for the mechanism, the zenoh citation and the damage-bound proof. This atom's own claim (the challenge-response establishment exchange) is unchanged; what R311y516 fixes is that the capability it negotiates now actually governs the receive path, which is the difference between a proven handshake and an enforced one.

R311y305 vs zenoh-shm + init.rs SHM challenge-response: REAL /dev/shm mmap, not descriptor-only (shm_provider.rs:61 alloc creates + map_mut, :131 resolve maps read-only + copies out, real-syscall round-trip test :149; live TX descriptor-swap push_build.rs:612 + RX un-swap pubsub.rs:714). R311y507 CLOSED the establishment half of the named residual: wz no longer negotiates SHM with a UNIT capability offer/reflect/`&=` but with zenoh's ZBuf-on-Init / z64-on-Open CHALLENGE-RESPONSE over a real POSIX auth segment, so the transport is wire-compatible with a `zenohd --features shared-memory` -- CROSS-IMPL PROVEN in BOTH directions (`wz_shm_establishment_zenohd_interop`, `shm negotiated = true` where R311y505 correctly measured `false`), damage-bound by storing the auth challenge un-inverted, which flips both legs to `false`. See the session-extshm atom for the exchange and its scoped limits. WHAT KEEPS THIS PARTIAL is now the DATA path, not establishment: the receiver still makes one bounded copy off the page into wz's owned Sample (wire zero-copy, local Sample single-copy), and there is no segment POOL / watchdog / generation -- one segment per payload. So a negotiated wz<->zenohd session agrees on SHM at establishment while the PAYLOAD interop (zenoh's `ShmBufInfo` descriptor + its metadata-segment `MetadataDescriptor{id,index}`, which wz collapses to a single segment_id) is the remaining gap and is NOT claimed. LOCAL-ONLY lane C1af (off-default, not dev-dep-unified); C4 preset build gate; Layer Z carries the establishment interop, which SKIPs on hosted CI (the shared-memory oracle needs a SOURCE build -- `ZENOHD_SHM=1 ZENOHD_SRC=<checkout> scripts/build-zenohd.sh`). R311y516 CLOSED an RX ENFORCEMENT hole in this data path, found by running the R311y514 enumeration technique (list every reader of a negotiated capability's state and name which one is on the data path) against the three unswept establishment extensions. The RX un-swap (pubsub.rs dispatch_push) consulted ONLY the body's 0x2 marker, never the negotiated is_shm: a peer that had NOT negotiated SHM could name a /dev/shm segment and this node would map it and deliver its contents, so the negotiation was decorative on the receive side. zenoh gates its whole un-swap on the negotiated per-transport capability -- io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/universal/rx.rs:50-51 wraps map_zmsg_to_shmbuf in `if self.config.shm.is_some()`, the same expression as its is_shm() at unicast/universal/transport.rs:349-350. wz now carries the counterpart: SubscriberRegistry gained a shm_negotiated gate plus a shm_unnegotiated_drops counter, RESTAMPED live every dispatch iteration from the unicast dispatch SSOT (Session::dispatch_iteration_event_with, wz's counterpart of zenoh's trigger_callback) rather than snapshotted -- negotiate_shm_against_peer is a monotonic &=, so a reconnect can only drive the capability DOWN and a construction-time snapshot would go stale in the fail-OPEN direction. Multicast never stamps and stays fail-closed at the default. PROVEN by an_unnegotiated_peer_cannot_make_this_node_map_its_segment (C1af, count pin 5 -> 6): the two arms differ in EXACTLY ONE bit, with the same live segment, the same installed PosixShmResolver and the same valid descriptor in both, so the refusing arm cannot pass for a boring reason. DAMAGE-BOUND: disabling the gate delivers the stranger's bytes and reds the arm. The atom stays PARTIAL on the residual named above -- the single bounded copy, and no segment pool / watchdog / generation.
